title: Grill-me needed: how should louiselm expose Neovim diagnostics through ACP?
description:
Do not resolve this in passing — this question needs a deliberate design discussion before implementation.

## The question

Should louiselm collect Neovim diagnostics and send them to ACP agents as prompt context, and should the louiselm/acp-llm-adapter stack negotiate a custom capability or request for fresh diagnostics?

## Context and evidence

The user wants to fix diagnostics shown by Snacks (for example diagnostics on Cargo.toml) without making the model spend tokens rediscovering them. Snacks is only displaying Neovim’s diagnostic store; diagnostics may come from rust-analyzer, taplo, lua-language-server, or another LSP, so the client-side feature should be language- and adapter-agnostic.

The ACP client is louiselm.nvim and the agent is acp-llm-adapter. ACP has no standard diagnostics capability, but supports custom capabilities and methods through _meta and underscore-prefixed JSON-RPC extensions. The adapter currently advertises embeddedContext: true, so the client can already send diagnostics as text or embedded resource prompt content. The adapter records incoming client capabilities but does not currently advertise or implement a diagnostics extension.

## Threads worth pulling

- Decide whether initial diagnostics should simply be collected by louiselm on an explicit fix action and attached to session/prompt, with no protocol extension.
- Decide whether a custom client capability should advertise a semantic feature such as current editor diagnostics, without exposing the implementation detail vim.diagnostic.
- Decide whether the adapter needs an on-demand custom request for fresh diagnostics after edits, versus relying on terminal/LSP rechecks.
- Define scope and selection: current line, current buffer, workspace, or user-selected Snacks diagnostics; errors/warnings only by default.
- Define a compact, typed representation containing absolute URI/path, 1-based line/column, severity, source, code, message, and freshness/change context.
- Decide whether diagnostics belong in standard prompt content, prompt _meta, an embedded resource, or a custom request response.
- Account for stale diagnostics, noisy hints, external/untrusted diagnostic text, prompt size, and cross-editor interoperability.
- Keep the standard ACP path usable by other clients and agents; any custom extension must be optional and namespaced.

## Out of scope

Implementing the diagnostics collector, changing ACP protocol code, or choosing a final wire format before this design question is deliberately opened.
close_reason: Design confirmed by maintainer; diagnostics collection contract recorded in issue comment

comments.author: codex/01a037d9-bf57-7921-86bc-79ca8584c171
comments.text: Maintainer-confirmed design: expose an explicit :LouiselmDiagnostics action; collect current-buffer errors and warnings; queue compact text on the next prompt without auto-sending; use standard ACP with no custom capability/request in v1; include path, 1-based line/column, severity, source, code, and message; include observation time and buffer-change state without silently refreshing diagnostics; cap diagnostic count and message length with explicit truncation counts; report a clear error and make no changes when no LouiseLM Session is active; delimit diagnostic messages as untrusted data rather than Agent instructions. Implementation can now be decomposed separately.

title: QA round: AGENTS.md resource_link injection (louiselm-ce6.20)
description:
# Manual QA review — AGENTS.md resource_link injection

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `fde8c6a` (feat(context): attach project instructions as
an ACP resource_link, closes louiselm-ce6.20), repo now at `6b2a69f` (two
later commits are unrelated agent health-check work, not part of this
feature's scope). **Restart Neovim after any fix** — this is a plugin loaded
from source, there is no build step, but Lua modules are cached per-process.

Origin: on a brand-new ACP session's first prompt, louiselm now attaches a
`resource_link` content block (name + URI, not the file body) pointing at a
configured project-instructions file (e.g. `AGENTS.md`), when
`context.instructions_file` is set and the file exists at the project root.
The automated suite (251/251 mini.test cases, including one real-wire-bytes
test via a fake ACP process) proves the block is *sent* correctly. It cannot
prove a real agent *does anything* with it, and it cannot show you what the
chat buffer actually looks like — that's this round.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | A real agent actually reads the linked file | **passed** — session `claude/25ef1772-…`, log `20260820-082942-635200-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`: first action is a native `Read` tool call on `/home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md`, answer cites AGENTS.md:229-239 verbatim-correct |
| 2 | Visible context chip on a brand-new session | **passed** — session `claude/8fe8fd28-…`, cursor lands after the chip |
| 3 | No duplicate/leaked link across two sibling new sessions | **passed** — user-confirmed, no duplication/leakage |
| 4 | Resumed session never gets the link | **passed** — session `claude/1dec0a6e-…` resumed, no `[context: ...]` chip |

## Setup

Add this to wherever you already call `require("louiselm").setup(...)` in
your Neovim config (I don't have that path — tell me if you want me to look):

```lua
require("louiselm").setup({
  -- ...your existing agents/skills/etc...
  context = { instructions_file = "AGENTS.md" },
})
```

Restart Neovim fully (`:qa` and relaunch) so the new commit's Lua is loaded
fresh, not the cached previous version. Confirm the running copy matches
source: `:lua print(require("louiselm.instructions") ~= nil)` should print
`true` with no error — that module didn't exist before this commit, so an
error here means you're still on stale Lua.

Run all cases from a project whose root already has `AGENTS.md` — this repo
(`/home/lotso/code/louiselm`) qualifies, since it has one. Open Neovim with
`cwd` set to this repo for that reason (`cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm && nvim`).

## Ground rules learned the hard way

(empty so far — append here whenever a case misses for an environmental
reason rather than a code reason)

## Cases

### 1. A real agent actually reads the linked file

Exercises the entire point of `fde8c6a` — a mock ACP process can prove the
bytes were sent, it cannot prove any real agent binary honors a
`resource_link`. Also worth knowing going in: louiselm's ACP client currently
advertises `fs = { readTextFile = false }` (`lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:195`,
predates this commit) — so a strictly spec-compliant agent should not even
attempt to fetch the link *through the ACP protocol*. The only way this can
work today is if the agent opens the local `file://` path directly off disk
itself. That's a real uncertainty this case is meant to settle, not a
predicted bug — some agents may ignore `resource_link` blocks entirely.

Steps:

> Open `:LouiselmChat` (or `:LouiselmNewSession`) against whichever real,
> responsive agent you normally dogfood with. As the very first prompt of
> the new session, type something that only makes sense if the agent has
> actually read this repo's `AGENTS.md`, e.g.:
>
> `> Without me telling you, name one thing this project's AGENTS.md says agents must do before finishing a code task.`

Expect: the agent's answer names something real from this repo's `AGENTS.md`
(e.g. "run stylua/lua-language-server/mini.test before handoff", "use
red-green-refactor", "don't add compatibility shims").

Failure signature: the agent says it doesn't have access to that file, asks
you to paste it, answers generically/incorrectly, or answers about a
*different* AGENTS.md-style convention it already knows from training rather
than this repo's actual content.

Evidence: if your agent is the default DeepSeek-backed
`acp-llm-adapter` wrapped by `acp-debug.sh`, its **stdout** (agent→client
direction) is logged to
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/<timestamp>-<pid>-*-stdout-jsonrpc.log`
(newest file for this run — match by the timestamp printed at session start,
not "most recent," since old logs pile up). That log will *not* show the
`resource_link` louiselm sent (that's client→agent, unlogged by this script)
but it will show whether the agent issued an `fs/read_text_file` request back
— which it shouldn't, given the capability is off — and whatever `session/prompt`-adjacent
traffic it produces. For any other agent: there's no log, so this case rests
on what you read in its answer. Say so plainly when you report back.

### 2. Visible context chip on a brand-new session

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` `Chat:new_session` (queues
`instructions_context`) and `queue_context`'s `context_prefix` rendering.
Purely synchronous UI state — doesn't need the agent to ever respond.

Steps:

> Run `:LouiselmNewSession` (or `:LouiselmChat` for the first session). Look
> at the prompt line before typing anything.

Expect: the prompt line reads `> [context: AGENTS.md] ` — one clean chip,
cursor positioned right after it, ready to type. Type `hi` and look again:
`> [context: AGENTS.md] hi`, chip text not duplicated, not overwriting itself.

Failure signature: chip missing entirely, chip text garbled/duplicated,
cursor lands before the chip instead of after it, or typing overwrites part
of the `[context: AGENTS.md]` marker itself.

Evidence: what you see in the buffer. No file/log needed for this one.

### 3. No duplicate/leaked link across two sibling new sessions

Exercises the once-per-new-session gating in `Chat:new_session` — automated
coverage only exercises a single session per test process, never two created
back-to-back sharing one `Chat` instance.

Steps:

> With the chat UI already open from case 2, run `:LouiselmNewSession` again
> to create a second, sibling session (don't resume/switch to the first).
> Look at its prompt line. Then switch back to the first session
> (`:LouiselmSwitchSession`) and look at its prompt line again.

Expect: the second session's prompt line also shows exactly one
`[context: AGENTS.md]` chip. The first session's line is unaffected by the
second session's creation (still whatever you left it at in case 2 — one
chip, not two).

Failure signature: either session shows the chip twice concatenated, the
second session shows no chip at all, or the first session's chip
duplicates/changes after the second session is created.

Evidence: what you see in each session's buffer, switching between them.

### 4. Resumed session never gets the link

Exercises the `Chat:resume_session`/`load_session` path, which — unlike
`Chat:new_session` — never queues `instructions_context`. This is the
mechanism AC #4 relies on; automated coverage only asserts it for a directly
`attach`-ed fake session, never through the real discovery/picker UI.

Steps:

> Close the chat UI (`:LouiselmCloseSession` or just `:qa` and relaunch
> Neovim). Run `:LouiselmResume` (or `:LouiselmResume!` for all workspaces)
> and pick one of the sessions created in cases 2/3 from the picker.

Expect: the resumed session's prompt line shows no `[context: ...]` chip at
all — plain `> `.

Failure signature: a `[context: AGENTS.md]` chip appears on a resumed
session's prompt line before you've typed or queued anything yourself.

Evidence: what you see in the buffer right after resume, before typing.

## Evidence check

There's no single command that verifies all four cases — 2 through 4 are
pure UI-state observations (that's the point: things a mock-ACP unit test
cannot see), and case 1 has a log only if you're on the default DeepSeek
agent. Report what you saw for each; I'll flag anything that sounds like a
recipe issue (wrong cwd, stale Lua) versus a real product bug before we
record it.

## Cleanup when the round closes

No fixtures created outside your own Neovim session state (no files written,
no repo state changed). Nothing to revert beyond closing the chat sessions
you opened for cases 2–4.

## Reporting back

Tell me which case, what you saw, and anything surprising — especially for
case 1, since "the agent answered correctly" only proves the happy path;
tell me if it hedged, refused, or answered from training data instead of the
actual file. I'll pull whatever log evidence exists myself before we call a
case passed or failed.

## Findings this round

**F1 — cursor landed before the queued context chip, not after** (`louiselm-muo`,
closed, fixed in `e15a846`). `Chat:attach` sets the cursor once at
`ui/chat/init.lua:1441` before `Chat:new_session` queues any automatic context;
`queue_context` rewrote the prompt line to prepend the chip but never moved the
cursor, so it stayed at the pre-chip column regardless of chip length. Affects
skill-catalog inject mode too, not just this feature — pre-existing bug this
round's case 2 was the first thing to exercise. Fixed: `queue_context` now
repositions the cursor to just past the full `context_prefix` after rewriting
the line. Regression test: `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` "positions the cursor
after queued context, not before it" (failed `{6,1}` vs expected `{6,27}`
before the fix). Full suite 267/267, stylua/lua-language-server clean.
Confirmed live by user in session `claude/8fe8fd28-ac0c-4293-bc77-5fc605d432ea`.
close_reason: 4/4 cases passed. Case 1 (real agent honors the resource_link) and case 2 (visible chip) each got direct session-log/user evidence; 1 real bug found and fixed (louiselm-muo, cursor position). Cases 3 and 4 confirmed by direct user observation per the working file's own evidence design (no artifact for pure UI-state cases).

title: Five-minute prompt watchdog kills active Codex turns
description:
A hard five-minute deadline kills active Codex turns even when the Agent completed a tool immediately before expiry. This destroys the Session and prevents the turn from returning its result; the working-tree edits survive, but the active conversation is lost. Regressed by commit `27cba00261a1bb93d0ace51cfac3b299a606b65c` while fixing `louiselm-5zhl`.

## Observed

Observed 2026-08-30 in Codex ACP Session `01a053b9-dd10-7b90-91c3-4dd6e42e5d5a`. Primary evidence: `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a053b9-dd10-7b90-91c3-4dd6e42e5d5a/log.jsonl`.

- Line 2387: `2026-08-30T17:51:23.063Z` client sends `session/prompt` id `28`.
- Lines 3007-3008: `2026-08-30T17:56:21.942Z` Codex executes and completes tool `exec-8cc6a77c-9d77-4c32-9cc6-6b543d12e1bb` (`git status` plus source inspection).
- Line 3009: `2026-08-30T17:56:21.962Z` Codex emits `usage_update`.
- Line 3011: `2026-08-30T17:56:23.069Z` the ACP process exits with code `137`, 300.006 seconds after prompt submission and 1.107 seconds after the last completed tool.
- No JSON-RPC response for prompt id `28` appears before LouiseLM reports `ACP session/prompt did not complete within 300000ms`.

## Symptoms

- The user sees `Error: ACP session/prompt did not complete within 300000ms` during productive work.
- A tool completed immediately before the error, but that progress does not extend the timeout.
- LouiseLM transitions the Session to error and closes the ACP client, leaving the turn without a final response.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:92` defines `DEFAULT_PROMPT_TIMEOUT_MS = 300000`. `schedule_prompt_timeout` at lines 244-251 captures the turn and schedules one callback. `Session:prompt` calls it once at line 842. Session updates and completed tools never reschedule it. Therefore the watchdog is an absolute maximum turn duration, not an inactivity timeout. At expiry, `fail` closes the client at lines 206-225 even when meaningful progress arrived one second earlier.

Commit `27cba002` intentionally added this behavior to bound a stuck OpenCode prompt, but the test only models a prompt that receives no terminal response and invokes the one scheduled callback. It does not model a valid turn lasting over five minutes while continuing to make progress.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/session/api_spec.lua` covers a prompt with no terminal response and asserts failure at 300000ms. It does not cover meaningful Agent output or completed tools near the deadline, nor a legitimate Codex turn longer than five minutes. The original `louiselm-5zhl` trace also streamed updates while unresolved, so update presence alone cannot distinguish productive work from the original peer defect.

## Fix direction

Correct the liveness policy at the shared Session lifecycle boundary. Recent meaningful progress such as tool execution/completion must prevent an immediate inactivity failure, while a peer that endlessly emits non-progress updates must remain bounded. If a separate absolute maximum turn duration is required, give it a distinct contract and a substantially longer limit rather than presenting it as a hung-prompt timeout. Do not reset blindly on every ACP update because the `louiselm-5zhl` failure streamed thousands of updates without resolving.

## Acceptance

- A regression fixture derived from Session `01a053b9-dd10-7b90-91c3-4dd6e42e5d5a` fails before the fix and passes after it.
- Completing tool activity immediately before five minutes keeps the active turn alive for the declared inactivity window.
- A healthy Codex turn may run longer than five minutes while making meaningful progress and still return its terminal `session/prompt` response.
- The genuinely unresolved OpenCode case from `louiselm-5zhl` remains bounded even if it streams non-progress updates.
- Timeout failure still emits one typed error, calls the prompt callback at most once, closes resources, and ignores stale timers.

## Not covered

- The exact threshold for any separate absolute maximum turn duration.
- Provider-side propagation of the OpenCode Go quota error from `louiselm-5zhl`.
- Recovery or automatic continuation of the already terminated Codex Session.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree: progress renews the prompt inactivity window at lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:244. Regression: tests/session/api_spec.lua:2093. Gates: MiniTest 796/796, StyLua, lua-language-server, API appendix.

comments.author: codex/01a053d7-4308-76c0-9eac-a9e424812c48
comments.text: Fix evidence: lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:244 now treats the 300000ms watchdog as inactivity. Agent message/thought and tool updates increment one prompt-owned progress generation; at expiry, changed progress schedules one fresh window instead of failing, avoiding one timer per streamed chunk. tests/session/api_spec.lua:2093 replays captured tool exec-8cc6a77c-d5dc-412b-95cc-398955dcb149 completion, fires the original deadline, then proves the prompt returns normally and the renewed timer is stale. Silent prompts still fail once with the revised no-progress error. Gates: focused session spec 60/60; full MiniTest 796/796; StyLua; lua-language-server zero diagnostics; generated API check. Lesson stays issue-local; AGENTS.md already requires lifecycle bounds, captured ordering, TDD, and generated docs.

comments.text: Correction: the captured completed tool id is exec-8cc6a77c-9d77-4c32-9cc6-6b543d12e1bb, matching the issue evidence and tests/session/api_spec.lua:2108.

title: Invoke native skills through advertised ACP commands
description:
## Goal

Make the local skill picker invoke adapter-native skills exactly once through current ACP command advertisement.

## Scope

- In scope: handle `available_commands_update` per session; every valid update replaces the cache, an empty update clears it, malformed entries are skipped and diagnosed, and duplicate entries remain visible to ambiguity detection.
- In scope: correlate only locally discovered configured skills. Prefer exact `$<skill-name>`; otherwise allow exact `<skill-name>` only when the whitespace-normalized advertised description matches the local SKILL.md description or OpenAI short description.
- In scope: make `$name` win over a colliding built-in `name`; reject ambiguous matches.
- In scope: keep picker selections pending when no command update exists, without guesses or timeouts; re-resolve against the latest cache at actual submission and queued-prompt release.
- In scope: if a command disappears or becomes ambiguous, send nothing and preserve the user's prompt and skill chip with an actionable error.
- In scope: send the advertised command and task as one first text block, such as `/$grill-me stress-test this` for Codex or `/grill-me stress-test this` for Claude.
- In scope: send no LouiseLM catalog or skill body in native mode and leave user-authored slash commands untouched.
- Out of scope: a general ACP command browser, adapter-name heuristics, and injected discovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Command state always reflects the latest valid update and recovers on later updates.
2. Malformed entries do not preserve a stale previous command list.
3. Codex-style dollar commands and Claude-style exact commands resolve using the strict agreed rules.
4. A built-in `plan` cannot steal a local `plan` skill when `$plan` is advertised.
5. Duplicate or weak description-only matches never trigger a command.
6. Picker activation before advertisement waits safely and is late-bound at submission.
7. Disappearing/ambiguous commands preserve unsent user input.
8. Mock ACP tests cover replacement, empty/malformed updates, duplicates, collisions, pending selection, queued release, command formatting, manual slash passthrough, and no-double-send behavior.

## Testing

Drive session command updates and captured prompt blocks through the mock ACP agent. Installed Codex/Claude adapters are manual smoke tests, not authenticated CI dependencies.
close_reason: Implemented native command invocation with full test coverage across session state, skill correlation, picker/submit wiring, and mock ACP integration. All 8 acceptance criteria met; full suite green (286 cases), stylua/lua-language-server clean.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Implemented in four layers, all TDD with mini.test:

1. Session state (lua/louiselm/session/{lifecycle,validation,events}.lua): new available_commands_update notification branch. Validation.available_commands() always replaces the cache (nil/malformed top-level -> empty, never a hard fail like config_option_update), skips malformed individual entries with a diagnostic message, and preserves duplicates for ambiguity detection downstream. New commands_changed event.

2. Correlation module (lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua, wired via skills/init.lua as Skills.resolve_command): unique $name (Codex) always wins and is never even compared against a colliding bare name (AC4's built-in-plan protection). Bare name (Claude) only resolves when its advertised description matches the local SKILL.md description or the new short_description field (lua/louiselm/skills/metadata.lua, sourced from metadata.short-description). Any name with >1 advertised entry (dollar or bare) is ambiguous and never resolves; duplicates are not collapsed first.

3. Picker + submit wiring (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua): native picks now set view.pending_skill instead of queuing resolved content immediately. build_content() (replacing prompt_content()) resolves the pending skill against the session's *current* command cache only at actual dispatch time -- called from both submit_prompt (immediate) and release_queued_prompt (deferred) -- so both paths always see the freshest cache, never one snapshotted when the picker ran. Resolution failure (disappeared/ambiguous) notifies and returns without touching the buffer, contexts, or pending_skill, preserving the user's typed text and the visible skill chip. Successful native mode sends one merged text block, e.g. "/$grill-me stress-test this", never a separate catalog/skill-body block.

4. Mock ACP coverage: tests/session/api_spec.lua (wire-level replace/empty/malformed/duplicate), tests/skills_spec.lua (resolve_command correlation matrix), tests/ui/chat_spec.lua (full picker->submit->queue->release flow, manual slash passthrough, no-double-send), tests/mock/agent_spec.lua (real subprocess mock agent now supports LOUISELM_MOCK_AVAILABLE_COMMANDS, proving the notification survives an actual process boundary).

All 8 acceptance criteria covered. Full suite green (286 cases), stylua and lua-language-server clean on all touched files.

Refs claude/

title: Bind fixtures to observed wire behaviour, including event order
description:
Three defects across two manual QA rounds share one cause: a test fixture encoding what the ACP wire
was assumed to do, rather than what an observed log shows it does. Each passed a green suite and each
was caught only by a human driving a real Agent. The pattern is now frequent enough to bind future
work as a rule in AGENTS.md rather than being re-learned per incident.

## The three instances

- louiselm-4tum (round 2026-08-24). `tests/session/api_spec.lua` invented a snake_case ACP usage
  payload. Real Agents send camelCase, so validation silently produced an empty usage table and no
  telemetry was ever persisted.
- louiselm-zufj (round 2026-08-25). The regression drives the completed `task_complete` tool update
  and *then* `turn_done`. Copilot emits `task_complete` 2.1 seconds AFTER `end_turn`, so the flush
  point is never reached and the conclusion is never rendered.
- louiselm-cv9u (round 2026-08-25). `lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua:196` accepts array-shaped params
  for `session/list`, where every real Agent rejects them with `-32602 Invalid params`. The mock is
  strictly more permissive than any production peer, and the all-workspace path is the only caller
  that produces empty params, so it is exactly the case the mock cannot fail.

Two distinct sub-shapes are present, and a rule should name both:

1. Wrong field shape or naming, invented rather than captured (4tum, cv9u).
2. Wrong event ordering, assumed rather than observed (zufj).

The second is the harder one. A fixture can carry perfectly correct field names and still encode a
sequence no Agent produces.

## Why this is not solved by "write more tests"

All three had tests. All three tests passed. The defect was in the fixture's fidelity to the peer,
which no amount of additional coverage over the same fixture detects. Coverage percentage is
orthogonal.

## Proposed rule

Add to AGENTS.md, most naturally in section 5 near the existing "Keep tests deterministic" and "Live
acceptance" material:

- When a change depends on how a real ACP peer behaves, derive the fixture from a captured log frame
  rather than authoring it. Cite the log path and the session id in the test or its comment, so the
  next reader can tell a captured shape from an invented one.
- Fixtures must encode observed event ORDER, not only observed field shapes. If the ordering was not
  observed, say so in the test.
- The mock agent is a test double, not a specification. When it accepts something a real Agent
  rejects, that gap is itself a defect; tighten the mock rather than relying on it as evidence of
  protocol correctness.

The exact wording is the maintainer's call; the three instances above are the evidence for whatever
form it takes.

## Acceptance

- AGENTS.md carries a rule covering both invented field shapes and assumed event ordering.
- The rule names the mock agent's permissiveness as a defect class rather than an acceptable
  simplification.

## Not covered

- No audit was done of existing fixtures to find further instances. That is plausible follow-up work
  but was not attempted, so the true count may be higher than three.
close_reason: Added AGENTS.md guidance for captured ACP fixtures, observed event ordering, and mock-Agent permissiveness

comments.author: codex/01a037d9-bf57-7921-86bc-79ca8584c171
comments.text: Added the accepted AGENTS.md rule beside deterministic-test guidance: derive ACP fixtures from captured log frames with cited path and Session ID, encode observed event order, and treat mock-Agent permissiveness versus real-Agent rejection as a defect. No code or test changes were needed; git diff --check passed.

title: Investigate automated AGENTS.md reminders for LouiseLM workflow
description:
## Goal

Understand the idea in the supplied Doodlestein X post and decide whether LouiseLM should adapt it: https://x.com/doodlestein/status/2093542094023413828

## Source status

The supplied X status is currently inaccessible to the research tooling (HTTP 403), and its numeric id did not resolve in search. Search did find a likely related Doodlestein post: https://x.com/doodlestein/status/2025993246191558929, published 2026-02-23, describing an automated reminder to read AGENTS.md in Claude Code. Treat the second URL as a lead, not as proof that it is the same post; verify the source or ask the maintainer for a screenshot/content before making a product decision.

## Investigation questions

- What exactly is automated: a startup hook, per-turn reminder, context injection, or an external watcher?
- What failure does it address (agents forgetting repository instructions), and what evidence suggests the reminder saves time?
- Does repetition improve compliance enough to justify additional context/tokens and notification noise?
- How would it interact with LouiseLM's existing AGENTS.md contract, skill discovery, session lifecycle, typed events, and headless session API?
- Could the smallest useful adaptation be an explicit Session-start instruction or event rather than a new persistent file/hook?
- Which concerns belong in shared LouiseLM skills versus repository-local AGENTS.md, avoiding duplicated workflow policy?
- What observable acceptance test would prove the reminder helps without requiring a real external Agent or network?

## Candidate LouiseLM fits to evaluate

1. Session admission/start emits one typed reminder or instruction-read event when repository guidance is present.
2. The Agent receives a compact pointer to AGENTS.md and related local guidance, with the full file loaded only through the existing workflow.
3. A configurable, bounded reminder is used only after evidence of missing/ignored guidance, not on every turn.
4. No feature is added if the current session bootstrap already provides equivalent guidance; document that conclusion instead.

## Constraints

- Investigation/design only; do not implement until the source and desired behavior are confirmed.
- Preserve the existing rule that remote Markdown is not an implicit or higher-priority instruction source.
- Do not log prompts, tokens, or sensitive repository content.
- Any automatic Generator introduced by a design must have a literal bound and fit the Run budget model.

## Acceptance

- Source content is verified or explicitly marked unavailable, with the evidence recorded in this issue.
- A short recommendation identifies whether LouiseLM should adopt, adapt, or reject the idea.
- If adoption is recommended, define the narrowest boundary, user-visible behavior, typed event/API impact, token/noise tradeoff, and deterministic test shape.
- If the choice needs maintainer discussion, create or reuse a focused needs-design question rather than silently implementing it.

comments.author: codex/01a04c83-defb-7e52-93ac-42f3c8824836
comments.text:
## Verified source content (2026-08-29)

The supplied screenshot confirms the tweet is an “Agent Coding Pro Tip,” not primarily an AGENTS.md reminder. It recommends:

1. Read ALL `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` files carefully and understand them.
2. Use a code-investigation agent mode to understand the code and technical architecture/purpose.
3. Run `/profiling-software-performance`.
4. Run `/repeatedly-apply-skill` at least 30 times sequentially to apply `/extreme-software-optimization`.
5. Inspect generated benchmark artifacts and compare baseline vs optimized results.

The attached images show a concrete FrankenMarkdown result: a “Core Pipeline Architecture,” a sequential 30-pass optimization ledger, benchmark verification JSON, test/lint/format checks, and a baseline-vs-optimized table claiming large speedups. The visible process also has the agent finding/reading performance artifacts, explaining speedup drivers, and asking whether the speedups were achieved.

## LouiseLM adaptation hypothesis

The reusable idea is an evidence-producing optimization loop: understand -> profile -> make one bounded change -> verify -> compare against baseline -> explain results. LouiseLM already has relevant surfaces in its skills, typed workflow/session model, Run budgets, Forensics, Assessment, Validation, and Beads routing.

The dangerous part is the literal “30 times sequentially” instruction. Repeatedly applying a work-producing skill is an automatic Generator and must be bounded by a Run budget, with a stop condition based on measured improvement/regression rather than a blind pass count. A safe LouiseLM design should preserve baseline artifacts, require deterministic verification after each pass, reject unsupported claims, and stop on no material improvement, failed gates, budget exhaustion, or maintainer decision.

Potential narrow fit: add a documented/profiled optimization workflow skill or workflow definition that stages a codebase investigation, baseline capture, one optimization pass, verification, and bounded continuation. Do not add a generic repeat skill or automatically mutate code merely because a prompt requests many passes. The bead remains investigation/design-only until the maintainer confirms the desired scope.

title: Resolve static per-agent skill policies and migrate configuration
description:
## Goal

Make `native`, `inject`, and `off` explicit, session-static Agent Skills policies with a native default and no inferred fallback.

## Scope

- In scope: keep skill paths global; add global `skills.policy = "native"` and permit only a per-agent `skills.policy` override.
- In scope: validate policy values through the existing configuration schema and expose the effective policy to session setup, UI status, help, and health.
- In scope: snapshot policy at session creation; never infer it from adapter names, command advertisement, filesystem capabilities, or runtime failures.
- In scope: remove `full_content` with a targeted migration error and remove the dormant `native_supported` automatic-fallback API.
- In scope: `off` disables the local picker and all LouiseLM skill automation; `native` does not require `lyaml` to start but local picker/validation is unavailable without it; `inject` is blocked without it.
- In scope: preserve user-authored slash commands in every policy.
- Out of scope: catalog formatting, native command correlation, runtime profile switching, and per-agent path overrides.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An agent with no override uses `native`.
2. DeepSeek/GLM-style agents can opt into `inject` without affecting Codex/Claude sessions.
3. Unknown policy values and per-agent path overrides fail validation clearly.
4. Legacy `full_content` configuration fails with exact replacement guidance.
5. No runtime event changes an existing session's policy.
6. Missing `lyaml` has the agreed profile-specific effects.
7. UI status can show a simple `skills: on` state while technical policy remains available in help/health.
8. MiniTest covers defaults, overrides, invalid/legacy keys, session snapshotting, dependency gating, off behavior, and lack of fallback.

## Testing

Exercise the declarative schema and session-facing policy API. Do not add adapter-name heuristics to tests or production code.
close_reason: Implemented static native/inject/off per-agent skill policies, lyaml gating, UI/health visibility, migration errors, docs, and deterministic MiniTest coverage; all 147 tests, StyLua, and lua-language-server pass

title: Retarget Android capture safely and preserve queue ownership
description:
## Goal
Let a paired phone change a receiver endpoint without re-enrollment while ensuring queued recordings never cross receiver identities silently.

## Scope
- In scope: one active endpoint in v1; lightweight endpoint-update QR or equally small explicit update flow; proof of the already pinned receiver identity before saving an endpoint; preservation of device ID and credential; receiver ownership in durable capture metadata; first-pair assignment of unowned captures; confirmed migration on identity replacement; phone-side delivery health.
- Out of scope: multiple active endpoints, automatic LAN/overlay discovery, cloud relay, automatic queue reassignment, database/coroutine/Compose additions, and deletion of original recordings.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Updating an endpoint for the same pinned receiver identity preserves the device credential and all queued captures, and uploads continue at the new endpoint.
2. An endpoint is not saved until the contacted server proves the already pinned identity; malformed, unreachable, or mismatched updates leave the prior configuration intact.
3. Captures recorded before first pairing are durably unowned. The first pairing states the pending count, assigns them to that receiver, and queues upload.
4. Every assigned capture persists its receiver identity across app restart. Pairing a different identity neither uploads, deletes, nor reassigns those captures without an explicit confirmation showing the affected count.
5. Confirmed migration changes only receiver ownership and retry eligibility; immutable local audio and the capture UUID remain unchanged.
6. Phone status shows pending count and oldest age, last successful synchronization, current endpoint, latest actionable failure, and manual retry.
7. WorkManager remains the only background scheduler and retains bounded retry behavior without a permanent foreground service or wake lock.

## Testing
- Add pure store/protocol/state tests for first pairing, same-identity endpoint change, restart, mismatched identity, declined migration, confirmed migration, and retained originals.
- Use a deterministic HTTPS/test boundary; no real receiver, credential, camera, microphone, or network.
- Run Android unit tests, lint, and assembleDebug when the SDK is available.

## Notes
This task depends on the stable receiver identity and pairing protocol established by the private-profile foundation task.
close_reason: Implemented safe Android receiver retargeting and durable queue ownership

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Implemented identity-owned upload state, unowned first-pair assignment with an explicit count, same-identity health verification that preserves the credential, confirmed cross-identity migration that changes only mutable upload state, receiver-scoped WorkManager delivery, and phone delivery-health status. Pure transition/eligibility tests cover first/same/different identity behavior. Android ./gradlew test lint assembleDebug passed; physical restart/cancel/migration acceptance remains in dependent QA bead louiselm-1chb.

title: Grill-me needed: what documentation should louiselm.nvim provide, and how does Neovim's own diagnostics/LSP self-reflection factor in
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing -- it wants full attention.**

Raised as explicit "food for thought" on 2026-08-20, while closing out a QA
round for louiselm-2w4/louiselm-s88/louiselm-j8j. The user explicitly asked
that this be filed in beads rather than kept in an agent's private memory --
louiselm is meant to be cross-adapter, and a note only one adapter's memory
can see is exactly the kind of context AGENTS.md says does not belong there.

## The question

What documentation should louiselm.nvim actually provide, for humans and for
agents, and does Neovim's own self-reflective diagnostic/LSP surface factor
into how that documentation gets authored, validated, or consumed?

## Evidence from the session that raised it

Checked during the QA round: there is no `doc/louiselm.txt` at all -- only
README.md. The only vimdoc-adjacent code, `lua/louiselm/schema/gen_vimdoc.lua`,
generates config-schema field fragments (types, defaults) only; it produces
nothing for commands, workflows, or `:help` tag anchors. Nothing currently
generates or maintains a real `:help louiselm` experience.

## Threads worth pulling

- Human vs. agent audiences may want different artifacts, not one document
  wearing two hats: a real `:help louiselm.txt` (tag-jumping, `gq`-wrapped,
  kept in sync with commands/schema somehow) versus something built for
  agents to consume, closer to this project's own AGENTS.md pattern or an
  llms.txt-style reference. Decide whether that's one source, two
  generated outputs, or genuinely two hand-maintained documents.
- Neovim's own self-reflective capabilities -- `vim.diagnostic`, LSP client
  introspection, `:checkhealth` -- as a second, related thread: could/should
  louiselm's documentation lean on or expose these (e.g. health checks as
  living documentation, diagnostics as a way to validate config against docs,
  LSP-style hover/signature info for louiselm's own config schema)? Not
  pre-decided whether this belongs in the same artifact as the human/agent
  docs question above or is a separate concern entirely -- that's exactly
  what the grill should surface.
- `gen_vimdoc.lua` already exists and already generates *something* from the
  schema -- worth understanding its current scope and whether it's the
  right foundation to extend, versus a fresh mechanism.

## Out of scope for the grill

Re-deriving the above. React to it.
close_reason: Design confirmed: generated human Vimdoc and curated public LuaCATS API appendix, with AGENTS.md as sole AX contract.

comments.author: codex-2026-08-22-handoff-buffer
comments.text: Follow-up design idea: make beads inspectable from chat. When the cursor is on a rendered beads issue reference (for example louiselm-3od or louiselm-handoff-command-d15l), provide a chat action/command that runs br show for that issue and opens the structured result in an editable or read-only Neovim buffer. Grill whether this should support issue IDs in prose, links, and code blocks; how to avoid shell interpolation by using argument arrays; and whether the same surface should offer ready/dependency context or only br show. This could make beads a first-class documentation/workflow surface rather than a separate tracker.

comments.author: copilot/1b49919a-7bb3-4249-b781-f5e494348443
comments.text: Grill evidence: README.md is the only human-facing reference. Schema.generate_vimdoc() deterministically renders configuration fields in memory; no doc/louiselm.txt exists, no emitter or CI freshness check consumes its output, and it cannot describe commands/workflows. :checkhealth louiselm validates active configuration, Agent executables/versions, local skills, and capture tools; it is operational diagnostics, not a documentation source. This makes a composed help document (static command/workflow prose plus generated configuration reference) feasible, but requires an explicit source/emission/freshness decision.

comments.author: copilot/1b49919a-7bb3-4249-b781-f5e494348443
comments.text: Additional implementation constraint from Neovim 0.12 package docs: a plugin may commit generated doc/tags so :help works immediately after installation; otherwise the installer must run :helptags. LouiseLM currently has neither doc/ nor tags. Provisional v1 proposal, pending user confirmation: README owns orientation/installation; committed doc/louiselm.txt plus generated tags owns human command/config/troubleshooting reference; generated config content is checked for drift in CI; AGENTS.md remains the sole AX contract; :checkhealth and vim.diagnostic remain troubleshooting surfaces, not live documentation APIs.

comments.author: copilot/1b49919a-7bb3-4249-b781-f5e494348443
comments.text: Design confirmed by maintainer: documentation should be as automatic as feasible. Decision: README is concise orientation/install; committed doc/louiselm.txt plus generated doc/tags is the canonical human reference; CI rejects drift. Derive configuration from Config.schema and the command index from registered Neovim user-command metadata. Retain hand-authored prose only for semantics, workflows, and troubleshooting that metadata cannot express. Existing LuaCATS annotations do help: lua-language-server --doc produces Markdown/JSON from them, but whole-workspace output includes ACP, mock, and other internals. Therefore an API appendix must opt in only the established public boundaries: headless Session API, typed events, permission policies, and Agent configuration. Do not create a second public AX reference; AGENTS.md remains the AX contract. :checkhealth and vim.diagnostic remain operational troubleshooting surfaces, not live documentation APIs.

title: QA round: stale Beads claim reconciliation
description:
# Manual QA review — stale Beads claim reconciliation

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; it will become a QA-round bead and be removed when
the round closes.

**Build under test:** `999547b`. **Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: `louiselm-8elc` tightened the Agent workflow so claim age alone never
permits takeover. Only snapshot-backed `abandoned_likely` evidence with
`reclaim_allowed_by_policy=true` permits an audited maintainer requeue, followed
by a normal atomic Agent claim.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Missing coordination evidence stays protected | **passed** — `qa-in7` is `fresh`, reclaim is false, and no commands were emitted |
| 2 | Confirmed abandoned claim stays out of next-work views | **passed** — snapshot yields `abandoned_likely`; ready and scheduler exclude `qa-in7` |
| 3 | Requeue permits one new holder and rejects a competitor | **passed** — audit recorded; contender rejected; final owner is `codex/new-session` |

## Setup

From `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`, confirm the documentation commit and installed
CLI, then create a disposable Beads workspace:

```sh
git show -s --format='%h %s' HEAD
br version

qa_dir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/louiselm-8elc-qa.XXXXXX)
cd "$qa_dir"
br init --prefix qa --quiet
claimed_id=$(br create "Claim under test" --type task --actor codex/old-session --silent)
ready_id=$(br create "Ready control" --type task --actor maintainer/session --silent)
br update "$claimed_id" --claim --actor codex/old-session --json
printf 'QA_DIR=%s\nCLAIMED_ID=%s\nREADY_ID=%s\n' "$qa_dir" "$claimed_id" "$ready_id"
```

Expect the first command to print `999547b docs(agents): guard stale claim
takeover`. Keep this shell open: cases 1–3 share its `qa_dir`, `claimed_id`, and
`ready_id` variables and must run in order.

Setup verified 2026-08-30 at `/tmp/louiselm-8elc-qa.rUzPY9`: `qa-in7` is
`in_progress` under `codex/old-session`; `qa-1mk` is open and unassigned.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- These cases never mutate the real LouiseLM Beads database.
- Case 2 deliberately ages the disposable SQLite row. Every later `br` command
  uses `--no-auto-import`, or the newer generated JSONL can restore the row and
  invalidate the fixture.
- An empty reservation snapshot is affirmative snapshot evidence that no
  matching reservation exists. Omitting the snapshot is materially different.

## Cases

### 1. Missing coordination evidence stays protected

Exercises `999547b` / `AGENTS.md:64`.

Steps:

```sh
br coordination status --json |
  jq --arg id "$claimed_id" '.claims[] | select(.issue.id == $id) |
    {classification:.assessment.classification,
     reclaim_allowed_by_policy,
     suggested_commands}'
```

Expect:

```text
classification: fresh
reclaim_allowed_by_policy: false
suggested_commands: []
```

The fresh classification is expected because the disposable claim is new. The
important result is that missing snapshot evidence supplies no reclaim command.

Failure signature: `reclaim_allowed_by_policy` is true or any suggested command
is emitted without a reservation snapshot.

### 2. Confirmed abandoned claim stays out of next-work views

Exercises `999547b` / `AGENTS.md:64` and the existing `br coordination status`,
`br ready`, and `br scheduler` behavior.

Steps:

```sh
sqlite3 .beads/beads.db \
  "UPDATE issues SET updated_at='2020-01-01T00:00:00Z' WHERE id='$claimed_id';"
printf '[]\n' > reservations.json

br coordination status --no-auto-import --reservations "$qa_dir/reservations.json" --json |
  jq --arg id "$claimed_id" '.claims[] | select(.issue.id == $id) |
    {classification:.assessment.classification,
     reclaim_allowed_by_policy,
     commands:[.suggested_commands[].purpose]}'

br ready --no-auto-import --json |
  jq --arg claimed "$claimed_id" --arg ready "$ready_id" \
    '{claimed_visible:any(.[]; .id == $claimed),
      ready_visible:any(.[]; .id == $ready)}'

br scheduler --no-auto-import --json |
  jq --arg claimed "$claimed_id" --arg ready "$ready_id" \
    '{claimed_visible:any(.recommendations[]; .issue.id == $claimed),
      ready_visible:any(.recommendations[]; .issue.id == $ready)}'
```

Expect the coordination result to show `abandoned_likely`, `true`, and the two
purposes `add_reclaim_audit_comment` and `claim_issue`. Both next-work results
must show `claimed_visible: false` and `ready_visible: true`.

Failure signature: the claim is reclaimable without the empty snapshot, remains
protected with the snapshot, or appears in either next-work view while assigned.

### 3. Requeue permits one new holder and rejects a competitor

Exercises the operator sequence documented by `999547b` / `AGENTS.md:72`.

Steps:

```sh
br comments add "$claimed_id" \
  --message "QA: abandoned_likely with empty reservation snapshot; operator confirms disposable fixture" \
  --actor maintainer/session --no-auto-import --json

br update "$claimed_id" --status open --assignee "" \
  --actor maintainer/session --no-auto-import --json

br update "$claimed_id" --claim --actor codex/new-session \
  --no-auto-import --json

if br update "$claimed_id" --claim --actor codex/contender \
  --no-auto-import --json; then
  echo 'FAIL: competing claim succeeded'
else
  echo 'PASS: competing claim refused'
fi

br show "$claimed_id" --no-auto-import --json |
  jq '.[0] | {id,status,assignee}'
```

Expect the requeue result to be `open` with no assignee, the next claim to be
`in_progress` with `codex/new-session`, the contender to receive

title: Render submitted prompt contexts as native Neovim folds
description:
## Goal

Keep pre-send chat uncluttered while making every LouiseLM-attached prompt context exactly inspectable after submission.

## Scope

- In scope: before submission, represent manually selected skills and other contexts as compact chips; never display the automatic injected catalog as editable text or a marker.
- In scope: after an accepted prompt, render one closed native Neovim fold for that user turn containing every attached context in exact transport order and exact sent content.
- In scope: include concise context labels in the fold summary and preserve the ordinary visible user prompt.
- In scope: use normal Neovim fold commands and the existing chat buffer/context model; the fold is transcript representation only and must never be resent.
- In scope: retain chips and editable prompt on local send failure or blocked skill read.
- In scope: limit behavior to the live nofile, swap-disabled chat buffer; do not reconstruct folds after session load or Neovim restart.
- Out of scope: tool-call folding, transcript persistence, summary-only context storage, custom fold widgets, and a generic fold framework.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A pending automatic catalog produces no visible `[context: skill-index]` line.
2. One submitted turn with several contexts produces one closed fold with exact ordered contents.
3. Opening the fold reveals what ACP received, not a lossy summary.
4. The visible user prompt remains distinct from its attached context.
5. Failed local submissions keep pre-send chips and do not create a misleading submitted fold.
6. Reopening or closing folds cannot affect future prompt payloads.
7. MiniTest/headless UI tests cover fold boundaries, summary labels, exact contents/order, failure retention, and no resend.

## Testing

Use native fold APIs in a headless chat buffer and assert both buffer lines/fold ranges and captured ACP payloads.

## Notes

The current buffer is intentionally ephemeral and memory-resident. Documentation must explain that inspectability lasts only for the live chat.
close_reason: Completed live native context folds with exact ordered contents, failure retention, hidden-buffer scheduling coverage, and no-resend tests

comments.text:
Implementation decisions, for .2/.3/.5 to build on.

Contract lives in lua/louiselm/workflow/phase.lua as a pure module: no UI, no process launch, no require-time side effects, so it stays independent of the estimator process boundary the grill left open.

A skill record now carries an optional resolved phase. When the first real workflow lands in .5, resolve through the same Phase.resolve rather than growing a second path.

Inference is hyphen-segment matching against the canonical names only. Rejected: a lookup table mapping the maintainer's own skill names (grill-me -> design, to-beads -> planning). That would bake one person's skill vocabulary into the plugin and contradicts the grill's decision that profiles express traits, not named things. A name that names no phase yields nil, so routing declines rather than guesses.

Confidence: explicit metadata is 1.0 (the author stated it). Inference is capped at 0.5 and scaled by the share of name segments that are phase vocabulary, so qa-review scores 0.5 and security-review scores 0.25. The cap and the scaling are judgement calls, documented at the constants; .2 consumes confidence for ranking and may want to revisit the numbers against real candidates.

A declared phase outside the canonical list rejects the whole skill, matching how metadata.lua already treats malformed optional frontmatter (license, compatibility, metadata). Chosen over a warning because a phase with no built-in profile would rank candidates against nothing.

title: Build ACP candidate inventory and ranking
description: Implement a pure ranking boundary that consumes configured Agents, advertised Models/options, ACP telemetry, phase profiles, current choice, and local evidence. comments.author: claude/55265ffa-7ddf-4cf2-970e-a6b8ce6c12df
comments.text:
Implementation decisions and the contracts .3/.4/.5 must match.

Module: lua/louiselm/workflow/routing.lua, public surface M.rank(request) -> Ranking?, error_message? and M.profile(phase) -> profile?. Purity is provable by inspection: the file never references `vim` at all, and requires only workflow/phase. A test asserts it does not mutate the caller's request.

TRAIT VOCABULARY -- the load-bearing contract for .5's documentation. Traits are matched against the `capabilities` string tags a user already sets per agent in `agents.<name>.capabilities` (config.lua, surfaced today only by :checkhealth, README:571). No new config surface was added; the existing tag channel was given meaning. Built-in profiles:

  design         prefers reasoning  min_headroom 0.5
  planning       prefers reasoning  min_headroom 0.4
  implementation prefers coding     min_headroom 0.3
  review         prefers reasoning, coding  min_headroom 0.3
  qa             prefers coding     min_headroom 0.2
  mechanical     prefers speed      min_headroom 0.1

So the canonical trait names a user is expected to tag with are reasoning, coding, and speed. Any other string still matches if a profile or an explicit constraint names it.

Secondary phases contribute their profile's traits at half weight and raise min_headroom to the maximum across phases, so qa+review demands review's stricter headroom.

Scoring: score = 0.4*trait_match + 0.4*evidence + 0.2*headroom - penalty, penalty 0 for continue, 0.05 for a model change, 0.15 for a handoff. Every number is a named constant with the reasoning at its definition. Unmeasured components contribute a neutral 0.5 rather than rejecting or recommending.

Confidence is separate from score: phase.confidence * mean(trait, evidence, context component confidence), each component 1 when backed and 0.5 when not. Evidence confidence is min(1, samples/5), multiplied by 0.75 when the record is a global fallback rather than phase-specific. This is where .1's inferred-phase confidence flows through -- an inferred phase lowers every candidate's confidence.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT for .4. rank() consumes a flat array of records, it does not own or read a store:
  { phase?: string, agent: string, model?: string, samples: integer, reliability: number, quality?: number }
A record with no phase is the global fallback. Lookup prefers an exact phase match, falls back to global, and lowers confidence when it does. quality, when present, is averaged with reliability.

Determinism: candidates sort by score desc, then agent name, then model. (agent, model) uniquely determines the action, so no action tie-break is needed. Near misses sort by agent then model. Both orderings are independent of the order agents are supplied in, and both are tested.

Hard filters, all fail-closed, all reported together rather than first-only: agent unavailable, handoff not allowed, missing a required trait, insufficient context headroom. When every candidate fails, candidates is empty and rejected carries the near misses with their reasons.

NOT BUILT here, deliberately: no evidence store (.4), no approval or suppression lifecycle (.3), no config surface, no UI, no documentation of built-in profiles (.5).

FINDING that raises .4's importance -- see the comment filed on louiselm-3s0l.4. ACP advertises no per-model metadata beyond value/name/description (session/validation.lua:1-4 drops everything else), so with no evidence every model within one agent scores identically and only the switching penalty separates them. Until evidence accumulates, routing can only ever recommend CONTINUE within an agent. Evidence is therefore the only thing that makes model-level routing work at all, not an enhancement to it.

Gates: stylua clean, lua-language-server clean, 412 mini.test cases pass. Note tests/mock/agent_spec.lua is independently flaky (louiselm-tum5), pre-existing and unrelated.

comments.text:
Finding from louiselm-3s0l.2 that changes what this issue is worth.

ACP advertises no per-model metadata beyond value, name, and description -- `parse_values` at lua/louiselm/session/validation.lua:100-114 drops every other field, and there is no context-window size, price, provider, or capability flag anywhere in the wire types. The consequence for ranking: with no evidence, every model within one agent produces an identical score, and only the switching penalty separates them. The ranking boundary can therefore only ever recommend CONTINUE inside an agent until evidence exists. Cross-agent handoffs still differentiate, because agents carry capability tags, but the model-change half of the feature is inert without this issue.

So local evidence is not an accuracy improvement layered on a working ranker -- it is the only signal that makes model-level routing function at all. Worth weighing when this is scheduled against .3.

The consumption contract rank() already expects (it owns no store, it takes a flat array):
  { phase?: string, agent: string, model?: string, samples: integer, reliability: number, quality?: number }
A record with no phase is the global fallback; phase-specific is preferred and a global fallback lowers confidence by a factor of 0.75. Confidence from sample size is min(1, samples/5). See the comment on louiselm-3s0l.2 for the full scoring model.

title: Routing decisions cannot be rejected or rated from Chat
description:
Phase-aware routing presents approval choices after a tagged turn, but users cannot reject a recommendation, reconsider suppressed choices, invalidate changed routing context, or submit phase-end feedback through Chat. The parent acceptance therefore remains unmet despite its implementation children being closed.

## Observed

Audited on 2026-08-23 in /home/lotso/code/louiselm at d0830f3.

`rg -n "workflow:feedback|workflow:reject|workflow:invalidate|reconsider" lua tests` finds production definitions in lua/louiselm/workflow/init.lua but no production callers. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1568-1593 maps every selected recommendation directly to `approve`; cancelling only calls `clear_pending`. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1779-1791 records the operational outcome and immediately opens recommendations without asking for feedback. tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:822-895 covers only approving CONTINUE.

## Symptoms

- The recommendation picker offers no rejection action, so the promised suppression lifecycle cannot be reached from the Chat UI.
- Good, Skip, and Poor phase-end feedback cannot be submitted, so qualitative evidence never accumulates in normal use.
- Model and Handoff execution, suppression, and persistence are not covered at the integrated Chat boundary required by louiselm-3s0l.

## Root cause

The pure coordinator modules implement feedback and rejection, but the integration in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua wires only observe, recommend, approve, and clear_pending. The integration test uses a synchronous fake and selects only CONTINUE.

## Why it was not caught

Focused module tests prove the internal state machines independently, while the sole Chat workflow test proves only the happy-path CONTINUE branch. No test exercises feedback, rejection, Model change, Handoff, or persisted evidence through the integrated boundary.

## Fix direction

Keep the pure modules. Add the smallest native Chat interaction that exposes one-click Good/Skip feedback, Poor feedback with required context, and approve/reject handling for a selected recommendation. Add integrated tests for feedback, suppression, Model change, Handoff, and persistent evidence. Do not add configuration or a second routing abstraction.

## Acceptance

- A Chat regression test fails before the fix because no feedback UI is presented and passes after Good/Skip/Poor reach the coordinator.
- A Chat regression test fails before the fix because a selected recommendation cannot be rejected and passes after rejection suppresses it.
- Integrated tests cover CONTINUE, Model change, Handoff creation with the source Session retained, and evidence persistence.
- Full MiniTest, StyLua, and lua-language-server gates pass.

## Not covered

Editable profiles, evidence export/sharing, enterprise policy, and the still-open estimator process boundary remain outside louiselm-3s0l.
close_reason: Fixed the incomplete Chat boundary: Good/Skip/Poor feedback persists, selected recommendations require explicit Approve/Reject, and rejection reaches phase suppression. Regression evidence: feedback and rejection tests failed before the fix; integrated tests now cover CONTINUE, Model change, Handoff with source retention, persistence reload, and late callbacks after disposal. Gates: 465 MiniTest cases, stylua --check ., and lua-language-server Warning check pass.

title: Grill-me needed: should louiselm track session-option changes (model/thinking-mode switches) as a usage/analytics feature?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing.

Question: should louiselm register session option changes (model switch, thinking-mode switch, and other per-session option changes) as first-class events, so they can later be analyzed for what they reveal about user intent/expectation — and should there be a skill that reviews past sessions and reports patterns in when/why options were switched?

Context / evidence that raised it:
Benoit's observation: changing a session option mid-session (reaching for a better model, or a stronger thinking mode) is itself a signal — it means the human felt the current option was insufficient for what they were about to ask. That signal is currently invisible: it isn't logged anywhere, so there's no way to later ask 'when did I upgrade model/thinking, and was it actually warranted' or spot patterns (e.g. always bumping to max thinking for a specific kind of task, or bumping late instead of starting there).

Proposed shape (not settled, for the grill to interrogate):
- Registering: capture option-change events (what changed, from/to, session id, timestamp, and ideally the triggering prompt/turn) as part of louiselm's session data, not bolted on separately.
- Analyzing: a skill that scans past sessions, finds option-change events, and surfaces what could be learned — e.g. correlating the change with the task that followed, flagging cases where the change seems to correlate with the option being wrong from the start.

Threads worth pulling:
- Where do these events live — new event type on the existing session/event log, or a separate usage store? Loading-bearing given louiselm already has a session API and typed events (see AGENTS.md section 8).
- Is 'usefulness' of an option change measurable at all without human labeling, or does this become a skill that surfaces candidates for the human to judge rather than an automated verdict?
- Scope: model switches and thinking-mode switches are the named examples — does this extend to other session options (permission mode, etc.), and where's the line?
- Relationship to existing skills (qa-review, grill-me, to-beads loop) — is this a new skill, or an extension of an existing analysis skill?
- Privacy/what's captured: prompts and payloads are already off-limits for logging by default (AGENTS.md section 11) — does correlating the change with 'what prompt triggered it' conflict with that, and if so what's the non-sensitive proxy?

title: QA round: <leader>lB cursor detection (local exact, bare-suffix, cross-workspace)
description:
# Manual QA review — `<leader>lB` / `:LouiselmInspectBead` cursor detection

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `23cfdb7` (sibling sweep), `7d59a1e` (bare-suffix),
`729c3f2` (prefix-scoped matching, closed as `louiselm-04cy`). Confirmed via
`$NVIM` RPC: your current Neovim process (pid 48900, started 12:14:18) started
*after* all three commits, and the installed plugin checkout at
`~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim` is at `23cfdb7`,
matching the repo. No restart needed to start this round — Case 6 below will
need one later, noted there.

Origin: `louiselm-r98e` extended `<leader>lB`'s cursor-based Beads ID
detection from one case (full local-prefix ID) to three (full local-prefix,
bare local suffix, cross-workspace foreign ID). All three are covered by fake
`br`-invocation unit tests in `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` and
`tests/schema/setup_spec.lua` (all passing). This round exists to catch what
those fakes cannot: the real `br` binary's actual JSON shape, real floating
window/popup rendering and focus, real `nvim.fn.glob`/`nvim.fn.expand`
filesystem behavior, and real config wiring through your actual
`require("louiselm").setup(...)` call — the same category of gap that made
`louiselm-04cy` a live-acceptance issue earlier today.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Local exact-match ID survives ordinary hyphenated prose | **passed** — popup title `:LouiselmPark ...`, `ID: louiselm-gc0z`; confirmed via RPC: floating win, `buf=louiselm://beads/louiselm-gc0z` |
| 2 | Bare local suffix — hit and miss | **passed** — hit confirmed via RPC (`buf=louiselm://beads/louiselm-gc0z`); miss showed the `louiselm Beads issue id: ` prompt, not a popup (disambiguated after initial confusing report) |
| 3 | Ambiguous multi-ID line still prompts | **passed** — `louiselm Beads issue id: ` prompt shown, confirmed no floating window opened (RPC) |
| 4 | Manual prompt sanity (bare-id prepend, `q`/`<Esc>` close) | **passed** — prepend and `q` close both confirmed via RPC |
| 5 | Cross-workspace ID, `sibling_roots` unset (default off) | superseded — `dotfiles-5wa` was already applied and committed (`beb13e7`, 12:12:21) before this round; default-off state no longer live-testable without reverting config + restarting, remains covered by the automated unit test only |
| 6 | Cross-workspace ID, `sibling_roots` configured (default on) | **passed** — same `daa-4hf` popup from the "Case 5" attempt: `ID: daa-4hf`, "acp-debug.sh logs full LLM request bodies by default", closed, priority 1, security — matches the real `acp-llm-adapter` issue exactly, confirmed via RPC (`buf=louiselm://beads/daa-4hf`) and direct popup content read |

## Setup

Nothing to rebuild — the running instance already matches source (see above).
Every case below happens **inside the live louiselm chat buffer**
(`louiselm://session-N`), because `LouiselmInspectBead` only acts when the
current buffer is the chat buffer that owns the session
(`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua`'s `inspect_bead()` checks this and
reports `"no chat session is open"` otherwise).

To stage a test line without sending it as a chat message: on the compose
line, type the line, then press `<Esc>` (do **not** press `<CR>` — that
submits it to the agent). Then move the cursor onto the token named in the
case and press `<leader>lB`.

After each case, tell me what you saw (popup opened with which issue, or the
`Beads issue id:` prompt appeared) — I'll pull the actual window/buffer state
over `$NVIM` RPC myself before we call it passed.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- If a case behaves like the *pre-fix* code (prompts when it should open
  directly, or vice versa), suspect a stale in-memory Lua module before
  suspecting the fix — restart Neovim and `:LouiselmResume` before filing
  anything (this exact failure mode already happened once today on
  `louiselm-04cy`).
- `<leader>lB` does nothing useful outside the live chat buffer — don't test
  from a scratch buffer.
- Staging a test line and actually submitting it are easy to conflate: the
  first Case 1 attempt pasted the line and it went out as a real chat
  message (visible as a `>`-prefixed line followed by the agent's own
  response). The agent then investigated the mentioned issue ID through its
  *own* `br` tool calls — which can look like a pass, but exercises nothing
  in `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`. After typing/pasting, press `<Esc>` as its
  own keypress and confirm nothing got sent (no new response starts) before
  moving the cursor and pressing `<leader>lB`.
- `$NVIM` in a shell only points at the Neovim instance that spawned that
  shell. Two chat sessions in two separate Neovim processes have two
  different `$NVIM` values — check `echo $NVIM` in the terminal you're
  actually testing from, don't assume it matches a value seen earlier in a
  different session.

## Cases

### 1. Local exact-match ID survives ordinary hyphenated prose

Exercises the `louiselm-04cy` fix (`729c3f2`) end-to-end against the real
`br` binary — the unit test uses a fake process, this uses yours.

Steps:

> `still open is louiselm-gc0z, the same time-travel vocabulary-drop bug`

Cursor on `louiselm-gc0z`, press `<leader>lB`.

Expect: `louiselm-gc0z`'s issue popup opens directly (title
":LouiselmPark command: lazy Run attach..."). No prompt.

Failure signature: the `Beads issue id:` prompt appears instead of opening
directly (would mean the ambiguity-inflation bug is back).

### 2. Bare local suffix — hit and miss

Exercises `louiselm-xyg8` (`7d59a1e`) — a token with no `louiselm-` prefix at
all.

> `check gc0z when you get a chance`

Steps (miss):

cancel it once confirmed).

Failure signature (hit): prompt appears instead of opening. Failure signature
(miss): an error notification appears instead of the prompt, or nothing
happens at all.

### 3. Ambiguous multi-ID line still prompts

Guards that bare-suffix/sibling-sweep additions didn't erode the existing
ambiguity safety net (already covered by a fake-`br` unit test — this just

### 4. Manual prompt sanity

Confirms the pre-existing manual-entry path (`louiselm-y8y1`'s bare-id
prepend, and the popup's `q`/`<Esc>` close keymaps) still works after
`command.lua`'s `inspect_bead()` gained the new `sibling_roots` parameter.

Steps:

> `no issue reference on this line`

Cursor anywhere on that line, press `<leader>lB`. At the `louiselm Beads
issue id:` prompt, type `gc0z` (no prefix) and press `<CR>`.

Expect: `louiselm-gc0z` opens (prefix auto-prepended). Then press `q` in the
popup.

Expect: popup closes, focus returns to the chat buffer's compose line.

Failure signature: prepend doesn't happen (prompt rejects `gc0z` or looks up
literally `gc0z`), or `q`/`<Esc>` fails to close the popup.

### 5. Cross-workspace ID, `sibling_roots` unset (default off)

Exercises `louiselm-gm8t` (`23cfdb7`) with the option in its **default**
(unset) state — confirms the feature is truly opt-in before you touch
`dotfiles-5wa`.

Steps:

> `the acp-llm-adapter fix was daa-4hf, worth checking`

(`daa-4hf` is a real, closed issue in `~/code/acp-llm-adapter`'s own Beads
workspace — picked because it actually exists, not a placeholder.)

Cursor on `daa-4hf`, press `<leader>lB`.

Expect: falls to the `louiselm Beads issue id:` prompt (no sibling sweep
happens at all, since `beads.sibling_roots` isn't configured yet). Press
`<Esc>` to cancel.

Failure signature: `daa-4hf` opens directly (would mean sweeping happens even
when unconfigured — a real bug, since the design is opt-in).

### 6. Cross-workspace ID, `sibling_roots` configured (default on)

Same line as Case 5, after actually turning the feature on.

Prerequisite: apply `dotfiles-5wa` — add `beads = { sibling_roots = { "~/code"
} }` to the `config` table in
`~/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua` — then
**restart Neovim** (same stale-module reason as the ground rule above) and
`:LouiselmResume` back into this session.

Steps: same line as Case 5 —

> `the acp-llm-adapter fix was daa-4hf, worth checking`

Cursor on `daa-4hf`, press `<leader>lB`.

Expect: `daa-4hf`'s issue popup opens directly (title "acp-debug.sh logs full
LLM request bodies by default"), proving the real glob of `~/code/*/.beads/beads.db`
found `~/code/acp-llm-adapter` and `br --db <that path> show daa-4hf` hit.

Failure signature: prompt appears instead (glob/config wiring broken), or an
error notification appears (e.g. `could not start br`, malformed data).

## Evidence check

After you report what you saw for a case, I'll independently confirm via
`$NVIM` RPC before marking it passed:

```
nvim --server "$NVIM" --remote-expr 'json_encode({"wins": map(nvim_list_wins(), {_, w -> {"buf": bufname(nvim_win_get_buf(w)), "relative": nvim_win_get_config(w).relative}}), "curbuf": bufname("%")})'
```

A passed "opens directly" case shows one window with `relative: "editor"` and
`buf` matching `louiselm://beads/<expected-id>` at the moment it's open (ask
you to run this and report back before closing the popup, for the first case
at least, to validate the check itself). This can't observe the `Beads issue
id:` prompt state (it's cmdline-based, not a window) — those cases rest on
your report of the exact prompt text and its outcome.

## Cleanup when the round closes

No fixtures created — every test line lives only in an unsent chat compose
buffer and is discarded. If Case 6 requires the `dotfiles-5wa` config change,
that stays applied (it's the point of filing it) unless you want it reverted.

## Reporting back

Send me the case number and what you saw. I pull the evidence myself before
confirming pass/fail.

## Findings this round

None. All three new cursor-detection cases (local exact-match, local
bare-suffix, cross-workspace sibling sweep) work correctly against the real
`br` binary, real popup UI, and real config wiring -- Cases 1-4 and 6 passed
with RPC-confirmed evidence; Case 5 (default-off) was superseded because
`dotfiles-5wa` was already applied and committed before this round started,
so the off-state is only verified by the automated unit test now, not live.

Process note, not a product finding: Case 1's first attempt looked like a
pass but wasn't -- pasting the test line into the chat compose area and
pressing Enter submitted it as a real message instead of staging it, so the
agent investigated the issue through its own `br` tool calls rather than
exercising `<leader>lB` at all. Caught by insisting on RPC evidence
(`relative: "editor"` window with the right `buf` name) instead of trusting
"it seem to work" at face value. Retested correctly afterward.

Why the automated suite couldn't have caught anything here: it fakes every
`br` invocation and stubs `vim.ui.input`/`nvim.fn.glob`, so it proves the
*decision logic* is correct but cannot prove the real `br show --json` output
shape still decodes, that the floating window actually renders and takes
focus, or that `beads.sibling_roots` threads correctly from a real
`setup()` call through to a real filesystem glob. This round proved all of
that, live.
