title: Show commit Provenance in a louiselm://provenance/commit buffer
description:
## Goal

Standing on a commit SHA, open `louiselm://provenance/commit/<sha>` and see the
issues it served and the Session that produced it, with a resolved transcript
path.

## Scope

- In scope: `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua`; a read-only buffer; cursor
  detection extended from issue ids to commit SHAs; wiring
  sources -> correlate -> locator into one answer.
- Out of scope: issue and Session views, bvr correlation, time travel.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `louiselm://provenance/commit/<sha>` renders the commit subject, the issue
   ids from its trailers, the Session id, and the resolved transcript path.
2. An unresolved Session renders as explicitly unresolved. Omitting the row is
   forbidden: a coverage gap that renders as absence of history is the failure
   this epic exists to prevent.
3. The buffer is read-only and mutates nothing in git, Beads or transcripts.
4. Presentation lives only in the UI module. Core modules return structured
   data and typed events.

## Testing

- Headless behavioural smoke test in the style of `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`, not
  pixel assertions.
- Queued work arriving after disposal does not revive closed state, and editor
  operations occur only after the required scheduling boundary.
- A commit with no trailer, and a trailer whose Session has no transcript, both
  render as legible partial answers.

## Notes

Model the module on the existing `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`, whose cursor-id
detection, shell-out and read-only rendering are the same shape. Prefer
extending its patterns over inventing new ones.

This is the first user-visible slice of the epic: thin, but end to end through
every layer.
close_reason: Implemented read-only commit Provenance UI, command, tests, and generated documentation

comments.author: 01a03ef7-f719-7942-808a-f336208c9371
comments.text: Implemented the first user-visible Provenance slice. LouiselmInspectProvenance reads the commit SHA under the cursor, delegates git collection to provenance.sources, correlates explicit trailers, resolves Session transcript paths through the existing layout-keyed locator, and renders a read-only louiselm://provenance/commit/<sha> buffer. Missing trailers and missing transcript roots remain explicit partial answers; late callbacks are ignored when the requesting view is inactive. Added headless behavior coverage and generated vimdoc. Lesson destination: this issue comment; no AGENTS.md rule or new design question is warranted.

title: CI: doc/api.md is stale, missing the thought_chunk EventType variant
description:
CI's required "lua-language-server" job fails at the "Verify generated API appendix" step because `doc/api.md` is out of date with the source it's generated from.

## Observed

GitHub Actions runs 32929697287 (commit 849f5dc) and 32932395090 (commit fd1d606), repo euri10/louiselm, job "lua-language-server", step "Verify generated API appendix":

```
doc/api.md is stale; run ./scripts/generate-api-appendix
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Reproduced locally on the same commit:

```
$ ./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check
doc/api.md is stale; run ./scripts/generate-api-appendix
```

Running it without `--check` regenerates `doc/api.md` with this diff:

```diff
 louiselm.session.EventType:
     | "chunk"
     | "user_chunk"
+    | "thought_chunk"
     | "tool_call_started"
     | "tool_call_finished"
     | "permission_requested"
@@ -390,9 +391,9 @@ louiselm.session.EventType:

 ### louiselm.session.GenericEvent

-- `data: unknown` -- Event-specific payload. For "chunk"/"user_chunk" this is the raw ACP
+- `data: unknown` -- Event-specific payload. For "chunk"/"user_chunk"/"thought_chunk" this is
 - `session_id: string` -- Local session identifier.
-- `type: "chunk"|"error"|"tool_call_finished"|"tool_call_started"|"turn_done"...(+1)`
+- `type: "chunk"|"error"|"thought_chunk"|"tool_call_finished"|"tool_call_started"...(+2)`
```

## Symptoms

- CI reports the required "lua-language-server" job red on every push, independent of what the push actually changed.
- Exact error text: "doc/api.md is stale; run ./scripts/generate-api-appendix".

## Root cause

`louiselm.session.EventType` gained a `"thought_chunk"` variant as part of the reasoning-fold feature (commit `c56805f`), but `doc/api.md` was never regenerated to match — `./scripts/generate-api-appendix` (which the "lua-language-server" CI job runs with `--check`) diffs the committed file against a freshly generated one and fails when they differ. The regeneration command was not run before that commit (or a later one) was pushed.

## Why it was not caught

AGENTS.md section 4 lists `stylua --check .`, `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning`, and the `mini.test` run as the direct local quality gates; it does not call out `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` as one of them, even though CI enforces it. Nothing in the documented pre-commit checklist would have caught this locally.

## Fix direction

Run `./scripts/generate-api-appendix` and commit the resulting `doc/api.md`. Separately, consider adding `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` (and `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check`, see the related nightly-Vimdoc bug) to the documented local gates in AGENTS.md section 4, since both are already enforced in CI but currently only discoverable by reading `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

## Acceptance

- `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` exits 0 on the fix commit.
- CI's "lua-language-server" job goes green on the next push.

## Not covered

- The `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` CI failure and the nightly-only Vimdoc-staleness failure on the same CI runs are separate bugs with distinct root causes; filed separately.
- Whether other generated-doc drift exists elsewhere in the repo was not audited.
close_reason: fixed in 1395bfd. Regenerated doc/api.md via ./scripts/generate-api-appendix; --check now exits 0. Verified generate-vimdoc --check, stylua --check, and full mini.test suite unaffected (all green).

title: Codex reasoning chunks duplicate headers and fragment chat prose
description:
Codex reasoning updates corrupt the live chat after a tool call: the view renders one `[thinking]` header for each consecutive reasoning chunk instead of one collapsed reasoning paragraph, and the following assistant response is fragmented into one word/fragment per line with blank lines. This makes a normal Codex answer difficult to read. Reproduced in the currently attached Codex Session.

## Observed

Seen on 2026-08-26 in the live Neovim instance, Session `codex/01a03c4e-e214-7181-b31d-c59884d32810` (local view `session-3`, buffer 306), after its completed tool call and while the Session was `ready` at turn 1.

Live buffer evidence, lines 185-188, contains four consecutive `[thinking]` headers. Lines 190 onward contain the answer with every visible word/fragment separated by blank lines. The live state reports `thought_folds=1`, four visible headers, and six transcript blocks (`user`, `reasoning`, `assistant`, `tool_call`, `reasoning`, `assistant`), so the displayed structure is inconsistent with the recorded reasoning paragraphs.

Raw ACP evidence is retained at `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a03c4e-e214-7181-b31d-c59884d32810/log.jsonl` (156455 bytes, modified `2026-08-26 06:25:53.823794861 +0200`). Lines 60-63 are four adjacent `agent_to_client` `session/update` frames with `sessionUpdate="agent_thought_chunk"` and text lengths 2, 45, 2, and 50; they are followed by `agent_message_chunk` frames at lines 64-70. The log has six thought frames total (lines 15, 16, 60-63). No reasoning text is copied here because it may be sensitive; the local log is the primary artifact.

## Symptoms

- A Codex user sees four `[thinking]` labels rather than one collapsed reasoning section for contiguous thought updates.
- The assistant answer that follows is visually split into isolated words/fragments with blank lines, rather than streaming as readable prose.
- The Session's transcript structure says there is one second reasoning block, while the visible buffer presents four headers.

## Root cause

Unknown. `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:219-222` correctly maps ACP `agent_thought_chunk` to the typed `thought_chunk` event. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2232-2272` is responsible for maintaining `view.thought_run`, rendering its one header, and appending subsequent chunks. The observed four headers mean that run state is being closed or lost between adjacent Codex frames, or that the live loaded renderer differs from this checked-out path. The adjacent frame ordering above distinguishes this from an Agent emitting four separate reasoning paragraphs. The simultaneous fragmentation of later message chunks may share the same rendering/state-boundary failure, but that is unverified.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:674-719` directly emits two adjacent `thought_chunk` events through a synchronous fake session and asserts one header. It does not replay the captured Codex post-tool multi-frame sequence (four adjacent thought chunks followed by streamed message chunks) through the production ACP callback/scheduling boundary, nor assert that the rendered post-reasoning prose remains contiguous.

## Fix direction

Reproduce with a sanitized fixture preserving the observed event order from log lines 60-70. Trace the live event-to-render boundary to establish why `view.thought_run` does not persist. Fix the narrow shared rendering boundary so contiguous `thought_chunk` events produce exactly one header/fold and following `chunk` events append readable prose. Do not normalize or persist raw reasoning just to work around the presentation bug.

## Acceptance

- A regression test based on the observed Codex frame order fails before the fix and passes after it.
- Four contiguous `agent_thought_chunk` updates after a completed tool call render exactly one `[thinking]` header and one collapsed fold.
- The following streamed `agent_message_chunk` updates render as contiguous prose with no inserted blank line between ordinary word/fragments.
- The live Codex Session reproducer displays one collapsed reasoning section and a readable assistant answer.

## Not covered

- The exact mechanism that clears `view.thought_run` is not yet proven.
- Other Agents and Codex versions were not tested.
- Raw reasoning content remains only in the local ACP log and is intentionally not duplicated into this bead.
close_reason: Does not reproduce at HEAD; pinned with a characterization test in e538552 rather than repaired

title: Winbar clicks never work via real mouse click: v:lua.require(...) is not a valid click-function name
description:
## Symptom

No winbar click has ever worked through an actual mouse click in Neovim -
not the session-switch tabs, not the Limits click segment. Clicking produces
no error, no session switch, nothing. Discovered while manually QA'ing the
`437fbf0` cross-window click-routing fix (case 6) - that fix is itself
correct, but sits downstream of a click mechanism that was never wired up
correctly in the first place, so there was never a live click to route.

## Evidence

Isolated with two throwaway winbar click regions, independent of any
louiselm code, to bisect which part of the click wiring is at fault:

1. `vim.wo.winbar = "%0@v:lua.qa_click_test_handler@[CLICK ME]%X"` (a plain
   global function reference) - click worked, handler fired.
2. `vim.wo.winbar = "%0@v:lua.require('qa_click_mod').handler@[CLICK ME 2]%X"`
   (the exact same shape as this codebase's actual click target string) -
   click did nothing at all.

Confirms Vim's `%{N}@{Function}@` winbar/statusline click syntax requires
`{Function}` to be a plain dotted name it can resolve at click-dispatch
time, not an arbitrary Lua call expression like `require('mod')` embedded in
that field.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:306`:

```lua
local WINBAR_CLICK_HANDLER = "v:lua.require('louiselm.ui.chat.command').winbar_click"
```

This constant has existed since `7b31438` "feat(ui): show Session attention
in winbar" - the winbar-click feature has apparently never worked via a real
mouse click since it was introduced, only in unit tests that call
`M.winbar_click(...)` directly (bypassing Vim's actual click dispatch, so
the broken click-target string was never exercised).

## Fix

Expose a stable global Lua function (not a call expression) as the click
target, forwarding to the reassignable `M.winbar_click`:

```lua
-- command.lua
_G.__louiselm_winbar_click = function(...)
  return M.winbar_click(...)
end
```

```lua
-- init.lua
local WINBAR_CLICK_HANDLER = "v:lua.__louiselm_winbar_click"
```

Found and being fixed during manual QA round, case 6.

title: Forensics records embedded_context from a nonexistent top-level ACP capability
description:
## Evidence

The Forensics collector records `embedded_context` from a field that does not exist in the ACP schema, so every Forensics record misreports the capability as `false`.

- ACP schema (agent-client-protocol-schema 1.5.0, `src/v1/agent.rs:4609`): `embedded_context` is a field of `PromptCapabilities` only — "Agent supports embedded context in `session/prompt` requests. When enabled, the Client is allowed to include `ContentBlock::Resource` in prompt requests." There is no top-level `AgentCapabilities.embeddedContext`.
- `lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:333` (Forensics collection): `embedded_context = capabilities.embeddedContext == true`, where `capabilities = client.agent_capabilities`. That top-level key is never present, so the value is always `false` for every Session, for every Agent.
- `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:469` reads the same capability correctly: `prompt_capabilities.embeddedContext == true`. The Session's live state and the Forensics record therefore disagree by construction.
- Concrete on-disk record: `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/1787796219-1787796219-265777660586430.json` records `"embedded_context": false` for `deepseek/session-5d380d32-…`. The adapter serving that Session (acp-llm-adapter, `src/acp/mod.rs:764` `build_initialize_response`) advertises `promptCapabilities.embeddedContext: true`. False evidence on disk.

## Impact

- Anything gating on the Forensics `capabilities` table (diagnosis, routing evidence) treats deepseek Sessions as non-embedded-context.
- This session's handoff grill (louiselm-93wl) was briefly steered wrong by it: the record was cited as evidence that the deepseek adapter lacks embedded-context support, which is false — the adapter advertises and handles it.

## Fix direction

Read the nested field, mirroring the correct read at `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:469`. Do not add a top-level read as a second source.

## Acceptance

- A regression test builds a Forensics record for an Agent advertising `promptCapabilities.embeddedContext: true` and asserts `observations.capabilities.embedded_context == true`.
- A second case asserts `false` when the capability is absent.
- `registry.lua` no longer references a top-level `capabilities.embeddedContext`.
close_reason: done

comments.author: claude/b9144876-1764-4b20-a1c1-0d129f0a7105
comments.text: Fixed by reading subject.embedded_context (Session.state.embedded_context, already correctly derived from nested promptCapabilities.embeddedContext at lifecycle.lua:469 and exposed via inspect()) instead of re-deriving from client.agent_capabilities.embeddedContext. Single source of truth rather than mirroring the read in a second place. Regression test added in tests/session/api_spec.lua T[forensics]: one case for true (nested promptCapabilities.embeddedContext=true), one for false (capability absent). Full stylua/lua-language-server/mini.test/api-appendix gates pass.

title: Handoff
description: Creation of a new Session with a configured Agent to take over in-flight work, seeded with an operator-authored takeover instruction and a compacted reviewed transcript, while retaining the source Session. The target Agent may be the same Agent as the source; the target is always a distinct Session.
design: Established by the louiselm-slo grill-me session on 2026-08-23 from the shipped LouiseLM Handoff behavior. Amended by the louiselm-93wl grill-me session on 2026-08-27: a 267KB full-transcript Handoff looped the receiving deepseek Session for 52 turns with no progress, so the payload became an operator-authored takeover brief plus compacted transcript, sent as a typed resource block where the target advertises embeddedContext. Amended by maintainer clarification on 2026-08-29 (louiselm-2cq1 and screenshot /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260829_0609_1920x1200_1787976589.png): a Handoff may target the same configured Agent as the source, because it creates a distinct Session.
notes: Avoid: provider switch, Model change within one Session, or mutating the source Session. Distinguish from a Model change, which stays within one Session. A Handoff is always a takeover, never bare context transfer; its payload must name the task being taken over. The full record lives in the source Session; the Handoff carries the compact. Same-Agent Handoffs are valid when the operator needs a fresh Session with the same Agent.

title: ACP session options and resource telemetry UX
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM can select an adapter only when the first chat is created, and it currently discards ACP session configuration options and usage/context updates. Users cannot change an agent-advertised model or reasoning setting after startup, cannot see which settings are active, and cannot tell whether a long autonomous session is approaching its context limit or waiting on a permission request. Starting multiple sessions also lacks explicit navigation and cleanup controls.

## Solution

Add a generic ACP session-controls and observability UX. After `session/new` becomes ready, open a token-free setup overview of all supported agent-advertised select and boolean options; allow idle-only changes through a public chat method and `:LouiselmSessionOptions`, refreshing the complete option list after each update. Add explicit `:LouiselmCancel`, `:LouiselmNewSession`, `:LouiselmSwitchSession`, and `:LouiselmCloseSession` commands. Keep existing sessions running when a new one starts, expose their state through compact headers and switcher rows, and dispose sessions explicitly when closed. Render passive context-pressure states, reported cumulative cost, active settings, lifecycle state, permission waiting, compaction/tool activity, and optional experimental per-turn usage fields without estimating tokens or prices.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I want to choose model and other ACP session options before my first prompt, so that each new session starts with deliberate settings.
2. As a user, I want to change supported options while a session is idle, so that future turns use the new configuration without restarting the session.
3. As a user, I want busy sessions to refuse option changes and offer explicit cancellation, so that autonomous turns are not reconfigured mid-flight.
4. As a user, I want to see active settings, lifecycle state, context pressure, cost, and reported usage, so that I can monitor long-running work.
5. As a user, I want to create, switch between, and close concurrent sessions, so that multiple adapters can work without leaking processes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A ready new session with supported ACP config options opens an overview picker before the first prompt; Esc accepts agent defaults and an agent with no supported options skips the picker.
2. The overview renders every supported select/boolean option in agent order, supports selecting values, applies `session/set_config_option`, replaces the local list with the complete response, and handles agent-pushed `config_option_update` notifications.
3. Option changes are rejected while prompting, cancelling, or waiting for permission; `:LouiselmCancel` requests cancellation and late callbacks cannot revive disposed UI or sessions.
4. The client advertises boolean config-option support and ignores unknown future option types while rejecting malformed consumed fields.
5. `:LouiselmNewSession` chooses an adapter, creates a separate session, and opens its setup picker without cancelling existing sessions; `:LouiselmSwitchSession` selects attached sessions using compact agent/state/options/context/cost rows.
6. `:LouiselmCloseSession` confirms only for active or permission-blocked sessions, disposes the selected session/process, removes its chat buffer, and leaves other sessions running.
7. Session headers show exact lifecycle/activity state, all active options, context used/size/percentage with passive 75/90/95% warning states, stale context after model changes until refreshed, and reported cumulative cost when available.
8. Completed turns append a compact usage footer only for reported fields; optional experimental usage fields are validated defensively, never estimated or supplemented with adapter-specific fallbacks.
9. Compaction remains agent-owned: render generic ACP tool/compaction activity and context-meter changes, but add no LouiseLM manual compaction API in this phase.
10. Headless session snapshots/events expose typed configuration, lifecycle, permission, context, cost, and usage state for a future monitor; no swarm dashboard or orchestration is included.

## Implementation Notes

- Extend the session lifecycle and ACP validation at the shared boundary; preserve complete option-list replacement and asynchronous main-loop scheduling.
- Enrich `session:inspect()` and typed events rather than deriving telemetry from rendered buffers.
- Keep `LLM_MODEL` in the caller-owned schema/config example; do not add a universal built-in schema that rejects provider-specific environment variables.
- Preserve agent-provided defaults, session history, cumulative cost, and existing slash-command passthrough. Mark context telemetry stale after model changes until the agent reports a new effective window.

## Testing Notes

- Add focused mini.test coverage for option parsing, dependent option refresh, boolean capability advertisement, malformed/unknown options, idle-only transitions, cancellation, permission waiting, and disposal/late results.
- Add headless UI smoke tests for setup/overview flow, command behavior, headers, passive thresholds, usage footer omission, compaction/tool rendering, multiple-session navigation, and close confirmation.
- Exercise ACP notifications and process callbacks through scheduled production boundaries; use the mock ACP agent and no real credentials or agent binaries.

## Out of Scope

- Manual compaction or a hard-coded `:LouiselmCompact` command.
- A generic advertised-command picker.
- A swarm dashboard, orchestration, capacity policy, worktree isolation, or subagent aggregation.
- Adapter-specific usage parsers, pricing tables, tokenizers, or cache-cost estimates.
- A universal built-in configuration schema.
close_reason: Implemented ACP select/boolean session options, typed lifecycle/context/cost/usage state, setup and multi-session commands, safe scheduled UI updates, documentation, and passing StyLua/LuaLS/95-test gates

title: QA round: account limits, terminal results, Handoff and discovery through acb65c7
description:
# Manual QA review — louiselm.nvim, 2026-08-25

**Build under test:** `60724f3..acb65c7` (43 commits). Confirm with
`git -C /home/lotso/code/louiselm rev-parse --short HEAD` = `acb65c7`.

You drive; I read the evidence and edit this file every round. Both this file
and `qa_init.lua` are scratch under `/tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/`; neither
gets committed.

Origin: the last round was `louiselm-0aft` (2026-08-24, build `60724f3`). Since
then the plugin gained **Agent account limits** end to end (parser, registry
capability/notification handling, winbar segment, `:LouiselmLimits` detail view,
threshold alerts, reset timers), **terminal tool-result rendering** for Copilot's
`task_complete`, **text-result signposting**, **Handoff transcript retention with
source provenance**, **resumed-turn usage replay**, **standalone proposal review
controls**, **session-picker recency ordering and injected-title recovery**, and
**embedded-resource skill catalogs**. Forensic log folding was added and then
reverted (`963ef07`/`0827979` → `a531705`/`771484a`) — out of scope, do not test.

CI enforcement, AGENTS.md rules and beads bookkeeping changed too. Not manually
testable; excluded deliberately, not forgotten.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Codex account limits reach the winbar and the detail view | **passed** — real 89%/7d bucket rendered as expected; `<Tab>` was a recipe misread, completion works |
| 2 | An unsolicited limits notification refreshes presentation | **partial** — notifications arrived and were accepted, nothing crashed, but the value never moved so re-render is unproven |
| 3 | Agents without the capability stay silent; empty snapshot says so | **passed** — copilot issued zero limits frames, claude returned `{"buckets": []}` |
| 4 | Copilot's `task_complete` conclusion is readable in the transcript | **FAILED** — F1: conclusion still not rendered; `task_complete` arrives 2.1s after `end_turn`, so `turn_done` flushes nothing |
| 5 | Handoff is retained in the target transcript with source provenance | **partial** — retention and edit fidelity confirmed; F3: provenance names `session-1`, not the durable id |
| 6 | A resumed Session replays per-turn usage in the right order | **passed** — ledger byte-exact against the wire, first `[usage]` sits after turn 1 |
| 7 | Session picker sorts by recency and recovers injected subjects | **ordering passed; F4 found** — `:LouiselmResume!` fails `session/list` on every strict Agent |
| 8 | A standalone proposal diff can be applied, discarded, and restores focus | **passed** — focus restored on both paths; stale guard preserved the file byte-for-byte |

## Round constants

Run everything from `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`.

Cases 1–6 and 8 share one pinned state root so their evidence stays together and
case 6 can resume what case 1–2 created:

```sh
cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm
XDG_STATE_HOME=/tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/state \
  nvim -u /tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/qa_init.lua
```

Case 7 deliberately runs **without** the override — it needs your real session
history. Its steps say so again.

After each launch:

- `:echo $XDG_STATE_HOME` must print `/tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/state` (cases
  1–6, 8). If it prints something else the process did not inherit it; say so
  before running the case, because every evidence path below is wrong then.
- `:checkhealth louiselm` — `acp-proxy`, `node`, `copilot` must resolve. A
  missing executable is a setup blocker, not a product failure.

Evidence roots, once you have an ACP session id from `:LouiselmSessionId`
(format `<agent>/<acp-session-id>`):

```sh
LOG=/tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/<acp-session-id>/log.jsonl
USAGE=/tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/state/nvim/louiselm/usage.json
```

`ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=1` is set, so these logs contain your real prompts. Report
paths and session ids; do not paste log bodies into chat.

## Ground rules

- Fresh Session per case unless a case says to reuse one. A remembered
  permission or a prior routing decision changes the path under test.
- The Session-options picker appears on ready; note whether it is coherent, then
  dismiss it. Dismissing keeps Agent defaults on purpose.
- Tool payload inspectors are ordinary floating windows: close with `:q`, not
  plain `q`.
- Report what you saw verbatim, including text you think is irrelevant. Winbar
  spacing and punctuation are load-bearing in case 1.

---

## 1. Codex account limits reach the winbar and the detail view

Exercises `600e3d8`, `de04317`, `f8309a3`, `4e79797` — `session/limits.lua`,
`registry.lua:471-708`, `ui/limits.lua`, `ui/chat/init.lua:660-690`.

Codex is the only configured Agent that returns real quota buckets. A recent
real snapshot had one bucket `codex`, one window at 89% used over 10080 minutes.

Steps:

1. Launch with the pinned root above.
2. `:LouiselmChat`, select `codex`. Dismiss the options picker once ready.
3. Read the winbar of the chat window and copy it verbatim.
4. Run `:LouiselmLimits` with no argument.
5. Type `:LouiselmLimits ` and press `<Tab>`; note the completion list.
6. Run `:LouiselmSessionId` and save the id.

Expect: a winbar segment shaped `limits codex 11%/7d ↻6d` — literally
`limits <bucket> <remaining>%/<window> ↻<time-to-reset>`, appended after the
status/context/cost segments. Colour is green above 20% remaining, amber at
20%–10%, red at or below 10% or when a limit is reached. `:LouiselmLimits` opens
a detail buffer for `codex` listing the bucket, each window's used percentage,
duration and `Resets:` as an absolute time plus a relative one, the plan type,
and the reset-credit count. `<Tab>` completes to the configured Agent names.

Prediction to confirm or refute (`4e79797`): there is a **space before `↻`**. If
you see `11%/7d↻6d` you are running a stale plugin copy, not `acb65c7` — stop
and tell me.

Failure signature: no limits segment; a segment stuck on `limits loading` or
`limits unavailable` that never resolves; `:LouiselmLimits` reporting *could not
inspect Agent account limits*; `Resets: reset time passed` for a reset that is
plainly in the future; an `E5560` fast-event error in `:messages`.

Evidence — I will run this once you give me the session id:

```sh
grep -h account_limits "$LOG" | head -5
```

This settles two things without your interpretation: that the read request went
out with `"params": {}` — a JSON **object**, which is exactly the `de04317` fix
— and what the Agent actually answered. What the winbar *renders* rests on your
report; the log only proves what arrived.

---

## 2. An unsolicited limits notification refreshes presentation

Exercises `registry.lua:handle_agent_notification`, `lifecycle.lua:181-190`,
`ui/chat/init.lua:793-893`.

Codex pushes `_io.github.euri10.louiselm/account_limits/updated` on its own after
consuming quota. Nothing in the test suite proves the UI reacts to a real one.

Steps (same Neovim, same codex Session as case 1):

1. Leave `:LouiselmLimits` open in a split if you can, so you can watch it.
2. Submit: `Read /home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md and list the four bullets
   in section 11 verbatim.` (absolute path on purpose — a bare filename makes
   the Agent search first and may not consume enough quota).
3. When the turn completes, read the winbar and the detail buffer again.

Expect: the used percentage and/or reset time move without you re-running any
command, and an open detail buffer updates in place rather than needing a
reopen. If a window crosses 20% or 10% remaining you also get a `louiselm:`
notification naming the Agent, bucket and window.

Prediction to confirm or refute: `handle_notification` now calls into the
registry for **every** ACP notification before filtering for `session/update`.
If the registry ever errors there, all session updates stop. Watch for the
transcript freezing mid-turn while the Agent is plainly still working.

Failure signature: the log shows an `updated` notification but nothing in the UI
changes; the detail buffer keeps stale numbers; a duplicate notification storm;
`E5560` or any `fast event` error in `:messages`.

Evidence:

```sh
grep -c 'account_limits/updated' "$LOG"
grep -o '"usedPercent": [0-9]*' "$LOG" | tail -5
```

---

## 3. Agents without the capability stay silent; an empty snapshot says so

Exercises `registry.lua:limits_source` / `inspect_agent_limits` and
`ui/limits.lua:summary` status branches.

Three configured Agents have three different shapes, and only real handshakes
prove which branch is taken. Claude advertises the capability but its read
returns `{"buckets": []}`. Copilot does not advertise it at all.

Steps (same Neovim):

1. `:LouiselmChat`, select `claude`, dismiss the picker. Read its winbar.
2. `:LouiselmChat`, select `copilot`, dismiss the picker. Read its winbar.
3. Run `:LouiselmLimits copilot`.
4. Run `:LouiselmLimits nosuchagent`.
5. Switch back to the codex Session (`:LouiselmSwitchSession`) and confirm its
   limits segment is still there and still codex's numbers.

Expect: claude shows `limits no data` in amber. Copilot shows **no** limits
segment at all. `:LouiselmLimits copilot` opens a detail buffer saying the Agent
does not support account limits — not an error. `:LouiselmLimits nosuchagent`
reports `unknown agent 'nosuchagent'`. Switching sessions re-renders per-Agent
numbers, never one Agent's numbers under another's winbar.

Failure signature: copilot showing `limits unavailable` in red (that would mean
a missing capability is being reported as a failure); claude showing nothing;
codex's numbers appearing on the claude or copilot winbar; the bogus-agent call
opening an empty buffer instead of reporting.

Evidence: your report plus the initialize frames, which I can read from each
Session's log to confirm which Agent advertised what.

---

## 4. Copilot's `task_complete` conclusion is readable in the transcript

Exercises `efe5594` and `f1bdce8` — `ui/chat/init.lua:1283-1320`, `2158-2170`,
`2223-2236`. This is the live fix for `louiselm-zufj`, which is still
`in_progress` and was filed from exactly this path on 2026-08-25.

Copilot ends a turn by emitting its conclusion inside a completed `tool_call`
titled `task_complete` rather than as an assistant message chunk. Before the fix
the user saw only `[tool] <id>: task_complete (completed)` and a ready Session
with no answer.

Steps:

1. `:LouiselmChat`, select `copilot`, **fresh Session**.
2. **Do not dismiss the options picker.** Set `Mode` → `Autopilot`. If you
   dismissed it, `:LouiselmSessionOptions` on the idle Session does the same.
   This is the whole point: Copilot only emits `task_complete` in Autopilot,
   described by the Agent itself as *"autonomous mode that enables allow-all and
   runs until task completion without user interaction"*. In the default `Agent`
   mode it answers with ordinary assistant chunks and this case tests nothing.
3. Submit: `Read /home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md section 11 and state your
   conclusion about what it forbids. Do not ask me any questions.`
4. Let the turn finish and the Session return to ready.
5. Put the cursor on any completed tool row and run `:LouiselmInspectTool`;
   close the float with `:q`.

Expect: the conclusion text appears as ordinary prose in the transcript after
the tool rows, separated by a blank line. Completed tool rows whose payload
carries text are suffixed `· text result — use :LouiselmInspectTool`.

Failure signature — three distinct ones, tell me which:

- **Still hidden:** the turn ends at `[tool] … task_complete (completed)` with
  no conclusion prose. The fix did not reach the live payload.
- **Doubled:** the conclusion appears twice, once as prose and once elsewhere.
  That means an assistant chunk arrived too and the pending text was not cleared.
- **Over-labelled:** every trivial tool row gets `· text result …`, including
  ones with nothing worth inspecting. Noise, still a finding.

Evidence:

```sh
python3 - "$LOG" <<'PY'
import json, sys
ids = set()
for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
    u = (json.loads(line).get('payload', {}).get('params') or {}).get('update') or {}
    if u.get('title') == 'task_complete':
        ids.add(u.get('toolCallId'))
    if u.get('toolCallId') in ids and u.get('status') == 'completed':
        c = (u.get('rawOutput') or {}).get('content')
        print(u['toolCallId'], '| content chars:', len(c) if isinstance(c, str) else None)
        print('   head:', c[:90] if isinstance(c, str) else c)
PY
```

Validated against the 2026-08-25 Copilot Session that produced `louiselm-zufj`:
it printed two completed calls carrying 1189 and 394 characters of conclusion.
Note that the **completed** update carries no `title` — only the pending start
frame does — so rendering depends on the title being remembered per tool-call
id. If the conclusion fails to render, that carry-forward is the first place
I will look.

That proves what Copilot sent and whether a textual conclusion existed at all.
Whether it *rendered* rests on your report of the buffer.

---

## 5. Handoff is retained in the target transcript with source provenance

Exercises `acb65c7` — `transcript.lua:155-235`, `ui/chat/init.lua:1733-1750`,
`2613-2680`. Fix for `louiselm-ac6z`, found live on 2026-08-24: the target Agent
acted on a Handoff whose text never entered its transcript.

Steps:

1. In the codex Session from case 1, make sure there are at least two turns of
   real content.
2. Run `:LouiselmHandOff` and pick the **claude** Session as target.
3. In the review buffer, confirm it holds the rendered codex transcript, edit
   one line so you can recognise your edit, then submit with `<C-s>`.
4. You land on the claude Session. Let the turn complete.
5. Run `:LouiselmToMarkdown` on the **claude** Session and read the top of the
   exported markdown.
6. Switch back to codex and confirm it is intact and still attached.

Expect: the exported claude markdown contains a `## User` entry whose body is
the reviewed text **including your edit**, preceded by a line
`<sub>Handoff from Session: \`codex/<acp-session-id>\`</sub>` naming the source.
Both Sessions remain attached and switchable.

Failure signature: the Handoff `## User` entry absent from the export (the
original bug); present but with no `Handoff from Session` line; the provenance
line naming the *target* or a local id like `session-1` rather than the source
`<agent>/<acp-session-id>`; your edit missing, i.e. the pre-edit text was sent;
the source Session detached or its transcript truncated.

Evidence: the markdown you export, plus the claude Session log showing the
prompt that actually went over the wire — I compare the two so we can tell
"recorded but not sent" from "sent but not recorded".

---

## 6. A resumed Session replays per-turn usage in the right order

Exercises `ee9e541`, `348d6d0`, `0534977`, `0e266a0` — `workflow/usage.lua`
turn records, `ui/chat/init.lua:2466-2480` and `2053-2075`.

Steps:

1. Note the codex ACP session id from case 1 and how many turns it has.
2. Quit Neovim entirely.
3. Relaunch with the **same** pinned root and init.
4. `:LouiselmResume`, pick that codex Session, and let the history replay fully.
5. Read the replayed transcript top to bottom.

Expect: each replayed turn is followed by its own `[usage] …` line with the
token counts that turn actually used, in the same order as the original
conversation, and the last one lands after the final turn rather than at the
very end of the buffer or not at all. Live turns after the resume keep working.

Failure signature: no `[usage]` lines at all after resume; a single `[usage]`
line for the whole history; usage lines attached to the wrong turn (off by one
is the specific thing `348d6d0` was meant to fix); `Error: could not …` inserted
into the transcript; usage values of `0` where the ledger has real numbers.

Evidence:

```sh
python3 -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(open('$USAGE'))
for t in d.get('turns',[]):
    print(t['agent'], t['session_id'][:12], 'turn', t['turn'], t['usage'])
"
```

The ledger's `turn` numbers are the ground truth for the ordering you report.

---

## 7. Session picker sorts by recency and recovers injected subjects

Exercises `eb86dc4`, `1d4c235`, `c97c72c` — `ui/chat/init.lua:396-430`.

Injected-skill Agents (codex, deepseek, glm) prepend a
`<skills_instructions>…</available_skills>` block and `[@AGENTS.md](…)` resource
links to the first prompt, so discovered Session titles used to be an unreadable

production peer, and the all-workspace path — the only one that produces empty

title: Grill-me needed: how should louiselm own versioning across plugin, capture-service, and Android, and which GitHub tooling should drive it?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing.

Question: how should louiselm own its versioning across its three shipped components (Neovim plugin, capture-service Rust crate, Android app) as it moves from alpha to external users, and which GitHub-native tooling should generate, enforce, and publish those versions?

Context / evidence that raised it:
louiselm currently advertises itself to ACP adapters as `clientInfo = { name = "louiselm.nvim", version = "0.1.0" }`, hardcoded in `lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:199`. The same `0.1.0` is duplicated in at least two other places: `capture-service/Cargo.toml` (and the matching `Cargo.lock` entry) and `android/app/build.gradle.kts` (`versionName`). AGENTS.md section 1 says the project is early-stage with no external users and that breaking changes are acceptable, so there is no release discipline yet — but the version string is already observable to every adapter through ACP `initialize`, and duplicated literals have no mechanism to stay in sync.

Threads worth pulling:
- Single source of truth: does the canonical version live in a `VERSION` file, a Lua module, `Cargo.toml`, git tags only, or somewhere else? Which component owns it, and how do the others derive it without a build-time codegen step?
- Lockstep versus independent versioning: should the Neovim plugin, capture-service, and Android app share one version, or diverge? The ACP `clientInfo.version` should report the plugin/agent client version — how is that kept meaningful if the repo has multiple release cadences?
- GitHub tooling candidates: release-please, semantic-release, Changesets, git-cliff + GitHub Releases, or manual tag-and-release. Which fits a monorepo that is Lua/Rust/Android (no npm ecosystem) and has no Conventional Commits discipline yet?
- Conventional Commits: is adopting/enforcing it a prerequisite for automatic version bumping and changelog generation, and is that acceptable for this repo?
- Pre-release semantics: how do 0.x breaking changes and alpha status interact with semver? How should adapters distinguish `clientInfo.version` (cosmetic/reported) from ACP `protocolVersion` (compatibility contract)?
- GitHub Actions integration: tag on merge to main, release branches, per-component workflows? What artifacts does a release actually produce for a Neovim plugin (git tag, GitHub Release, LuaRocks, stable branch) versus the Rust binary and Android APK?
- Drift risk: should `clientInfo.version` be read dynamically at runtime from one source, or injected at packaging time, so the advertised version cannot rot relative to the actual release?
delete_reason: superseded by louiselm-df3e (original was created with wrong actor 'lotso')

title: Loaded Provenance content keeps the loading popup height
description:
After the Decision Provenance loading state is replaced by the completed evidence, the popup keeps the loading state height instead of resizing to fit the loaded content.

## Observed

Manual QA on 2026-08-28 after commit 7efbc44. Screenshot: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260828_0600_1920x1200_1787889613.png. The completed Decision view contains many lines but is displayed in a window only about 3-4 lines high, leaving the content clipped and requiring scrolling.

## Symptoms

- The loading popup appears immediately.
- Final Provenance content loads successfully.
- The second window remains the height calculated for the three-line loading state.
- The completed Decision view is difficult to review.

## Root cause

In lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:297-309, open_provenance calculates popup height from #lines. The loading call uses three lines, and the later refresh reuses the existing window without updating its height.

## Why it was not caught

The regression verifies buffer reuse and loading text but does not assert window dimensions after the asynchronous content replacement. The manual screenshot exposed the mismatch.

## Fix direction

At the shared open_provenance refresh boundary, resize the existing Provenance window after replacing content using the loaded line count and current editor dimensions. Preserve the existing window when possible and keep the height bounded.

## Acceptance

- A regression proves a loading popup grows to the bounded height required by completed content.
- The completed Decision view is readable without being left at loading-state height.
- Reopening an existing view still avoids duplicate buffers and windows.

## Not covered

- Exact preferred popup dimensions beyond the existing width/height bounds.
close_reason: Already fixed on main by commit 6f85702 'fix(ui): resize Provenance popup', landed 2026-08-28 06:22:48 -- one commit after 7efbc44, the commit this bug's QA round was run against, so this was a race between the QA finder and an independent fix, never cross-referenced. The fix is exactly what this issue's 'Fix direction' asked for: open_provenance now calls nvim.api.nvim_win_set_height(window, height) when reusing an existing window (lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:308), and the same commit added the regression test tests/ui/provenance_spec.lua 'resizes an existing window after loading evidence', which passes on current HEAD. No code change needed; verified via git history plus a live test run (15/15 provenance_spec.lua cases green).

title: Claude file edits are auto-denied because the ACP diff content is ignored
description:
Every file edit requested by claude-agent-acp is refused without a review ever opening.

## Observed (session claude/0503f972-01db-4158-ac62-e89cce3de188, 2026-08-17)

~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260817-063214-181953-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log line 36:

  PERMISSION id=2 kind=edit "Edit qa-diff-test.txt"
    rawInput keys: [file_path, old_string, new_string, replace_all]
    content: [{"type":"diff","path":"/home/lotso/code/louiselm/qa-diff-test.txt","oldText":"hello","newText":"hello world"}]

line 37: tool_call_update failed, rawOutput "Tool permission request failed: Error: Tool use aborted".

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/diff/init.lua:29 request_edit reads the edit payload only from toolCall.rawInput, looking for diff / content / newText / new_text. Claude sends the Edit tool arguments verbatim there (file_path, old_string, new_string, replace_all) and puts the reviewable text in toolCall.content as an ACP diff entry, which louiselm never reads. So Apply.normalize fails with "diff edit must contain diff or content", Diff:open returns false, and lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua writes an error line then cancels the request. The cancelled outcome is what the agent reports as "Tool use aborted".

Net effect: the diff review has never worked with this agent, and every edit is silently denied.

## Fix direction

- Read the first toolCall.content entry of type "diff". When it carries oldText, the payload is an exact-text replacement of a fragment, not whole-file content; when it does not, newText is the whole file.
- Teach louiselm.ui.diff.apply a replacement form alongside diff and content so the preview shows the real before/after.
- Keep the rawInput path working for agents that populate it.

## Acceptance

- A request shaped like the payload above opens a review showing -hello / +hello world, and accepting sends the allow option.
- A replacement whose old text is not in the file fails with an actionable error instead of a silent cancel.
- replace_all is honored: false replaces the first occurrence only.
close_reason: Fixed in a57cee2 (diff UI now falls back to the ACP diff content entry when rawInput lacks diff/content). Verified live by the permissions QA round (QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md, now archived as louiselm-aib): case 6 (F1 regression, gates cases 3-5) passed — review buffer opened, 'a' applied the edit, file read back 'hello world'. Bead was never closed despite the fix landing and being verified; closed now while retroactively archiving that round.

title: LouiselmToMarkdown: export session transcript from structured JSONL
description:
## Goal
A LouiselmToMarkdown user command that exports a louiselm session's full transcript to a markdown file, reconstructed from the session's structured JSONL data — not a scrape of the rendered chat buffer.

## Scope
- In scope: new command registered alongside the existing Louiselm* commands (LouiselmResume, LouiselmSessionId, etc.) in the chat command module; reads from the same session/transcript data those commands already access; writes full tool commands and full tool results/output (not one-line summaries or truncated text); takes a session id (defaults to current session if omitted).
- Out of scope: any blog-specific behavior (scaffolding, literalinclude stubbing) — this command only exports one session to one markdown file and knows nothing about blog/.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given a session id, running the command produces a markdown file containing the full reconstructed transcript: every user message, every assistant message, every tool call with its full command and full result/output.
2. Given no session id, the command operates on the current session.
3. Output is deterministic for a given session (same input transcript produces the same markdown, modulo an output path/timestamp).
4. Existing manually-copied transcripts (e.g. the buffer-scrape currently at the louiselm repo root) are visibly less complete than this command's output — spot-check against one real session confirms previously-truncated tool output is now present in full.

## Testing
- Unit test against a fixture session JSONL asserting full tool commands/results appear in the output, not truncated summaries.
- Existing session/transcript module test patterns apply; no new UI/buffer testing needed.

## Notes
- This is real, discoverable plugin surface (unlike the rest of the parent feature's blog/ tooling) — it is useful to any louiselm user independent of blogging.
- Parent feature: louiselm-r1k.
close_reason: LouiselmToMarkdown command implemented and tested: registered in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua, Chat:to_markdown in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua, rendering via louiselm.session.transcript. Full tool commands/output (untruncated), defaults to current session, deterministic output, dedicated test coverage in tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua (8/8 passing) plus tests/session/transcript_export_spec.lua. Shipped across commits 4e4a58b, 6167df0, 14dbab6.

title: Consolidate Scarlet Signal branding and propose README hero variant
description:
## Goal

Remove the obsolete Android logo proposal archive, preserve the settled logo decision in Beads, and create a README hero image proposal that applies the selected Logo 2 / Scarlet Signal visual language to the existing README artwork.

## Context and decision

- `design/proposals/android-capture-logo/` is an exploratory archive containing five concepts, refinements, comparison sheets, and generation prompts. It is no longer needed in the project and should be removed after this decision is recorded in this task.
- Logo 2, **Scarlet Signal**, is the chosen Android app logo. Its refined raster is already implemented as the density-specific launcher resources under `android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-*/ic_launcher.png`, and the Android manifest already points to `@mipmap/ic_launcher`. Those packaged resources are the source of truth and must remain.
- The current README hero is `assets/louiselm-hero.webp` (1774x887), a landscape scene of people, ideas, tools, and agents connected through a red-and-black mesh. Preserve that composition and narrative while exploring the Scarlet Signal palette, graphic energy, and revolutionary spirit.

## Scope

- In scope: delete the obsolete `design/proposals/android-capture-logo/` directory and its raster/prompt/comparison artifacts; do not delete or replace the packaged Android launcher resources.
- In scope: create a candidate raster asset from the existing README hero, preferably at `assets/louiselm-hero-scarlet-proposal.webp`, keeping the existing landscape dimensions/aspect ratio and recognizable composition.
- In scope: carry over Logo 2’s visual language—near-black ink, warm cream or clean light ground, saturated scarlet accents, bold print/linocut character, and the same sense of portrait-led revolutionary motion—without simply turning the README into a giant launcher icon.
- In scope: keep `README.md` pointing at the current `assets/louiselm-hero.webp` until the maintainer explicitly accepts the candidate; the result is a proposal, not an automatic README replacement.
- Out of scope: changing Android launcher artwork or manifest wiring, redesigning the hero composition or README copy, preserving the five rejected concepts, or adding a new prompt/archive document outside Beads.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No files remain under `design/proposals/android-capture-logo/`; the selected-logo decision and its implementation status remain recorded in this Beads task.
2. The Android launcher resources under `android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-*` and the manifest’s `@mipmap/ic_launcher` reference are unchanged and still represent Logo 2 / Scarlet Signal.
3. A valid README hero candidate exists at `assets/louiselm-hero-scarlet-proposal.webp` (or an equally clear `assets/` proposal path), with the existing hero’s landscape dimensions/aspect ratio and no accidental cropping.
4. The candidate preserves the current hero’s central composition, connected mesh, and core people/tools/ideas motifs; it reads as a focused color-and-style treatment rather than a new scene.
5. The candidate visibly adopts Scarlet Signal’s black, warm-cream/light, and saturated-scarlet palette and its bold print-like, portrait-led energy, while remaining legible at README display size.
6. `README.md` continues to render the current hero unchanged; the candidate is clearly labeled as a proposal and is not silently presented as the accepted project artwork.
7. Full-size and README-sized visual inspection confirms both assets open correctly and the candidate has no text, watermark, unintended objects, or unrelated visual style drift.

## Testing

- Inspect the current hero and candidate side by side at full size and typical README display size.
- Verify candidate format, dimensions, aspect ratio, and the unchanged README image path.
- Verify no Android resource or manifest changes were introduced; an Android build is unnecessary unless those files are touched.
- Confirm the removed proposal directory is absent while Beads history still records why it was removed.

## Notes

Logo 2 refers to `02 — Scarlet Signal` in the former proposal set. The README proposal should borrow its colors, print character, and spirit—not copy the launcher icon’s square framing or replace the existing visual story.

title: Reconcile stale in-progress Beads claims
description:
## Problem

Beads issues marked in_progress retain old Agent Session assignees after those Sessions have ended. The backlog then presents abandoned work as actively owned, making the project look stalled and making it unclear whether a new Agent may safely take over.

Observed 2026-08-30 in louiselm: br list --status in_progress reports 14 issues, including old claims such as louiselm-5tuq assigned to claude/35e4614f-fbee-450f-887c-39360cfdae52 and multiple capture issues assigned to codex Sessions from 2026-08-22. br coordination status classifies these claims as no_mail_snapshot with stale/abandoned ages, but the ordinary backlog still shows only in_progress.

## Goal

Make in_progress work distinguish active ownership from stale or abandoned claims, and provide a safe reconciliation path that respects live claims.

## Acceptance

- Triage exposes stale/abandoned in_progress claims distinctly from live work.
- A maintainer can inspect the evidence and release or requeue an abandoned claim without overwriting a live holder.
- The default ready/next-work view does not imply that an old assignee is actively working.
- The workflow documents what evidence permits takeover and what remains protected.
- No automatic reassignment or claim deletion occurs solely because coordination evidence is missing.

## Not covered

Do not reclaim any current Agent's issue as part of this task; first establish the detection and operator-confirmation behavior.
close_reason: Established snapshot-backed stale-claim reconciliation in AGENTS.md: only abandoned_likely plus reclaim_allowed_by_policy permits takeover; uncertain/live classifications remain protected; maintainer requeue followed by atomic claim prevents direct reassignment. Verified with disposable Beads transitions and all 751 mini.test cases; stylua, lua-language-server, API appendix, diff check, and dependency-cycle check passed. Related CLI defect louiselm-8elc.1 remains open and does not block the documented operator path.

comments.author: codex/01a0517b-2081-7ff1-b37d-9d03860da2aa
comments.text:
Implementation and lesson routing (2026-08-30):

The existing br 0.5.2 surfaces already satisfy the detection/default-view halves of this task: `br coordination status` distinctly reports fresh, no_mail_snapshot, active-reservation, stale-candidate, and abandoned-likely evidence; `br ready` and `br scheduler` exclude assigned in_progress work. The missing project contract was the operator boundary. AGENTS.md now requires supplied Agent Mail snapshots, permits takeover only for `classification=abandoned_likely` plus `reclaim_allowed_by_policy=true`, explicitly protects no_mail_snapshot/ambiguous/fresh/active-reservation claims regardless of age, and documents audit comment -> maintainer requeue -> atomic Agent claim. A disposable Beads workspace proved requeue clears status/assignee and a subsequent `--claim` succeeds while a competing claim refuses with VALIDATION_FAILED.

No existing stale project claim was released or reassigned. Documentation-only change, so no artificial red test was added. title: Coordination reclaim command rejects retained stale assignee
description:
`br coordination status` can mark a retained `in_progress` claim reclaimable and emit a suggested direct `br update --claim`, but following that command fails because the old assignee remains set. Operators therefore cannot follow the machine-generated reconciliation path without discovering an undocumented requeue step.

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed 2026-08-30 with `br version 0.5.2 (release) (main@8d5af3a)` while implementing louiselm-8elc.

In a disposable Beads workspace:

```text
$ br update test-fwc --claim --actor codex/new-session --json
[{"id":"test-fwc","status":"in_progress","assignee":"codex/new-session"}]

$ br update test-fwc --claim --actor codex/other-live-session --json
{"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_FAILED","message":"Validation failed: claim: issue test-fwc already assigned to codex/new-session","context":{"field":"claim","reason":"issue test-fwc already assigned to codex/new-session"}}}
```

The same refusal applies to an abandoned claim because classification is advisory and does not clear its assignee. `beads_rust/src/coordination.rs:657-675` nevertheless emits `br update '<id>' --claim --json` as `claim_issue` whenever policy allows reclaim.

## Symptoms

- A maintainer follows `suggested_commands` and cannot reclaim the classified issue.
- The CLI reports that the retained, abandoned assignee already owns it.

## Root cause

`reclaim_suggested_commands` in `/home/lotso/code/beads_rust/src/coordination.rs:657-675` recommends an ordinary atomic claim. The claim operation correctly refuses any already-assigned issue, and coordination classification is read-only, so the recommendation omits the required assignee-clearing/requeue transition.

## Why it was not caught

`/home/lotso/code/beads_rust/tests/e2e_coordination.rs:270-323` asserts only that the suggested string contains `br update`; it never executes the emitted sequence against the retained stale assignee.

## Fix direction

Make the generated reconciliation sequence executable end to end while preserving live-claim safety. The narrow fix may be an explicit audited requeue command before atomic claim, or a dedicated guarded reconciliation operation bound to the reviewed coordination evidence. Do not weaken ordinary `--claim` refusal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An end-to-end test creates an assigned stale claim, supplies snapshot evidence that produces `abandoned_likely` and `reclaim_allowed_by_policy=true`, executes the generated reconciliation sequence, and successfully transfers ownership.
- The same path refuses `fresh`, `blocked_by_active_reservation`, `ambiguous`, and `no_mail_snapshot` claims.
- Ordinary `br update --claim` still refuses to overwrite an assigned live holder.

## Not covered

LouiseLM documents the currently working operator workaround in AGENTS.md under louiselm-8elc. This bug does not reclaim any existing project issue or define how Agent Mail snapshots are collected.

title: Standalone proposal acceptance loses Session focus
description:
Accepting a proposal-only diff applies the file correctly and closes the review, but does not return focus to the Session buffer that opened it. The user must run :LouiselmSwitchSessions manually.

## Observed

Reported during live retest on 2026-08-24 after eb02204. The target file was modified correctly; focus did not return, and the user recovered through the <leader>ls mapping for :LouiselmSwitchSessions.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/diff/buffer.lua captures no origin buffer. Its standalone a/d/q mappings call M.close, which only deletes the review buffer. The ACP controller in lua/louiselm/ui/diff/init.lua already owns the correct pattern: capture previous_buffer before opening, close the review, then restore it when still valid.

## Why it was not caught

The standalone mapping tests assert file contents and review-buffer disposal but never assert the current buffer after a decision. Only the ACP controller has focus-restoration coverage.

## Fix direction

Capture the current buffer before focusing the standalone review and restore it after successful accept or discard. Keep stale-apply failures in the review. Avoid changing ACP controller behavior.

## Acceptance

- A standalone a applies the proposal, closes the review, and returns to the originating buffer.
- Standalone d and q discard, close, and return to the originating buffer.
- A stale a keeps the review focused and open.
- Existing ACP permission review behavior remains green.

## Not covered

The accepted AGENTS.md proposal is user work and must remain untouched.
close_reason: Fixed in the working tree. Standalone reviews capture the originating buffer and restore it after successful accept or discard; stale acceptance remains focused. Red: focused diff suite failed with Neovim selecting distractor buffers. Green: focused 14/14 and full mini.test 477/477. Gates: stylua --check ., lua-language-server at Warning, and git diff --check all passed.

title: Session stuck in "Starting" forever when the agent process hangs before the ACP handshake
description:
A session stuck in "starting" because its ACP transport process never exits
and never completes the `initialize` handshake hangs the winbar on "Starting"
forever, with no error, no timeout, and no way for the user to tell the
session is dead rather than slow.

## Observed

Live repro on 2026-08-30, agent config from ~/dotfiles' louiselm.lua:
`agents.opencode = { command = "acp-proxy", args = { "--", "opencode", "acp" } }`.

Real-world trigger: opencode CLI's npm postinstall script hadn't run, so
`opencode acp` exited immediately (exit 1, stderr message) without ever
speaking ACP. Selecting the opencode agent in Neovim left the winbar reading
"Starting" indefinitely with no error surfaced.

Synthetic repro isolating the mechanism (bypassing the opencode-specific
cause): wrapped a script that immediately fails with acp-proxy, the same way
louiselm does:

```
$ cat /tmp/fake-broken-agent.sh
#!/bin/sh
echo "Error: fake broken agent, postinstall never ran" >&2
exit 1

$ timeout 5 acp-proxy -- /tmp/fake-broken-agent.sh
Error: fake broken agent, postinstall never ran
# process is still running after the 5s timeout elapses; `timeout`'s SIGTERM
# has no effect. Confirmed via `ps aux`: the acp-proxy process (pid 433857)
# is still alive well after its wrapped child exited. Had to `kill -9` it.
```

`acp-proxy` (0.7.3, from ~/code/acp-llm-adapter) forwards the wrapped child's
stderr but does not exit or otherwise signal failure when that child dies
before the handshake completes — that is a separate defect, tracked in the
acp-llm-adapter repo, not here.

## Symptoms

- User sees the winbar's turn label stuck on "Starting" (rendered by
  `turn_label` at lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:552-554 for
  `status == "starting"`) with no further change, ever.
- No error, no timeout message, nothing in the chat transcript.
- Nothing distinguishes "the agent process is slow to start" from "the agent
  process (or a proxy wrapping it) is permanently hung."

## Root cause

louiselm.nvim's own on_exit wiring is correct and not the bug: `Session:start`
(lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:660-676) passes `on_exit` through to
`Acp.connect`, which reaches `lua/louiselm/acp/transport.lua:112-125`'s
`on_exit`, which calls back into `handle_exit`
(lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:475-484), which calls `fail(...)` and
correctly flips `status` to `"error"` — *when the spawned process actually
exits*.

The gap is that nothing in the session lifecycle ever times out or health-checks
a session sitting in `"starting"`/`"configuring"` status. `vim.system`'s
on_exit callback is the *only* signal path out of "starting" besides a
successful `initialize` response
(`handle_initialized`, lifecycle.lua:489 onward). If the spawned process (here,
`acp-proxy` wrapping a dead child) never exits and never sends a handshake
response, there is no other exit condition — the session, and the winbar,
hang forever.

## Why it was not caught

No existing test exercises a spawned process that neither completes the ACP
handshake nor exits. The test suite's mock ACP agent (per AGENTS.md's testing
section) presumably always exits or always completes the handshake in its
fixtures — a permanently-silent, permanently-alive child was never modeled.

## Fix direction

Add a bounded startup timeout (e.g. via `vim.defer_fn` scheduled at
`Session:start()` and cancelled on `handle_initialized`/`handle_exit`) that
calls `fail(self, "agent did not respond within Ns of starting")` if the
session is still in `"starting"`/`"configuring"` when it fires. Options
rejected: relying solely on downstream proxies (acp-proxy, acp-llm-adapter) to
self-terminate correctly is not sufficient — louiselm spawns an arbitrary
user-configured command and cannot assume every wrapper behaves; a client-side
timeout is the only boundary louiselm fully controls.

## Acceptance

- A regression test that starts a session against a transport double which
  never calls its stdout/on_exit callbacks, and asserts the session
  transitions to `"error"` after the timeout rather than staying in
  `"starting"` indefinitely.
- Live: selecting an agent whose process hangs pre-handshake surfaces a
  timeout error in the transcript and updates the winbar, instead of leaving
  "Starting" displayed forever.

## Not covered

- The acp-proxy defect itself (not exiting/propagating when its wrapped child
  process dies) — tracked separately in ~/code/acp-llm-adapter's beads
  tracker, not here.
- Whether a configurable timeout duration is needed vs. a fixed default —
  left to implementation.
close_reason:
Fixed. Added a bounded startup timeout to Session:start() (lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua):
after the ACP initialize request is sent, schedules a timer via a new testable
`self.schedule` boundary (defaults to vim.defer_fn, same pattern as
workflow/run.lua's `schedule` option). If the session is still "starting" when
the timer fires, it calls fail() with "agent did not respond within Nms of
starting" instead of hanging forever. Timeout defaults to
DEFAULT_START_TIMEOUT_MS = 20000, configurable per-session via the new
`start_timeout_ms` session option (validated and plumbed through
lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua's closed option schema).

Root cause confirmed as filed: acp-proxy (external dependency, tracked in
acp-llm-adapter as daa-yrsj, since fixed and rebuilt by the maintainer) never
exited when its wrapped child died pre-handshake, so louiselm's on_exit-based
detection never fired. This fix makes louiselm's own session lifecycle
self-bounding regardless of how a spawned process or proxy misbehaves,
matching the filed fix direction (a client-side timeout is the only boundary
louiselm fully controls).

Tests added in tests/session/api_spec.lua ("new" set):
- "fails a session that never completes the ACP handshake after the start
  timeout" - injects a captured schedule callback, fires it, asserts status
  transitions "starting" -> "error" with the expected message and that
  ready_callback receives the error.
- "ignores a stale start timeout after the Session becomes ready" - confirms
  the guard (status ~= "starting") prevents a late timer from clobbering an
  already-ready session.
- "honors a custom start_timeout_ms option" - asserts the configured value is
  what gets scheduled.
- "rejects a negative start_timeout_ms session option" - registry-level
  validation.

Gates: full mini.test suite (all files) - 0 fails, 0 notes.
`stylua --check` - clean. `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning`
- no problems found. `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` - regenerated
doc/api.md for the new public LuaCATS fields (schedule, start_timeout_ms,
stderr_buffer) and verified clean afterward.

Deviation: implementation was written before the regression tests rather than
strict red-green-refactor (tests were added and verified to exercise the new
code paths afterward, not proven red against pre-fix code first). Full test
suite is green and the new tests are behavioral (they'd fail against the
prior always-schedule-nothing behavior), but this is a self-report rather than
witnessed red-before-green.

title: myst build --html fails with ECONNREFUSED to its own localhost:3000 prerender server under Docker bridge networking
description:
`myst build --html --strict` (the exact command the new `.gitlab-ci.yml` pages job runs, on the exact `node:24-bookworm` image it pins) fails deterministically inside a plain `docker run` container using Docker's default bridge network, but succeeds on a bare host and succeeds inside the same container under `--network host`. This is an open risk for the real GitLab CI pipeline (louiselm-zce), unconfirmed because this sandbox has no live GitLab Runner to test against.

## Observed

Session: CI setup work for louiselm-zce (GitLab CI build+deploy of blog/ to GitLab Pages), 2026-08-18, in /home/lotso/code/louiselm sandbox with Docker 29.6.2 (overlayfs, cgroup v2, kernel 7.0.13+deb13-amd64).

Three reproductions of the identical command sequence `npm install -g mystmd@1.10.1 && cd blog && myst build --html --strict`:

1. Bare host, asdf-managed Node v24.16.0, no container: exit 0, `blog/_build/html/index.html` produced with real content. Ran twice, succeeded both times.
2. `docker run --rm -v <repo>:/repo -w /repo --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" node:24-bookworm bash -c '...'` with Docker's default bridge network (`docker network inspect bridge` shows `"EnableIPv6": false`, subnet `172.17.0.0/16`): exit 1, 3/3 runs. Build log (identical each time):
   ```
   🔌 Server started on port 3000!  🥳 🎉
   	👉  http://localhost:3000  👈
   Fetch of http://localhost:3000 threw an error (Attempt #1) FetchError: request to http://localhost:3000/ failed, reason: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000
   ... (repeats for /post-example/blog, /index.json, /post-example.blog.json, /robots.txt)
   Fetch of http://localhost:3000 threw an error (Attempt #2) ...
   Fetch of http://localhost:3000 threw an error (Attempt #3) ...
   Failed to fetch http://localhost:3000 after 3 attempts.
   Myst CLI Versions:
    - node                        24.19.0     Required: >= 18.0.0
    - npm                         11.17.0     Required: >=8.6.0
    - myst                         1.10.1
   ```
3. Same container/command but `docker run --network host ...`: exit 0, 1/1 run, full successful build log with `GET / 200`, `GET /post-example/blog 200`, etc.

Root cause is unknown — not simple loopback breakage: a minimal manual repro in the same bridge-mode container (`node -e "http.createServer(...).listen(4000, () => fetch('http://localhost:4000/'))"`) succeeded fine, both with default `::` bind and explicit `127.0.0.1` bind. So the failure is specific to mystmd's book-theme dev-server startup path under bridge networking, not a blanket "loopback fetch doesn't work" issue.

## Symptoms

- What a CI job running this exact command inside a Docker-executor container with default (bridge) networking might see: the `myst build --html --strict` step fails with exit 1 and the pipeline job goes red, even though nothing about the blog content is broken.
- Error text: `FetchError: request to http://localhost:3000/ failed, reason: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000`, followed by `Failed to fetch http://localhost:3000 after 3 attempts.`

## Root cause

Unknown. Hypotheses, not yet discriminated:

1. Docker bridge-mode NAT/userland-proxy hairpin latency delays the container's own published port becoming reachable via `localhost`, and mystmd's book-theme prerender step's 3 retries (short interval, not measured) aren't enough margin under that added latency — would be a timing/robustness gap in mystmd's book-theme server startup (fixed asynchronously logs "started" possibly before actually ready to accept), not a hard capability gap.
2. Something specific to this sandboxed/nested-Docker environment's bridge network implementation (this sandbox is itself a constrained/virtualized environment) that would NOT reproduce on a normal cloud VM running a normal GitLab Docker-executor runner.

Nothing in this investigation distinguishes between these two. A real GitLab Runner is required to know which applies.

## Why it was not caught

There is no automated CI yet (this bug was found while building the very first `.gitlab-ci.yml` for this repo) and no live GitLab Runner reachable from this sandbox, so the only verification possible was local reproduction of the exact command/image, which surfaced this discrepancy but can't confirm whether it will recur on the real runner.

## Fix direction

Do not speculatively patch `.gitlab-ci.yml` for this (e.g. forcing host networking isn't controllable from `.gitlab-ci.yml` — it's a GitLab Runner `config.toml` `[runners.docker] network_mode` setting, out of this repo's control). Instead:

1. Watch the first real pipeline run of the `pages` job (in `.gitlab-ci.yml`, already carries an inline comment flagging this) for the exact `ECONNREFUSED ... :3000` signature during the `myst build` step.
2. If it recurs on the real runner: escalate to whoever administers the GitLab Runner to check/change the Docker executor's `network_mode`, or file upstream against `jupyter-book/mystmd` (book-theme prerender retry/backoff robustness).
3. If it does NOT recur: close this as sandbox-environment-specific and not a real risk.

## Acceptance

- A real GitLab CI pipeline run of the `pages` job in `.gitlab-ci.yml` either succeeds (closes this as sandbox-specific noise) or reproduces the same `ECONNREFUSED :3000` signature (confirms the risk and triggers the escalation above).

## Not covered

- Whether GitLab.com shared runners vs. this project's actual self-hosted `gitlab.bartab.fr` runner(s) would behave differently — runner topology for `gitlab.bartab.fr` is unknown from this sandbox.
- Whether pinning a different Node major (e.g. `node:20-bookworm`, `node:22-bookworm`) avoids the issue — not tested; the discrepancy was isolated to bridge-vs-host Docker networking, not Node version, so this seems unlikely to matter but wasn't ruled out.
close_reason: Confirmed on real gitlab.bartab.fr pipeline #38205: HOST=127.0.0.1 CI variable fixes the ECONNREFUSED. Root cause was mystmd's dev server binding to hostname 'localhost' racing IPv4/IPv6 resolution under Docker bridge networking.

comments.author: 3869f178-9bdd-4a0f-981c-2b01567e1e60
comments.text:
Confirmed on the real gitlab.bartab.fr runner: identical ECONNREFUSED signature on 4/4 pipeline runs (2026-08-19 through 2026-08-22, pipelines #37950/#37998/#38076/#38120), so this is real, not sandbox-specific.

Root cause pinned down: mystmd's book-theme dev server (myst-cli/dist/build/site/start.js) binds via `app.listen(port, host)` with `DEFAULT_HOST='localhost'` (a hostname, not an IP). Under this runner's Docker bridge network (IPv6 disabled per the original bead's `docker network inspect`), resolving `localhost` races IPv4/IPv6 and the self-fetch prerender step hits ECONNREFUSED on the unreachable family before its 3-attempt/exponential-backoff retry (`fetchWithRetry`, ~750ms total budget) gives up. Confirmed via mystmd's own escape hatch: it already special-cases this exact failure for ReadTheDocs by forcing `HOST=127.0.0.1` (`warnOnHostEnvironmentVariable` in myst-cli). Setting `HOST=127.0.0.1` as a CI variable reproduced success 3/3 times locally in the same bridge-mode `docker run node:24-bookworm` setup that previously failed 3/3.

Fix applied: added `variables: HOST: "127.0.0.1"` to the `pages` job in `.gitlab-ci.yml`. No runner infra change needed (network_mode stays default bridge, group-wide runner untouched) — chosen over changing the runner's network_mode specifically, to keep blast radius to this one job.

Next: watch the next real pipeline run (triggered by this commit) to confirm the fix holds under the actual runner, then close.

comments.author: 3869f178-9bdd-4a0f-981c-2b01567e1e60
comments.text: Confirmed fixed: pipeline #38205 (triggered by commit 60f1e0f) passed with the HOST=127.0.0.1 CI variable in place. Closing.
