title: Collect Session Forensics for Agent and human diagnosis
description:
## Problem Statement

When LouiseLM is used to diagnose a faulty LouiseLM Session, an Agent currently has to rediscover where the useful evidence lives. Raw ACP logs are repeatedly valuable and Agent-friendly, but ad hoc discovery loses provenance and encourages either overly broad filesystem searches or unsafe attempts to package and sanitize arbitrary content. Humans also need a readable intervention surface without making a rendered UI the canonical artifact.

## Solution

Add explicit Session Forensics: read-only collection of a small, immutable, private, versioned JSON record anchored to exactly one subject Session, identified by Agent plus ACP Session ID. The record stores bounded typed observations and pointers to primary evidence in place. It is the canonical Agent-facing representation; an optional Neovim view renders a human-facing projection from the same record.

Selecting a subject Session for diagnosis authorizes the diagnosing Agent to inspect that Session's raw ACP log as ordinary evidence. Metadata and pointers make evidence discoverable but do not replace primary evidence. Unrelated Sessions remain outside the boundary, and export or sharing outside the diagnosing Session remains a separate future consent boundary.

## User Stories

1. As an Agent diagnosing LouiseLM, I want one structured record that identifies a subject Session and its evidence sources so I can begin analysis without rediscovering filesystem conventions.
2. As a user diagnosing Session A from Session B, I want the relationship recorded and the Forensics record queued into Session B's next prompt so the Agent can inspect Session A without collecting unrelated Sessions.
3. As a user whose chat UI is broken, I want collection available through the headless Session API and an Ex command outside chat so diagnostics do not depend on the failing UI.
4. As a human intervening in diagnosis, I want an optional readable projection of the same canonical record so I can understand identity, chronology, missing evidence, and sensitive sources without reading compact JSON.
5. As a security-conscious user, I want collection to leave logs, transcripts, and worktrees untouched and never claim arbitrary raw evidence is sanitized or safe to share.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a valid Agent and ACP Session ID, explicit collection asynchronously creates one new canonical JSON record under a private `stdpath("state")/louiselm/forensics` directory and reports its path through the caller's completion boundary.
2. Every record has a schema version, unique identity, observation timestamp, exactly one subject containing Agent plus ACP Session ID, and optional diagnosing-Session provenance.
3. The record contains only a fixed typed allowlist: Agent-reported name/version, known normalized capability flags, selected ACP option IDs and current string/boolean values, cwd, Neovim/LouiseLM versions, Git commit/branch and a bounded dirty-filename inventory, and typed evidence-source entries.
4. Evidence sources use explicit metadata/known pointers only and record a typed state such as present, absent, inaccessible, unsupported, or omitted, plus bounded source facts and failure reasons. Collection never broadly scans the filesystem to guess locations.
5. Partial source failures still produce a usable record. Collection produces no record only when the subject cannot be identified validly or the record cannot be durably written.
6. Collection does not store raw log, transcript, prompt, tool-payload, file, diff, environment, Agent-definition, raw command-argument, raw capability-payload, or option-catalogue contents.
7. Collection never moves, renames, rewrites, truncates, deletes, normalizes, or cleans up source evidence. Live sources are marked mutable and observed-at rather than described as frozen.
8. A completed record is immutable. Re-collection creates another timestamped record, records have no automatic TTL, and referenced sources retain their independent retention policies.
9. When collection is invoked with an attached diagnosing chat, the canonical record is queued as an ACP `resource_link` for the next prompt without automatically sending a prompt or starting analysis. The selected subject Session's raw ACP log remains available for targeted Agent inspection without repeated consent prompts.
10. When invoked outside chat, the Ex-command adapter reports the created path through normal Neovim feedback. A headless adapter exposes the same outcome to scripts without requiring chat UI.
11. `:LouiselmForensics` defaults to the current Session or accepts Agent plus ACP Session ID. `:LouiselmForensicsView <record>` renders an optional human projection from the canonical JSON without persisting a second rendered copy.
12. The human projection clearly distinguishes subject and diagnosing Sessions, observation time, source availability/mutability/sensitivity, omissions/failures, and paths/actions; it does not display raw sensitive source contents by default.
13. Reproduction narratives, hypotheses, diagnoses, remediation, and fix verification are not written into the immutable record; a report or Beads item may reference its record ID separately.
14. Directory and record permissions are private by default, record fields with potentially unbounded cardinality or text are capped with total/truncation metadata, and no runtime or test dependency is added.

## Implementation Notes

- Keep the domain named `forensics`; do not reuse `workflow.evidence`, which owns routing-quality history.
- Put transformation, schema validation, rendering, and lifecycle rules outside UI and filesystem/process adapters.
- The core collection API must be asynchronous and must not use `vim.wait`, polling, or blocking process calls. Use `vim.system()` argument arrays for Git facts and marshal any editor work from fast-event callbacks onto the main loop.
- Reuse the existing headless Session API, validated Session state, ACP resource-link context path, and Agent/session metadata. Missing adapter metadata is an explicit `unsupported`/`absent` result, not permission to infer paths by scanning.
- Write records atomically with private permissions. Do not mutate an existing record after publication.
- Adapter-side ACP redaction is defense-in-depth only. The feature makes no safe-to-share claim.

## Testing Notes

- Develop observable behavior red-green-refactor through public APIs.
- Cover current-Session and explicit Agent/session targeting, no-chat/headless use, resource-link queuing without auto-submit, human rendering, immutable repeated collection, atomic/private persistence, bounded inventories, and every partial-source state.
- Prove source evidence is not mutated and unrelated Sessions are never inspected.
- Use the mock ACP agent and deterministic temporary repositories/files; no real Agent binaries, credentials, network, or user state.
- Async tests must model production callback/fast-event context and prove editor APIs run only after the scheduling boundary, including disposal and late callbacks.

## Out of Scope

- Copying evidence into a snapshot, manifest, bundle, or archive.
- Bug-report authoring, reproduction narrative, diagnosis, remediation, or fix-verification storage.
- Exporting, uploading, attaching, publishing, or otherwise sharing evidence outside the diagnosing Session.
- Sanitizing arbitrary ACP logs or claiming they are safe to share.
- Multi-Session or whole-workspace collection.
- Persisted Markdown/human-rendered duplicates.
- A record browser, automatic retention cleanup, or deletion UI.
- Changes to ACP adapter logging/redaction behavior, workflow routing evidence, commit/Beads/Session graph design, or worker-recovery artifacts.

title: Show account usage limits for configured Agents
description:
## Problem Statement

Humans cannot see shared account capacity while working through LouiseLM, so they may start or continue expensive work without knowing that an Agent is near a Provider limit, when capacity resets, or whether a failure is quota-related.

## Solution

Present normalized Agent-level account limits through a compact always-visible winbar summary and a read-only :LouiselmLimits [agent] detail view. Start with Codex, while keeping the state and UI contract Provider-neutral so a Claude adapter can supply equivalent data later.

## User Stories

1. As a user, I can glance at remaining capacity and reset timing before continuing work.
2. As a user, I can inspect all buckets, windows, plan and credit metadata for a configured Agent.
3. As a user, I receive deduplicated low, critical and reached notifications.
4. As a user, I can distinguish fresh, stale, unavailable, unsupported and empty limit states.
5. As a user, I can inspect known state for another Agent before deciding on a Handoff.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The winbar shows the default bucket with at most two exact-duration windows and +N overflow; urgent additional buckets take precedence.
2. :LouiselmLimits [agent] shows every deduplicated bucket/window with remaining and used capacity, relative and local reset timing, plan, credits and freshness.
3. Notifications fire at most once per reset cycle when remaining capacity crosses 20 percent, 10 percent and reached.
4. Sparse valid updates merge; malformed updates preserve the last good snapshot and mark it stale.
5. Missing, unsupported, empty, stale and explicit unlimited states remain distinct and never imply unconfirmed capacity.
6. Limits are shared per Agent rather than copied into Session telemetry, and notifications are deduplicated across Sessions.
7. The command does not start an Agent solely to fetch limits and performs no account or workflow mutation.

## Implementation Notes

- The accepted UX evidence and exact presentation decisions live on louiselm-u56l.
- The cross-process contract is blocked on louiselm-iexg because louiselm-ce6 requires a pure ACP client while current codex-acp does not emit structured limits.
- Use a structured typed boundary; never parse rendered /status text.
- Keep AX, automatic Agent selection/Handoff, reset-credit consumption, workspace-owner email and turn cancellation out of this feature.

## Testing Notes

- Test normalization and state transitions through public APIs.
- Cover multiple buckets, unlabeled buckets, arbitrary durations, fractional remaining capacity, sparse and malformed updates, reset expiry and notification deduplication.
- Exercise the real async scheduling boundary with a deterministic fake transport.
- Smoke-test the winbar, command view, completion and click behavior headlessly.

## Out of Scope

Agent-facing AX, automated switching, capacity prediction, per-Session attribution, credit consumption, owner notification, automatic cancellation and automatic Handoff.
close_reason: Delivered provider-neutral Agent account-limit state and complete Codex human UX.

Live acceptance exercised the committed source adapter and a real rolling update. The provider boundary is documented in codex-acp docs/account-limits-extension.md; human behavior is documented in README and the accepted design record louiselm-u56l. AX and automatic provider switching remain intentionally separate future work, so no AGENTS.md change is warranted here.

Such a helper must create no conversation Session, send no prompt, consume no model quota, perform no account mutation, sanitize failures, and terminate after the read. Copilot needs this because stock ACP does not expose account.getQuota while the official SDK does.

title: Encode empty object params correctly for ACP requests
description:
Live evidence: the account-limits ACP request returned JSON-RPC -32602 Invalid params, and the Codex App Server log contained no account/rateLimits/read request. In this Neovim, vim.json.encode({}) is [] while vim.json.encode(vim.empty_dict()) is {}. The extension parser requires an object.

Root scope: empty object-valued ACP request/notification parameters must be represented as JSON objects at call sites; empty arrays must remain representable.

title: Grill-me needed: How should reset-only Copilot quotas fit the account-limits extension?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; agree the versioned wire shape before implementing Copilot account limits.

Question:
How should a Provider quota that exposes used/entitled requests and a next-reset timestamp, but no exact window duration, fit the provider-neutral ACP account-limits extension without inventing data?

Context and evidence:
- Live LouiseLM inspection for Agent copilot reports status unsupported because stock copilot --acp does not advertise io.github.euri10.louiselm accountLimits.
- The configured Codex Agent uses the local /home/lotso/code/codex-acp build, whose adapter owns Provider parsing and emits the accepted v1 extension. Copilot is configured directly as copilot --acp --stdio, with no equivalent adapter.
- Installed GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.80 ships a typed headless SDK method account.getQuota.
- A read-only live call returned premium_interactions with entitlementRequests=1500, usedRequests=1500, remainingPercentage=0, and no overage. This proves the quota signal is available without parsing rendered /usage output or scraping the billing page.
- The same call returned resetDate=2026-08-26T06:41:26.790Z, effectively the query time, while the authenticated GitHub billing UI reportedly shows the quota resets in six days. The SDK reset timestamp therefore cannot yet be accepted as correct on this account.
- v1 requires every window to carry an exact positive windowDurationMins plus resetsAt. Copilot quota snapshots expose neither an exact duration nor a trustworthy reset timestamp in the observed result.
- LouiseLM can accept buckets with no windows and a credit balance, but that loses percentage/reset display and threshold alerts, so it does not satisfy the existing limits UX.
- The accepted pure-ACP boundary remains: an external Agent adapter normalizes Provider data and advertises the custom capability; LouiseLM must not learn Copilot internals, parse prose, scrape a webpage, expose credentials, or start a second Agent solely to fetch limits.

Threads worth pulling:
- Extend the wire contract so a quota period can omit exact duration while retaining used percentage and reset time, versus define a distinct reset-only quota shape.
- Whether the extension should become v2 or add a backward-compatible optional field under v1.
- How winbar labels, details, expiry and alert deduplication behave when duration is unknown.
- Which Copilot source supplies the authoritative next reset and how its semantics are verified against a captured live response without recording auth material.
- Whether a local copilot-acp bridge can reuse the already-authenticated Copilot runtime, or whether the capability must be implemented upstream in Copilot CLI to avoid a second process.
- Stable bucket IDs for chat, completions and premium_interactions, and how unlimited entitlements coexist with the metered premium bucket.

Decision boundary:
Choose the truthful normalized wire shape and runtime ownership. Do not implement a guessed monthly duration or trust the currently observed resetDate until live evidence establishes its meaning.
close_reason: Agreed and implemented an independent Copilot ACP wrapper using the existing exact-window v1 contract and a bounded read-only SDK quota helper.

comments.author: codex/01a03cbb-7210-7df1-a27c-1d47aac42eda
comments.text:
2026-08-26 focused design evidence:

Wire shape:
- Keep resetsAt required: LouiseLM uses it for freshness expiry and alert deduplication by reset cycle.
- Make windowDurationMins optional: Copilot can then truthfully report percentage plus next reset without inventing a fixed calendar-month duration.
- Existing Codex and Claude snapshots remain unchanged. This is an additive relaxation of the experimental v1 payload, so a v2 handshake adds no value in this early-stage/local ecosystem.
- UI behavior for an unknown-duration window can omit the duration label and render only remaining capacity plus reset timing. Detail omits the Window line. Alert identity uses bucket plus resetsAt, with a fixed unknown-duration marker.
- Do not make resetsAt optional in the same change; doing so would require a new cycle identity and different expiry/alert semantics not raised by the observed Provider shape.

Runtime evidence:
- A sanitized probe sent initialize followed by account.getQuota to stock Copilot CLI 1.0.80 in ACP mode. Copilot returned JSON-RPC -32601 Method not found.
- The public structured headless SDK does expose account.getQuota, but starting CopilotClient launches a separate headless Copilot runtime.
- Official Copilot CLI extensions run as separate Node processes connected to the existing Session, but their documented public surface adds tools and slash commands. It does not extend the ACP server. Reaching global account.getQuota from an extension and carrying it to an ACP wrapper would require private SDK connection access plus a custom side channel.
- Therefore there are three runtime postures: require an upstream/same-process Copilot ACP capability (clean, unavailable now); build an experimental private-SDK extension plus proxy/socket (works in principle, high fragility); or allow a proxy to launch a second headless Copilot runtime for quota reads (smallest working local bridge, but contradicts louiselm-ce6.25 acceptance criterion 7).

Recommended posture:
Adopt the optional-duration v1 shape, then require a supported same-process Copilot surface rather than building a private experimental bridge. File the Copilot adapter task with needs-capability:copilot-acp-account-limits until Copilot ACP or its extension SDK exposes a supported control-plane method.

comments.author: codex/01a03cbb-7210-7df1-a27c-1d47aac42eda
comments.text:
Maintainer preference was a local Copilot ACP fork analogous to the Codex and Claude source adapters. Upstream verification found that this route is unavailable:

- npm metadata for @github/copilot 1.0.80 points to https://github.com/github/copilot-cli.
- Cloned upstream HEAD 65006ce into /home/lotso/code/copilot-cli.
- The repository contains only README.md, changelog.md, install.sh and LICENSE.md; it has no Copilot CLI or ACP implementation source.
- The npm package files are only npm-loader.js and README.md; the loader downloads the platform binary.
- LICENSE.md section 3 explicitly does not grant the right to modify, adapt, translate, or create derivative works of the Software.

Therefore do not patch or reverse-engineer the Copilot binary and do not describe github/copilot-cli as a source fork. The closest viable local architecture is a separately licensed ACP wrapper that launches the unmodified upstream binary, or an upstream feature request/change implemented by GitHub. A wrapper still needs a supported structured quota source; stock ACP rejects account.getQuota, while a second SDK runtime violates the accepted no-extra-Agent constraint and a same-runtime experimental extension currently requires private SDK access.

comments.author: codex/01a03cbb-7210-7df1-a27c-1d47aac42eda
comments.text:
Decision accepted and implemented:

- Keep version 1 and its exact windowDurationMins plus resetsAt contract unchanged.
- GitHub documents legacy premium-request counters resetting on the first day of each month at 00:00:00 UTC. The Copilot adapter derives the exact UTC calendar-month duration and next reset from that Provider contract rather than trusting the observed incorrect SDK resetDate.
- Implement Copilot support in the independent local /home/lotso/code/copilot-acp repository. It delegates all ordinary ACP traffic to the unmodified copilot --acp --stdio binary, augments initialize capability metadata, and intercepts only the account-limits read method.
- A bounded read-only @github/copilot-sdk helper runtime is allowed for quota reads. It creates no conversation Session, sends no prompt, consumes no premium request, and always stops after the read.
- Do not modify, reverse-engineer, fork, or contact upstream Copilot as part of this work. /home/lotso/code/copilot-cli remains an untouched verification clone of the distribution-only repository.
- No LouiseLM, codex-acp, or claude-agent-acp source change is needed. The local dotfiles Copilot Agent now launches the wrapper through acp-proxy.

Evidence:
- Red tests first failed because the normalization/proxy modules did not exist.
- Final wrapper gates: 6 tests pass, Node syntax check passes, git diff check passes.
- Live wrapper smoke: initialize capability v1, limits read, and ordinary session/list delegation all pass.
- Live headless LouiseLM acceptance against the real wrapper reports Agent copilot status=fresh, premium_interactions bucket, used_percent=100, duration_mins=44640, resets_at=1788220800, reached_type=quota.
- LouiseLM gates: StyLua passes, LuaLS reports no diagnostics, all 547 MiniTest cases pass.
- Dotfiles LouiseLM config passes StyLua.

Lesson routing: the adapter-specific billing/reset rationale and bounded-helper behavior live in /home/lotso/code/copilot-acp/README.md. The revised helper allowance is recorded on louiselm-ce6.25. No AGENTS.md change is warranted.

title: Grill-me needed: What should :q do from LouiseLM detail buffers with live Sessions?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; decide the quit safety contract for every LouiseLM-owned buffer and Session lifecycle state.

Question:
What should ordinary :q do when the last Neovim window is showing LouiseLM-owned UI such as louiselm://limits/copilot while one or more LouiseLM Sessions remain alive?

Observed reproduction:
- In the maintainer's current resumed Copilot Session, :LouiselmLimits copilot opened a read-only buffer named louiselm://limits/copilot.
- The buffer is a nofile, bufhidden=wipe detail view created by lua/louiselm/ui/limits.lua:326-339.
- Pressing ordinary :q from that buffer closed the only window and exited Neovim while the Session remained alive. The maintainer had to resume the Session.
- The existing QuitPre guard in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:280-302 only runs Chat:should_block_quit().
- Chat:should_block_quit() in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2903-2922 requires the current buffer to be an attached chat buffer and more than one non-disposed Session. It therefore does not cover a limits detail buffer or the one-live-Session case.
- Prior art: louiselm-yk67 fixed accidental last-window :q with multiple attached chat Sessions, but its accepted contract explicitly allows normal quit with one Session, an ordinary buffer, or another window.

Threads worth pulling:
- Scope: protect every LouiseLM-owned buffer (chat, limits, diff, tool inspection, workflow/evidence views) or only detail buffers that hide a live Session?
- Meaning of alive: any non-disposed Session, only a Session with an active turn, or any attached Session even when idle?
- Action on :q from a LouiseLM detail buffer: block with an actionable warning; close the detail window and return to the owning chat buffer; or allow exit while persisting a resumable Session?
- Last window versus multiple windows: should the protection apply only when :q would terminate Neovim, or also prevent closing a LouiseLM detail split while another window remains?
- Force commands: preserve :qall! / :qa! as explicit escape hatches, and distinguish :q from editor shutdown/autocmd-driven exits.
- Ownership and lookup: how a louiselm:// buffer maps back to its Agent/Session, especially when several Sessions or Agents share one detail view.
- Tests: production QuitPre through a real Neovim command, one live Session from a limits buffer, multiple Sessions, ordinary buffer, another split, and explicit force quit.

Decision boundary:
Choose whether a live Session can ever be abandoned by ordinary :q from LouiseLM-owned UI, and the minimal recovery action. Do not implement a broader quit guard until this is settled.
close_reason: Resolved by grill-me on 2026-08-26. Session-scoped invariant on ExitPre/VimLeavePre with a three-clause refusal predicate; :qa as the free escape hatch; breadcrumb recovery because exit-time narration is impossible. Work filed as louiselm-ce6.34 and louiselm-ce6.35; vocabulary promoted as louiselm-cyb2 and louiselm-b79f.

comments.author: ef5f2ba3-8f5c-4322-9c60-c49dcd1e48a2
comments.text:
Resolved by grill-me session on 2026-08-26.

Decision: the invariant is session-scoped, not buffer-scoped. Three threads from this issue are dissolved rather than answered -- buffer scope, last-window-vs-splits, and buffer-to-Session ownership lookup -- because buffer identity is causally unrelated to the loss (`:b other_file` then `:q` abandons the same Session). Do not implement a louiselm:// namespace check; note also that diff buffers use a different scheme (louiselm-diff://), so any name-prefix guard would have missed them.

Mechanism: ExitPre refuses, VimLeavePre disposes and records. QuitPre stops being the anchor, superseding louiselm-yk67's accepted contract.

Two probe results drove the design and are recorded in full on louiselm-ce6.34:
1. The open-a-window escape blocks :q AND :q! but not :qa/:qa!/:wqa. So :qa is the escape hatch for free, and :q! is NOT one -- backwards from muscle memory, which is why the refusal message must name :qa.
2. Messages emitted at VimLeavePre are destroyed by the ^[[?1049l altscreen teardown that immediately follows. Narration at exit is impossible; the recovery action had to become a persisted breadcrumb surfaced at the next setup().

Rejected: blanket refusal on any live Session. It fires on every exit, forms the :qa reflex within a week, and then protects nothing -- its coverage is high-and-decaying, not high.

Also found while resolving this, and folded into ce6.34 rather than filed separately: the existing guard's first line is 'if chat == nil or not chat:should_block_quit()' (ui/chat/command.lua:280-284), so a Session created through the headless API with no chat buffer exits entirely unguarded today.

Vocabulary promoted: Abandonment (louiselm-cyb2), Staged context (louiselm-b79f).

title: Grill-me needed: Should LouiseLM ship global default keymaps?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; use it to frame a focused design discussion.

Question: Should the global <leader>l* mappings currently living in the maintainer's dotfiles become LouiseLM defaults, and if so how should collisions, disabling, and overrides work?

Evidence: /home/lotso/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua defines global normal/visual maps for chat, sessions, inbox, export, cancel, options, permissions, skills, file/buffer mentions, and inline edit. LouiseLM already installs <leader>lB as a buffer-local mapping in its Chat UI, which works without dotfile config. The plugin also owns other buffer-local UI mappings.

Threads: global defaults versus personal leader/collision policy; buffer-local versus global scope; whether setup should own installation and teardown; explicit disable/override schema; documentation and regression coverage.

title: Session-scoped quit guard: refuse ExitPre when a live Session would be lost
description:
## Goal

Ordinary `:q` must not silently abandon a live Session whose loss is unrecoverable; when exit does proceed, LouiseLM disposes cleanly and leaves a breadcrumb that reaches the maintainer at the next session.

Resolves the design question in louiselm-ce6.28. See that issue for the full grill-me record and the rejected alternatives.

## Decided contract

The invariant is session-scoped, not buffer-scoped: *Neovim must not exit silently while a Session would be lost*. Buffer identity is causally unrelated to the loss -- `:b other_file` then `:q` abandons the same Session. This dissolves three threads from ce6.28 outright (buffer scope, last-window-vs-splits, buffer-to-Session ownership lookup); do not implement a `louiselm://` namespace check.

**Mechanism.** `ExitPre` refuses; `VimLeavePre` disposes and records.

- `ExitPre` fires only when the quit actually ends Nvim, and is the documented place to "close any non-essential window" (nvim 0.12.5 `doc/autocmd.txt:640`). `QuitPre` explicitly cannot distinguish exit from closing a window (`autocmd.txt:996`), so it stops being the anchor.
- `VimLeavePre` cannot refuse -- `autocmd.txt:645` says to use it "for really exiting". It is the disposal hook only.

**Refusal predicate -- three clauses. Refuse only when exiting destroys something unrecoverable:**

1. the Agent does not advertise ACP `loadSession` (recorded at `lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:268`) -- the conversation is gone, not resumable;
2. a turn is in flight -- `session/load` replays history, not an interrupted turn;
3. the view holds Staged context (`contexts`, `pending_skill`, or `queued_prompt` on `louiselm.ui.ChatView`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:40-56`).

**Accepted residual:** recoverable + idle + nothing staged exits freely, costing a `session/load` replay and nothing else. Blanket refusal on any live Session was considered and rejected: it fires on every exit, forms the `:qa` reflex within a week, and then protects nothing. Its coverage is high-and-decaying, not high.

**Escape hatch -- `:qa` / `:qa!` / `:wqa`, free by construction.**

Probed on nvim 0.12.5 with an `ExitPre` autocmd that opens a split (the yk67 technique), each run under `timeout 3`:

```
:q    exit=124  -> still running at 3s -> BLOCKED
:q!   exit=124  -> still running at 3s -> BLOCKED
:qa   exit=0    -> exited              -> NOT blocked
:qa!  exit=0    -> exited              -> NOT blocked
:wqa  exit=0    -> exited              -> NOT blocked
```

`ExitPre` fired in all five cases. The trick defeats the `:q` family because `:q` closes the current window and the spare gives it something to close; it is self-cleaning (net zero window change). `:qa`/`:wqa` close all windows regardless, so the trick cannot touch them.

`:q!` is therefore **not** an escape and is refused identically to `:q`, which is backwards from muscle memory. The refusal message must name `:qa` explicitly or the guard is a trap. Shape:

```
louiselm: 2 live sessions (claude: turn in flight; copilot: 3 queued contexts). :qa to exit anyway.
```

Do **not** attempt to detect the bang. `vim.fn.histget(":", -1)` is inference, not information -- commands issued from mappings and `<cmd>q<cr>` keymaps never reach command-line history, so it silently mis-fires. Shadowing `:q` with a user command or `cnoreabbrev` is monkey-patching an editor builtin, ruled out by AGENTS.md section 10.

**Recovery -- breadcrumb, because narration at exit is impossible.**

Probed: messages emitted at `VimLeavePre` are drawn and then destroyed by the `^[[?1049l` alternate-screen teardown that immediately follows. `echomsg`, `nvim_echo`, and `io.stdout:write` all land in the doomed region. Moving the message earlier to `ExitPre` does not help; teardown still follows. Do not implement an exit-time notification.

Instead `VimLeavePre` writes `stdpath("state")/louiselm/abandoned.json`, surfaced once at the next `setup()` and cleared after surfacing. This path is already idiomatic here -- `permissions.json` (`permission/store.lua:442`), `usage.json` (`workflow/usage.lua:509`), `routing-evidence.json` (`ui/chat/command.lua:135`), `forensics/` (`session/registry.lua:187`).

The breadcrumb **must distinguish recoverable from lost**, or it lies: telling the maintainer to `:LouiselmResume` a Session whose Agent never advertised `loadSession` is worse than silence. Recovery itself already exists and is Agent-driven -- `:LouiselmResume` discovers prior Sessions through ACP `session/list` (`session/registry.lua:534`), not through anything LouiseLM persists. What is missing is only the prompt to use it.

The disposal-and-record path runs regardless of route: whether exit was reached via `:qa` past a refusal, or via the accepted residual.

## Placement

AGENTS.md section 8: core modules never notify, print, open UI, or choose presentation. The predicate straddles the boundary, so split it by ownership and compose at the UI edge:

- **Core** (`session/`) exposes a pure verdict -- live Sessions, each with `recoverable` and `turn_active`. No notify, no autocmd, no presentation.
- **UI/setup** registers `ExitPre`/`VimLeavePre`, contributes clause (iii) from the views it owns, and performs presentation: refusal message, window trick, breadcrumb write.

The registration must no longer bail on `chat == nil`. Today the guard's first line is `if chat == nil or not chat:should_block_quit()` (`ui/chat/command.lua:280-284`), so a Session created through the headless API with no chat buffer exits **entirely unguarded**. That is a hole under a session-scoped invariant, not a detail.

Rejected: a new top-level `quit.lua` reaching into both registry and Chat -- it inverts the layering by making a lifecycle module depend on the UI.

## Scope

- In scope: the `ExitPre` refusal, the three-clause predicate, the `VimLeavePre` disposal, `abandoned.json` and its one-shot surfacing at `setup()`, retirement of the `QuitPre` guard.
- Out of scope: persisting and restoring Staged context (separate slice; it retires clause (iii)). Any `louiselm://` buffer-namespace logic. Bang detection.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `:q` is refused when the only live Session's Agent lacks `loadSession` (clause i).
2. `:q` is refused when a turn is in flight (clause ii).
3. `:q` is refused when an idle, recoverable Session's view holds Staged context (clause iii).
4. `:q` proceeds when the live Session is recoverable, idle, and holds no Staged context.
5. `:q!` is refused identically to `:q` -- this guards the counterintuitive probe result and must be asserted, not assumed.
6. `:qa` exits despite all three clauses **and** writes the breadcrumb.
7. The guard fires for a Session created through the headless API with zero chat buffers.
8. `abandoned.json` distinguishes recoverable from lost Sessions, and is cleared after one surfacing.
9. The refusal message names `:qa` as the way out.
10. Live acceptance (AGENTS.md section 5): the maintainer confirms against the original reproduction -- `:LouiselmLimits copilot`, then `:q`, with a live Session.

## Testing

- Drive production `ExitPre` through a real `:q` Ex command, not a synthetic callback invocation. AGENTS.md section 5 treats a directly-called callback as insufficient coverage for this class.
- Core verdict function gets headless unit coverage with no Chat constructed at all -- that is what proves the layering split.
- louiselm-yk67's regression test describes a contract this change intentionally replaces. AGENTS.md section 5 permits displacing it on exactly that ground; record the obsolete behavior and the replacement contract when doing so, and port anything it covers that still holds.

## Notes

- Known gap, to be stated rather than papered over: `VimLeavePre` is not triggered when `v:dying >= 2` (`autocmd.txt:1348`), so a hard crash leaves no breadcrumb. `ExitPre` has the identical hole, so this is not a regression -- but it must be named in the handoff, not discovered later.
- Clause (i) trusts a capability advertisement. An Agent that advertises `loadSession` and then restores lossily is treated as safe, and the maintainer finds out at resume time. No predicate removes this; it is a priced residual, not an oversight.
- Vocabulary: this issue uses Abandonment (louiselm-cyb2) and Staged context (louiselm-b79f) as defined.
close_reason: Live acceptance passed across all reachable clauses; implemented in 32665fd

VimLeavePre writes a private atomic abandoned.json breadcrumb, disposes every registry, and setup consumes the breadcrumb once with :LouiselmResume guidance only for capability-advertised recoverable Sessions.

The louiselm-yk67 contract is intentionally obsolete: protection is no longer limited to multiple attached Sessions, the current chat buffer, or QuitPre. Its still-valid mechanism (a temporary split because autocmds cannot cancel quit) is preserved, and its synthetic callback regression is replaced by real Ex :q/:q! coverage plus child-Neovim :q/:qa exit coverage. comments.text:
Live acceptance PASSED. Manual QA round on 2026-08-27 at HEAD f44e0fd, maintainer at the keyboard, five cases against 32665fd. Evidence per case:

1. Breadcrumb consume-once. A real breadcrumb left by an earlier exit surfaced exactly once at startup as 'louiselm: previous exit ended 1 live Session; resume codex with :LouiselmResume' -- truthful recoverable classification, agent named, resume command named. A direct second call to surface_abandonment() returned false and re-notified nothing; the file was unlinked. A subsequent chatless exit wrote no breadcrumb.

2. Clause 2, turn in flight. Session deepseek/session-af10ba94-1b6f-4bb1-8829-12ef35c0187e: ':q' refused with 'louiselm: 1 live Session (deepseek: turn in flight). :qa to exit anyway.' winnr('$') was 1 afterwards with no visual disturbance, so the ExitPre temporary-split technique is net-zero and leaves no stray window.

3. Clause 3, Staged context. Session deepseek/session-9673cfd7-a022-474c-9fc0-2ce1d5d00d10 with two contexts staged: ':q' refused with '1 live Session (deepseek: 2 queued contexts)'. Session deepseek/session-5af6ecbd-af8c-4e75-8eea-9b810a31eb30 with one staged: ':q!' refused identically with '1 queued context'. Plural/singular agreement correct at both n=2 and n=1. The ':q!' leg is the trap-shaped one and it holds.

4. Accepted residual. Session deepseek/session-af10ba94 idle after its turn: ':q' exited immediately, no refusal. Breadcrumb confirms all three clauses false (recoverable=true, turn_active=false, staged.contexts=0). The blanket-refusal behaviour the design rejected did not appear.

5. ':qa' escape and trail. ':qa!' from an active clause-3 refusal exited immediately and VimLeavePre still recorded the loss: mode 0600, staged.contexts=2 matching the refusal message exactly.

Not reached live, by design: refusal clause 1 (Agent does not advertise ACP loadSession). Every agent exercised advertises it (recoverable=true in all breadcrumbs), so the clause is unreachable without an agent that lacks loadSession; tests/ui/command_spec.lua covers it together with the other two.

Raised but deliberately NOT filed: VimLeavePre writes a breadcrumb whenever a live Session exists, including the accepted-residual exit that loses nothing, so an ordinary clean quit produces a resume nag on the next start. Confirmed live (03:42 breadcrumb). This is the stated contract -- 'when exit does proceed, LouiseLM disposes cleanly and leaves a breadcrumb that reaches the maintainer at the next session' -- not a defect. Whether the nag is wanted is a product decision for the maintainer, left open rather than filed unilaterally.

Also observed: notifications are delivered through snacks.notifier in this configuration, which replaces vim.notify and writes nothing to :messages. Not a louiselm defect, but it made a first QA attempt read as total non-delivery. Anyone writing future live-acceptance steps for notification behaviour must name the notifier's own history, not :messages.

Claim note: the issue was assigned to codex/01a03df9-6992-71e2-9050-1d4dd466011c, whose claim was abandoned (751m, past the 480m threshold). No takeover was performed. The fix was already merged and the only outstanding item was maintainer live acceptance, which is not agent work; closing on that acceptance rather than on reclaim.

Routing: evidence to this comment. No AGENTS.md rule warranted. No new design question warranted -- the breadcrumb-on-clean-exit judgement is recorded above and belongs to the maintainer, not to a grill-me.

title: Persist and restore Staged context across restart, retiring quit-guard clause (iii)
description:
## Goal

Staged context survives Neovim exit and returns when the Session is resumed, so LouiseLM stops refusing to quit over state it could simply have persisted.

Depends on the quit guard slice, whose clause (iii) this retires.

## Why this exists

Clause (iii) of the quit guard refuses exit because Staged context (louiselm-b79f) -- queued `contexts`, a `pending_skill`, a `queued_prompt` on `louiselm.ui.ChatView` (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:40-56`) -- cannot survive a restart. ACP `session/load` replays the **Agent's** conversation history and has never seen any of it, so a Session being recoverable does not make it lossless.

That refusal is LouiseLM charging the maintainer for its own forgetfulness. If Staged context is durable, there is nothing to refuse: a guarantee replaces a warning, and the refusal predicate shrinks back to two clauses that are about the Agent rather than about LouiseLM's own limitations.

This is why the slice is structurally worth doing rather than merely nice: it **deletes** a clause instead of building around it, and the quit predicate converges on pure core state with no UI contribution -- see the placement section of the guard issue.

## Scope

- In scope: persisting Staged context keyed by ACP session id; restoring it into the view on resume, with per-item validation; removing clause (iii) from the quit predicate and the code that fed it; moving the predicate wholly into core once the UI no longer contributes to it.
- Out of scope: persisting transcript or Agent history (the Agent owns that, reached via `session/load`). Anything about the `ExitPre`/`VimLeavePre` mechanism itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Queued context items, a pending skill selection, and a queued prompt survive a full Neovim restart and are re-attached when that Session is resumed.
2. Persistence is keyed by ACP session id -- the same identity `session/load` takes -- so restore targets the right Session.
3. A staged item that no longer resolves at restore time (moved or deleted path, stale selection) is **dropped with a diagnostic**, never silently re-injected. Stale context reaching an Agent unannounced is the failure mode this must not have.
4. Clause (iii) is removed from the quit refusal predicate, and quitting with only Staged context outstanding no longer refuses.
5. With clause (iii) gone, the quit predicate is computed entirely from core session state; the UI contributes nothing to the verdict.
6. Live acceptance (AGENTS.md section 5): the maintainer stages context, exits, restarts, resumes, and confirms the staged material returns intact.

## Testing

- Round-trip coverage per staged kind: context item, pending skill, queued prompt.
- Restore-time validation: a persisted item whose path no longer exists is dropped and reported; assert the Agent never receives it.
- A regression asserting the quit guard no longer refuses on Staged context alone -- this is the point of the slice and must fail against the pre-change predicate.
- The core verdict function is exercised with no Chat constructed, proving the UI contribution is gone rather than merely unused.

## Notes

- Validate-then-drop matches how this project handles every other untrusted-at-boundary case (AGENTS.md section 9); do not deep-merge or coerce a stale item into something plausible.
- Do not persist Staged context for a Session whose Agent lacks `loadSession`. There is nothing to restore it onto, and writing it would imply a recovery that cannot happen.
- Vocabulary: Staged context (louiselm-b79f), Abandonment (louiselm-cyb2).
close_reason: Implemented ACP-session-keyed Staged persistence and restore, removed Staged from the quit predicate, passed 693 MiniTest cases and quality gates, and maintainer confirmed live restore.

title: Multi-line tool titles break the markdown export's <sub> caption and inject fake ## sections
description:
A tool call whose title contains newlines — every multi-line shell command — breaks the markdown export's structure. The `` caption is emitted as a single concatenated string, so a multi-line title splits it across the document: the element is left unclosed for up to 150 lines, and every intervening line is emitted as raw markdown body text. Where that text contains `##` headings, the export gains fabricated sections indistinguishable from its own. ## Observed Real export from session `cae87c06-bd44-429f-823e-6b18a361129f`, produced by `:LouiselmToMarkdown` on build `cd37ab2` during the QA round covering `ec19281..HEAD`, 2026-08-20: `/home/lotso/code/louiselm/louiselm-session-2-20260820-061038.md` (5543 lines, 680 KB, 120 tool calls). 12 of 120 `` captions span more than one line: ``` opened line 1262, closed line 1348 (span 87) opened line 2208, closed line 2352 (span 145) opened line 2825, closed line 2974 (span 150) opened line 3197, closed line 3208 (span 12) opened line 3698, closed line 3722 (span 25) opened line 5271, closed line 5407 (span 137) ... 6 more ``` Headings present in the export, counted by text: ``` 120 ## Tool <- real 41 ## Assistant <- real 14 ## User <- real 4 ## Observed <- fabricated 4 ## Symptoms <- fabricated 4 ## Root cause <- fabricated 4 ## Why it was not caught <- fabricated 4 ## Fix direction <- fabricated 4 ## Acceptance <- fabricated 4 ## Not covered <- fabricated ``` 28 fabricated `##` sections, all leaked out of `br create ... --description "$DESCRIPTION"` calls whose heredoc body became part of the tool title. A concrete block, at line 4434: ``` **ACTOR="${BR_ACTOR:-assistant}"; br comment add louiselm-euj --actor ... <- blank line, inside the element That is now two consecutive rounds finding it present and deliberately ... <- blank line
``` The `` opens on 4434 and closes on 4436, with document-level markdown in between. ## Symptoms - Rendered exports show a broken caption followed by loose body text where a one-line tool label was intended. - The document outline gains sections that were never in the conversation. - Any consumer that splits the export on `^## ` — which the format explicitly invites — mis-sections the document. ## Root cause `lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua:182-185`: ```lua "**" .. tostring(title) .. "** — " .. status .. "", ``` This is one element of the returned lines table, but `title` comes from `raw.title`, which for a Bash tool call is the literal command string and may contain newlines. `Chat:to_markdown` then runs the joined text through `split_lines`, so every embedded newline becomes a real line break inside what was supposed to be a single-line element. Nothing normalizes or escapes the title. `status` has the same exposure, though no observed payload puts a newline there. Not introduced by `14dbab6`, and that matters for triage: the previous format (`"## Tool: " .. title .. " (" .. status .. ")"`) had the identical flaw and would split the heading itself. `14dbab6` changed the shape of the breakage — an unclosed inline HTML element rather than a broken heading — and made the leaked text more prominent by collapsing the payload it sits next to. The bug is older than the commit the QA round was testing. ## Why it was not caught Every title in `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` and `tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` is a short single-line literal ("Run tests", "tool-9"). The specs assert the caption's exact text with `markdown:find("**Run tests** — completed", 1, true)`, which is a substring search — it cannot notice that the surrounding element is unclosed, and it never sees a title that could break it. The fixtures were invented rather than captured, and the invented ones are all well-behaved. A single fixture carrying an embedded `\n` would have failed immediately. ## Fix direction Normalize the title (and status) before interpolation, in `render_entry`: collapse any run of whitespace containing a newline to a single space, so the caption is one line by construction. Truncation with an ellipsis past some width is worth considering alongside it — a 150-line shell command is not a useful caption at any length — but that is a separate judgement about presentation, and the correctness fix should not wait on it. Rejected: escaping newlines as `
`. It keeps the element well-formed but preserves a 150-line caption, which is not the intent of a `` label, and it puts raw HTML into a field that is already being interpolated into HTML. Rejected: moving the title inside the `
` payload. That discards the collapsed-block affordance `14dbab6` was added to provide. ## Acceptance - A regression test with a tool title containing `\n` (and ideally a `##` line, matching the real payload that exposed this) asserting the rendered caption occupies exactly one line and the export's `^## ` count equals the number of real blocks. - Re-exporting the session above yields 120 `## Tool`, 41 `## Assistant`, 14 `## User` and no other `##` headings. ## Not covered - Whether any other field interpolated into a single-line construct has the same exposure has not been audited; `status` is the obvious sibling. - The effect on the blog pipeline is unverified: `:lines: N-M` excerpt ranges are computed against this file's line numbers, so a 150-line caption makes ranges shift unpredictably between exports. QA cases 6-9 of this round have not been run yet.
close_reason: Fixed in a6484ea. render_entry interpolated raw.title straight into the single-line <sub> caption, so a multi-line shell command split the element across the document; title and status now go through single_line(), which collapses newline runs to a space and trims. Tests: 'keeps the caption on one line when the tool title spans several' (asserts every <sub> line ends with </sub> and that a '## Observed' inside the title does not become a section) and 'keeps the caption on one line when the tool status spans several'; both confirmed red before the fix, failing on the caption ending in '<<EOF'. Gates: mini.test 0 fails/0 notes, stylua clean on both changed files, lua-language-server no new warnings. Deviation from the filed acceptance criteria: truncation was considered and deliberately not implemented -- a 150-line command is still a poor caption even when it is one line, but that is a presentation decision, filed thinking only, not a correctness gap. Re-export verification by the tester is still pending.

title: State sole copyright and retained relicensing right in CONTRIBUTING
description:
Amend `CONTRIBUTING.md` to state the copyright and relicensing position plainly.

The existing no-merge policy already explains *why* outside code is not merged (review burden, product coherence). This adds the licensing consequence of that policy, which is currently unstated.

## Content to add

A short factual paragraph, not a threat and not a legal wall of text:

- Copyright in LouiseLM is held solely by the maintainer.
- No outside code is merged, so no CLA is required and none will be asked for.
- The maintainer retains the right to license future versions under different terms.

## Why stated rather than silent

Sole ownership is already inferable in ten seconds from the public no-merge policy, so concealment buys no real surprise. The community LouiseLM wants — people bringing workflows and judgment over years — punishes ambush hardest and forgives disclosed risk easily. A pre-announced possibility converts an eventual relicense from betrayal into a term everyone accepted going in.

## Acceptance criteria

- `CONTRIBUTING.md` states all three points above.
- The tone matches the existing document: explicit about an unusual constraint, so nobody wastes effort or gets hurt feelings.
- Nothing elsewhere in the repo contradicts it by implying a perpetual open-source guarantee.
close_reason: Completed copyright and relicensing disclosure in CONTRIBUTING.md; documentary verification passed.

title: Investigate unexpected repeated browser opening of external issue URL
description:
## Observation

On 2026-08-29, the maintainer reported that a live Session `codex/01a04b63-d5b5-7fc0-8456-06c6281c7744` appeared to open `https://github.com/org/repo/issues/42` four times in Chrome without an intentional user action.

## Evidence collected

- The Session is live in Neovim and owns `louiselm-f8r1`, the beads_viewer_rust/bvr custom-status and historical-load bug.
- Its ACP log is `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a04b63-d5b5-7fc0-8456-06c6281c7744/log.jsonl`. The log contains no browser, URL-open, `xdg-open`, Playwright, or web-search tool call.
- Around the relevant event it was running `cargo test --tests`, not a bvr TUI process.
- Chrome Profile 5 history recorded visits to the URL at `04:49:56` and `04:49:57` local time on 2026-08-29; the copied read-only History database reported three visits in that interval.
- Chrome session file `/home/lotso/.config/google-chrome/Profile 5/Sessions/Session_13432442774644676` contains the URL repeatedly. These repetitions are serialized tab-state data and do not establish 18 openings.
- Chrome renderer processes were created at approximately `04:49:55`, consistent with Chrome reusing/opening tabs.
- beads_viewer_rust has an explicit external-link action: `src/tui.rs:5336` handles `o` when an external reference is available, and `src/tui.rs:14218` invokes `xdg-open` (with fallbacks).
- Repository tests and fixtures intentionally contain this placeholder URL as an external reference, but no evidence showed test rendering itself opening it.

## Assessment

The target Codex Session did not open the URL according to its durable ACP log. The strongest hypothesis is that a bvr TUI received `o` while an external issue link was selected, possibly repeated input; this is not proven. The browser history/session files cannot attribute the opener to a process.

No code change was made. Preserve this issue as the evidence record unless a reproducible trigger is found.

title: All-workspace session discovery sends empty params as a JSON array and every Agent rejects it
description:
`:LouiselmResume!` (all-workspace discovery) sends `session/list` with `"params": []` — an empty JSON
array — and every strict ACP Agent rejects it with `-32602 Invalid params`. The user gets a warning
naming each Agent and a silently truncated session list: 30 sessions instead of the 238 the
cwd-filtered path returns. This is the same defect class as louiselm-ce6.25.4 / de04317, which fixed
empty-object encoding for `account_limits/read` but not for `session/list`.

## Observed

Manual QA round 2026-08-25, build acb65c7, case 7, run against the real state root
(~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy), Agents claude, codex, copilot — all via acp-proxy.

Tester saw:

    louiselm: session discovery: claude: ACP session/list failed: Invalid params; codex: ACP
    session/list failed: Invalid params; copilot: ACP session/list failed: Invalid params

`:LouiselmResume!` then listed 30 sessions. `:LouiselmResume` (cwd-filtered) listed 238 with no
warning. So the bang, which is supposed to widen the search to every workspace, returns an order of
magnitude FEWER sessions than the narrow form.

Wire evidence, six independent connection logs under
/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/connections/ (6718d38b, f3183b4f, e61ced5f, 7f40d206,
01aa06f2, 32511725), all identical:

    request  {"method": "session/list", "params": [], "id": ...}
    response {"code": -32602, "message": "Invalid params",
              "data": {"_errors": ["Invalid input: expected object, received array"]}}

The cwd-filtered path is unaffected and works, including cursor pagination — connection fba1d164
shows `{"params": {"cwd": "/home/lotso/code/louiselm"}}` succeeding and paginating through
`{"cwd": ..., "cursor": "2026-08-23T12:31:10.449Z"}` and onwards, returning real session titles.

## Symptoms

- `:LouiselmResume!` warns once naming every configured strict Agent, then shows a partial list.
- The partial list is not marked as partial; the count simply looks small.
- A user comparing the two commands sees the broader query return fewer results, which reads as data
  loss rather than as a failed request.

## Root cause

`vim.json.encode({})` produces `[]`, not `{}`. Lua cannot distinguish an empty table from an empty
array, so an empty params table serializes as a JSON array and strict ACP Agents reject it.

Two sites build that empty table:

- lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:379 — `local params = {}`, then `cwd` and `cursor` are added only
  when non-nil. With `:LouiselmResume!` there is no cwd, and the first page has no cursor, so the
  first request goes out with an empty table. This is the site that fires in practice.
- lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:273 — `self:request("session/list", params or {}, callback)` has the same
  hazard for any caller passing nil.

The already-fixed comparison is in the same file: `Registry:refresh_agent_limits` passes
`nvim.empty_dict()` to `client:request(capability.read_method, ...)`, which is exactly why
`account_limits/read` goes out as `{}` and works.

## Why it was not caught

lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua:196 handles `session/list` without validating the params shape, so
the mock accepts `[]` where every real Agent refuses it. The discovery tests therefore exercise a
peer more permissive than any production peer, and the all-workspace path — the only one that
produces empty params — is precisely the case the mock cannot fail.

This is the third finding in two QA rounds where an invented fixture stood in for observed wire
behavior; see louiselm-4tum (snake_case vs camelCase usage keys) and louiselm-zufj (assumed
tool-update-before-turn_done ordering).

## Fix direction

Send `nvim.empty_dict()` rather than a bare table whenever the params object may end up empty, at
both sites above. Match `refresh_agent_limits`, which already does this.

Worth considering at the same time, but not required by this bug: an audit of every
`client:request(...)` call for the same hazard, and a mock-agent params-shape check so `[]` fails
there too. Filed as fix direction rather than acceptance because widening scope silently is how this
recurred after de04317 fixed one instance.

## Acceptance

- A regression test that fails while empty params serialize as `[]` and passes once they serialize as
  `{}`, asserting the encoded JSON rather than the Lua table.
- `:LouiselmResume!` against a strict Agent produces no `Invalid params` warning and returns at least
  as many sessions as `:LouiselmResume` for the same Agent.
- The mock agent rejects array-shaped params for `session/list`, so this cannot regress unnoticed.

## Not covered

- Which Agent supplied the 30 sessions that did appear under `:LouiselmResume!` was not confirmed;
  the warning named claude, codex and copilot, so the remainder presumably came from an
  acp-llm-adapter Agent that tolerates `[]`. Not verified.
- Other `client:request` call sites were surveyed but not individually tested for empty params.
close_reason: Fixed empty session/list params and passed live acceptance: 235 cwd-scoped sessions, 517 all-workspace sessions, no errors

title: Add explicit per-agent Agent Skills profiles
description:
## Problem Statement

LouiseLM currently injects one global skill index into every session, including adapters such as Codex and Claude that already provide native Agent Skills support. This exposes an implementation marker in chat, wastes context, can send a skill twice, and leaves users unable to understand which component discovers or invokes a skill.

## Solution

Add explicit per-agent Agent Skills profiles. Global skill paths remain shared, the default policy is `native`, and an agent may override only `skills.policy` with `native`, `inject`, or `off`. Native mode delegates discovery and invocation to the adapter. Inject mode provides a hidden, bounded Agent Skills catalog and attaches a selected full SKILL.md only once per activation. Off disables LouiseLM skill automation and the picker. Never infer or switch policy at runtime.

## User Stories

1. As a Codex or Claude user, I want native skills used without LouiseLM reinjecting them, so that skills are not duplicated.
2. As a custom-adapter user, I want to opt one agent into injected discovery, so that natural-language skill matching still works.
3. As a user, I want a picker that invokes a known local skill safely in both native and injected profiles, so that explicit activation is predictable.
4. As a user, I want skill context hidden before submission but inspectable afterward, so that chat stays clean without concealing what was sent.
5. As a skill author, I want malformed, shadowed, explicit-only, truncated, or inaccessible skills diagnosed clearly, so that configuration failures are understandable.
6. As a user configuring an unfamiliar ACP adapter, I want documentation explaining Agent Skills, ACP transport, host responsibilities, and filesystem assumptions, so that I can choose the correct policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Global `skills.policy` defaults to `native`; agent definitions may override only the policy, while paths remain global and session-static.
2. `native` sends no automatic catalog or skill body. Picker activation resolves against the adapter's latest advertised command list and sends exactly one advertised command plus task.
3. `inject` sends one hidden catalog only on the first accepted non-slash prompt of a new session, then sends a selected complete SKILL.md once per deliberate activation. It never falls back to native or reinjects after uncertain accepted requests.
4. `off` sends no skill automation and disables the skill picker without intercepting user-authored slash commands.
5. The old `full_content` setting and dormant automatic-native-fallback API are removed with clear migration errors and documentation.
6. Agent Skills core metadata is parsed with `lyaml` and semantically validated; Codex and Claude invocation-control extensions are recognized without treating them as ACP requirements.
7. Missing `lyaml` blocks injected sessions and local native picker/validation, but does not block native sessions themselves or off sessions.
8. The injected catalog uses the agreed Agent Skills XML shape, fixed behavioral preamble, XML escaping, and an 8,000-byte UTF-8-safe total budget with deterministic diagnostics.
9. Submitted prompt contexts are represented as one closed Neovim fold containing exact sent content in order; automatic hidden catalog text never appears as a pre-send marker.
10. README, generated configuration help/annotations, checkhealth, and migration guidance explain policy selection, no-double-send behavior, dependency installation, trust/path rules, filesystem limits, and live-only fold persistence.
11. Automated tests cover configuration, discovery, YAML, invocation metadata, native command correlation, injection lifecycle, slash deferral, failures/cancellation, no-double-send invariants, and context folds. Installed Codex/Claude checks remain documented manual smoke tests.

## Implementation Notes

- Agent Skills defines the skill format; ACP transports prompts and command updates; LouiseLM is the host responsible for policy and injected discovery.
- Explicit-only wins when `disable-model-invocation: true` or OpenAI's `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` is present. Such skills remain picker-visible but are excluded from injected catalogs.
- Root order defines duplicate precedence; path handling is deterministic, symlink-aware, and diagnostic without adding a trust database.
- The 8,000-byte mechanism intentionally mimics Codex's conservative fallback behavior; it is not part of ACP or the Agent Skills specification.
- Use native Neovim folds and existing context transport. Do not introduce a generic fold framework.

## Testing Notes

Use MiniTest for module behavior and a mock ACP agent for command updates and prompt transport. Test public behavior and exact no-double-send invariants. Do not require authenticated live adapters in automated tests.

## Out of Scope

- Runtime policy switching or inference.
- A general UI for every ACP advertised command.
- A LouiseLM ACP filesystem service.
- Recursive embedding of skill resources.
- Persistent transcript reconstruction.
- Automatic dependency installation.
- Generic adapter-native skill implementation.
- Tool-call fold rendering; track that as a separate design question.
