title: Diagnose installed lyaml outside Neovim search paths
description:
## Problem

Local skill discovery reports:

```
louiselm: lyaml is required for local skill discovery; install it with `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 install lyaml`
```

However, LuaRocks confirms that lyaml is already installed for Lua 5.1. The actual failure is that the active Neovim process does not search the LuaRocks tree, so the message sends the user toward an installation command that will not fix the search-path mismatch.

## Reproduction evidence

- `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 show lyaml` succeeds with lyaml 6.2.9-2 under `$HOME/.asdf/installs/lua/5.1.5/luarocks`.
- Neovim 0.12.2 embeds LuaJIT 2.1.
- In `nvim --headless -u NONE`, `pcall(require, "lyaml")` returns `module 'lyaml' not found`.
- Neovim's `package.path` and `package.cpath` contain system paths, but not the asdf LuaRocks share/lib paths reported by `luarocks path --lua-version 5.1`.

## Expected behavior

When lyaml cannot be loaded, LouiseLM should preserve enough of the loader failure to distinguish an absent installation from an installed-but-unreachable LuaRocks tree (and from native module load failures), then give a corrective action that matches the failure.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The user-facing/checkhealth diagnostic distinguishes at least package-not-found/search-path mismatch from a native loader failure instead of always saying to install lyaml.
2. Documentation gives a supported way to make a Lua 5.1 LuaRocks tree visible to Neovim, including non-system/asdf installs.
3. Tests cover the generic `require("lyaml")` failure mapping without depending on a real LuaRocks installation.
4. Diagnostics do not expose unrelated environment values or sensitive data.
close_reason: Shortened interactive lyaml failures to point at checkhealth, added detailed persistent zsh/asdf guidance to health and README, and covered both surfaces. Verified 181 MiniTest cases, StyLua, and LuaLS.

title: Abandonment
description: Loss of a live Session because Neovim exited without disposing it.
design: Established by the louiselm-ce6.28 grill-me session on 2026-08-26, from a reproduction in which ordinary :q from a louiselm://limits detail buffer exited Neovim while a Session remained alive.
notes: Avoid: using Abandonment for a deliberate lifecycle end. Distinguish from Disposal, which deliberately ends a Session, and from Cancellation, which ends a turn but leaves the Session alive. All three appear in the quit-safety contract; conflating them changes lifecycle behavior.

title: Add Session edges from Beads actor fields to issue Provenance
description:
## Goal

Show which Sessions worked an issue, using the Session ids that the claim
convention already writes into Beads.

## Scope

- In scope: issue -> Session edges from `assignee` and `created_by`; those rows
  in the issue Provenance view; transcript resolution through the locator.
- Out of scope: time travel, Session-rooted views.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The issue view lists Sessions from Beads actor fields, deduplicated against
   Sessions already found through commit trailers.
2. Actor values that are not Session ids (`assistant`, `lotso`) are shown as
   non-Session actors rather than being resolved or silently dropped. 169 of the
   backlog's issues predate the convention, so this is the common case for older
   work, not an edge case.
3. Edges are read through `br`, never by parsing `.beads/*.jsonl`.

## Testing

- Fixtures covering a Session-id actor, a bare-name actor, an empty assignee,
  and an issue whose commit trailer and assignee name the same Session, which
  must appear once.

## Notes

Coverage is uneven by construction and the view must not imply otherwise:
Beads actors are codex-heavy (codex 123, claude 34, copilot 14) while commit
trailers are claude-heavy (claude 25, deepseek 7). An issue can therefore have
a Session on one edge and nothing on the other.
close_reason: Completed: issue Provenance reads actors through br, classifies legacy actors, resolves and deduplicates Session edges, with 682-case suite and all quality gates passing.

comments.author: codex/01a0428e-6b0e-7fa3-a088-c03e6b235bf4
comments.text: Lesson: the issue view needed two independent read paths: BVR history for commit correlations and br show --json for authoritative assignee/created_by actors. Preserving BVR commit messages let the pure correlation layer derive trailer Sessions, while the merge boundary deduplicates those against actor-derived Sessions. No standing AGENTS.md rule or unresolved design question is warranted.

title: Pairing QR is oversized, clipped, and exposes payload
description:
The Neovim pairing screen renders a terminal QR nearly twice as wide as it is tall, and it is clipped in a normal split. This makes the core phone-pairing flow difficult to photograph and can leave the user believing pairing succeeded when the receiver still has no registered device. The same screen also prints the raw one-time pairing JSON above the QR, unnecessarily exposing the token as selectable text.

## Observed

Physical QA round `louiselm-qbr.1.9` on 2026-08-21, 1920x1200 terminal.

- `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260821_0612_1920x1200_1787285559.png`: in a two-column split, the QR extends beyond the right window edge and its right side is clipped.
- `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260821_0612_1920x1200_1787285570.png`: even full-screen, the rendered QR is about twice as wide as tall and occupies almost the whole editor.
- Both screenshots show a serialized pairing object above the QR, including a `token` field. The token value is intentionally omitted from this issue.
- Immediately after the reported scan, `louiselm-capture status` returned `devices: []`; no pairing completed.

## Symptoms

- The user must maximize the editor and carefully frame a distorted, oversized code.
- A split clips QR modules, preventing reliable scanning.
- The raw short-lived credential is displayed as ordinary text in addition to being encoded in the QR.

## Root cause

`capture-service/src/cli.rs:191-196` renders `unicode::Dense1x2` with `module_dimensions(2, 1)`. `Dense1x2` already packs two vertical modules per terminal row; doubling only the horizontal module width produces roughly four character columns per row and the observed wide code. Line 196 prints `{payload}` before `{rendered}`, so the Neovim buffer exposes the serialized token.

## Why it was not caught

Pairing tests cover offer validation, credential issuance, persistence, and HTTP authentication, but no test constrains the CLI pairing output's geometry or asserts that the raw offer is absent. The Neovim command smoke test only asserts command registration.

## Fix direction

At the CLI output boundary, render `Dense1x2` at its native module width and print only the QR. Keep the pairing protocol and Neovim buffer mechanism unchanged.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and proves terminal QR character geometry is approximately 2 columns per row rather than 4.
- A regression test proves the CLI-visible rendering does not contain the serialized token or raw JSON payload.
- In the same Neovim split used in the screenshot, the complete QR fits and a physical phone scan registers the device on the receiver.

## Not covered

Terminal font aspect ratios and color-scheme contrast outside the reported Ghostty/Neovim environment are not evaluated.
close_reason: Fixed in 456031b, 13dfe23, and f7d85fc. Root causes: redundant horizontal QR scaling, raw offer output, colorscheme-dependent inverted polarity, and listchars corruption of the quiet zone. Tests: pairing_outputs_a_compact_qr_without_the_raw_offer and pairing QR is black on white independently of the colorscheme were red before their fixes and green after. Gates: full Rust suite/format, StyLua, lua-language-server zero diagnostics, mini.test 316/316. Physical verification: fresh Neovim QR paired successfully; receiver registered device 62e8883e-2f0d-47f0-84dd-832879ad1453 and subsequently accepted the previously rejected 7c7353dc-1c2c-474a-a4c8-a39d102f82e8 capture.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Automated fix landed in 456031b: Dense1x2 now uses native width and CLI prints only rendered QR. Public CLI regression pairing_outputs_a_compact_qr_without_the_raw_offer was red on both raw-offer and geometry assertions, then green. Gates passed: cargo fmt/check + full Rust suite; stylua; lua-language-server zero diagnostics; mini.test 315/315. Release binary installed at /home/lotso/.local/bin/louiselm-capture without modifying TLS/pairing state. Physical same-split scan remains required before closure.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Physical retest partial: user reports the corrected QR screen in the same environment seems okay, so layout/raw-line presentation is provisionally passed. However objective receiver status remains devices: []; scan/registration is not yet proven, so bug remains open and Case 8 has not started.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Physical scan still fails after 456031b. User tried repeated portrait/landscape photos; Android reports exactly: No QR code was found. Move closer. Receiver remains devices: []. Inspection confirms Dense1x2 represents dark modules as foreground glyphs; under the reported dark colorscheme the screenshot is light-on-dark/inverted. Android uses ML Kit 17.3.0 photo scanning and returns no barcode. Follow-up must force black foreground/white background on the QR region independent of colorscheme; first fix remains valid for size and raw-payload removal.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Follow-up fix committed in 13dfe23: :LouiselmCapturePair highlights only QR lines with explicit black foreground/white background, independent of colorscheme. UI regression test pairing QR is black on white independently of the colorscheme failed before the fix (no highlight) and passes after. Gates: stylua, lua-language-server zero diagnostics, mini.test 316/316. Physical scan/receiver registration still required before closure.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Third physical attempt: QR is visibly black-on-white after 13dfe23, but Android pairing error persists and receiver remains devices: []. Exact environment check via a fresh configured Neovim: vim.wo.list=true and listchars={trail="·", tab="» ", nbsp="␣"}. The CLI QR quiet zone is made of leading/trailing spaces; listchars replaces every trailing quiet-zone space with dots and turns fully blank top/bottom quiet rows into dotted rows, corrupting the barcode despite correct contrast. Next regression/fix: :LouiselmCapturePair must set the pairing window list=false.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Quiet-zone fix committed in f7d85fc: pairing window sets list=false, preventing listchars.trail=· from replacing QR border spaces. The existing public UI test was extended to start with list=true; assertion was red before the fix and green after. Gates: stylua, lua-language-server zero diagnostics, mini.test 316/316. Fresh-Neovim physical scan remains required before closure.

title: Resumed-session export silently drops nested/subagent tool calls
description:
`:LouiselmResume`'s replay of a prior ACP session silently drops nested/child
tool calls (a tool call made *by* a Task subagent, i.e. one carrying a
`parentToolUseId`), while still replaying the parent Task call's own summary
text. Anyone exporting a resumed session — including the blog publishing
pipeline, which exports whatever the agent replays on `session/load` — gets a
transcript that is missing subagent-internal tool-call detail, with no error
or signal that anything is missing.

## Observed

QA round for the transcript-export/blog-publishing features
(`4e4a58b`, `674939b`), case 4 ("resumed-session export vs live export"),
session `21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384`, 2026-08-18.

Prompt that produced the nested call (case 1 of the same round):
"Do these three things in order, in this one turn. (1) Run the Bash tool on
the absolute path: `wc -l .../transcript.lua`. (2) Use the Task tool to
launch one general-purpose subagent whose prompt is exactly: 'List the
top-level directories of /home/lotso/code/louiselm as one comma-separated
line.' (3) Write me a two-sentence summary of what you found."

Original live export, captured right after that turn ended:
`louiselm-session-1-20260818-150448.md` (repo root at the time). Contains 3
tool-call blocks — Bash (`wc -l`), Task (`List top-level directories`), and a
nested Bash call made by the Task subagent:
```
toolCallId = "toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr"
parentToolUseId = "toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a"  (the Task call)
title = "ls -d /home/lotso/code/louiselm/*/ | xargs -n1 basename | paste -sd, -"
rawOutput = "android,assets,blog,capture-service,configured,lua,scripts,tests"
status = "completed"
```

Resumed export (`:LouiselmResume` on the same session, immediate
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` → `/tmp/qa-resumed.md`, no other prompt sent first):
same acp session id (session/load reconnects rather than creating a new
session). Contains the parent `## Tool: List top-level directories
(completed)` block with its rawOutput summary intact, but grepping the full
573KB resumed export for the toolCallId `toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr`, the
literal command text `paste -sd`, and `xargs -n1 basename` finds zero
tool-call blocks — those strings appear exactly once, incidentally, inside
unrelated later text content (a grep-output dump quoted in a much later
turn), not as a `## Tool:` entry.

Raw jsonrpc log:
`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260818-150022-1160867-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`
(818 lines). The nested `tool_call` event for
`toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr` appears exactly once, at line 19, during the
original live turn:
```
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":{"sessionId":"21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384","update":{"_meta":{"claudeCode":{"toolName":"Bash","parentToolUseId":"toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a"}},"toolCallId":"toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr","sessionUpdate":"tool_call","rawInput":{"command":"ls -d /home/lotso/code/louiselm/*/ | xargs -n1 basename | paste -sd, -"},"status":"pending", ...}}}
```
No second occurrence appears later in the log during the replay burst
triggered by `session/load` — the agent process itself never re-emits this
event on replay.

Everything else about the resumed export checked out clean: 65 of the 66
total tool calls in the session (by then spanning many turns) present and in
correct relative order, and the case-1 `## User` block matches the typed
prompt verbatim. Only this one nested call is missing.

## Symptoms

- User sees: a resumed-session export (or a blog post built from one) that
  looks complete — full assistant text, the parent Task call's own summary —
  but is silently missing the detail of what the subagent actually did
  internally.
- System reports: nothing. No error, warning, or count mismatch anywhere;
  `Chat:to_markdown` and `create-blog.sh` both report success normally.

## Root cause

Unknown, and outside this repo (`louiselm.nvim`). `louiselm`'s own
`Transcript:record`/`Transcript.render` (lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua)
only records whatever `session/update` events it receives over ACP — the
live stream sent the nested tool_call event and louiselm recorded it
correctly (see the original export above); on replay, the same event simply
never arrives, so there is nothing to fix on this side.

Hypothesis (unverified): `claude-agent-acp`
(`/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter`, a sibling project) or the underlying
Claude Code SDK reconstructs the Task/subagent call tree differently when
replaying a resumed session's history than when streaming it live — possibly
only replaying top-level tool calls and treating subagent-internal calls as
already-summarized by the parent's own output. Nothing in this investigation
confirms which layer (adapter vs. upstream SDK) is responsible; that needs a
look at the adapter/SDK's own session/load implementation, not louiselm's.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/session/transcript_export_spec.lua` and
`tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` exercise `Transcript` against synthetic,
hand-built event fixtures for both the live and "loaded" replay paths — no
fixture in the suite includes a nested/subagent tool call in a replay
scenario, because nobody had a real payload to model one on. This QA round
was the first time a resumed session containing a Task-subagent call was
actually exported and diffed against its own live-captured original.

## Fix direction

Not in this repo. If the root cause is confirmed to be in
`claude-agent-acp`, the fix belongs there (ensure `session/load` replay
re-emits every historical `tool_call`/`tool_call_update`, including nested
ones with `parentToolUseId` set, not just top-level calls). If it turns out
to be inherent to how the upstream Claude Code SDK exposes subagent history
on resume, this may not be fixable without a scope change to what
`session/load` guarantees — in which case the practical mitigation is
documentation: warn blog-pipeline users that `create-blog.sh` on a resumed
session may omit subagent-internal tool-call detail, and recommend exporting
live when that detail matters.

## Acceptance

- A regression test in whichever repo owns the fix: replay a session
  containing a Task call with a nested tool call, and assert the replayed
  event stream includes the nested `tool_call`/`tool_call_update` events,
  not just the parent's.
- Re-run this round's case 4 comparison
  (`louiselm-session-1-20260818-150448.md` vs. a fresh `:LouiselmResume` +
  immediate `:LouiselmToMarkdown` export of the same session) and confirm
  `toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr` (or an equivalent nested call in a new
  repro) is present in the resumed export.

## Not covered

- Which of `claude-agent-acp` vs. the upstream Claude Code SDK is actually
  responsible — unverified, needs investigation in that repo, not this one.
- Whether the same gap exists for other nested-call shapes (e.g. a tool call
  made by a tool call, rather than by a Task subagent specifically) — only
  one nested-call example existed in the session under test.
- Whether `create-blog.sh` (case 5, not yet run at time of filing) actually
  reproduces the same gap end-to-end through the headless path — this bug is
  filed from the interactive `:LouiselmResume` path only; case 5 should
  re-check this once it runs.
close_reason: Fixed in owner repo /home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp commit 041da5b; exact historical session headless export restores the missing nested tool call and parent attribution; full owner-repo gates pass.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Confirmed reproducing through the headless path too (case 5 of the same QA
round). `./blog/scripts/create-blog.sh qa-round claude/21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384`
succeeded (exit 0, expected messages, scaffold created), and the exported
`blog/post-qa-round/conversations/claude-21a0ede3-....md` (664KB, 87 tool
calls by then) has no `## Tool: ls -d ...` block for the nested call either
— checked precisely for a genuine top-level `## Tool:` header, not just a
text match, since by this point the session transcript also contains this
bug's own filing (which quotes the missing toolCallId and command verbatim),
so a plain grep for those strings alone would false-positive. Confirms the
gap is in the shared `session/load` replay path itself, not specific to the
interactive `:LouiselmResume` UI flow.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Claimed for root-cause investigation in /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter. Intended source scope: session/load replay and its tests only; LouiseLM code remains unchanged unless adapter evidence disproves ownership. Existing sibling .beads schema-migration artifacts will be preserved.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Root cause confirmed in official claude-agent-acp replay. getSessionMessages reads only the main JSONL; the missing call is stored in the SDK-managed subagents/agent-a37d72065ac3f3d29.jsonl and is returned by listSubagents plus getSubagentMessages. Upstream main commit 8663170 preserved nested messages only when already supplied, so its split-storage unit assumption did not cover the real session. Implemented local owner-repo fix at /home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp commit 041da5b: load all persisted subagent histories, recursively interleave them after their parent tool-use messages, then reuse the existing replay converter. TDD: new test failed with only parent-agent-call and passed with parent-agent-call then child-tool. Gates: 811 passed, 20 skipped; ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript build, and diff check pass. Exact headless acceptance passed against session 21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384: exported child toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr with parentToolUseId toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a and original output.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Manual acceptance passed on 2026-08-20 with the local owner-repo build 041da5b. User visually confirmed the resumed first turn rendered the parent Agent/Task call, nested Bash call, then assistant response in order. Pinned stderr proves the configured process was node /home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp/dist/index.js. ACP log 20260820-183053-1060915-node-stdout-jsonrpc.log emitted child toolu_01AB1x1SdnkvcFoPF6EcmTqr with parent toolu_018NnXLu4qGQc7e4bei8C52a. Fresh Markdown export /tmp/louiselm-d2o-local.md preserved parent at line 89, child at line 124, and assistant heading at line 130 with the original command and output. No QA findings.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Published the owner-repo fix to fork https://github.com/euri10/claude-agent-acp on branch fix/replay-persisted-subagents. Review history is explicitly test-first: fece865 adds the split-storage regression and fails with expected parent-agent-call plus child-tool but actual parent-agent-call only; e8f2df4 adds the implementation and makes that same focused test pass. Final gates on the pushed tip: npm run check passed, npm run build passed, full Vitest 811 passed and 20 skipped. Upstream agentclientprotocol remote was not pushed.

The PR contains the red/green regression history, real-session evidence, and the owner-repo implementation that closes this out-of-repo finding.

title: stylua --check . fails on a clean tree because blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua is unformatted
description:
`stylua --check .` — the formatter gate AGENTS.md section 4 declares, unscoped
and whole-repo — exits 1 on a clean checkout of `main`. It has done so since
`674939b` (2026-08-18). Every contributor and every CI run that enforces the
documented gate fails on an untouched tree, which trains people to ignore the
gate.

## Observed

Found during setup of the QA round covering `ec19281..HEAD`, on a clean tree at
`cd37ab2` (2026-08-20), before any case was run.

```
$ git status --porcelain
$ stylua --check .; echo "exit=$?"
Diff in blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua:
26       |-vim.cmd('packadd nvim.tohtml')
    26   |+vim.cmd("packadd nvim.tohtml")
...
39       |-	io.stderr:write('tohtml-driver: ' .. msg .. '\n')
    39   |+  io.stderr:write("tohtml-driver: " .. msg .. "\n")
...
exit=1
```

`blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua` is the only file that differs; every file under
`lua/` and `tests/` is clean.

## Symptoms

- `stylua --check .`, copied verbatim from AGENTS.md section 4, exits 1 with no
  local changes.
- The reported diff is entirely in private blog tooling, not in plugin code, so
  the failure looks unrelated to whatever the contributor is actually doing.

## Root cause

`blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua` was authored with tab indentation and
single-quoted strings, matching the shell scripts it sits beside rather than
`.stylua.toml` (`indent_type = "Spaces"`, `indent_width = 2`,
`quote_style = "AutoPreferDouble"`). It was added by `674939b` and has never
been run through StyLua. Concretely: lines 26, 32, 39-40, 43, 45-46, 49, 51-52,
54, 59-60, 64-91, 93, 96.

## Why it was not caught

Two gaps, both real:

- CI does not yet enforce the gates (AGENTS.md section 4: "CI must enforce all
  gates once their configuration/harness exists"), so nothing runs
  `stylua --check .` except a human choosing to.
- The QA round that had `674939b` in scope (`louiselm-vj0`) exercised the blog
  pipeline's behaviour end to end and never ran the formatter gate. Behavioural
  QA does not substitute for the gate, and the round plan did not list it.

## Fix direction

Two defensible options; this is a decision, not a lookup.

1. Format the file: `stylua blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua`. Narrowest, keeps
   the gate's whole-repo scope honest. Cost: this one Lua file stops matching
   the tab-indented shell scripts it lives with.
2. Add a `.styluaignore` for `blog/`, on the argument already made in
   `blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh`'s header — that `AGENTS.md` governs
   `lua/`, not private blog tooling. Cost: makes the exclusion explicit and
   permanent, and future Lua under `blog/` is then unformatted by policy.

Rejected: narrowing the documented gate command to `stylua --check lua/ tests/`.
That silently shrinks a rule stated as whole-repo, and the next Lua file added
outside those two directories inherits the same invisible hole.

## Acceptance

- `stylua --check .` exits 0 on a clean tree.
- Whichever option is taken is recorded where the next person looks: either the
  file is formatted, or `.styluaignore` exists with a comment saying why.

## Not covered

- `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning`, the other AGENTS.md
  gate, was not run during this round's setup — its status on a clean tree is
  unverified.
- Deferred deliberately: not fixed during the QA round, because the round's
  case 0 records the clean-tree gate result and editing the tree mid-round
  invalidates that premise. Fix after the round closes.
close_reason: Formatted blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua under the repository StyLua policy and bound Neovim's injected vim global through a narrowly suppressed local. Verification: stylua --check . passed; lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning reported zero problems; blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh passed 20/20; full MiniTest suite passed 315/315; git diff --check passed; dependency graph has no cycles.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
The 'Not covered' item is now resolved, and it makes this worse than filed: blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua fails BOTH documented AGENTS.md section 4 gates, not just StyLua.

'lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning' on a clean tree at cd37ab2 reports 'Diagnosis complete, 9 problems found', all 9 in that one file, all 'Undefined global vim (undefined-global)' -- the file is a headless Neovim driver script, so it uses the vim global but sits outside whatever library/workspace config covers lua/ and tests/.

Verified during this round by running the gate before and after an unrelated fix: 11 problems in 2 files with a temporary vim.gsplit call in a test, 9 problems in 1 file once that was removed. Every file under lua/ and tests/ is clean.

This strengthens fix option 2 (a .styluaignore-style exclusion for blog/): whatever is decided, it should cover both gates, since a fix that only silences StyLua leaves the same file failing lua-language-server. Option 1 (format the file) does not address the undefined-global warnings at all -- those need either a workspace/library setting for blog/ or an exclusion.

title: Grill-me needed: how should louiselm own versioning across plugin, capture-service, and Android, and which GitHub tooling should drive it?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing.

Question: how should louiselm own its versioning across its three shipped components (Neovim plugin, capture-service Rust crate, Android app) as it moves from alpha to external users, and which GitHub-native tooling should generate, enforce, and publish those versions?

Context / evidence that raised it:
louiselm currently advertises itself to ACP adapters as `clientInfo = { name = "louiselm.nvim", version = "0.1.0" }`, hardcoded in `lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:199`. The same `0.1.0` is duplicated in at least two other places: `capture-service/Cargo.toml` (and the matching `Cargo.lock` entry) and `android/app/build.gradle.kts` (`versionName`). AGENTS.md section 1 says the project is early-stage with no external users and that breaking changes are acceptable, so there is no release discipline yet — but the version string is already observable to every adapter through ACP `initialize`, and duplicated literals have no mechanism to stay in sync.

Threads worth pulling:
- Single source of truth: does the canonical version live in a `VERSION` file, a Lua module, `Cargo.toml`, git tags only, or somewhere else? Which component owns it, and how do the others derive it without a build-time codegen step?
- Lockstep versus independent versioning: should the Neovim plugin, capture-service, and Android app share one version, or diverge? The ACP `clientInfo.version` should report the plugin/agent client version — how is that kept meaningful if the repo has multiple release cadences?
- GitHub tooling candidates: release-please, semantic-release, Changesets, git-cliff + GitHub Releases, or manual tag-and-release. Which fits a monorepo that is Lua/Rust/Android (no npm ecosystem) and has no Conventional Commits discipline yet?
- Conventional Commits: is adopting/enforcing it a prerequisite for automatic version bumping and changelog generation, and is that acceptable for this repo?
- Pre-release semantics: how do 0.x breaking changes and alpha status interact with semver? How should adapters distinguish `clientInfo.version` (cosmetic/reported) from ACP `protocolVersion` (compatibility contract)?
- GitHub Actions integration: tag on merge to main, release branches, per-component workflows? What artifacts does a release actually produce for a Neovim plugin (git tag, GitHub Release, LuaRocks, stable branch) versus the Rust binary and Android APK?
- Drift risk: should `clientInfo.version` be read dynamically at runtime from one source, or injected at packaging time, so the advertised version cannot rot relative to the actual release?

title: Stack LouieLM transcript content in chronological order
description:
## Problem

In the latest screenshot of a LouieLM session, the transcript content feels split by type: the conversation text appears above while tool activity/status lines are grouped at the bottom near the prompt. This makes the sequence of the session awkward to follow.

## Desired behavior

Render each printed item in one chronological vertical stack, including model text, user text, tool calls, tool results, and status messages. New items should appear after the preceding item in the same transcript flow, with the composer/input area remaining at the bottom.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Model text, user text, tool activity, tool results, and status messages appear in a single chronological transcript order.
2. Tool output is positioned next to or directly after the event that produced it rather than in a separate bottom group.
3. The input/composer remains clearly separated from transcript history at the bottom.
4. Existing session header and chat behavior remain unchanged.

Source report: /tmp/nvim-wtu.md
close_reason: Reset streamed response cursor after tool and error transcript items so interleaved chat content remains chronological; added regression coverage. Verified focused and full mini.test suites, StyLua, LuaLS, and git diff --check.

title: LouiselmToMarkdown crashes with uncaught E482 instead of a clean write error
description:
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` crashes with an uncaught Lua/Vimscript error instead of
the clean "could not write markdown file: ..." message when the destination's
parent directory does not exist.

## Observed

Manual QA round on commits 674939b (blog publishing pipeline) and 4e4a58b
(session transcript export), case 2.2/2.3 in QA_REVIEW.md. User ran
`:LouiselmToMarkdown`, typed `~/tmp/qa-export.md` (nonexistent dir):

```
louiselm markdown path (blank for default): ~/tmp/qa-export.md
Lua :command callback: Vim:E482
: Can't open file ~/tmp/qa-export.md for writing: no such file or directory
stack traceback:
        [C]: in function 'writefile'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1561: in function 'to_markdown'
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:276: in function 'on_confirm'
        ...installs/neovim/0.12.2/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/ui.lua:114: in function 'input'
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:272: in function <.../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:266>
```

Reproduced identically with the absolute path `/tmp/nope/qa-export.md`
(missing dir), ruling out `~`-expansion as the sole cause — the real trigger
is any nonexistent parent directory.

## Symptoms

- User sees a raw `E482` Lua stack trace in `:messages`, not a `louiselm:`
  notification.
- The chat UI's own error path (`report_error`) never fires for this failure.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1561`:

```lua
if nvim.fn.writefile(split_lines(markdown), destination) ~= 0 then
  return nil, "could not write markdown file: " .. destination
end
```

This assumes `writefile()` reports failure via a nonzero return. In Neovim,
when the destination cannot be opened at all (missing parent directory, no
permission), `writefile()` throws `E482` as a Lua error instead of returning
a value — so the `~= 0` check is dead code for this failure mode and the
error propagates uncaught through `Chat:to_markdown` ->
`command.lua:276 on_confirm` -> `vim.ui.input`.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` covers the success path, "no chat
session", "not attached", and "disposed" errors, but has no case where
`writefile` itself fails (e.g. destination inside a nonexistent directory).
The suite never exercises the real `writefile()` call against an unwritable
path.

## Fix direction

Wrap the `writefile` call in `pcall` in `Chat:to_markdown` (init.lua:1561) so
any thrown error is caught and converted into the existing
`"could not write markdown file: " .. destination` return.

## Acceptance

- A regression test in tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua that calls
  `to_markdown` with a path inside a nonexistent directory and asserts a
  clean `(nil, "could not write markdown file: " .. path)` return with no
  thrown error.
- Manually confirmed: `:LouiselmToMarkdown` against a missing directory shows
  a `louiselm: could not write markdown file: ...` notification, no stack
  trace in `:messages`.

## Not covered

`~` is not expanded by `vim.fn.writefile` either (a second, separate
usability issue: paths starting with `~` will still fail even inside an
existing directory tree, just with a clean error now instead of a crash).
Not filing separately since the pcall fix already turns it into the correct
clean-error path; only worth a follow-up if users expect `~` to expand.
close_reason: Fixed in 6167df0. Root cause: nvim.fn.writefile throws E482 (Lua error) instead of returning nonzero when the destination directory doesn't exist, so Chat:to_markdown's `~= 0` check never caught the failure. Fix: wrapped the writefile call in pcall (init.lua:1561), converting any thrown error into the existing clean 'could not write markdown file: ...' return. Tests: added 'reports a clean error instead of crashing when the destination directory does not exist' to tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua -- failed with the exact E482 traceback before the fix, passes after. Gates: full mini.test suite (235/235 cases) and stylua --check on both changed files pass. No deviation from filed acceptance criteria.

title: Selecting a Provenance Decision takes about 11 seconds
description:
Selecting a row in the Provenance Decision index eventually opens the correct evidence popup, but the interaction takes about 11 seconds before the second window appears.

## Observed

Manual QA on 2026-08-28 after fix commit d6851c6, in the maintainer environment. The user reported: "it takes 11s to see the 2nd window...but it loads". Screenshot evidence: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260828_0551_1920x1200_1787889089.png. The screenshot shows the selected Decision evidence popup populated for issue louiselm-c274, proving the result eventually loads. No timing trace or pinned process log was captured, so the 11-second duration is a user measurement.

## Symptoms

- Decision index buffer appears quickly.
- Pressing CR on a row waits about 11 seconds.
- The second Provenance window then appears and contains the expected Decision evidence.
- There is no duplicate-buffer error after d6851c6.

## Root cause

Unknown. The selection path runs asynchronous bvr history and br issue lookups before rendering in lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:514-565. Measure each subprocess and callback boundary before choosing a fix; do not assume the delay is Neovim window creation.

## Why it was not caught

Automated tests stub process execution and invoke callbacks immediately, so they cover ordering and rendering but not real bvr/br latency or user-visible time-to-popup.

## Fix direction

Capture timings for the bvr history call, br issue lookup, and popup render in a real Session. Optimize only the measured bottleneck while preserving explicit partial-error behavior.

## Acceptance

- Selecting a Decision row displays the evidence popup without the duplicate-buffer error.
- The measured time from row selection to popup is reduced to an acceptable interactive delay, with the target agreed from the captured baseline.
- Regression coverage or a deterministic timing boundary prevents reintroducing unnecessary serial work.

## Not covered

- The screenshot does not prove the exact duration independently.
- The previous duplicate-buffer failure is tracked separately by louiselm-g2ya.
close_reason: Fixed in 7efbc44 by opening the Decision Provenance popup immediately with a loading state, then refreshing the same named buffer with final evidence. Regression asserts the loading view before the BVR callback; full MiniTest 703/703, stylua, lua-language-server, and API appendix checks pass. Manual QA confirmed the popup appears immediately and final Decision content loads successfully. BVR latency remains tracked in louiselm-cvlc.

comments.author: 01a0465c-762f-73f3-90ff-b096b27607fc
comments.text: Lesson: when enrichment is materially slower than view creation, render a truthful loading state at the UI boundary and refresh the same Provenance buffer when data arrives. The expensive BVR subprocess remains a separate performance concern; no design question is warranted.

title: Resolve a Session id to its transcript with a layout-keyed locator
description:
## Goal

Given a Session id such as `codex/01a0343a-...`, return the path to that
Session's transcript on disk, for every Agent the maintainer actually uses.

## Scope

- In scope: `lua/louiselm/session/locator.lua`; a config surface mapping an
  Agent entry to a transcript layout; layouts for claude, codex, deepseek and
  copilot; a `nil, err` result when no transcript exists.
- Out of scope: reading, parsing or rendering transcript contents. This task
  returns a path and nothing more. No UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `locator.resolve("<agent>/<session-id>")` returns an absolute path, or
   `nil, err` with an actionable message.
2. Resolution keys on transcript LAYOUT, never on Agent name. `config.agents`
   is a `map-of` with default `{}`, so Agent names are arbitrary user labels;
   two Agents configured with different names but the same CLI must resolve
   through one layout implementation.
3. An Agent renamed in config after its Sessions were recorded still resolves
   those Sessions.
4. A malformed id, an unknown layout, and a well-formed id whose transcript
   file is absent are each distinguishable failures, not one generic error.
5. Public API is LuaCATS-typed; no editor or UI calls anywhere in the module.

## Testing

- Temporary directory trees, one per layout, asserting resolution and the
  missing-file path.
- Two differently-named Agents sharing one layout both resolve.
- An Agent renamed between recording and lookup still resolves.
- No network, no real Agent binaries, no reliance on the maintainer's home
  directory.

## Notes

First slice of louiselm-h00g deliberately: self-contained, unblocked by the
bvr defect (louiselm-f8r1), and independently wanted by louiselm-3x9p, so it
retains value even if the rest of the epic is reshaped.

glm is expected to resolve through the OpenAI-compatible layout shared with
deepseek. There are no glm Session ids in the record yet, so do not claim glm
support until a real glm Session resolves; leave it unverified rather than
asserted.
close_reason: Implemented layout-keyed transcript resolution for all four observed layouts; live acceptance and 557-test suite pass.

title: Read git commit trailers into structured Provenance edges
description:
## Goal

Turn `Refs <id>` commit trailers into structured Provenance edges, so a commit
can name the issues and Sessions it belongs to.

## Scope

- In scope: the git half of `lua/louiselm/provenance/sources.lua`; the trailer
  parsing and edge construction in `lua/louiselm/provenance/correlate.lua`.
- Out of scope: bvr correlation, time travel, and any UI. Beads actor fields
  are a separate slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given a commit range, produce edges of commit -> issue id and
   commit -> Session id derived from `Refs` trailers.
2. `correlate` performs no I/O at all. It takes already-collected input and
   returns edges, so the whole join is fixture-testable.
3. `sources` spawns git with `vim.system()` and an argument array, never a
   built command string, and passes cwd explicitly.
4. Commits with no trailer, several trailers, and a trailer naming an id that
   no longer exists are each handled without error.
5. Both are LuaCATS-typed and return structured errors rather than notifying,
   printing or opening UI.

## Testing

- `correlate` against captured real `git log` output from this repository,
  cited in the test per AGENTS.md section 5 so observed shapes stay
  distinguishable from invented ones.
- The pre-convention era, where commits carry no trailers at all, yields
  partial edges rather than failure.
- `sources` callbacks are exercised in the production callback context, and the
  test proves no editor API is touched before a scheduling boundary.

## Notes

The trailer convention is already established: of the last 200 commits every
one carries a `Refs` line, and they already mix both node types.
close_reason: Implemented typed git Refs parsing/correlation and scheduled git source; focused and full 571-case MiniTest, StyLua, LuaLS, and diff checks pass.

comments.author: codex/01a03df9-6992-71e2-9050-1d4dd466011c
comments.text: Implemented with git's NUL/record-separated log format: sources parses bounded commit records and schedules all completion work out of vim.system's fast event; correlate remains pure and preserves unknown/stale Refs as typed issue or Session edges. Tests cite the captured repository log and prove no-trailer partial output plus callback scheduling. Lesson destination: this issue comment; no standing AGENTS.md rule or design question is warranted.

title: Open every UI selector outside insert mode
description:
## Problem

Commit 1eb309a fixed permission selection by leaving insert mode immediately before vim.ui.select. That diagnosis is correct: Chat:attach enters insert mode, and list-focused select providers can otherwise receive the wrong mode and confirm or edit the wrong picker state.

The same bug remains in session configuration. Chat:attach schedules open_session_options after entering insert mode, while both the options overview and its nested model/value picker call vim.ui.select without normalizing mode. This affects the automatic first-session overview and can also affect :LouiselmSessionOptions when invoked from an insert-mode mapping.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Attach a ready session that advertises a model or boolean configuration option.
2. Let Chat:attach focus the prompt and enter insert mode.
3. Wait for the scheduled initial options overview, or invoke :LouiselmSessionOptions from an insert-mode mapping.
4. Observe that vim.ui.select is called while the inherited mode is insert; with a list-focused provider, navigation or confirmation targets the wrong picker state.
5. Select an option such as Model and observe the nested value picker has the same unnormalized boundary.

## Investigation

There are 12 vim.ui.select call sites across chat, context, and diff UI. In addition to session options, selectors that are asynchronous, nested, or exposed through public Chat methods can inherit insert mode: resumed-session selection, remembered-permission selection and confirmation, session switch/close, agent selection, and file/skill context selection. The permission picker is now protected. The diff-review selector is currently protected indirectly because the focused diff buffer exits insert mode before its normal-mode actions run.

## Scope

- Normalize mode at the narrowest shared LouiseLM selection boundary immediately before opening every vim.ui.select picker.
- Cover both stages of the session-options flow, especially the model/value picker opened by :LouiselmSessionOptions and the automatic picker scheduled by Chat:attach.
- Migrate or audit every raw vim.ui.select call in lua/louiselm/ui so no insert-mode-sensitive sibling remains.
- Preserve provider ownership of picker layout and interaction; do not detect or configure Snacks or another provider.
- Preserve selection values, cancellation behavior, asynchronous scheduling, and disposal guards.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The automatically opened session-options overview is invoked outside insert mode after Chat:attach starts the prompt in insert mode.
2. The nested model/boolean value picker is also invoked outside insert mode.
3. Every LouiseLM vim.ui.select call either uses the shared normalization boundary or has a tested invariant proving insert mode cannot reach it.
4. The existing permission-picker mode regression remains green, and diff review remains in normal mode.
5. Headless behavioral tests cover the session-options regression and at least one representative shared/public or asynchronous selector path without relying on provider internals.
6. The focused UI tests, full MiniTest suite, StyLua check, and lua-language-server check pass.
close_reason: Normalized all 12 vim.ui.select call sites through one normal-mode picker boundary. Added red-green regressions for automatic/nested session options and file context selection. Verification: focused chat 44/44, context 5/5, diff 5/5; full MiniTest 185/185; StyLua and LuaLS passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Keep the chat header compact instead of dumping session metadata
description:
## Problem

The chat buffer header expands into a long Markdown heading containing every session option and context field. At normal split widths it wraps across visual rows, dominates the top of the conversation, and is difficult to scan.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat session whose agent reports several configuration options plus context or cost telemetry.
2. Display the chat in a typical narrow vertical split.
3. Observe that the level-one Markdown heading includes all metadata and wraps across multiple visual rows.

## Observed

A Codex session currently renders a heading such as:

`# codex · session-1 · ready · Mode=agent-full-access · Collaboration mode=default · Model=gpt-5.6-sol · Reasoning effort=xhigh · Fast mode=off · context=62585/258400 (24% normal) · Your turn`

The screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0534_1920x1200_1786246460.png` shows this heading wrapping in the chat split.

## Expected

The transcript heading remains a compact, stable summary of session identity and current turn state, for example `# codex · session-1 · ready · Your turn`. Detailed configuration and telemetry remain discoverable through session options or a separate secondary status surface instead of being concatenated into an unbounded Markdown heading.

## Likely Root Cause

`session_summary()` appends every `config_options` entry plus context and cost telemetry, and `session_header()` uses the complete summary as the level-one Markdown heading. The heading length therefore scales with agent capabilities and enabled metadata.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The level-one chat heading contains only concise session identity/lifecycle/turn information and stays readable at a typical vertical split width.
2. Static/default fields such as mode, collaboration mode, model, reasoning effort, and fast mode are not dumped into the transcript heading.
3. Detailed configuration remains accessible through the existing session-options flow or another clearly defined secondary surface; do not silently remove the ability to inspect or change supported options.
4. Useful dynamic telemetry such as context pressure or cost, if retained in the UI, is presented outside the primary Markdown heading and does not make that heading grow without bound.
5. Header updates for state changes, renamed sessions, loaded sessions, and turn transitions continue to work.
6. Add or update headless UI behavior tests using a session with several config options and context telemetry. Assert the compact buffer heading and continued access to configuration; use a manual narrow-split smoke check for wrapping rather than a pixel assertion.

## Scope

- In scope: chat header/status presentation and its behavioral tests.
- Out of scope: changing ACP session metadata, removing configuration controls, or redesigning the rest of the transcript.
close_reason: Split compact session identity from the detailed switcher summary so chat headings contain only name/agent/id/lifecycle/turn while options and telemetry remain accessible. Verification: focused chat suite 27/27 passed; full mini.test suite 112/112 passed; stylua --check . passed; lua-language-server reported zero diagnostics; 48-column headless smoke passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Beads inspector cannot locate workspace from session
description:
The Beads issue inspector fails to locate the workspace when invoked with `<leader>lB` on a Beads issue in a LouiseLM chat session, reporting `louiselm: could not locate Beads workspace`. This prevents inspecting the issue under the cursor from the session buffer.

## Observed

Reported 2026-08-28 in session `codex/01a04621-223a-7c83-982e-94c88435ed5b`, with the cursor on line 281. Reproduction: press `<leader>lB`.

Observed error:

> louiselm: could not locate Beads workspace

The keymap routes `<leader>lB` to `:LouiselmInspectBead` (`lua/louiselm/ui/keymaps.lua:35`). The command invokes `Beads.inspect` (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:398-426`). Workspace discovery runs `br where --json` with `cwd = options.cwd or nvim.fn.getcwd()` (`lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:215-226`). Any nonzero `br where` exit is collapsed into the reported error at `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:225-227`.

## Symptoms

- Pressing `<leader>lB` on a line containing a Beads issue does not open the issue inspector.
- LouiseLM reports that it could not locate a Beads workspace.
- The session and line context are not enough to make the lookup succeed.

## Root cause

Unknown. The reported message does not preserve `br where`'s stderr, exit status, or resolved cwd, so it is not yet possible to distinguish an incorrect cwd, a missing/unavailable workspace, or another `br` failure. Capture the command result and working directory for this reproduction before assigning the mechanism.

## Why it was not caught

Existing tests cover successful workspace discovery and issue inspection with explicit test cwd values, but do not cover a real Session buffer invoking the keymap with the session's actual cwd and a failing `br where` result.

## Fix direction

Reproduce using the supplied session and capture the actual cwd plus `br where --json` stderr/exit status. Then make the inspector use the requesting Session's workspace cwd, or report the underlying lookup failure if the workspace genuinely is absent. Preserve actionable command diagnostics instead of reducing every nonzero exit to the same message.

## Acceptance

- `<leader>lB` on the supplied session's line 281 successfully resolves and opens the Beads issue when the session belongs to a Beads workspace.
- If lookup genuinely cannot run, the user-visible error identifies the actual cause and cwd.
- A regression test covers the Session/keymap path and the relevant workspace lookup failure or cwd behavior.

## Not covered

The issue ID under the cursor and the exact `br where` stderr/exit code were not captured in the report. No root cause is asserted yet.
close_reason: Fixed in the current working tree (not committed because the repository contains pre-existing user changes). Root cause: inspect_bead omitted the active Session's working_dir, causing Beads discovery to use the unrelated current editor cwd. The command now forwards state.working_dir. Regression: tests/ui/command_spec.lua 'inspects Beads from the active Session workspace'. Verification: focused command tests 32/32 pass; beads tests 10/10 pass; full suite 701/701 pass; stylua --check passes; lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning passes. No deviation from acceptance criteria.

comments.author: codex/01a04621-223a-7c83-982e-94c88435ed5b
comments.text: Root cause confirmed: :LouiselmInspectBead called Beads.inspect without cwd, so discovery defaulted to nvim.fn.getcwd() instead of the active Session's authoritative state.working_dir. Fixed in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua by forwarding that cwd. Added tests/ui/command_spec.lua regression that changes editor cwd after session creation and verifies Beads receives the Session workspace. No standing AGENTS.md rule is warranted; this is an issue-local ownership bug.

title: Show the current Decision evidence timeline
description:
## Goal
From a Decision anchor, show how agreement became implementation and human confidence.

## Scope
- In scope: a read-only Decision detail/evidence timeline composed from the question issue, implementation slices, commits, Sessions, QA acceptance markers, and Forensics pointers when available.
- Out of scope: historical snapshots, inferred QA acceptance, automatic judgments of correctness, and a separate evidence database.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The timeline shows the Decision anchor and attributable implementation relationships.
2. Explicit and inferred relationships are visibly distinct with method/confidence.
3. A human QA acceptance marker is shown only when attributable and tied to a commit.
4. Missing Sessions, transcripts, QA evidence, or Forensics remain explicit unresolved gaps.
5. The view is read-only and preserves source ownership.

## Testing
Fixture-based core tests plus a headless UI smoke test covering complete, partial, unresolved, and inferred evidence paths.

## Notes
Trust is represented as an evidence lifecycle, not a single score.
close_reason: Implemented in ca9b72b; Decision detail now renders read-only evidence timeline with commit/Session attribution, explicit QA acceptance, Forensics pointers, and unresolved gaps. Focused and full MiniTest, StyLua, LuaLS, API appendix, and diff checks pass.

comments.author: codex/01a0437d-5ba4-7ca0-b49f-722c5d4e29aa
comments.text: Implemented in ca9b72b. The pure Decision timeline derives existing bvr issue-to-commit edges and attributable Session edges, preserves recorded versus inferred method/confidence, accepts only an attributable QA accepted marker whose commit matches correlated history, and surfaces optional Forensics pointers plus unresolved gaps. The UI now opens louiselm://provenance/decision/<id> read-only from the Decision index. Tests cover complete, inferred, unresolved, and disposal-safe paths; no AGENTS rule or design question warranted.

title: State the emission rule and needs-capability vocabulary in AGENTS.md
description:
## Goal
Add the emission obligation and the label vocabulary to AGENTS.md, so a session
that cannot finish its work, or that notices something outside it, records that
as data instead of prose.

## Scope
- In scope: one rule in AGENTS.md section 2 naming both triggers concretely
  ("you could not complete the work" / "you noticed something outside it"); the
  label-versus-blocker test in one line; the `needs-capability:*` namespaced
  vocabulary; an explicit carve-out on the existing `br scheduler` preference.
- In scope: applying the resulting label to louiselm-qbr.1.10 as the first real
  use, and replacing its prose comment's role (the comment stays as history).
- Out of scope: the louiselm agent `capabilities` config field (sibling task),
  any skill, documenting the other 90 undocumented labels, and fixing
  `br scheduler`.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. AGENTS.md names both emission triggers in concrete terms, not as "facts worth
   keeping" -- vagueness is what produced the original prose comment.
2. The label-versus-blocker test appears as one line: does something have to
   change before anyone can do this?
3. `needs-capability:*` is documented as the namespace for standing requirements.
4. The `br scheduler` preference in section 2 carries a carve-out stating that
   capability-aware selection must use `br ready --label-any`, referencing
   louiselm-scheduler-labels-xw1i, and stating the carve-out is removed when that
   bug closes.
5. louiselm-qbr.1.10 carries `needs-capability:image-generation`, and
   `br ready --label-any needs-capability:image-generation` returns it.
6. The rule is stated so an agent with no skills available can comply from
   AGENTS.md alone.

## Testing
Documentation change; no automated test applies. Verify by running
`br ready --label-any needs-capability:image-generation` and confirming
louiselm-qbr.1.10 is selected, and that a plain `br ready` still lists it (a
label is not a blocker).

## Notes
Reasoning and rejected alternatives are on the parent, louiselm-capability-routing-m3sc.
Keep the addition short. Section 2 is already dense, and a rule nobody finishes
reading is the failure mode being fixed.
close_reason: Added emission rule, label-vs-blocker test, and needs-capability:* vocabulary to AGENTS.md section 2, plus the br scheduler carve-out for capability-aware routing. qbr.1.10 already carries the label; see comment on AC5.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: AC5 verification note: louiselm-qbr.1.10 already carries needs-capability:image-generation (confirmed via 'br label list louiselm-qbr.1.10'), but a codex session closed it before this task ran, so 'br ready --label-any needs-capability:image-generation' now returns nothing -- br ready only surfaces open work, and the issue it would have surfaced is done. The label and the routing mechanism both work as designed; the specific verification command in the AC is unsatisfiable post hoc because the target issue completed in the interim.

title: Assistant fails to recognize available OpenCode session ID
description:
## Problem

The assistant sometimes claims that no attributable OpenCode session ID is available and refuses to perform a Beads mutation, even when the session ID is present in the interaction context.

## Observed

On 2026-08-30, while processing the shared ChatGPT URL https://chatgpt.com/share/6a943166-c51c-83eb-ba80-9d8a79830de8, the assistant repeatedly said it could not file a Beads issue because no actor/session ID was exposed. The maintainer then supplied the valid actor: opencode/ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney.

The assistant had also discovered related OpenCode session identifiers in tool results and existing Beads records, but did not reliably distinguish the current session identifier from missing environment variables.

## Impact

The assistant unnecessarily blocks requested issue filing and asks the maintainer for information that may already be available, adding friction and risking untracked work.

## Expected behavior

Before declaring the actor unavailable, inspect the complete interaction/tool context for the current OpenCode session ID. If a valid opencode/<session-id> is available and points to an open transcript, use it as the Beads --actor value. Only ask the maintainer when no current attributable ID can be established.

## Acceptance

- A reproducible test or documented harness check demonstrates that the current OpenCode session ID is discovered when present outside the environment-variable list.
- The assistant does not substitute a stale session ID from another Beads record or a child-agent task ID.
- When no current ID exists, the assistant still asks rather than inventing one.

## Related

- louiselm-adapter-session-id-exposure-fq4k tracks the upstream adapter problem where session IDs are absent from shell environment variables. This bug concerns assistant-side failure to recognize an ID that is available in context.
close_reason: Document live OpenCode actor lookup and cover it

comments.author: codex/01a053d7-4308-76c0-9eac-a9e424812c48
comments.text: Completion evidence: AGENTS.md:291 now requires using the live Chat:session_id() result verbatim, including opencode/<ACP-session-id>, and rejecting stale Beads/child-task IDs. tests/ui/command_spec.lua covers an OpenCode Session ID with no environment variable. Existing :LouiselmSessionId and Chat:session_id() already provide the value; no runtime code change was needed. Lesson: adapter environment variables are not the authority when live Session state is available; related adapter exposure gaps remain in louiselm-adapter-session-id-exposure-fq4k.

title: QA round: resumed Codex chat fixes (4296678)
description:
# Manual QA review — resumed Codex chat fixes

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `4296678` (`fix(chat): stabilize resumed session
submission`). **Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: this round covers the two fixes that landed after the previous QA
round: prompt submission now follows the visible prompt through transcript
edits (including undo/redo), and an ACP load conflict from a second live client
now reports an actionable active-writer message instead of the opaque `Internal
error`.

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Submit a visible draft after transcript undo/redo edits | **passed** — `codex/01a02236-1ab0-7373-bba1-b266d9f69c79`; buffer snapshot and response log contain the second token |
| 2 | Active-writer resume failure is actionable and recovery succeeds | **passed** — `codex/01a02239-911a-7b72-9b46-857886cdcf6e`; exact sanitized notification and recovered response log verified |

## Setup

Use two terminals for Case 2. From the repository root, verify the checkout:

```sh

nvim -u ./manual_init.lua
```

The first command must print `4296678` (or a descendant containing this
commit). In each Neovim process, configure the real Codex ACP agent before
opening chat:

```vim
:lua print(require("louiselm.acp").PROTOCOL_VERSION)
:lua assert(require("louiselm").setup({ agents = { codex = { command = "codex-acp", args = {} } }, skills = { policy = "off" } }))
:checkhealth louiselm
```

The protocol print must succeed, health must show `codex` usable, and the chat
header must identify the Codex agent. Restart Neovim after any code change;
Lua modules are cached per process. Start each case with a fresh chat session.

Create an isolated evidence directory and clear only old matching response
logs (move them somewhere recoverable if you need to inspect them later):

```sh
qa_root=/tmp/louiselm-qa-4296678
mkdir -p "$qa_root/old-logs"
mv ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*codex-acp*stdout-jsonrpc.log "$qa_root/old-logs/" 2>/dev/null || true
```

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Use a fresh ACP session for each case. Case 2 deliberately needs the first
  Neovim process to remain the active writer while the second process tries to
  load it.
- Run both processes from `/home/lotso/code/louiselm` so `:LouiselmResume`
  (without `!`) searches the same workspace. Use `:LouiselmResume!` only as a
  diagnostic if the current-workspace picker is empty, and record that as a
  recipe/setup problem rather than silently changing the case.
- The adapter debug wrapper records replies, not the outgoing
  `session/prompt` request. The response token and the exact UI notification
  are therefore the decisive evidence.
- If a permission or options overview appears, complete or dismiss it before
  typing the case prompt. Do not use a mock agent or a debug/approval-skip mode
  for these live cases.

## Cases

### 1. Submit a visible draft after transcript undo/redo edits

Exercises commit `4296678`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` prompt extmark
tracking and the real buffer-local `<CR>` mapping.

Steps:

1. In the first Neovim, run `:LouiselmNewSession` (or `:LouiselmChat` if no
   chat exists) and wait for `Session: status=ready`.
2. Submit this exact first prompt and wait until the answer and a new editable
   `> ` prompt are visible:

   ```text
   Reply with exactly QA-4296678-FIRST and nothing else.
   ```

3. Type, but do not submit, this second draft:

   ```text
   Reply with exactly QA-4296678-SECOND and nothing else.
   ```

4. Press `Esc`, search for the visible `QA-4296678-FIRST` answer with `/`,
   delete that answer line with `dd`, then press `u` and `Ctrl-r` to exercise
   the same undo/redo boundary movement that can shift the transcript. Press
   `G` to return to the last prompt line, re-enter insert mode with `A`, and
   ensure the draft still visibly ends in `QA-4296678-SECOND`.
5. Press Enter. Wait for the second turn to finish.
6. Run `:LouiselmSessionId` and retain the `<agent>/<ACP-session-id>` shown in
   the notification. Capture the visible buffer immediately:

   ```vim
   :lua vim.fn.writefile(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0,0,-1,false), "/tmp/louiselm-qa-4296678/case-1-buffer.txt")
   ```

Expect: the second turn is submitted once; the assistant returns
`QA-4296678-SECOND`; focus ends in the new editable prompt; the visible draft
is not lost or replaced by an empty prompt.

Failure signature: Enter produces no turn, a `prompt cannot be empty`/similar
error, the second token never appears, the draft disappears, or focus remains
inside the old transcript instead of the new prompt.

## Evidence check

From another shell, locate the response log by the unique token and print only
agent chunks:

```sh
for f in ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*codex-acp*stdout-jsonrpc.log; do
  grep -q 'QA-4296678-SECOND' "$f" 2>/dev/null || continue
  echo "LOG=$f"
  python3 - "$f" <<'PY'
import json, sys
for line in open(sys.argv[1]):
    try:
        msg = json.loads(line)
    except Exception:
        continue
    update = msg.get("params", {}).get("update", {})
    if update.get("sessionUpdate") == "agent_message_chunk":
        print(update.get("content", {}).get("text", ""), end="")
print()
PY
done
```

Pass evidence is one response containing `QA-4296678-SECOND`, plus the saved
buffer showing a final editable `> ` line. The log proves the real peer
responded; it cannot prove cursor placement, which comes from the buffer and
the tester's observation.

### 2. Active-writer resume failure is actionable and recovery succeeds

Exercises commit `4296678`, `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua` active-writer
error sanitization, and the real `:LouiselmResume`/`session/load` path.

Steps:

1. In Neovim A, start a fresh Codex session and wait until it is ready. Submit:

   ```text
   Reply with exactly QA-4296678-WRITER and nothing else.
   ```

2. Wait for the response, run `:LouiselmSessionId`, and record the exact
   `codex/<session-id>`. Leave Neovim A open; it is intentionally still the
   active writer. Do not run `:LouiselmCloseSession` yet.
3. In Neovim B, repeat Setup, run `:LouiselmResume` **without** `!`, and select
   the `QA-4296678-WRITER` session from the current-workspace picker.
4. Expect the load to fail visibly. Record the complete notification and take
   a screenshot or copy the message before doing anything else.
5. Close the writer in Neovim A with `:LouiselmCloseSession`, then close that
   Neovim process. In Neovim B, run `:LouiselmResume` again and select the same
   session.
6. Wait for `Session: status=ready`. The replayed `QA-4296678-WRITER` turn
   should be visible, followed by a usable editable `> ` prompt. Submit:

   ```text
   Reply with exactly QA-4296678-RECOVERED and nothing else.
   ```

7. Run `:LouiselmSessionId` and retain the id for the recovered process.

Expect on the first load: a specific message equivalent to
`ACP session/load failed: session is already open in another client; close it
there before resuming`; no thread id, raw JSON, or generic-only `Internal error`
is shown. The failed load must not make Neovim B hang. After Neovim A closes,
the second resume succeeds, replays the old turn, accepts a new prompt, and
returns `QA-4296678-RECOVERED`.

Failure signature: the picker cannot find the session in the same workspace;
load reports only `Internal error`; a thread id or raw adapter payload leaks;
Neovim B hangs/crashes; the second resume remains poisoned after A closes; or
the recovered prompt is lost.

## Evidence check

For the first failed load, save the exact notification text from Neovim B. It
must contain `session/load failed` and `session is already open in another
client`, and must not contain `Internal error` or `thread `.

For the successful recovery, save a buffer snapshot and locate the response
log containing the unique recovery token:

```vim
:lua vim.fn.writefile(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0,0,-1,false), "/tmp/louiselm-qa-4296678/case-2-recovered.txt")
```

```sh
rg -l 'QA-4296678-RECOVERED' ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*codex-acp*stdout-jsonrpc.log
```

The notification proves sanitization and non-hanging failure handling. The
recovered buffer plus the token-bearing response log prove the loaded session
became usable; neither alone proves the other part.

## Cleanup when the round closes

Close both Neovim processes and remove the isolated evidence directory:

```sh
rm -rf /tmp/louiselm-qa-4296678
```

The moved old logs in `/tmp/louiselm-qa-4296678/old-logs` are included in that
cleanup. No repository files should remain changed except this scratch file.

## Reporting back

Send me the case number, the exact session id, what you saw, and the relevant
evidence path or notification text. If something is wrong, stop before
repairing or retrying it; I will pull the evidence, file a beads bug before
fixing it, and tell you which cases need a fresh Setup rerun.

## Findings this round

No product findings yet.

## Results this round

  `/tmp/louiselm-qa-4296678/case-1-buffer.txt` shows both authored prompts,

  `QA-4296678-SECOND` response followed by a fresh editable `> ` prompt. The

  `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260821-044605-1285383-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`
  contains streamed chunks for both `QA-4296678-FIRST` and
  `QA-4296678-SECOND`, proving the second Enter reached the real peer after
  the transcript delete/undo/redo edits.

- Case 2 passed on `codex/01a02239-911a-7b72-9b46-857886cdcf6e` (the same
  agent-scoped ACP id was correctly shown in both clients). Neovim B reported
  `ACP session/load failed: session is already open in another client; close it
  there before resuming`, with no thread id or raw `Internal error` exposed.
  The adapter evidence for that failed load is
  `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260821-045143-1291981-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`;
  its raw peer error contains the active-writer details that the UI sanitized.
  After Neovim A closed, the load succeeded and
  `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260821-045336-1293760-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`
  contains the replayed `QA-4296678-WRITER` turn and the new
  `QA-4296678-RECOVERED` response. No buffer snapshot was captured for this
  case, so the exact UI replay/focus appearance rests on the tester's report;
  the protocol log proves the recovered session accepted and completed a new

## Round conclusion

Both cases passed on build `4296678`; no product findings were discovered.
The round confirmed the two behaviors automated tests cannot fully settle:

title: LouiselmToMarkdown prompts for a path before validating an explicit session id
description:
`:LouiselmToMarkdown <session_id>` prompts for a destination path before
checking whether `<session_id>` is actually attached, so an invalid id wastes
a full path-entry interaction before failing.

## Observed

Manual QA round on commits 674939b/4e4a58b, case 2.4 in QA_REVIEW.md. User
ran `:LouiselmToMarkdown not-a-session-id`, was shown the
"louiselm markdown path (blank for default):" prompt, typed a path, and only
then got the `louiselm: session is not attached` error. Expected (and every
other id-consuming failure in this command family gives) an immediate error
with no interactive prompt in between.

## Symptoms

- User types and confirms a file path for an export that was never going to
  happen.
- No data loss or crash — the eventual error message is correct — but the
  ordering is surprising and wastes an interaction.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:266-282`:

```lua
nvim.api.nvim_create_user_command("LouiselmToMarkdown", function(arguments)
  ...
  local session_id = arguments.args ~= "" and arguments.args or nil
  nvim.ui.input({ prompt = "louiselm markdown path (blank for default): " }, function(path)
    ...
    local written_path, write_error = chat:to_markdown(session_id, path ~= "" and path or nil)
    ...
```

The session-id validity check lives inside `Chat:to_markdown`
(`init.lua:1553-1557`), which only runs after `vim.ui.input`'s callback
fires. `command.lua` has no way to check `session_id` validity up front
without reaching into `Chat`'s private `self.views` table.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` covers "not attached" at the
`Chat:to_markdown` level directly (bypassing the command layer), and
`tests/ui/command_spec.lua` stubs `vim.ui.input` so it never observes prompt
ordering relative to session validation. No test exercises the command's
real `vim.ui.input` flow with a bad session id end to end.

## Fix direction

Add a small public predicate, e.g. `Chat:is_attached(session_id)` (mirroring
the existing inline check in `Chat:switch`, init.lua:1444-1461), and have
`LouiselmToMarkdown` call it before opening the `vim.ui.input` prompt when an
explicit session id was given, reporting the error immediately instead.

Deliberately not fixing in the same pass as louiselm-dim, to keep that fix's
batch to the one crash bug; this is UX ordering, not a crash.

## Acceptance

- A test (likely in tests/ui/command_spec.lua, alongside its existing
  `vim.ui.input` stub) asserting that `:LouiselmToMarkdown <bad-id>` reports
  "session is not attached" without ever invoking the input prompt.
- Manually confirmed: `:LouiselmToMarkdown not-a-session-id` shows the error
  immediately, no path prompt.

## Not covered

Whether other future id-taking commands should share this predicate — only
`LouiselmToMarkdown` takes a raw typed session id today.
close_reason:
Added Chat:is_attached(session_id) (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua, immediately before Chat:switch) and had LouiselmToMarkdown validate an explicitly typed session id before opening its destination-path prompt (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua). An unknown id now reports 'louiselm: session is not attached' immediately, with no path prompt.

TDD: the new test 'rejects an unknown session id without prompting for a path' failed first with input_calls == 1 against an expected 0 -- the exact ordering defect -- and passes after the change. The pre-existing explicit-id test could not catch this because its vim.ui.input stub invokes its callback at once and never observes that the prompt opened; the new stub counts calls. A second test asserts a VALID explicit id still prompts (input_calls == 1), covering the over-rejection risk the fix introduces.

Acceptance criteria 1 met. Criterion 2, interactive confirmation at a real keyboard, was NOT performed: the new test drives the production command path through nvim_cmd with a counting vim.ui.input stub, which is the same code path, but no human ran it. Worth one step in the next QA round.

Gates: full MiniTest suite Fails (0) Notes (0); stylua --check . exit 0; lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning no problems found; git diff --check clean.

Filed while here: louiselm-f0n2 -- this spec has no post_case hook, so the red phase of this very fix turned 1 real failure into 9 reported ones, 7 pure cascade from leaked chat buffers. The two new tests clean up before asserting to avoid it; the existing cases were left alone.

comments.text:
