That is now two consecutive rounds finding it present and deliberately not fixing it. Worth deciding rather than re-testing: either fix the ordering (validate the session id before calling vim.ui.input) or downgrade to wontfix, so a third round does not spend a step re-establishing a known state.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Fixed on the third reconfirmation, per the rule louiselm-ini's round set (fix or wontfix, not another re-test).

Followed the issue's fix direction with one correction: the issue's line references had drifted. Chat:to_markdown is at init.lua:1820 (not 1553-1557) and its 'session is not attached' check is at :1827; Chat:switch is at :1714 with the mirrored check at :1720. command.lua:331-352 was accurate.

Added Chat:is_attached(session_id) returning (boolean, string?) immediately before Chat:switch, and had LouiselmToMarkdown call it before nvim.ui.input when, and only when, an explicit session id was given. The predicate checks self.disposed before self.views so the disposed-chat path keeps reporting 'chat UI is disposed' rather than being flattened into 'session is not attached' -- the pre-check does not change any existing error string.

Two tests, not one. The issue asked for the bad-id case; the valid-id case is the regression risk the fix introduces (a predicate that rejects too much would silently break normal exports), so 'still prompts for a path when an explicit session id is attached' asserts input_calls == 1. That test also exposed that views are keyed by the session's own state.id, not the ACP sessionId the spec echoes, so it reads the id back from the chat buffer's 'louiselm://<id>' name instead of hardcoding one.

The 'Not covered' question stands unchanged: LouiselmToMarkdown is still the only command taking a raw typed session id, so is_attached has one caller. Nothing was generalised for hypothetical future ones.

title: Write the example workflow document under docs/
description:
Write the maintainer's own workflow loop as an explicitly non-binding example document, at a `docs/` path.

This is the loop actually run today: **grill-me** (an idea gets direct attention and is interrogated one question at a time) → **to-beads** (the agreed plan becomes beads work items at the right abstraction level) → **sessions** (tasks get executed, automated or not) → **qa-review** (the maintainer manually tests what was just committed, and a defect found routes to `to-beads-bug`).

## Why this document exists

Two reasons, and both matter:

1. Other people, and other agents, may invent entirely different loops. Writing this one down as an *example* rather than a rule is what makes that possible without it reading as deviation from a contract.
2. louiselm intends to eventually ship this loop as an example **workflow config** — the maintainer's standing goal is that their workflow becomes expressible as configuration rather than convention. This document is the first draft of that spec. When the workflow-engine issues are picked up, this is what they implement against, rather than the loop being reconstructed from memory.

## What to write

Descriptive voice, not imperative — this describes what one person does, it does not instruct the reader. It must self-identify as a non-binding example in its opening, because the reader may arrive here without having read the link text in `AGENTS.md`.

Cover: what triggers each stage, what each stage hands to the next, and what "skill chaining" means here (one skill's output is designed to trigger another — grill-me ends by invoking to-beads; a qa-review defect invokes to-beads-bug).

Be honest about the known gap: a qa-review round can surface a *process* finding rather than a code bug, and there is currently no formalized route for that. It survives only by the maintainer noticing and calling for a grill-me session.

## Placement

A `docs/` path, not repo root. A root-level uppercase filename reads as law regardless of any disclaimer inside it, and that misreading is the specific thing this document must avoid. Do not create additional structure under `docs/` beyond what this one file needs.

## Acceptance criteria

- The document exists under `docs/` and declares itself a non-binding example within its opening lines.
- Each stage of the loop is described with its trigger and its handoff to the next stage.
- The unresolved process-finding gap is stated rather than papered over.
- It is written so that a future workflow-config implementation could use it as a starting spec, without committing to a config schema that does not exist yet.
- Voice is descriptive throughout; it never instructs the reader to adopt the loop.
close_reason: AGENTS.md section 2 added (sections renumbered 3-12), CLAUDE.md pointer added, docs/example-workflow.md written, triage requirement commented onto qbr.3/qbr.5, all seven memory notes migrated to repo or user-level instructions

title: Surface agent_thought_chunk reasoning in Sessions
description:
## Goal

Stop dropping ACP `agent_thought_chunk` reasoning updates. LouiseLM should emit
them as typed Session events, render them in chat (folded by default), and
include them in transcript export, for every Agent whose adapter emits them.

## Evidence

- ACP spec (`agent-client-protocol-schema` 0.13.6, built by the adapters):
  `agent_thought_chunk` is a stable `SessionUpdate` variant carrying a
  `ContentChunk` ("A chunk of the agent's internal reasoning being streamed",
  client.rs v1/v2). The `usage.thoughtTokens` counter is separate and
  feature-gated UNSTABLE — not what this issue is about (that path is already
  handled, see louiselm-4tum).
- `acp-llm-adapter` maps DeepSeek `delta.reasoning_content` →
  `AgentThoughtChunk` (llm/stream.rs parse_chat_completion_chunk, turn.rs).
- `claude-agent-acp` maps SDK `thinking` / `thinking_delta` stream events →
  `agent_thought_chunk` when the text is non-empty (acp-agent.ts ~8381);
  subagent thinking forwards under the same stream.
- `codex-acp` maps `item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta` and `item/reasoning/textDelta`
  (plus completed reasoning items on history/replay) → `agent_thought_chunk`
  (CodexAcpServer.ts createReasoningUpdates).
- Live evidence on this machine:
  `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/connections/*.jsonl` contains 6,403
  `agent_thought_chunk` frames across 7 captured sessions (all DeepSeek so
  far), e.g. actual chain-of-thought text chunks with `messageId`.

## Current behavior

`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua` `handle_notification` branches on
`agent_message_chunk`, `user_message_chunk`, tool calls, config, usage, and
commands; `agent_thought_chunk` falls through silently.
`lua/louiselm/session/events.lua` defines no thought event type, and
`lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua` records only user/assistant/tool blocks.
The reasoning text therefore exists only in the adapter's raw ACP log.

## Scope

- In scope: a typed thought/reasoning event emitted during live turns, in
  stream order; chat rendering collapsed/folded by default, expandable per
  turn; reasoning blocks included in transcript export; replay of resumed
  sessions whose agent history carries thought chunks (codex-acp does).
- Out of scope: thought token counts (already normalized/rendered/persisted);
  a separate durable reasoning store beyond the transcript; the forensics
  `acp_log` omission (separate finding, louiselm-6qt style).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A live Agent emitting `agent_thought_chunk` produces thought events ordered
   between the user content and the assistant response.
2. Chat renders each turn's reasoning in a collapsed fold by default and can
   expand it.
3. Transcript export includes reasoning blocks; resuming an exported session
   does not duplicate them.
4. Agents that never emit thought chunks (mock agent, Claude without extended
   thinking, Codex without reasoning) behave exactly as today — no empty folds.
5. Regression tests drive a fake ACP agent emitting the camelCase wire shape
   and assert the full session-event → chat-fold → transcript path.

## Testing

Red-first through the Session API and UI specs with a fake agent fixture that
emits `agent_thought_chunk` frames; gates are stylua, lua-language-server, and
the headless MiniTest suite.

## Notes

Reasoning text is the model's chain of thought and can be sensitive; it stays
in local Session state and transcript only, no new persistence surface.
Coverage differs by provider: DeepSeek emits full chain-of-thought text,
Claude emits extended-thinking text when the model streams it (recent models
may default to signature-only/omitted display, in which case the adapter skips
empty chunks), and Codex emits reasoning summaries.
close_reason: Already implemented in c56805f and 1395bfd; verified end-to-end and all Lua gates pass.

Live A/B proof (2026-08-25), from this machine's own codex logs:

1) Why the Codex TUI shows nothing: the TUI's TurnInputRequest sends summary: None (Submission debug line for thread 01a03975-7cdd-7fd3-90b8-2dccf5ab095d: model: Some("gpt-5.6-luna"), effort: Some(Some(Medium)), summary: None). 2) Why louiselm WILL get reasoning: codex-acp overrides summary:"auto" in runTurn (CodexAcpClient.ts:904) and does not fall back to the catalog default. Live proof: this louiselm codex session itself (acp-proxy pid 2162131 -> codex-acp -> codex.js app-server pid 2162168) is emitting item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta events right now (20 this turn), and the acp-proxy session log proxy/sessions/01a0397c-0711-72b0-9d48-76eda8f591d6/log.jsonl contains 64 agent_thought_chunk frames, 34 with real text.

3) Implementation-relevant format note: codex reasoning summaries arrive as headline-style markdown chunks, e.g. '**Planning bug filing with image inspection****Inspecting images and searching duplicates**' (adjacent bold headlines, no separators). The chat fold should probably render these as a list/section rather than raw concatenated prose. Also observed: the messageId is the Responses API id (rs_...) so chunk correlation works the same as message chunks.

comments.author: claude/9587f553-1d67-4622-9726-fda85bbfc85b
comments.text:
Took over from the stalled deepseek session (louiselm/session-790f2160-642e-4d77-b794-706b754acda1, assignee of record) at the user's explicit request; that session's own claim was still fresh by coordination policy, not abandoned, so noting the handoff here rather than silently reassigning.

Root cause of the 4 failing tests it left behind: Neovim cannot close a fold spanning a single buffer line — `:fold`/`zf` on a 1-line range is a documented no-op, confirmed directly against a bare scratch buffer. The implementation folded only the reasoning *content* line, leaving the `[thinking]` header outside the fold; since a streamed reasoning paragraph almost always lands on one buffer line (chunks append to the same line unless the text itself contains a newline), that fold could never close. The stalled session spent its remaining turns poking at `:fold`/foldmethod/foldenable state without ever hitting this constraint.

Fix: fold the header together with its content instead of leaving it outside (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`, `close_thought_fold_run`). This always spans >=2 lines, and Neovim's default foldtext renders the fold's first line — the header — as the closed summary, which matches the intended UX with no custom foldtext needed. Updated the now-incorrect fold-range assertions in `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` and the equivalent case in `tests/mock/agent_spec.lua`.

Full suite: 540 cases, 0 failures attributable to this feature (one unrelated pre-existing vimdoc_spec failure remains, caused by a different concurrently-active agent's in-flight command.lua change for louiselm-zmab — left untouched). stylua and lua-language-server clean on the touched files.

comments.author: claude/161e0a06-dea4-471b-99de-caa1ea641212
comments.text:
User-facing gap found downstream of this feature: the plugin's own README
example config (`claude = { command = "claude-agent-acp", args = {} }`, no
`env`) never enables extended thinking on the Claude side, so a user following
the README verbatim gets zero `agent_thought_chunk` frames regardless of how
correct the fold/render/transcript work here is - `claude-agent-acp` leaves
its SDK `thinking` option unset (no reasoning stream) unless
`MAX_THINKING_TOKENS` is set in its process environment (confirmed against
that adapter's own test suite, create-session-options.test.ts ~L513-573: 0 ->
disabled, positive int -> `{ type: "enabled", budgetTokens: N }`, unset ->
`undefined`/"SDK default").

Fixed the doc gap: README.md:193 now sets
`env = { MAX_THINKING_TOKENS = "16384" }` on the example `claude` agent
definition (16384 chosen as a round power-of-two ceiling in the ~8K-16K range;
it's a cap billed only on actual use, not a reservation).

Filed a follow-up, louiselm-2bar, for the more durable fix: `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS`
maps to the deprecated `budget_tokens` thinking config, which the current
Anthropic model family (Opus 5 / Sonnet 5 / Fable 5) rejects with a 400 - only
Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 still accept it. `claude-agent-acp` also accepts a
session-level `_meta.claudeCode.options.thinking = { type: "adaptive" }`
override that works regardless of model tier, but louiselm has no passthrough
for arbitrary `_meta` on `session/new`/`session/load` today - `options` on
`agent.Definition` is validated/stored and never read
(lua/louiselm/agent/config.lua:426, lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:522,526).
Not blocking this issue; the env-var fix holds until the adapter's default
model tier moves past 4.6.

title: tests/ui/command_spec.lua has no post_case hook, so one failing test cascades into seven more
description:
Every case in tests/ui/command_spec.lua opens a chat buffer and cleans it up
by calling delete_chat_buffers() as its last statement. MiniTest aborts a case
at the first failed expectation, so a case that fails before that line leaves
its "louiselm://<id>" buffer open, and every later case that opens a chat
buffer dies with:

  Vim:E95: Buffer with this name already exists
  lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1616

Observed 2026-08-21 while writing the louiselm-euj regression test: one
genuine assertion failure produced 9 reported failures, 7 of them pure
cascade. The real failure was third in the list, and the cascade failures name
a different file and line than the test that actually broke, which is actively
misleading when reading a red run.

Workaround used in the two tests added for louiselm-euj: call
delete_chat_buffers() before the assertions rather than after. That works but
relies on every future author remembering it, and the existing cases in this
file all still have the fragile ordering.

Fix direction: give T["command"] a hooks table with a post_case that calls
delete_chat_buffers() (and ideally restores vim.ui.input / vim.notify /
vim.system, which have the same abort-leaks-state problem), then drop the
manual trailing calls. MiniTest runs post_case hooks even when a case fails,
which is the property the manual call lacks.

Worth checking whether tests/ui/chat_spec.lua and the other UI specs share the
shape before fixing, so this is done once rather than per file.
close_reason: Completed: added a MiniTest post_case cleanup hook for louiselm:// chat buffers; focused 24-case and full 351-case suites pass.

title: bvr drops every custom-status record and hard-fails all time travel on this backlog
description:
## Symptom

`bvr` cannot see this project's vocabulary. Every invocation silently drops all
nine `status: reference` records, and every time-travel query fails outright.

One root cause, two different failure modes.

## Evidence

Live path — `bvr --stats` (v0.3.0, built from the synced fork today) prints to
stderr and continues:

```
Warning: skipping invalid issue on line 52 ...: issue louiselm-7bm3 has unknown status: reference
Warning: skipping invalid issue on line 54 ...: issue louiselm-7rjr has unknown status: reference
... (9 total: 7bm3, 7rjr, 9ohh, b79f, cvv3, cyb2, hb3p, qh7m, y3f3)
```

`br list --status all` reports 309 issues; bvr analyses 300. The nine it drops
are exactly the `vocabulary/reference` records that AGENTS.md ("Project
vocabulary") makes the canonical semantic source of truth. So every bvr
triage ranking, graph metric, PageRank/betweenness score, search result and
insight on this repo is computed over a corpus with the vocabulary removed.

This has presumably been true for as long as the vocabulary records have
existed (first created 2026-08-23) and was never noticed, because the warnings
go to stderr and agents read stdout — AGENTS.md itself instructs `bvr --robot-*`
usage whose output is routinely piped.

Historical path — same data, hard failure:

```console
$ bvr --robot-diff --diff-since HEAD~20
error: invalid argument: could not resolve --diff-since=HEAD~20 to a historical beads JSONL snapshot
```

The message is misleading: ref resolution is fine. `git cat-file -s
HEAD~20:.beads/issues.jsonl` returns 1449541, the blob decodes as clean UTF-8,
and all 285 lines parse as valid JSON. The snapshot simply contains 7 records
with `status: reference`, and the historical loader rejects the whole file
because of them.

Proof by contrast — the identical bytes load successfully through the
file-path form, which uses the lenient loader:

```console
$ git show d68b9d2:.beads/issues.jsonl > /tmp/old-issues.jsonl
$ bvr --robot-diff --diff-since /tmp/old-issues.jsonl     # works
```

And the same command against the beads_viewer_rust repo, whose backlog uses
only stock statuses, resolves `HEAD~20` fine on v0.3.0. The bug is data-shaped,
not ref-shaped.

## Root cause

`beads_viewer_rust/src/model.rs:6-16` — `KNOWN_STATUSES` is a fixed list
(open, in_progress, blocked, deferred, pinned, hooked, review, closed,
tombstone). `Issue::validate()` (model.rs:213) rejects anything else. `br`
supports custom statuses; `bvr` does not, and the two disagree about the same
JSONL file.

The two load paths then diverge in how they handle that rejection:

- `loader::load_issues_from_file` warns and skips the line (lenient).
- `parse_issues_from_jsonl_text` (main.rs:3619-3635) propagates with `?`, so a
  single unknown status aborts the entire historical load (strict).

Only the historical path uses the strict one. `load_issues_from_git_ref`
(main.rs:3363-3369) then wraps every underlying error in
`map_err(|_| ...)`, discarding the real cause and reporting it as a resolution
failure — which is why this reads as "git refs are unsupported" rather than
"one record has a status I do not know".

## Why it matters here

1. Correctness of everything bvr says about this backlog, today. Vocabulary
   records are invisible to triage and metrics, and nothing announces it on
   stdout.
2. It blocks the louiselm-06yh Door B design directly: `history/vintage.lua` is
   the module that reaches historical beads state by git ref, and on this repo
   that path cannot work at all until this is resolved.

## Disposition

Upstream defect in beads_viewer_rust (v0.3.0, reproduced against a build from
today's upstream `main`). The maintainer has explicitly deferred any upstream
action for now, so nothing has been filed or pushed to
Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer_rust or the euri10 fork. This bead exists so the
constraint is part of this project's record rather than one transcript.

Workaround available meanwhile: extract the snapshot first and use the
file-path form, `git show <ref>:.beads/issues.jsonl > tmp && bvr --robot-diff
--diff-since tmp`. That path is lenient, so it succeeds — while still silently
dropping the vocabulary records, which is the half of the bug the workaround
does not address.

Refs louiselm-06yh
Refs claude/ce71a8b9-3415-4247-a8a5-9e1ecf6ff943
close_reason: Implemented and pushed a fork fix in aac3e14; custom statuses and historical loads now work with preserved errors.

comments.text:

The report carries a two-line self-contained reproduction that does not depend on this backlog, so it can be verified without access to anything of ours. It proposes three separable changes: stop discarding the underlying error in load_issues_from_git_ref, give both load paths the same tolerance, and carry unknown statuses through as opaque values. It also offers a PR for the first two.

title: Grill-me needed: How should GitHub bug reports request Forensics/logs without leaking secrets?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing. Facilitate a dedicated decision
about how LouiseLM asks users for debugging evidence on GitHub without
handing them a way to accidentally leak secrets.

Question:
LouiseLM already has a Forensics command that writes a debugging JSON
record (e.g. ~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/<id>.json). Today that
record is metadata only - cwd, model, git commit/branch, dirty files,
capabilities, agent, session id - and its evidence_sources array already
has an acp_log entry, currently always "omitted" with a stated reason
(e.g. "ACP adapter did not advertise a log path"), meaning attaching real
log content is a foreseeable direction, not yet built. lua/louiselm/forensics
has zero redaction/secret-handling logic today (grepped for
acp_log/log_path/redact/secret/sensitive, no hits beyond the state field
name itself).

If a future version starts attaching real ACP log content to that JSON,
and a GitHub issue template then asks users to upload it for bug reports,
the log could contain prompts, tool payloads, file contents, or API
keys/tokens - anything the session touched. The maintainer's idea: use a
GitHub issue form that requests the Forensics JSON (and any attached
logs) as a required field, gated by an automated secret scan (e.g.
gitleaks) that runs against the submission and warns or blocks before the
report becomes visible.

Threads worth pulling:
- Does GitHub support blocking issue *submission* on a check, or only
  reacting after creation (Action triggered on issues: opened/edited)? If
  only reactive, what's the actual UX: auto-comment warning, auto-label,
  auto-redact-and-edit, or auto-close-and-ask-to-resubmit?
- Should redaction happen at the source (LouiseLM redacts known-sensitive
  fields - API keys, file contents, absolute paths with usernames - before
  the Forensics JSON is even written to disk) rather than relying on a
  GitHub-side net? A local redaction pass is the only option that also
  protects users who paste the file somewhere other than GitHub (Discord,
  a support DM, a public gist).
- If ACP log content is added to Forensics at all, what's the retention/
  inclusion default: opt-in flag at capture time, always-omitted-unless-
  requested, or included with an explicit interactive confirmation prompt
  each time?
- What does gitleaks (or an equivalent) actually catch here - it's tuned
  for credential patterns (API keys, tokens), not arbitrary sensitive
  content like a user's private file contents, proprietary code snippets,
  or PII in a prompt. Is a secret scanner sufficient, or does the issue
  template need a plain-language warning plus a manual review step
  regardless?
- Should the issue form require the Forensics JSON, or make it optional
  with instructions, given it may itself need to be sanitized before
  upload?
- Where does this fit relative to louiselm-h00g (Provenance: queryable
  commit/issue/Session lineage) and the wider Forensics feature - is this
  a Forensics-capture-time concern, a bug-report-tooling concern, or both?

Decision boundary:
Decide whether/how to add real log content to Forensics at all, what
redaction (if any) happens before a Forensics record is written or
exported, and what the GitHub issue-reporting flow (template + automated
scan + user-facing warning) looks like. Do not implement the issue
template or any redaction logic until the lifecycle and authority
boundary here are agreed.

title: Chat buffer filetype=markdown lets image.nvim re-scan the whole transcript on every keystroke
description:
Typing in the louiselm chat buffer's prompt line is noticeably laggy, at rest
-- not during active LLM response streaming. Reported by the user mid-session
while typing with no chunks arriving.

## Observed

Session claude/6a76322f-4f96-430b-93f3-578808c4692c, 2026-08-20, connected
directly to the user's live `nvim --embed` instance over RPC
(`/run/user/1000/nvim.253565.0`) to inspect real state instead of guessing.

Ruled out with direct measurement, in order:
- `render-markdown.nvim` (installed in dotfiles) is not loaded at all:
  `luaeval('tostring(package.loaded["render-markdown"] ~= nil)')` -> `false`.
- Buffer size/decoration overhead is trivial: the chat buffer (bufnr 12,
  `louiselm://session-1`, filetype `markdown`) was 714 lines / 121121 bytes,
  with only 7 extmarks total (all in louiselm's own `louiselm.chat.header`
  namespace). Treesitter highlighter was active but on a buffer this small
  that's not a plausible lag source.
- System load: `uptime` showed load average 0.60/0.52/0.32 on a 16-core
  machine, `free -h` showed 20Gi available of 27Gi, 0B swap used. Not resource
  contention.
- No LSP clients attached to the chat buffer:
  `vim.lsp.get_clients({bufnr=12})` returned empty.

What IS confirmed present:
`nvim --server /run/user/1000/nvim.253565.0 --remote-expr
"luaeval('table.concat(vim.tbl_map(function(a) return a.event .. \"|\" ..
(a.group_name or \"-\") .. \"|\" .. (a.pattern or \"*\") .. \"|\" ..
tostring(a.buflocal) end,
vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({event={\"InsertCharPre\",\"TextChangedI\",\"CursorMovedI\"}})),
\"\\n\")')"` listed, among 12 global autocmds on those three events:

  TextChangedI|image.nvim|*|false

A global (non-buffer-local, pattern `*`) TextChangedI autocmd owned by
image.nvim.

## Symptoms

- User sees: typing in the chat prompt feels unresponsive, specifically
  while it is their turn to type (no active stream).
- System reports: nothing -- no error, no warning. Silent per-keystroke cost.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1366` sets the chat buffer's `filetype` to the
literal `"markdown"`:

    nvim.api.nvim_set_option_value("filetype", "markdown", { buf = buffer })

`~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/image.nvim/lua/image/integrations/markdown.lua`
registers image.nvim's markdown integration for `filetypes = { "markdown",
"vimwiki" }` (see `default_options.filetypes` in that file, wired up via
`document.create_document_integration`). That integration's
`query_buffer_images` function runs on every `TextChangedI` event: it calls
`vim.treesitter.get_parser(buf, "markdown")`, `parser:parse(true)`, and then
walks the full `markdown_inline` tree with two treesitter queries
(`(image (link_destination) @url) @image` and the shortcut-link variant),
looking for markdown image syntax to render inline in the terminal.

Because the chat buffer's filetype is the real `"markdown"`, image.nvim
cannot distinguish it from an actual markdown file the user is editing. It
therefore re-parses and re-queries the buffer's entire inline tree on every
character typed in insert mode, searching for images that don't exist and
never will in a live chat transcript -- pure, unconditional, per-keystroke
waste, scaling with growing transcript length as a session goes on.

`lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:27` has the identical pattern
(`nvim.bo[buffer].filetype = "markdown"`) on a second buffer, but that buffer
is short-lived and not continuously growing/streamed like the chat buffer, so
it is noted here as the same root-cause class but not fixed by this bead.

## Why it was not caught

No test in the suite exercises interactive typing latency in the chat
buffer, or asserts anything about which global autocmds/integrations attach
to it. This class of defect -- a buffer silently opting into a third party's
filetype-keyed behavior it never intended to invite -- has no automated
signature; it only surfaces as felt input lag during real interactive use,
which is exactly how it was found here (user report, not a failing test).

## Fix direction

Give the chat buffer a distinct filetype (e.g. `"louiselm-chat"`) instead of
the real `"markdown"`, so filetype-keyed third-party integrations (image.nvim
today, anything else keyed on `ft=markdown` later) do not attach to it at
all, then explicitly re-attach markdown treesitter highlighting via
`vim.treesitter.start(buffer, "markdown")` (which takes the language
explicitly and is decoupled from `filetype`), so syntax highlighting is
preserved.

Rejected: asking image.nvim to opt out per-buffer instead. Would require
depending on that specific plugin's own opt-out mechanism (if any), and would
not protect against the next filetype=markdown-keyed plugin the user's config
gains later. Fixing the buffer's own identity is the narrower, more durable
fix and is entirely within this repo's control.

## Acceptance

- `nvim_get_autocmds({event={"TextChangedI","InsertCharPre","CursorMovedI"}})`
  filtered to ones matching the chat buffer's new filetype returns none from
  image.nvim (or any other third-party ft=markdown integration).
- The chat buffer still renders with markdown treesitter highlighting
  (verified via `vim.treesitter.highlighter.active[bufnr] ~= nil` after
  `Chat.new():open()`/equivalent).
- No existing test in `tests/` asserts the chat buffer's filetype is the
  literal string `"markdown"` (confirmed absent before this fix; grep
  `tests/` for `filetype.*chat\|chat.*markdown` stays empty after too).

## Not covered

- `lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:27`'s identical pattern is not fixed
  here -- noted as the same root-cause class, lower priority given that
  buffer's short-lived usage pattern, left for a separate bead if it proves
  to matter in practice.
- Whether other globally-registered filetype=markdown integrations besides
  image.nvim (render-markdown.nvim, markdown linters, etc.) were also
  incidentally attaching -- render-markdown.nvim was directly confirmed not
  loaded in this session, but was not re-checked after the fix; not every
  possible third-party integration in the user's config was enumerated.
close_reason: Fixed: chat buffer filetype changed from the literal "markdown" to "louiselm-chat" (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1366), with vim.treesitter.start(buffer, "markdown") added explicitly to preserve highlighting independent of filetype. Root cause: image.nvim's markdown integration keys off filetype in {markdown, vimwiki} and re-parses/re-queries the whole buffer's markdown_inline tree on every TextChangedI event; the chat buffer no longer matches. Regression tests added: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'uses a distinct filetype, not the literal markdown third parties key off' (failed before the fix, confirmed) and 'keeps markdown treesitter highlighting despite the distinct filetype'. Full suite: 237/237 pass. luacheck: 59 warnings, all pre-existing, 0 introduced. stylua --check: clean. Not covered by this fix, as filed: lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:27 has the same pattern on a different, short-lived buffer -- left open per the bead's 'Not covered' section.

title: CI: nvim-nightly-only Vimdoc-staleness check fails while stable passes on the same commit
description:
The advisory "mini.test (nvim nightly)" CI job's "Verify generated Vimdoc" step fails, but `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` passes cleanly when run locally against nvim stable on the same commit — suggesting the check's result differs between nvim stable and nvim nightly rather than the doc actually being stale.

## Observed

GitHub Actions runs 32929697287 (commit 849f5dc) and 32932395090 (commit fd1d606), repo euri10/louiselm, job "mini.test (nvim nightly)", step "Verify generated Vimdoc":

```
louiselm Vimdoc is stale; run ./scripts/generate-vimdoc
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

This step runs identically in the "mini.test (nvim stable)" job (per `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, both `stable` and `nightly` are the same matrix job differing only in `neovim: ${{ matrix.neovim }}`), and it passes there — only the nightly leg fails.

Reproduced (partially) locally: `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` exits 0 with nvim stable installed locally, on the same commit (fd1d606) where the nightly CI leg reports it stale. Nightly was not installed locally to cross-check directly.

## Symptoms

- The nightly matrix leg of "mini.test" reports failure on "Verify generated Vimdoc", though this job has `continue-on-error: true` for `matrix.neovim == 'nightly'` (per `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), so it does not fail the overall required checks — it only shows as a red/crossed-out leg in the Actions UI.

## Root cause

Unknown — not yet isolated. Hypotheses:

1. `./scripts/generate-vimdoc` (or the `:helptags`/doc-generation machinery it drives) produces byte-for-byte different output between nvim stable and nvim nightly (e.g. a changed `:h` formatting default, a Lua stdlib behavior change nightly introduced), so the committed `doc/*.txt` matches stable's output but not nightly's.
2. The nightly Neovim build used by `rhysd/action-setup-vim@v1` in that run had a transient/unrelated regression unconnected to the actual doc content.

What would discriminate: install nvim nightly locally (or in a disposable container) and run `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` directly against it, then compare its regenerated output to the committed doc file to see the actual diff.

## Why it was not caught

The documented local gates (AGENTS.md section 4) run against local/stable Neovim only; there is no local nightly Neovim in the loop, so a stable-vs-nightly divergence in generated-doc output is invisible until CI's nightly leg runs. Because that leg is advisory (`continue-on-error`), a failure there produces no blocking signal and is easy to miss entirely — this was only noticed because of an unrelated report about the required jobs failing on the same run.

## Fix direction

Not yet chosen — depends on which hypothesis above holds. If it's genuine stable/nightly output drift in the doc generator, the fix likely lives in `./scripts/generate-vimdoc` (make its output version-independent, or gate the `--check` comparison on stable only). If it's a nightly build flake, no code fix is needed, just noting it as expected nightly noise.

## Acceptance

- Root cause identified with a reproduced diff (or confirmed flake) rather than a hypothesis.
- `./scripts/generate-vimdoc --check` passes on nvim nightly in CI, or the check is explicitly scoped to stable only with a documented reason.

## Not covered

- The `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` CI failure and the stale-`doc/api.md` failure on the same CI runs are separate bugs with distinct root causes (both on the *required* stable/lua-language-server jobs); filed separately. This bug is lower priority since the affected job is advisory and does not block merges.
close_reason: fixed in 8e4a427. nvim_get_commands() changed the user-command description field from definition on stable to desc on nightly; documented_commands() now prefers non-empty desc and falls back to definition. Added regression coverage for both shapes. Exact CI stable 0.12.5 and nightly 0.13.0-dev-1418+gf97bcbdf77 pass the Vimdoc check and all 546 tests with VIM/VIMRUNTIME unset.

title: Show attached Session attention in the chat winbar
description:
## Problem Statement

When several Sessions are attached, the user can see only the current Session status without opening the Session picker. Permission requests, completed background responses, and failures can therefore wait unnoticed.

## Solution

Show a right-aligned, clickable strip for attached background Sessions in every LouiseLM Session winbar. Keep all Sessions visible when space permits, make attention states visually prominent, and preserve the existing picker as keyboard and overflow navigation.

The strip is always enabled when at least two Sessions are attached and absent with one. Entries use the renamed Session title when present, otherwise the Agent name. ACP Session IDs are not shown.

A completed response becomes attention-worthy only when its turn_done event occurred while the Session was not focused. Focusing that Session acknowledges the response. Permission and error attention persist until resolved or disposed.

## User Stories

1. As a user working in one Session, I want to see all other attached Sessions so I know their state without opening a picker.
2. As a user, I want permission requests, unseen completed responses, and errors to stand out so I notice required action.
3. As a user, I want to click a Session entry to switch directly to it.
4. As a user in a narrow window, I want attention-needed Sessions protected from overflow.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given one attached Session, its winbar remains the existing single-Session presentation with no background strip.
2. Given two or more attached Sessions, every Session is represented by the current Session segment or a clickable background entry when width permits.
3. Clicking a background entry switches the window to that Session; keyboard users can continue to use :LouiselmSwitchSession.
4. A renamed Session uses its name; otherwise its Agent name is shown; ACP Session IDs are omitted.
5. Ready and seen Sessions use a green dot, active Sessions use a blue ellipsis, unseen completed responses use a yellow dot, permission requests use a yellow exclamation, and errors use a red cross.
6. A background turn_done marks that Session unseen; focusing it clears only that completed-turn attention.
7. Permission attention remains until answered and error attention remains until resolved or disposed.
8. Under width pressure, labelled attention entries remain visible, quiet entries collapse into a neutral clickable +N entry, and +N opens the Session picker.
9. Repeated setup, Session changes, window changes, and disposal do not leak handlers or mutate unrelated winbars.

## Implementation Notes

- Reuse the existing Session event stream, status highlights, winbar renderer, Session picker, and rename state.
- Track unread completion state in the Chat UI owner, not the core Session lifecycle: attention is presentation-specific and depends on window focus.
- Use stable Neovim APIs and marshal editor operations through existing scheduling boundaries.
- Add no configuration option, dependency, compatibility shim, or speculative extension point.

## Testing Notes

- Extend behavioral headless chat tests.
- Cover background turn completion versus initial ready state, focus acknowledgement, persistent permission/error attention, direct click routing, overflow priority, disposal, and scheduled UI rendering.
- Preserve existing single-Session winbar behavior.

## Out of Scope

- Global tabline or statusline integration.
- ACP protocol changes.
- Desktop notifications, animation, sound, or user-configurable visual themes.
- Replacing the existing Session picker.
close_reason: Implemented and verified clickable multi-Session attention winbar

title: Resume picker hides last-updated time at line end
description:
In the session picker opened by `:LouiselmResume`, the last-updated timestamp is placed after the session title and cwd, so long titles consume the available width and hide the timestamp. Users cannot quickly tell which resumable Session is newest without moving to the far end of the picker line, which is especially painful in a narrow picker.

## Observed

Screenshot evidence captured 2026-08-24 at 09:31 local time after running `:LouiselmResume`:

`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_0931_1920x1200_1787556713.png`

The selected row visibly contains:

`is your next best task · cwd=/home/lotso/code/louiselm · updated=2026-08-24T06:54:07.000Z`

and the `updated=` portion is at the far right, beyond the useful visible width for long rows. The lower row shows the same layout with `updated=2026-08-23T19:09:52.000Z` after the title and cwd.

Source path inspected: `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:378-389`, where `discovered_session_summary()` appends the cwd and then the updated timestamp after the title.

## Symptoms

- The resume picker shows session identity/title first, then cwd, then `updated=`.
- Long titles push the recency information out of view.
- The user must navigate to the end of each picker line to compare when Sessions were last updated.

## Root cause

Confirmed in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:378-389`: `discovered_session_summary()` builds the display parts in the order agent/session id, title, cwd, updated timestamp. The timestamp is therefore the least likely field to remain visible when the picker width is scarce.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:1980` asserts a full summary string but does not exercise display behavior with a constrained picker width or a long title that obscures the trailing metadata.

## Fix direction

Change the summary ordering at `discovered_session_summary()` so the last-updated information appears before the long title/cwd fields, while preserving enough session identity to distinguish rows. Keep the result compact; do not solve this by requiring horizontal navigation to inspect recency.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after, asserting that `updated=` precedes the title and cwd in the discovered-session summary.
- In a picker with scarce width and a long session title, the last-updated value is visible near the beginning of the row without navigating to the line end.
- Session identity remains visible and existing resume selection behavior is unchanged.

## Not covered

The exact compact timestamp format and final ordering of title versus cwd are implementation choices. This report does not require changing picker width, truncation behavior, or the underlying persisted timestamp.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree. Reordered discovered_session_summary() in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua so updated= appears immediately after the session identity, before title and cwd, keeping recency visible in scarce picker width. Regression updated in tests/ui/chat_spec.lua and failed before the implementation change. Focused chat suite: 105/105. Full MiniTest suite: 469/469. Gates: stylua --check . and lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning pass. Existing test-environment warnings about a missing temporary grill-me skill and clipboard/write output remain unrelated.

title: Enter does nothing with a visible draft in a ready resumed chat
description:
A resumed louiselm chat can display an intact non-empty draft under a ready session while buffer-local Enter produces no ACP prompt and no visible error. The affected user cannot continue that session through the primary chat path, although the agent process remains healthy and the draft is recoverable.

## Observed

Seen 2026-08-21 in live Codex ACP session `01a01fd3-bcf8-74d2-bf0c-edc7b9329101`, Neovim 0.12.2, louiselm buffer on `/run/user/1000/nvim.1020915.0`.

Read-only live probes returned: `name=louiselm://session-1`, `mode=i`, `modifiable=1`, `line=598`, `line_count=598`, `last_len=181`, `last_prefix=> can you ch`, and insert `<CR>` mapping description `Submit louiselm prompt` with a buffer-local callback. `undotree()` reported `seq_cur=268`, `seq_last=268`; the user reported using normal-mode `U` and `Ctrl-r` before the failure.

The Codex rollout `/home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/08/20/rollout-2026-08-20T17-39-25-01a01fd3-bcf8-74d2-bf0c-edc7b9329101.jsonl` ends with `task_complete` at `2026-08-20T16:55:34.216Z` and contains no later user turn. The adapter log `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260820-173923-1021245-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log` contains no later `session/prompt`; the live `codex-acp` and Codex app-server processes remain running. `v:errmsg` is empty and `:messages` contains no louiselm submission error.

## Symptoms

- Header says `Your turn`; typing works, but pressing Enter appears to do nothing.
- Draft remains visible and no prompt reaches ACP/Codex.
- No error explains why submission was rejected or skipped.

## Root cause

Unknown. The failure is below Codex and after louiselm rendered the ready state, but it has not yet been discriminated between (a) the key callback not executing despite the installed mapping, and (b) `Chat:submit()` reading an empty or wrong range because `view.prompt_line` is plain Lua state while normal-mode undo/redo mutates only the buffer. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:722` reads from `view.prompt_line`; `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1637` installs the Enter callback; `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1910` silently returns for an empty prompt.

## Why it was not caught

Chat tests call `chat:submit()` directly and exercise buffer edits, but there is no behavioral test that drives the installed Enter mapping after real normal-mode undo/redo in an attached/resumed transcript. Empty-prompt rejection is also silent at the keymapping boundary.

## Fix direction

First capture the failure in a headless UI test that feeds the actual mapping after transcript changes and undo/redo. At the narrowest boundary, make the prompt location track buffer edits (for example, an extmark owned by the view) or explicitly prevent transcript undo from invalidating UI state. The Enter callback must surface any returned submission error instead of silently appearing dead. Do not patch Codex or restart the adapter as the evidence shows no request reaches it.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and proves Enter submits the visible draft after `U`/undo and redo on a ready attached or resumed chat.
- The prompt sent to the fake ACP session exactly matches the visible draft and prior transcript text is never included.
- If the draft cannot be resolved, Enter emits one actionable louiselm error rather than doing nothing.
- Existing queueing, multiline prompt, and resume tests remain green.

## Not covered

The exact key event has not been injected into the live user session because that would submit their draft. A clean synthetic 1:1 undo/redo probe did not reproduce the defect, so the live undo branch and callback-vs-boundary hypotheses remain unverified. No code fix is included in this diagnostic.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree. Root cause: the prompt boundary was a Lua row number, so undoing streamed transcript lines left submission reading past the visible draft; a left-gravity extmark now tracks the boundary and the real Enter mapping test passes after :undo. Tests: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 75/75; full mini.test 315/315. Formatting: changed files pass. Project-wide StyLua/LuaLS remain blocked only by pre-existing blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua issues.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Recovery follow-up, 2026-08-21: `:LouiselmResume` (without bang) correctly discovered the same-workspace session. `:LouiselmResume!` means all workspaces and was unnecessary here. The load then failed independently because the original live Neovim/ACP chain still owns the Codex thread. Exact JSON-RPC error in `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260821-040016-1245805-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log:2`: `{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"details":"thread 01a01fd3-bcf8-74d2-bf0c-edc7b9329101 already has an active writer"}}`. Original writer processes remain live under Neovim PIDs 1020909/1020915 and codex-acp PID 1021253. Safe recovery requires exiting the original stuck Neovim to release the writer before loading from the fresh instance; do not kill or restart Codex while preserving the draft.

title: Codex edit permissions are answered with a -32602 protocol error
description:
codex-acp sends edit permission requests with no reviewable payload at all:

  {"toolCall":{"toolCallId":"call_SObIFxWtTS90EE6K7JbBTfgX","kind":"edit","status":"pending"},"options":[...]}

(from ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260717-163626-2991539-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log)

No rawInput, no content, no path. lua/louiselm/permission/gates.lua from_acp therefore returns {kind = "file_edit", path = nil}, gates.check rejects it with "permission file edit must have a non-empty path", and lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua handle_request answers the agent with JSON-RPC error -32602 instead of asking the user anything. The user never sees a prompt and codex sees a protocol error.

Separate from the claude case: there is nothing to review here, so the fix is not a better diff. A file-edit request that carries no path or reviewable text should fall back to the generic permission picker (allow/reject options are present in the payload) rather than being answered with a protocol error.

Found while fixing the claude payload bug; not verified live with codex, only from the logged payload and reading the code.
close_reason: Completed: pathless edit requests now reach the generic permission decision flow; regression and full suite pass

title: Grill-me needed: should manual QA rounds use a native louiselm://qa-review workspace
description:
Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this question in passing.

Should manual QA rounds use a native `louiselm://qa-review` workspace instead of making a long `QA_REVIEW.md` file the tester's primary interface?

## Context and evidence

During the 2026-08-24 manual QA round, Case 5 required different setup from earlier cases. A shared Setup section forced the tester to navigate backward and reconstruct which commands applied. The screenshot at `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_0708_1920x1200_1787548138.png` shows the practical cost: separate panes for the QA recipe, LouiseLM Session under test, setup terminal, and conversation/evidence, with the current case detached from the setup it needs.

The immediate process improvement is clear: every case should be self-contained and repeat its exact launch, reset, action, and evidence-capture steps. A small global constants section may hold the build and scratch-state path, but completing a case should never require scrolling elsewhere to reconstruct its apparatus.

## Threads to pull

- Is the native buffer a transient controller/view while Beads remains the durable round and finding record?
- Which case-local actions belong in the buffer: launch recipe, pass, fail, blocked, retest, next, cleanup?
- How should keyboard navigation and commands work for a human tester without turning the interface into a second test framework?
- How should Agent Session IDs and Forensics pointers be captured without copying, rewriting, or exposing raw evidence?
- When and how should findings be created and parented to the QA round?
- What survives editor restart, and who owns cleanup of scratch state and test Sessions?
- Does `QA_REVIEW.md` remain as a generated/exportable view, or disappear?
- How does the same structure remain legible to an Agent performing analysis and a human intervening at the keyboard?

title: Beads inspector hard-codes louiselm prefix for other workspaces
description:
LouiseLM's Beads inspector cannot inspect issues from a different Beads workspace when the issue uses that workspace's prefix. In a Neovim terminal working in /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter, placing the cursor on daa-nk1l and pressing <leader>lB invokes br in that cwd but looks up louiselm-daa-nk1l, which does not exist.

## Observed

Seen in the maintainer's other Neovim terminal / Codex Session codex/01a03ed8-9e9f-77d0-b771-a8b18f97ba81 on 2026-08-26.

Verified workspace prefixes:
- /home/lotso/code/louiselm: br where --json => {"path":"/home/lotso/code/louiselm/.beads","prefix":"louiselm",...}
- /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter: br where --json => {"path":"/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/.beads","prefix":"daa",...}

Verified target:
- cd /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter && br show daa-nk1l --json succeeds and returns the issue "Migrate agent-client-protocol to 2.x".
- LouiseLM reports: "louiselm: could not read Beads issue louiselm-daa-nk1l".

## Symptoms

- Pressing <leader>lB on daa-nk1l in a chat buffer rooted in acp-llm-adapter fails.
- The command attempts the wrong ID, with louiselm- prepended to the adapter-local ID.
- The same inspector is currently coupled to the louiselm Beads prefix even though its br cwd is configurable/current-working-directory based.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua:23 hard-codes the louiselm- prefix in valid_issue_id(). Line 34 only recognizes louiselm- IDs under the cursor. Lines 237-241 prepend louiselm- to bare prompted IDs and reject IDs without that prefix. The lookup at lines 173-176 correctly runs br with options.cwd or the current working directory, but the ID validation/normalization does not derive the prefix from that workspace.

## Why it was not caught

tests/ui/beads_spec.lua:78-268 use only louiselm-kpod, louiselm-zmab, and other louiselm-prefixed fixtures. There is no fixture for a workspace whose br where prefix differs from louiselm, and no assertion that the inspector derives the prefix from the same cwd used for br.

## Fix direction

Resolve the Beads prefix from the selected cwd using br where (or an equivalent br-supported machine-readable lookup), then use that prefix for cursor extraction, prompted-ID normalization, and validation. Keep the existing br show cwd identical to the prefix-discovery cwd. Do not infer a prefix from the issue text or silently fall back to louiselm- when the workspace reports another prefix.

## Acceptance

- A regression test with a br workspace prefix daa and issue daa-nk1l fails before the fix and passes after it.
- From a chat buffer using cwd /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter, <leader>lB on daa-nk1l invokes br show daa-nk1l --json and displays the issue.
- Manual entry of a bare issue suffix uses the discovered workspace prefix.
- A LouiseLM workspace continues to inspect louiselm-prefixed issues.
- Missing or malformed br where output produces a specific actionable error without starting an incorrect br show lookup.

## Not covered

The live Neovim instance was not modified and the bug was not fixed in this report. Prefix discovery behavior for nested Beads workspaces, if br where resolves a different workspace than cwd, remains unverified.
close_reason: Fixed prefix-scoped Beads inspection in lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua: the inspector asynchronously runs br where --json in the lookup cwd, derives and validates the workspace prefix, then uses it for cursor parsing, prompts, and br show. Added daa cross-workspace cursor and manual-entry regressions; focused tests pass (11/11), full suite passes for the changed behavior, lua-language-server reports no diagnostics, and git diff --check passes. Full suite has one unrelated pre-existing failure in tests/docs/vimdoc_spec.lua because committed generated help is already out of sync with user-modified sources; stylua --check . likewise reports unrelated existing differences in lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua, both left untouched.

comments.author: codex/01a03ed8-9e9f-77d0-b771-a8b18f97ba81
comments.text: Lesson: Beads issue IDs are workspace-scoped; derive the prefix from br where in the exact lookup cwd before parsing cursor text or prompting. The regression models the production async ordering (where callback schedules show), which was the relevant test gap. No AGENTS.md rule or design question is warranted.

title: Selecting a Provenance Decision fails with duplicate buffer name
description:
Selecting a row in the Provenance Decision index opens a popup window but fails to populate the selected evidence view because Neovim rejects the buffer name as already in use.

## Observed

Manual QA on 2026-08-28 in resumed Session codex/01a0461a-382d-7fb0-b46e-0a552b0bb40b. The Decision index buffer appeared quickly. Pressing CR on a row was very slow, then another window appeared and LouiseLM reported:

louiselm: could not display Provenance: .../louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:290: Vim:E95: Buffer with this name already exists

The relevant code at lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:287-290 creates a new buffer and calls nvim_buf_set_name(buffer, name). No raw log artifact was available; the exact user-visible error and source location are preserved here.

## Symptoms

- Decision index loads.
- Selecting a Decision row opens another window after a delay.
- The selected Provenance view is not displayed.
- The user receives Vim:E95 about a duplicate buffer name.

## Root cause

Likely duplicate URI buffer ownership in open_provenance at lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:287-290. The function always creates a fresh buffer and assigns the requested URI without handling an existing buffer with that name. Confirm whether the existing buffer is the index, an already-open selected view, or a stale hidden buffer before fixing.

## Why it was not caught

Automated tests assert the first Decision index buffer and mocked navigation output, but do not exercise a real Neovim window sequence with an existing named Provenance buffer and the actual asynchronous Beads callback.

## Fix direction

Handle an existing Provenance URI at the shared open_provenance boundary while preserving read-only behavior and avoiding stale content. Add a headless behavioral regression that opens the Decision index, selects a row, and verifies the selected URI view is displayed.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.
- Selecting a Decision row displays its Provenance content without Vim:E95.
- Reopening an already-open Provenance view does not create duplicate named buffers or stale windows.

## Not covered

- The perceived slowness is not independently attributed yet; isolate it after the duplicate-buffer failure is fixed.
close_reason: Fixed in d6851c6 by reusing existing named Provenance buffers and windows at open_provenance; added regression coverage. Focused Provenance suite 14/14 and full MiniTest suite 703/703 pass; stylua and lua-language-server pass. Manual QA screenshot /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260828_0551_1920x1200_1787889089.png confirms the selected Decision evidence popup renders without Vim:E95. The separate approximately 11-second latency remains open as louiselm-dkga.

comments.author: 01a0465c-762f-73f3-90ff-b096b27607fc
comments.text: Lesson: Provenance URI buffers are reusable view identities. The shared open_provenance boundary must look up an existing named buffer, make it writable while refreshing content, then restore read-only state and reuse an existing window when present. The regression must keep a valid URI buffer alive; a test that lets the popup be wiped does not reproduce E95. No AGENTS.md rule or design question is warranted.

title: Malformed ACP file-edit permission request terminates session
description:
## Reproduction

In session codex/019ff53a-629d-71a3-a1de-1a2506b42912, the agent sent an ACP session/request_permission file-edit request without a non-empty path. louiselm reported:

`Error: invalid ACP permission request: permission file edit must have a non-empty path`

The invalid request currently calls the session fatal-error path, closes the ACP client, and prevents the grilling session from continuing.

## Expected

Reject only the malformed permission request with a JSON-RPC invalid-params error. Keep the ACP session alive so the agent can continue or retry with a valid request.

## Acceptance criteria

- A file-edit permission request with a missing or empty path receives an error response with code -32602 and the validation message.
- The session remains ready/waiting for subsequent work and does not emit a fatal session error.
- Existing valid permission requests and malformed fatal startup/update handling remain unchanged.
- Add deterministic regression coverage.
close_reason: Changed malformed ACP permission requests to receive JSON-RPC -32602 errors without terminating the session; added regression coverage. Verification: focused api_spec 17/17, full MiniTest 132/132, stylua --check ., lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning.

title: :LouiselmPark command: lazy Run attach, staged-context warning, auto-claims, named-precondition errors
description:
## Goal

An operator can cold-Park the current chat session with one Neovim command, exercising the real `Run:park_cold` ownership and capability checks instead of a CLI-only shortcut.

## Scope

- In scope: new `:LouiselmPark` command; lazy `Run.new()` + attach-as-sole-worker when the session is not already Run-backed; Staged-context warn-and-confirm; auto-queried `br` claims attached to the Park record; named-precondition error surfacing (loadSession capability, live client, working_dir) instead of raw ACP errors; wiring the existing `Service.admit`/`attach`/`park` calls as production callers.
- Out of scope: `:LouiselmResumePark` changes (separate task, see dependent), warm Park exposure, a `stage` schema field, multi-Run selection UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given an ordinary chat session with no existing Run, when the operator runs `:LouiselmPark`, then a Run is created, the session is attached as its sole worker, and it is cold-Parked, with no separate prior command required.
2. Given a session with staged context (queued prompt, pending skill selection, context chips), when `:LouiselmPark` runs, then the operator is warned it will not survive cold Park and must confirm before it proceeds.
3. Given the session actor holds live `br` claims, when `:LouiselmPark` runs, then those claims are attached to the Park record automatically, with no picker or manual entry.
4. Given the Agent lacks `agent_capabilities.loadSession`, has no live ACP client, or has no `working_dir`, when `:LouiselmPark` runs, then the specific failing precondition is named to the operator, never a raw ACP error string.
5. Warm Park is not exposed as a manual action anywhere in this command.

## Testing

- Headless test: session with staged context triggers the warning branch; confirming proceeds, declining does not Park.
- Headless test: session actor with live `br` claims produces a Park record carrying exactly those claims.
- Headless test: each of the three `cold_park_record` precondition failures produces a distinct, named error message (use the mock ACP agent, degrading its advertised capabilities per case).
- Full StyLua, LuaLS, and MiniTest gates.

## Notes

title: OpenCode Session stays prompting after permission handling
description:
An OpenCode Go Session can remain in status prompting after the user interacts with permission choices, leaving the chat unable to accept another prompt. The maintainer reports: "im stuck in opencode/ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney after i think i choose allow always". The exact lifetime choice is not verified by the transport trace: no allow_always option was recorded as selected.

## Observed

Reported on 2026-08-30 for ACP Session ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney, OpenCode Go with model opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna in the captured run.

Live Neovim inspection via /run/user/1000/nvim.566712.0 found Chat view session-3 attached to this ACP Session with status = "prompting", current_turn = 1, permission_active = nil, permission_queue = 0, and one pending local ACP client callback (request id 5).

The authoritative ACP proxy trace is /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney/log.jsonl. It records session/prompt id 13 at line 1527, then permission requests at lines 1610, 1612, 1615, and 1622. The recorded client responses are: id 7 selected optionId once (line 1611), id 8 cancelled (line 1614), id 9 cancelled (line 1621), and id 10 selected optionId once (line 1623). No allow_always selection appears. The trace also contains an ACP session/prompt response id 13 with stopReason = end_turn at line 1620, interleaved before the final permission responses.

OpenCode diagnostics at /home/lotso/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log:1750-1762 show the gpt-5.6-luna turn starting, then four external_directory permission checks being asked.

## Symptoms

- Chat remains in "prompting" / Model responding state.
- A new prompt cannot be submitted because the Session is not ready.
- Permission requests appear to have been answered, but the Session does not visibly reach a stable ready state.

## Root cause

Unknown. Candidate causes are a client-side response-correlation/lifecycle race around a session/prompt terminal response arriving while permission requests remain outstanding, reuse of an ACP Session through a new local client with stale pending state, or an OpenCode/proxy ordering defect. The exact live local request-to-proxy frame mapping still needs to be discriminated.

## Why it was not caught

Existing permission coverage tests synchronous selection and ordinary serialized requests. Existing prompt-timeout coverage models a missing terminal response but does not model a terminal session/prompt response interleaved with outstanding permission requests or a reattached OpenCode Session.

## Fix direction

Reproduce from the captured ACP frame ordering through the lifecycle boundary. Ensure each permission response and the session/prompt response is correlated exactly once, terminal prompt completion cannot be overwritten by late permission callbacks, and a reattached Session cannot retain stale pending request state. Preserve the client-side watchdog from louiselm-5zhl as a last-resort bound.

## Acceptance

- A regression fixture derived from the proxy trace covers the observed permission and terminal-response ordering.
- The Session reaches a correct terminal state after all observed permission responses, without leaving a stale pending prompt callback.
- The user can submit a subsequent prompt or receives a specific actionable error.
- The test distinguishes an actual allow_always selection from once/cancelled outcomes.

## Related

- louiselm-4wx fixed the earlier concurrent permission-picker deadlock.
- louiselm-5zhl added a generic watchdog for an ACP prompt that never resolves. This report is separate because the captured trace includes a terminal session/prompt response and the live Session still reports prompting.

Once the terminal session/prompt response has been observed, the final permission response transitions to ready instead of prompting; late permission requests are still answered through the existing serialized queue. Regression coverage reproduces proxy Session ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney ordering from ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney/log.jsonl: permission IDs 7-9, terminal prompt response, request 10, then all responses. The old behavior fails at the terminal response because it reports ready before permission 9; the fixed behavior ends ready with one prompt completion and all four permission responses. Focused session suite: 58 cases; full MiniTest: 786 cases; StyLua, LuaLS, and API appendix checks pass. Lesson: terminal ACP completion and permission draining are separate lifecycle boundaries; a terminal response must not erase the active permission phase. No AGENTS.md change is warranted. Live acceptance remains pending maintainer retest.

title: Beads inspector: cross-workspace sibling sweep + beads.sibling_roots config
description:
## Goal

`<leader>lB` opens an issue from a sibling repo's Beads workspace when the
cursor is on a full `<foreign-prefix>-<suffix>` ID that does not resolve
locally, using a new user-configured list of sibling roots.

## Scope

- In scope: add a `beads` table to the config schema in
  `lua/louiselm/config.lua`, following the existing `Schema.define` DSL
  already used there (see e.g. the `capture` or `context` entries for the
  pattern). Add `beads.sibling_roots`: `type = "array-of"`, `items =
  "string"`, `default = {}`. No custom validator function is needed beyond
  what `array-of`/`string` already enforces; do not hand-roll extra checks.
- In scope: in `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`, when the cursor token already
  looks like a full `<prefix>-<suffix>` ID (i.e. it failed the *local*
  workspace lookup, both the existing exact-prefix path and the sibling
  bare-suffix task's local lookup if that task has landed first -- check
  before assuming either exists yet) but has the general Beads ID shape, glob
  one level under each configured `sibling_roots` entry for a `.beads/beads.db`
  and try `br --db <that path> show <token>` against each, in the order
  configured, stopping at the first hit. Fall through to the existing manual
  prompt if none hit or if `sibling_roots` is empty/unset.
- Out of scope: bare-suffix matching against siblings (rejected in the
  parent design -- bare tokens stay local-only, see `louiselm-r98e` and the
  closed `louiselm-qmmk` grill for why).
- Out of scope: caching the glob result, persisting a registry, or any UI to
  configure `sibling_roots` -- it is a plain config-table value the user sets
  in their own `setup()` call (see the reference file at
  `~/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua` for what a
  real user config call looks like, if you need an example of the shape).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given `beads.sibling_roots` is unset (default empty list), when
   `<leader>lB` is pressed on any token, then no sibling sweep happens at
   all -- behavior is byte-identical to before this task.
2. Given `beads.sibling_roots` contains one or more paths and the cursor is
   on a full `<foreign-prefix>-<suffix>` ID that exists in the second
   configured sibling's workspace but not the first, when `<leader>lB` is
   pressed, then the first sibling is tried and misses, the second is tried
   and hits, and that issue opens (proves ordering and short-circuit, not
   just "some sibling matched").
3. Given `beads.sibling_roots` is configured but the ID exists in none of
   them (and not locally either), when `<leader>lB` is pressed, then the
   existing manual `Beads issue id:` prompt appears, unchanged.
4. Given a `sibling_roots` entry whose value is not a table of strings
   (e.g. a bare string or a number in the list), when the config is loaded,
   then validation rejects it with a clear error, consistent with how other
   `array-of` fields in this schema already fail on bad input.

## Testing

- Add cases to `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` following its existing fake-`br`
  pattern (no real subprocesses, per AGENTS.md determinism rules): the
  unset-default no-op case, the ordering/short-circuit case across two fake
  siblings, the exhausted-sweep-falls-to-prompt case.
- Add a config-schema test (wherever `lua/louiselm/config.lua`'s existing
  schema fields are tested -- find that spec file first) covering the new
  `beads.sibling_roots` field: valid list of strings accepted, invalid entry
  type rejected, default is an empty list when omitted.

## Notes

- Full design context and rejected alternatives (no persisted registry, no
  hardcoded `~/code/*`, no piggybacking on beads_rust's own user config) live
  in the parent feature `louiselm-r98e` and the closed grill question
  `louiselm-qmmk` -- read those before starting, do not re-derive or
  re-litigate the design.
- Live-measured cost (2026-08-28): a `--db`-pointed `br show` call costs
  ~25-60ms regardless of hit/miss, dominated by process startup. A full
  sweep of a handful of siblings is well under 500ms -- acceptable for an
  explicit per-keypress action.
- Config addition and sweep logic are folded into one task rather than split,
  since the config addition alone is too small (a few lines following an
  existing DSL pattern) to be independently worth grabbing on its own.
close_reason: done

comments.author: claude/b59dc4cb-7c9d-4efc-908a-2cca0884acca
comments.text:
Implemented:

- lua/louiselm/config.lua: new `beads.sibling_roots` schema field (array-of string, default {}), following the existing capture/skills.paths DSL pattern exactly.
- lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua: candidate_token_at_cursor() (renamed/refactored from the bare-suffix tasks helper) now feeds a branch in inspect_with_prefix() -- a token containing a hyphen is treated as a foreign-workspace-shaped ID and handed to the new try_sibling_ids(), which globs each configured sibling_roots entry one level for `.beads/beads.db` (sibling_db_paths()) and tries `br --db <path> show <token> --json` against each in order, stopping at the first hit. A hyphen-free token still goes through the existing local bare-suffix path. Exhausting all siblings (or having none configured) falls through to the manual prompt, matching the local bare-suffix path's speculative-miss behavior.
- decode_issue()/run_show() prefix parameter is now optional: sibling calls pass no prefix (a sibling's own prefix is unknown without an extra round trip) and instead rely on the exact `issue.id == token` equality check already performed by callers.
- lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua: threads `configured.beads.sibling_roots` into the Beads.inspect() call.

Caught by the new tests before merging: the hyphen-shape branch check used `token:find("%-", 1, true)` -- with plain=true, `%-` is a literal 3-char search string, not an escaped hyphen, so it never matched and every foreign-looking token silently fell into the bare-suffix path instead (producing a broken double-prefixed guess like "louiselm-codex-acp-a1b2"). Fixed to `token:find("-", 1, true)`. This is exactly the kind of thing the acceptance-criteria tests exist to catch.

Tests added: tests/ui/beads_spec.lua (sibling-sweep hit proving order/short-circuit across two fake siblings, sweep-exhausted falls to prompt, sibling_roots-unset produces zero sibling calls / identical pre-feature behavior); tests/schema/setup_spec.lua (valid sibling_roots accepted, default empty list, non-string entry rejected without mutating caller config).

doc/louiselm.txt and doc/tags regenerated via scripts/generate-vimdoc for the new config option (generate-api-appendix --check stayed clean -- no public LuaCATS surface changed).
