title: Provenance: queryable commit/issue/Session lineage with backlog time travel
description:
## Problem Statement

Starting from a commit, there is no way to answer "which issue was this for"
and "which Session produced it" without hand-archaeology. The same holds in
reverse: an issue does not say which commits implemented it, and a closed
design question does not say what the backlog looked like when it was decided.

The maintainer works across several Agents, and the record of what happened is
already split three ways -- git commits, Beads issues, Session transcripts --
with no join between them. When a past decision needs revisiting, the context
it was made in has to be reconstructed by hand every time. This has already
happened: louiselm-ce6.27 revisited the boundary accepted on louiselm-iexg two
days earlier and re-derived the surrounding context from scratch.

## Solution

Make Provenance a first-class, queryable thing inside LouiseLM.

Nothing new is stored. All three edges already exist as data:

- issue <-> commit: bvr already correlates these from git history, with a
  method and confidence per correlation and a curation loop for the inferences.
- commit <-> Session: the maintainer's `Refs <id>` commit trailer convention
  already carries both issue ids and Session ids.
- issue <-> Session: the `br update --claim --actor "<session id>"` rule in
  AGENTS.md section 2 already puts Session ids in `assignee`/`created_by`.

What is missing is a query surface and one resolver: Session id -> transcript
on disk, which is per-Agent, local-machine, and the only part that actually
evaporates.

On top of that, time travel. `.beads/issues.jsonl` is committed, so git holds a
snapshot of the whole backlog at every commit. Combining the closed question,
the backlog state at its closing commit, the diff since, and the Session
transcript makes a past decision re-interrogable on evidence rather than on
memory: here is what we knew then, here is what has drifted, does the decision
still hold.

## User Stories

1. As a maintainer reading a commit, I want to see which issue(s) it served and
   which Session produced it, so that I can recover intent without guessing.
2. As a maintainer reading an issue, I want to see every commit that touched it
   and every Session that worked it, so that I can find the reasoning behind a
   change.
3. As a maintainer revisiting a closed design question, I want the backlog state
   as of its closing commit plus everything that changed since, so that I can
   judge whether the decision still holds.
4. As a maintainer, I want to jump from a Session id to that Session's
   transcript, so that the reasoning is one keystroke away rather than a
   filesystem hunt.
5. As an Agent picking up related work, I want machine-readable Provenance for
   an issue, so that I can load prior context without re-reading the repository.
6. As a maintainer, I want an unresolved Session to be shown as unresolved, so
   that a gap in coverage never reads as an absence of history.
7. As a maintainer whose commits predate the trailer convention, I want partial
   Provenance rather than an error, so that old work still yields what it can.
8. As a maintainer, I want Provenance to be read-only, so that inspecting the
   past can never mutate the record.
9. As an Agent, I want correlation confidence surfaced rather than hidden, so
   that an inferred edge is never presented as a recorded fact.

## Implementation Decisions

Vocabulary: this work introduces the term Provenance (louiselm-tsxh), agreed
with the maintainer on 2026-08-26. It is deliberately distinct from Forensics
(louiselm-cvv3): Forensics is a durable immutable record indexing evidence for
exactly one subject Session, while Provenance is recomputed per query, spans
entities, and persists nothing. Forensics is not being widened.

Modules:

- `provenance/correlate.lua` -- pure join over already-collected inputs,
  producing the edge set. No I/O whatsoever, so the entire graph logic is
  fixture-testable. This is the deep module of the epic.
- `provenance/sources.lua` -- bounded `vim.system` calls to `bvr --robot-*` and
  `git`, returning structured data or `nil, err`. Isolates process and
  fast-event discipline from logic.
- `provenance/vintage.lua` -- time travel: resolve a git ref to the historical
  `.beads/issues.jsonl` and diff it. Encapsulates a live upstream defect
  (louiselm-f8r1) behind a stable interface so it can be deleted when upstream
  lands, without touching callers.
- `session/locator.lua` -- per-Agent registry mapping `<agent>/<session-id>` to
  a transcript path. Independently valuable beyond this epic; louiselm-3x9p
  wants the same capability.
- `ui/provenance.lua` -- read-only `louiselm://provenance/<kind>/<id>` buffer,
  modelled directly on the existing `ui/beads.lua`, whose cursor-id detection,
  `br` shell-out and read-only buffer rendering are the same shape. Extends id
  detection to commit SHAs and Session ids.

Agent coverage: every Agent that appears in the record is supported on day
one -- claude, codex, deepseek and copilot -- by maintainer decision on
2026-08-26. Staging them was considered and rejected as false economy.

The reason it is cheap is that the resolver must not key on Agent name in the
first place. `config.agents` is a `map-of` with default `{}` (lua/louiselm/
config.lua): Agent names are arbitrary user labels, not a known enum. Two
setups can call the same CLI different things, and renaming a config entry
would silently break Provenance for every historical Session under the old
name. So `session/locator.lua` keys on transcript LAYOUT, with configuration
mapping an Agent entry to a layout. Layouts are shared -- the OpenAI-compatible
CLIs (deepseek, glm) resolve the same way -- so once the registry exists the
marginal cost of an Agent is a layout entry, not a module. glm is expected to
work through the OpenAI-compatible layout without separate work, but this is
unverified and must not be claimed until a real glm Session resolves.

Measured coverage at the time of writing, which is why no single Agent could
have been treated as the default: the two edges disagree, so name-keyed or
partial support would leave holes whose shape depends on which direction the
graph is queried.

| Agent    | Beads actors | commit trailers |
|----------|--------------|-----------------|
| codex    | 123          | 1               |
| claude   | 34           | 25              |
| copilot  | 14           | 1               |
| deepseek | 0            | 7               |

Contracts:

- Provenance is strictly read-only. It never writes to Beads, git, or a
  transcript.
- Correlation confidence and method from bvr are carried through to the surface,
  never flattened into an assertion.
- An unresolved Session renders as explicitly unresolved. Omitting the row is
  forbidden, because a coverage gap that looks like data is worse than a
  visible hole.
- Core modules return structured errors and typed events; only the UI module
  presents them (AGENTS.md section 8).

## Testing Decisions

- `correlate` is tested against captured real `bvr --robot-history` and
  `git log` output, cited per AGENTS.md section 5 so observed shapes stay
  distinguishable from invented ones. Cover: explicit-id and co-committed
  methods, an issue with no commits, a commit with no trailer, a Session id that
  resolves to nothing, and the pre-convention era where trailers are absent.
- `vintage` is tested against a temporary git repository fixture with a
  committed `.beads/issues.jsonl`, including the custom-status case that
  currently breaks upstream, so the workaround has a red test proving why it
  exists and a signal for when it can be removed.
- `session/locator` is tested against a temporary directory tree per transcript
  layout, plus the missing-transcript path, an Agent renamed in config after the
  Session was recorded, and two differently-named Agents sharing one layout.
- `sources` is tested for the fast-event boundary: process callbacks must not
  touch editor APIs directly, per AGENTS.md section 10.
- `ui/provenance` gets a headless behavioural smoke test in the style of the
  existing chat UI specs, not pixel assertions, plus the queued-work-after-
  disposal case.
- Prior art to follow: `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` for UI behaviour, and the
  existing Beads inspector for the shell-out-and-render shape.

## Out of Scope

- Writing or mutating any Provenance data. Derived only.
- Visualisation beyond a text buffer. No graph rendering in this epic.
- Fixing the upstream bvr defect (louiselm-f8r1). Encapsulated, not fixed. The
  maintainer has explicitly deferred upstream action.
- Widening or redefining Forensics.
- Analytics over Session option changes (louiselm-3x9p), which will consume
  `session/locator` but is separate work.

## Further Notes

Direction settled with the maintainer on 2026-08-26 as "door B", chosen over a
shell-and-skill join that would have delivered lookup only. Full evidence,
including the measured state of every edge and the bvr capability audit, is on
the louiselm-06yh comment.

louiselm-06yh is resolved as a design gate by explicit maintainer decision.
Door B answers "build it, derive rather than store, LouiseLM owns the surface";
transcript-resolution semantics are settled as local, adapter-specific,
best-effort lookup with explicit unresolved states. The agreed
Decision/Provenance model and implementation slices are recorded in this epic.

Known blocker: louiselm-f8r1. bvr drops every custom-status record and
hard-fails all time travel on this backlog, so `vintage` cannot work through
bvr's git-ref path until that is resolved or worked around. The workaround is
recorded on that bead.

Refs louiselm-06yh
Refs claude/ce71a8b9-3415-4247-a8a5-9e1ecf6ff943
close_reason: All 11 descendants closed; epic delivered. Housekeeping close, no remaining work.

comments.author: claude/ce71a8b9-3415-4247-a8a5-9e1ecf6ff943
comments.text:
Adapter scope changed before any implementation started: all Agents supported on day one (claude, codex, deepseek, copilot), not the staged claude+codex split originally drafted. Maintainer decision 2026-08-26, on the grounds that glm is OpenAI-compatible and therefore shares deepseek's shape.

Recording the design consequence, since it is the part that would be expensive to discover late: this only stays cheap if session/locator keys on transcript LAYOUT rather than Agent name. config.agents is a map-of with default {} — names are arbitrary user labels, so a name-keyed resolver breaks on a config rename and cannot share one implementation between two Agents that use the same CLI. If a future change reintroduces name keying, the day-one-all-Agents decision stops being cheap and this comment is the reason why.

comments.author: codex/01a03e4b-eeca-7ce3-93ab-96163bc74a42
comments.text: Design resolved through louiselm-06yh on 2026-08-26. End state: LouiseLM owns a derived, read-only Provenance/Decision browser over git, Beads/bvr, and local adapter-specific transcript locators; no graph database or persisted Decision entity. Decisions are question-issue anchors. Current and historical views share one perspective-aware model. Recorded and inferred edges remain distinct; Session links require attributable evidence; explicit QA acceptance is part of the evidence lifecycle; explicit supersession/reconsideration is shown, while drift is never judged automatically. Implementation is split into small slices: existing core/current/history slices plus Decision-anchor, Decision-index, current-timeline, and historical-drift tasks.

title: Investigate duplicate allow_always permission options
description:
## Observation

Screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260810_0558_1920x1200_1786334287.png` shows the LouiseLM command permission picker with four entries:

1. `allow_once`
2. `allow_always`
3. `allow_always`
4. `reject_once`

This appeared while running the commit/sync workflow in the Codex session.

## Question

Determine whether the two `allow_always` entries are intentional because they represent distinct permission scopes/operations, or whether the renderer is duplicating/collapsing distinct option labels.

## Acceptance criteria

- Trace the ACP permission options from the agent response through normalization and chat picker rendering.
- Identify the semantic difference between the two `allow_always` options, if any.
- If distinct, make the picker labels explain their scopes; if duplicate rendering is a bug, fix it.
- Add focused regression coverage for the resolved behavior.
- Preserve the existing allow/reject semantics.
close_reason: Confirmed duplicate allow_always entries are intentional: Codex uses distinct names and option IDs for session-scoped versus persistent permission grants. Fixed chat rendering to prefer ACP option names over generic kinds; added regression coverage. title: :LouiselmForensicsView refuses a bare invocation with a raw E471
description:
`:LouiselmForensicsView` cannot be invoked the way a human reaches it -- immediately
after `:LouiselmForensics`, to read the record just written. It is declared
`nargs = 1`, so a bare call aborts with Neovim's own `E471: Argument required`, and
the only place the generated record path is ever shown is a transient INFO
notification from the collect command. The user must recover a 40-character
generated filename from a toast that has already faded, or list the state
directory by hand, to use the command at all.

## Observed

Manual QA round 2026-08-27, session `deepseek/session-5d380d32-0e8d-4396-afa4-82cc1ee5c4fb`,
HEAD `e0d27d8`, Neovim 0.12.5. Maintainer at the keyboard.

`:LouiselmForensics` succeeded and notified:

```
louiselm: Forensics record written to /home/lotso/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/1787796219-1787796219-265777660586430.json
```

The resource link was staged into the chat (`[context: forensics...]` visible).
`:LouiselmForensicsView` typed with no argument then failed with `E471: Argument
required`. The record itself is well-formed: 841 bytes, mode `0600`,
`schema_version: 1`, correct `subject.acp_session_id`, and truthful
`evidence_sources` (the `acp_log` source is honestly marked `omitted` with reason
"ACP adapter did not advertise a log path" -- verified correct, deepseek does not
route through the acp-llm-adapter proxy, so no log exists to point at).

## Symptoms

- Collect a Forensics record, try to read it, and the viewer refuses to open.
- The error is Neovim's raw `E471`, with no mention of Forensics, the expected
  argument, or where records live.
- The one command that names the path prints it to a notification; in a
  `snacks.notifier` configuration that toast is transient and is not recoverable
  from `:messages`.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:540-560`. The command is registered with
`{ nargs = 1, complete = "file" }`, so Neovim rejects a bare invocation before the
callback runs. The callback's own guard at `command.lua:541-545`:

```lua
local path = arguments.args
if path == "" then
  report_error("Forensics record path is required")
  return
end
```

is therefore unreachable dead code -- `nargs = 1` guarantees `args` is non-empty.
The intended friendly error can never be delivered.

`:LouiselmForensics` (`command.lua:523-538`) holds the path only long enough to
pass it to `nvim.notify`; nothing records a "last record" the viewer could default
to.

## Why it was not caught

The prior QA round (`louiselm-wnpd`, case 5) exercised collect + view + resource
link and passed, because the reviewer supplied the path explicitly. No test or
manual step covers the bare invocation, which is the way the command is actually
first reached. The unreachable `path == ""` branch also reads, to anyone skimming,
as though the no-argument case is handled.

## Fix direction

Narrowest correct fix: make the argument optional (`nargs = "?"`) and default to
the most recently written record for the current Session, which `:LouiselmForensics`
already knows. That makes the existing `path == ""` branch live and turns it into
a real fallback rather than dead code.

Rejected: keeping `nargs = 1` and only improving the error text -- it leaves the
common path (view what I just collected) requiring a copied 40-character filename.
Rejected: a picker over the state directory -- more surface than the problem needs;
revisit only if multi-record browsing is wanted.

## Acceptance

- A regression test that fails before the fix and passes after, invoking the
  command with no argument and asserting the most recent record opens.
- Live: `:LouiselmForensics` then `:LouiselmForensicsView` with no argument opens
  the record just written, with no `E471`.
- Invoking with no record ever collected reports a LouiseLM-worded error, not a
  raw Neovim one.

## Not covered

Whether the rendered buffer should be a readable human projection rather than the
raw JSON it currently shows (`readfile` + `buf_set_lines` + `filetype = "json"`,
`command.lua:546-560`) is deliberately out of scope here: that is louiselm-ce6.24's
own outstanding acceptance item, recorded as a comment there rather than duplicated
as a bug. Multi-record selection, records from a different Session than the current
one, and the behaviour when the state directory is unreadable are untested.
close_reason: done

title: Render a session transcript into an editable handoff prompt buffer
description:
## Goal
Render a live session's transcript into an editable buffer that becomes the first
prompt of another session, with nothing sent until the user submits.

## Scope
- In scope: turning `Transcript:snapshot()` entries into buffer text; opening it
  for editing; submitting the edited buffer as a prompt to a target session;
  abandoning it without sending.
- Out of scope: choosing the provider, creating the target session, and the
  user command -- all in the sibling task. This task is the payload half only.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given a session with recorded entries, a buffer is produced containing the
   transcript with full tool commands and results, not one-line summaries.
2. Nothing is sent to any session while the buffer is open.
3. Submitting sends exactly the buffer's current contents, so edits are honoured.
4. Abandoning the buffer sends nothing and leaves both sessions untouched.
5. An empty buffer refuses to send with an actionable message rather than
   prompting with nothing.

## Testing
Headless: entries in, buffer text out; edit-then-submit sends the edited text;
abandon sends nothing; empty refuses. Assert on the payload actually handed to
the session, not on buffer appearance.

## Notes
`lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua` (`snapshot`, `render`) and
`lua/louiselm/session/transcript_export.lua` already turn entries into markdown
untruncated; reuse rather than write a third renderer. Check whether
`Transcript.render` is directly usable before adding anything.

Reasoning is on the parent, louiselm-provider-handoff-3e2p. The review step is a
hard requirement, not a convenience: it is both the disclosure gate and the way a
wrong frame gets cut before it contaminates the second provider.
close_reason: Completed: added editable transcript handoff buffers with edit-and-submit, abandon, empty-input rejection, and cleanup; focused and full mini.test suites pass

title: Wire the provider handoff command and keep the source session attached
description:
## Goal
Wire the handoff command: pick a target provider, open a session on it, feed it
the reviewed transcript buffer, and leave the source session attached.

## Scope
- In scope: the user command and its error paths; the provider picker excluding
  the current agent; creating the target session through the existing
  `new_session` seeding path; handing the buffer from the sibling task to it;
  keeping the source session attached and switchable.
- Out of scope: rendering the buffer (sibling task), capability routing, and any
  automatic or policy-driven switching.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The command opens a picker of configured providers excluding the current one,
   and does nothing on dismissal.
2. The target session is created through the same path as `new_session`, so
   initial contexts, skill catalog, and instructions context are seeded, and the
   target provider's own `skills_policy` is applied rather than the source's.
3. The source session stays attached and reachable through the existing session
   switcher after the handoff.
4. Errors are distinct and actionable for: no chat session, an open permission
   decision, a non-idle source session, fewer than two configured providers, and
   target session creation failure.
5. A test proves a permission remembered for the source agent does not apply to
   the target agent.
6. No command, option, or user-facing string uses "model" to mean provider.
7. README documents the command in the interactive-controls list.

## Testing
Headless with the mock ACP agent configured twice under different names. Cover
each error branch, the dismissal path, source-session survival, and permission
isolation. Async paths must exercise the production callback context.

## Notes
Depends on the buffer task; wire against its interface rather than reimplementing
rendering.

Naming: the maintainer's earlier phrasing was `:LouiselmModelChange`, which was
the wrong word and cost a reverted implementation (louiselm-model-change-cl59,
db39f96). Repository convention is verb-first --- `LouiselmSwitchSession`,
`LouiselmRenameSession`, `LouiselmPickSkill` --- so something like
`:LouiselmSwitchProvider` or `:LouiselmHandOff` fits. Confirm the name with the
maintainer before implementing; do not infer it.

Reasoning is on the parent, louiselm-provider-handoff-3e2p.
close_reason: Wired :LouiselmHandOff end to end: picker excluding the current agent, target session created via the existing new_session seeding path, source stays attached/switchable, distinct errors for every listed case, permission isolation proven by test, README updated. See implementation-notes comment for file-level detail.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Command name confirmed with maintainer: :LouiselmHandOff. Rejected :LouiselmSwitchProvider -- the picker is over named agent config entries, not vendors; two entries can share a provider/binary and differ only in model (e.g. codex/Luna vs codex/Sol), so 'provider' would misdescribe what's being picked. 'Handoff' names the mechanic (hand the conversation to another configured entry) without asserting what changed underneath. PascalCase per repo convention (LouiselmSwitchSession, LouiselmPickSkill).

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Implementation notes: wired :LouiselmHandOff (chat:hand_off()) in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua and lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua. Reuses chat:new_session(agent_name) for target creation (same seeding path, target's own skills_policy applied) after resolving the target via a Picker.select excluding the source agent. Errors: disposed, open permission decision (DECISION_OPEN_ERROR), no chat session attached, non-idle source (status ~= ready or a queued prompt), fewer than two configured agents, and target creation failure (notified async in the picker callback, source untouched). Permission isolation across agents proven in tests/permission_spec.lua (store-level, per the parent's implementation decision that this needs no new mechanism, only a test). README documents the command. No 'model' wording anywhere. Full mini.test suite (351 cases), stylua --check, and lua-language-server all pass.

title: QA round: automatic Provenance transcript lookup
description:
# Manual QA review — automatic Provenance transcript lookup

Working file for the current round. Run the cases and report the case number,
what you saw, and the Session id or transcript path involved.

**Build under test:** louiselm commit `e9386db`; dotfiles working tree change
removing explicit `transcript_layout` entries. **Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: Provenance should locate Agent-owned historical transcripts for all
supported adapters without requiring `transcript_layout` in the user's config.
Louiselm must use a unique match and refuse to guess when the same ACP Session
id exists in multiple transcript stores.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Dotfiles load with no explicit transcript layouts | **passed** — `:LouiselmProvenanceDecisions` opened successfully; `:checkhealth louiselm` reported no transcript configuration error; config grep returned no matches |
| 2 | Provenance resolves a real historical Session automatically | **passed** — raw ID resolved to `/home/lotso/.codex/sessions/2026/08/30/rollout-2026-08-30T08-01-44-01a05142-72b8-73b0-9123-9fbef695a8cd.jsonl`; correlated commit `e9386dbd859c7cfb44be09cf4116ffcf952b8abf` and three Beads issues. **F1**: literal Markdown backticks around the same ID were treated as part of the ID and failed lookup |
| 3 | Provenance reports an unresolved Session clearly | **passed** — `codex/qa-no-such-session` rendered an explicit supported-layouts unresolved message; no crash or random transcript |
| 4 | Existing Provenance navigation still works | **passed** — detail closed with `q` and returned focus to the Provenance Decisions list |

## Setup

1. From the dotfiles Neovim config, restart Neovim completely so the local
   `file:///home/lotso/code/louiselm` plugin reloads commit `e9386db`.
2. Confirm the user config contains no active layout settings:

   ```sh
   rg --hidden -n "transcript_layout" /home/lotso/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua
   ```

   Expected: no output.
3. In Neovim run `:checkhealth louiselm`. Expected: no configuration error for
   missing transcript settings. Existing unrelated health warnings should be
   recorded separately, not treated as this round's failure.

The real adapters may require credentials and their normal permission mode.
Cases 1 and 4 do not start an Agent. For case 2, use a Session that already
exists on disk; do not create a new Session just for this round unless needed.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Do not use a “most recent transcript” shell glob as evidence; identify the
  exact ACP Session id first.
- Do not run `:LouiselmInspectProvenance` from a dense JSONL line containing
  several IDs; the detector correctly refuses to guess and opens the prompt.
  Use a one-ID scratch buffer for Session lookup.
- Enter test IDs as raw text. Do not include Markdown backticks around the ID;
  backticks become part of the lookup key and guarantee an unresolved result.
- Avoid long hexadecimal suffixes in fake Session IDs: the cursor detector
  treats a standalone 7–40 character hexadecimal token as a commit SHA.
- A successful chat response does not prove Provenance lookup. Provenance must
  display the Agent transcript path in its own buffer.

## Cases

### 1. Dotfiles load with no explicit transcript layouts

Exercises `e9386db` and `/home/lotso/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua`.

Steps:

1. Restart Neovim using the dotfiles configuration.
2. Run `:checkhealth louiselm`.
3. Run `:LouiselmProvenanceDecisions`.

Expect: setup succeeds without asking for transcript configuration; the
Provenance Decisions buffer opens or reports only its normal data-source state.
No “no transcript layout is configured” error appears.

Failure signature: setup rejects the config, health reports a missing layout as
an error, or Provenance immediately reports that no transcript layout is
configured.

## Evidence check

```sh
rg --hidden -n "transcript_layout" /home/lotso/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua
git -C /home/lotso/dotfiles diff --check
```

This proves the setting is absent and the config diff is clean; it cannot prove
that a running Neovim instance reloaded the local plugin. The restart and
`:checkhealth` result prove that part.

### 2. Provenance resolves a real historical Session automatically

Exercises `e9386db`, `lua/louiselm/session/locator.lua`, and the real adapter
transcript store.

Steps:

1. Run `:enew` to create a scratch buffer.
2. Enter only one known Session id as raw text, for example
   `codex/01a05142-72b8-73b0-9123-9fbef695a8cd` (without the backticks) if its
   transcript exists.
3. Put the cursor on that Session id.
4. Run `:LouiselmInspectProvenance`.
5. Wait for the Provenance buffer to finish loading, then inspect the `Transcript:`
   section.

Expect: the Session Provenance buffer opens, the transcript is shown as a
resolved absolute path, and focus is in the Provenance buffer. No
`transcript_layout` setting exists in the user config.

Failure signature: the Session is shown as unresolved solely because no layout
was configured, the wrong adapter path is shown, or the command leaves focus
in the source buffer without an error.

## Evidence check

```sh
find "$HOME/.codex/sessions" "$HOME/.claude/projects" "$HOME/.copilot" \
  "$XDG_STATE_HOME/acp-llm-adapter" -type f 2>/dev/null | rg '01a05142-72b8-73b0-9123-9fbef695a8cd|history.jsonl|events.jsonl'
```

Use the exact path displayed by the Provenance buffer to identify the matching
file. This command proves candidate files exist, not that the UI chose the
correct one; the displayed Session id and path are the UI evidence.

### 3. Provenance reports an unresolved Session clearly

Exercises the zero-match branch in `lua/louiselm/session/locator.lua`.

Steps:

1. Open any scratch buffer and insert the exact raw text
   `codex/qa-no-such-session`.
2. Put the cursor on the id and run `:LouiselmInspectProvenance`.

Expect: the Provenance buffer remains usable and says the transcript was not
found in the supported layouts. It does not crash, open a random file, or say
that configuration is missing.

Failure signature: an exception, an empty/misleading Transcript section, a
random transcript path, or the old “no transcript layout is configured” error.

### 4. Existing Provenance navigation still works

Exercises the command/UI path in `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua` and
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua`.

Steps:

1. Run `:LouiselmProvenanceDecisions`.
2. If the index loads, move to an issue or Session entry and press `<CR>`.
3. Close the detail buffer with `q`, then return to the source buffer.

Expect: the index and detail buffers open in the expected floating/scratch
windows; `<CR>` follows the selected entry; closing the detail returns focus
without damaging the source buffer.

Failure signature: the index cannot open, `<CR>` follows the wrong entry,
focus is lost, or closing the detail deletes/changes the source buffer.

## Cleanup when the round closes

Delete the scratch buffer created for case 3. Do not edit or delete Agent
transcript files. Leave the dotfiles change unstaged unless the maintainer
explicitly wants it committed in the dotfiles repository.

## Reporting back

Send the case number, exact Session id used, what appeared in the Provenance
buffer, and any surprising focus/error behavior. I will pull the evidence and
update this file.

## Round result

Cases 1–4 passed. Automatic transcript lookup works from the user's default
dotfiles config, resolves a real Codex transcript, reports missing Sessions
explicitly, and preserves Provenance list/detail navigation. The round found
one follow-up product bug: literal Markdown backticks around Session IDs are
treated as part of the ID; it is filed as `louiselm-6d29` and remains open.

The two initial misfires were recipe issues, not product findings: a dense
JSONL line contained multiple IDs, and a fake ID ended with an 8-character hex
token that the detector recognized as a commit SHA. Both are documented above
as reusable QA ground rules.

## Findings this round

**F1 — Markdown-formatted Session IDs fail lookup** (`louiselm-6d29`, open).
Entering the same Session ID with literal inline-code backticks produced an
unresolved lookup; raw text resolved. The UI detector only strips a few trailing
punctuation characters (`lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:79`) and the prompt path
only trims whitespace (`lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:865`). The automated suite
uses raw IDs, so it missed model-formatted output. Fix deferred to a follow-up.
close_reason: Cases 1-4 passed: config-free automatic lookup, real Codex transcript resolution, explicit missing-session handling, and Provenance navigation. Follow-up bug louiselm-6d29 filed and parented.

title: Derive Decision anchors and explicit Decision relations
description:
## Goal
Derive trustworthy conceptual Decisions from existing Beads records without creating a new persisted entity.

## Scope
- In scope: treat `question` issues, especially `needs-design`, as Decision anchors; carry anchor identity through Provenance; parse explicit human-authored relations such as `Decision relation: supersedes <issue-id>`; preserve recorded versus inferred edge metadata.
- Out of scope: UI, historical snapshots, QA acceptance parsing, and a new Beads schema or database.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A question issue is represented as a stable Decision anchor using its Beads issue ID.
2. Explicit supersession/reconsideration markers produce typed relationships.
3. Unrelated issue/file/time overlap never creates a Decision relationship.
4. Recorded and inferred edges retain distinct methods and confidence.
5. Missing or malformed optional relation data yields a partial result, not a fabricated edge.

## Testing
Pure fixture tests through the public Provenance API, covering question anchors, explicit relations, absent relations, malformed markers, and recorded versus inferred edges.

## Notes
The Decision is a browsing concept only. Do not persist or migrate Decision records.
close_reason: Implemented Decision anchors and explicit relation derivation with tests and quality gates passing

comments.author: 01a03ef7-f719-7942-808a-f336208c9371
comments.text: Implemented the pure Correlate.decisions() projection. Question issues become stable Decision anchors keyed by Beads issue ID; only explicit line-oriented Decision relation: supersedes|reconsiders <question-id> markers create recorded Decision edges. Unknown or malformed optional markers return diagnostics without fabricated edges, and unrelated text overlap creates no relation. Existing commit refs now carry method=recorded and confidence=1 so future bvr inferred edges can retain distinct provenance metadata. Lesson destination: this issue comment; no AGENTS.md rule or new design question is warranted.

title: capture-service reaper has never run: br is unresolvable in the serve daemon's PATH
description:
## Observed

Found live while running louiselm-y8vj Case 4. Parked a fresh disposable Run
(121046b7-dd43-4026-8922-b1978dbad0d8, 15s TTL, claim louiselm-qced) via
louiselm-capture run admit/attach/park. 35+ seconds after expiry, `run list`
correctly omitted it (list_resumable's own now_ms filter), but its on-disk
record (~/.local/state/louiselm/workflow/runs/121046b7-*.json) still shows
`"state":"cold_parked"`, not `"disposed"` -- meaning the reaper never touched
it, even though louiselm-pck2's fix (AF_UNIX) already made `serve` stable.

Checked the rest of the runs directory: several Runs are far older and equally
stuck, proving this is not new and not specific to this fixture:

- `555af6cc-b8ce-4b60-b72d-231abbc84dc6.json` -- ~48h past expiry, still
  `cold_parked`, unreleased claim on `louiselm-rcuv` (the louiselm-t6mx QA
  fixture from 2026-08-28).
- `db7b3a0e-0de8-4477-a968-418fafecc78d.json` -- ~47h past expiry, unreleased
  claim on `louiselm-rcuv` too.
- `a998611f-bc18-414a-9a94-97c962b343b0.json` -- ~14h past expiry, unreleased
  claim on `louiselm-8tzl`. `br show louiselm-8tzl` confirms: the issue is
  already `closed`, but still carries `Assignee: codex/01a04b99-...` -- a
  stale claim that outlived the issue's own closure because the reaper never
  released it.
- `72a8fa90-b11a-4dc7-a918-57f3c8fc5a64.json` -- ~14h past expiry, empty
  `cleanup` (no claim at all), also never disposed.

The reaper has evidently never disposed a single Run since this deployment
existed, independent of and in addition to louiselm-pck2's crash-loop (fixing
the crash loop did not fix this).

## Root cause

`BeadsCleanup::release` (`capture-service/src/runs.rs:237-250`) calls
`Command::new("br")` -- a bare executable name resolved via the process's
`PATH`. The `serve` systemd unit sets no `Environment=PATH=...`, so the
process inherits systemd's minimal default
(`/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin`), which does not include
`~/.cargo/bin`, where `br` is actually installed:

```
$ env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin br --version
env: 'br': No such file or directory
```

Every `Command::new("br")` call inside the reaper thread therefore fails with
`ENOENT`. This is an inconsistency already fixed once elsewhere in this same
file: `BeadsGenerator` (used by `run generate`) takes an explicit configured
executable path (`required_environment("LOUISELM_REAL_BR")`, `cli.rs:197-198`)
precisely to avoid this bare-PATH dependency. `BeadsCleanup` never got the
same treatment.

## Compounding: one failing release blocks reaping for every other Run

`RunStore::reap_expired` (`runs.rs:830-888`) loops over every Run file and,
for each one, calls the caller's `cleanup` closure per unreleased claim:

```rust
cleanup(&action).map_err(RunStoreError::Cleanup)?;
```

The `?` propagates the *first* failure out of the entire function -- out of
the whole `for entry in fs::read_dir(&self.root)?` loop, not just the current
Run. So even a single failing claim release (whether from the PATH bug above,
a deleted issue, or a `br` lock contention) aborts reaping for every other Run
in the store for that poll cycle, including Runs with no claims at all (see
`72a8fa90` above, empty `cleanup`, still never disposed).

## Silent: no observability

`cli.rs:444`: `let _ = runs.reap_expired(now_ms(), |action| cleanup.release(action));`
discards the `Result` entirely. There is no log line anywhere in the reap
path on success or failure. The only way to observe this failure today is
manually diffing on-disk Run JSON against wall-clock time, which is how this
was found.

## Fix direction

- Give `BeadsCleanup` the same explicit-executable-path pattern `BeadsGenerator`
  already uses (e.g. thread `LOUISELM_REAL_BR`, or an equivalent, through to
  `BeadsCleanup::new` at the `serve` call site, `cli.rs:441`), instead of a
  bare `Command::new("br")`.
- Make `reap_expired` resilient to one failing action: continue processing
  other Runs/other cleanup entries rather than propagating the first error via
  `?`, and surface which Run(s)/action(s) failed to the caller instead of
  aggregating into a single early return.
- Add a log line (success count, failure count/reason) at the `serve` call
  site so a stuck reaper is observable without manual JSON archaeology.

## Acceptance

- With `serve` running under the systemd unit's actual (unmodified apart from
  louiselm-pck2's AF_UNIX addition) environment, a freshly expired cold-Parked
  Run transitions to `disposed` and its claim's assignee is cleared within one
  poll interval.
- The existing stuck Runs (555af6cc, db7b3a0e, a998611f, 72a8fa90, and this
  bug's own 121046b7 fixture) are reaped once the fix is deployed, without

title: Resumed Sessions omit completed-turn usage
description:
A Session shows a [usage] line after each live completed turn, but those lines disappear when the same Agent Session is closed and resumed. A new turn after resume produces a new usage line; the completed-turn telemetry from earlier turns is what is lost.

## Observed

Subject Session: deepseek/session-5b4fb715-7267-4f09-848b-54e84fca2dfc on 2026-08-24.

Primary evidence: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/connections/3b75a6dd-f56b-407c-84ad-f9194c74e416.jsonl.

- Line 3 is session/load request id=2 for the subject Session.
- Line 161 is its response; result keys are _meta, configOptions, and modes, with no completed-turn usage.
- Replay includes conversation/tool chunks and usage_update notifications, but those usage_update values are context/cost telemetry, not the completed-turn input/output/thought/cache breakdown.
- Line 2086 is the subsequent live prompt response id=3 and contains totalTokens=624499, inputTokens=621517, outputTokens=2982, thoughtTokens=1706, cachedReadTokens=21888, cachedWriteTokens=599629. LouiseLM rendered exactly those values as [usage].

The adapter Session history has 294 entries and zero usage-bearing entries. LouiseLM state usage.json has 14 aggregate records, but its schema contains neither session_id nor turn identity.

## Symptoms

- Live completed turns show [usage] total_tokens=... with the provider breakdown.
- Closing and resuming the Session replays the conversation without those usage lines.
- Completing another turn after resume shows usage for only that new turn.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua assigns state.usage only from a live session/prompt result in handle_prompt_result. Loaded Session state starts without usage, and on_session_ready consumes configOptions but no turn usage. lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua appends [usage] only while handling live turn_done. lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua intentionally ignores turn_done and usage events. lua/louiselm/workflow/usage.lua persists aggregates by Agent option value, not by Session or turn, so it cannot restore the annotation.

## Why it was not caught

The resume tests cover replayed user/assistant/tool content but expect no usage annotations. Usage tests cover only live session/prompt results and aggregate persistence; no test closes and reloads a Session after a measured turn.

## Fix direction

Persist completed-turn usage under the stable Agent plus ACP Session identity when it is received, and restore the corresponding visible annotation during replay. Do not infer the detailed breakdown from usage_update context telemetry or from Agent-wide aggregates.

## Acceptance

- Completed-turn usage observed by LouiseLM survives closing and resuming the same Agent Session.
- Restored usage remains associated with the correct turn and retains all reported fields.
- A new post-resume turn appends its own usage without duplicating restored usage or aggregate accounting.
- Sessions created outside LouiseLM or turns recorded before persistence exists degrade cleanly when no usage is available.

## Not covered

ACP session/load does not provide historical completed-turn usage for this Agent, so LouiseLM cannot reconstruct telemetry it never persisted.
close_reason: Loaded Sessions now expose their validated ACP identity at construction, allowing Chat:attach to read exact persisted turn usage before replay.

The first ee9e541 load replayed 11 user_message_chunk updates (connection 1623ff68-7b2b-4129-a6f4-f9396bf028f0.jsonl lines 4-161); the next replay contains 12 user chunks (connection 57902114-99cf-42b6-ae4c-d88b46a85b04.jsonl lines 4-170), so the recorded completion belongs to turn 12. Real tool replay emits intermediate state_changed events. Because chat handle_event checks the latest Session snapshot rather than event.data.status, the first queued historical state event observes the already-ready snapshot and ends replay counting after turn 1. The prior test omitted intermediate replay state events.

comments.text: Manual retest on 348d6d0 proves turn accounting is now correct but presentation restore is still skipped. Live DeepSeek view on /run/user/1000/nvim.1167161.0: status=ready, source=loaded, replay_turn=14, current_turn=0, buffer_line_count=513, usage_line_positions=[], restored_turns=[]. Before the latest load, /home/lotso/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/usage.json already contained exact records for this ACP Session at turns 2, 13, and 14; the aggregate picker separately reports mode=accept-edits samples=1. Latest structural replay /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/connections/54497bd0-2fd8-43dd-8f82-87ef7314f3e8.jsonl has session/load request line 3, 14 user_message_chunk updates, and response line 176 in 11ms. Root cause: Lifecycle.new stores the known load_session_id but leaves self.acp_session_id nil; Registry returns the asynchronously starting Session, and Chat:attach reads persisted turns only when inspect().acp_session_id is nonnil. The ID becomes visible later in initialize_session before the ACP load request. The chat regression masked this by setting restored.state.acp_session_id before attach. Narrow fix direction: loaded Sessions must expose their already-validated ACP identity from construction; add a lifecycle/API assertion before initialization completes and make the chat test use the real timing.

Green: the headless API exposes prior-acp immediately, the resumed chat replay test restores exact [usage] lines, and all 481 cases/34 groups pass. stylua --check, lua-language-server Warning check, and git diff --check pass.

comments.author: codex/01a03349-c229-74e2-8d06-81fb2d016869
comments.text:
Workflow reflection after live confirmation on 0534977:

The first implementation persisted the right data but solved a narrower interpretation than the maintainer was testing. The requested outcome was observable: resume the same Session and find the prior per-turn [usage] lines in the view. Aggregate option samples and newly emitted post-resume usage were neighboring signals, not acceptance.

A full grill-me was not required for this focused defect, but a one-sentence acceptance lock was: “Resume the same Session; searching \\[usage finds the previously displayed per-turn lines beside the correct turns; the lines remain client-only; aggregate samples are separate.” Without that lock, automated evidence was allowed to substitute for the actual view.

Two test doubles then hid two production orderings. The first omitted intermediate historical state_changed events, so it missed scheduled handlers reading a later mutable Session snapshot. The second manually supplied acp_session_id before Chat:attach, so it missed the asynchronous load identity race. The regressions became trustworthy only after they reproduced those structural timings without copying sensitive Session payloads.

The efficient debugging path is now clear: inspect the exact live view first; trace one value end to end from prompt result to usage ledger to Session identity to replay turn to buffer line; encode the real ordering in a regression; and keep the bug open while the exact live reproduction remains available, until the maintainer confirms it. Diagnostic- or tracking-only commits must be called out as non-retest builds so commit movement is not mistaken for behavior movement.

Engineering invariants exposed by this bug: scheduled event handlers decide from the immutable event payload, not a later mutable Session snapshot; and an asynchronously loaded object exposes identity already known and validated at construction immediately.

title: Orphaned mock-agent headless Neovim processes leak across test runs
description:
95 orphaned headless Neovim processes (`nvim --headless --noplugin -u tests/mock/init.lua -c "lua require('louiselm.dev.mock_agent').run()"`) were found running on the maintainer's machine, all reparented to PID 1, using ~265MB RSS combined. Oldest observed start: Mon Aug 24 11:08:15 2026; newest: Wed Aug 26 07:46:45 2026 -- so this has been accumulating for at least 4 days across repeated mini.test suite runs.

## Observed

`ps -eo pid,ppid,lstart,cmd | grep mock_agent` on the maintainer's live machine (2026-08-28) showed 95 matching processes, all with ppid=1 (orphaned -- their original parent, presumably the test runner or an earlier nvim instance, exited without reaping them).

## Root cause

Unknown. The mock ACP agent (`tests/mock/init.lua` + `louiselm.dev.mock_agent.run()`) is spawned as a subprocess for protocol/integration tests per AGENTS.md section 5 ("Use the mock ACP agent for process/protocol integration tests"). Something in the test harness or the process/session lifecycle under test is not terminating these subprocesses when a test run ends -- possibly a disposal path that isn't invoked on test failure/abort, or a session that never receives a shutdown signal.

## Impact

Resource leak (RAM, process table entries) that grows with every test run over time; not currently causing failures, but unbounded accumulation on a long-lived dev machine.

## Not covered

No code investigation was done into which test(s) leave the subprocess unreaped, or whether disposal/cancellation code has a gap. This report only establishes that the leak exists and quantifies it live.

## Remediation taken

Killed the 95 currently-orphaned processes found live (see comment) to reclaim ~265MB RAM. This is symptom cleanup, not a fix -- the underlying leak in the test harness remains open.
close_reason: done

comments.author: claude/b59dc4cb-7c9d-4efc-908a-2cca0884acca
comments.text:
Root cause: tests/mock/agent_spec.lua disposed the ACP client/session Api only as the last line of each test body. A failing assert/wait_for earlier in the same test aborted the function before that line ran, leaking the spawned headless mock-agent subprocess -- with 6 tests in this file each spawning one, any flaky/failing run leaks one or more.

Fix: added a track(resource, method) helper that registers the live client/api right after creation, plus a post_case hook on the 'mock agent' MiniTest.new_set() that force-disposes any still-tracked resource after every case, pass or fail. Client:close()/Api:dispose() are already idempotent, so this is safe alongside the existing inline disposal calls.

Verified live: injected a deliberate error() right after resource creation in one test, ran just that test -- it failed as expected, and `ps` immediately after showed 0 mock_agent processes (previously this would have leaked one). Reverted the injected failure; full suite (706 cases) green, stylua clean, lua-language-server zero diagnostics, generate-api-appendix --check clean. --json

title: Grill-me needed: How should Agent account limits cross the pure-ACP boundary?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; run a focused design decision before implementing account-limit transport.

Question:
How should structured Provider account-limit state reach LouiseLM while preserving the core pure-ACP boundary and enabling both Codex and, where possible, Claude?

Context and evidence:
- The accepted human UX contract is recorded on louiselm-u56l.
- The core epic louiselm-ce6 says LouiseLM is a pure ACP client and that non-ACP capabilities arrive through external bridges, never in-plugin Provider adapters.
- Codex App Server provides account/rateLimits/read and account/rateLimits/updated with the required structured data.
- Installed @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.2 receives and caches that structured data but exposes it only as rendered /status text, not as a structured ACP event.
- Parsing /status would bind behavior to prose and is rejected.
- Starting a Codex App Server sidecar inside LouiseLM would provide data quickly but introduces a Provider protocol into the pure ACP client and does not generalize to Claude.
- A provider-neutral structured ACP extension emitted by external Agent adapters would preserve the boundary and give Codex and Claude a shared normalized contract, but requires adapter work and a clear capability negotiation/fallback rule.

Threads worth pulling:
- Standard ACP extension mechanism versus a LouiseLM-namespaced method or session update.
- Capability advertisement and behavior for Agents that do not implement account limits.
- Whether the external adapter normalizes Provider data or forwards a lossless Provider payload.
- Ownership and deduplication when several Sessions share one Agent or account.
- Versioning, validation, sparse updates, and compatibility with other ACP clients.
- Which repository owns the codex-acp and Claude adapter changes and how LouiseLM tests them deterministically.

Decision boundary:
Choose the cross-process contract and ownership. Human UX is already decided. AX and automated switching policy remain separate follow-up work.
close_reason: Maintainer accepted a capability-advertised, provider-neutral ACP custom extension owned by external Agent adapters.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: 2026-08-24 protocol finding: ACP v1 officially supports extension methods. Custom request and notification names must start with underscore, unrecognized notifications are ignored, and extensions should advertise support in agentCapabilities._meta. Source: https://agentclientprotocol.com/protocol/v1/extensibility. LouiseLM already preserves the agentCapabilities table and its ACP transport can send arbitrary request methods and receive arbitrary notifications; session lifecycle currently ignores non-session/update notifications. codex-acp uses the ACP SDK custom-handler path already for other extensions, and its schema preserves _meta, so adding a limits extension is structurally supported. Recommended boundary: external Agent adapters advertise a versioned provider-neutral account-limits capability, answer an underscore-prefixed read request, and emit an underscore-prefixed updated notification. The adapter owns Provider-specific parsing and sparse-update merging, and sends a complete normalized snapshot. LouiseLM validates snapshots and owns Agent-level freshness, UI, notification deduplication and source failover across live Sessions. This preserves the pure-ACP core, avoids /status parsing and sidecars, and lets a Claude adapter implement the same contract. Stock codex-acp 1.6.2 must be changed before the live Codex slice can work.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: Decision accepted by maintainer: use the official ACP custom-extension mechanism. External Agent adapters advertise a versioned Provider-neutral account-limits capability in agentCapabilities._meta, answer an underscore-prefixed read request and emit an underscore-prefixed update notification. Adapters own Provider parsing and sparse-patch merging and emit complete normalized snapshots. LouiseLM remains a pure ACP client and owns validation, Agent-level source selection/state, freshness, UX and notification deduplication. Incubate under a collision-resistant LouiseLM namespace; pursue ACP standardization separately only if broader adoption warrants it. No sidecar and no rendered-text parsing. Lesson routing: this decision is already enforced by parent epic louiselm-ce6 pure-ACP boundary and the child feature; no duplicate AGENTS.md rule is warranted now.

title: Start louiselm chat input in insert mode
description:
## Goal

When opening a `louiselmchat`, place the cursor directly after the `>` prompt and enter insert mode so the user can start typing immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Opening a `louiselmchat` positions the cursor immediately after the visible `>` prompt.
2. The chat buffer enters insert mode automatically.
3. The user can type and submit a message without manually moving the cursor or entering insert mode.
4. Existing chat rendering, prompt behavior, and non-chat buffers are unchanged.
5. Add or update a headless behavioral test for the initial mode and cursor position, if the current test harness supports it.

title: QA round: session filetype, collapsed tool blocks, blog wiring
description:
# Manual QA review — session filetype, collapsed tool blocks, blog wiring

**Round closed 2026-08-20.** All ten cases (0–9) run. Six findings, two fixed
and verified during the round, four filed and deliberately left open. This is
the round's sole durable record; the working file it was written in has been
deleted, per `louiselm-ri1`.

**Build under test:** `ec19281..HEAD` (15 commits). The ones with testable
behaviour:

| Commit    | What changed                                                        |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `6167df0` | writefile errors in `Chat:to_markdown` (re-verify, `louiselm-dim`)   |
| `14dbab6` | tool-call blocks collapse to `<details>` in the markdown export      |
| `f0b4d9c` | blog fragments wired into built pages (re-verify, `louiselm-xrf`)    |
| `cd37ab2` | chat buffer filetype `markdown` → `louiselm-session` + explicit TS   |

Doc/bookkeeping only, nothing to test: `ec86d89`, `a515c01`, `e9d801a`,
`3140b93`, `b1f2781`, `a8af349`, `10ba83c`, `e0c6269`, `0d53644`, `9856288`,
`cd47617`.

**Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: the last round (`louiselm-vj0`) closed on build `4e4a58b`/`674939b` and
produced two fixes that were never re-driven by hand. Since then the chat
buffer's filetype changed under every filetype-keyed plugin the user has
installed, and the export format grew raw HTML — both changes whose real
consequences live entirely outside the test process.

## Status

| #   | Case                                                        | State                          |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| 0   | `stylua --check .` on a clean tree                          | **found a defect** — see F1    |
| 1   | image.nvim no longer attaches to the transcript             | **PASS** — 1.1/1.2/1.3 all confirmed, see below |
| 2   | Markdown highlighting survived the filetype change          | **PASS** — `:Inspect` shows `markdown` + `markdown_inline` captures |
| 3   | What else was keyed on `filetype=markdown`                  | **PASS** — options identical in both buffers, nothing lost |
| 4   | `:LouiselmToMarkdown` into a missing directory (re-verify)  | **PASS** — clean notification, no E482; `louiselm-euj` reconfirmed |
| 5   | Collapsed tool blocks in a real export                      | **2 defects, both fixed and re-verified** (`a6484ea`, `3d6557d`) — F4, F5 |
| 6   | `:lines: 1` placeholder fails loudly                        | **PASS** — exit 1 naming `blog.md:5`, nothing written, `myst.yml` untouched |
| 7   | Fragment reaches the built page, in a browser (re-verify)   | **PASS** — wiring verified, page looks right; width prediction refuted |
| 8   | Same under `myst start`, not just `myst build`              | **PASS** — excerpt renders in the dev server too |
| 9   | Re-run idempotency in the real repo                         | **found a defect** — see F6 (`louiselm-qcq`); `blog.md`/`myst.yml` stable, fragment is not |

## What the test suite already covers — skip these

- `render_entry`'s exact `<sub>`/`<details>` output and block ordering
  (`tests/session/transcript_spec.lua`), and the same assertions end-to-end
  through the file (`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua`).
- `Chat:to_markdown` returning `nil, "could not write markdown file: ..."` for a
  missing destination directory — the new test added by `6167df0`. Case 4 only
  covers what the *command* shows the user, which no test reaches.
- Buffer filetype is not the literal `markdown`, and a treesitter highlighter is
  active on the chat buffer (`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`, both added by `cd37ab2`).
  They prove the two assertions in isolation; they cannot see any third-party
  plugin, which is the entire point of the change.
- Fragment bytes matching an independent TOhtml capture, three-way idempotency
  (fragments/blog.md/myst.yml), excerpt removal cleanup, and a real
  `myst build --html --strict` producing a page that references the fragment
  (`blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh`, parts 1–3). Cases 7–9 are what that
  suite structurally cannot reach: a browser, the dev server, and this repo's
  own `myst.yml` rather than a synthetic fixture root.
- Scaffold shape and marker-comment stubbing (`test-create-blog.sh`).

Baseline for this round: the full `mini.test` suite is green (0 fails, 0 notes)
at `cd37ab2`. `stylua --check .` is not — see F1.

## Setup

The installed plugin clone is already at `cd37ab2`, same as the repo, so there
is nothing to update before starting. Confirm and restart nvim:

```bash
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim log --oneline -1
git -C ~/code/louiselm log --oneline -1
```

After any fix I commit mid-round:

```vim
:lua vim.pack.update({ 'louiselm.nvim' })
```

then `:write` the buffer it opens, restart nvim, and re-confirm both commits
match.

Cases 7–9 need `nvim`, `node` (v24.16.0 here, CI pins node:24) and `myst`
(v1.10.1) on PATH — all three confirmed present.

Throughout, `<bufnr>` means the transcript buffer's number. Get it with
`:lua =vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()` while the transcript window is focused.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Carried from `louiselm-vj0` / `docs/example-workflow.md`: when the round runs
  inside louiselm's own session, the ACP log covers the whole conversation, not
  the turn being examined. Restrict the log's tool-call ids to the prefix ending
  at the last id that also appears in the export before diffing.
- Cases 1–3 share one open session on purpose (a fresh transcript has too
  little content for the perf question). Cases 4 and 5 are independent; run
  them in whatever order suits.
- Case 7 writes into `blog/` and `blog/myst.yml` in the real repo. That is
  deliberate — a fixture root is what the automated test already does — but see
  Cleanup, and do not commit any of it.
- **`:messages` is the wrong place to look for any louiselm notification on this
  machine.** louiselm surfaces user-facing errors and successes through
  `vim.notify`; snacks.nvim replaces `vim.notify` with `Snacks.notifier`, which
  renders floating windows and keeps its own history. Nothing it shows lands in
  `:messages`. Use `:lua Snacks.notifier.show_history()` (`<leader>n`) for every
  case in this file that expects a notification — 4, 5 and 6 all do. Cost of
  learning this the hard way: one round of case 4 where the expected evidence
  could not have appeared no matter what the code did.

## Cases

### 0. `stylua --check .` on a clean tree

Already run by me, before handing this over. Recorded here so the round's record
is complete.

```bash
git status --porcelain    # was empty at the time
stylua --check .; echo "exit=$?"
```

Result: `exit=1`, one diff, in `blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua`. See F1. The
tree is no longer clean after this — filing F1 wrote `.beads/issues.jsonl`, and
this file is untracked. Neither affects any case below.

### 1. image.nvim no longer attaches to the transcript

Exercises `cd37ab2` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1366`.

This is the whole reason the commit exists, and nothing in-process can assert
it. Parts 1.1–1.3 share one session; do not restart between them.

**1.1** "Transcript" here just means the conversation text that accumulates in
the louiselm window — header, then every user turn, assistant reply and tool
call, then the `> ` input line at the bottom. It is all **one buffer** (see
`Chat:attach`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1376-1378`), so the input line is
part of it too and you do not have to aim at a particular window: anywhere in
the louiselm window is the right place to stand.

So there is nothing to set up. Just use louiselm normally for a few turns —
ideally ones where the agent runs tools, since tool payloads are what make the
buffer grow fast — until it is long enough to scroll through. Length is the
whole point: a per-keystroke rescan costs nothing on a three-line buffer, which
is why a fresh session cannot show this bug.

Then, with the cursor anywhere in that louiselm window:

```vim
:lua =vim.bo[vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()].filetype
```

Expect: `louiselm-session`.

Failure signature: `markdown` — the fix did not reach the running copy, stop and
redo Setup.

**1.2** With the transcript window still focused (nothing to substitute — the
command reads the current buffer itself):

```vim
:lua =vim.iter(vim.api.nvim_get_autocmds({ buffer = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf() })):map(function(a) return a.event .. " / " .. (a.group_name or "-") end):totable()
```

Expect: no entry whose group name mentions `image`.

Failure signature: an `image.nvim`-ish group is still bound to the buffer, which
would mean it keys off something other than filetype and the fix targeted the
wrong mechanism.

**1.3** Type a sentence into the input line at a normal speed, in a session with
that long transcript loaded.

Expect: no perceptible per-keystroke lag.

Failure signature: the stutter you originally reported. If it is still there,
say so before we theorise — the mechanism check in 1.2 passing while 1.3 fails
would mean the cause was never image.nvim.

Optional, only if 1.3 is ambiguous — the A/B that settles it:

```bash
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim stash list   # expect empty
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim checkout 14dbab6
```

restart, reproduce the same transcript, type, then
`git -C ... checkout cd37ab2` and restart again. Tell me if you do this so I
know which build a later case ran against.

### 2. Markdown highlighting survived the filetype change

Exercises `cd37ab2` / the `nvim.treesitter.start(buffer, "markdown")` line.

`vim.treesitter.start` is called unprotected, so a missing parser would throw
inside `Chat:attach` and take the whole attach down. Your nvim (0.12.2) bundles
the markdown parser — I confirmed that outside the test — so this case is about

F1 is different and simpler: the gate exists, is documented, and nothing runs

## Findings this round

**F2 — Ghostty dies and takes every Neovim window with it** (`louiselm-tcb`,
P1, open investigation, likely not ours). Reported mid-round as "neovim simply
crashed". It did not. `journalctl --user` shows all three
`app-ghostty-surface-transient-*.scope` units ending within one second at
05:14:18-19, then a fresh ghostty process at 05:14:27 — eleven seconds before
Neovim was relaunched at 05:14:38. Ghostty is single-process/multi-surface, so
one death closes every window; Neovim was hung up, which is why there was no
deadly-signal banner. Ruled out: Neovim crash (no `ERR` in `nvim.log`), OOM
(`oom_kill 0` in the user slice), a Ghostty panic (no trace in a journal that
holds its full lifecycle), and `cd37ab2`'s `vim.treesitter.start` — the user's
config already ran `vim.treesitter.start()` on `FileType *`, so treesitter load
on that buffer is unchanged by the commit. Still open: the kernel log for an
AMDGPU reset, and whether image.nvim's kitty-graphics traffic is involved —
**which makes case 1.2 the discriminator, so run it.** Found by the tester when
the editor vanished, not by any case in this plan.

**F6 — `render-post` fragments are not byte-identical across runs**
(`louiselm-qcq`, P3, not fixed). `render-post.sh`'s header promises fragment
output is "a pure function of the current input" and that "running twice
against unchanged input is byte-identical". Ten consecutive runs on identical
input in an identical environment produced **four distinct fragments**; holding
`TERM` fixed still flips it, so it is run-to-run nondeterminism, not
environment sensitivity. The entire diff is CSS rule order and property order
within a rule (`.-conceal {}` moving position;
`.-markup-strong {color: …; font-weight: bold}` vs the reverse) — the `<pre>`
is identical every time and every variant renders the same, which is why case 7
looked fine. Origin is upstream: `:TOhtml` emits its `<style>` block from an
unordered table, and this pipeline preserves it verbatim by design.
`test-render-post.sh` part 2 runs precisely the right check (`diff -rq` across
two runs) and passes anyway, because its fixture excerpts are 4–5 lines of
prose and a three-line Lua snippet — too few highlight groups for the order to
move. The real excerpt produces 11 rules. Not fixed because the obvious fix
(sort the CSS in `render-post.mjs`) collides with part 1's assertion that the
fragment matches an *independent* TOhtml capture byte-for-byte; that is a
design decision, written up in the bead.

**F5 — Single-line captions run to thousands of characters** (`louiselm-u1r`,
P2, **fixed in `3d6557d`**, closed). Exposed by F4's own fix: once captions
were one line, the longest in the verified export was **7319 characters** (then
6963, 6490) — whole `br create --description` invocations with the bead body
inlined. Correct but useless as a label, and a live risk to case 7, which
renders these exports through `:TOhtml` into an iframe whose width the theme
fixes and does not expose. Bounded at 120 characters via
`strchars`/`strcharpart` rather than `string.sub`, since real titles carry em
dashes and a byte-wise cut would emit invalid UTF-8 mid-character; the full
title is untouched in the `<details>` payload. Worth noting how this was found:
not by a case, but by measuring the artifact after a fix instead of declaring
victory on the assertion that the fix targeted.
