symlinks to a whole Rust repo, discovery walks 3133 directories of which 2839
are `target/`. Measured in-process against the real config: `discover()` takes
381 ms, of which the `bvr` subtree alone accounts for 376 ms. `skills_spec.lua`
misses it because its fixtures build symlinks inside a temp root, so no case
models a symlink to a large real repository. Not fixed: nothing in
`ec19281..HEAD` touches skills, and the fix is a behavioural decision about
what "outside the root" should mean.

**F1 — `stylua --check .` fails on a clean tree** (`louiselm-d7l`, not fixed).
`blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua` is not StyLua-formatted (single-quoted strings
where the repo config sets `quote_style = "AutoPreferDouble"`), so the gate
AGENTS.md §4 declares — `stylua --check .`, unscoped, whole repo — has exited 1
since `674939b`. Introduced by the blog pipeline commit, which the previous
round (`louiselm-vj0`) had in scope and did not catch, because that round tested
the pipeline's behaviour and never ran the formatter gate. Not fixed during the
round: it is a one-command fix, but it is out of scope for the cases below and
touching the tree mid-round invalidates case 0's clean-tree premise.
close_reason:
Round complete: all ten cases were run on 2026-08-20 and all six findings are now closed (louiselm-d7l, louiselm-tcb, louiselm-msg, louiselm-cmr, louiselm-u1r, louiselm-qcq). The last one, louiselm-qcq, was fixed in this session; rollup reads 6 closed, 0 open.

The round's durable record is this issue's description, per louiselm-ri1 -- the working file it was written in was deleted at close and not committed.

Two leftovers survive this issue and are tracked elsewhere:
- louiselm-euj (LouiselmToMarkdown prompts before validating an explicit session id) was reconfirmed for a second consecutive round and remains parented under louiselm-vj0, where it was filed. Per the round's own note, a third reconfirmation should come with a fix or a wontfix rather than another re-test.
- The crash instrumentation the round installed in ~/dotfiles/zsh/.zshrc (ulimit -c unlimited plus an nvim stderr tee) was to be removed when louiselm-tcb closed. louiselm-tcb is now closed, so that removal is outstanding. It is in a different repository, so it is not actioned here.

title: Grill-me needed: how should qa-review rounds be archived, and does beads belong in the loop
description:
Not actionable as-is — this is a seed for a future grill-me session, not a
spec to implement from. Surfaced at the close of the transcript-export/
blog-publishing QA round (2026-08-18), when a process question came up that
didn't fit anywhere in the existing skill chain.

## The open questions

- **Archiving authority.** Once a qa-review round closes, does the working
  file (`QA_REVIEW.md`-style) become the durable record of what was tested
  and found, or is it disposable scratch once findings are filed to beads?
  Right now nothing says either way, so rounds just accumulate as loose
  untracked files.
- **Where archiving sits in the qa-review process.** Should the qa-review
  skill itself have a defined "closing" step that decides what happens to
  the file (commit it, summarize it into beads, delete it), or is that
  always a manual call by whoever's running the round?
- **Could beads be leveraged more directly.** Instead of (or alongside) a
  markdown working file, could a qa-review round's cases/results live in
  beads itself — e.g. as a parent issue with the plan, sub-issues per case?
  Unclear if that's better or just adds ceremony to something that works
  fine as a file today.

## Why this doesn't fit the usual chain

Their standing workflow is grill-me -> to-beads -> tasks executed across
sessions ("skill chaining"). Within a qa-review round, a code bug correctly
triggers to-beads-bug — that chain already works. But this round produced a
different kind of finding: not a bug, a question about the skills/workflow
itself. There's currently no formalized way for a skill to route that kind
of self-reflective finding anywhere — it only survived this time because the
user happened to notice and say it was worth a grill-me session. Whether
findings like this should sometimes get folded directly into a skill's own
instructions (when concrete enough) versus always deferred to a grill-me
session (when still vague) is itself part of what's open here.

## A concrete proposal already on record

This question isn't new — the user raised it explicitly at the *start* of
this same QA round, in an earlier session (`claude/85f97534-8fa6-4d95-a05a-7c0851bec937`):
"while we do this i want you to think if those reviews conversation or
document you produce as part of the review could leverage beads for
historical / archiving purposes." That session's assistant answered with a
concrete sketch the user liked and wants preserved verbatim here for the
grill-me session to react to, not re-derive:

1. **One bead per round**, type `chore`, label `qa-round`, created with
   `--description-file QA_REVIEW.md`. The whole plan lands in
   `.beads/issues.jsonl`, which is committed — so the round becomes
   greppable history instead of an untracked file you have to decide about
   at the end. That's the exact question that ended the *previous* round
   (the permissions round) unresolved too: "commit it as a record, or
   delete it."
2. **Findings hang off it as children.** `br create -t bug --parent
   <round-id>` — the graph then answers "which round found this?" and `br
   graph` shows a round's blast radius. This round's findings
   (`louiselm-dim`, `louiselm-euj`, `louiselm-d2o`, `louiselm-xrf`) are
   already beads but orphaned from the round that produced them — exactly
   the gap this proposal closes.
3. **Round-by-round narration goes in `br comments add`** — append-only and
   timestamped, matching the loop shape (plan, run, learn, edit). The
   markdown file stays the live scratchpad *during* the round since it
   churns every round; beads takes the final state on close.
4. **`--external-ref` holds the session id** (e.g.
   `claude/21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384` for this round), which
   dovetails with the user's global commit-message rule (`Refs <id>` for
   named sessions/issues), and `br orphans` catches anything referenced in a
   commit but still open.

The convergence the prior session flagged as the nice part: the
transcript-export feature this very round was testing turns a session into
a publishable artifact. So under this proposal the bead becomes the index,
the exported transcript is the evidence, and a blog post (via the same
publishing pipeline, once `louiselm-xrf` is fixed) is the human-readable
version of the same round — three layers of the same feature set reused for
QA's own record-keeping instead of a fourth bespoke mechanism.

## Bigger context

Connects to a broader, previously-discussed wish: the user's own workflow
(grill-me/beads/session-chaining) eventually being expressible as a
configurable part of louiselm itself, not just a convention they follow by
hand. Not fully re-litigated here — worth pulling that thread in the
grill-me session too.

## Not covered

No decision on the concrete proposal above — it was well-received when
sketched, but never evaluated against the three open questions or actually
tried on a round (this round still used a plain `QA_REVIEW.md`). Left for
the grill-me session: whether to adopt it as-is, adapt it, or reject it in
favor of something else.
close_reason: Resolved via grill-me. Routed to feature louiselm-ri1 (Give qa-review rounds a mandatory archiving/closing step backed by beads), with child tasks louiselm-ri1.1 (skill closing step) and louiselm-ri1.2 (retroactive close of QA_REVIEW.md and QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md, blocked on ri1.1). Adopted the concrete proposal on record as-is: one chore/qa-round bead per round via --description-file + --external-ref, findings as children via the existing to-beads-bug chain, cases stay flat (never beaded), narration via br comments, working file deleted on close. Bigger workflow-config-engine thread explicitly left out of scope per agreement.

title: Show Session Provenance: every commit and issue a Session produced
description:
## Goal

From a Session id, see everything that Session produced: its commits and the
issues it worked.

## Scope

- In scope: `louiselm://provenance/session/<id>`; the reverse traversal;
  cursor detection for Session ids.
- Out of scope: reading or rendering transcript contents.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `louiselm://provenance/session/<id>` lists commits carrying that Session in a
   trailer and issues carrying it as actor.
2. The view offers the resolved transcript path, or states plainly that it could
   not be resolved.
3. A Session id with no commits and no issues renders as an empty result, not an
   error.

## Testing

- Headless behavioural smoke test.
- A Session appearing on only one of the two edges renders the populated side
  and marks the other empty.

## Notes

Completes the third traversal direction. With commit-rooted and issue-rooted
views already in place, this is the slice that makes Provenance navigable from
whichever end the maintainer happens to be holding.
close_reason: Completed: added reverse Session Provenance over git trailers and br actor fields, with transcript resolution and empty-side rendering; 688 MiniTest cases and all quality gates pass.

comments.author: codex/01a0428e-6b0e-7fa3-a088-c03e6b235bf4
comments.text: Lesson: reverse Provenance can stay derived and read-only by joining git log --all trailer edges with br list --status all actor edges. Session IDs must be detected before issue IDs because the trailing session component can otherwise be mistaken for a Beads issue. No standing AGENTS.md rule or unresolved design question is warranted.

title: Skill/file/buffer/selection context pickers are unreachable through the documented :LouiselmChat setup path
description:
The chat context-queuing API (`pick_skill`, `pick_file`, `mention_buffer`, `send_selection`) documented in README.md under "Chat context" is completely unreachable through the plugin's own documented setup path, so no user who follows the README can ever attach a file, skill, buffer mention, or visual selection to a prompt.

## Observed

Found 2026-08-20 while setting up a manual QA round for louiselm-2w4 (native ACP skill invocation): asked the user to invoke the skill picker to test it, and they had never wired anything for it -- because there is nothing to wire it to.

`grep -rn "pick_skill\|pick_file\|mention_buffer\|send_selection" lua/ --include="*.lua" | grep -v chat/init.lua` returns nothing: these four `Chat` methods are defined in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua and never called anywhere else in the tree -- not in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua (which backs `:LouiselmChat` and every other registered `:Louiselm*` command), not anywhere.

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua` registers 12 `:Louiselm*` ex commands (LouiselmChat, LouiselmNewSession, LouiselmResume, LouiselmSwitchSession, LouiselmRenameSession, LouiselmSessionId, LouiselmToMarkdown, LouiselmCloseSession, LouiselmCancel, LouiselmSessionOptions, LouiselmPermissions, LouiselmInline) -- none of them calls pick_skill/pick_file/mention_buffer/send_selection.

The `chat` object these methods live on is a local upvalue private to `Command.register()`'s closure (command.lua:194 `local chat`); nothing exposes it, and `Louiselm.setup()` (lua/louiselm/init.lua) returns only a boolean. So even a user willing to write their own keymap has no object to call these methods on unless they bypass `Louiselm.setup()`/`:LouiselmChat` entirely and hand-construct a second, parallel `Chat` instance via the low-level `require("louiselm.ui.chat").new(sessions, {...})` constructor -- which would not be attached to the same session as their real chat buffer.

README.md documents these four methods under "## Chat context" (around line 438) as plain Lua snippets (`chat:mention_buffer()`, `chat:send_selection()`, `chat:pick_file()`, `chat:pick_skill()`) with no indication that `chat` here is a user-constructed low-level object, not the one `:LouiselmChat` creates -- reading the README top to bottom gives no working path to ever call them.

## Symptoms

- Following the README exactly (`Louiselm.setup(config)` + `:LouiselmChat`), there is no command, keymap, or other UI affordance to pick a skill, pick a file, mention the source buffer, or send a visual selection.
- The entire native/inject skill-invocation feature (including the just-shipped louiselm-2w4) is unreachable in practice for the documented setup path.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua never registers commands for these four `Chat` methods, and never exposes the `chat` instance it privately constructs.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` and `tests/ui/context_spec.lua` call `chat:pick_skill()` etc. directly on a `Chat` object constructed in the test, which is exactly the low-level path the README also (accidentally) documents -- so the tests exercise the methods correctly but never assert that the *shipped, documented, high-level setup path* (`:LouiselmChat`) can reach them. No test covers `command.lua`'s command surface for context actions because there was never a command to cover.

## Fix direction

Add `:LouiselmPickSkill`, `:LouiselmPickFile` (optional root arg, `nargs = "?"`, mirroring `:LouiselmToMarkdown`'s optional-arg pattern), `:LouiselmMentionBuffer`, and `:LouiselmSendSelection` to command.lua, following the existing `if chat == nil then report_error("no chat session is open") ... end` pattern used by `:LouiselmCancel`/`:LouiselmSessionOptions`/`:LouiselmCloseSession` (these need an already-open session to queue context onto, unlike `:LouiselmChat`/`:LouiselmPermissions` which use `ensure_chat()` to open one on demand). Update README's command list (around line 269) and the "Chat context" section to stop implying the low-level constructor snippet is reachable from the documented setup path.

## Acceptance

- New `:Louiselm*` commands registered and covered by a test in tests/ui/command_spec.lua that drives them through the real `:LouiselmChat` + `Command.register()` path (matching the file's existing "through the normal chat path" test style), not just calling the Chat method directly.
- README updated to list the new commands and no longer implies the raw snippets are usable from a documented setup.

## Not covered

- Whether default keymaps (not just ex commands) are also warranted -- left as a separate decision; this bug is about there being no path at all, not about ergonomics beyond a command existing.
close_reason: Fixed in 9e553a1. Added :LouiselmPickSkill, :LouiselmPickFile [root], :LouiselmMentionBuffer, :LouiselmSendSelection to lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua, matching the existing chat==nil guard pattern used by :LouiselmCancel/:LouiselmSessionOptions. Tests: command existence check, a combined 'no chat session is open' case for all four, and a real end-to-end test driving :LouiselmMentionBuffer through :LouiselmChat + a fake ACP process, asserting the chip renders and the queued context is sent in the next session/prompt. Updated README's command list and Chat context section. Gates: full mini.test suite green, stylua and lua-language-server clean repo-wide (excluding a pre-existing unrelated blog/ script). Deferred: default keymaps beyond the ex commands, per the bead's own 'Not covered' note.

title: Investigate default availability of LouiselmResume
description:
## Goal

Determine whether the new `:LouiselmResume` command is available for a normal louiselm.nvim installation using the user configuration in `~/.config/nvim`, and make it available by default if it is not.

## Evidence

The previous commit `798712b` added `LouiselmResume` registration inside `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua`, but registration appears to depend on an explicit `require("louiselm.ui.chat.command").register()` call. The repository test and manual init files call this explicitly; verify whether the production plugin entrypoint does so for ordinary Neovim startup.

## Scope

- Reproduce/check command availability from the normal plugin runtime path and from the user configuration path.
- Trace plugin load order and setup behavior, including whether `louiselm.setup()` is required before the command exists.
- If missing by default, add the narrowest production registration fix and update/extend headless behavioral coverage and documentation as needed.
- Preserve explicit configuration behavior and avoid duplicate-registration side effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The task records the observed behavior and root cause for a normal installation.
2. `:LouiselmResume` and `:LouiselmResume!` are available after ordinary plugin loading, without requiring users to manually require/register the command.
3. Existing command registration remains repeatable and tests cover the production startup path.
4. Focused tests, the full mini.test suite, StyLua, and lua-language-server checks are run or their unavailability is reported.
close_reason: Registered all chat commands from successful louiselm.setup(), added a regression test proving LouiselmResume and bang support are available after setup, and updated README wording. Verification: focused setup test passed; full mini.test suite passed (126 cases, with swap files directed to /tmp); stylua --check passed; lua-language-server --check passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Inline human-readable rendering for jsonl log lines
description:
Idea from conversation, not yet designed: for jsonl files, render each line's *display* as a compact human-readable string (e.g. "14:23:05 WRN nvim.175374 server_start:197 Failed to start server...") via conceal/virtual-text, without touching the underlying buffer content — the file stays true jsonl on disk (greppable/diffable/pipeable).

Context: jsonl.nvim already renders jsonl nicely via treesitter formatting. jsonlogs.nvim takes a different approach — splitting into an expanded pretty-printed panel/view — which trades away the one-line-per-record structure that makes jsonl useful in the first place. That's judged as doing too much for the goal here.

Closer prior art: render-markdown.nvim's approach of decorating a buffer's *display* without mutating its content. Worth checking whether treesitter's line-level virtual text/decoration hooks, or the same conceal machinery jsonl.nvim already uses, can drive this before reaching for a new plugin/dependency.

Not yet scoped as an implementation task — needs design: what subset of jsonl schemas to target (arbitrary vs known log formats), how much configurability, conflict with existing jsonl.nvim formatting.

comments.author: claude-code/01e02390-3c65-4332-a93e-a9f1a4ff9bef
comments.text:
Implemented as lua/louiselm/forensics/{log_view.lua,command.lua} + :LouiselmForensicsLogView.

Confirmed target: acp-llm-adapter/acp-proxy stdout-jsonrpc.log files under
~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter -- real JSON-RPC 2.0 ACP traffic, one message
per line. Design landed on Neovim's native fold machinery instead of extmark
overlay: foldexpr forces one fold per line, foldtext renders a compact human
summary (dispatches on session/update's sessionUpdate kind, reusing the same
kind vocabulary session/lifecycle.lua already handles), buffer content is
never touched, zo/zO reveals the exact raw line. Reuses acp/protocol.lua's
decode/validate rather than re-parsing JSON-RPC.

Verified live against a real 1051-line log: all lines fold/render, widths
stay bounded, zero errors.

Known limitation, not fixed here: streamed text arrives as one JSON-RPC line
per small delta, so a paragraph of agent_message_chunk/agent_thought_chunk
becomes many one-or-two-word folds rather than one merged block. Fixing that
means multi-line folds keyed on messageId -- a materially bigger feature than
this one-line-to-one-fold v1. Left as a possible follow-up, not filed as a
separate issue yet pending user reaction to v1.

comments.author: claude-code/01e02390-3c65-4332-a93e-a9f1a4ff9bef
comments.text:
Follow-up from live testing: za felt sluggish, and a request to keep this
free of regex.

Regex removed: the only pattern-matching in the file was single_line's gsub
collapsing embedded newlines for display; replaced with plain (non-pattern)
vim.split/table.concat/vim.trim. JSON parsing itself was never regex -- it
already went through vim.json.decode via acp/protocol.lua.

Investigated delegating fold *boundaries* to the already-installed jsonl/json
treesitter fold query instead of the hand-rolled foldexpr, per the instinct
that hand-rolling is redundant when a treesitter parser is already there.
Tested directly: wired foldexpr to vim.treesitter.foldexpr() against a real
log and foldlevel() came back 0 for every line. Root cause: every ACP
JSON-RPC record is exactly one physical line, and Neovim's/Vim's fold model
only ever folds a node whose start and end line differ -- a same-line node
never registers as a fold, treesitter or not. There's no existing
one-fold-per-line building block to delegate to for this shape; forcing a
fold boundary at every line via a custom foldexpr remains the only way to
get it. Documented this finding in the module's doc comment so it isn't
re-litigated later.

Real fix for the sluggishness: foldtext had zero caching -- it re-decoded
and re-summarized the raw line from scratch on every redraw of every visible
closed fold. Added a per-buffer, per-line cache keyed against the exact raw
line text (self-invalidating on edit, no changedtick bookkeeping needed).
Added a test that spies on render_line to prove a repeated foldtextresult()
call for an unchanged line hits the cache instead of re-rendering.

Caveat: benchmarked the fix against the real 1051-line log used earlier
(lines up to 55KB) and could not reproduce dramatic sluggishness even before
this fix -- full-buffer foldtextresult sweep ~26ms, 50x za ~1ms in headless
timing. So either this fix already resolves what was felt live, or the
tested file differs from what's slow, or the slowness is in real terminal
redraw rather than computation. Asked the user to re-test and report back
with which file if still slow.

comments.author: claude-code/01e02390-3c65-4332-a93e-a9f1a4ff9bef
comments.text:
Reverted (commits a531705, 771484a): the ACP-only forensics implementation
did not satisfy after two rounds of live testing, even after the caching
fix -- za still didn't feel right in practice.

Redirecting scope back to the original framing: fast and generic, not
ACP-log-specific. It must work on arbitrary jsonl, including this project's
own .beads/issues.jsonl -- the ACP-only implementation didn't (it only
understood JSON-RPC envelopes via acp/protocol.lua).

New technical direction to explore: jsonlogs.nvim's split-panel approach is
still judged as doing too much (see original description), but its
rendering logic might be replicable faster and more generically by building
on an actual jsonl treesitter parser (jsonl.nvim's tree-sitter-jsonl grammar
is already installed) rather than hand-decoding each line with
vim.json.decode + hand-written per-field-shape summarizers in Lua. Worth
investigating before the next attempt: whether treesitter's own incremental
parse/query caching (as opposed to this repo's foldtext-per-redraw
recompute) is what actually gets the performance and genericness right, and
whether fold boundaries still need the hand-rolled one-line-forces-a-fold
trick (still true per the prior finding: same-line nodes never register as
a Vim fold) or whether a non-fold display mechanism reads better anyway.

Deferred pending a redesign; not closing since the underlying need (some
of these logs are unreadable one-line JSON) is still real.

title: Park
description: Non-destructive suspension of a Run: every in-flight turn is Cancelled, Sessions are retained where possible, and the Run waits for an operator decision under a declared expiry. Warm Park stays within one Neovim lifetime and resumes exactly. Cold Park has survived an editor exit, so its Sessions are gone and resume is lossy reconstruction via ACP loadSession.
design: Established by the louiselm-qbr.8 grill-me session on 2026-08-26, with explicit maintainer confirmation of the final summary. Chosen over killing an over-budget Run, because an attention control plane whose response to 'this needs a decision' is to destroy the work has inverted its own thesis. The warm/cold split follows from Agents being vim.system children of Neovim (lua/louiselm/acp/transport.lua:164).
notes: Distinguish from the existing triad: Park is not Disposal (a deliberate end) and not Abandonment (loss). Park expiry converts a Park into a Disposal, releasing claims and retaining Forensics. Per the Staged context record, cold-Park resume is recoverable, NOT lossless. An Agent that does not advertise loadSession cannot be cold-Parked at all, and admission must say so up front. Resuming a Park is an operator act, never an Agent act, and cannot exceed the original envelope on any axis.

title: Analyse DDD and AI-coding lessons for the LouiseLM workflow
description:
## Goal

Analyse Miłosz Smółka's article, Domain-Driven Design matters more when AI writes your code, and translate its findings into concrete improvements or deliberate non-changes for the LouiseLM agent workflow.

Source: https://threedots.tech/post/ddd-and-ai-coding/

## Scope

- In scope: the article claims about domain modeling as shared understanding, design before code generation, ubiquitous language and bounded contexts, developer accountability, and not delegating thinking.
- In scope: map those claims against LouiseLM concepts and practices including canonical vocabulary, grill-me design sessions, Beads work tracking, AGENTS.md contracts, Sessions, Runs, Handoffs, Validation, Assessment, Forensics, and tracer-bullet tasks.
- In scope: recommend a small set of actionable workflow changes, with expected benefit and tradeoff.
- Out of scope: adopting tactical DDD patterns in the Lua implementation, introducing ceremony for simple CRUD-like work, or treating the article as authoritative evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Summarize the authors findings accurately and distinguish direct claims from interpretation.
2. Produce an application map showing which LouiseLM workflow surfaces already embody each idea and where gaps remain.
3. Recommend no more than five concrete changes, each with rationale, scope, and a way to test whether it helps.
4. Explicitly identify practices to avoid because they would add ceremony without improving domain clarity.
5. Record unresolved product or architecture choices as separate needs-design questions rather than silently deciding them.

## Testing

- Verify each article-derived claim against the source URL.
- Check proposed terminology against the repository vocabulary reference records.
- Ensure recommendations preserve the project contract: correctness and safety first, explicit lifecycle ownership, bounded work generation, and no unnecessary abstractions.

## Notes

The article is an opinion piece about complex, long-lived software rather than a universal process prescription. The analysis should treat LouiseLM itself as the domain under discussion and focus on improving how humans and Agents build shared understanding before implementation.
close_reason: Analysis complete, posted as a comment on this issue. Summary: LouiseLM's existing loop (Grill, vocabulary/reference records, Live acceptance discipline) already embodies nearly every claim in the article -- likely because both were independently designed around the same values (shared understanding over artifacts, human accountability, explicit reasoning capture). 3 recommendations (not padded to 5): R1 write down the already-practiced but unstated grill-proportionality rule; R2 filed separately as louiselm-n83s since it changes the vocabulary contract; R3 confirmed the existing close-discipline already satisfies the article's 'don't delegate thinking' concern, no new mechanism needed. 4 practices explicitly flagged to avoid as ceremony. Full AC-by-AC mapping and verbatim article verification in the comment.

comments.author: claude/ea8b846d-3700-44ed-aa39-ffb9e68c8973
comments.text:
## 1. Summary: direct claims vs. interpretation

Source verified directly (https://threedots.tech/post/ddd-and-ai-coding/, Miłosz Smółka,
2026-08-20).

**Direct claims** (the author states these as the article's thesis, not hedged):

1. Eric Evans' 2003 claim still holds: "the hard part of software engineering is understanding
   the problem domain and modeling it well in code" -- AI changes *what* is hard to produce, not
   *what* is hard to understand.
2. A domain model's value is the team's shared understanding built while making it, not the
   artifact itself; letting AI generate a domain model from documents skips the part that
   mattered.
3. Design and team discussion should happen *before* code generation, not be reconstructed
   afterward through PR review -- otherwise review becomes "the start of a discussion" instead of
   "a double-check."
4. Ubiquitous language matters *more* with agents because "they'll look for the names you give
   them" and may naively unify entities that are legitimately distinct (bounded contexts).
5. Trusting AI output requires someone accountable who understands the domain well enough to
   catch it when the output is wrong.
6. Much of engineering is thinking, not typing; delegating the thinking erodes the mental models
   needed to judge future AI output, so working problems by hand still has value.

**Interpretation / more contestable** (author's own framing, illustrative rather than argued):

- The "agentic setup optimization" trap as a direct successor to framework-obsession -- an
  analogy, not demonstrated.
- The $1/month anecdote is one illustrative failure, not a controlled finding.
- "Keep documentation in Markdown near code" is a specific tooling preference, not a general law.
- The closing "mix old-school and new" stance is explicitly hedged by the author as uncertain.

## 2. Application map

LouiseLM's own working loop (`docs/example-workflow.md`) and vocabulary system
(`br list --type vocabulary --status all`) were designed independently of this article, before it
existed, but converge on nearly every one of its claims -- which is itself the most useful finding
here.

| Article idea | LouiseLM surface | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Domain model's value is team understanding, not the artifact | **Grill** stage: "The stage ends when both sides can state the same plan. Not before." Vocabulary records carry a `design` field citing *which grill session* produced them, not just a definition. | Strong match |
| Design before code generation | **Grill -> Route to beads**: reasoning and rejected alternatives are captured in the issue *before* Execute. | Match, but heavier by default than the article's "sticky notes" framing -- see gap below |
| Ubiquitous language; agents will naively unify distinct entities | 15 `vocabulary/reference` Beads records, each with an explicit `notes` field naming what to **avoid** and what to **distinguish**. `louiselm-7bm3` (Provider) exists *because* Provider/Agent got conflated once already -- the exact failure mode the article warns about, already caught. `AGENTS.md` requires loading this vocabulary before any semantic work. | Strong match, arguably exceeds the article -- it's a durable, queryable glossary with negative space, not just a team agreement |
| Bounded contexts: same concept, different valid names per subsystem | Not present. Current convention is one canonical name, enforced project-wide, with everything else listed as "avoid." | Gap, but arguably correct at this scale -- see Avoid-list below |
| Developers (or the maintainer) stay accountable, domain-expert-trusted | "the decisions, and only the decisions, belong to the human" (Grill). `AGENTS.md` section 5.2, Live acceptance: automated gates cannot close a defect while a live reproduction exists -- "keep it open until the maintainer confirms." | Strong match -- LouiseLM structurally refuses to let an agent self-certify domain-level correctness |
| Don't delegate thinking | Grill's one-question-at-a-time-with-a-recommended-answer protocol is a *structural* answer to this: the human reacts and corrects rather than generating from a blank page, which keeps judgment engaged without maximal friction. This is a genuine LouiseLM-specific mechanism the article doesn't describe -- the article's own remedy is individual (spend time thinking), LouiseLM's is procedural. | Strong match, and a real point of originality worth naming, not just a mapping |

One structural point the article doesn't address at all, because it doesn't apply to a human
team: every LouiseLM agent session starts with *zero* memory of prior sessions. `AGENTS.md` plus
the vocabulary records are the mechanism by which a domain-illiterate newcomer (every session, by
construction) becomes domain-literate fast enough to be trusted with real decisions. This
session's own bootstrap -- reading `AGENTS.md` cold, loading vocabulary, following the
close-discipline correctly across four issue closes today -- is itself evidence the mechanism
works, not just a claim that it should.

## 3. Recommendations (3, not padded to 5)

**R1 -- Write down the grill-proportionality rule that is already being practiced but never
stated.**
Today's session closed `louiselm-7tvl`, `louiselm-qbr.3.2.5`, and `louiselm-nwrv` on evidence
alone, no grill; `kd2b` (this one) and prior architecture work (Park, Run, Generator) went through
full grill-me sessions. The size-matching already happens correctly, but there's no written
criterion an agent or the maintainer could consult to check a borderline case, or teach it to a
new contributor. *Scope:* a short addition to `docs/example-workflow.md`'s Grill section, not a
new mechanism. *Test:* take five recently-closed issues, hide their actual resolution path, and
check whether the written criterion predicts which ones needed a grill and which didn't.

**R2 -- Decide whether the vocabulary schema should ever support a bounded-context-style
surface-specific name, before it's forced under time pressure.**
Today's vocabulary already contains one near-miss: AX and UX are a deliberate split of what is
largely the same underlying state into two audience-facing names. As AX surfaces grow relative to
UX, LouiseLM may need the same concept to legitimately read differently in an agent-facing surface
vs. a human-facing one -- exactly what DDD bounded contexts exist for. Today's convention (one
canonical name, everything else is "avoid") would fight that if it happens. This changes a
project-wide contract (the vocabulary schema and its consumption rule in `AGENTS.md`), so per the
project's own vocabulary-conflict rule ("If competing meanings would materially change
architecture... stop and ask"), **I filed this as a needs-design question
(`louiselm-n83s`) instead of deciding it here.**

**R3 -- Nothing further to build; the existing close-discipline already does what the article asks
for.**
I looked for a gap in "does an agent's solo decision get checked for real understanding, not just
pattern-matching" (the sharpest form of "don't delegate thinking" applied to an agent instead of a
human). `AGENTS.md`'s close-discipline already requires routing what the work taught -- evidence,
false starts, or a named destination -- before closing a bug/task/feature, which is exactly the
"write down why, not just what" mechanism the article recommends. This session's own closes today
complied with it every time. No new rule needed; recorded here so the "don't delegate thinking"
claim was actually checked against a mechanism rather than assumed satisfied.

## 4. Practices to avoid (ceremony without domain-clarity benefit)

- **A full grill-me session for every closeable issue.** Today's evidence-based closes (`7tvl`,
  `qbr.3.2.5`, `nwrv`) would have been pure overhead if forced through interrogation; the decision
  was already unambiguous from the code and tests.
- **Adopting DDD's bounded-context tooling wholesale** (context maps, anti-corruption layers,
  per-subsystem glossaries). LouiseLM is one small codebase without the multi-team integration
  costs that justify bounded-context pluralism. The current single-canonical-name-with-explicit-
  avoid-list is stricter and correct at this scale; loosening it without the underlying problem
  (R2 aside, which is a narrow, deliberate exception, not a wholesale adoption) would just
  reintroduce naming drift.
- **A mandatory domain-model diagram or UML artifact as a Grill deliverable.** The article's own
  central warning is that an AI-generated domain model fails because it substitutes an artifact
  for the understanding that was supposed to produce it. Adding a required diagram step would risk
  exactly that trap inside the mechanism meant to prevent it.
- **A formal prompt-precision style guide for Beads issue descriptions**, modeled on the article's
  vague-vs-precise prompting example. Today's issue descriptions (including several read closely
  this session) are already precise by convention. Formalizing an already-solved problem is
  ceremony, not improvement.

## 5. Unresolved question filed separately

`louiselm-n83s` -- "Grill-me needed: should the vocabulary schema support a bounded-context-style
surface-specific name, and if so, what's the rule for when it's allowed vs. drift?" -- labeled
`needs-design`, per R2 above. Not resolved here.

title: Run
description: One execution instance of a workflow definition. A Run owns a supervision tree of Sessions, a bounded budget for generated work, a capability envelope, and a durable record held by capture-service that outlives the Neovim process.
design: Established by the louiselm-qbr.8 grill-me session on 2026-08-26, with explicit maintainer confirmation of the final summary. Established because Validation (definition-scoped, static) and admission (Run-scoped, live) are provably different contracts: an open skill graph makes recursion undecidable from any single document.
notes: Use Run for the execution instance and for anything scoped to it (Run budget, Run ancestry, Run record). Distinguish from the workflow definition, which is a static SKILL.md graph shared by many Runs. Avoid: execution, job, invocation. A Run owns Sessions; it is not itself a Session.

title: Export curated public LuaCATS API appendix
description: Use lua-language-server documentation export to generate a committed API appendix for only the supported extension boundaries: headless Session API, typed events, permission policies, and Agent configuration. Exclude ACP transport internals, UI, schema machinery, mocks, development helpers, and implementation state. Make scope and output deterministic; CI rejects drift. Do not create a second AX contract or add runtime dependencies.
close_reason: Added lua/louiselm/docs/api_appendix.lua: a pure function that renders a curated Markdown appendix from a lua-language-server --doc export (doc.json), filtered to an explicit per-file allowlist across four sections matching AGENTS.md section 1's extension boundaries (Headless Session API: session/init,api,lifecycle,registry,limits,validation.lua; Typed Events: session/events.lua; Permission Policies: permission/init,policy,store,human-prompt.lua; Agent Configuration: agent/init,config,health,spawn.lua). scripts/generate-api-appendix (+ generate_api_appendix.lua) shells out to lua-language-server --doc, decodes doc.json, and writes/checks doc/api.md, mirroring generate-vimdoc's --check pattern. Wired ./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check into the typecheck CI job (the only job with lua-language-server on PATH) and verified the check actually fails on injected staleness before wiring it up (louiselm-w726's lesson). README links to doc/api.md and documents the regen commands. TDD red-green with 6 focused unit tests on the pure filter/render function (no dependency on the real LSP binary in the test suite -- see comment for why). Full suite green (507+ cases), StyLua clean, LuaLS zero diagnostics.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: lua-language-server's rendered doc.md drops the underlying type for --doc alias definitions with no piped union (e.g. a plain fun(...) alias renders with an empty body in doc.md), and even piped-union aliases' rendered text only lives in doc.json's defines[].desc, not doc.md. Parse doc.json (vim.json.decode) instead of doc.md: each top-level entry has name/fields/defines, each field has name/view/desc, and defines[1].view holds the alias's raw underlying type when desc is absent. Verified against lua-language-server 3.18.2-dev.

Verified afterward by running the suite (all green) rather than confirming a prior failure. Flagging for consistency with how louiselm-b638's deviation was recorded.

title: QA round: cold Park command + tool inspector close + onboarding Tutor (ab8e71c..HEAD)
description:
# Manual QA review — cold Park feature + tool inspector close + onboarding Tutor

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `ab8e71c..HEAD` (7 commits, 2026-08-28 14:53–16:21):
`44b7cdd` close tool inspector with `q`, `71a6ae3` add cold Park command,
`64523ac` restore Park Run state, `097bcd6` add first-run onboarding Tutor.
(`f092fec`, `862fd1e`, `8782442` are README/CI-only — no manual case.)
**Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: last QA round closed at `ab8e71c`. Everything since is untested by a
human. The headline change is `:LouiselmPark`/`:LouiselmResumePark` growing
real state: zero-claim Park is now allowed (previously rejected), and resume
now reconstructs `claims`/`generated_work` instead of discarding them.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Tool inspector closes with `q` / `<Esc>` | **passed** — both keys close the floating window and return focus, per user report |
| 2 | `:LouiselmTutor` opens read-only Tutor | **passed** — well-formatted content, resolved from runtime path not cwd, edits blocked, per user report |
| 3 | `:LouiselmPark` succeeds with zero live claims | **passed (partial)** — proven via case 4's run record (`claims:[]`, `state:cold_parked`); the "no picker when nothing staged" half wasn't separately exercised |
| 4 | `:LouiselmPark` with staged context asks to confirm; Cancel aborts | **passed** — `claude/6b80a87e-…380d`: Cancel produced no notification and no run; Park produced run `72a8fa90-b11a-4dc7-a918-57f3c8fc5a64`, `state:"cold_parked"`, `claims:[]` |
| 5 | `:LouiselmResumePark` restores claims + generated-work budget | **blocked on F1** — resume never completes, so restoration can't be observed |

## Setup

The nvim plugin checkout at `~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim`
is a separate git worktree tracking this repo (`origin` = `file:///home/lotso/code/louiselm`),
currently at `097bcd6` — already matches HEAD, no reinstall needed for the Lua
side.

**`louiselm-capture` is stale and will block cases 3–5.** The binary on `PATH`
at `~/.local/bin/louiselm-capture` is dated 2026-08-26 20:46 — built *before*
`run admit`/`run attach` existed and before the Run schema moved to version 4
(commit `c65ca9f`, 2026-08-27). Confirmed by hand: it rejects `run admit`/`run
attach` outright ("run supports only list and park") and fails `run list`
against any schema-v4 file with `invalid run: stored Run is invalid` — that is
what's currently happening against your own `~/.local/state/louiselm/workflow/runs/`
(two already-expired parked runs from earlier today trip the same stale
check; they're harmless leftovers that a rebuilt binary will just filter out
as expired, no cleanup needed).

Rebuild and install before cases 3–5:

```bash
cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm/capture-service && cargo build --release
cp target/release/louiselm-capture ~/.local/bin/louiselm-capture
louiselm-capture run list   # expect: [] (not an error) — proves the binary is current
```

I already ran the `cargo build --release` — it succeeded and `target/release/louiselm-capture`
is current. I have **not** copied it over `~/.local/bin/louiselm-capture` yet:
that file also backs your running `louiselm-capture.service` (systemd
`ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/louiselm-capture serve`), so say go-ahead before I
overwrite it. You don't need to restart the service — the CLI subcommands used
by Park (`run admit`/`attach`/`park`/`list`) touch the filesystem directly,
never the daemon.

**Do not run `:LouiselmPark` from the session you're reading this in.** I
checked the live instance (`$NVIM`): your current chat view's session *is*
this Claude Code session (`claude/5f934d18-b9b8-42b3-91cc-35fb293d14dc`).
Cold-Parking it would suspend the session you're driving me from. For cases
3–5, open a **second**, disposable chat session in the same Neovim instance
(`:Louiselm` → new session, any agent) and drive Park/Resume from that one.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- A `louiselm-capture` binary on `PATH` that predates the Run schema it's
  asked to read fails closed with a generic "stored Run is invalid" — no
  version number in the message. If case 3/4/5 fails with exactly that text,
  suspect a stale binary before suspecting the Lua change; re-run the `run
  list` sanity check in Setup.
- `br list --assignee <session_id> --status in_progress` is what `:LouiselmPark`
  queries for live claims — it needs `session_id` to be `<agent>/<acp_session_id>`
  exactly, and needs the `br` binary in the shim'd `PATH` `service.lua` builds
  (see `Run tools require the br shim, br, and louiselm-capture executables`).
  If claims come back empty when you expected one, confirm the issue is really
  claimed by that exact session id: `br list --assignee <id> --status in_progress --json`.

## Cases

### 1. Tool inspector closes with `q` and `<Esc>`

Exercises `44b7cdd` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1230-1237`.

The automated test only asserts the inspector *buffer* becomes invalid after
calling the keymap callback directly — it never asserts what happens to the
*floating window* on a real close, which is the part a human notices.

Steps:

> In your live chat buffer, trigger any tool call (e.g. ask the agent to read
> a file). Move the cursor onto the tool-call summary line and inspect it
> (however you normally open the tool inspector — winbar click or its mapped
> keymap). With the floating inspector window focused, press `q`.

Expect: the floating window disappears entirely and focus returns to the chat
buffer/window you were in before opening the inspector. Repeat, but press
`<Esc>` instead of `q`, from a fresh tool inspection — same result.

Failure signature: the window stays open but goes blank/empty (buffer deleted
but window not closed — Neovim can replace a deleted buffer's window with an
alternate buffer instead of closing it), or focus lands somewhere unexpected
(e.g. a different existing window) rather than back on the chat.

### 2. `:LouiselmTutor` opens a read-only onboarding Tutor

Exercises `097bcd6` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:295-310`.

Steps:

> Run `:LouiselmTutor`.

Expect: opens `docs/tutorial.md` (resolved from the plugin's `runtimepath`,
not your cwd) in the current window, `filetype=markdown`, and the buffer is
non-modifiable — try `i` + type a character, or `:normal! ihello`, and confirm
Neovim refuses the edit (`E21: Cannot make changes, 'modifiable' is off`).

Failure signature: command errors with "could not find the bundled Tutor"
(runtime-file resolution broken — check `nvim_get_runtime_file("docs/tutorial.md", false)`
directly), or the buffer opens editable.

### 3. `:LouiselmPark` succeeds with zero live Beads claims

Exercises `71a6ae3` (`service.lua` dense-array validation, no longer requires
`#claims > 0`) + the `capture-service` CLI fix filtering empty `--claims`
entries. This is the actual behavior change in this round: before, Park
*required* at least one `in_progress`-claimed issue for the parking session or
it errored; now zero is fine.

Needs: Setup done (rebuilt `louiselm-capture` installed), a **second** chat
session (see Setup), and that session's `<agent>/<acp_session_id>` must have
**no** Beads issue currently claimed to it — sanity-check with
`br list --assignee <agent>/<acp_session_id> --status in_progress --json` and
expect `{"issues":[]}` before you start.

Steps:

> In the second session, with no staged context (no queued prompt, no pending
> skill, no staged file), run `:LouiselmPark`.

Expect: a single `louiselm: Session cold-Parked` notification, no error. No
confirmation picker (there's nothing staged to warn about).

Failure signature: `louiselm: Park record claims must be a non-empty array`
(old validation still active — binary not actually rebuilt) or any other
`louiselm: ...` error notification.

Evidence: `louiselm-capture run list` should show the new run, `cold_parked`,
with `"claims":[]`.

### 4. `:LouiselmPark` with staged context asks to confirm first

Exercises `71a6ae3` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` — the `has_staged`
branch of `Chat:park`, entirely new UI-interaction code with no automated
coverage (the existing test only exercises the no-staged-context path).

Steps:

> In a second, disposable session (same rule as case 3), stage something —
> easiest is typing a prompt into the input and *not* sending it (a queued
> prompt), or stage a file/context item the way you normally do. Then run
> `:LouiselmPark`.

Expect: a picker appears with prompt text naming what will be lost, e.g.
`louiselm: queued prompt will not survive cold Park; proceed? ` with options
`Park` / `Cancel`. Choosing **Cancel** leaves the session open and unparked —
your queued prompt/staged item is still there afterward. Re-run `:LouiselmPark`
and choose **Park** this time: it proceeds and cold-Parks (same notification
as case 3), and the staged item is gone (Park doesn't survive it — that's the
whole point of the warning).

Failure signature: no picker shown (staged context silently discarded or
silently blocks Park with no explanation), or `Cancel` still parks the
session, or the reasons text doesn't match what was actually staged (e.g. says
"pending skill selection" when you only queued a prompt).

### 5. `:LouiselmResumePark` restores claims and generated-work budget

Exercises `64523ac` end to end — this is the one case that needs a *real*
claimed issue threaded all the way through `br` → cold Park → durable storage
→ resume, which the mocked unit tests (fake `nvim.system`, fake picker)
cannot prove.

Needs: Setup done, a second disposable session, and one Beads issue actually
claimed to that session — e.g.
`br update <some-ready-issue-id> --claim --actor "<agent>/<acp_session_id>"`
(pick a low-stakes issue you don't mind claimed-then-released; unclaim it in
Cleanup below regardless of outcome).

Steps:

> With the issue claimed, run `:LouiselmPark` in that second session (expect
> `louiselm: Session cold-Parked`, same as case 3 but now with one live
> claim). Then close/detach that chat view (however you normally dismiss a
> session without disposing the plugin), and run `:LouiselmResumePark`. Pick
> the just-parked run from the picker.

Expect: `louiselm: cold Park resumed (recoverable, lossy)`. Tell me when
you're at this point and I'll pull `owner_run.claims` / `owner_run.generated_work`
off the live resumed session through the `$NVIM` socket to confirm the claim
id round-tripped and the budget numbers match what `run admit` set
(`ceiling=1`, since `PARK_GENERATED_WORK_MAX = 1` in `init.lua`).

Failure signature: resume notification never fires / fires with an error
instead, or (only checkable via the evidence pull) `owner_run.claims` is `{}`
or missing the claimed issue id, or `generated_work` is `nil`/zeroed instead
of the admitted ceiling.

## Evidence check

`louiselm-capture run list` after each Park (case 3, 4-Park-branch, 5) prints
the durable run JSON including `claims` — this is the one thing that proves
Park actually persisted rather than just showing an optimistic UI
notification. It does *not* prove the UI-side `owner_run` object matches;
for case 5 I'll pull that separately through the `$NVIM` socket once you
confirm the resume notification appeared.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- Unclaim the Beads issue used in case 5:
  `br update <issue-id> --status open --actor "<agent>/<acp_session_id>"` (or
  whatever its prior status/assignee was — check before you claimed it).
- Dispose the second chat session(s) opened for cases 3–5.
- Any leftover `cold_parked` run records from these cases self-expire
  (`PARK_TTL_MS` = 24h) — no manual deletion needed unless you want
  `run list` clean immediately: `rm ~/.local/state/louiselm/workflow/runs/<id>.json`.

## Reporting back

Send me the run id, which case, what you saw, and anything surprising. I pull
the evidence myself. If something is wrong I will fix it, and you will need to
redo Setup before retesting.

## Findings this round

**F1 — `:LouiselmResumePark` fails unconditionally for `claude` sessions** (`louiselm-aaw0.1`, open,
not fixed). `ACP session/load failed: Resource not found: <acp_session_id>` on every resume
attempt, including one in the same still-running Neovim process that created the Park — rules out
"lost on editor restart" as the cause; `session/load` itself doesn't work here. Reproduced twice
(runs `72a8fa90-b11a-4dc7-a918-57f3c8fc5a64` and `a998611f-bc18-414a-9a94-97c962b343b0`, both
`claude/6b80a87e-54dd-4f7b-ab9f-e2fb0ebc380d`). Root cause not yet isolated — see the bead for the
discriminating experiment needed. Blocks case 5 entirely. Full evidence and reproduction in the
bead description.

title: Usage telemetry is unreadable when flush against transcript content
description:
The chat transcript renders the `[usage] ...` line without a blank line above or below it, making usage telemetry hard to read when it is adjacent to prose or tool output. Add vertical spacing around the usage line, following the existing transcript block-spacing precedent used for tools and terminal completion.

## Observed

Seen in the maintainer screenshot on 2026-08-25 at 17:13 local time (Europe/Paris), Neovim chat buffer in `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`:

`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260825_1713_1920x1200_1787670818.png`

The visible transcript contains:

```text
Recorded all of this as a comment on **louiselm-exw0** and committed (`5dd00ba`). Ready to tackle the implementation when you are.
[usage] total_tokens=3468175 · input_tokens=...
> i just asked in codex for reason but it showed nothing ...
```

The usage row is directly adjacent to the preceding and following transcript content, with no empty line separating it.

## Symptoms

- Human-facing chat transcript usage telemetry is difficult to scan.
- Usage should be presented as its own block with one newline above and below.

## Root cause

Likely in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2250-2263`: the `turn_done` handler calls `insert_transcript(self, view, { line })` for the usage line, but does not surround it with empty lines. The neighboring terminal-completion path explicitly inserts blank lines, which suggests the usage path omitted equivalent block spacing. This mechanism is a hypothesis based on the current source and screenshot; verify with a focused UI regression test.

## Why it was not caught

Existing tests cover usage formatting and transcript ordering/data, but no headless UI assertion currently requires blank lines around the rendered usage line in the live chat transcript.

## Fix direction

At the transcript presentation boundary in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`, insert one empty line before and after the usage line while preserving existing behavior for turns without usage and avoiding duplicate blank lines where the preceding/following block already supplies spacing. Add a behavioral headless regression test for the rendered transcript.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.
- In the chat buffer, `[usage] ...` has exactly one blank line above and below it, including when adjacent to prose or tool output.
- Usage formatting and persistence remain unchanged.

## Not covered

The screenshot does not establish whether every usage-producing agent or replay path has the same spacing issue. Verify live and replay rendering when implementing the fix.
close_reason: Fixed in the current working tree. Root cause was usage presentation inserting only the usage line, unlike neighboring transcript blocks with explicit separators. Added neighbor-aware spacing for live and replay usage. Tests: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 117/117; full MiniTest suite 517/517. Gates: stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported no problems. Acceptance met: usage is separated from surrounding transcript content.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Fix evidence: added a focused assertion in tests/ui/chat_spec.lua requiring a blank line around live reported usage and the missing leading separator in replayed usage. Implemented neighbor-aware insert_usage() at lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1904, used by both restore_turn_usage() and turn_done. Focused chat_spec: 117/117 passed; full suite: 517/517 passed; lua-language-server: no problems; stylua --check: passed.

title: Show whose turn it is in LouieLM chat
description:
## Problem

During a LouieLM chat session, the top red header shows the session option, but it does not indicate whether the model is currently sending text or whether it is the user's turn to respond.

## Desired behavior

Add a visible status indicator in the chat header that distinguishes at least:

- Model is responding/sending text
- Your turn / waiting for user input

The indicator should update as the conversation state changes and remain consistent with the actual session state. Preserve the existing red session-option header.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A LouieLM chat session visibly shows whether the model is currently responding or it is the user's turn.
2. The status changes promptly when model output starts, finishes, or the session becomes ready for user input.
3. The indicator is understandable without relying on color alone (for example, include text or an icon with accessible labeling).
4. Existing session-option header behavior remains intact.
close_reason: Already implemented by commit 106aa9c: the window-local winbar persists Your turn and Model responding while scrolling, updates on lifecycle changes, and restores the previous winbar. Current chat coverage also exercises Waiting for permission, Starting, Stopping, Error, and Unavailable labels; the latest full MiniTest run passed 185/185.

title: Correlate issues to commits through bvr history with confidence intact
description:
## Goal

From an issue, see every commit that implemented it, with bvr's correlation
method and confidence carried through rather than flattened into a claim.

## Scope

- In scope: the bvr half of `provenance/sources.lua`; issue -> commit edges in
  `correlate`; `louiselm://provenance/issue/<id>`.
- Out of scope: Session edges from actor fields, and time travel.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `louiselm://provenance/issue/<id>` lists correlated commits with their
   created and closed milestones.
2. Correlation method (`explicit_id`, `co_committed`) and confidence reach the
   surface. An inferred edge is never presented as a recorded fact.
3. The default git range is set explicitly. A bare `bvr --robot-history` reports
   zero correlations on this repository because it only scans the last N
   commits, which reads as "unimplemented" and is a trap worth encoding once.
4. An issue with no correlated commits renders as such, not as an error.

## Testing

- `correlate` against captured real `bvr --robot-history` output, cited per
  AGENTS.md section 5.
- A regression proving the history window is passed explicitly, since the

- Fixtures encode observed event order as well as field shape.

## Notes

Prior art proving this works: `bvr --robot-history --bead-history louiselm-w726
--history-since 2026-08-10 --history-limit 500` returns real SHAs, authors and
milestones for that issue.

title: How should AGENTS.md compose the LouiseLM workflow across multiple repositories?
description:
Moved from acp-llm-adapter (daa-86y9) - the maintainer felt this design
discussion belongs in louiselm, since it's about the shared LouiseLM
workflow's contract with per-repository AGENTS.md files, not about
acp-llm-adapter specifically.

## Context

The repository needs a clearer AGENTS.md design that integrates the LouiseLM workflow without duplicating the workflow inside project instructions. The current AGENTS.md mixes Rust policy, test procedure, Beads operations, and LouiseLM process. A proposed rewrite made LouiseLM the top-level lifecycle and used bvr for triage plus br for persistence, but the structure still needs design validation.

## Design question

What should live in a repository AGENTS.md versus shared LouiseLM skills or shared documentation when the workflow spans multiple repositories?

## Requirements to preserve

- LouiseLM should own the lifecycle: understand, confirm, route, and execute.
- The project should use bvr for read-only Beads triage and br for Beads mutations.
- Behavioral changes should use a red-green-refactor loop: failing test, minimal fix, refactor, full validation.
- Repository instructions should remain short, high-signal, and resistant to drift.
- Shared workflow rules should not be copied into every repository.
- Repository-specific Rust, architecture, testing, and safety constraints must remain local.
- Remote Markdown must not become an implicit or higher-priority instruction source.

## Options to evaluate

1. Thin repository AGENTS.md that points to shared LouiseLM skills and contains only local constraints.
2. A shared parent AGENTS.md for the multi-repository workspace, with small child AGENTS.md adapters per repository.
3. A versioned shared workflow document or repository template, synchronized deliberately into each repository.
4. A hybrid: shared lifecycle and vocabulary rules, local execution and validation rules.

## Questions to resolve

- Which repository is authoritative when the same project is opened independently?
- How should shared instructions be versioned and updated across repositories?
- Should vocabulary live in one shared Beads project or be repository-local?
- Where should red-green-refactor be specified: shared LouiseLM skill, project AGENTS.md, or both?
- How should bvr triage operate when several repositories share one backlog?
- What is the minimum local AGENTS.md content that still gives an agent reliable context?

## Acceptance

- A documented multi-repository instruction structure is chosen.
- Ownership is explicit for shared workflow, repository-specific policy, vocabulary, and Beads state.
- The resulting AGENTS.md template avoids duplicated work-selection instructions.
- The red-green-refactor test process is placed at the correct shared/local boundary.
- The current acp-llm-adapter AGENTS.md rewrite is either accepted, revised, or reverted based on the decision.

## Original state (as of the move)

The acp-llm-adapter working tree contained an uncommitted AGENTS.md
rewrite from this design discussion at move time. No Rust source or test
files were changed there. That uncommitted rewrite was left as-is in
acp-llm-adapter; it was not copied here and not reverted.

title: Pair Android through one explicit private receiver profile
description:
## Goal
Make first-time Android pairing and upload work through one deliberately configured private LAN or overlay endpoint, while preserving receiver trust across routine TLS certificate changes.

## Scope
- In scope: one persisted network profile shared by serve, pair, status, and the systemd installation; loopback as the unconfigured state; explicit LAN, private-overlay, and advanced-private configuration; fail-closed pairing; stable receiver public-key identity in the pairing protocol; Android validation of that identity; direct breaking replacement of the current exact-certificate pairing format.
- Out of scope: public-internet exposure, port-forwarding, installing or managing overlay software, simultaneous listeners, cloud discovery/relay, and compatibility with the version-1 QR payload.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A fresh installation remains loopback-only and pair refuses with actionable configuration guidance rather than printing an unusable QR.
2. Configuring one selected LAN or detected private-overlay address makes serve, pair, and status agree on the bind and advertised HTTPS endpoint.
3. Obvious wildcard and public configurations are rejected when they can be classified reliably; unusual private setups require the explicit advanced path.
4. The pairing offer carries a stable receiver public-key identity and one-use enrollment token. Android stores that identity separately from the endpoint and device credential.
5. Android accepts a renewed TLS certificate that proves the same receiver key and rejects a different receiver key.
6. A paired phone uploads a capture through either supported profile with the existing UUID, authentication, size, digest, atomic-ingest, and immutable-original invariants intact.
7. The installer, systemd unit, example configuration, and both READMEs describe the same supported profiles and do not claim public exposure support.

## Testing
- Start with failing Rust CLI, identity, pairing, and receiver tests plus Android protocol/pinning tests.
- Use deterministic local fixtures only; no live LAN, overlay, credentials, or external services.
- Run the capture-service Rust suite and Android test/lint/assemble gates when their toolchains are available.

## Notes
Prefer the narrowest shared configuration source over separate bind and advertised URL settings that can drift. The receiver identity may reuse the persistent TLS key if continuity is pinned at the public-key level; do not add a second key unless the implementation proves it necessary.
close_reason: Implemented one private receiver profile and stable public-key pairing identity across Rust, Android, and Neovim; all automated quality gates pass.

comments.author: codex/01a02367-afa7-7e10-8123-6f6eb4dced28
comments.text: Implemented with red-green coverage. Initial Rust tests failed on missing NetworkProfile/NetworkProfileKind, PairingOffer receiver identity, and TlsIdentity public-key fingerprint; Android failed on the missing public-key identity matcher; the Neovim capture test then failed because :LouiselmCapturePair still required and forwarded receiver_url. Final behavior: one atomic XDG network profile drives serve/pair/status; loopback pairing refuses; private LAN/overlay/advanced profiles reject unsafe addresses; pairing protocol v2 pins the persistent TLS SubjectPublicKeyInfo; Android trusts renewed certificates with that key and rejects another key; Neovim uses the persisted profile; installer and docs match. Gates passed: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings, full cargo test; ./gradlew test lint assembleDebug; stylua --check ., lua-language-server zero diagnostics, all 321 MiniTest cases; sh -n installer and git diff --check. Physical LAN/overlay validation remains intentionally in louiselm-1chb.

title: QA round: live ACP user-message echoes
description:
# Manual QA review — live ACP user-message echoes

Working file for the current round. Run the cases and report the run id,
adapter, what appeared in the chat buffer, and anything surprising.

**Build under test:** `b9f2c82`. Re-run Setup after any fix.

Origin: Grok can echo a submitted prompt as `user_message_chunk`. LouiseLM
already renders live prompts locally, so the echo previously appeared twice.
The fix suppresses `user_chunk` events during an active prompt while retaining
them for `session/load` replay.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Grok live prompt renders once and remains healthy | **PASS** — `grok/01a05659-34a0-7b30-b130-975c93102c21`; prompt once, reload responses non-fatal |
| 2 | Codex live prompt remains correct | **PASS** — `codex/01a0565c-15d4-7f51-9d78-5167dfae0f29`; prompt once, normal `end_turn` |
| 3 | Claude live prompt remains correct | **PASS** — `claude/cd38faac-2d93-4e74-9d36-9b467a100eef`; prompt once, normal `end_turn` |
| 4 | OpenCode live prompt remains correct | **PASS** — `opencode/ses_fa9a1b6faffeWEgUPaplYE0kVN`; prompt once, normal `end_turn`, no permission request |
| 5 | Resumed history still renders | **PASS** — `grok/01a05659-34a0-7b30-b130-975c93102c21`; replayed prompt and reply once, in order |

## Setup

1. Restart Neovim from the dotfiles configuration so the running plugin is the
   committed build. Confirm the source checkout is at `b9f2c82` with:

   ```sh
   git -C /home/lotso/code/louiselm rev-parse --short HEAD
   ```

2. Confirm the Grok executable is available:

   ```sh
   grok --version
   ```

3. Start a fresh Session for every case. Select the named adapter explicitly
   in `:LouiselmChat`; do not reuse a Session after changing agents.

4. Before pressing Enter, record the LouiseLM Session id with
   `:LouiselmSessionId` if available. Keep the corresponding proxy log path
   for the evidence check below; do not use an unpinned “latest log.”

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- A previous prompt or resumed Session can hide whether the current prompt was
  duplicated. Use a fresh Session per adapter case.
- The prior available Grok proxy log covered only handshake/session setup, not
  the failing prompt. A passing visual result without a prompt-turn log proves
  only what was visible, not which ACP event sequence arrived.
- Do not use a debug/skip-approval mode for these cases. The Grok configuration
  routes through `acp-proxy` with `ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED=1`; keep that path so the
  live event can be checked.

## Cases

### 1. Grok live prompt renders once

Exercises `4058bc9` / `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:315-323`, `b9f2c82` /
`lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua:73-78`, and the Grok
`acp-proxy -- grok agent stdio` configuration.

Steps:

1. Start a fresh Grok Session.
2. Enter exactly:

   > Reply exactly `trge-grok-qa-20260831`; do not modify files.

3. Press Enter once. Wait for the turn to finish.
4. Observe the submitted prompt block before and after the reply.

Expect: the prompt appears exactly once, the reply appears normally, focus
returns to the prompt area, and the Session reaches ready/idle state.

Failure signature: two identical `> Reply exactly...` blocks appear after one
Enter, or the prompt is missing while the agent still replies.

## Evidence check

After recording the proxy log for this run, set `LOG` to that absolute path and
run:

```sh
jq -r 'select(.direction == "agent_to_client" and .payload.method == "session/update") | .payload.params.update.sessionUpdate' "$LOG" | sort | uniq -c
```

The pass evidence is a prompt turn containing `user_message_chunk` from Grok;
the UI must still show one prompt. This command proves the wire event type,
not the rendered buffer, so report both results. If no `user_message_chunk`
appears, the case did not exercise the reported Grok behavior.

### 2. Codex live prompt remains correct

Exercises the shared session boundary with the Codex adapter.

Steps:

1. Start a fresh Codex Session.
2. Enter exactly:

   > Reply exactly `trge-codex-qa-20260831`; do not modify files.

3. Press Enter once and wait for completion.

Expect: one submitted prompt, one normal reply, no new duplicate or missing
prompt.

Failure signature: any duplicate prompt, prompt loss, or a Session that does
not return to ready/idle after the reply.

Evidence: repeat the pinned proxy-log check from Case 1 for this Session. The
case passes visually even if Codex emits no `user_message_chunk`; that absence
is expected for the normal live path.

Result: PASS in `codex/01a0565c-15d4-7f51-9d78-5167dfae0f29`. The maintainer
observed one prompt. The pinned trace records one `session/prompt` at line 9
and its `end_turn` result at line 26, with no `user_message_chunk` or process
exit. The log proves the normal Codex wire path completed; the single rendered
prompt is the maintainer's visual evidence.

### 3. Claude live prompt remains correct

Exercises the same boundary with Claude.

Steps:

1. Start a fresh Claude Session.
2. Enter exactly:

   > Reply exactly `trge-claude-qa-20260831`; do not modify files.

3. Press Enter once and wait for completion.

Expect: one submitted prompt and one normal reply.

Failure signature: duplicate or missing prompt, or a changed reasoning/reply
layout attributable to this turn.

Evidence: repeat the pinned proxy-log check from Case 1 and record whether any
`user_message_chunk` was emitted during the live prompt.

Result: PASS in `claude/cd38faac-2d93-4e74-9d36-9b467a100eef`. The maintainer
observed one prompt. The pinned trace records one `session/prompt` at line 12
and its `end_turn` result at line 19, with no `user_message_chunk` or process
exit. The log proves the Claude wire path completed; the single rendered
prompt is the maintainer's visual evidence.

### 4. OpenCode live prompt remains correct

Exercises the same boundary with OpenCode, including its permission-capable
ACP path.

Steps:

1. Start a fresh OpenCode Session.
2. Enter exactly:

   > Reply exactly `trge-opencode-qa-20260831`; do not modify files.

3. Press Enter once and wait for completion. If a permission picker appears,
   handle it normally and continue observing the original prompt block.

Expect: one submitted prompt, normal permission/reply behavior, and no prompt
duplication.

Failure signature: duplicate or missing prompt, permission UI replacing the
prompt block, or failure to return to ready/idle.

Evidence: repeat the pinned proxy-log check from Case 1 and include any
permission/request ordering that coincided with the visual result.

Result: PASS in `opencode/ses_fa9a1b6faffeWEgUPaplYE0kVN`. The maintainer
observed one prompt. The pinned trace records one `session/prompt` at line 5
and its `end_turn` result at line 132, with no `user_message_chunk`, permission
request, or process exit. The log proves the OpenCode wire path completed; the
single rendered prompt is the maintainer's visual evidence.

### 5. Resumed history still renders

Exercises the preserved `session/load` replay path; automated coverage already
checks the event contract, but this confirms the real Agent payload and UI.

Steps:

1. Use a previously completed Session with visible user history, or create one
   with a first prompt and wait for completion.
2. Close/detach the chat without deleting the Agent-side Session.
3. Resume/load that exact Session in LouiseLM.

Expect: each historical user prompt appears once, followed by its historical
reply; no history is lost because the new guard only suppresses user messages
while a live prompt is active.

Failure signature: historical user prompts disappear, appear twice, or appear
in the wrong order after load.

Evidence: the load proxy log must show `session/load` followed by
`user_message_chunk`; compare those events with the resumed chat buffer.

Result: PASS in `grok/01a05659-34a0-7b30-b130-975c93102c21`. The maintainer
observed the historical prompt and reply once and in order. The pinned trace
records `session/load` at line 150, replay user resource/text updates at lines
152/153, and the replay agent answer at line 155; each replay update carries
`_meta.isReplay=true`, and the load request completes successfully.

## Cleanup when the round closes

Delete only temporary fixtures created for these cases. Keep the pinned proxy
logs until the round is recorded; do not alter tracked dotfiles or credentials.

## Findings this round

**F1 — Grok Session enters Error after successful prompt** (`louiselm-tw9d`,
fixed in `b9f2c82`; maintainer-confirmed).
The fatal trigger was Grok's unsolicited JSON-RPC response with id
`skills-reload`, not the later exit 137. LouiseLM treated the uncorrelated
response as a transport error, closed `acp-proxy`, and that cleanup killed the
Grok child, producing 137. The fix ignores responses that have no pending
LouiseLM request. Controlled live Session
`grok/01a05654-dfd6-7981-897b-280a5a34a494` received two `skills-reload`
responses, refreshed its commands, completed its prompt, and remained ready
for 30 seconds. Automated gates pass. The maintainer reran Case 1 in
`grok/01a05659-34a0-7b30-b130-975c93102c21`; the pinned proxy log records
successful prompt completion at lines 70/72 and two `skills-reload` responses
at lines 76/77, with no subsequent process exit. Case 1 passes and
`louiselm-tw9d` is closed.

## Round summary

All five manual cases passed. Grok's live echo is suppressed without losing
resumed history, and Codex, Claude, and OpenCode retained their normal live
prompt behavior.

The round found one related defect: `louiselm-tw9d`. Grok's private,
unsolicited `skills-reload` response was incorrectly fatal; `b9f2c82` now
ignores responses without a pending LouiseLM request, and the maintainer
confirmed the fixed Grok Session remained healthy. The bug was closed in the
Beads update committed as `90e50cc`.

The automated suite missed the complete live failure because its ACP double
did not reproduce Grok's combination of live `user_message_chunk` echoes and
an unsolicited private response after the prompt; buffer duplication and
focus/ready state also require live UI confirmation.

No temporary fixtures or deferred bugs remain. Proxy logs are retained as the
pinned evidence for this round.
close_reason: 5/5 manual cases passed. Finding louiselm-tw9d fixed in b9f2c82 and confirmed live; no deferred bugs or temporary fixtures.

title: Add root MIT LICENSE and reconcile licence metadata
description:
Add the root `LICENSE` file and make every licence declaration in the tree agree with it.

## Steps

1. Create root `LICENSE` with the standard MIT text, correct copyright holder and year.
2. Grep the tree for licence declarations and reconcile them. Known: `capture-service/Cargo.toml` already declares `license = "MIT"` — this was a scaffolding default that happens to be correct, so it is ratified, not changed. Check the Android/Gradle side and any packaging metadata for declarations that disagree or are missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- Root `LICENSE` exists, is MIT, names the right holder.
- Every licence field in the repo says MIT or is absent; none contradicts.
- No file claims Apache-2.0. Apache is specifically rejected because its §3 patent grant would give away the one instrument that reaches independent reimplementation.

## Do not

Do not add SPDX headers to every source file. Not wanted, high churn, no benefit at this stage.
