title: Grill-me needed: should the vocabulary schema support bounded-context-style surface-specific names?
description:
Do not resolve this in passing during unrelated work; it changes a project-wide contract (the
vocabulary schema and its consumption rule in AGENTS.md) and deserves its own grill.

## The question

Should the `vocabulary/reference` schema ever support a bounded-context-style surface-specific
name for a canonical term -- the same underlying concept legitimately called something different
in an agent-facing (AX) surface than in a human-facing (UX) surface -- and if so, what's the rule
for when that's a deliberate split versus naming drift creeping back in?

## Context that raised it

Filed while analysing "Domain-Driven Design matters more when AI writes your code"
(https://threedots.tech/post/ddd-and-ai-coding/) against LouiseLM's own vocabulary system
(`louiselm-kd2b`). The article's bounded-contexts section argues the same domain concept can
validly have different names in different subsystems (e.g. "profile" in support, "customer" in
CRM), and that forcing one name everywhere is itself a source of friction, not clarity.

Today's vocabulary already contains one near-miss: `louiselm-y3f3` (AX) and its UX counterpart are
a deliberate split of largely the same underlying state into two audience-facing names -- not
formalized as a bounded-context rule, just handled once, informally. The current convention for
every other term is one canonical name, enforced everywhere, with every synonym explicitly listed
as "avoid" (see e.g. `louiselm-tsxh` Provenance: "Avoid: history, archaeology, audit trail").

As AX surfaces grow relative to UX (more agent-facing affordances, more of AGENTS.md itself as an
AX surface per `louiselm-y3f3`'s own definition), the same underlying concept may need to read
differently depending on audience more often than it has so far. Today's one-name convention would
fight that if and when it happens.

## Threads worth pulling

- Is the AX/UX split actually the first instance of a recurring pattern, or a one-off that doesn't
  generalize? Check whether any other current vocabulary term is under similar pressure, or
  whether this is purely speculative.
- If a bounded-context-style exception is warranted, what distinguishes "this is a deliberate
  per-surface name for the same concept" from ordinary naming drift that the current "avoid" list
  exists to prevent? The article's own examples (support/CRM/e-commerce) come from genuinely
  separate subsystems with real integration costs; LouiseLM is one small codebase, so the
  justification DDD relies on (multi-team, multi-subsystem seams) may not transfer directly.
- Would this need a schema change to the `vocabulary/reference` record shape (e.g. a `surface`
  field or a linked-alias mechanism), or is it better handled as a documented exception process
  with no schema change at all?
- Is there a real cost to *not* deciding this now versus waiting until a second genuine case
  appears and generalizing from two data points instead of one?

title: QA round: streaming undo prompt-boundary recovery
description:
# Manual QA review — streaming undo prompt-boundary recovery

Scratch working file for the live acceptance of `louiselm-znux` / commit
`414a858`. It is intentionally untracked and will be deleted when this round
closes.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Undo rendered transcript while the Model is responding | **passed** — live Session `codex/01a04bd4-9fa2-70a3-9e3f-603a7f214238`; marker submitted cleanly and `:messages` had no new traceback |

## Setup

1. Restart Neovim so the running plugin loads commit `414a858`.
2. Confirm the checkout with `:!git rev-parse --short HEAD` (expect
   `414a858`, or a later commit containing it).
3. Open a fresh LouiseLM Codex Session. Do not use a skip-approval/debug mode.

## Case 1 — undo during streaming

Exercises `414a858` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1361` and the scheduled
event path.

Steps:

1. Submit a prompt that streams for a while, for example:
   `Write a detailed 2000-word explanation of Neovim extmarks, with 30 numbered lines and a code block. Keep going until complete.`
2. As soon as assistant text is visible and the winbar still says
   `Model responding`, press `<Esc>` to leave insert mode, then press `u`
   once. This should undo the most recent rendered transcript change. If the
   response finishes too quickly, retry with a longer prompt.
3. Wait for the next assistant chunk or tool row. Do not press Enter when the
   response completes unless the command line is clear.
4. After the turn finishes, enter insert mode at the prompt and submit the
   literal marker `undo-boundary-check`.

Expect: the next chunk/tool renders normally; no red traceback or repeated
`Press ENTER or type command to continue` appears; the marker is shown as its
own user prompt, without a tool row or assistant text appended to it.

Failure signature: `Invalid 'line': out of range` naming `nvim_buf_set_extmark`
and `mark_prompt`, repeated scheduled-callback tracebacks, a stuck response,
or the submitted marker containing transcript/tool text.

## Evidence check

Observed in live Session `codex/01a04bd4-9fa2-70a3-9e3f-603a7f214238` after
submitting `undo-boundary-check`: the marker is present as its own prompt at
buffer line 279, and `:messages` contains no new `Invalid 'line'`,
`nvim_buf_set_extmark`, or `vim.schedule callback` traceback.

Run `:messages` immediately after the turn. A pass has no new `Invalid 'line'`,
`nvim_buf_set_extmark`, or `vim.schedule callback` traceback. This proves what
Neovim retained in its message history, but cannot prove a transient message
that was cleared before the command.

## Cleanup and reporting

Close the smoke-test Session when done. Report the Session ID, whether Case 1
passed or failed, and the exact visible failure signature. If it fails, leave
the buffer and messages intact and capture a screenshot before restarting.
close_reason: Completed: live Session codex/01a04bd4-9fa2-70a3-9e3f-603a7f214238 passed the streaming-undo acceptance; marker remained standalone and :messages had no extmark or scheduled-callback traceback.

title: Resume hint omits the live session id
description:
When a LouiseLM session exits with code 1 while another session is live, the resume hint does not identify the session that should be resumed. This makes the message ambiguous when multiple sessions exist, even though `:LouiselmResume` is offered as the recovery command.

## Observed

Reported 2026-08-28 in the louiselm session:

> louiselm: previous exit ended 1 live Session; resume codex with :LouiselmResume

The message says there is 1 live Session but omits its session id. No session id was available in the observed message.

## Symptoms

- The user cannot tell which session `:LouiselmResume` will resume.
- The diagnostic identifies a count (1 live Session) but not the corresponding session identifier.
- The user must invoke the command or inspect state to determine the target.

## Root cause

Unknown from the report. Likely the exit/recovery notification formats the live-session count and command but does not include the selected live session's id. Confirm by tracing the code that emits this exact `previous exit ended` message and the `:LouiselmResume` target selection.

## Why it was not caught

The existing behavior appears to test that a recovery message and resume command are present, but not that the message identifies the session target when session identity matters.

## Fix direction

Include the session id in the recovery message, ideally in the same form accepted by `:LouiselmResume`, while preserving the command hint. Add a regression test around the observable notification text and selected resume target.

## Acceptance

- A failing-exit recovery message includes the relevant session id when offering `:LouiselmResume`.
- The displayed id unambiguously identifies the session the command will resume.
- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.

## Not covered

The report does not establish whether the issue occurs only with multiple live sessions, whether the command accepts an explicit id, or why the previous exit ended with status 1.
close_reason: Include ACP Session ID in recovery hint; regression covered

comments.author: codex/01a04635-f2b8-7e70-9485-7a931923ec99
comments.text: Root cause confirmed: the abandonment breadcrumb already persisted acp_session_id, but recovery_message() projected only the configured Agent name. Added a session label including the ACP ID when present, with the existing agent-name fallback when absent. Regression test failed before the fix and passes now. No separate lesson warranted beyond this issue-local evidence.

title: Render the skill index as compact resource context
description:
## Goal
Make a submitted skill index read as structured context rather than a large block of user-authored prompt text.

## Scope
- In scope: give the skill-index its own compact resource-style presentation in the chat transcript; expose its URI/type and keep the catalog body inspectable on demand under a dedicated fold.
- In scope: preserve clear ordering alongside other submitted contexts such as AGENTS.md.
- Out of scope: changing Agent Skills discovery, progressive disclosure, skills policy, ACP prompt content, or when the catalog is sent.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A first prompt in an inject-policy Session renders skill-index as compact structured resource context rather than immediately presenting the full catalog as ordinary prompt text.
2. The catalog body remains locally inspectable on demand and is folded independently from the user prompt and other context items.
3. Copying or reading the normal submitted-turn view makes the boundary between attached context and the user prompt unambiguous.
4. ACP transport is unchanged: Agents advertising embeddedContext still receive an embedded resource, and the existing fallback remains intact.
5. AGENTS.md and other resource_link contexts retain their current behavior.

## Testing
- Extend the headless chat UI specs for compact rendering, fold boundaries, mixed skill-index plus AGENTS.md context, and unchanged prompt payloads.
- Run the focused chat spec and the required project quality gates.

## Notes
The current renderer expands any ContextItem carrying text directly into transcript lines, while a URI-only ContextItem renders resource_link metadata. That makes the dynamically generated skill catalog look materially different from AGENTS.md even though Codex receives structured context in both cases.

title: Answering a diff review no longer returns to the previous buffer
description:
Regression introduced by the BufWipeout handler in 0ed18d0. Accepting or rejecting a review left the user in whatever buffer Neovim picked after the wipe instead of the chat.

clear() in lua/louiselm/ui/diff/init.lua read self.previous_buffer AFTER calling Buffer.close(buffer). nvim_buf_delete runs BufWipeout synchronously, and that handler clears every field including previous_buffer, so clear() then saw nil and skipped nvim_set_current_buf.

Found by manual QA (case 3, session ade1d689-6c62-4753-ad00-4c78c995b1ef): the edit was allowed and applied correctly, but the chat buffer never came back.

Fixed by reading every field before closing the buffer. Regression test: tests/ui/diff_spec.lua "returns to the buffer focused before the review".
close_reason: Fixed in 348c6fc. Regression test added; full suite 201 cases, stylua and lua-language-server clean.

title: blog/scripts/render-post.sh: batch-render nvim-transcript excerpts to namespaced HTML/CSS
description:
## Goal
A batch script that renders every literalinclude block tagged :class: nvim-transcript in a finished post through the author's real Neovim config into namespaced HTML fragments, so the blog theme and the Neovim theme cannot collide on the same page.

## Scope
- In scope: blog/scripts/render-post.sh <post-dir>. Parses blog.md for code blocks tagged nvim-transcript, extracts the referenced source file + :lines: range for each, opens the author's real Neovim config headlessly (not nvim --clean) once for the whole batch, renders each excerpt (via TOhtml / tohtml.tohtml()), extracts only the <pre> fragment and generated CSS from each, namespaces every generated selector under a wrapper class, deduplicates the CSS into one shared stylesheet file, writes fragment HTML files into the post directory.
- Out of scope: any MyST build-time plugin (rendering is a separate, explicit, pre-build step by design — not invoked from myst build/myst start); any interactive/visual-selection preview UX (explicitly rejected — plain Neovim navigation is how line ranges get picked).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Given a blog.md with one or more nvim-transcript-tagged blocks, running the script produces one HTML fragment per block and one shared namespaced CSS file.
2. Generated CSS selectors are scoped under a wrapper class (e.g. .Comment becomes .nvim-transcript .Comment) — verified selectors cannot affect anything outside that wrapper.
3. Running the script twice against unchanged input is idempotent: byte-identical output both times.
4. The author's actual Neovim config (Catppuccin colorscheme, Tree-sitter highlighting) is what produces the rendering — not a generic/default Neovim config.

## Testing
- Focused test on the CSS-namespacing step: given sample TOhtml output, assert every generated selector is correctly prefixed.
- Idempotency test: run twice against the same fixture post, diff the outputs, assert no difference.
- No UI/buffer testing needed — headless tooling only.

## Notes
- Flagged in the parent feature as the highest-risk piece of this decomposition — may reasonably exceed typical task size given TOhtml extraction, CSS parsing/rewriting, and batch orchestration are all part of one coherent capability.
- No dependency on the other tasks — testable against hand-crafted fixture conversation files and a fixture blog.md, independent of create-blog.sh or LouiselmToMarkdown.
- Parent feature: louiselm-r1k.
close_reason: render-post.sh/render-post.mjs implemented and covered by 20/20 passing tests in test-render-post.sh (fragment content matches real TOhtml capture, idempotency across fragments/blog.md/myst.yml, cleanup on block removal, and a real 'myst build --html --strict' regression test proving the fragment is wired into the deployed page). Note: original AC #1/#2 (shared namespaced CSS file) were superseded per louiselm-xrf's investigation -- MyST's HTML build has no raw-HTML passthrough, so delivery moved to per-excerpt standalone documents via {iframe}, which makes CSS-selector namespacing unnecessary since each iframe already isolates its own styling. That supersession is documented and closed under louiselm-xrf. AC #4 (real Neovim config, Catppuccin/Tree-sitter) verified by test part 1's independent TOhtml capture comparison.

title: Show the Provenance Decision index
description:
## Goal
Provide a small read-only index of browsable Decisions for maintainers, Agents, reviewers, and newcomers.

## Scope
- In scope: `louiselm://provenance/decisions`; list question-based Decision anchors with explicit status, recent activity, and links to evidence views.
- Out of scope: onboarding workflows, tutorials, graph visualization, historical reconstruction, and new persistence.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The index renders question-based Decision anchors from current Provenance data.
2. Each row clearly distinguishes open, accepted, superseded, or unresolved state when evidenced.
3. Selecting a Decision provides navigation to its issue, commits, Sessions, and evidence timeline.
4. Empty and partially resolved Decisions remain legible rather than disappearing.
5. The buffer is read-only and queued work after disposal cannot revive it.

## Testing
Headless behavioral smoke tests for rendering, navigation targets, empty/partial data, read-only behavior, and disposal/late-result handling.

## Notes
This is a general history browser, not an onboarding process.
close_reason: All five acceptance criteria are satisfied by existing code, verified line-by-line: AC1/AC2 by Correlate.decisions' decision_state (open/accepted/superseded/unresolved) feeding decisions_lines; AC3 by the <CR> handler routing to show_decision's full evidence timeline; AC4 by the explicit empty-state line and graph.diagnostics rendering; AC5 by modifiable=false plus the is_active() guard on every async callback. All covered by the 8-case 'Decision index' test group in tests/ui/provenance_spec.lua, 15/15 passing on a fresh run just now. Blocking dependency louiselm-hobm is closed. Built in 90f3ca1 feat(provenance): add Decision index, polished in d6851c6/7efbc44/6f85702. determination -- the coordination tool's own claim-age heuristic couldn't be trusted here, since
my earlier read-only comment on this issue bumped `updated_at` and made the claim look "fresh"
despite the underlying session having gone quiet ~2 days ago.

Per my prior comment on this issue: the work already appears complete (all 5 acceptance criteria
map to existing code in lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua, all covered by passing tests in the
"Decision index" group of tests/ui/provenance_spec.lua, blocking dependency louiselm-hobm
closed). Proceeding to re-verify and close.

title: br search silently excludes closed issues by default, so searching a mostly-closed backlog reads as absence of evidence
description:
`br search <QUERY>` excludes closed issues unless `-a/--all` is passed. On a backlog that is overwhelmingly closed, a default search returns an empty or near-empty result that is easily mistaken for "this has never happened", when in fact the entire relevant corpus was filtered out before matching.

This is the same failure class as beads_rust#416 ("br search does not search comment bodies", closed 2026-08-17), whose own acceptance argued: "At minimum, `br search --help` should state that comment bodies are excluded so a zero-result search is not mistaken for absence." #416 fixed the comment-indexing half. The closed-exclusion half produces an identical false negative and is still live.

## Observed

Session claude/8b826fbf-4771-4ab2-8231-e7aef6fe98ba, 2026-08-24, br 0.4.0, louiselm backlog (249 issues: 222 closed, 27 open/other).

Agent was asked whether a workflow failure had recurred historically. It ran `br search "retrospective"` and `br search "BypassPermissions"` without `-a`, got no relevant hits, and reported the absence as evidence of a first occurrence.

Direct reproduction on this backlog — `BypassPermissions` occurs exactly once, in a comment on the closed issue louiselm-w726, and nowhere in any title or description:

```
br search BypassPermissions          -> 0 hits
br search BypassPermissions -a       -> 1 hit (louiselm-w726, closed)
```

Same split for `uninterrupted` (0 / 1), `restraint` (0 / 1), `under-restraint` (0 / 1).

## Symptoms

- A zero-result `br search` on a mature backlog is indistinguishable from "term is genuinely absent", because nothing in the output states that a status filter was applied or how many issues it excluded.
- The effect scales with project maturity: the healthier the close rate, the larger the hidden corpus. Here it hides 222 of 249 issues (89%).
- It interacts badly with the retrospective convention in docs/example-workflow.md, which routes durable lessons into issue comments. Retrospectives are written at close time, so they live on closed issues almost by definition — precisely the set the default query cannot see.

## Root cause

`br search` treats "closed" as noise to be filtered rather than as history to be searched, and inherits that default from list-style commands where hiding closed work is correct. Search is not a work-surface command; it is a recall command, and recall over a work tracker is mostly recall over finished work.

`br search --help` documents the flag (`-a, --all: Include closed issues (default excludes closed)`) but the runtime output gives no indication the filter fired.

## Why it was not caught

#416 established that a silently-narrowed search corpus causes false "absence" conclusions, but scoped its fix to comment bodies. No test or doc line covers the status dimension of the same problem, and the failure is invisible by construction — the query returns success with zero rows.

Compounding, `br list --json` carries no `comments` field at all (fields: close_reason, closed_at, compaction_level, created_at, created_by, dependency_count, dependent_count, description, id, issue_type, labels, original_size, priority, source_repo, source_repo_path, status, title, updated_at). An agent scripting a comment scan over `br list --json` therefore gets zero matches by construction rather than by evidence. That is arguably a second, separate reporting gap.

## Fix direction

Not yet chosen; this is an upstream (beads_rust) change, not a louiselm code change. Candidates:

- Make `br search` include closed by default, on the grounds that search is recall, not a work surface; add `--open-only` for the narrowing case. Aligns with beads_rust#349, which removed silent default caps from `br list`/`br ready` for the same "make work surfaces complete" reason.
- Keep the default but emit a stderr note on zero or filtered results: "0 results; 222 closed issues excluded (use -a)". Cheapest option, kills the false negative without changing semantics.
- Include the excluded count in `--json` output as a sibling of `total`, so scripted callers can detect the narrowing.

## Acceptance

- A search whose corpus was narrowed by the status filter cannot be mistaken for a genuinely empty result — either the closed issues are searched, or the exclusion and its magnitude are stated in the output.
- Agent guidance in this repo (AGENTS.md) reflects whatever the resolution is, so cold-start recall over comments is reliable.

## Not covered

- Whether `br list --json` should carry comments is filed here as context only; if it is worth fixing it deserves its own issue.
- No claim that the `-a` default is wrong for `br list`/`br ready`, where hiding closed work is the point.
close_reason: Out of scope: upstream runtime defect tracked at Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust#445; local AGENTS.md workaround already present.

title: Switching to a Session with a drifted prompt boundary crashes with 'Invalid cursor line: out of range'
description:
Switching to an attached Session whose prompt boundary has drifted past the
buffer's real end crashes with `nvim_win_set_cursor`'s "Invalid cursor line:
out of range", making the Session unreachable through the primary switch path
(winbar click, `Chat:switch_session()` picker, or a direct `Chat:switch(id)`
call) until the buffer is otherwise touched.

## Observed

Reported live by the maintainer while switching Sessions with the picker in
Neovim on `/run/user/1000/nvim.2240119.0`. Traceback:

```
vim.schedule callback: .../lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2938: Invalid cursor line: out of range
stack traceback:
        [C]: in function 'nvim_win_set_cursor'
        .../lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2938: in function 'switch'
        .../lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3011: in function 'on_choice'
        .../lua/snacks.nvim/lua/snacks/picker/select.lua:59: in function <...>
```

Read-only live introspection of that same running instance (reached through
the `chat` upvalue of `louiselm.ui.chat.command.winbar_click`, per AGENTS.md
§ Live-instance introspection) reproduced the exact defect on the attached
Session `claude/141676c9-b6a4-4fc1-9af4-67534b15756d` (internal view key
`session-1`, agent `claude`, status `ready`, `replay_active=false` — a live,
non-resumed Session, not a replay):

```
prompt_line=1362
buffer_line_count=1362
extmark_pos={1362, 0}
target_cursor_line=1363   -- prompt_line + 1, what Chat:switch passes
line[1361]={ "> click worked" }   -- the real, current prompt row
line[1362] -> nvim_buf_get_lines returns {} -- nothing there; 1362 is one past EOF
```

The prompt tracking is not a stale-cache issue in the `view.prompt_line`
Lua field (which louiselm-fp3r already fixed by backing it with an extmark):
the extmark itself (`view.prompt_namespace`/`view.prompt_mark`) is sitting one
row past the buffer's real last line. `current_prompt_line(view)`, which
re-derives `view.prompt_line` from that same extmark, would return the same
wrong value. `Chat:switch` (line 2938) and the initial-render cursor
placement (lines 2715/2718) both convert it straight to a 1-indexed cursor
row (`view.prompt_line + 1`) with no bounds check against
`nvim_buf_line_count`.

The adapter log for that acp_session_id
(`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/141676c9-.../log.jsonl`)
shows the last turn ended with two tool calls, a 3-chunk `agent_message_chunk`
answer, then `usage_update` — i.e. the crash-inducing state was produced by
completely ordinary turn completion, not by undo/redo or any editor
manipulation (undo/redo is what louiselm-fp3r's fix addressed).

## Root cause (hypothesis, not yet confirmed by a test)

Almost certainly the same defect already diagnosed on louiselm-1yei ("Usage-line
spacing: accumulated blank lines pile up during resumed multi-turn replay"),
manifesting as a crash instead of cosmetic spacing:

- The first-response-chunk branch of the `chunk` handler
  (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` ~2195-2219) writes a trailing blank line
  into the buffer but captures `response_line_count = #lines` *before*
  appending it, so `view.response_tail`/`view.transcript_tail` end up one
  line short of the real last written row (the trailing blank is physically
  present but untracked).
- `insert_usage`/`insert_transcript` (~1974, ~1652) both derive their
  insertion point as `view.transcript_tail + 1`, which — because
  `transcript_tail` already undercounts by one — lands *on* that untracked
  blank instead of past it. `insert_transcript` then does a pure insert
  (`nvim_buf_set_lines(buf, insertion_line, insertion_line, false, ...)`),
  pushing the untracked blank further down instead of reusing/counting it,
  and finishes with `mark_prompt(view, view.prompt_line + #replacement)`.
- Doing that arithmetic on `view.prompt_line` (which was already correctly
  one-past-real-content) rather than re-deriving from the actual buffer state
  compounds the pre-existing one-line undercount instead of correcting it,
  so `prompt_line` ends up pointing past where the next real line will ever
  be written once no further content follows the usage line in that turn.

louiselm-1yei frames this as a replay-only cosmetic bug ("Live single-turn
sessions are unaffected"); this report is evidence that the same untracked
extra-blank bookkeeping is live-reachable in a single-turn, non-replayed
Session too, just with a more severe consequence (a hard crash on switch
instead of an extra blank line) once nothing else happens to touch the buffer
before a `switch` call reads the stale `prompt_line`. If fixed together, the
regression coverage for whichever one lands first should include the other's
observed symptom.

## Symptoms

- `Chat:switch(session_id)` (winbar click, `switch_session()` picker choice,
  or `Chat:to_markdown`/other direct-id callers) throws instead of returning
  `false, error_message`, escaping the function's own declared contract.
- Because the throw happens inside `vim.schedule`, it surfaces as a bare
  `E5108`-style traceback in `:messages`, not a louiselm-owned error — nothing
  tells the user which Session or what to do about it.
- The affected Session remains attached but the user cannot switch focus to
  it — it is unreachable through the primary UI path — even though its ACP
  process is healthy.

## Why it was not caught

`current_prompt_line`/extmark-backed tracking (louiselm-fp3r) covers drift
from buffer edits happening *outside* the tracked write path (manual undo,
external edits). It does not cover the tracked write path itself computing a
wrong target line, which is what this is. No test drives `Chat:switch`
against a view whose prompt boundary has been advanced by the untracked-blank
arithmetic in the `chunk`/`insert_usage`/`insert_transcript` path.

## Fix direction

Not yet chosen. Two independent angles, not mutually exclusive:

- Fix the shared root cause on louiselm-1yei (stop undercounting the trailing
  blank in `transcript_tail`, or make `insert_usage`/`insert_transcript`
  re-derive their insertion point from real buffer state instead of trusting
  `transcript_tail + 1`), and confirm it also removes this crash.
- Defense in depth regardless of the above: clamp any `view.prompt_line + 1`
  passed to `nvim_win_set_cursor` to `[1, nvim_buf_line_count(view.buffer)]`
  at the point of use, so a future bookkeeping bug degrades to a slightly
  wrong cursor position instead of an uncaught throw inside `vim.schedule`.

## Acceptance

- A regression test drives `Chat:switch` (or the underlying cursor placement)
  against a view state reproducing this exact numeric relationship
  (`prompt_line == buffer_line_count`) and fails before the fix.
- `Chat:switch` never throws; an out-of-range prompt boundary is either
  impossible by construction or handled as a returned `error_message` like
  every other failure mode in that function.
- Whatever lands here is cross-checked against louiselm-1yei's repro (2+
  replayed turns) to confirm both symptoms share one fix, or documented as to
  why they don't.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree via the shared root cause on louiselm-1yei: transcript_tail now always correctly counts a completed prose block's trailing blank, so it never drifts past the buffer's real last line, which is what was crashing Chat:switch's nvim_win_set_cursor. Also live-verified on the maintainer's actual running instance (the exact reported session) that the drifted extmark was one row past the real prompt content; nudged it back live to unblock the session immediately, independent of this code fix. One side effect: a mid-turn snapshot ending right after a tool call with no turn_done yet (tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'renders session events and forwards slash prompts') now shows no blank between the tool line and the live prompt, instead of a coincidental one from the old orphan-blank bug -- correct, since spacing there is only guaranteed once turn_done's insert_usage dynamically settles it; test updated. Full suite 544/544, stylua and lua-language-server clean.

title: QA round: uncovered Provenance, reasoning, Handoff, and Park gaps
description:
# Manual QA review — uncovered behavior after the recent QA rounds

Working file for the current round. It is scratch and intentionally untracked;
the final record belongs in the round bead when the round closes.

**Build under test:** `HEAD` (`0077e17`), including the changes after the
recorded rounds `louiselm-p0kz` (Provenance), `louiselm-43g8` (Beads cursor
detection), `louiselm-klm2` (Park/UI), and `louiselm-n8w8` (streaming undo).
Re-run Setup after any fix.

Origin: a history audit found that several behavior changes landed after, or
outside, those rounds. This pass targets only those unverified live boundaries:
historical Provenance/drift, resumed reasoning-fold repair, real Handoff
transport, and the Parked-Run safety/expiry cases explicitly left unrun in
`louiselm-y8vj`.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Historical Decision view separates snapshot from later drift | **blocked on F1** — snapshot/drift rendered, but commit drill-down failed with valid SHA |
| 2 | Resumed reasoning folds are rebuilt and remain interactive | **passed (initial)** — real Session `codex/01a04c83-defb-7e52-93ac-42f3c8824836`; historical folds opened and closed normally |
| 3 | Handoff sends reviewed context, including same-agent targets | **passed (initial)** — target Session `codex/01a050d3-c734-7f13-a275-5edcd97a2a58`; operator reported normal completion |
| 4 | Parked Run rejects unsafe mutation and expiry releases claims | **blocked on F2** — `:LouiselmPark` reports `louiselm-capture: invalid run: Run was not found` for live Session `codex/01a050d8-1fe2-7d22-a7c2-6146807a3c6a` |

## Setup

Start a fresh Neovim instance from `/home/lotso/code/louiselm` with the real
plugin and real ACP Agent, not the mock:

```sh
cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm
nvim -u ./manual_init.lua
```

Confirm the source revision from inside Neovim:

```vim
:lua print(vim.fn.getcwd(), vim.fn.system({"git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"}))
```

Use fresh Sessions for cases 2–4. Do not use a skip-approval/debug launch mode
for case 3 if the target Agent needs to receive a real first prompt. Record the
Agent/ACP Session id for every case. Do not Park the Session driving this QA
conversation.

For case 4, use the current `louiselm-capture` release binary and verify:

```sh
cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm/capture-service && cargo build --release
export PATH="$PWD/target/release:$PATH"
louiselm-capture run list
```

If Neovim resolves another binary, restart it or set its PATH before testing.
Use only disposable `qa-*` Runs and a disposable Beads issue claim.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- `louiselm-capture run list` lists resumable cold Parks, not active Runs.
- A shell-created Park is not valid evidence for ACP `session/load`; case 4
  must create the Park through `:LouiselmPark` and use the CLI only to inspect
  durable state.
- Resume/Provenance logs must be pinned to the exact Session id, never selected
  as “the newest” log.
- A picker or review that appears briefly is not evidence of success: report
  the final buffer name, focus, and notification as well.

## Cases

### 1. Historical Decision view separates history and drift

Exercises `4605900`, `5d8ad8b`, `lua/louiselm/provenance/vintage.lua`, and
`lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua`. Automated tests cover constructed data, not
the real Beads history lookup and rendered navigation.

Steps:

1. Run `:LouiselmProvenanceDecisions` — this opens the Decision index; it
   should not ask for an issue id. **Do not use `<leader>lP` here:** that keymap
   runs `:LouiselmInspectProvenance`, a separate cursor-sensitive inspector.
2. In the index, move to and open a row whose issue is a closed **Decision**
   with a closing commit and later issue activity. Do not enter a QA-round id.
   If the index is empty or asks for an id unexpectedly, obtain candidates with
   `br list --type decision --status closed --format toon` and use one of those
   Decision ids.
3. Inspect the rendered sections and select its historical evidence/commit
   links. Open a second Decision with no usable historical source if available.

The screenshot for this run shows the expected `Historical backlog` section
with a reference and counts at decision time, followed by later additions and
changes. The remaining check is navigation to the selected historical evidence
and, if available, the missing-source variant.

Expect: the selected Decision identifies its historical snapshot/anchor, then
shows later backlog changes as explicit drift rather than rewriting the old
Decision as current truth. Missing commit, Beads, or Session evidence is named
while the remaining evidence still renders. Selection opens the chosen item and
does not reuse the wrong existing popup.

Failure signature: current issue fields appear under the historical heading,
later activity is presented as if it existed at the closing commit, one missing
source blanks the whole view, or selection navigates to another Decision.

Evidence: save the `louiselm://` buffer name and capture its rendered lines. The
buffer text proves section identity and explicit unavailable-source markers;
focus and popup placement remain observational.

### 2. Resumed reasoning folds are rebuilt and remain interactive

Exercises `c1b293d` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`. The regression test uses
a fake replay; this case checks real replay timing and the actual Neovim folds.

Steps:

1. Resume a real Session containing at least two historical reasoning paragraphs
   separated by prose or a tool call.
2. Wait until replay finishes and the chat is ready.
3. Place the cursor on each historical `[thinking]` header and press `za` twice.
4. Send a short follow-up prompt and repeat on the new reasoning header, if the
   Agent emits reasoning.

Expect: every historical header has a real fold after replay, each fold opens
and closes without an error, and the follow-up turn renders normally.

Failure signature: a historical header has no fold while a new one folds, `za`
throws an extmark/line-range error, the cursor jumps to an unrelated line, or
the follow-up remains stuck after replay.

Evidence: report the Session id and run `:messages` immediately after toggling
and after the follow-up. No new `nvim_buf_set_extmark`, `Invalid 'line'`, or
scheduled-callback traceback is a necessary pass condition, but it cannot prove
a transient error that was cleared.

### 3. Handoff sends reviewed context, including a same-agent target

Exercises `60b58c1`, `858883f`, and the real `open_handoff`/`submit_handoff`
path. Unit tests cover payload shape; they do not prove picker behavior, focus,
or that an ACP peer consumes the resource context as its first prompt.

Steps:

1. Open two idle Sessions using the same Agent. Keep the source Session open.
2. From the source, invoke Handoff and select the same Agent as the target.
3. In the review buffer, confirm the `## Handoff`, `## Context`, and `## Source`
   sections. Fill in a concrete takeover task, for example:
   `Inspect /tmp/louiselm-qa-handoff.txt and report its first line.`
4. Submit and watch the target Session until its first turn completes.

Expect: the source remains intact; the target is created/selected without an
“agent already in use” or same-agent rejection; the review buffer is editable
before submit; the target receives the takeover task plus compact context, and
the target transcript records the Handoff marker. Focus returns to a usable
chat after submission.

Failure signature: same-agent selection is rejected, the source disappears or
is mutated, the target receives the raw review template, context is absent or
replayed as a new task, or the review/input window traps focus.

Evidence: record source and target Session ids, target buffer name, and the
first target prompt as rendered locally (redact sensitive content). The ACP log
proves the target received text/resource blocks; it cannot prove the operator
found the review readable.

### 4. Parked Run rejects unsafe mutation and expiry releases claims

Exercises the previously unrun Park cases from `louiselm-y8vj`, now against the
production `:LouiselmPark` path and the current `Run` restoration code.

Steps:

1. In a **new disposable chat Session**, run `:LouiselmSessionId` and copy the
   exact result, which looks like `codex/<acp-session-id>`. Call this
   `SESSION_ID`.
2. In a shell, choose a low-stakes issue from `br ready --format toon`, then
   claim it to that exact Session identity. For example:

   ```sh
   SESSION_ID="codex/<acp-session-id>"
   ISSUE_ID="<one-ready-issue-id>"
   br update "$ISSUE_ID" --claim --actor "$SESSION_ID"
   br show "$ISSUE_ID" --json
   ```

   The `br show` result must show the issue in progress and assigned to the
   same `SESSION_ID`. Record its original status/assignee so Cleanup can undo
   this temporary claim.
3. In that disposable Session, send one harmless prompt such as `Reply with
   exactly: ready` and wait for the turn to finish. A brand-new Session with
   zero prompts is intentionally rejected by the shipped cold-Park guard
   (`e2fd0c2`): `louiselm: cold Park requires a Session that has sent at least
   one prompt`.
4. Run `:LouiselmPark`, then `:LouiselmResumePark` and select that Run.
5. While it is parked/resuming, attempt an ordinary advancement or generated
   work request without the required operator resume/raise action. Dispose or
   cancel the resumed Run, then attempt one late action.
6. Create a second disposable Run through the same production Park path with a
   short TTL if the configuration allows it. Wait past expiry and inspect the
   resumable list and the test issue claim.

Expect: parked state refuses unsafe generation/advancement; the restored
`claims` and generated-work ceiling remain bounded; disposal/cancellation does
not revive the Run or affect another Session. After expiry the Run is absent
from resumable results and its test claim is released by the reaper.

Failure signature: a parked Run mutates without explicit operator action, the
budget widens or claims disappear on resume, a late callback revives disposed
state, an expired Run remains selectable, or an unrelated claim changes.

Evidence:

```sh
louiselm-capture run list
br show <test-issue-id> --json
```

The durable JSON and Beads state prove persistence/reaping; the exact error and
whether another chat stayed usable must be reported from the UI. If no reaper
is configured, mark this case blocked rather than treating it as a product
failure.

## Cleanup when the round closes

Dispose temporary Sessions, release the disposable issue to its original state,
remove only `qa-*` Run records/fixtures, and verify no temporary permission
rule or staged prompt remains.

## Reporting back

Send the case number, exact Session/Run/issue ids, what you saw, and the exact
failure signature if any. Leave the UI and messages intact when a case fails;
I will inspect the evidence before classifying it.

## Findings this round

**F1 — Historical Provenance commit inspection rejects valid Git output**
(`louiselm-wi0y`, open). The Decision view rendered the historical snapshot and
drift, but selecting SHA `097bcd6d2f5c6cb021a0ff31f78280d9c02a3d5e` through
`<leader>lP` produced `louiselm: git returned malformed commit data`. Direct
`git show` succeeds. Git appends a newline after the parser's record separator;
`parse_git_log` treats that trailing newline as an incomplete record. Case 1 is
blocked until fixed and retested.

**F2 — Production cold Park reports Run was not found** (`louiselm-psz9`, open).
After the disposable Session sent and completed a first prompt and had a Beads
claim, `:LouiselmPark` failed with `louiselm: louiselm-capture: invalid run: Run
was not found`. The stale-binary hypothesis was eliminated: Neovim and the
shell now use identical SHA-256 `def2e918f9d9d71deacb6ab3c9d8e8e16a02dac0c6a6c861559f31ccbb5c0566`,
and the store contains an `active` Run for the failing Session. No durable Park
was created, so mutation-safety and expiry remain untested. The remaining
problem is between Run admission/attachment and the Park lookup.

## How the round closed

Cases 2 and 3 passed against real Codex Sessions. Case 1 verified the
historical snapshot and drift rendering but was blocked at commit drill-down by
F1. Case 4 was blocked by F2 before mutation-safety or expiry could be tested.
The disposable Beads issue used for the Park attempt was `louiselm-n83s`; it
was restored to `open` and unassigned. Re-run Cases 1 and 4 after their fixes;
the round bead is the durable record of this review.
close_reason: QA round already recorded as closed in its own body (How the round closed); all 4 filed findings (oaib.1, oaib.2, psz9, wi0y) closed. Housekeeping close.

title: Repeat :LouiselmPark on an already cold-Parked Session is silent
description:
## Observed

Live QA of louiselm-psz9's fix, 2026-08-30, Session codex/01a050f8-93e9-7f00-847f-be08e6920e77.
First `:LouiselmPark` correctly produced `louiselm: Session cold-Parked` and created a durable Run.
A second and third `:LouiselmPark` on the same, already-Parked Session produced no notification at
all -- no success message, no error -- it "does nothing" from the operator's perspective.

## Root cause

`Chat:park()` (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3210-3213) treats a Session with `owner_run ~= nil` as
already owned and calls `cold_park()` again, which calls `run:park_cold(...)` -> `Run:park(callback)`
(lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua:324-330):

```
if self.status == "parked" then
  return true
end
```

This early return never invokes `callback`, so the `cold_park()` closure's notify (success or
failure) in lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3198-3204 never fires. The caller has no way to distinguish
"already Parked, nothing to do" from a hung or dropped command.

## Fix direction

Either have `Run:park`'s early `status == "parked"` return also invoke `callback(true)` so a caller
that supplied one gets a definitive answer, or have `Chat:park()`/`cold_park()` notify explicitly
(e.g. `louiselm: Session already cold-Parked`) when `run.status` is already `"parked"` before issuing
the redundant `park_cold` call. Keep the fix at whichever boundary is shared by every caller of
`Run:park`/`Run:park_cold`, not special-cased in the UI alone.

## Not covered

Whether repeated Park should be a true no-op, refresh the existing durable record (e.g. bump
claims/TTL), or be rejected outright was not decided here -- this issue is only about the missing
notification.
close_reason: Fixed at 238c848; live acceptance confirmed by maintainer 2026-08-30

title: Run was not found after cold Park validation rejects the first attempt
description:
## Observed

Live re-verification of louiselm-psz9's fix, 2026-08-30, Session
codex/01a050f8-93e9-7f00-847f-be08e6920e77. First `:LouiselmPark` call reported:

`louiselm: cold Park requires a Session that has sent at least one prompt`

A subsequent `:LouiselmPark` call (after the Session had a completed prompt) reported:

`louiselm: louiselm-capture: invalid run: Run was not found`

## Root cause

Same defect class as louiselm-psz9, a second manifestation. `Chat:park()`
(lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3191-3195, pre-fix) only ever remembered a Run's admitted id via
`run.park_record.id`, which is set solely by a *successful* `Run:park_cold` call
(lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua). When `park_cold`'s own validation in `cold_park_record` rejects
the request (e.g. `current_turn < 1`, "has not sent a prompt yet"), it returns before ever touching
`park_record` -- but `WorkflowService.admit`/`attach` already ran and `session.owner_run` was already
set via `adopt_session`. On the next `:LouiselmPark`, `session.owner_run ~= nil` skips admit/attach
(chat/init.lua:3210) and `run.park_record` is still nil, so `run_id` falls through to a fresh
`park_run_id()` -- an id the capture-service never admitted. Park then fails with "Run was not
found" against that fresh id, while the durably admitted Run from the first attempt sits orphaned.

louiselm-psz9's fix addressed one path to this same symptom (an async ordering bug that also left
`park_record` nil after a successful park). This is a second, independent path to the identical
symptom, and also latent (not yet observed live) in `Chat:resume_park()`
(lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4068-4071), which reconstructs a Run from a durable record via
`Workflow.new_run({claims=..., generated_work=...})` without threading through the durable record's
own `id` (`selected.id`, already available from the picker at line 4053) either.

## Fix

Track the admitted/resumed Run id as its own field (`Run.id`), independent of `park_record`, set
once at `Workflow.new_run({id = ...})` and never mutated afterward:
- lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua: added `id` to `RunOptions`/`Run`, validated and stored in `M.new`.
- lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3191-3195: `Chat:park()` now derives `run_id` from `run.id` instead
  of `run.park_record.id`, and passes `id = run_id` when constructing a new Run.
- lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4068-4071: `Chat:resume_park()` now passes `id = selected.id` so a
  resumed-then-re-Parked Run also reuses its original durable id.

## Acceptance

- A cold Park attempt that fails `cold_park_record` validation, followed by a retry after the
  Session becomes eligible, reuses the id from the original admit/attach rather than minting a new
  one.
- Regression coverage: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua "reuses the admitted Run id after a cold Park attempt
  fails validation" (red before the fix, green after).
- Full mini.test suite, stylua --check, lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning, and
  generate-api-appendix --check all pass.

Live acceptance still needed from the maintainer: after a rejected first Park attempt, a subsequent
successful Park on the same Session no longer reports "Run was not found".

Dependencies:
  -> louiselm-psz9 (related) - same defect class, first manifestation, already closed
close_reason: Fixed at 309bbe7; live acceptance confirmed by maintainer 2026-08-30

title: Separate the first assistant output from the user blockquote
description:
## Problem
The first assistant output after a submitted prompt is not visually separated from the user turn and can inherit the pink Markdown blockquote styling. This makes the first commentary and following tool-call line look like part of the user message.

## Reproduction
1. Open a LouiseLM chat buffer and submit a prompt.
2. Have the agent emit a text chunk as its first event, followed by a tool call.
3. Observe the boundary between the final line of the `> ` user prompt and the initial assistant commentary/tool timeline.

## Observed
- The initial assistant commentary begins immediately below the user prompt with no blank separator.
- The first tool-call line follows inside the same visually pink region.
- In `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260809_0534_1920x1200_1786246460.png`, lines 4 onward initially appear attached to the user turn and inherit its pink presentation.

## Expected
Every assistant turn begins as a visually distinct transcript block. Assistant commentary and tool-call lines must not inherit the user prompt blockquote styling, regardless of which event arrives first.

## Likely Root Cause
`Chat:submit()` creates a single empty response placeholder immediately after the `> ` prompt. The first `chunk` event replaces that placeholder with response text instead of preserving a blank turn separator. With the chat buffer using Markdown filetype, text directly following a blockquote can be parsed as a lazy continuation, so the initial assistant content and adjacent tool-call lines inherit the blockquote highlight. This is a rendering-boundary issue; do not special-case tool colors unless investigation disproves it.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A blank separator remains between each submitted user blockquote and the first assistant transcript content.
2. Initial assistant text and tool-call lines render outside the user blockquote/pink region.
3. The boundary is correct when the first event is a text chunk, tool call, error, or other transcript-producing event.
4. Streaming multiple chunks and updating a started tool call in place do not accumulate extra blank lines or disturb chronological order.
5. Existing prompt placement, cursor behavior, and subsequent-turn rendering remain unchanged.
6. Add a headless behavioral regression test that asserts the buffer lines for a submitted prompt followed by asynchronously scheduled chunk and tool events; exercise the real scheduling boundary rather than only invoking the renderer synchronously.

## Notes
Fix the shared transcript/turn boundary rather than applying presentation logic to one tool-call event. Buffer-line behavior is the primary assertion; no pixel test is required.
close_reason: Preserved assistant turn boundary before first streamed text or tool event

title: Collapse tool-call blocks in LouiselmToMarkdown transcript rendering
description:
## Goal
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` / `Chat:to_markdown` tool-call blocks take up huge vertical space (full `vim.inspect` dump always expanded) and visually compete with `## User`/`## Assistant` at the same heading weight. Make tool-call blocks compact and collapsed by default, without dropping any information.

## Scope
- In scope: `lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua` — `render_entry()` and its module doc comment (the "M.render turns a snapshot..." section describing tool block format).
- In scope: `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` — update the four assertions that do `markdown:find("## Tool: ...", 1, true)` to match the new multi-line shape.
- Out of scope: `Chat:to_markdown` (init.lua:1549) and `transcript_export.lua` — both just call `Transcript.render`, no changes needed, no API change.
- Out of scope: fixing any blog-pipeline (`blog/scripts/render-post.sh`, MyST `:lines:` literalinclude ranges) friction this causes — explicitly deferred, see Notes.

## Agreed format (discussed with user)
Replace the current single line:
```
## Tool: <title> (<status>)

```
<vim.inspect dump>
```
```
with:
```
## Tool

<sub>**<title>** — <status></sub>

<details>
<summary>payload</summary>

```
<vim.inspect dump, unchanged>
```

</details>
```
- `## Tool` stays its own heading, same weight as `## User`/`## Assistant`.
- Title/status move to a `<sub>` line — smaller, one line, no expansion needed to see what ran.
- The full raw payload dump is unchanged in content, just wrapped in `<details><summary>payload</summary>...</details>` so it renders collapsed by default in GitHub/VS Code/Obsidian (falls back to expanded, not lost, in renderers without HTML passthrough).
- Fallback cases (`raw.title` absent → id, `raw.status` absent → "unknown") keep working the same way, just placed in the `<sub>` line instead of the heading.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `render_entry()` for a `tool_call` entry produces the new `## Tool` / `<sub>` / `<details>` shape described above, with the full `vim.inspect(raw)` dump byte-for-byte unchanged inside the `<details>` block.
2. `## User` and `## Assistant` blocks are unchanged.
3. `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` assertions updated to match (still checking title/status and full raw dump presence, just via the new shape — e.g. assert the `<sub>` line and `<details>`/`<summary>` markers appear, and the dump content is still present).
4. `busted`/test suite passes (`make test` or repo's standard Lua test runner).
5. Module doc comment in `transcript.lua` (lines ~19-24) updated to describe the new tool-block format instead of the old one-line heading.

## Testing
- Run existing Lua test suite for `tests/session/transcript_spec.lua` (and `tests/session/transcript_export_spec.lua`, `tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` as regression checks — they should not need format-specific changes since they likely just check the file was written, but verify).

## Notes
- Risk, explicitly accepted by user: `transcript.lua's doc comment says this markdown format is a dependency of the blog-publishing pipeline (`blog/scripts/render-post.sh`, feature `louiselm-mia`), which uses MyST `{literalinclude}` with `:lines: N-M` ranges against these exported files. Adding multi-line `<sub>`/`<details>` markup shifts line numbers for any existing blog post literalinclude ranges pointed at old-format transcripts. User: "happy with both, it's alpha software so I'll fix it after if that creates friction with louiselm-mia." Do not attempt to fix the blog pipeline as part of this task — file a separate bug if/when it actually breaks something.
close_reason: Implemented: render_entry() in lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua now emits ## Tool heading + <sub> title/status line + collapsed <details><summary>payload</summary> block, exactly per the agreed spec. Updated tests/session/transcript_spec.lua and tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua assertions. All 3 quality gates pass: stylua --check clean, lua-language-server --check clean, full mini.test suite 235/235 (0 fails). Blog-pipeline (louiselm-mia) line-number friction risk left as accepted/deferred per prior discussion.

title: Add tweet-fetch agent skill (twitterapi.io ingestion into tweets.jsonl)
description:
## Summary

Added the `tweet-fetch` skill in the owned skill catalog
(`~/.config/agentskills/tweet-fetch/`), the fetch-side companion to
tweet-corpus (louiselm-vg72).

## What it does

Wraps two verified twitterapi.io REST endpoints directly (no dependency on
the unverified third-party `kaitoInfra/twitterapi-io` package the original
opencode session had floated):

- `GET /twitter/user/last_tweets` (timeline, ~3200-tweet cap, X's own limit)
- `GET /twitter/tweet/advanced_search` (date-windowed `from:user
  since_time:/until_time:` search, for going further back)

`scripts/fetch_tweets.py` normalizes results into the exact schema
tweet-corpus/scripts/build_corpus.py ingests and appends to a shared
`tweets.jsonl`. Duplicate lines across overlapping fetch windows are
harmless — corpus build upserts by tweet id.

Cost guard: defaults `--max-tweets` to 200 since twitterapi.io bills per
tweet returned; SKILL.md instructs the agent to quote an estimate and get
explicit confirmation before a larger pull.

## Verification

- Offline smoke test of `normalize()` (Twitter date format -> ISO,
  entities.urls -> links list, retweet/reply detection), `build_search_query()`
  (since/until -> since_time:/until_time: unix timestamps), and CLI arg
  validation (missing env var, missing user, mutually exclusive
  --timeline/--search) — all correct. No live API call made (no
  TWITTERAPI_IO_KEY available in this environment; the endpoint shapes were
  confirmed against docs.twitterapi.io, not guessed).
- Catalog entry seeded (with a golden task: confirm-before-large-fetch),
  `inventory_skills.py`, `manage_lifecycle.py check`, `build_installation.py`,
  `generate_openai_metadata.py --check`, the unittest suite, and
  `run_golden_tasks.py` all pass. `generated/tweet-fetch` present.

## Related

louiselm-vg72 (tweet-corpus, the storage/query side this feeds).

title: Show select option labels in chat UI
description:
In `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`, select config options were rendered with their wire values (`current_value`, e.g. `small`) in three UI surfaces:
- session summary text
- ACP options header line
- session option picker labels

Fix by resolving select option values through `option.options[*]` and displaying the matching `name` when present, with a safe fallback to `tostring(current_value)`.

Regression coverage: update `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` to assert picker text uses the human-readable label.

title: QA round: Provenance, resumed folds, and recovery
description:
# Manual QA review — recent UI and Provenance changes

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; it becomes the round bead when the review closes.

**Build under test:** `ca9b72b..ded81aa` (last five commits). **Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: recent Provenance UI work, recovery-warning fixes, and the live report
that resumed reasoning paragraphs are recorded but not installed as Neovim
folds.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Resumed reasoning paragraphs fold and toggle | **passed** — maintainer confirmed folds in Session `codex/01a0461a-382d-7fb0-b46e-0a552b0bb40b` |
| 2 | Decision index renders and navigates | **passed** — screenshot shows selected Decision `louiselm-c274` in a populated Provenance popup after fix `d6851c6`; latency recorded as F2 |
| 3 | Decision evidence timeline separates history and drift | **blocked** — historical snapshot/drift is the separate open task `louiselm-97qw`, blocked by `louiselm-8tzl` |
| 4 | Missing Provenance sources remain explicit | **passed** — Decision `louiselm-parallel-worker-tracker-substrate-6mtc` retained implementation/Session evidence and explicitly rendered unresolved QA acceptance and Forensics |
| 5 | Recovery warning reflects actual recoverability | **passed** — first restart identified one abandoned Session and offered `:LouiselmResume`; next restart emitted no warning |

## Setup

Start a fresh Neovim instance from the repository root with the plugin loaded.
The running instance must be restarted after any Lua change. Confirm the source
tree is the build under test with:

```vim
:lua print(vim.inspect(require("louiselm.ui.provenance")))
```

For Case 1, resume a Session that has multiple historical reasoning paragraphs
separated by prose or tool output. The known live reproduction was
`codex/01a04635-f2b8-7e70-9485-7a931923ec99`; use a fresh equivalent if it is
not available. Do not use a synchronous test fixture for this case.

For Provenance cases, use the repository's existing closed Decision issues and
open them through the normal LouiseLM commands. Record the Session id or issue
id used so evidence can be pinned to it.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- `:LouiselmInspectProvenance` is the cursor/object inspector and prompts for
  Beads/Session identifiers when the cursor is not on a supported object. The
  Decision index is `:LouiselmProvenanceDecisions` or `<leader>lP` in chat.
- The shipped Decision view (`ca9b72b`) shows current correlations and explicit
  unresolved evidence. Historical backlog state and later drift are not part of
  that slice; they belong to `louiselm-97qw` and its `louiselm-8tzl` dependency.

## Cases

### 1. Resumed reasoning paragraphs fold and toggle

Exercises `ded81aa` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` and the resumed Session
rendering path.

Steps:

1. Resume the prepared Session.
2. Wait until replay completes and the chat view is interactive.
3. Find at least two historical `[thinking]` headers and one reasoning block
   produced after resume.
4. Place the cursor on each header and press `za` twice.

Expect: every historical and post-resume reasoning block has a real manual fold;
each closes and opens with `za`, and the view remains interactive after replay.

Failure signature: a historical header has `foldlevel=0`, `foldclosed=-1`, or
`za` does nothing while a post-resume block folds normally.

### 2. Decision index renders and navigates

Exercises `90f3ca1` / `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua`.

Steps:

1. Run the normal command for the Provenance Decision index.
2. Confirm the buffer opens and wait for source collection to finish.
3. Select a Decision row and follow its issue Provenance link.

Expect: the index is readable, shows Decision state and recent activity, and
navigation lands on the selected issue rather than a different row or the
source chat.

Failure signature: empty output despite known Decisions, rows reorder while
selecting, navigation opens the wrong issue, or a source error closes the view.

### 3. Decision evidence timeline separates history and drift

Exercises `ca9b72b` / `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua`.

From the Decision index, open a Decision with a closing commit.

Expect: the view identifies the Decision anchor and historical reference, then
shows later changes as separate evidence. It does not present current state as
if it were historical state.

Failure signature: historical and current issue state are conflated, or later
changes appear without an explicit drift/reconsideration relationship.

### 4. Missing Provenance sources remain explicit

Exercises `ca9b72b` / `lua/louiselm/provenance/sources.lua`.

Open a Decision or issue whose commit, Beads snapshot, or Session evidence is
unavailable.

Expect: the available sections still render and the missing source is named as
unavailable; one missing source does not erase the rest of the answer.

Failure signature: a blank buffer, generic success with omitted evidence, or a
single missing source preventing unrelated evidence from appearing.

### 5. Recovery warning reflects actual recoverability

Exercises `5b2312f` / `lua/louiselm/ui/abandonment.lua`.

Trigger the normal startup recovery path once with a known abandoned Session,
then repeat startup after the breadcrumb has been consumed.

Expect: the first startup reports the truthful recovery state once; the second
startup does not repeat a stale warning or claim a recoverable Session when it
cannot be resumed.

Failure signature: stale warning repeats, recovery claims success without a
Session, or the warning disappears before the operator can act.

## Evidence check

For Case 1, report the Session id and inspect the live buffer through the
maintainer's Neovim instance; the verdict is that historical and new headers
have equivalent fold behavior. This proves UI behavior, not just recorded fold
ranges.

For Cases 2–5, report the exact `louiselm://` buffer name and capture the
rendered buffer text or the relevant session/log artifact. Pin logs by Session
id, never by newest-file order.

## Cleanup when the round closes

Close temporary Sessions if desired, remove any temporary fixtures, and delete
this scratch file only after its contents have been transferred to the round
bead.

## Reporting back

Send me the case number, what you saw, the Session or buffer id, and any exact
failure signature. I will inspect objective evidence, update this file, and
file any product finding before changing code.

## Findings this round

**F1 — Selecting a Provenance Decision fails with duplicate buffer name**
(`louiselm-g2ya`, fixed in `d6851c6`).

The Decision index loads, but selecting a row reports `Vim:E95: Buffer with this
name already exists` at `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:290`. The likely shared
boundary is `open_provenance`, which always assigned a requested URI to a new
buffer without handling an existing named buffer. The fix reuses an existing
named buffer and window, with regression coverage. Focused Provenance tests
(14/14), full suite (703/703), and manual QA passed. The perceived slowness is
tracked separately as F2.

**F2 — Selecting a Provenance Decision takes about 11 seconds**
(`louiselm-dkga`, fixed in `7efbc44`).

The selected Decision eventually renders, but the user measured approximately
11 seconds from `<CR>` to the second window. The screenshot
`/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260828_0551_1920x1200_1787889089.png` proves the
eventual populated result. The fix shows a loading view immediately; the BVR
latency investigation is tracked separately as `louiselm-cvlc`.

**F3 — Loaded Provenance content keeps the loading popup height**
(`louiselm-7tvl`, not fixed).

Screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260828_0600_1920x1200_1787889613.png`
shows the completed Decision content in a 3–4-line popup. The loading-state
height is not recalculated after the buffer refresh.

title: Large resumed Sessions remain Starting while replay renders
description:
A large resumed Session visibly remains Starting for about 20 seconds before its chat view reaches ready, even though the Agent completes session/load almost immediately.

## Observed

Manual retest on 2026-08-24 with deepseek/session-5b4fb715-7267-4f09-848b-54e84fca2dfc and build ee9e541. The current replay connection is /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/connections/57902114-99cf-42b6-ae4c-d88b46a85b04.jsonl. session/load request id=2 is line 3 at 11:54:40.491Z and its response is line 172 at 11:54:40.506Z: 15ms. Between them the Agent emits 12 user chunks, 11 assistant chunks, and 145 completed tool updates. The user observed the winbar on Starting for roughly 20 seconds.

## Symptoms

- Resume appears stuck on Starting for a large Session.
- The ACP wire has already completed load, so the visible delay is client-side replay presentation.

## Root cause

Unknown. The chat schedules each replay event separately and performs incremental buffer, header, fold, and Treesitter work. A main-loop replay backlog is the leading hypothesis; measure it before choosing a fix.

## Why it was not caught

Resume tests replay only a handful of tiny events and assert ordering, not bounded readiness/render latency for a large history.

## Fix direction

Benchmark a captured structural replay fixture without payload contents, identify the dominant UI work, and batch or defer that work at the narrowest presentation boundary.

## Acceptance

- A deterministic regression models a large replay and fails before the fix.
- Ready state becomes visible promptly after the load response.
- The full replay remains ordered and complete without blocking normal editing for tens of seconds.

## Not covered

The missing restored usage annotation is tracked by reopened louiselm-hxvc and has a separate event-state root cause.
close_reason: Manual retest on 348d6d0 is instant. The stale-snapshot fix prevents historical state events from repeatedly entering ready-only presentation; latest 14-turn/145-tool replay completes ACP load in 11ms and becomes visibly ready without the prior delay.

comments.author: codex/01a03349-c229-74e2-8d06-81fb2d016869
comments.text: User confirmed the Starting delay is solved and resume is instant. Latest structural connection 54497bd0-2fd8-43dd-8f82-87ef7314f3e8.jsonl lines 3-176 replays 14 user chunks, 13 assistant chunks, and 145 completed tools in 11ms under 348d6d0.

title: Document the LouiseLM diagnostics action contract
description:
## Goal
Document the confirmed diagnostics action and its Agent-facing payload contract.

## Scope
- In scope: document `:LouiselmDiagnostics`, current-buffer errors/warnings scope, next-prompt queueing, freshness metadata, truncation behavior, and no-active-Session error.
- In scope: state that diagnostics are untrusted data and that v1 uses standard ACP content without a custom capability/request.
- In scope: keep command/help/schema-generated surfaces consistent with the implementation.
- Out of scope: implementing diagnostics collection or transport, adding automatic behavior, and documenting unsupported workspace or Snacks integrations.

## Acceptance Criteria

2. Documentation states that the action queues but does not send a prompt.
3. Documentation states the exact default scope, fields, freshness semantics, caps/truncation signal, and no-Session behavior.
4. Documentation warns that diagnostic messages are untrusted data, not instructions.
5. Generated/help checks and documentation tests remain green.

## Testing
- Add or update documentation/help consistency coverage where the project supports it.
- Run focused documentation checks and the full project gates.
