title: Grill-me needed: how should grill-me support challenger passes and non-interrupting side capture
description:
**Grill-me needed. Do not resolve this in passing — it wants full attention.**

Raised as an explicit meta-idea during the 2026-08-21 grill of `louiselm-parallel-worker-tracker-substrate-6mtc`. The user did not ask to redesign grill-me now; they asked to preserve the improvement opportunity while the foreground grill continued without losing its thread.

## The question

Should the grill-me workflow gain two cooperating capabilities:

1. a distinct challenger skill or role, possibly run by another model, that stress-tests the primary grill's framing, assumptions, and conclusions; and
2. an isolated side-capture worker that can inspect beads, deduplicate or file an interjected idea, and return control without making the foreground facilitator stop grilling?

The product requirement behind both is continuity of human attention: useful meta-ideas should survive, but recording or challenging them should not silently replace the conversation the user was having.

## Evidence from the session that raised it

A Claude grill hit its model limit immediately after the user's answer. A different model could read the transcript and resume at a clean boundary, which exposed a broader possibility: model diversity may be useful not only for handoff but as an intentional challenge pass.

While discussing that possibility, the user interjected this improvement idea but explicitly said they did not want to take on a new grill. They proposed that a background subagent could search beads and preserve the side idea while the foreground agent resumed the live question “as if nothing happened.” This issue is the durable result of that experiment.

## Threads worth pulling

- When should a challenge pass run: during a grill, at explicit checkpoints, only after convergence, or on request? It must add scrutiny without repeatedly reopening settled decisions.
- What context should the challenger inherit? Full transcript continuity preserves nuance; an intentionally fresh model may expose anchoring. The workflow may need both a settled-decision ledger and a bounded challenge brief.
- Is this best expressed as a skill, a declarative workflow stage, a model/role policy, or some combination? Do not assume “another skill” is automatically the right implementation boundary.
- Define the side-capture worker's narrow contract: search via `br`, choose comment versus issue, preserve provenance and nuance, avoid changing the live issue's claim/status, sync the mutation, and report back asynchronously.
- Preserve foreground UX: one-question cadence and conversation ownership stay with the grilling agent; a recorder must not become the facilitator or force the user to context-switch.
- Evaluate the improvement empirically. Compare ordinary grills, handoff grills, and challenger-assisted grills for missed assumptions, needless re-litigation, time to convergence, and quality of the resulting beads.
- Coordinate with `louiselm-parallel-worker-tracker-substrate-6mtc` before implementing a writable background worker: that live question owns tracker-state isolation and reconciliation, not this one.

## Why this is separate from its parent

`louiselm-qbr.3` broadly owns persisted workflows and grill history. This is a narrower unresolved product/design fork about adversarial review and side-channel capture. It is substantial enough for its own grill, while remaining deferred with the parent rather than interrupting current work.

## Out of scope for this grill

Reconstructing the 2026-08-21 conversation, taking over its live tracker-ownership question, or treating the user's interjection as authorization to implement workflow machinery now. React to the recorded requirement and design the improvement when this issue is deliberately opened.

title: Validate workflow definitions and admit Runs against safety contracts
description:
## Problem Statement

A workflow that can invoke Agents can grow work without bound, and the growth is invisible until
Agents have already started. The motivating failure is not a cycle: a qa-review stage whose Agent
invokes `louiselm-to-beads-bug` files a new issue, which becomes ready work, which re-enters
execute, which re-enters qa-review. `br dep cycles` reports no cycles the whole way down, correctly,
because every iteration mints a new issue id. Acyclicity is not termination.

## Solution

Two contracts over workflow definitions and Runs, settled by the louiselm-qbr.8 grill-me session.

**Validation** is a pure, total function over one workflow definition, using frontmatter only. It is
binary: accept or reject. There is no warn tier and no run-it-anyway override. The escape valve for
a disagreement is editing the SKILL.md, which is versioned, reviewable and attributable.

**Admission** checks live Run state at every stage entry and every spawn. It cannot reject
retroactively; it stops or escalates. Recursion, fan-out and budget are only knowable here, because
the skill graph is open and an Agent is a nondeterministic edge-generator.

The bounding unit is the Generator: a back edge, a work-filing stage, or an Agent invoking a
work-producing skill. Automatic Generators declare a literal integer bound. Human-resolved
Generators need no number, because the human is the bound.

## User Stories

1. As a workflow author, I want a malformed workflow rejected at discovery time, so that I find out
   before any Agent starts rather than at 3am on the sixth iteration.
2. As a workflow author, I want the bound to appear only on edges no human ever sees, so that review
   cycles do not acquire fake numbers nobody believes.
3. As an operator, I want a workflow's generated-work budget enforced against my Run before the
   `br create`, so runaway work never reaches the backlog.
4. As an operator, I want to intervene in any stage without destroying the work in flight.
5. As an operator, I want cancellation to actually reach every worker the Run owns.

## Acceptance Criteria

Validation rejects, with a message naming the offending transition:

1. A transition targeting an ancestor stage without `back-edge: true`.
2. An automatic Generator with no literal iteration bound.
3. A bounded loop whose exhaustion outcome transitions back inside the loop it exits.
4. A named stage outcome with no mapped transition.
5. A transition whose target skill does not resolve against the discovered skill manifest.
6. A stage from which no terminal stage is reachable.
7. A stage unreachable from the entry stage.
8. A stage declaring a detached or fire-and-forget worker the Run does not own.

Validation is pure:

9. Given any workflow document, when Validation runs, then no Agent is started, no `br` command is
   run, no git or network access occurs, and no document content enters a context window.
10. Given ambiguity in a document, Validation rejects rather than inferring — no model in the loop.
11. Given an unchanged document and manifest, Validation returns a cached result keyed on
    `hash(document) + hash(manifest)`. Adding an unrelated skill invalidates the cache.

Escape and cancellation:

12. Every stage has a synthesized, non-destructive human escape transition the author does not write
    and cannot remove; taking it Parks the Run.
13. The escape is takeable unilaterally by the operator, with no Agent outcome required and no Agent
    cooperation needed — verified against a deliberately wedged mock agent.
14. A global emergency stop exists, is destructive (Disposal), and is not the ordinary intervention.
15. Cancellation walks the Run's supervision tree; the wait for acknowledgment is bounded and a
    silent worker escalates to Disposal.

Budget:

16. Generated work is attributed to the Run through the `--actor "<session id>"` provenance already
    required by AGENTS.md, and the budget is per-Run, so a human filing bugs by hand is unaffected.
17. Exceeding the budget Parks the Run rather than killing it or silently degrading it.

## Implementation Notes

- Frontmatter parsing reuses the existing lyaml path (`lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua`); this is
  the reason `louiselm-4gif` refused a hand-rolled parser, so parser correctness is now load-bearing
  beyond skills.
- Topology comes from structured frontmatter only, never prose — the settled `louiselm-uqip` ruling.
- Which skills a stage's Agent may invoke is a capability question and belongs to
  `louiselm-qbr.5.1`'s envelope, not to a second authority mechanism here. This feature depends on
  that boundary but must not reimplement it.
- Accepted coupling: "who resolves this transition" becomes a safety-relevant field. Changing a
  resolver from human to agent can turn a valid workflow invalid, so the attention model and the
  validator cannot be edited independently.
- Stated limit to write into the contract: cancellation reaches every worker LouiseLM can address,
  not every process. An ACP Agent ignoring both cancel and dispose is the outer harness's problem.

## Testing Notes

- Validation is a pure function and should be tested as one: a table of malformed documents against
  expected rejection identifiers, no fixtures beyond the document and a manifest.
- The wedged-agent escape test needs `lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua` extended to ignore
  cancellation.
- The generative-growth case deserves an explicit regression test asserting that budget, not cycle
  detection, is what stops it — the failure mode is a design that passes a DAG check forever.

## Out of Scope

- Durable Run state and Park expiry reaping — see the capture-service feature.
- Assessment (model reading prose) — separate feature, advisory, never gates.
- Capability envelopes themselves — `louiselm-qbr.5.1`.
- The full workflow execution engine — `louiselm-qbr.3` owns schema and runtime mechanics.

title: Rename louiselm.workflow to louiselm.routing to free the workflow namespace
description:
## Goal

Free the `louiselm.workflow` namespace for workflow definitions by renaming the existing
Agent-routing coordinator to `louiselm.routing`.

## Scope

- In scope: rename `lua/louiselm/workflow/` to `lua/louiselm/routing/` (approval, evidence, init,
  phase, routing, usage), rename `tests/workflow/` to `tests/routing/`, update every
  `louiselm.workflow.*` reference including LuaCATS `---@class` / `---@field` annotations, and
  update the require sites in `lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua`,
  `lua/louiselm/skills/metadata.lua`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua`,
  `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`, `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua`.
- Out of scope: any behaviour change, any new module, any file split. `routing.lua` staying inside
  `louiselm.routing` (giving `louiselm.routing.routing`) is acceptable for this task; renaming it is
  a separate judgement call, not part of a mechanical move.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No reference to `louiselm.workflow` remains anywhere outside `.git` — 223 references across 17
   files at the time of filing.
2. The full test suite passes with no behavioural diff; this is a pure rename.
3. `lua/louiselm/workflow/` does not exist, leaving the namespace free for `louiselm-qbr.3.2`'s
   validator.
4. Generated docs regenerate cleanly if `louiselm.schema.gen_luacats` / `gen_vimdoc` cover these
   types.

## Testing

- The existing `tests/workflow/*_spec.lua` suite, moved to `tests/routing/`, is the regression
  check. It must pass unchanged apart from the renamed requires.
- No new tests. If a test needs changing beyond its require line and type names, the rename has
  stopped being mechanical — stop and say so rather than adjusting the test.

## Notes

- Why: `louiselm.workflow` currently means *Agent routing* — `Coordinator:recommend(phase, state)`
  ranks Agents and Models, with approval and observed-reliability evidence. It has no stages, no
  transitions, no topology. The promoted vocabulary from the `louiselm-qbr.8` grill-me (Run,
  Generator, Validation, Assessment, Park) is entirely about workflows-as-stage-machines, which is
  also how `louiselm-qbr` uses the word throughout. The existing module is the misnamed one.
- Caught before either meaning has many callers. The cost is monotonically increasing, which is the
  whole argument for doing it now.
- Maintainer decision, 2026-08-26: "rename first, way more appropriate naming."

Pure rename, no behavioural change: full MiniTest suite 45 spec files, Fails (0) Notes (0), identical to the pre-rename baseline; tests/routing/*_spec.lua all collected and green. stylua --check clean; lua-language-server --check --checklevel=Warning reports no problems. The *louiselm-workflow* vimdoc help tag was deliberately left alone: it documents the user's workflow (configure Agent, start Session, submit prompt), not the module.

title: Define the workflow frontmatter schema and pure Validation rejection table
description:
## Goal

A pure function that accepts or rejects one workflow definition from its frontmatter, where the set
of rejections *is* the schema's specification.

## Scope

- In scope: the minimal workflow frontmatter schema (only the fields the eight rejections require,
  nothing speculative), a pure `validate(document, manifest)` in the freed `louiselm.workflow`
  namespace, and the rejection table with a stable identifier and message per case.
- Out of scope: purity enforcement and caching (own task), escape synthesis, cancellation,
  budgets, and any execution. No runtime, no Run, no Agent.

## Acceptance Criteria

Validation rejects, naming the offending stage or transition:

1. A transition targeting an ancestor stage without `back-edge: true`.
2. An automatic Generator (resolver is trigger, resolver, or agent) with no literal integer bound.
3. A bounded loop whose exhaustion outcome transitions back inside the loop it exits.
4. A named stage outcome with no mapped transition.
5. A transition whose target does not resolve against the discovered skill manifest.
6. A stage from which no terminal stage is reachable.
7. A stage unreachable from the entry stage.
8. A stage declaring a detached or fire-and-forget worker.

And:

9. A human-resolved back edge with no bound is ACCEPTED. This is the case a universal-bound rule
   would get wrong, and it must have an explicit passing test.
10. The result is binary. There is no warning severity, no `severity` field, and no option,
    flag, environment variable, or config key that permits a rejected definition to run.
11. Topology is read from structured frontmatter fields only. No prose is parsed, and no field is
    inferred from the document body.
12. The rejection identifier is stable and machine-readable, so callers can assert on the reason
    rather than on message text.

## Testing

- This is a pure function: test it as a table of `(document, manifest) -> expected identifier`,
  with no fixtures beyond those two inputs. No Neovim state, no filesystem, no mock agent.
- One accepting document per shape that is legal but looks suspicious: a human-resolved back edge
  with no bound, and a bounded automatic loop whose exhaustion exits correctly.
- A regression test asserting that a *generative* workflow (a stage that files tracker issues,
  minting a new id each pass) is not rejected by any cycle or reachability rule. It is legal
  topology; only a Run budget stops it. This test exists to prevent a future contributor from
  "fixing" unbounded growth with a graph check that cannot see it.

## Notes

- Blocked on the namespace rename; land that first.
- Parse frontmatter through the existing `lyaml` path used by `lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua`,
  as a data read. Do not route through skill activation: nothing here may enter a context window.
  `louiselm-4gif` kept lyaml deliberately, so parser correctness is now load-bearing beyond skills.
- `lua/louiselm/schema/` already provides a field/validator DSL (`louiselm.schema.Field`,
  `array-of`, `one-of`). Prefer expressing the frontmatter schema in it over a second hand-rolled
  shape checker.
- Design the schema from the rejections outward. Each rejection forces exactly one field into
  existence and no more; `louiselm-qbr.3` owns the eventual full schema and should inherit this
  minimum rather than a guess at it.
- The Generator is the bounding unit, not the back edge: a work-filing stage and an Agent invoking
  a work-producing skill are Generators too. Rejection 2 must be written against the Generator
  concept so the other two cases fall under it rather than needing new rules later.
close_reason: Completed: lua/louiselm/workflow/{init,schema,validate}.lua with tests/workflow/validate_spec.lua, 22 cases, all green. All eight rejections implemented with stable identifiers: undeclared_back_edge, unbounded_generator, exhaustion_inside_loop, unmapped_outcome, unresolved_target, no_reachable_terminal, unreachable_stage, unknown_field; plus duplicate_outcome, unnamed_outcome, missing_exhaustion_outcome, wrong_field_type, missing_entry, ambiguous_entry. Criterion 9 covered by an explicit ACCEPTING test for a human-resolved back edge with no bound. Criterion 10 covered by a test asserting no severity field and no override argument -- lua-language-server proves both statically, and the two diagnostics are suppressed with the justification that the warning is the assertion. Criterion 11 covered by a test that an unrecognized prose-carrying field rejects. Criterion 12 covered by asserting reason and message are distinct strings. The generative-growth regression asserts a work-filing workflow that grows without forming a cycle is ACCEPTED, so no future contributor can 'fix' unbounded growth with a graph check that cannot see it. Gates: MiniTest 46 spec files Fails (0) Notes (0); stylua --check clean; lua-language-server --check --checklevel=Warning no problems.

comments.author: claude/0929f4e1-c8f2-4717-998f-1902618ce5f8
comments.text:
Two design refinements made while implementing, both worth carrying into louiselm-qbr.3's full schema.

1. Rejection 8 (detached worker) is satisfied by OMISSION, not by a check. The schema gives no way to declare a detached or fire-and-forget worker, so the attempt surfaces as unknown_field. This is the same move as the synthesized escape in qbr.3.2.4: an obligation met by construction cannot be forgotten by a later contributor, and it costs a field nobody can write rather than a rule someone can delete. Consequence: the schema is closed -- any unrecognized key rejects.

2. Validation is rooted at a WORKFLOW NAME, not handed a single document. louiselm-uqip settled that a workflow is a set of discovered SKILL.md files with named outcomes mapping to next-skill transitions, so the graph is the transitive closure over the manifest, not one file's contents. Each stage block declares 'workflow: <name>' for membership and one declares 'entry: true'. Signature is validate(workflow, manifest) where manifest maps skill name to its parsed workflow block. This is what makes rejection 7 (unreachable stage) meaningful: without membership, everything reachable is reachable by construction and the rule could never fire. It also catches the real authoring error -- a typo in a 'to' silently orphaning a stage.

Implementation note worth keeping: back edges are classified by ANCESTRY from the entry via DFS, not by mutual reachability. The first attempt used 'target can reach source', which is symmetric -- in any cycle it marks the forward edge as a back edge too, and rejected the reference workflow. Caught by the accepting test for the reference loop, which is the argument for having written it.

title: Enforce and test Validation purity, and cache on document plus manifest
description:
## Goal

Make Validation's purity an enforced, tested property rather than a convention, and cache its result
on a correct key.

## Scope

- In scope: purity enforcement and its tests, the cache keyed on `hash(document) + hash(skill
  manifest)`, and manifest-change invalidation.
- Out of scope: the rejection rules themselves, anything runtime-scoped.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given any workflow document, when Validation runs, then no Agent process is started, no `br`
   command is run, no git or network access occurs, and no filesystem access happens beyond skill
   discovery.
2. No document content — frontmatter or prose — enters any context window.
3. Given an ambiguous or unparseable document, Validation rejects. It never resolves ambiguity by
   asking a model; there is no inference path.
4. Given an unchanged document and manifest, a second Validation returns the cached result without
   re-parsing.
5. Given an unrelated skill added to the manifest, the cache is invalidated. This is correct, not a
   bug: transition-target resolution depends on which skills exist.
6. A changed document invalidates only its own entry.

## Testing

- Purity is asserted by the test harness observing that the forbidden calls did not happen, not by
  reading the implementation. Stub or intercept the process, `br`, and network paths and assert
  zero invocations.
- Cache-key behaviour is deterministic: same inputs, one parse; manifest delta, two.
- An explicit test that adding an unrelated skill invalidates a cached result, so the coupling is
  documented as intentional rather than discovered later as a stale-cache bug.

## Notes

- The manifest dependency is the non-obvious part and belongs in the contract, not in a comment.
- Ambiguity-rejects is the same rule as no-override at a different level: an inference escape hatch
  would recreate "run it anyway" one layer down.
close_reason: Implemented document and manifest keyed Validation cache

title: Synthesize an unremovable human escape into every stage
description:
## Goal

Every stage carries a human escape the author never writes and cannot remove, and taking it Parks
the Run without destroying work.

## Scope

- In scope: runtime synthesis of a non-destructive human escape transition into every stage,
  Validation checking the synthesized graph, the destructive global emergency stop, and optional
  author-declared domain escapes.
- Out of scope: the Park record's durability and expiry (`louiselm-qbr.3.3`), budget accounting.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every stage has a synthesized human escape transition; the author writes nothing and cannot
   suppress it.
2. Validation runs against the synthesized graph, so the reachable-human-override obligation is
   satisfied by construction and cannot fail.
3. The escape is takeable unilaterally by the operator: no Agent outcome is required and no Agent
   cooperation is needed. Verified against a mock agent that ignores everything.
4. Taking the escape Parks the Run — turns Cancelled, Sessions retained — and does not Dispose.
5. A global emergency stop exists, is destructive (Disposal of the whole Run), and is separate from
   the escape.
6. An author-declared escape with domain semantics is accepted and is optional; its absence is
   never a rejection.

## Testing

- The wedged-agent test is the important one. `lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua` needs a variant that
  ignores cancellation, so that "reachable in the graph but unreachable in fact" is actually
  exercised.
- Assert the escape is enforced at the runtime's transition boundary, not delivered to the Agent as
  a request it may decline.

## Notes

- Graph reachability of a human gate is NOT the property wanted: a gate two hops away behind an
  Agent-only edge is reachable on paper and unreachable behind a hung Agent. Synthesis is what makes
  the correct property trivially true, which is most of why it was chosen over an authoring rule.
- A global stop alone does not satisfy the invariant, because it is destructive. The property is
  "a human can intervene without losing the work", not "a human can end this".
close_reason: Implemented synthesized human Park escape and emergency stop

comments.text: Implemented and verified: Workflow.validate now validates a copied graph with a reserved human __louiselm_park terminal outcome synthesized on every stage; Run:park requests cooperative cancellation without waiting or disposing, and Run:emergency_stop remains destructive. Tests cover graph immutability, synthesized validation, wedged-agent Park retention, emergency stop, cooperative cancellation, bounded escalation, and ownership. Full suite: 604 cases, 0 failures; stylua, lua-language-server, and git diff --check pass. Lesson: keep the human escape as a runtime-synthesized reserved outcome and keep Park separate from bounded Cancellation, because Park must remain available when an Agent ignores cancellation. No further destination warranted.

title: Enforce Run ownership and bounded-ack Cancellation escalating to Disposal
description:
## Goal

Cancellation reaches every worker a Run owns, because no worker can exist outside the Run's
supervision tree.

## Scope

- In scope: the ownership invariant and its Validation rejection, the supervision tree, broadcast
  Cancellation with bounded acknowledgment, and escalation to Disposal for a silent worker.
- Out of scope: durable Run state, Park expiry, budgets.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A Run owns a supervision tree of Sessions; no Session created during a Run exists outside it.
2. A workflow declaring a detached or fire-and-forget worker is rejected by Validation.
3. A skill invoked by a stage's Agent inherits Run ownership by construction, because the
   invocation happened inside a Run-owned Session. This needs an explicit test, since it is the
   case that motivated the whole contract.
4. Cancellation walks the tree and reaches every owned worker.
5. The wait for acknowledgment is bounded by a declared value; it is not open-ended.
6. A worker that has not acknowledged within the bound is escalated to Disposal.
7. Cooperative cancellation is attempted first as the fast path but is never the guarantee.
8. The contract states its limit explicitly in code documentation: propagation reaches every worker
   LouiseLM can address, not every process. An ACP Agent ignoring both cancel and dispose is the
   outer harness's problem.

## Testing

- A wedged mock agent that acknowledges nothing must end Disposed within the bound, not hang.
- An ordinary agent must Cancel cooperatively without ever reaching the Disposal escalation.
- The invoked-skill inheritance test should mirror the motivating scenario: a stage Agent invoking
  a work-producing skill, then the Run cancelled, then the invoked work stopped.

## Notes

- An unbounded wait-for-ack is exactly the "cancellation path that does not reach every active
  worker" the design set out to prevent: it reaches them and then hangs, which is indistinguishable
  from not reaching them.
- Cooperative cancel is unreliable precisely in the case being cancelled — the wedged Agent — which
  is why it is the fast path and not the mechanism.
close_reason: All acceptance criteria satisfied. Most of the ownership/bounded-cancellation contract was already implemented and tested by prior work in this tree; audit details and what was actually added (the invoked-skill-inherits-ownership test) are in the preceding comment. Full suite (742 cases) and stylua clean.

comments.author: claude/ea8b846d-3700-44ed-aa39-ffb9e68c8973
comments.text:
## Audit

Before implementing anything, checked each acceptance criterion against the current codebase.
Almost the entire contract was already implemented and tested by prior work on this tree
(`qbr.3.2.1`-`.4`):

1. "No Session created during a Run exists outside it" -- satisfied by construction:
   `Run:create_session` is the only Run-aware session-creation path and always calls
   `adopt_session`, which is the only way into `self.workers`. Tested:
   `tests/workflow/run_spec.lua` "creates stage Sessions through the Run owner".
2. "A detached/fire-and-forget worker declaration is rejected" -- already done via the schema's
   closed-world unknown-field rejection (`lua/louiselm/workflow/schema.lua`'s own comment:
   "There is no way to declare a detached or fire-and-forget worker, so a document that tries
   produces an unknown field"). Tested by name in `tests/workflow/validate_spec.lua`: "a stage
   declaring a detached worker" and "a stage declaring a fire-and-forget worker".
4-7. Bounded-ack Cancellation with Disposal escalation -- already fully implemented in
   `Run:cancel` (`lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua`) and tested in the `T["cancellation"]` group:
   cooperative cancel without disposal, disposal after the bound for a non-acknowledging worker,
   and Cancellation reaching every owned worker.
8. The contract's limit is already stated in `Run:cancel`'s docstring almost verbatim to this
   criterion's wording ("covers every worker LouiseLM can address, not every process...").

The only gap was criterion 3 and its matching Testing bullet: an explicit test for "a skill
invoked by a stage's Agent inherits Run ownership by construction... since it is the case that
motivated the whole contract." `Executor` (`lua/louiselm/workflow/executor.lua`) is a pure stage
state machine with zero Session/ACP coupling today (no live wiring from a stage's Agent to a
skill invocation exists yet -- that's `qbr.3`'s still-deferred workflow execution engine, out of
this issue's scope), so there is no real end-to-end path to test this against yet. Added the
most faithful test buildable at the current architectural layer: a stage Session already owned
by a Run, whose Agent invokes a skill that reaches the Run through the same
`Run:create_session` every other stage worker uses (mid-flight, after the Run already has one
worker) -- proving it is owned the moment it exists and that cancelling the Run reaches it too,
with no special-casing for how or when it was created. This test passed against the existing
implementation with no code change required; it fills a documentation/coverage gap, not a bug.

Full suite (742 cases) and `stylua --check .` clean.

title: Bound generated work per Run and Park on exhaustion
description:
## Goal

A Run that generates more work than its budget allows Parks for an operator decision, before the
work reaches the backlog.

## Scope

- In scope: per-Run accounting of generated work, attribution through the `--actor "<session id>"`
  provenance, admission checks at stage entry and spawn, and Park on exhaustion.
- Out of scope: the durable Park record and the expiry reaper (`louiselm-qbr.3.3`), capability
  envelopes (`louiselm-qbr.5.1`), Assessment.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Work generated during a Run is attributed to that Run through the `--actor` session id already
   required by `AGENTS.md:30`.
2. The budget is checked BEFORE the mutation, not reconciled after: an over-budget `br create` never
   happens.
3. The budget is per-Run. A human filing issues by hand, or a second concurrent Run, is unaffected.
4. Exceeding the budget Parks the Run. It does not Dispose it, and it does not silently remove the
   generating capability.
5. Resuming a Parked Run with a raised budget is an operator act. A request originating from an
   Agent is refused.
6. A resumed Run may not exceed the original envelope on any axis other than the raised budget.
7. Admission surfaces the budget and its consumption to the operator at the Park.

## Testing

- The motivating scenario end to end: a qa-review stage whose Agent invokes a work-producing skill
  repeatedly, Parking at the bound with the expected number of issues created and no more.
- A regression test asserting that the beads graph in that scenario contains NO cycle — `br dep
  cycles` is clean throughout — proving the budget, not cycle detection, is what stopped it.
- Attribution is verifiable through `br` actor fields; assert on the actor string, not on counts
  alone.
- A concurrent-Run test showing budgets do not pool.

## Notes

- Blocked on `louiselm-qbr.3.3`: a budget that Parks needs somewhere durable to Park into, and an
  expiry that fires while Neovim is closed.
- Degrading instead of Parking was rejected: an Agent that cannot file issues writes them into its
  transcript, which is unbounded growth somewhere with no schema, no provenance and no actor.
  Removing the mechanism does not remove the pressure.
- `br policy.yaml` capacities were investigated and rejected as the bound: workspace-global, no Run
  concept, and they fire after the work exists.

title: Grill-me needed: where is the pre-mutation Run budget gate?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; run a focused louiselm-grill-me session before implementation continues.

Question: Where must LouiseLM enforce a per-Run generated-work budget so an over-budget Agent-originated Beads mutation is refused before br create runs?

Context/evidence:
- qbr.3.2.6 requires a pre-mutation guarantee, per-Run isolation, Session actor attribution, durable Park on exhaustion, and operator-only budget increases.
- Workflow Validation already identifies Generators and their declared literal maxima, but runtime Run state currently has no generated-work ledger.
- Run owns Sessions, so a Session can be mapped to one Run.
- ACP session/request_permission exposes some command operations, but an Agent or adapter is not guaranteed to request permission for every subprocess; this cannot be the sole security boundary.
- The louiselm-to-beads skills currently invoke br create directly.
- Workspace-global Beads capacities were already rejected because they have no Run identity and apply after work exists.

Threads worth pulling:
1. Mediated API: require work-producing skills to call a LouiseLM/capture-service endpoint that atomically reserves budget then invokes br. How is bypass prevented?
2. Agent execution boundary: launch Run-owned Agents with a constrained br wrapper/PATH and Run token. Can absolute paths or alternate clients bypass it, and is that acceptable for correctness rather than adversarial security?
3. Beads boundary: add a pre-create policy/authorization hook keyed by actor and Run. Does this improperly make Beads understand workflow Runs?
4. Atomicity and restart ownership: which process owns reserve/create/commit so concurrent Sessions in one Run cannot overspend and failed creates do not consume budget incorrectly?
5. Admission and resume: what exact envelope is shown, persisted, and allowed to change when an operator raises only the generated-work budget?
6. Scope of generated work: only br create, or every Generator named by Validation, including back edges and Agent-invoked work-producing skills?
close_reason: Design resolved with explicit supported-path gate, crash-safe output accounting, durable Park, operator authority, workflow ceiling, and local Run socket. Lessons routed to issue comments; implementation sliced under qbr.3.2.6; no additional AGENTS.md rule warranted.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text:
Grill decision confirmed by maintainer (2026-08-26), first boundary:

Use supported-path enforcement, not an adversarial subprocess sandbox. All isolated worker worktrees borrow one canonical Beads graph, preserving the earlier qbr.6 decision: workers may claim, comment, and file findings; the coordinator alone owns integration, closure, and .beads Git commits. Until br exposes a documented worktree redirect command, workers can target the canonical SQLite database explicitly through BEADS_DB/--db; br's workspace write lock serializes mutations.

capture-service owns the durable per-Run budget ledger and a mediated generated-work broker. Run-owned Agent environments receive a br shim: ordinary tracker operations reach the canonical graph, while issue-producing commands (br create and br q) route through the broker. Deliberate absolute-path or alternate-client bypass is outside this supported-path correctness contract and remains the outer Agent harness's responsibility.

Use one Run-level Generator budget with typed consumption entries rather than separate unrelated counters. The first adapter meters issue creation, but the ledger shape must also admit automatic back edges and work-producing skill invocation so those mechanisms cannot evade the same Run bound.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Grill decision confirmed by maintainer (2026-08-26), exhaustion authority:\n\nWhen the generated-work broker finds no remaining Run budget, capture-service atomically refuses the mutation and durably transitions the Run to Parked. This is enforcement of a transition pre-authorized at Run admission, not a discretionary orchestration decision. Neovim observes the durable state change and cancels live turns/Sessions without waiting for Agent cooperation. If Neovim is absent, the Park still exists and its normal expiry/reaper contract applies. Refusal without Park and a Neovim-only transition were rejected because either leaves the Run active or creates a loss window when the cockpit disappears.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Grill decision confirmed by maintainer (2026-08-26), budget increase semantics:\n\nA generated-work budget is persisted as one monotonic absolute ceiling plus cumulative typed consumption. Resuming does not reset consumption. For example, a Run parked at 5/5 may be raised to an absolute ceiling of 8, leaving three generations; a later raise to 10 leaves five. Human UI may offer relative phrasing such as “add 3”, but it sends and persists the resulting absolute ceiling. A resume request may not lower the ceiling or rewrite prior consumption.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Grill decision confirmed by maintainer (2026-08-26), resume authority:\n\nUse scoped capabilities rather than trusting a caller-supplied origin flag. Run-owned Agents receive only generate/status authority. The Neovim operator path holds separate raise_budget/resume authority and never places it in Agent environments, prompts, or advertised tools. capture-service refuses raise/resume through the Agent capability even when the payload claims operator origin. After a cold restart, Neovim recovers operator authority through the owner-only local service connection. This is structural supported-path enforcement, not a claim of adversarial filesystem isolation.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Grill decision confirmed by maintainer (2026-08-26), crash-safe accounting:\n\nUse durable conservative reservations. Before any external mutation, capture-service journals a pending typed Generator entry with a unique mutation id; pending entries occupy Run budget immediately, so concurrent Sessions cannot overspend. Brokered br create carries that identity in external_ref. A confirmed success becomes consumed and records the created issue id; a definite failure releases the reservation. A crash or ambiguous result leaves the reservation occupied until startup reconciliation against the canonical Beads graph. Uncertainty may temporarily Park a Run, but it must never produce uncounted work or exceed the ceiling.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Grill decision confirmed by maintainer (2026-08-26), accounting unit:\n\nCount generated outputs, not Generator invocations. One created Beads issue consumes one unit; one automatic back-edge traversal consumes one unit because it creates another stage execution. Invoking a work-producing skill does not consume a second unit: admission reserves that Generator's declared maximum, each resulting output converts one reserved unit to consumed, and unused reservations are released when the Generator completes. A Generator cannot start unless its required reservation fits the remaining Run budget. This prevents both double charging and one nominal invocation producing unbounded outputs.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text:
Grill decision confirmed by maintainer (2026-08-26), initial Run ceiling:

A workflow containing any automatic Generator must declare one explicit workflow-level generated-work maximum. This is the authored total ceiling for the whole Run and is presented for operator approval at admission. Local Generator maxima remain separate per-invocation reservation bounds; the global ceiling is not derived by summing them because repeated and nested topology makes that sum misleading. The operator may narrow the ceiling at admission; once admitted, the persisted absolute ceiling is monotonic and can only be raised through operator authority. If a Generator's required reservation exceeds the remaining Run budget, it cannot start and the Run Parks.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text:
Grill decision confirmed by maintainer (2026-08-26), async service observation:

Use an owner-only Unix-domain socket as capture-service's local control and event boundary rather than coupling Neovim to filesystem watcher semantics. capture-service remains the sole writer of durable Run state. A client receives an initial state snapshot and then typed run_changed notifications carrying a Run id and monotonic revision; notifications are invalidation hints, not a second source of truth. On disconnect or restart, the client reconnects and obtains another snapshot, so missed or duplicate events cannot corrupt state. The socket supports one durable Rust owner with multiple future consumers, not multiple services independently mutating Run records. Android remains behind the existing authenticated network boundary and receives no local operator authority. Treat this socket as a separate qbr.3.2.6 implementation slice.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text:
Grill decision confirmed by maintainer (2026-08-26), local authority API:

Expose narrow capability-scoped socket operations: Agent authority may generate work and inspect status; read-only consumers may get or subscribe to Run state; operator authority alone may raise_generated_work_ceiling with an absolute ceiling and resume_run. Both operator mutations require the caller's expected Run revision. Keep raise and resume separate: a successful raise followed by a failed resume safely leaves the Run Parked and retryable. Do not expose a generic update_run or arbitrary envelope payload, so generated-work increases cannot widen another envelope axis by accident.

title: Admit Runs with a durable generated-work ceiling
description:
## Goal
A workflow with an automatic Generator admits a Run only with an explicit, operator-approved generated-work ceiling that survives service restart.

## Scope
- In scope: workflow-level generated-work maximum schema and Validation, admission presentation, operator narrowing at admission, and durable per-Run initialization in capture-service.
- Out of scope: generated Beads mutations, socket subscriptions, operator resume, and non-issue Generator execution.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Validation rejects a workflow containing an automatic Generator when the workflow-level maximum is absent, non-literal, non-positive, or otherwise malformed.
2. Local generates.max and max-iterations remain per-Generator bounds and are not summed into the Run ceiling.
3. Admission presents the authored ceiling and initializes one Run with consumed=0 and no pending reservations.
4. An operator may narrow the ceiling before admission; the admitted absolute ceiling is persisted and cannot be lowered afterward.
5. Separate Runs have separate ledgers and service restart preserves each value.

## Testing
- Red-green Lua schema/Validation and admission tests.
- Rust persistence, malformed-input, monotonic-ceiling, and concurrent-Run tests.
- Focused tests followed by the full required gates.

## Notes
Use the canonical Run and Generator vocabulary. Keep Run state owned by capture-service; do not add a second Lua-owned durable ledger.
close_reason: Admitted Runs now persist an operator-approved generated-work ceiling before generation

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Completion evidence (2026-08-26): workflows with an automatic Generator now require one literal positive generated-work.max on the entry stage; prepare_admission exposes the authored maximum and permits only operator narrowing. capture-service now admits an active Run before generation, persists an isolated {ceiling, consumed, reserved} ledger, requires prior admission before cold Park, and exposes the ledger in durable Park summaries. The Run record schema intentionally advances to version 2; this early-stage project has no compatibility migration. Verification: 634 MiniTest cases, all Rust targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo fmt, StyLua, LuaLS, and git diff checks pass. Lesson routing: this issue comment records the schema and boundary; no new AGENTS.md rule or unresolved design question is warranted.

title: Broker crash-safe Beads generation through the Run budget
description:
## Goal
A Run-owned Agent can create Beads work only through a broker that reserves capacity before mutation and Parks before an over-budget issue reaches the graph.

## Scope
- In scope: capture-service reservations, typed issue-output consumption, mutation ids, br create/q mediation, external_ref reconciliation, canonical BEADS_DB targeting, actor preservation, and the Run Agent br shim.
- Out of scope: Neovim socket observation/operator UI and automatic back-edge execution.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The broker durably reserves one unit before invoking br; if capacity is unavailable, no br mutation runs and the Run atomically becomes Parked.
2. Confirmed creation consumes the reservation and records the issue id; definite failure releases it.
3. Ambiguous exit or service crash leaves capacity reserved until reconciliation finds the mutation id in canonical Beads state.
4. Concurrent Sessions in one Run cannot overspend, while another Run and manual human br use remain unaffected.
5. Created issues retain the requesting Session actor, and isolated worktrees target one canonical graph.
6. The supported Agent environment routes br create and br q through the broker while ordinary br reads and coordination operations still work.

## Testing
- Rust state-machine and restart tests plus deterministic broker/shim integration tests with a temporary canonical Beads database.
- Assert mutation-before-budget ordering is impossible and sensitive process data is not logged.
- Focused tests followed by full Rust and Lua gates.

## Notes
This is supported-path correctness, not an adversarial subprocess sandbox. Deliberate absolute-path or alternate-client bypass remains the outer Agent harness responsibility.
close_reason: Crash-safe Beads generation is budgeted before mutation, reconciled by external_ref, attributed to the attached Session, and routed through the supported Agent br shim; focused and full Rust/Lua gates pass.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Implementation paused before the reservation state machine: service-originated budget exhaustion must create a Park with a declared expiry, but admission currently persists no relative expiry policy. Filed blocking design supplement louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.3.1; choosing an undeclared timeout here would violate the accepted Park contract.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Implemented the supported-path gate as a two-phase capability: capture-service admits the Run and returns a secret token before ACP process launch; the initialized Session is attached afterward to preserve its truthful actor. Every create/q reserves under a filesystem lock before br starts, uses a deterministic external_ref for restart reconciliation, and retains ambiguous capacity. Explicit and budget-triggered Parks now derive absolute expiry from the admission TTL using the service clock. The repo br shim only intercepts create/q; reads and coordination pass through to the real br. No standing AGENTS.md rule is warranted; the architecture and expiry decision are issue-local and the latter is recorded on closed design question louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.3.1.

title: Grill-me needed: what expiry governs a service-originated budget Park?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; run a focused design supplement before the generated-work broker is implemented.

Question: What declared expiry policy must capture-service apply when budget exhaustion Parks an active Run without Neovim participating?

Context/evidence:
- qbr.8 requires every Park to have a declared expiry that eventually Disposes.
- qbr.3.2.6.1 gives capture-service authority to atomically refuse an over-budget mutation and durably Park the Run, including while Neovim is absent.
- qbr.3.2.6.2 now admits an active Run with identity and generated-work ceiling, but its durable record carries no Park-expiry policy.
- The existing cold-Park command receives an absolute expires_at_ms from Neovim. That cannot help a later service-originated budget Park when Neovim is absent.
- Choosing silently would either create a Park the reaper can never expire or hide a global timeout outside the workflow envelope.

Threads worth pulling:
1. Prefer a workflow-authored relative Park TTL persisted at Run admission, with exhaustion recording parked_at and expires_at atomically.
2. An absolute timestamp fixed at admission can expire before a long-running Run ever Parks.
3. A service-global default is operationally simple but makes the workflow envelope incomplete and harder to review.
4. Settle the human-facing frontmatter representation and whether warm and cold Parks share the same expiry policy.
close_reason: Resolved: workflow-authored relative Park TTL is persisted at admission and applied by capture-service at Park time

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text:
Design supplement confirmed by maintainer (2026-08-27):

Every workflow declares one relative Park expiry on its entry stage using strict duration syntax: a positive integer followed by s, m, h, or d (for example park-expiry: 24h). Validation rejects missing or malformed expiry. Admission normalizes and durably persists park_ttl_ms. Whenever any Park begins, capture-service records parked_at_ms and computes the absolute expires_at_ms from its own clock in the same durable transition. Warm and cold Parks use this one policy. Absolute timestamps fixed at admission and service-global defaults were rejected because they can expire before Park or hide part of the workflow envelope.

title: Observe and resume budget Parks over the local Run socket
description:
## Goal
Neovim reacts asynchronously when capture-service Parks a Run and lets only the operator raise its generated-work ceiling and resume it.

## Scope
- In scope: owner-only Unix-domain socket, initial snapshots, monotonic Run revisions, typed run_changed notifications, reconnect reconciliation, live Session cancellation, Park presentation, and narrow raise/resume operations.
- Out of scope: Android transport, generic orchestration, arbitrary Run updates, and additional envelope-axis changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A connecting Neovim receives an authoritative snapshot, then typed run_changed hints containing Run id and revision.
2. Duplicate or missed events are harmless; reconnect rereads state and stale expected revisions are rejected.
3. A service-originated budget Park is marshalled from the libuv callback to Neovim's main loop before cancelling live turns/Sessions or touching UI.
4. The Park view shows ceiling, consumed, pending/reserved capacity, and the triggering mutation without sensitive payloads.
5. Agent authority cannot raise or resume. Operator authority may raise only to a greater absolute ceiling and resume separately.
6. Socket permissions are owner-only, stale socket cleanup is safe, and shutdown/reconnect does not leak handles or callbacks.

## Testing
- Rust protocol, permission, revision, reconnect, and capability tests.
- Neovim async tests that exercise a real fast-event scheduling boundary and late events after disposal.
- Focused tests followed by full required gates.

## Notes
The event stream is an invalidation channel; the durable Run record remains the source of truth. Android stays on the separately authenticated network boundary.
close_reason: All children closed: authoritative Run socket streaming (.4.1), safe Park reaction with live-Session cancellation (.4.2), operator raise/resume with revision checks and warm/cold handoff (.4.3). Acceptance criteria met and verified under full Rust + Neovim gates.

title: Stream authoritative Run invalidations over a local socket
description:
## Goal
A Neovim client can connect to an owner-only local Run socket, receive an authoritative snapshot, and treat revisioned run_changed messages as invalidation hints.

## Scope
- In scope: Unix-domain listener lifecycle, owner-only permissions, safe stale-socket handling, durable monotonic Run revisions, snapshot framing, typed run_changed hints, reconnect reconciliation, and a minimal asynchronous Lua client.
- Out of scope: Park UI/cancellation, mutations, Android, and generic orchestration.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Connection starts with a complete authoritative Run snapshot and revision.
2. Every durable Run mutation advances its revision and emits only Run id plus revision.
3. Duplicate, stale, and missed hints are harmless because the client rereads authoritative state.
4. Socket mode is owner-only; stale cleanup never removes a live listener.
5. Client disposal/reconnect ignores late callbacks and leaks no handles.

## Testing
- Rust protocol, permissions, stale-listener, monotonic revision, and reconnect tests.
- Neovim async tests using real fast-event scheduling and late delivery after disposal.
- Full required gates.

## Notes
The socket is an invalidation channel; durable Run files remain source of truth.
close_reason: Owner-only revisioned Run socket and scheduled Neovim snapshot client implemented; full Rust/Lua gates pass.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Implemented the local Run socket as an invalidation channel over durable schema-v4 Run revisions. The capture-service daemon binds a lock-protected 0600 Unix socket, refuses live/non-socket collisions, sends sanitized snapshots, and detects revisions written by separate broker processes. Lua requests a fresh snapshot for newer hints, marshals parsing and callbacks through vim.schedule, closes EOF handles, and ignores queued work after disposal. Reconnect correctness comes from the mandatory initial snapshot, not replaying events. No AGENTS.md rule or design supplement is warranted; this is the issue-local realization of the accepted socket architecture.

title: React safely when a budget Park arrives
description:
## Goal
A service-originated budget Park cancels the matching live Run on Neovim's main loop and presents bounded, non-sensitive accounting to the operator.

## Scope
- In scope: matching durable Run identity to the live Run, scheduled cancellation boundary, typed Park state, and operator presentation of ceiling, consumed, reserved/pending, and triggering mutation id.
- Out of scope: raising/resuming, Android notifications, and arbitrary Run inspection UI.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A budget Park hint is reconciled from durable state before local action.
2. Fast-event callbacks schedule before touching Session lifecycle or UI.
3. The matching live Run is Parked/cancelled once; duplicates are idempotent.
4. Presentation includes accounting and mutation identity but no token, arguments, prompt, or payload.
5. Events arriving after Run/client disposal perform no editor operation.

## Testing
- Headless behavioral async tests model the production callback context and disposal race.
- Full required gates.
close_reason: Revision-idempotent Park reconciliation cancels live work after scheduling and presents only bounded non-sensitive state; all gates pass.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Implemented a distinct accept_park lifecycle path for service-originated durable Parks, avoiding duplicate persistence while cancelling active workers once. ParkObserver reconciles only newer snapshots, maps durable ids to live Runs through an injected owner lookup, and emits a copied bounded projection containing accounting, pending/triggering mutation ids, and expiry. Integrated fast-event coverage drives the real RunClient through uv.new_async and proves lifecycle/presentation happen on the main loop; a disposal race proves queued snapshots are inert. No standing rule or design question is warranted.

title: Raise and resume a budget Park with operator authority
description:
## Goal
An operator can explicitly raise a Parked Run's generated-work ceiling and resume it through narrow revision-checked operations unavailable to Agent authority.

## Scope
- In scope: separate raise and resume requests, expected-revision checks, greater-absolute-ceiling validation, operator capability, reconnect-safe results, and warm/cold resume handoff.
- Out of scope: lowering budgets, changing other envelope axes, Agent-originated resume, Android, and generic Run mutation.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Raise rejects stale revision, non-increase, invalid capability, and non-Parked Run.
2. Resume is a separate operator act and rejects Agent generate capability.
3. Raising changes only the generated-work ceiling; all other admitted envelope state is byte-for-byte unchanged.
4. Successful mutations durably advance revision and publish run_changed.
5. Retry after an ambiguous connection loss reconciles from the authoritative snapshot without applying twice.

## Testing
- Rust capability/state/revision and restart tests.
- Neovim operator-flow tests for warm and cold Park handoff.
- Full required gates.
close_reason: Operator raise/resume implemented: separate raise and resume operator ops, revision-checked, greater-absolute-ceiling validation, reconnect-safe idempotent retry via authoritative snapshot reconciliation, warm/cold Park handoff. Fixed a real concurrency gap found during verification: expiry reap now takes the same durable-store lock as resume, with a regression test forcing resume/reap to serialize (resume_lease_expiry_disposes_and_warm_resume_activates_directly). Full gates green: stylua, lua-language-server, MiniTest 652/652, cargo fmt, clippy -D warnings, cargo test (all crates) all clean.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Paused before operator resume mutation: cold resume has an asynchronous reconstruction gap where immediately activating loses expiry safety, while remaining ordinarily Parked allows expiry cleanup to race session/load. Filed blocking grill question louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.4.3.1 before encoding an undeclared lifecycle.

title: Grill-me needed: when does cold-Park resume relinquish expiry protection?
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing; use a focused grill-me session and obtain explicit shared understanding.

When an operator resumes a cold-Parked Run, what durable state machine owns the interval between the operator decision and successful ACP session/load?

Context/evidence:
- The Run is durably cold_parked with an expiry and claim-release journal.
- session/load is asynchronous and can fail, hang, or be interrupted by Neovim exit.
- Marking the Run active before load risks an ownerless active Run and disables expiry cleanup.
- Keeping it simply Parked during load lets expiry race a legitimate resume and release claims underneath it.
- Warm resume has a live Session and does not have this reconstruction gap.
- Raise and resume must remain separate operator acts; Agent generate authority cannot perform either.

Threads worth pulling:
- Whether resume uses a durable intermediate state/lease, and which clock/TTL governs it.
- What happens on load success, load failure, Neovim crash, and Park expiry during the attempt.
- Whether retry uses the same operation id and how stale expected revisions reconcile.
- When claims stop being eligible for expiry cleanup.
- What state the operator sees while reconstruction is in progress.
close_reason: Maintainer confirmed the durable resuming lease, transition, retry, timeout, and operator-capability contract.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Decision thread 1: maintainer chose a durable resuming state. Cold resume must not mark the Run active before ACP session/load succeeds, and must not remain an ordinary cold Park vulnerable to uncoordinated expiry cleanup during reconstruction. Still unresolved: the resuming deadline/lease policy and exact crash/failure transitions.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Decision thread 2: maintainer chose a fresh bounded resume lease. An explicit operator resume may extend claim protection beyond the original Park expiry solely for the asynchronous ACP reconstruction attempt. The Run remains non-active and cannot generate work during this lease. Still unresolved: who specifies the lease duration and the terminal transitions on success/failure/timeout.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Decision thread 3: maintainer chose a documented daemon-owned five-minute resume lease. It is a fixed lifecycle/transport timeout, not another workflow envelope field and not an operator-selected value. Repeated extension still requires a new explicit operator resume act. Still unresolved: explicit load-failure behavior and final success/timeout transitions.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Decision thread 4: maintainer chose explicit ACP load failure -> cold_parked with expiry equal to the current resume lease deadline. No time is added by failure handling. A later deliberate operator retry is a new attempt; replay after ambiguous transport loss uses the same attempt id and must not refresh the lease.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Decision thread 5: maintainer chose resume-lease expiry -> Disposal with claim release through the existing durable cleanup journal. Late ACP load/finalize results after expiry are rejected and the reconstructed local Session must be disposed. Remaining question: durable operator-capability delivery to reconnecting Neovim instances.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Decision thread 6: maintainer chose a daemon-managed operator capability persisted in a private 0600 file and read by reconnecting Neovim instances. It is never included in Run-owned Agent environments; those receive only the generate capability, which raise/resume rejects. Deliberate same-user filesystem theft remains outside the supported-path threat model already accepted for the br shim.

comments.author: codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee
comments.text: Shared understanding confirmed: cold resume is a durable resuming state keyed by an operation id, protected by a fresh daemon-owned five-minute lease. The Run remains unable to generate work until ACP session/load succeeds and an idempotent finalize activates it. Explicit load failure returns it to cold_parked with the lease's remaining time; ambiguous replay reuses the operation id without extending the lease; lease expiry Disposes and releases claims, rejecting late results. Raise and resume remain separate revision-checked operator acts. Reconnecting Neovim reads a daemon-managed 0600 operator capability that is never injected into Agent environments; deliberate same-user theft is outside the supported-path model.

title: Bound every Generator and prove the complete Run safety contract
description:
## Goal
Every automatic Generator consumes the same Run budget, and the motivating repeated qa-review scenario Stops by Parking without creating excess work or graph cycles.

## Scope
- In scope: automatic back-edge accounting, work-producing skill reservations, output-based consumption, unused reservation release, and end-to-end acceptance across Lua, capture-service, the br broker, and Neovim.
- Out of scope: Assessment, arbitrary capability envelopes, Android notifications, and new Generator kinds not present in the accepted workflow schema.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. One created Beads issue consumes one unit and one automatic back-edge traversal consumes one unit.
2. Invoking a work-producing skill reserves its declared maximum, each output converts reserved to consumed, and unused capacity is released at completion.
3. A Generator cannot start unless its full required reservation fits remaining capacity.
4. The qa-review scenario repeatedly produces issues up to the ceiling, then Parks with exactly that many issues and no mutation beyond the bound.
5. br dep cycles remains empty throughout, demonstrating that the budget—not cycle detection—stopped growth.
6. Concurrent Runs do not pool capacity, Provenance resolves every generated issue to its Session actor, and resume cannot widen another envelope axis.

## Testing
- Deterministic end-to-end test with the mock Agent and temporary Beads workspace.
- Explicit concurrent-Run, restart/pending-reservation, cancellation, and clean-cycle assertions.
- Full Rust, MiniTest, StyLua, LuaLS, and graph-cycle gates.

## Notes
This task closes the parent only after all preceding slices are green and the parent acceptance criteria are demonstrated end to end.
close_reason: All six acceptance criteria proven, each by a named test, across five child slices (louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5.1 through .5) — see the accounting comment for the criterion-to-test mapping. The Run safety contract now holds end to end: an Agent generating over ACP, an executor traversing bounded back-edges, and a work-producing Generator all charge one shared per-Run ledger, and the motivating qa-review loop Parks at its ceiling having created exactly that many issues with br dep cycles empty throughout. Closing the largest structural gaps found on the way: the ledger seam had no production implementer at all and its synchronous contract could not back a real subprocess, and reserve/confirm/release were exposed on no transport. Lesson routing: an AGENTS.md section 8 rule on async seams, and louiselm-qbr.3.7 filed for the missing document-to-manifest path. Gates: full MiniTest 0 fails, LuaLS 0 problems, StyLua, API appendix, cargo test/clippy/fmt all clean.

comments.author: claude/70be7a6a-8674-45f2-ae6e-37ab67c8eac9
comments.text: Claiming this leaf. Parent louiselm-qbr.3.2.6's claim by codex/01a03ec2-dede-7c62-958c-0dd56e12b1ee was at 486m, past the 480m abandoned threshold, and the session is confirmed dead. comments.author: claude/004cc6f2-daa2-4bdf-b0b1-136c23318dc6
comments.text:
Acceptance accounting, criterion by criterion, with the test that carries each.

AC1 (one issue = one unit, one automatic back-edge = one unit): tests/workflow/ledger_integration_spec.lua 'an executor back-edge and an Agent br create charge one shared budget'. Before this the two halves were charged through unrelated mechanisms with no test that they met the same store; that was the gap louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5.2 existed to close.

Verified against an off-by-one mutation of the fit check.

AC5 (br dep cycles empty throughout): asserted at every round boundary and after the Park in the same test. This is what makes AC4 mean anything: the workflow is acyclic by construction and still unbounded, so a halt only credits the budget if cycle detection provably did nothing.

title: Expose Generator reservations on the capture CLI
description:
## Goal

Expose the existing `RunStore` reservation API on the capture CLI so a Generator reservation can be expressed from outside the Rust process. Today `capture-service/src/cli.rs:110` dispatches only `list`, `admit`, `attach`, `generate`, and `park`, and the error at `cli.rs:163` is authoritative: reserve/confirm/release are in-process Rust only. `generate` hardcodes `kind: "beads_issue", units: 1` (`generation.rs:97-103`), so there is no way to express a multi-unit `skill_generator` reservation or a `back_edge` consume from any caller.

This is the transport `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5` AC2 and AC4 need. It is deliberately the narrow surface: expose what `RunStore` already implements, add nothing to the ledger itself.

## Scope

- In scope: `run reserve`, `run confirm`, `run release` subcommands over the existing `reserve_generated_work` / `confirm_generated_work` / `release_generated_work` (`capture-service/src/runs.rs:389,461,513`); token + typed-kind + units argument validation; the AC3 fit-check regression.
- Out of scope: Lua callers (own slice), socket verbs (the socket carries the operator capability, not the Run generate token), any change to reservation semantics.

## Design constraint

Follow the `run generate` precedent for authority: the Run generate token authorizes the mutation, passed the same way `generate` takes it. Do not add these to the Unix socket — `run_socket.rs:189-231` is the operator-capability surface, and reservations are Run-scoped, not operator-scoped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `run reserve --kind <kind> --units <n>` reserves typed multi-unit capacity and reports reserved/exhausted/pending distinguishably to a caller (exit status or parseable output, not prose).
- `run confirm` converts exactly one reserved unit to consumed per output; `run release` returns the whole remaining reservation.
- Replay of the same mutation id is idempotent through the CLI, matching the in-process guarantees at `runs.rs:398,478`.
- **AC3 regression (currently unproven anywhere):** a reservation of `units: N` is refused when `N > ceiling - consumed - reserved`, in a case where `N-1` would have fit. Every existing test either reserves 1 unit against exhausted capacity or 3 against a ceiling of 5 where it fits, so the fit check at `runs.rs:423` has no test that isolates it.
- An invalid kind, non-positive units, or wrong token is refused without mutating the ledger.

## Not covered

Executor wiring and the Lua adapter, which is the sibling slice.
close_reason: Added run reserve/confirm/release to capture-service/src/cli.rs over the existing RunStore API, with the Run token taken from the environment and every ledger outcome named in a JSON state field alongside the resulting budget. Tests: capture-service/tests/cli.rs gains generator_reservations_round_trip_through_the_cli_and_replay_safely, a_cli_reservation_beyond_the_ceiling_reports_exhausted_and_parks, and cli_reservations_refuse_a_wrong_token_and_malformed_arguments; capture-service/tests/runs.rs gains a_generator_reservation_larger_than_remaining_capacity_cannot_start, which isolates the AC3 fit check (two units fit, three do not, against identical occupancy) and was verified to fail against an off-by-one mutation of runs.rs:431. Gates: cargo test/clippy/fmt, full MiniTest 0 fails, LuaLS 0 problems, StyLua, API appendix all clean.

comments.author: claude/004cc6f2-daa2-4bdf-b0b1-136c23318dc6
comments.text:
Design decision worth carrying into the sibling adapter slice: the Run id and generate token arrive through LOUISELM_RUN_ID/LOUISELM_RUN_TOKEN rather than as arguments. This follows run generate, the only other Run-token-authorized subcommand, and it is a security choice rather than a stylistic one — argv is world-readable in the process table, so a token passed as a flag leaks to every other user on the host. admit/attach/park take --id as a flag precisely because they carry no token. The adapter must pass the token by environment too.

Second decision: every outcome the ledger can legitimately report succeeds and is named in the JSON state field, including exhausted. Exhaustion is a Park awaiting an operator decision, not a command failure, and mapping it to a non-zero exit would force the caller to distinguish 'budget is spent' from 'the CLI broke'. Only malformed input, a forged token, and genuine I/O failures exit non-zero.

Third: each response carries the resulting generated_work snapshot, so a caller never re-reads the Run to learn what its own request did. This matters for the adapter, where a second read would be a second process spawn.

Deliberately NOT added: a composite consume verb. executor.lua's ledger contract has consume(mutation_id, kind, units) for back-edges, which is reserve+confirm collapsed, but confirm_generated_work requires a non-empty external issue id and a back-edge traversal has no Beads issue to name. Resolving what identity a back-edge confirms against is the adapter's design problem and belongs in louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5.2, not in a ledger verb invented here.

title: Bind the workflow executor to the real Run ledger
description:
## Goal

Bind `lua/louiselm/workflow/executor.lua`'s ledger callback to the real capture-service Run ledger. This closes the single largest gap in `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5`: `executor.lua` declares an `ExecutorLedger` contract (`executor.lua:13-17`) and calls `consume`/`reserve`/`confirm`/`release` against it, but **no production code ever supplies one** — `grep new_executor` finds only the export at `init.lua:60` and six lines in `tests/workflow/executor_spec.lua`. Every budget guarantee proven on the Lua side today is proven against a hand-rolled recording table.

## Scope

- In scope: a ledger adapter that implements the `ExecutorLedger` contract against the `run reserve/confirm/release` CLI surface, plus the back-edge `consume` path; token plumbing; async/fast-event discipline; wiring it as the ledger a real executor is constructed with.
- Out of scope: the CLI surface itself (blocking sibling slice), the qa-review scenario fixture, mock Agent changes.

## Design constraints

- `service.lua:43-50` already builds the Run environment (`LOUISELM_RUN_ID`/`LOUISELM_RUN_TOKEN`/`LOUISELM_CAPTURE`) and `service.lua:104-269` already shells out to `run admit/attach/park/list`. Extend that established path rather than inventing a second transport. `run_client.lua`'s socket carries the *operator* capability and is the wrong channel for a Run-scoped reservation.
- Per AGENTS.md section 10: `vim.system()` with argument arrays, never shell strings; treat its callbacks as fast-event callbacks and marshal editor work at the narrowest boundary. `executor.lua`'s ledger calls are currently synchronous-return (`"consumed"|"exhausted"|"pending"`); reconciling that with async `vim.system` is the real design work in this slice, and the resolution belongs in a comment here.
- Per AGENTS.md section 8: core modules return structured errors, never notify or open UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A real executor constructed through the production path charges an automatic back-edge traversal against the actual `RunStore`, and the resulting consumption is observable in `run list`.
- A `skill_generator` stage reserves its declared `generates.max`, each recorded output converts one reserved unit to consumed, and `end_generator` releases the remainder — verified against the real ledger, not a fake.
- Ledger exhaustion Parks the executor (`executor.lua:182,323`) and the Run's own state agrees; the two are not independently tracked.
- **AC1 joint proof:** a `br create` through the shim and a back-edge traversal through the executor both charge one unit against the *same* Run ledger. Today these are two unrelated mechanisms with no test that they meet.
- A ledger transport failure surfaces as a structured error and does not silently un-charge or double-charge.

## Not covered

The end-to-end qa-review Park scenario, which is a sibling slice that consumes this adapter.
