title: QA round: durable cold-Park resume
description:
# Manual QA review — durable cold-Park resume

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; its final content becomes the round Beads record
when the round closes.

**Build under test:** `ecb7b46..a983ea4` (`a983ea4` pushed to `origin/main`).
Re-run Setup after any fix.

Origin: `louiselm-brp7` found that `:LouiselmResumePark` loaded an ACP Session
and reported success while the capture-service Run stayed `cold_parked`. The
fix routes the UI through the authoritative revisioned `resume` → ACP
`session/load` → `finalize_resume(active)` sequence before attaching the
Session.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Successful cold Park resume finalizes the durable Run | **passed** — Run `6df99a74-...` active after resume; follow-up accepted |
| 2 | A finalized Run cannot be resumed a second time | **passed** — saved Run absent from second picker; six unrelated cold Parks remained |

## Setup

From `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`:

```sh
git rev-parse --short HEAD                 # expect a983ea4
cargo build --release --manifest-path capture-service/Cargo.toml
systemctl --user is-active louiselm-capture.service
PATH="$PWD/capture-service/target/release:$PATH" nvim -u ./manual_init.lua
```

Use the same state-root environment as the already-running capture service.
Do not start a second service. If the service was started with
`LOUISELM_CAPTURE_STATE_DIR` or a non-default `XDG_STATE_HOME`, export that
same value before launching Neovim. Inside Neovim verify the CLI path:

```vim
:lua print(vim.fn.exepath("louiselm-capture"))
```

It must point at `capture-service/target/release/louiselm-capture`. Use a fresh
real Session in its normal Agent mode; do not use a skip-approval/yolo mode.
The Agent must advertise ACP `loadSession`; the prior Claude QA setup did.
Record the Session id with `:LouiselmSessionId`.

Do not use the capture-service CLI to create the Run. The Park must be created
by `:LouiselmPark` from a live Session that has completed at least one prompt.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- The CLI list and the UI Run socket must use the same state root as the
  service. A mismatched `XDG_STATE_HOME` makes the picker or evidence look
  empty without testing the product path.
- Restart Neovim between Park and resume. `Chat:dispose()` closes the original
  Session; a fresh process proves the picker reconstructs the cold Run instead
  of reusing a local owner.
- Pin the selected Run id and Session id. Never inspect whichever JSON file or
  ACP log happens to be newest.
- Automated tests already cover failed `session/load` finalization and late
  disposal. This manual round focuses on the real Agent/service boundary,
  durable state, and UI timing.

## Cases

### 1. Successful cold Park resume finalizes the durable Run

Exercises `ca30c28`, `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:4365`,
`lua/louiselm/workflow/resume_controller.lua:94`, and the real
`louiselm-capture` Run socket.

Steps:

1. Start a fresh real Session and send a harmless prompt such as: “Reply
   exactly `park-qa-ready`; do not modify files.” Wait for it to finish.
2. Run `:LouiselmPark`. Expect `Session cold-Parked`.
3. Run `louiselm-capture run list` in a shell using the same state root. Save
   the new Run id; it must be listed as a cold Park. Also save the ACP Session
   id from `:LouiselmSessionId`.
4. Quit Neovim completely. Start it again with the Setup command.
5. Run `:LouiselmResumePark`, select the saved Run, and wait. Expect
   `cold Park resumed (recoverable, lossy)` and a focused loaded chat buffer.
6. Send a follow-up: “Reply exactly `park-qa-followup`; do not modify files.”
   It must complete normally.

Current retest attempt: select Run
`6df99a74-12f7-4c75-8484-cfb5874b88c7`, paired with ACP Session
`claude/803f0f3d-926a-45dc-baa9-c1bcd81bf4cb`. The prior failed-test Run is
`a1dff263-9874-4332-8f8a-77e586a739a5`; the remaining listed Runs pair with
older Session `01a050f8-93e9-7f00-847f-be08e6920e77`.

Observed pass: the user selected the matching Run, saw `cold Park resumed
(recoverable, lossy)`, and Claude accepted `park-qa-followup`. The durable
record is `state=active`, `revision=5`, `park_expires_at_ms=0`, and
`resume_attempt.result=active`; the Run is absent from `louiselm-capture run
list`.

Expect: the loaded Session is usable, and the Run is no longer a resumable
cold Park. The success notification must occur only after the ACP Session has
loaded and the durable service has finalized the Run active.

Failure signature: the old bug — the notification appears and the follow-up
works, but the Run remains `cold_parked`, retains a nonzero expiry, or appears
again in the cold-Park picker; the picker has no Run; ACP `session/load` fails;
or the loaded chat cannot accept the follow-up.

### 2. A finalized Run cannot be resumed a second time

Exercises the same durable boundary and the operator’s post-resume view.

Steps:

1. After Case 1 succeeds, run `:LouiselmResumePark` again.
2. If the picker opens, do not select anything; dismiss it and mark the case
   failed. A successfully finalized Run must not be offered as a cold Park.

Expect: LouiseLM reports `no durable cold Parks found` (or shows only other,
unrelated cold Parks), and the saved Run id is absent from
`louiselm-capture run list`.

Failure signature: the same Run is offered again, a second ACP Session is
loaded, or the service list still reports it as `cold_parked`.

Observed pass: the second picker showed `6/6` remaining entries, all older
Runs from unrelated Codex Sessions; saved Run `6df99a74-12f7-4c75-8484-cfb5874b88c7`
was absent. The Claude Session remained ready with the successful follow-up
visible.

## Evidence check

Set `RUN_ID` to the saved id and use the same state root as Setup:

```sh
STATE_ROOT="${LOUISELM_CAPTURE_STATE_DIR:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}}"
RUN_FILE="$STATE_ROOT/louiselm/workflow/runs/$RUN_ID.json"
jq '{id,state,revision,park_expires_at_ms,resume_attempt}' "$RUN_FILE"
louiselm-capture run list
```

Case 1 passes when the JSON says `state: "active"`,
`park_expires_at_ms: 0`, and `resume_attempt.result: "active"`; the saved Run
id must not be in `run list`. Case 2 passes when the same absence remains.
The JSON and CLI prove durable service state and the socket/session evidence
proves the local UI reached the loaded Session; neither command proves focus or
what the user saw, so report that observation separately.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- Remove any disposable Beads claim created for QA and restore its exact prior
  status/assignee.
- Dispose the disposable Session and close extra Neovim windows.
- Do not delete the finalized Run JSON; record its id and outcome first, then
  remove only deliberately created test artifacts if needed.
- Delete this scratch file only after its final content becomes the round bead.

## Reporting back

Send the case number, what you saw, the Run id, the ACP Session id, and any
surprising detail. I will inspect the durable evidence before classifying it.

## Findings this round

**F1 — Resume Park crashes while creating operation id** (`louiselm-q2hp`,
fixed in `a983ea4`, live retest passed).
`resume_controller.lua:27` called `vim.uv.random(16, callback)` although the
local API requires `random(length, buffer?, callback)`. The valid Run
`a1dff263-9874-4332-8f8a-77e586a739a5` in Session
`codex/01a0560a-40aa-75d3-bd30-eb978b8052df` therefore left the user in an
empty buffer before any durable `resume` mutation. The UI regression failed
with a faithful three-argument fake before the fix and passes after changing
the call to `random(16, nil, callback)`.

**F2 — Cold Park picker does not show newest Parks first**
(`louiselm-6d2b`, open task).
The picker made the operator identify the current Session among seven Parks.
`capture-service/src/runs.rs:838` sorts `list_resumable` by UUID, while the
summary does not expose Park creation time. The current retest succeeded after
manual Session matching, but the ordering is avoidable UX friction.
close_reason: Cases 1-2 passed; q2hp fixed and retested; 6d2b filed for picker ordering.

title: Switching sessions leaves chat input in Normal mode
description:
Switching between attached LouiseLM chat sessions leaves the selected chat buffer in Normal mode, so typing and pressing Enter does not submit a prompt. The session appears idle and its ACP process remains alive, but no new prompt reaches the agent until the user manually presses i.

## Observed

Seen 2026-08-22 in the same Neovim instance with Codex sessions codex/01a02a74-274c-79d2-967e-597c37d997ed and the current session. The old session transcript stopped at its previous task completion; no new user turn was recorded after switching to it and pressing Enter. The associated ACP processes were alive.

## Symptoms

- Switching sessions succeeds, but the selected chat does not accept a prompt normally.
- Text typed after switching is handled as Normal-mode input; Enter does not submit.
- Manually pressing i restores the expected behavior.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2027` (`Chat:switch`) changes the current buffer and renders it, but does not restore insert mode or move the cursor to the prompt. `lua/louiselm/ui/picker.lua` stops insert mode before opening the session picker. Initial attachment calls `startinsert` at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1837`, but switching does not.

## Why it was not caught

Existing switch tests assert buffer/session selection and queued prompt behavior, but do not assert the editor mode or cursor state after switching through the picker.

## Fix direction

Make `Chat:switch` restore the selected view prompt cursor and insert mode, using the same narrow behavior as initial attachment. Add a headless regression assertion for switching to a session and submitting through the restored prompt.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after it.
- After `:LouiselmSwitchSession` selects a session, the cursor is on that session prompt and Neovim is in Insert mode.
- Pressing Enter submits a prompt to the selected session without requiring a manual i.

## Not covered

No changes to ACP process lifecycle or persisted Codex sessions are required.
close_reason: Fixed in the working tree: Chat:switch now restores the selected prompt cursor and Insert mode. Regression test tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'restores prompt input after switching sessions' failed before the fix and passes after it. Verification: focused chat_spec.lua 87/87; full MiniTest suite 334/334; stylua --check . passed; lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning passed; git diff --check passed. The full test output still emits pre-existing skill-discovery/write warnings, but no test failures.

title: Agent process stderr is captured by the transport but never surfaced on failure
description:
When the ACP agent process exits (crashes, fails to start, misconfigured
command) before or without completing the handshake, the user only sees a
generic "agent process exited with code N" — the process's own stderr, which
usually names the actual problem, is captured by the transport layer and then
discarded.

## Observed

Code reading, 2026-08-30 (louiselm.nvim main, related to session investigated
in louiselm-8hau).

`lua/louiselm/acp/transport.lua:94-108` defines and wires `on_stderr`:

```lua
local function on_stderr(self, err, data)
  if err ~= nil then
    report_error(self, err)
    return
  end
  if data ~= nil and data ~= "" then
    local callback = self.options.on_stderr
    if callback ~= nil then
      callback(data)
    end
  end
end
```

`M.start` (transport.lua:147-154) registers this as the `stderr` handler
passed to `vim.system`, so stderr chunks do reach `on_stderr` — but
`self.options.on_stderr` is only ever populated if the *caller* of
`Acp.connect`/`Transport.start` sets it.

`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:661-676`, the only production call site
(`Session:start`), builds the options table with `on_notification`,
`on_request`, `on_error`, and `on_exit`, but no `on_stderr` key. So every
stderr chunk hits `if callback ~= nil then callback(data) end` with
`callback == nil` and is silently dropped.

## Symptoms

- A failing agent process (bad command, missing dependency, broken install,
  crash) only ever surfaces `"agent process exited with code N"` in the
  transcript (via `handle_exit`, lifecycle.lua:475-484 -> `fail`).
- The actual diagnostic text the process printed — e.g. an npm CLI's own
  human-readable error message explaining exactly what's wrong — never
  reaches the user, and is not logged anywhere in this code path either.

## Root cause

`Session:start` (lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:661-676) omits an
`on_stderr` callback in the options table passed to `Acp.connect`, even
though `lua/louiselm/acp/transport.lua` fully supports one
(on_stderr defined at lines 97-108, wired at lines 152-154).

## Why it was not caught

No test asserts that stderr output from the agent process becomes visible to
the user or reaches any log. Existing lifecycle tests presumably only cover
the `on_exit`/`handle_exit` path with an exit code, not process output.

## Fix direction

Wire an `on_stderr` callback in `Session:start`'s options table that appends
the captured text to the failure context — e.g. buffer recent stderr lines on
`self.state` and include them in the message `fail()` emits when `handle_exit`
subsequently fires, or surface them as a distinct transcript event. Keep
consistent with AGENTS.md's redaction requirements (`ACP_LOG`/
`ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED` already governs sensitive wire content for the ACP
protocol layer; stderr here is process-level output rather than protocol
payload, but should not be assumed automatically safe to display verbatim —
review before implementation whether it needs the same redaction gate).

## Acceptance

- A regression test that starts a session against a transport double which
  emits stderr output and then exits nonzero, and asserts the resulting error
  event/message includes the emitted stderr text.
- Live: an agent command that prints a diagnostic to stderr before failing
  (e.g. the postinstall-not-run npm error reproduced in louiselm-8hau) shows
  that diagnostic text in the transcript, not just a bare exit code.

## Not covered

- Whether stderr should be shown unconditionally or gated behind
  ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED-style redaction — left as an open question for
  implementation, flagged above.
- The louiselm-8hau startup-timeout gap (a session whose process neither exits
  nor completes the handshake) — separate defect, filed separately.
close_reason:
Fixed. Session:start() (lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua) now wires
`on_stderr` into the Acp.connect options table; a new buffer_stderr() helper
appends incoming chunks to self.stderr_buffer, capped to the most recent
STDERR_BUFFER_LIMIT = 4096 bytes so a chatty process can't grow it unbounded.
handle_exit() now appends the trimmed buffered stderr text to the failure
message ("agent process exited with code N: <stderr>") instead of emitting a
bare exit code.

Tests added in tests/session/api_spec.lua ("new" set):
- "appends buffered agent stderr to the exit error message" - reproduces the
  exact scenario from louiselm-8hau's evidence (the opencode postinstall
  error text), asserts it now reaches the error event message.
- "caps buffered agent stderr to the most recent output" - asserts the
  STDERR_BUFFER_LIMIT truncation keeps the tail.

Gates: full mini.test suite (all files) - 0 fails, 0 notes. `stylua --check` -
clean. `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning` - no problems
found. `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check` - clean after regenerating
doc/api.md alongside louiselm-8hau's LuaCATS changes (same commit scope).

Not covered, as filed: whether stderr should be gated behind an
ACP_LOG_UNREDACTED-style redaction switch was left open in the original bug
and is still open - stderr is shown unconditionally in this fix. Flagging for
a follow-up if that turns out to matter (e.g. an agent CLI that echoes secrets
to stderr on failure).

Deviation: same as louiselm-8hau - implementation preceded the regression
tests rather than witnessed red-green-refactor; tests are behavioral and
verified green against the fix, not proven red against the pre-fix code.

title: Native skill picker never resolves against the real Claude ACP adapter (exact description match rejects its scope-annotation suffix)
description:
Native skill invocation via the picker never resolves against the real Claude Code ACP adapter, because Claude appends a scope annotation to every advertised command description and the correlation code requires exact equality.

## Observed

Found 2026-08-20 during a qa-review round for louiselm-2w4 (native ACP command invocation, commit 763ba78), before any human test case was run -- by inspecting a pre-existing real ACP debug log on this machine (louiselm.nvim itself is run through claude-agent-acp for this very session).

Log: ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260820-100019-702281-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log, line 3 (session/update, sessionUpdate=available_commands_update). The "grill-me" entry:

  "name":"grill-me","description":"Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases. (user)","input":null

The local SKILL.md at ~/.config/agentskills/generated/grill-me/SKILL.md has description:

  Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

-- identical text, but the advertised one carries a trailing " (user)" that the local one does not.

Checked systematically: parsed all 76 entries in that available_commands_update payload. Every command whose name matches a configured local skill path (br, bvr, caveman, caveman-commit, caveman-help, caveman-review, grill-me, htmx, karpathy-guidelines, lightweight-charts, playwright-cli, playwright-qa-review, ponytail*, qa-review, rscss, rtk, rust-architecture, terraform-skill, to-beads*, write-a-skill -- 27 total) ends with " (user)". Claude's own built-in/plugin commands in the same payload (compact, config, model, doctor, mcp, loop, schedule, security-review, etc.) do not have this suffix.

## Symptoms

- User picks a configured skill via the native picker, types a task, submits.
- louiselm silently notifies "louiselm: advertised command '"'"'<skill>'"'"' description does not match the skill" and does not send the prompt; typed text and the skill chip are preserved (per louiselm-2w4 AC7), so it looks like a transient hiccup rather than a permanent break.
- This happens for every skill, every time, against the real Claude adapter -- native mode is a no-op for Claude in practice, despite ~40 unit/mock tests passing.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua, description_matches() (around line 45): compares the whitespace-normalized advertised description to the whitespace-normalized local skill.description (or skill.short_description) with `==`. Real claude-agent-acp always appends " (user)" (or, presumably, another scope word for project/plugin-scoped commands) to the description of any command sourced from a user-configured skill path, so the strings are never equal even though the command is a correct, unambiguous match. The $-prefixed (Codex-style) tier is unaffected since it never checks description.

## Why it was not caught

Every existing test (tests/skills_spec.lua resolve_command cases, tests/ui/chat_spec.lua native-picker cases, tests/mock/agent_spec.lua) constructs its own advertised-command fixtures with hand-typed descriptions that exactly echo the local skill's description -- none of them models the real adapter's annotation behavior, because that behavior was never observed before this bead was implemented. The acceptance criteria for louiselm-2w4 specified "the whitespace-normalized advertised description matches the local SKILL.md description" without anticipating an adapter-appended suffix.

## Fix direction

In description_matches(), treat the advertised (normalized) description as matching when it *starts with* the local skill's normalized description or short_description, not only on exact equality -- tolerating a trailing annotation without weakening the $-tier or the ambiguity/duplicate rules (those are untouched). Reject anything where the local description is not a prefix of the advertised one, so an unrelated built-in that merely shares a name still fails to match.

## Acceptance

- A regression test in tests/skills_spec.lua using the real captured pair (grill-me description with and without the trailing " (user)") that fails before the fix and passes after.
- Existing exact-match cases keep passing (equality is the size-27-prefix special case of starts-with).

## Not covered

- Whether Codex's $-tier ever needs a similar tolerance -- not verified; no codex-acp session in the available debug logs got far enough to emit available_commands_update. Left as a follow-up if codex turns out to need it too.
- Whether Claude ever uses a different annotation word (e.g. "(project)", "(plugin)") for non-user-scope local skills -- not directly observed, but the starts-with fix is annotation-word-agnostic so it should not matter.
close_reason: Fixed in c230f8c. Root cause: description_matches() in lua/louiselm/skills/native_command.lua required exact whitespace-normalized equality; real claude-agent-acp appends a scope annotation (" (user)") to every command sourced from a user-configured skill path. Changed to starts-with matching against the local description/short_description. Tests: new resolve_command case using the real captured grill-me description pair (tests/skills_spec.lua), plus full existing resolve_command suite re-verified green. Gates: full mini.test suite green (287 cases), stylua and lua-language-server clean. No deviation from filed acceptance criteria. Codex's $-tier tolerance remains unverified (no codex-acp session reached available_commands_update in available logs) -- left as a known gap, not blocking this fix.

title: Resuming a Session dies with 'malformed ACP usage_update notification' when used > size
description:
A `usage_update` reporting `used > size` — which the real Claude agent emits on
the first mid-turn frame after `session/load` — is rejected as malformed, and
the rejection tears down the whole Session: status goes to `error`, the ACP
client is closed, and the in-flight prompt is aborted. The user sees only
`Error: malformed ACP usage_update notification` and loses the resumed
conversation.

## Observed

Reported live by the maintainer on 2026-08-28 against build `bbe82e7`: resumed
`claude/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d`, typed `ok`, session died.

Log: `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d/log.jsonl`
Session ID: `claude/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d`

Observed frame order at the end of that log:

```
07:33:39.017 client_to_agent  session/load
07:33:40.646 agent_to_client  result                     (replay complete)
07:34:21.836 client_to_agent  session/prompt             ("ok")
07:34:21.874 agent_to_client  session/update available_commands_update
07:34:25.340 agent_to_client  session/update usage_update {"used": 237031, "size": 200000}
07:34:25.349 internal         (connection torn down; log ends here)
```

The log's own earlier frames, from the same Session before the editor exit,
carry `{"used": 233011, "size": 1000000}` — i.e. the Session really is running
on a 1M-context model, and 237031 tokens is a perfectly ordinary occupancy for
it. The `size: 200000` in the fatal frame is the agent's pre-correction
default, not a real window.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/session/validation.lua:283-291` rejects any update where
`value.used > value.size`, returning `nil` context.
`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:239-243` maps that `nil` to
`fail(self, "malformed ACP usage_update notification")`, and `fail`
(`lifecycle.lua:136-161`) sets status `error`, closes the ACP client, drops the
permission queue, and completes the pending prompt callback with the error.

`used > size` is not a malformed frame. It is an over-full context window,
which is precisely the condition the `pressure` ladder exists to report. The
guard treats a representable state as a protocol violation.

The agent-side reason it happens on resume is documented in the agent's own
source, `/home/lotso/code/claude-agent-acp/src/acp-agent.ts:6800-6813`: a model
alias resolving to an extended-context model with no `1m` token in its id
"stream[s] `usage_update.size: 200000` until the first result's modelUsage
corrects it". So the wrong `size` is transient and self-correcting — the client
only has to survive it.

## Symptoms

- Resuming a Session on a 1M-context model whose accumulated context exceeds
  200k kills the Session on the first prompt after resume.
- The failure is not recoverable in place: the ACP client is already closed by
  the time the error is displayed.
- The error message names a protocol fault, pointing debugging at the agent
  rather than at louiselm's own validation.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/session/api_spec.lua:1084` covers only the `used = -1, size = 0` case,
where every guard in the condition fires at once. No test isolates
`used > size` with otherwise valid values, and no resume test drives a
`usage_update` whose `size` is smaller than the already-accumulated `used`.

## Fix direction

Accept `used > size` as valid over-full occupancy: clamp `percentage` at 100
and report `pressure = "critical"`. Keep rejecting genuinely unrepresentable
input (`used < 0`, `size <= 0`, malformed `cost`).

## Acceptance

- A regression test feeds `{used = 237031, size = 200000}` (the observed live
  values) and asserts the Session stays `ready` with `pressure = "critical"`.
- Maintainer resumes `claude/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d`, sends a
  prompt, and the turn runs.

## Not covered

Whether *any* malformed `usage_update` should be fatal to a Session at all —
telemetry that cannot be parsed is not a reason to close a working ACP
connection. Filed separately.
close_reason: Live acceptance confirmed via louiselm-rlu7: maintainer resumed claude/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d and sent a prompt; the session survived and the turn completed normally (see rlu7's close reason for log evidence).

comments.author: claude/05f3738e-26f0-4f87-8d8e-2af8dfd11aca
comments.text:
Fixed in the working tree: Validation.usage_update no longer rejects used > size; percentage is clamped to 100 so an over-full window reports pressure=critical instead of failing the Session. Regression test tests/session/api_spec.lua 'accepts an over-full context window' uses the live values (used=237031, size=200000) and cites the log path and Session ID; it fails before the fix with status=error. Full suite green, stylua/lua-language-server clean, doc/api.md regenerated for the ContextUsage.percentage annotation change.

Kept open pending the maintainer's live acceptance: resume claude/ef254b92-acbf-44c3-84fd-3eedb982f46d and send a prompt.

Rejected alternative: making the fail() non-fatal for usage telemetry generally. That is the right fix for the blast radius but changes failure policy for every session/update type, so it is louiselm-apxu, not this issue.

Reusable lesson for the record: the guard was written as if used <= size were a protocol invariant. It is not — the agent's own source (claude-agent-acp src/acp-agent.ts:6800-6813) documents streaming a default 200k size until the first turn result corrects it. Deriving a bound from what a value 'should' mean, rather than from what the wire actually carries, is what turned a self-correcting telemetry glitch into a session kill.

title: LouiseLM reports stale codex-acp version after terminal upgrade
description:
LouiseLM reports the configured codex Agent as outdated even though the same terminal environment reports codex-acp 1.7.0. The notification claims 1.6.2 is installed and 1.7.0 is upstream, so the health check appears to resolve a different executable/environment or stale process state than the user-facing shell.

## Observed

Reported by the maintainer on 2026-08-28 in the louiselm.nvim session. The exact notification was:

louiselm: codex is outdated (@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.2 installed, 1.7.0 upstream)

In the terminal, the same user ran:

 ~/code/louiselm  main *1 !1 ?1  ❯ codex-acp --version
@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.7.0

## Symptoms

- LouiseLM shows an outdated warning for codex.
- The terminal command reports the current installed version as 1.7.0.
- The warning reports an installed 1.6.2, which conflicts with the terminal result.

## Root cause

Unknown. The health path invokes the configured version command through vim.system() in lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:150-162 and compares its output with the configured latest check in lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua:194-197. A likely cause is that the running Neovim process has a different PATH/environment or executable resolution than the terminal, but this is unverified.

## Why it was not caught

Existing tests cover parsing and comparison of mocked version outputs, but do not verify executable/environment parity between a running Neovim instance and the terminal after an agent upgrade.

## Fix direction

Trace the exact argv, cwd, PATH, and resolved executable used by the running Neovim health check without logging sensitive environment contents. Ensure the check observes the same installed codex-acp as the configured Agent, or make the discrepancy actionable if Neovim must be restarted.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails for the displaced version-resolution behavior and passes after the fix.
- When codex-acp --version returns 1.7.0 in the active LouiseLM environment, the notification must not report 1.6.2 installed or mark codex outdated against upstream 1.7.0.

## Not covered

- No reproduction was performed in the maintainer live Neovim instance during filing.
- The upstream version source and configured agent definition were not changed.
close_reason: Ignore superseded asynchronous version results; regression covered

comments.author: codex/01a04635-f2b8-7e70-9485-7a931923ec99
comments.text: Root cause confirmed as a stale asynchronous health callback: a newer chat check can observe the upgraded 1.7.0 executable while an older check later returns 1.6.2 and emits a false warning. Added a generation guard so superseded callbacks are ignored. Regression test failed before the fix and passes now; live shell and Neovim checks both currently report 1.7.0. No separate lesson warranted beyond this issue-local evidence.

title: br scheduler --json returns empty labels, hiding label-based routing from the command AGENTS.md prefers
description:
`br scheduler --json` emits `labels: []` for every recommendation, even when the
issue demonstrably carries labels. The field exists in the `br.scheduler.v1`
envelope and is always empty, so it reads as authoritative absence rather than
as missing data.

## Evidence (br 0.3.2, 2026-08-21)

`br scheduler --limit 6 --json`, labels as reported by the scheduler versus the
same issues via `br label list`:

| issue | scheduler | `br label list` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| louiselm-ce6.21 | `[]` | acp, chat, multimodal, qa-finding, ready-for-agent, ui |
| louiselm-ufx | `[]` | ui |
| louiselm-qbr.1.11 | `[]` | android, capture, qa-finding, ready-for-agent, ui |
| louiselm-qbr.1.12 | `[]` | android, capture, pairing, qa-finding, ready-for-agent, ui |
| louiselm-qbr.1.14 | `[]` | android, capture, privacy, qa-finding, ready-for-agent, ui, usability |
| louiselm-qbr.1.15 | `[]` | android, capture, qa-finding, ready-for-agent, status, ui |

`br list --json` and `br show --json` both populate `labels` correctly for the
same issues, so this is specific to the scheduler envelope.

## Why it matters here

AGENTS.md section 2 tells agents to prefer `br scheduler` over hand-scanning,
because it excludes claimed work and explains its ranking. An agent that follows
that instruction receives issues stripped of their labels.

That closes both routes for label-aware work selection at once. `br scheduler`
has no `--label`/`--label-any` filter of its own (unlike `br ready`), so
server-side filtering is unavailable; and because the returned labels are empty,
client-side filtering on the scheduler's own output is unavailable too. Any
convention that routes work by label is invisible to the command the contract
tells agents to use.

This was found while designing capability-based work routing
(`needs-capability:*` labels). It is not blocking that design -- `br ready`
carries labels and supports `-l` and `--label-any` -- but it does mean the
documented preference for `br scheduler` and label-based routing are mutually
exclusive until one of them changes.

## Not this repository

This is a defect in `br` (beads), not in louiselm. Filed here because it
constrains a louiselm workflow decision and would otherwise be lost. Upstream
report still to be raised.

## Suggested resolution

Populate `labels` in the `br.scheduler.v1` issue envelope from the same source
`br list --json` uses. A `--label`/`--label-any` filter matching `br ready`
would be a separate, larger ask.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text: Deferred intentionally: upstream br change is not in scope right now; revisit when we are ready to work on Beads tooling.

title: QA round: quit guard acceptance, Forensics viewer, Codex reasoning repro
description:
# Manual QA review — Neovim acceptance queue (2026-08-27)

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; it becomes a `qa-round` bead and gets deleted when
we close.

**Build under test:** `f44e0fd` (main, clean tree). Relevant commits:
`32665fd` (quit guard, ce6.34), `faf8cbf` (za fold, already accepted),
forensics slice (ce6.24). **Restart nvim after any fix.**

Origin: four Neovim-side issues sat `in_progress` not because the code was
unfinished but because AGENTS.md requires live maintainer acceptance and nobody
sat down to give it. This round converts "agent says done" into closed or into
a filed bug.

## Scope

In: **ce6.34** (quit guard, P1 — cases 1–5), **ce6.24** (Session Forensics,
P3 — case 6), **6ze7** (Codex reasoning fragmentation, P1 — case 7, *repro
only*, the fix was never written).

Out: **zufj** — dropped, not deferred. Its acceptance needs a live Copilot
Autopilot `task_complete`, and the 2026-08-26 comment records GitHub billing
showing premium quota unavailable for ~6 more days (≈2026-09-01). No amount of
keyboard time reaches it today.

Also out: Android (`1chb.1`, `qbr.1.15`, `1chb.2`) — needs a device, and
`1chb.2` is separately blocked on no tailscale/wireguard binary on the receiver.

Not tested because unit tests already cover it: **refusal clause 1** (Agent does
not advertise ACP `loadSession`). Reaching it live needs an agent that lacks
`loadSession`; codex advertises it (`recoverable: true` in the breadcrumb
below). `tests/ui/command_spec.lua` covers all three clauses together.

## Status

| # | Case | Issue | State |
|---|------|-------|-------|
| 1 | Breadcrumb from the fold session surfaces once at startup | ce6.34 | **passed** — 1a delivered the message, 1b `false`, 1c silent, file unlinked |
| 2 | Clause 2 — turn in flight refuses `:q`, message names `:qa` | ce6.34 | **passed** — refused, message names `:qa`; layout unconfirmed |
| 3 | Clause 3 — staged context refuses `:q`; `:q!` refused identically | ce6.34 | **passed** — both `:q` and `:q!` refused, counts truthful |
| 4 | Accepted residual — idle + recoverable + unstaged exits freely | ce6.34 | **passed** — exited freely, breadcrumb `recoverable:true, turn_active:false, contexts:0` |
| 5 | `:qa` escape exits and still records the breadcrumb | ce6.34 | **passed** (via `:qa!`) — exited, breadcrumb recorded `contexts: 2` |
| 6 | `:LouiselmForensics` collection + human projection | ce6.24 | **partial** — collect + resource link passed; view fails (F1), projection absent (F2) |
| 7 | Codex reasoning after a tool call — repro for the unfixed bug | 6ze7 | **does not reproduce** — trigger shape matched on the wire, renders correctly |

## Setup

Run every case in a **separate Neovim instance** from the one you are reading
this in, exactly as you did for the fold test. Cases 2–5 deliberately quit the
editor.

Confirm the running copy matches source before starting:

```
git log --oneline -1   # expect f44e0fd
```

The breadcrumb is a **single overwritten file** at
`~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/abandoned.json`. It is not append-only, so never
identify a run by "most recent file" — pin on `acp_session_id` and
`recorded_at`. Tell me the ACP session id of each instance you test with.

**Important ordering:** a breadcrumb from your fold-test session is sitting
there right now, unconsumed. Case 1 must run first or it will pollute the
later cases.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- **A concurrent agent is live in the worktree.** Between writing the scope
  section and writing the cases, uncommitted changes appeared in
  `capture-service/tests/runs.rs` and four `tests/workflow/*_spec.lua` files —
  Park-expiry work, matching `f045008` and the open question
  `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.3.1`. **None of them touch any file this round exercises**
  (`ui/chat/*`, `ui/abandonment.lua`, `session/*`), so the round is safe to run.
  But do not `git stash`, and if a case fails, check whether that agent has
  landed something before blaming the build. This is the same collision that
  blocked 6ze7 in the first place.
- **R1 — there is no `:LouiselmSetup` command.** Setup is the Lua entry point
  `require("louiselm").setup(config)`, invoked by the plugin manager at startup;
  the full registered command list is 32 `Louiselm*` commands and Setup is not
  among them. Any case that wants to re-run setup must either restart nvim or
  call the module function directly. My error, case 1 rewritten.
- **R2 — `:messages` is the wrong channel; notifications go to snacks.** Your
  config loads `snacks.nvim` at `config/plugins/init.lua:6`, before louiselm at
  line 19, and `snacks.notifier` replaces `vim.notify` with a transient float
  that keeps its **own** history and writes nothing to `:messages`. Every
  louiselm notification in this round — the breadcrumb message, the quit-guard
  refusal — arrives that way. Read them with `<leader>n`
  (`Snacks.notifier.show_history()`), never `:messages`. Applies to cases 1, 2,
  3 and 5.
- Append here every time a case misses for an environmental reason rather than a
  code reason.

## Cases

### 1. Breadcrumb from the fold session surfaces once at startup

Exercises `32665fd` — `lua/louiselm/ui/abandonment.lua:131` (`M.consume`) and
the setup consumption path.

There is already an un-consumed breadcrumb on disk, written at 03:15 today when
you quit the fold-test Neovim:

```json
{"version":1,"recorded_at":1787793346,"sessions":[{"agent":"codex",
"acp_session_id":"01a040c5-40ae-7891-b5a5-a39ea279e6f7",
"recoverable":true,"turn_active":false,
"staged":{"contexts":0,"pending_skill":false,"queued_prompt":false}}]}
```

Mode is `0600` — private permissions already confirmed from here, no keyboard
needed for that part.

There is no `:LouiselmSetup` Ex command — setup is
`require("louiselm").setup(config)`, which your plugin manager calls at startup,
and `surface_abandonment()` runs inside it (`lua/louiselm/init.lua:60`). So the
trigger is simply **starting nvim**.

**Attempt 1 (2026-08-27) did not reach the code as intended.** The breadcrumb
was consumed and unlinked — the file is gone, so `surface_abandonment` ran — but
I sent you to `:messages`, which snacks.notifier never writes to (ground rule
R2). I have recreated the identical breadcrumb on disk (same session id, same
`recorded_at`, mode `600`) so this is a clean rerun.

Steps:

> **1a.** Start a fresh nvim. Do not open a chat. Watch the top-right corner
> during startup, then immediately press `<leader>n` for the snacks
> notification history.
>
> **1b.** Still in that instance, run:
> `:lua print(require("louiselm.ui.chat.command").surface_abandonment())`
>
> **1c.** Quit with `:q`. You opened no chat, so there is no live Session and
> nothing should be written. Start nvim again and check `<leader>n`.

Expect: **1a** — one entry in the notification history, approximately
`louiselm: previous exit ended 1 live Session; resume codex with :LouiselmResume`.
**1b** prints `false` and adds no new entry — the breadcrumb is consumed once
and deleted. **1c** — no louiselm entry at all.

Failure signature: 1b prints `true` or re-notifies (consume did not delete);
codex reported as unrecoverable when the breadcrumb says `recoverable: true`;
1c nags from a breadcrumb a chatless exit should never have written; or **1a's
history is empty**, which is the interesting one — see the prediction below.

**Result (2026-08-27): passed.** 1a delivered
`louiselm: previous exit ended 1 live Session; resume codex with :LouiselmResume`
— truthful: recoverable codex, named, with the resume command. 1b printed
`false` and added no entry. 1c was silent. I confirmed the file is unlinked. All
three of consume-once, truthful classification, and no-write-on-chatless-exit
hold end to end.

**Prediction REFUTED — the delivery question.** `M.consume`
(`abandonment.lua:151`) unlinks the file *unconditionally*, before it has any
idea whether the message was seen, and before it even validates the record. The
delivery surface is a single transient WARN toast during startup churn. On
attempt 1 you were deliberately looking for that message, knowing exactly what
it should say, and did not see it — and the record was deleted anyway. If 1a's
history is empty too, then the guard's whole second half ("leaves a breadcrumb
that reaches the maintainer at the next session") does not reach the maintainer,
and fails silently and irreversibly.

Refuted: the toast rendered and was legible on a fresh start. Attempt 1's miss
was entirely my wrong observation channel (R2) — it was never evidence of
non-delivery. **No finding filed.** The unconditional unlink stays a
theoretical sharp edge, not an observed defect; it is not worth a bead on this
evidence.

Evidence: I check the file is gone after the first setup.

### 2. Clause 2 — turn in flight refuses `:q`

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:347-368`.

Steps:

> Open a chat, send a prompt that takes a while (e.g. *"read AGENTS.md and
> summarise every rule in it"*), and **while the turn is still streaming** type
> `:q` and hit enter.

Expect: nvim does **not** exit. A warning appears **as a snacks toast** (check
`<leader>n` if it flashes past) naming the session and the reason, ending
`. :qa to exit anyway.` The chat window is still there and the editor looks
unchanged.

Failure signature: nvim exits; or it refuses but the message omits `:qa` (the
design record calls a guard that hides its escape hatch "a trap"); or you are
left sitting in a stray extra split that did not clean itself up.

**Result (2026-08-27): passed.** Session
`deepseek/session-af10ba94-1b6f-4bb1-8829-12ef35c0187e`, `:q` during a live turn
was refused with:

```
louiselm: 1 live Session (deepseek: turn in flight). :qa to exit anyway.
```

Correct singular agreement, correct clause attribution, and the escape hatch is
named — the guard is not a trap. Count and parenthetical agree at n=1, so the
second prediction below is still untested.

Outstanding: window layout after the refusal was not reported. Folded into
case 3, which reuses the same instance.

**Prediction to confirm or refute:** the refusal works by opening a temporary
split of the *current* buffer and letting `:q` close that instead. Watch where
the cursor and window layout end up. If the current buffer was a normal file
rather than the chat, you should still end up net-zero windows.

**Second prediction:** the message counts `#sessions` (all live sessions) but
lists reasons only for `blocked` ones. With one blocked and one free session
you would read `2 live Sessions (codex: turn in flight)` — a count that does not
match its own parenthetical. Only observable with two sessions attached; note it
if you happen to see it.

### 3. Clause 3 — staged context refuses `:q`, and so does `:q!`

Exercises the same handler via the Staged-context clause
(`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:40-56`).

Steps — **reuse the case 2 instance**, so the layout check carries over:

> **3a.** First, before anything else: `:echo winnr('$')` and tell me the
> number, plus whether the chat window still looks the way it did before you
> pressed `:q`. This closes out case 2's untested half — the refusal works by
> opening a temporary split, and a leftover window is the failure.
>
> **3b.** Let the turn finish, or `:LouiselmCancel` it. Confirm the Session is
> idle — a still-running turn masks clause 3 behind clause 2 and the case
> proves nothing.
>
> **3c.** Attach a context (file/selection, your normal staging keymap) but
> **do not send**. Confirm the chat shows the staged item. Then `:q`. Then `:q!`.

**Result (2026-08-27): `:q` leg passed.** Session
`deepseek/session-9673cfd7-a022-474c-9fc0-2ce1d5d00d10`, two contexts staged:

```
louiselm: 1 live Session (deepseek: 2 queued contexts). :qa to exit anyway.
```

Staged count is truthful and matches the breadcrumb's `contexts: 2`.

**Still untested: `:q!`.** The run used `:qa!`, which is case 5's escape hatch,
not this case's bang. `:q!` is the one that matters — it is refused *identically*
to `:q` by design, which is backwards from muscle memory, so it is the single
most trap-shaped keystroke in the feature. One keystroke closes it; see the
retry step below.

Expect: **both** are refused, with the staged count in the message.

Failure signature: `:q!` exits. Per the design probe, `:q!` is refused
identically to `:q` — this is intentional and backwards from muscle memory, so
the *message* is the only thing that rescues it. If `:q!` exits, the guard has a
hole; if it refuses silently, it is a trap.

### 3b. Retry — the `:q!` leg only

> Fresh nvim, open a chat, stage **one** context, do not send. Then `:q!`.

Expect: refused, exactly like `:q`, message naming `:qa`.

Failure signature: nvim exits. That is a hole in the guard — `:q!` reads as
"force" to every Vim user alive, and clause 3 losses are unrecoverable.

**Result (2026-08-27): passed.** Session
`deepseek/session-5af6ecbd-af8c-4e75-8eea-9b810a31eb30`, one context staged:

```
louiselm: 1 live Session (deepseek: 1 queued context). :qa to exit anyway.
```

Refused, and singular agreement is correct at n=1 where case 3 showed the plural
at n=2. **ce6.34 is fully accepted and closed.**

### 4. Accepted residual — a clean idle session exits freely

Steps:

> Fresh instance. Open a chat with codex, send nothing (or let a turn fully
> finish), stage nothing. `:q`.

Expect: nvim exits immediately, no refusal. This is the deliberate residual —
you pay one `session/load` replay and nothing else.

Failure signature: it refuses anyway. That would be the blanket-refusal
behaviour the design explicitly rejected as "high-and-decaying coverage".

**Result (2026-08-27): passed**, reached accidentally via case 3 step 3b. Session
`deepseek/session-af10ba94-1b6f-4bb1-8829-12ef35c0187e` went idle and `:q` exited
immediately with no refusal. Breadcrumb confirms all three clauses were false:
`recoverable: true`, `turn_active: false`, `staged.contexts: 0`. Also confirms
deepseek advertises ACP `loadSession`, so clause 1 stays unreachable live.

**Prediction CONFIRMED, but by design — no finding.** `VimLeavePre` writes
the breadcrumb whenever `#sessions > 0`, *not* only when the exit was blocked
(`command.lua:370-378`). So this free, blessed exit should still leave a
breadcrumb, and your **next** nvim start will greet you with
`previous exit ended 1 live Session; resume codex with :LouiselmResume` — after
an exit that was entirely correct and lost nothing. That is exactly how the
`:qa` reflex forms, one rung down. The breadcrumb already on disk from your fold
session is this case, unblocked and pre-confirmed. If it nags you on the next
start, I file it.

### 5. `:qa` escape with a blocked session

Steps:

> Fresh instance. Reproduce case 2 or 3 (get a refusal). Then `:qa`.

**Result (2026-08-27): passed**, via `:qa!` from the case 3 instance. nvim
exited immediately despite an active clause-3 refusal, and `VimLeavePre` still
recorded the loss: breadcrumb at 03:45:49, mode `600`, session
`session-9673cfd7-a022-474c-9fc0-2ce1d5d00d10`, `staged.contexts: 2` matching the
refusal message exactly. Escape hatch and trail both intact. `:qa` without the
bang is not separately tested; `:qa!` is the strictly harder case.

Expect: nvim exits immediately. On the next start you get the breadcrumb
message naming the abandoned session.

Failure signature: `:qa` is also refused (the escape hatch is gone, the guard is
now unescapable), or it exits but writes no breadcrumb (you lost the session
*and* the trail).

### 6. `:LouiselmForensics` collection and human projection

Exercises the ce6.24 first slice. Its own comment says collection is verified;
what is *not* verified is "explicit human projection / resource-link /
targeting coverage" — so that is all this case tests.

Steps:

> With a live chat session, run `:LouiselmForensics`. Then `:LouiselmForensicsView`.
> (Both are real Ex commands — verified against the registered command list.)

Expect: a record is written under `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/`, a
resource link is queued into the chat's next prompt, and the view renders a
readable projection showing session identity, chronology, and which evidence
sources are missing or sensitive.

Failure signature: the view is raw JSON (the projection is the whole point), or
the queued resource link points at a path that does not exist, or the record
targets the wrong session.

**Result (2026-08-27): two of three legs pass.** Session
`deepseek/session-5d380d32-0e8d-4396-afa4-82cc1ee5c4fb`, from an empty baseline
directory.

- Leg 1 **passed**: record written, 841 bytes, mode `0600`, `schema_version: 1`,
  correct `subject.acp_session_id`. `evidence_sources` honestly marks `acp_log`
  as `omitted` with reason "ACP adapter did not advertise a log path" — verified
  correct, deepseek does not route through the acp-llm-adapter proxy, so there is
  genuinely no log to point at. Truthful, not merely populated.
- Leg 2 **passed**: `[context: forensics...]` staged into the next prompt.
- Leg 3 **failed twice over**: see F1 and F2.

Evidence: I diffed the forensics directory before/after and read the record.

### 7. Codex reasoning after a tool call — repro only

**This is not acceptance.** 6ze7 was never fixed: the assigned agent stopped
before editing because uncommitted changes had appeared in its target files.
Those changes are now committed and the tree is clean, so the blocker is gone —
and its claim is 1244m old, well past the 480m abandoned threshold, so it is
takeable. I want fresh evidence at current HEAD before anyone writes the fix,
because `faf8cbf` since touched the same renderer.

Steps:

> Fresh instance, codex session. Send a prompt that forces a tool call followed
> by reasoning and prose — e.g. *"read /home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md and
> then explain in three paragraphs what its actor rules are for"* (absolute path
> on purpose, so it does not burn a search first).
> When the answer lands, look at the reasoning region and the prose after it.

Expect (if it has silently healed): one `[thinking]` header for the contiguous
reasoning run, and the answer streaming as normal prose.

Failure signature (the filed bug): several consecutive `[thinking]` headers
where there should be one, and the answer split one word/fragment per line with
blank lines between.

**Result (2026-08-27): does not reproduce.**

Attempt 1, `codex/01a040fc-493c-75e1-89a5-9c494fc67d39`, missed the trigger — my
prompt gave codex nothing to reason about after the tool result, so the only
thought frames arrived *before* the tool call. Useful negative only: 203 post-tool
message chunks with no fragmentation.

Attempt 2, `codex/01a04106-62aa-71e1-a127-82a02a8be68f`, hit it exactly:

```
tool_call             lines 34-35  (completed)
agent_thought_chunk   x2  lines 38-39
tool_call             lines 40-41  (completed)
agent_thought_chunk   x4  lines 44-47   <- the recorded trigger
agent_message_chunk   x183 lines 48-230
```

Thought-chunk text lengths at 44-47 are **2, 43, 2, 40**; the bug's own recorded
frames at its lines 60-63 were **2, 45, 2, 50** — same count, same alternating
2/N pattern, same position immediately after a completed tool call. The buffer
showed one `[thinking]` header and readable prose.

Caveat kept deliberately: one non-reproduction at HEAD is not a proven fix, and
**no regression test pins this shape**. Recorded on the issue; the close/pin
decision is the maintainer's.

## Evidence check

Breadcrumb state, pinned by session id rather than mtime:

```
stat -c '%a %s %y' ~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/abandoned.json 2>&1
python3 -m json.tool < ~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/abandoned.json 2>&1
```

Pass conditions: mode `600`; `acp_session_id` matches the instance you just
quit; `turn_active`/`staged` match what you actually had open. Absence of the
file after a setup is the pass condition for case 1.

Codex reasoning frames for case 7 (substitute your session id):

```
grep -c '"sessionUpdate":"agent_thought_chunk"' \
  ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/<ID>/log.jsonl
```

What this cannot prove: the frame count tells me what the *peer sent*, not how
the buffer rendered it. The rendering half of case 7 rests on what you see, so
describe the buffer, or tell me the buffer number and I will read it live.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/abandoned.json` — delete if a case leaves a
  stale one behind.
- Forensics records written by case 6 under
  `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/`.
- This file: becomes a `qa-round` bead, then deleted. Never committed.

## Reporting back

Tell me the case number, the ACP session id, what you saw, and anything
surprising. I pull the evidence myself before agreeing or disagreeing with your
reading. If I commit a fix, you re-run Setup before retesting and I will say
which cases to redo.

## Findings this round

**F1 — `:LouiselmForensicsView` refuses a bare invocation with a raw `E471`**
(`louiselm-h65x`, filed, not fixed).
Registered `nargs = 1` (`ui/chat/command.lua:560`), so Neovim rejects the bare
call before the callback runs — which makes the callback's own
`if path == "" then report_error("Forensics record path is required")` guard
(`command.lua:541-545`) unreachable dead code that can never deliver its friendly
error. The only place the 40-char generated path appears is a transient INFO
toast from `:LouiselmForensics`, unrecoverable under snacks.notifier. Fix
direction: `nargs = "?"` defaulting to the last record, which makes the existing
branch live. Missed because the prior round (`louiselm-wnpd` case 5) supplied the
path explicitly and never tried the bare form.

**F2 — the "human projection" is a JSON pager** (recorded on `louiselm-ce6.24`,
not filed separately).
`:LouiselmForensicsView` is `readfile` + `nvim_buf_set_lines` + `filetype="json"`
(`command.lua:546-560`): no rendered identity, no chronology, no marking of
missing or sensitive sources. ce6.24 user story 4 is unimplemented. Deliberately
**not** a new bead — it is ce6.24's own declared remaining acceptance, and a
duplicate would be noise. Also flagged there that `wnpd` case 5's "view passed"
covered readability, not projection, so it should not be read as prior
acceptance.


## Round summary (closed 2026-08-27)

Seven cases run, six behaviours accepted, two findings, one non-reproduction.

**Accepted and closed: louiselm-ce6.34** (P1). All three reachable refusal
clauses, the accepted residual, the `:qa` escape and the breadcrumb trail
verified live. Clause 1 (Agent without ACP `loadSession`) was unreachable — every
agent exercised advertises it — and stays unit-tested. Closed in `e0d27d8`.

**Still open: louiselm-ce6.24** (P3). Collection, targeting and resource-link
queueing accepted; the human projection is not implemented (F2). Comment added,
issue left open and unclaimed.

**Filed: louiselm-h65x** (P3, F1). Not fixed this round.

**Not reproducing: louiselm-6ze7** (P1). Trigger matched on the wire, symptoms
absent, but no code change was ever made against it and no regression test pins
the shape. Evidence recorded; close-or-pin left to the maintainer.

**Dropped, not deferred: louiselm-zufj.** Acceptance needs a live Copilot
Autopilot `task_complete` and premium quota is unavailable until ≈2026-09-01.

### Why the suite missed each finding

- **F1** — the prior round (`louiselm-wnpd` case 5) supplied the record path
  explicitly, so the bare invocation was never exercised. The unreachable
  `path == ""` branch also makes the code *read* as though the no-argument case
  is handled, which is how it survived review. Nothing in the suite invokes an Ex
  command the way a user first types it.
- **F2** — no test asserts what the view buffer *contains*, only that it opens.
  A JSON pager and a rendered projection are indistinguishable to a test that
  checks for a non-empty buffer.

### Leftovers

- `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/1787796219-1787796219-265777660586430.json`
  — the record from case 6, left in place as F1/F2 evidence.
- One breadcrumb may exist at `~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/abandoned.json` from
  the final case; harmless, consumed on next start.
- Two predictions refuted (breadcrumb non-delivery; stray split after refusal)
  and one confirmed-but-by-design (breadcrumb on a clean exit). None filed.
close_reason: Round complete: 7 cases, ce6.34 accepted and closed, 2 findings routed, 6ze7 non-reproduction evidenced
