comments.text: Implemented TRADEMARK_POLICY.md and linked it from README.md. The 317-word policy reserves the LouiseLM marks, permits truthful reference and derived-from attribution, requires forks to use their own identity, states the structural majority-revenue class refusal without naming companies, and explicitly preserves identical software-licence rights for the refused class. Verification: git diff --check passed; Markdown targets exist; no named company appears in the policy.

title: Grok prompts appear twice after pressing Enter
description:
When using the Grok ACP agent from LouiseLM, submitting a prompt with Enter can render the same user prompt twice in the chat buffer. The issue was reported against session grok/01a0562e-62af-7bf1-b3bb-452b60d9423f on 2026-08-31. The duplicate is visible at the user-facing chat boundary; the prompt is still sent, so this is degraded UI/transcript behavior rather than a failed turn.

## Observed

The referenced Grok session is stored at ~/.grok/sessions/%2Fhome%2Flotso%2Fdotfiles/01a0562e-62af-7bf1-b3bb-452b60d9423f. Its updates.jsonl contains user_message_chunk events for the submitted messages. Reproduction was observed while typing a prompt in LouiseLM and pressing Enter; the exact LouiseLM ACP proxy log for that turn is not yet captured.

## Symptoms

- The typed prompt appears twice after Enter in the LouiseLM chat buffer when the selected agent is Grok.
- The agent continues processing the turn.
- Other configured ACP agents do not currently show the same behavior, according to the report.

## Root cause

Unknown. Two concrete paths can both render user text: chat/init.lua submit_prompt records and inserts the locally submitted prompt at lines 1912-1928, while lifecycle.lua emits user_chunk for ACP user_message_chunk at lines 317-320 and chat/init.lua inserts that event at lines 2299-2320. lifecycle.lua currently assumes user_message_chunk is only session/load replay and that a live prompt is never echoed. Grok may be emitting user_message_chunk for a live session, or the duplication may be in another adapter/UI path. Capture the raw ACP proxy log while reproducing to distinguish those cases.

## Why it was not caught

Existing chat tests cover local submission and replay separately, but there is no Grok-backed regression fixture asserting that a live submitted prompt plus a user_message_chunk for the same turn is rendered once.

## Fix direction

Reproduce with Grok routed through acp-proxy and inspect the raw JSON-RPC log. If Grok echoes the live prompt, deduplicate at the session/UI boundary using the turn and text provenance while preserving replay rendering. Do not suppress legitimate user_message_chunk events during session/load replay.

## Acceptance

- A regression test reproduces the duplicate before the fix and passes after it.
- A live Grok prompt renders exactly once after Enter.
- Resumed-session user history still renders correctly.
- Raw ACP/proxy evidence identifies whether the duplicate originates in Grok or LouiseLM.

## Not covered

The referenced standalone Grok session log shows normal user_message_chunk records but does not by itself prove a duplicate LouiseLM render. No fix is included in this filing.
close_reason: Fixed in 4058bc9. Live acceptance: Grok/Codex/Claude/OpenCode each rendered one prompt; Grok replay rendered user then agent once. Related louiselm-tw9d fixed in b9f2c82. Evidence/lessons: comments, regression, QA round louiselm-lfwb; no AGENTS.md change.

title: Comment in-progress-first triage requirement onto workflow-engine issues
description:
Attach the in-progress-first triage requirement to the deferred workflow-engine issues as `br` comments, so it is discoverable from the issues themselves rather than from a conversation transcript.

## The requirement

When a workflow engine sequences beads work on the operator's behalf, it should default to draining in-progress or claimed work before opening new work, even when a scoring pass ranks an unstarted item higher. That is what a human operator does by hand, and it is the behaviour the current tooling cannot express.

## The evidence behind it

`bv`'s triage score is a weighted sum across eight components. Urgency (weight 0.1) already rewards in-progress work — raw 1.0 for `in_progress` against 0.8 for `open` — but it is one component among eight, and a fresh `open` task carrying a real `blocks` edge (BlockerRatio, weight 0.13) plus a deeper unlock chain (TimeToImpact, weight 0.1) out-scores an in-progress epic comfortably. Observed in this repo: roughly 0.459 against 0.405.

None of the five built-in weight presets fix it. `priority-first` raises Urgency only to about 0.146, still not a gate, and there is no custom-weights file. So the preference cannot be extracted from `bv` by configuration — it has to be applied on top of its output, which is exactly why it belongs in the engine that consumes that output.

## Where it goes

Comment on the deferred workflow-engine issues — the ones covering persisted declarative workflows and sequential execution of beads graphs by policy-controlled agents. Both sit under the attention-control-plane epic.

Frame it as a **candidate requirement for that design conversation, not a decision already made.** The sequencing policy is the engine's to define; this records why the question exists and what the evidence was.

## Acceptance criteria

- Both relevant deferred issues carry a comment stating the requirement and the scoring evidence.
- The comment is explicit that this is input to a future design decision rather than a settled one.
- `br sync --flush-only` has been run so the comments reach JSONL and are committed.
