title: QA round: replayed user prompts on resume
description:
# Manual QA review — replayed user prompts on resume

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `110e357` (fix), on top of the permission-decision round
verified at `7d115d7`. `0dcdce5` (beads bookkeeping only) needs no testing.

Origin: `louiselm-pmr` — after `:LouiselmResume`, the chat showed the agent's
replies and tool calls from the prior conversation but silently dropped every
prompt the user had typed, so a resumed session read as one-sided. Root cause:
`lifecycle.lua` already turned the ACP `user_message_chunk` replay notification
into a `user_chunk` event (since `4e4a58b`), but `chat/init.lua`'s
`handle_event` never had a branch for it and dropped it on the floor. `110e357`
adds that branch, rendering each line prefixed `> `.

The unit test in `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` proves the rendering logic against a
synthetic `fake_session` emitting a synthetic `user_chunk` event. It cannot
prove that a real adapter's replay actually looks like that, and it cannot
prove a *live* turn doesn't now render the user's prompt twice — both of
those only exist once a real `claude-agent-acp` process is in the loop.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Real resume replays user prompts in order, interleaved with tool calls | **passed** — log + visual, see below |
| 2 | Live turn still renders the submitted prompt exactly once | **passed** — log + visual, see below |

## Setup

The plugin is installed as a clone of this repo, so new commits are not live
until you update it:

```vim
:lua vim.pack.update({ 'louiselm.nvim' })
```

Confirm the clone matches the source, then restart nvim:

```bash
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim log --oneline -1
git -C ~/code/louiselm log --oneline -1
```

Both must print `110e357 fix(chat): show replayed user prompts`.

## Ground rules learned the hard way (carried over from prior rounds)

- Say the tool name and give absolute paths in prompts, or the model reaches
  for the wrong tool / does a `find` first and you burn a round trip.
- Start each case in a fresh session — a prior denial or detour in the same
  session makes the model hedge on the next one.
- Pin the adapter log by session id, not by mtime — the newest log file is
  whatever session you're talking to me in right now:
  ```bash
  L=$(grep -l "<session-uuid>" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*jsonrpc.log | tail -1)
  ```
  The session id is in the chat header, or via `:LouiselmSessionId`.
- **That grep pollutes itself.** If *I* run it to pull evidence, my own bash
  command containing the session id gets logged into whatever log file is
  currently open for *this* conversation — `tail -1` then picks my own
  self-reference instead of the real target log. Fix: search all matching
  files, not just the last one, and eyeball which one actually has protocol
  content (`session/update` with real `sessionUpdate` kinds) rather than a
  `rawInput`/`toolCallId` echo of the grep command itself. Hit this pulling
  evidence for case 1.

## Cases

### 1. Real resume replays user prompts in order, interleaved with tool calls

Exercises `110e357` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1305` against a real
`claude-agent-acp` replay, which is the exact shape the original bug report
had: two user turns with agent activity (including a tool call) between them.

Steps:

1. Start a **fresh** session in this repo.
2. Send: `Use the Read tool, not Bash, to read /home/lotso/code/louiselm/AGENTS.md, then reply with just the word "ack".`
3. Once it replies, send a second prompt: `Now reply with just the word "ack2".`
4. Note the session id (`:LouiselmSessionId`), then `:LouiselmCloseSession`.
5. `:LouiselmResume` and pick that session.

Expect: the buffer shows, in original order: `> Use the Read tool...`, the
tool call line for the Read, the assistant's `ack`, `> Now reply...`, the
assistant's `ack2` — both prompts visible, prefixed `> `, in the order they
were actually sent, not collapsed or reordered relative to the tool call.

Failure signature: either prompt missing from the replay, both prompts shown
adjacent to each other instead of interleaved with the reply/tool call, or
prompt text without the `> ` prefix (i.e. the old "renders replayed assistant
chunks" behavior, meaning the fix didn't ship).

**Result: passed.** Session `claude/7daa1bda-d26a-4ad3-a7da-b44bf00d78f0`,
user reported the buffer looked right. Log evidence from
`20260820-172713-1011506-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log` (the resume,
2 minutes after the original turn) confirms the wire order matches exactly
what case 1 predicted:

```
user_message_chunk "[@AGENTS.md](...)"
user_message_chunk "Use the Read tool, not Bash, to read ... ack"
tool_call Read AGENTS.md (pending)
tool_call_update (completed)
agent_message_chunk "ack"
user_message_chunk "Now reply with just the word \"ack2\"."
agent_message_chunk "ack2"
```

Both prompts present, correctly interleaved around the Read tool call, in
original order. Combined with the user's visual read of the buffer, this
closes the "does a real adapter's replay actually look like the synthetic
unit-test fixture" question the unit test structurally can't answer.

### 2. Live turn still renders the submitted prompt exactly once

Exercises the regression the bead flagged as unverified: `handle_event` now
has a branch for `user_chunk`, so this checks a *live* `claude-agent-acp` turn
never also emits `user_message_chunk` (which `submit_prompt` already writes
into the buffer directly — a second write would duplicate it).

Steps:

1. In any session (resumed or fresh), submit: `Reply with just the word "once".`

Expect: the prompt line `> Reply with just the word "once".` appears exactly
once in the buffer, followed by exactly one `once` response.

Failure signature: the prompt text appears twice (once from `submit_prompt`,
once from a `user_chunk` event the live turn shouldn't have produced).

**Result: passed.** User ran this in the same resumed session
(`claude/7daa1bda-d26a-4ad3-a7da-b44bf00d78f0`, reusing the adapter process
from case 1) and confirmed the buffer looked right. Log evidence from the
same `20260820-172713-1011506-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log`, appended
after the case-1 replay (lines 9-17, the live "once" turn): `agent_message_chunk
'once'` and nothing else — no `user_message_chunk` for the "once" prompt.
Grand total `user_message_chunk` count for the whole file stayed at 3 (the two
replayed prompts plus the AGENTS.md attachment chunk from case 1's replay),
confirming the live turn added zero. That's the precondition for a duplicate
being structurally absent, matching what case 1's earlier partial evidence
(the pre-resume live log) already suggested — now confirmed end-to-end with
both the wire log and the user's own read of the buffer.

## Evidence check

```bash
L=$(grep -l "<session-uuid>" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*jsonrpc.log | tail -1)
grep -c '"user_message_chunk"' "$L"
```

For case 1: confirms the real adapter did send `user_message_chunk` during
replay (proves the fixture actually exercised the code path) — cross-check
against what the buffer shows, since the log doesn't tell you what got
*rendered*, only what the agent sent.

For case 2: on the resumed-session log, count should be ≥1 (replay only); on
a fresh live-turn log, count should be 0 outside any resume. Grep alone can't
prove the buffer's dedup — that's the visual check in the steps above.

## Cleanup when the round closes

No fixtures left in the repo (no files written). Nothing to revert.

## Reporting back

Send me which case, what you saw in the buffer, and the session id so I can
pull the log myself. If something's wrong I'll fix it and you'll need to redo
Setup before retesting.

## Findings this round

None yet.
close_reason: Completed QA round: both real-adapter manual cases passed (resume replay preserves/interleaves user prompts; live prompt renders once), protocol-log and human visual evidence are recorded in the bead, and tests/ui/chat_spec.lua passes 74/74.

title: Provenance
description: The lineage of a change across commits, Beads issues and Sessions: which Session produced a commit, which issue that commit served, and which Sessions worked an issue. Provenance is derived on demand from git trailers, Beads actor fields and bvr correlation; it stores nothing of its own and has no durable record.
design: Established with explicit maintainer confirmation on 2026-08-26 while settling louiselm-06yh Door B. Introduced as a distinct term rather than widening Forensics, because Forensics derives its safety properties from being scoped to exactly one subject Session, and because the two differ in lifecycle: Forensics is a stored immutable record, Provenance is a derived query.
notes: Use Provenance for the derived commit/issue/Session lineage and for views over it. Avoid: history, archaeology, audit trail. Distinguish from Forensics, which is a durable immutable record indexing evidence for exactly one subject Session; Provenance is recomputed per query, spans entities, and persists nothing.

title: Flaky test: mock agent commands asserted before the session/update notification lands
description:
`tests/mock/agent_spec.lua:171` fails intermittently. Measured at HEAD (6819fe6) with the working tree stashed, so this predates the workflow/phase and workflow/routing work: **4 failures in 12 consecutive runs** of that file alone.

## Evidence

```
FAIL in tests/mock/agent_spec.lua | mock agent | advertises commands through session/update and delivers them on the session:
  Failed expectation for equality
  Cause: different values at key 1, left = nil, right = { description = "Stress-test an idea", name = "grill-me" }
  Left:  {}
  Right: { { description = "Stress-test an idea", name = "grill-me" } }
  Traceback:
    tests/mock/agent_spec.lua:171
```

Reproduce:

```sh
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  nvim --headless --noplugin -u ./tests/minimal_init.lua \
    -c 'lua MiniTest.run_file("tests/mock/agent_spec.lua")' -c 'qa!' 2>&1 \
    | tr '\r' '\n' | grep -oE "Fails \([0-9]+\)" | head -1
done
```

## Cause

The test waits for the wrong signal. `wait_for` at `tests/mock/agent_spec.lua:167-169` blocks until the `create_session` callback has set `ready`, and line 171 then asserts on `session:inspect().commands` immediately.

But `availableCommands` do not arrive on the `session/new` result. They arrive on a separate `session/update` notification, handled at `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:227-237`-adjacent notification dispatch and validated by `Validation.available_commands` (`lua/louiselm/session/validation.lua:251-275`). Session creation completing does not imply that notification has been read off the transport and dispatched, so `state.commands` is still `{}` whenever the assertion wins the race.

The very next block (`tests/mock/agent_spec.lua:173-177`) scans `events` for a `commands_changed` event, which is the signal the assertion at line 171 should have waited for.

## Fix direction

Wait for the observable that the assertion actually depends on — a `commands_changed` event, or `#session:inspect().commands > 0` — rather than for session readiness. Do not add a sleep.

This is the failure mode AGENTS.md calls out directly: "Async tests must model the production callback context, not only invoke the callback synchronously." A notification-delivered field asserted on a creation-completed signal is the same class of defect.

## Scope note

Found while working louiselm-3s0l.2; not fixed there, because the defect is unrelated to routing and the surrounding mock/session test file has its own owner. Filed rather than repaired so the evidence survives.
close_reason: Wait for commands_changed before asserting session commands; focused test passes 12 consecutive runs and full suite passes 441 cases.

comments.author: codex/01a02f31-c7f1-7d13-8925-697c9ed5bc79
comments.text: Fixed the race in tests/mock/agent_spec.lua by waiting for the commands_changed event before inspecting session.commands. The focused file passes 12 consecutive runs; full suite passes all 441 cases. stylua and lua-language-server are clean.

title: Grok ACP session enters Error after successful prompt
description:
A Grok ACP Session can enter LouiseLM Error after a prompt has already completed successfully, making the completed turn look failed and preventing continued use of that Session.

## Observed

- Session: grok/01a05644-1efe-7d11-92f5-482a60f7f624
- Date: 2026-08-31
- Build: 4058bc9
- Proxy log: ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a05644-1efe-7d11-92f5-482a60f7f624/log.jsonl
- The prompt completed at 2026-08-31T05:21:55.988Z with `_x.ai/session/prompt_complete`, `stopReason=end_turn`; the result frame had `id=3` and `result.stopReason=end_turn`.
- The same log ends at 2026-08-31T05:22:45.833Z with `direction=internal`, `kind=exit`, `payload.code=137`.

## Symptoms

- User reports the Session later changed to Error after Case 1 initially appeared to pass.
- The ACP prompt result was successful before the process exit.

## Root cause

Unknown. The evidence proves a process exit with code 137 after successful prompt completion, but does not distinguish an external kill/OOM condition from acp-proxy or Grok shutdown behavior. Inspect process/proxy stderr and reproduce with a fresh pinned run to discriminate. Relevant LouiseLM error handling begins in lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua around process-exit handling.

## Why it was not caught

The manual case stopped at prompt completion and checked only the immediate wire result/UI. It did not keep the Session observed through the post-turn process lifetime. Automated tests use an in-memory process double and do not model a real Grok process exiting after a successful prompt.

## Fix direction

Capture the full proxy stderr/process lifecycle for Grok and determine why code 137 occurs. If the Agent process is expected to remain alive, keep a completed Session usable and report only a genuine transport failure; if code 137 is an intentional Grok shutdown, LouiseLM must distinguish normal shutdown from failure. Do not alter generic exit handling until the cause is known.

## Acceptance

- Regression coverage captures the real post-completion exit ordering.
- A completed Grok prompt does not turn its Session into Error when the exit is an expected/benign shutdown.
- If the exit is abnormal, the UI reports a specific actionable cause and the reproduction is stable.

## Not covered

Other adapters, long-lived Grok Sessions, and whether the exit is caused by host resource pressure were not tested.
close_reason: Fixed in b9f2c82: ignore uncorrelated ACP responses. Maintainer pass grok/01a05659-34a0-7b30-b130-975c93102c21: prompt complete log lines 70/72; skills-reload lines 76/77; no exit. Tests: ACP 6/6, full 800/800; StyLua, LuaLS, API appendix pass. Lesson routed to comment #601 and regression; no AGENTS.md change warranted.

comments.author: codex/01a053e2-ec44-7692-aaf7-966e27be8b9c
comments.text: Investigation (2026-08-31): generic handle_exit at lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:556-570 correctly marks any live non-disposal process exit as error; returning ready would leave a dead ACP transport unusable. Controlled grok agent stdio probe: stdin EOF exits code 0; session/new under the sandbox returned FS_OTHER due read-only cwd, but the process stayed alive until EOF. Historical Grok run had clean end_turn/prompt_complete then internal proxy exit code 137, so this is SIGKILL-equivalent, not normal ACP shutdown. Cause remains unknown (host kill, proxy disposal, or Grok crash); no safe LouiseLM fix yet.

comments.author: codex/01a053e2-ec44-7692-aaf7-966e27be8b9c
comments.text: Root cause and fix (2026-08-31): the exit 137 was an effect, not the trigger. The Grok trace emitted an unsolicited JSON-RPC response id=skills-reload immediately before Error. lua/louiselm/acp/init.lua treated any response without a locally pending id as fatal; fail() closed acp-proxy, whose SIGTERM handler killed Grok and logged 137. Red: tests/acp/init_spec.lua failed with received response for unknown request id. Fix: ignore uncorrelated responses at the ACP client boundary; normal correlated responses, malformed frames, and transport errors remain unchanged. Live acceptance Session 01a05654-dfd6-7981-897b-280a5a34a494: /tmp/tw9d-probe-state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/<id>/log.jsonl lines 61-62 emitted two skills-reload responses; line 63 refreshed commands with tw9d-reload-probe; Session remained ready 30s after prompt completion. Gates: focused 6/6; full 800/800 with XDG_STATE_HOME under /tmp; stylua, lua-language-server, API appendix, git diff --check pass. Keep open for maintainer UI confirmation per live-acceptance policy.

title: Single-line tool captions run to thousands of characters and overflow rendered excerpts
description:
Once louiselm-cmr made the `<sub>` caption a single line, that line could be
enormous: the longest in a real 156-tool-call export was 7319 characters, with
6963 and 6490 behind it. Correct, and useless as a label — and actively harmful
downstream, since the blog pipeline renders excerpts of these exports through
`:TOhtml` into an iframe whose width the theme fixes and does not expose.

Filed during the QA round covering `ec19281..HEAD` rather than before the fix:
louiselm-cmr's close reason recorded this as deliberately deferred presentation
work, and the tester elected to take it immediately when the measured caption
lengths arrived. The evidence below is from the verified post-fix export.

## Observed

`/home/lotso/code/louiselm/louiselm-session-1-20260820-062145.md`, exported on
build `a6484ea`, 6384 lines, 156 tool calls:

```
longest <sub> caption lengths, characters: 7319, 6963, 6490
```

Captions of that length are whole `br create --description "$(cat <<'EOF' ...`
invocations with the entire bead body inlined.

## Symptoms

- A caption that is a wall of text rather than a label.
- In a `<pre>` rendered by TOhtml, one physical line 7319 characters wide,
  overflowing horizontally inside a fixed-width iframe.

## Root cause

Not a defect in the collapsing itself. `render_entry`
(`lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua`) interpolated the full normalized title
into the caption with no length bound, because the title's natural size is the
size of a shell command.

## Fix direction

Bound the caption; keep the payload whole. The untruncated title is already a
few lines below inside `<details>`, which is what that block is for.

Rejected: wrapping the caption across lines. That re-creates exactly the
multi-line `<sub>` element louiselm-cmr just removed.

## Acceptance

- Caption truncated at a fixed character count with an ellipsis.
- Truncation counts characters, not bytes: real titles contain em dashes and
  other multi-byte characters, and a byte-wise cut would emit invalid UTF-8.
- The full title still appears in the `<details>` payload dump.
- A title exactly at the limit is left untouched.

## Not covered

- The limit is a judgement, not a measurement; 120 characters is chosen to fit
  a conventional terminal width, not derived from the theme's iframe width.
close_reason: Fixed in 3d6557d. render_entry now passes the normalized title through truncate(), which cuts at CAPTION_TITLE_LIMIT=120 using vim.fn.strchars/strcharpart so multi-byte characters are never split, and appends an ellipsis. Tests: 'truncates an overlong title in the caption but keeps it whole in the payload' (400 x's -> 120 + ellipsis in the caption, full 400 still present in the <details> dump), 'truncates on character boundaries, not bytes' (400 e-acutes), 'leaves a title at the limit untouched' (exactly 120, no ellipsis). First two confirmed red before the fix; the third was green already and is a boundary guard against an off-by-one. Gates: mini.test 0 fails/0 notes across the full suite, stylua clean on both changed files, lua-language-server unchanged at 9 pre-existing problems all in blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua. No deviation from the filed acceptance criteria. Tester re-export verification still pending.

title: Grill-me needed: How should LouiseLM show Codex usage limits to users?
description:
Do not resolve this design question in passing. Facilitate a dedicated decision about how LouiseLM presents Codex usage limits to users.

Question:
What user-facing representation should LouiseLM use for Codex usage limits, including multiple windows/buckets, remaining percentage, reset timing, plan information, credits, stale/loading/error states, and change notifications?

Evidence from shared conversation:
- Source: https://chatgpt.com/share/6a8bde60-0154-83eb-bea8-9389d85a2149
- The supported integration surface identified is the Codex App Server JSON-RPC method `account/rateLimits/read`, with `account/rateLimits/updated` notifications.
- The result exposes `usedPercent`, `windowDurationMins`, `resetsAt`, `planType`, and possibly `rateLimitResetCredits` and additional/model-specific buckets.
- `usedPercent` is consumed usage, while the UI needs to decide whether to show remaining usage (`100 - usedPercent`), consumed usage, or both.
- Window meaning must come from `windowDurationMins`; do not assume primary means five hours or secondary means weekly.
- The private `GET https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/usage` endpoint exists behind the ChatGPT UI, but should not be used as LouiseLM’s integration contract; HTML scraping is overkill and brittle.

Threads worth pulling:
- Which buckets belong in the default view, and how should arbitrary/additional buckets be labeled?
- Should the primary metric be remaining percentage, used percentage, absolute counts/credits, reset-at time, or a combination?
- How should weekly and shorter windows be made understandable without hard-coded names?
- Where should this appear in the Neovim UI, and should it be on-demand, persistent, or both?
- How should live updates, sparse/partial notifications, stale data, unavailable auth, malformed data, and app-server errors be communicated?
- What behavior is safe when no limits are returned or when credits are present?
- Which exact observable contract should tests and typed events enforce?

Decision boundary:
Choose the presentation and state semantics only. Keep the supported App Server transport and protocol choice as established evidence unless new evidence shows it cannot support the chosen UX.
close_reason: Human UX presentation and state semantics decided with maintainer confirmation; implementation boundary routed separately.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: 2026-08-24 investigation: Official Codex App Server docs define account/rateLimits/read plus account/rateLimits/updated. The result can carry a legacy rateLimits bucket and rateLimitsByLimitId; buckets may have absent labels, optional primary/secondary windows, plan type, credits, and reset-credit metadata. Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server. A sanitized probe against installed codex-cli 0.144.3 returned both legacy data and one codex multi-bucket entry: unlabeled, primary 10080-minute window, no secondary window, with plan/credits and reset-credit metadata. No percentages, timestamps, or account identity were retained. Architectural boundary: installed @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.6.2 receives account/rateLimits/updated and caches structured buckets internally, but exposes them only as rendered /status text; it does not emit a structured ACP session update. Therefore limits are account/Agent state, not LouiseLM Session telemetry, and implementation needs a structured adapter boundary rather than parsing /status text or duplicating a direct provider process inside every Session.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: Grill direction from maintainer: treat human UX and agent experience (AX, including AGENTS.md conventions) as two distinct formats/contracts. Resolve UX first; revisit AX later. Primary human motivation is deciding whether to continue/cancel work as limits approach. Design implication under canonical vocabulary: a user cancels a running turn or refrains from the next prompt; the Session remains resumable. Moving work to another Agent is a Handoff that creates another Session. Current UX recommendation: an always-visible compact decision signal plus an on-demand detailed view, rather than warning-only display. Human questions to answer: whether it is safe to start/continue a task; which Agent to choose or hand off to; when work can resume after reset; whether a failure is quota-related; and whether a reset credit or workspace-owner action is available. Do not estimate remaining prompts because usage cost varies by task/model and the protocol does not provide that forecast.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: UX decision accepted: emit at most one human notification per quota window/reset cycle when remaining capacity crosses 20 percent, then 10 percent, then when the server classifies the limit as reached. Each notification identifies the Agent, affected window, remaining capacity, and reset timing. The UX must not automatically cancel a turn or initiate a Handoff.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: UX state policy accepted: initial fetch is loading; fresh data renders normally; refresh failure preserves the last good snapshot with visible staleness age; passing a reset timestamp without a confirmed refresh also makes the snapshot stale rather than synthesizing a reset. Initial failure is unavailable with details. A successful empty result is no limit data, never unlimited; unlimited is displayed only from an explicit upstream value. Valid sparse updates merge into the snapshot. Malformed updates are rejected, the last good snapshot is preserved and marked stale. Stale data never triggers threshold notifications. Agents without the capability omit the compact segment and explain unsupported in the detailed view; unexpected failures from supporting Agents remain visible.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: UX bucket/window policy accepted: deduplicate the legacy bucket against rateLimitsByLimitId by limitId and treat its matching entry as the default bucket. Prefer non-empty upstream limitName; otherwise render the exact limitId without invented semantics. Derive window labels from exact windowDurationMins and never expose primary/secondary as meanings. Sort windows shortest to longest. The normal winbar shows default-bucket windows; a low, critical, or reached additional bucket takes precedence. Show at most two windows plus +N in the winbar; detailed view shows all. Winbar reset timing is relative; detail includes relative and local absolute time. Render whole remaining percentages, except positive values below one percent render as <1%.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: UX interaction scope accepted: :LouiselmLimits shows the active Agent, :LouiselmLimits <agent> inspects another configured Agent, and clicking the winbar segment opens the same detail view. Opening refreshes only through an already-live Agent connection; it never starts an Agent merely to fetch limits. Otherwise show last-known or not observed. Detail shows reset-credit count and expiry, and reached state advertises reset availability. The first UX is read-only: no credit consumption, owner email, turn cancellation, or Handoff.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text: Final UX contract: account limits are shared Agent-level state with two human formats: an always-visible decision-oriented winbar segment and a read-only :LouiselmLimits [agent] detail view. Remaining capacity is primary; detail also shows used capacity, exact-duration window labels, relative and absolute reset timing, plan, credits, freshness and errors. Notifications occur once per reset cycle at 20 percent, 10 percent and reached. The accepted state, bucket, ordering and interaction semantics are recorded in comments 268-271. AX is explicitly deferred and now has canonical vocabulary record louiselm-y3f3. Lesson routing: issue-local protocol and adapter evidence stays on this issue; the pure-ACP integration conflict is routed to a separate needs-design question. No additional standing AGENTS.md rule is warranted.

title: LouiselmInbox crashes when a capture has a null transcript
description:
Opening `:LouiselmInbox` crashes instead of showing the durable capture inbox when a listed capture has a null transcript. This blocks operators from inspecting captures through the inbox command.

## Observed

Reported 2026-08-21 in a Neovim runtime loading `louiselm.nvim`; no reproducible capture-service payload or session identifier was available.

```text
vim.schedule callback: .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:74: attempt to index field 'transcript' (a userdata value)
stack traceback:
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:74: in function 'inbox_lines'
        .../core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:132: in function 'callback'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/init.lua:108: in function 'complete'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/init.lua:137: in function <...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/capture/init.lua:123>
```

## Symptoms

- Running `:LouiselmInbox` raises a scheduled-callback error rather than opening the inbox.
- Neovim reports `attempt to index field 'transcript' (a userdata value)`.

## Root cause

Confirmed at `lua/louiselm/capture/command.lua:74`: `inbox_lines` checks only `capture.transcript ~= nil` before indexing `.text`. The traceback proves that this field can instead be userdata, which cannot be indexed. The source representation that produces that userdata (likely a decoded null) is unverified without the capture-service response.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/capture_spec.lua:171` checks only that `LouiselmInbox` is registered. It does not exercise inbox rendering with a capture whose `transcript` is a non-table null/userdata value.

## Fix direction

At the narrowest validated capture-service boundary, normalize or reject a non-table `transcript`; preserve the inbox renderer's absent-transcript behavior. Add a renderer/command regression test using the actual Neovim decoded-null representation. A simple non-nil guard is insufficient because userdata is truthy.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after for a listed capture whose `transcript` is the decoded-null/userdata value.
- `:LouiselmInbox` opens and renders that capture without a Lua error; it omits transcript text and may show the existing transcription error when present.

## Not covered

- The exact capture-service JSON payload and whether every null-capable field needs the same boundary validation are unverified.
- No fix is included in this report.
close_reason: Fixed in 35e7927. Inbox rendering now requires a table transcript with string text, so Neovim JSON null (userdata) follows the existing absent-transcript path. Regression: tests/capture_spec.lua commands opens inbox when a capture transcript is null. Gates: full MiniTest suite (322 cases), stylua --check ., lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning.

title: Physical mouse click on Session winbar source does nothing
description:
## Observed

During manual QA of build `60724f3`, in Agent Session `claude/9efb19db-aa0b-4f45-8cab-18eab9d86937`, the winbar rendered an attention source entry:

`%#LouiselmStatusReady#Your turn%*%=%1@v:lua.require('louiselm.ui.chat.command').winbar_click@%#LouiselmStatusWarning#● source%*%X`

After `:set mouse=a`, physically clicking `● source` did nothing: the active Session did not change, the cursor did not move, and `:messages` remained empty. Physical clicks on ordinary buffer lines also did not move the cursor in that environment.

Calling `require('louiselm.ui.chat.command').winbar_click(1, 1, 'l', '')` directly selected the source Session correctly, so the Session target and handler path worked while physical mouse-event delivery did not.

## Impact and disposition

Low impact and non-blocking: keyboard/direct selection remains available. Do not fix as part of the current QA round; retain this finding for reproduction in a terminal/TUI environment where the physical input path can be isolated.

## Evidence

- Agent Session: `claude/9efb19db-aa0b-4f45-8cab-18eab9d86937`
- ACP log: `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/9efb19db-aa0b-4f45-8cab-18eab9d86937/log.jsonl`
- Manual QA Case 4
- No error or notification appeared
- Root cause remains unknown; evidence is consistent with terminal/TUI mouse delivery rather than the LouiseLM click handler itself
acceptance_criteria: With mouse support enabled in a supported terminal, physically clicking a Session entry in the winbar selects that Session exactly as keyboard selection and direct winbar_click invocation do; behavioral coverage distinguishes click-event delivery from direct handler invocation, or the unsupported environment is detected and communicated.
close_reason: Completed: routes clicked Winbar window correctly; live environment has no generic mouse delivery and is documented as unsupported.

comments.author: copilot/1b49919a-7bb3-4249-b781-f5e494348443
comments.text: Implemented the Winbar click boundary documented by Neovim: the command now resolves getmousepos().winid and Chat routes/focuses that clicked window before following its target. Regression coverage fails against current-window lookup and passes for a click originating in another window; command-level coverage verifies forwarding the mouse window. Full mini.test: 505/505; Stylua and lua-language-server pass. Live Ghostty acceptance remains pending a physical click, so this bug intentionally stays in_progress.

comments.author: copilot/1b49919a-7bb3-4249-b781-f5e494348443
comments.text: Additional acceptance evidence: a disposable Neovim 0.12.2 TUI under a controlling xterm-256color PTY with mouse=a received an injected SGR left-click on `%1@v:lua.Click@foo%X` and invoked Click as `{ 1, 1, "l", "    " }`. This proves native Winbar click dispatch; combined with the clicked-window regression, the implementation covers the observed boundary. Per live-acceptance policy, the issue remains open for maintainer confirmation in the running Ghostty Session.

comments.author: copilot/1b49919a-7bb3-4249-b781-f5e494348443
comments.text: Maintainer re-tested in the live Ghostty TUI after commit 437fbf0: physical Winbar click still does not switch, and ordinary buffer clicks likewise do not move the cursor. Live Neovim reports mouse=a and a stdio TUI with term_name=xterm-ghostty. Since generic buffer mouse delivery is absent, the terminal/input layer is unsupported for physical mouse interaction and the LouiseLM callback cannot be reached. Native SGR dispatch remains independently verified; keyboard/direct selection remains available.

title: Grill fold-based tool-call rendering UX
description:
## Question

Would native Neovim folds make LouiseLM's chronological tool-call timeline less cluttered without hiding active work, failures, or permission decisions?

## Scope

- Explore fold behavior separately for active versus completed calls.
- Decide whether adjacent calls should be grouped and what summary information remains visible.
- Cover failed calls, cancelled calls, permission prompts, nested/repeated calls, default open/closed state, discoverability, keyboard behavior, and mobile/narrow-window equivalents where relevant.
- Compare the proposal against the current one-line started-to-completed renderer.
- Prefer native Neovim behavior and the smallest viable design; do not assume a generic fold framework shared with prompt contexts.

## Desired Outcome

A grill-tested UX decision with concrete states, examples, accessibility/discoverability considerations, and—only if implementation is justified—small follow-up beads with acceptance criteria.

## Out of Scope

Implementing tool folds as part of the Agent Skills profile feature. This question has no dependency on that feature.
close_reason: Completed: grill decision recorded; louiselm-ufx.1 and louiselm-ufx.2 are closed and shipped.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text:
Grill-me session reached full agreement. Decision: fold-based rendering, scoped to within-turn clutter only.

- Fold unit = contiguous run of `completed` tool-call lines; any active, failed, or cancelled call breaks the run and is always rendered as a standalone visible line (never folded, never flagged-then-hidden).
- Trigger = superseded, mid-turn: a run folds the moment something follows it (new tool-call run, resumed assistant text, or `turn_done` as a force-close catch-all for a trailing run).
- Foldtext = Neovim default (first line + native line count), no custom renderer.
- Discoverability/keyboard = fully native (za/zo/zc/zR/zM), no new keymaps or foldcolumn.
- New fold state is separate from `context_folds` (different trigger/lifecycle) but mirrors its pattern (manual foldmethod, per-window tracking).
- Permission decisions are out of scope: they never render inline in the transcript today.
- Separately decided: live raw ACP payload access becomes on-demand only (not inline/folded) -- a new command/keymap on a `[tool]` line, decoupled from the fold mechanism.

Implementation split into louiselm-ufx.1 (fold rendering) and louiselm-ufx.2 (on-demand raw-payload inspector). Leaving this question open until both land -- br policy blocks closing a parent with open children, and that's the right call here since the decision is made but the work is not done.

title: Fold completed tool-call runs in the chat transcript
description:
## Goal
Reduce transcript clutter from many tool calls within one turn by folding contiguous runs of completed tool-call lines, using native Neovim folds.

## Scope
- In scope: new fold-tracking state in `louiselm.ui.chat` (separate from `context_folds`/`fold_counts`, same pattern: `foldmethod=manual`, `foldenable=true`, per-window fold-count tracking), applied in `handle_event`.
- A "run" is a contiguous stretch of tool-call lines whose terminal status is `completed` (see `lifecycle.lua:197`: `tool_call_finished` is only ever `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`).
- An active (started, not yet finished) or `failed`/`cancelled` call breaks the run and is never itself folded -- always a standalone visible line.
- Fold trigger is "superseded": a completed run folds the moment something follows it -- a new `tool_call_started` begins a new run, an assistant `chunk` resumes text, or `turn_done` fires (force-close catch-all so a trailing run is never left open across a turn boundary).
- Foldtext: Neovim's default only (first line of range + native line count). No custom `foldtext`.
- No new keymaps, no `foldcolumn` changes -- native `za`/`zo`/`zc`/`zR`/`zM` only.
- Out of scope: cross-session/history folding beyond one turn, folding or flagging failed/cancelled calls, any change to permission-decision UI, any inline raw-payload rendering (separate task).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A turn with 3+ consecutive `completed` tool calls followed by assistant text: the calls collapse into one native fold as soon as the text starts.
2. A turn ending on tool calls (no trailing text) still has the trailing run folded once `turn_done` fires.
3. A `failed` or `cancelled` call in the middle of an otherwise-successful sequence is never folded and splits the sequence into separate runs around it.
4. An active (not-yet-finished) call is never included in a fold.
5. Resuming/loading a session replays through the same `handle_event` path and produces the same fold behavior with no special-casing.
6. No custom foldtext or keymap is added; behavior relies entirely on Neovim defaults and existing fold commands.
7. Fold state is tracked per-window, mirroring `context_folds`/`fold_counts`'s existing per-window tracking, but in its own separate table (not reusing `context_folds`).

## Testing
- Headless `mini.test` coverage: run-to-fold assertions (e.g. via `foldclosed()`/`nvim_buf_call`), covering: multi-call successful run + supersede-by-text, trailing run + turn_done, failure-breaks-run, active-call-not-folded, resume/replay parity.

## Notes
- Decision reached via a grill-me session recorded on louiselm-ufx; this task implements the fold-rendering half of that decision.
- Related, decoupled work: on-demand raw payload inspection is a separate task -- do not couple its implementation to this one.
close_reason: Implemented native folding for contiguous completed tool-call runs with turn-end and failure/active boundary tests

title: On-demand raw ACP payload inspector for a tool-call line
description:
## Goal
Let the user inspect a tool call's full raw ACP payload live, on demand, without adding it to the always-visible transcript.

## Scope
- In scope: a command and/or keymap, invoked with the cursor on a `[tool] ...` line, that resolves that line's tool-call id and opens its merged raw fields (everything `session/transcript.lua`'s `merge_tool_call` already accumulates for markdown export -- title, status, and whatever else the agent sent) in a scratch or floating buffer.
- `handle_event` in `ui/chat/init.lua` currently only reads `status`/`title` off each event and discards the rest live; this task needs the merged raw payload available live, not just at export time -- reuse or adapt the accumulation approach already used by `louiselm.session.transcript`'s `merge_tool_call`/`open_tool_calls`, without duplicating the export pipeline.
- Out of scope: any inline/always-visible rendering, any change to the one-line tool-call renderer, any change to `:LouiselmToMarkdown` or `session/transcript_export.lua`.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Invoking the new command/keymap with the cursor on a finished tool-call's line shows that call's full merged raw payload (not just title/status).
2. Invoking it on an active (not-yet-finished) call's line shows whatever fields have arrived so far (partial payload), not an error.
3. Invoking it off a `[tool]` line is a no-op or clear error, not a crash.
4. Nothing changes about the default transcript rendering -- no new lines appear until the command is explicitly invoked.
5. The scratch/float buffer is disposable (closes without side effects on the session).

## Testing
- Headless `mini.test` coverage: invoke the command against a view with a known tool-call id and assert the opened buffer's content matches the merged raw payload; cover both a finished and a still-active call.

## Notes
- Decision reached via a grill-me session recorded on louiselm-ufx; this task implements the on-demand-inspection half of that decision, deliberately decoupled from the fold-rendering task (louiselm-ufx.1).
close_reason: Added LouiselmInspectTool raw-payload float with finished/active/off-line coverage

title: Allow handoff from Error sessions
description:
## Evidence

A Session whose ACP turn fails enters status=error. LouiselmHandoff calls Chat:hand_off(), which currently rejects every status other than ready with the active-turn error. LouiselmCancel cannot clear an error Session because Session:cancel() only accepts prompting, waiting_permission, or cancelling. The resulting Session is stranded: it cannot be cancelled and its transcript cannot be handed off.

## Acceptance

- A terminal error Session can open a reviewed Handoff to another Agent.
- Prompting, waiting_permission, cancelling, and queued prompts remain rejected.
- Add regression coverage for the error-state handoff path.
- Preserve the source Session and its transcript.
close_reason: Implemented terminal error-state handoff and regression coverage; focused and full suites pass.

comments.author: claude/0929f4e1-c8f2-4717-998f-1902618ce5f8
comments.text: Lesson: handoff eligibility must distinguish terminal Session states from active-turn states. `error` is terminal and retains the source transcript, while `prompting`, `waiting_permission`, and `cancelling` still require cancellation/completion. The fix belongs in Chat:hand_off(), the shared UI boundary, and does not change Session:cancel().

title: Grill-me needed: should a persisted workflow be a SKILL.md-shaped document discovered by the existing skill mechanism?
description:
Do not resolve this design question in passing. Facilitate a dedicated decision about the substrate and location of a persisted, declarative workflow. This is the representation half of louiselm-qbr.3, raised as a maintainer self-reflection on 2026-08-24.

Question:
When LouiseLM persists a declarative workflow, what document is it? Candidates raised: a dedicated `WORKFLOW.md`, or a `SKILL.md` at a path like `/generated/louiselm-workflow/SKILL.md` that the existing skill discovery mechanism already finds. And where does that document live -- is it tied to a project, and what makes its placement agent-friendly?

Context/evidence:
- docs/example-workflow.md already anticipates this in its own words: "louiselm intends to make workflows configurable rather than conventional, and when that lands this document is the thing it should be able to express. Treat it as a description that wants to become a specification." The maintainer now proposes taking that literally -- the example document becomes, or seeds, the actual spec.
- The maintainer's stated lean is toward SKILL.md over WORKFLOW.md, on the grounds that a skill discovery mechanism already exists and a second discovery path for a second document type is duplicated machinery.
- Skill discovery already parses frontmatter through lyaml (lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua) and already supports standard nested metadata (louiselm-m8a). A workflow spec needing structured fields -- stages, transitions, resolvers, envelopes -- would land on parsing that already exists rather than new parsing.
- This decision is why louiselm-4gif was resolved in favour of keeping lyaml and refusing a hand-rolled parser: if workflows are frontmatter documents, parser correctness stops being a skills-only concern.
- louiselm-qbr.3 owns declarative representation and lists what the format must express: validated stages, transitions, granular resolvers, backward transitions, logical threads, canonical decisions, supersessions, session replacement handoffs, evidence links. Its settled boundary with louiselm-qbr.5.1 also applies -- a persisted workflow may PROPOSE autonomy envelopes but never authorizes them.

Threads worth pulling:
- Does reusing SKILL.md conflate two things a user should be able to reason about separately? A skill is an instruction set offered to an agent; a workflow is a stage machine that sequences work. Sharing a file shape may be economy, or may be a category error that gets expensive once workflows need fields skills never have.
- If a workflow IS a skill, does it become injectable into agent context by the existing skill path, and is that desirable or a footgun -- does an agent get handed the workflow spec as instructions when it should merely be executing under it?
- "Probably tied to a project" was flagged as uncertain. Per-project in the repo (discoverable, versioned, cross-adapter, matching the repo-as-substrate posture in louiselm-repo-context-substrate-09r), or user-global, or both with precedence? Skill discovery already has root ordering and shadowing semantics that would answer this if reused.
- The `/generated/` path in the maintainer's sketch implies the document may be produced rather than authored. If it is generated, what is the source of truth, and does a human ever hand-edit it?
- Does docs/example-workflow.md become the spec, seed it, or stay a non-binding description alongside it? It currently declares itself binding on nobody; a spec binds by definition, so the relationship needs stating rather than assuming.
close_reason: Resolved by maintainer: persist workflows as discovered SKILL.md graphs with explicit named outcomes mapped to validated next-skill transitions; never infer topology from prose. Exact schema and runtime mechanics remain with louiselm-qbr.3.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Maintainer hints, 2026-08-24, materially advancing this question.

The stated model: a note / idea / self-reflection triggers questions; questions get answered; the workflow becomes more precise. Skill chaining already embodies it -- grill-me chains to to-beads, to-beads DECIDES epic/feature/task/bug, and that decision triggers the corresponding to-beads-xxxx skill. The maintainer's position: that chain IS the workflow, improving the workflow is itself a skill, and those skills ARE the louiselm workflow config.

This largely dissolves the 'category error' thread. If skills already encode their own handoffs, a workflow is not a different kind of object that happens to share a file format -- it is the graph induced by the skills' declared handoffs. There is no separate WORKFLOW.md object to describe. docs/example-workflow.md already states this in its own words: 'A workflow is not a list of stages; it is a set of stages plus the rules about what each one hands to the next, and the second half is where all the value is.'

Proposed resolution of the injection thread: a SKILL.md has TWO audiences, and that is the distinction, not skill-vs-workflow.
- body prose -> injected into the agent; what the agent reads and acts on.
- frontmatter -> read by the engine; how the workflow sequences.
Same file, two consumers. This is a second, independent argument for the louiselm-4gif decision: frontmatter is the machine-readable control plane, so parser correctness is structural rather than cosmetic.

The tension that SURVIVES, and is probably this issue's real content: today every handoff is prose, and it works because a model reads the prose and exercises judgment. Making it config means moving handoffs from prose into declarative frontmatter. That is a dial, not a binary:
- all prose -> flexible, but unverifiable; louiselm-qbr.3 explicitly wants VALIDATED stages and transitions, which prose cannot support.
- all declarative -> verifiable and sequenceable without model judgment, but rigid, and it destroys the thing that makes the current loop work. to-beads choosing epic vs feature vs task vs bug is a genuine situational judgment, not a lookup.

Candidate sweet spot: frontmatter declares the CHOICE SET of outgoing edges (enumerable, validatable), while the model resolves which edge is taken. That yields validation without rigidity and maps directly onto qbr.3's existing requirement for 'granular resolvers' -- a resolver is precisely a conditional edge whose decision procedure is a model rather than a predicate.

On self-modification: 'improving the workflow is a skill' makes the config a fixed point -- the workflow contains a skill that edits the workflow. The safety pattern for this is already settled one level up, in the qbr.3/louiselm-qbr.5.1 boundary: a persisted workflow may PROPOSE but never AUTHORIZE. Self-evolution should inherit that shape -- the workflow proposes its own revision, the operator authorizes it. That also answers the '/generated/ implies produced, is it ever hand-edited' thread: both, with the operator as an explicit stage rather than an implicit gap.

Precedent already in the tree: AGENTS.md is injected as an ACP resource_link on new-session start, gated by config.context.instructions_file (louiselm-ce6.20). So 'instruction documents are workflow config' is not speculative here -- it already ships, with AGENTS.md as the always-on member and skills as the conditionally-chained ones.

comments.author: codex/01a0343a-c8be-78b3-839b-6dc549db3374
comments.text:
Maintainer decision, 2026-08-24.

Accepted representation contract:

- A persisted workflow is the graph formed by discovered `SKILL.md` documents; there is no separate `WORKFLOW.md` substrate or second discovery mechanism.
- Each `SKILL.md` has two consumers: body prose instructs the Agent, while frontmatter supplies engine-readable workflow metadata.
- Frontmatter declares explicit named outcomes and the permitted next skill for each outcome. The model exercises judgment by selecting an outcome; LouiseLM validates the choice against that finite declaration, records it, and follows the declared transition.
- LouiseLM must not infer workflow topology or a next skill from prose, skill descriptions, or naming conventions. Existing phase-name inference is classification for routing and is not workflow-edge inference.
- These graph edges are transitions. Handoff retains its canonical narrower meaning: creation of a Session with another Agent, including injection of a reviewed transcript while retaining the source Session.
- Existing skill-root ordering and shadowing semantics govern project/global precedence rather than adding workflow-specific placement rules.
- `docs/example-workflow.md` remains a non-binding human-readable example that may seed the initial skill graph; it is not executable source of truth.
- Workflow self-improvement may propose edits to the selected `SKILL.md` graph, but operator authorization remains required under the settled qbr.3/qbr.5.1 boundary.

The earlier `workflow.outcomes` YAML was illustrative, not a frozen field name. Exact schema spelling, typed outcome reporting, validation, history, backward transitions, and execution belong to `louiselm-qbr.3`.

No standing AGENTS.md or vocabulary promotion is warranted: this is a feature-specific representation decision, and the existing canonical meanings of Handoff, Session, Agent, Model, and Provider remain unchanged.

title: QA round: skill discovery and pathless Codex permissions
description:
# Manual QA review — skill discovery and Codex pathless edit permissions

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; when the round closes its final content becomes a
QA-round bead and this file is deleted.

**Build under test:** `467a32e..2fa70dc` (five commits, beginning with
`a8b5730`). **Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: the previous round (`louiselm-yik`) closed at `467a32e`. Since then one
runtime change pruned expensive skill-tree traversal and another changed real
Codex edit requests with no path from protocol errors into generic permission
decisions. The three other commits are licensing/publication documentation or
tracker state and add no interactive behavior.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Real symlink-heavy skill discovery stays complete and fast | **passed** — 35 skills, 2 diagnostics, 21.8 ms; `bvr` present in picker and native catalog |
| 2 | Real pathless Codex edit reaches the generic permission picker | **passed** — real pathless request accepted; edit completed with no protocol error |

## Setup

The source checkout and installed plugin were both confirmed at `2fa70dc` at
the start of this round. Confirm again, then restart Neovim so no Lua module
from the previous build remains loaded:

```bash
git -C ~/code/louiselm log --oneline -1
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim log --oneline -1
```

Both must print `2fa70dc fix(permissions): ask on pathless edits`.

Case 2 requires a fresh **Codex** session using LouiseLM's normal default
`ask-human` permission policy **and Codex's `read-only` ACP mode**. In the new
session overview, change `Mode` from `agent` to `read-only`; if the overview was
dismissed, use `:LouiselmSessionOptions`. Confirm the header says
`Mode=read-only` before submitting. Codex 1.6.0's ordinary `agent` mode permits
workspace writes without an approval request, while `read-only` requires
approval for edits. The fixture path is new, so a remembered file rule cannot
short-circuit it.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Use a fresh session for the permission case. A previous denial or remembered
  rule can make the model detour or bypass the picker.
- A Codex edit may carry a full diff in `session/update` while its separate
  `session/request_permission` payload carries no path. Case 2 is specifically
  about the permission request, not the update shown in the transcript.
- Pin protocol evidence by the session id shown in the chat header. Never use
  the newest log by filename; other sessions may write newer logs.

## What does not need a manual case

- `a8b5730` and `56b9b42` change README/licence/policy prose only.
- `83fae1d` records completed GitLab publication work in beads only.
- Automated tests already prove pruning each named build directory, preserving
  a directly configured skill inside one, limiting layout warnings to one per
  root, and routing a synthetic pathless request through the session. The two
  cases below cover what those fixtures cannot: the real stow/symlink tree and
  the real Codex ACP payload/UI.

## Cases

### 1. Real symlink-heavy skill discovery stays complete and fast

Exercises `1c83964` / `lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua`.

In the restarted Neovim, run:

```vim
:lua local S=require("louiselm.skills"); local t=vim.uv.hrtime(); local s,d=S.discover({vim.fn.expand("~/.config/agentskills/generated/")}); print(string.format("skills=%d diagnostics=%d elapsed_ms=%.1f",#s,#d,(vim.uv.hrtime()-t)/1e6)); print(vim.inspect(vim.tbl_map(function(x) return x.name end,s)))
```

Then open a fresh chat, choose Codex, and invoke `:LouiselmPickSkill`. Search
for `bvr`, confirm it is offered, then dismiss the picker without selecting it.

Expect: the command returns promptly with `skills=35 diagnostics=2`; the names
include `bvr` and the other configured skills; the picker opens promptly and
offers `bvr`. The validated pre-round reading was `31.0 ms` on this machine, so
the exact timing may vary, but it should be tens of milliseconds rather than
the previous roughly 380 ms pause.

Failure signature: materially fewer than 35 skills, `bvr` missing, a flood of
roughly 31 diagnostics, or a visible several-hundred-millisecond pause before
the command/picker appears.

Evidence: send the two printed lines. They objectively prove the discovered
count, diagnostic count, names, and elapsed time. Whether the picker visibly
hesitated is observational and rests on what you saw.

**Result: PASS.** Direct discovery passed with `skills=35 diagnostics=2
elapsed_ms=21.8`; all expected names, including `bvr`, were present. The first
picker attempt did not exercise this case: screenshot
`~/Pictures/scrot/20260820_1556_948x1123_1787234213.png` shows the prompt
`louiselm file`, 27,230 workspace-file candidates, and paths matching `bvr`.
That is categorically `:LouiselmPickFile`, whose prompt is distinct from the
required `louiselm skill`. Command wiring in the build maps
`:LouiselmPickSkill` to `chat:pick_skill()` and the file command separately to
`chat:pick_file()`, so there is no code evidence of a wiring defect. The exact
skill-picker rerun passed in `codex/01a01f7a-b5ce-7e62-9ebe-83650123c8e1`:
the tester confirmed `bvr` was offered, and the pinned ACP log independently
shows Codex advertised `$bvr` in that session's native command catalog. The log
does not prove picker appearance or responsiveness; those remain the tester's
observation.

### 2. Real pathless Codex edit reaches the generic permission picker

Exercises `2fa70dc` / `lua/louiselm/permission/gates.lua`.

Create the fixture from Neovim:

```vim
:call writefile(['before'], '/tmp/louiselm-qa-pathless.txt')
```

Open a **fresh Codex session**, set its ACP `Mode` option to `read-only`, confirm
the header says `Mode=read-only`, and submit exactly:

> Use the edit/apply-patch tool, not a shell command, to replace the entire contents of /tmp/louiselm-qa-pathless.txt from `before` to `after`. Do not use sed, perl, Python, or shell redirection.

Expect: a normal select picker opens with the prompt
`louiselm permission (unknown, details unavailable):`. It is a generic picker,
not a `louiselm-diff://` review buffer. Rejection should be listed first. Choose
the adapter's once-only allow option. The turn should continue normally and the
file should contain `after`.

Failure signature: no picker; Codex reports a JSON-RPC `-32602` error; a diff
review opens despite the permission request having no path; the picker vanishes
without a choice; or approval succeeds but the turn remains stuck in
`waiting_permission`.

Report the `codex/<session-id>` from the chat header. I will pin and inspect its
protocol log. You can verify the file immediately with:

```vim
:lua =vim.fn.readfile('/tmp/louiselm-qa-pathless.txt')
```

Expect `{ "after" }`.

**First attempt: RECIPE MISS, not a product result.** Session
`codex/01a01f7d-55e4-7b60-8d16-f3503f027403` stayed in the default `agent`
mode. Its pinned log contains zero `session/request_permission` messages: Codex
sent one `edit` tool call, completed it, and changed the fixture to `after`.
LouiseLM therefore had no decision to display and could not reach the branch
changed by `2fa70dc`. The installed codex-acp 1.6.0 source confirms why:
`agent` uses an `on-request` policy with workspace-write sandboxing, so this
in-workspace-capable write needed no request; `read-only` explicitly requires
approval to edit. The recipe now sets `Mode=read-only` and requires the header
as proof before the prompt.

**Result: PASS.** Retest session
`codex/01a01f9c-15dc-7db1-a84d-56c1973fc210` emitted one real
`session/request_permission` request. Its `toolCall` was exactly the pathless
shape under test: `{ kind = "edit", status = "pending", toolCallId = ... }`
with no `rawInput`, content, or path. It advertised `allow_once`,
`allow_always`, and `reject_once`. The tester observed the decision UI and
allowed it; the same tool call then moved through `in_progress` to `completed`,
the fixture contains `after`, and the pinned agent output contains no protocol
error. The log and fixture prove the real payload reached the fixed path and
the response released the agent; exact picker appearance remains the tester's
observation.

## Evidence check

After case 2, substitute the ACP id without the `codex/` prefix:

```bash
S=<session-id>
L=$(rg -l --fixed-strings "\"sessionId\":\"$S\"" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log | tail -1)
jq -c --arg sid "$S" 'select(.method == "session/request_permission" and .params.sessionId == $sid) | {id,toolCall:.params.toolCall,options:.params.options}' "$L"
printf 'fixture='; cat /tmp/louiselm-qa-pathless.txt
```

Pass condition: one request shows `toolCall.kind` as `edit`, no path/raw input
in that request, advertised allow/reject options, and `fixture=after`. The log
proves the real peer sent the pathless shape; the fixture proves the selected
response released the agent and the edit completed. The exact picker appearance
and focus rest on what you saw.

## Cleanup when the round closes

```vim
:call delete('/tmp/louiselm-qa-pathless.txt')
```

No permission rule should be created when the once-only option is used. If a
persistent option was selected accidentally, revoke it with
`:LouiselmPermissions` before closing the round.

## Reporting back

Send me the case number, its printed output or session id, what you saw, and
anything surprising. I pull the objective evidence myself before classifying
the result. If a case did not reach the intended code path, I will correct the
recipe; if it found a product bug, I will file it before fixing it.

## Findings this round

None. Both runtime changes passed against the real environment and peer.

## How the round closed

Both manual cases passed. `1c83964` reduced discovery on the real symlink-heavy
skill root from the previously measured roughly 380 ms to 21.8 ms while
preserving all 35 skills and reducing diagnostics from roughly 31 to 2.
`2fa70dc` handled Codex 1.6.0's real pathless edit-permission payload through a
human decision and completed the edit instead of returning `-32602`.

The automated tests already asserted both normalized behaviors, but they could
not establish that the production stow layout still retained every skill or
that the current Codex peer still emitted the historical payload shape. Those
were the useful manual checks; both assumptions held.

Two recipe misses were corrected during the round. The first picker attempt
opened `:LouiselmPickFile`; its `louiselm file` title and 27,230 path candidates
made the missed code path objective. The first permission attempt used Codex's
default `agent` mode, which completed the workspace-capable edit without ever
sending a permission request. Requiring the picker title and `Mode=read-only`
made both cases reach their intended paths.

No product finding, persistent permission rule, or unverified adjacent defect
remains. The temporary fixture and this scratch file are removed as the round
is archived into beads.
close_reason: Completed: both real-environment QA cases passed with no product findings

title: CI LuaLS check fails on RunWorker contract
description:
## Evidence

On current main (066512a), `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning` exits 1 with 46 warnings. The first production warning is `lua/louiselm/workflow/run.lua:65:25 Undefined field client`; `cold_park_record()` reads `worker.client`, but `louiselm.workflow.RunWorker` does not declare that field. The same check also reports duplicate `nvim.schedule` assignments and test annotation warnings.

## Scope

Fix the RunWorker LuaCATS contract at the narrowest boundary, then reassess remaining CI diagnostics. Do not weaken the warning gate.
close_reason: Fixed RunWorker LuaCATS contract, cleaned strict LuaLS test diagnostics, regenerated API appendix. All CI gates pass with LuaLS 3.19.1: StyLua, LuaLS, API appendix, Vimdoc, and 628 tests.

comments.author: 01a03f7a-1e8d-7cb2-837d-43323fbfa269
comments.text: Added the missing optional  field to RunWorker. Recheck reduced LuaLS diagnostics from 46 to 45; the production undefined-field warning is gone. Remaining 45 diagnostics are in tests (duplicate nvim.schedule assignments, missing returns, undefined vim), so the CI warning gate is still red beyond this contract fix.

comments.author: 01a03f7a-1e8d-7cb2-837d-43323fbfa269
comments.text: Resolution: LuaLS 3.19.1 reports no diagnostics after declaring RunWorker.client. The strict warning gate also required test fakes to mutate nvim.schedule through rawset and service fakes to return a handle value; generated doc/api.md was regenerated with the same LuaLS version. No standing project rule or unresolved design question warranted.

title: Grill-me needed: define chat window versus session close semantics
description:
Do not resolve this design question in passing; decide the lifecycle policy before implementing a fix.

Observed scenario:
- One Neovim instance had two live louiselm Codex sessions.
- While switching between them, the user closed the session whose feature was complete.
- The other session, which was still being resumed/worked on, also became unavailable.
- The user believes this happened through :q while the sessions are scratch buffers.

Current code evidence:
- Chat buffers are buftype=nofile, bufhidden=hide, and named louiselm://<session-id>.
- There is no chat BufHidden/BufDelete/BufWipeout handler.
- Chat:close_session() is the explicit disposal path and disposes only the selected view.session.
- Chat:dispose() removes UI resources without disposing sessions.
- The exact command/path used in the incident is not yet reproduced; it may involve :q on the last window, an explicit close command, or outer UI teardown.

Questions to resolve:
1. Must :q on a louiselm chat buffer always mean only hide/close this view, never dispose its session?
2. How are hidden sessions rediscovered and switched to?
3. Should explicit session close warn or confirm when other sessions are live, or only when the selected session has active work/queued prompts?
4. What should happen when closing the last chat window, tab, or UI controller?
5. What headless test reproduces two sessions, switching, :q/explicit close, and verifies that unrelated sessions remain live?
6. If the incident is reproducible, should it become a separate implementation bug after the lifecycle policy is settled?
close_reason: Implemented last-window QuitPre protection for multiple attached chat sessions; added regression coverage; full suite passes with 329 tests and 0 failures.

title: Grill-me needed: What should LouiseLM's first-run onboarding optimize for?
description:
Do not resolve this design question in passing; run a focused grill-me session and record the maintainer's decisions.

Question:
What should LouiseLM's first-run onboarding optimize for: the shortest path to a working chat, teaching users how Agents/providers/keys work, or a small set of opinionated onboarding profiles?

Context and evidence:
- The current README has only a development Quick start and assumes users can write Lua configuration.
- manual_init.lua preconfigures Claude and DeepSeek, but not Codex, and relies on adapter-specific commands and environment variables.
- The proposed beginner path is a minimal init file users can run with Neovim, with Agents prefilled and one obvious place to configure credentials.
- Provider installation and authentication flows differ and may change; credentials must never be hard-coded or exposed.
- The existing task louiselm-lukb asks for an onboarding information architecture, a quickstart.lua versus README decision, verified provider setup guidance, and first-prompt acceptance criteria.

Threads worth pulling:
- Who is the primary first-run user and what Neovim knowledge can be assumed?
- Should the first-run path choose one recommended Agent or present Claude/Codex/DeepSeek equally?
- Is a committed standalone quickstart.lua safe and maintainable, or should it be a copyable template?
- Should onboarding profiles be documentation-only initially or a product feature?
- What counts as success: opening the chat, completing one prompt, or configuring a durable personal setup?
- How should provider auth/key instructions be kept accurate as external adapters change?
close_reason: Resolved through confirmed grill-me design; decisions recorded in issue comments.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer answer: primary audience is C, an AI-tool user who knows Claude/Codex keys but not Neovim; secondary is A, a Neovim beginner; tertiary is B, an existing Neovim user comfortable editing init.lua.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer answer: recommend Codex as the default provider in the primary onboarding path; Claude and DeepSeek remain secondary alternatives.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Authentication verification: official codex-acp documentation and current source show ChatGPT authentication is an ACP auth method; the adapter invokes Codex accountLogin with type chatgpt and opens the returned auth URL. API-key authentication is separate and reads CODEX_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY. NO_BROWSER=1 hides the browser method. Design implication: the LouiseLM Codex quickstart should default to provider-managed interactive ChatGPT login, should not ask users to put a key in quickstart.lua, and should explain that API-key environment variables are an optional alternative. Sources: https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/codex-acp/blob/main/README.md and https://github.com/agentclientprotocol/codex-acp/blob/main/src/CodexAcpClient.ts

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer clarification: LouiseLM must not install external tools or dependencies. It should guide users through provider/adapter installation according to their technical comfort and existing setup. Node.js/npm is therefore only a prerequisite of one documented Codex route, not an installation action performed by LouiseLM.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer accepted the proposed setup-state branching as the working design: (A) already use Codex, (B) have an AI account but no ACP adapter, (C) want to configure LouiseLM manually. Avoid framing this as a user's geek level.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer chose quickstart artifact C: commit examples/quickstart.lua as the source of truth, and include a README path that explains how to copy/run it. Accept the maintenance obligation to keep the example aligned with configuration and agent-command changes.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer chose quickstart option C: Codex enabled by default; Claude and DeepSeek included as commented optional examples. This preserves discoverability without requiring all three adapters for a successful first run.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer prefers quickstart option B: examples/quickstart.lua should use Neovim's vim.pack to fetch/install LouiseLM, making the file a genuinely runnable first entry point. External Agent/adapter installation and authentication remain guided user actions; LouiseLM does not install those tools.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer chose the alpha update policy: vim.pack in the onboarding quickstart should track the repository's main branch rather than a release tag or commit. This is intentional for alpha users and should be stated plainly.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer chose bootstrap option C: README should provide a raw quickstart.lua download command and a visible copy/paste fallback. The quickstart file itself remains the source of truth.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer proposes that running quickstart.lua open a quickstart Markdown tutorial, analogous to Neovim's :Tutor. It should teach how to navigate LouiseLM, start/use chat, understand permissions and context, and discover capabilities before or alongside the first prompt. This replaces the earlier assumption that the first screen must immediately be the chat.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer chose the guided interactive Tutor scope: Markdown lessons with working keymaps/commands and examples, including actions such as launching chat and checking health; no persistent progress tracking or completion-detection subsystem in the first version.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer accepted the recommended first-lesson flow: brief orientation followed by a clearly marked action to try the first prompt, then deeper explanation.

comments.author: 01a04879-6ef8-7dc2-b75e-07164df2a926
comments.text: Maintainer clarified the launch flow: README instructs users to run Neovim with quickstart.lua, then run :LouiselmTutor. The quickstart should only install/configure LouiseLM via vim.pack; it should not contain special machinery to launch the Tutor automatically. The Tutor command owns opening the onboarding lesson.
