title: Add tweet-corpus agent skill (local SQLite+FTS5 tweet history store)
description:
## Summary

Created the `tweet-corpus` skill in the owned skill catalog
(`~/.config/agentskills/tweet-corpus/`, source of truth in
`~/dotfiles/agentskills/.config/agentskills/tweet-corpus/`).

## What it does

Local storage/analysis layer for tweet-history research, picking up where a
fetching skill (e.g. `kaitoInfra/twitterapi-io`, `xurl`) leaves off:

- Ingests `tweets.jsonl` (id, author, date, text, links, reply/retweet flags,
  engagement counts) into a SQLite database via `scripts/build_corpus.py`,
  upserting by tweet id so repeated/paginated fetches stay idempotent.
- Maintains an FTS5 full-text index (`tweets_fts`, external-content over
  `tweets.text`) so keyword/date-range/engagement queries do not require
  loading the raw corpus into context.
- SKILL.md instructs the agent to answer historical-analysis questions
  (opinion evolution, chronological summaries) by querying the index and
  citing tweet id + date per claim, not paraphrasing from memory.

## Provenance

Continues opencode session `ses_fad1ec8d3ffeTYD4TzGM755ney`, which converged
on this spec (informed by a shared ChatGPT conversation about tweet-history
analysis skills) but got derailed filing adapter/session-id bugs before any
skill file was written. See related: louiselm-eqg7 (session-id
recognition bug filed in that same session) and
louiselm-adapter-session-id-exposure-fq4k (the underlying adapter exposure
gap). No skill files existed on disk before this issue.

## Verification

- `scripts/build_corpus.py` smoke-tested standalone: builds the schema,
  upserts, FTS5 `MATCH` query returns correct rows, rerun is idempotent
  (no duplicate rows).
- Catalog entry seeded, `inventory_skills.py` run cleanly.
- `manage_lifecycle.py check`, the unittest suite, and `run_golden_tasks.py`
  (added one golden task: cite-not-paraphrase) all pass.
- `build_installation.py` for the full catalog currently fails — but on a
  **pre-existing, unrelated** pin drift: the `bvr` skill's source repo
  (`/home/lotso/code/beads_viewer_rust`) has moved one commit past its pinned
  commit. Confirmed via `git diff` that this catalog.json change only adds
  the new tweet-corpus entry and does not touch the bvr entry. Verified
  tweet-corpus builds correctly in isolation by calling
  `build_installation.install_skill()` directly against a scratch directory
  (correct openai.yaml, correct symlinked scripts/).

## Remaining

- `~/dotfiles` has the catalog.json + tweet-corpus source changes staged but
  uncommitted (commit is a repo-owner action, not automated here).
- The `bvr` pin-drift build failure blocks a full clean
  `build_installation.py` run; unrelated to this skill and not fixed here — a
  deliberate pin review, per this catalog's own README, not a
  silent adopt.

title: QA round: transcript export & blog publishing pipeline
description:
# Manual QA review — transcript export & blog publishing pipeline

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.
(The previous, closed round is archived next to it in
`QA_REVIEW-permissions-round.md`.)

**Build under test:** `4e4a58b` (session transcript export) and `674939b` (blog
publishing pipeline). `ec19281` is beads bookkeeping, nothing to test.
**Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: two features shipped together with heavy unit coverage but zero contact
with a real agent's payloads or a real published page. Everything below is what
the suite structurally cannot reach.

## Status

| #   | Case                                                                           | State                                                           |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Live export of a real claude turn                                              | **PASS** — evidence-checked below                               |
| 2   | `:LouiselmToMarkdown` input paths (cancel, blank, `~`, bad dir, bad id)        | **DONE** — 2.1-2.3, 2.5 pass; 2.4 still open (`louiselm-euj`, reconfirmed, deferred) |
| 3   | Export mid-stream and while a permission decision is open                      | **PASS** — 3a and 3b both confirmed                             |
| 4   | Resumed-session export vs the live export of the same session                  | **found a gap** — `louiselm-d2o`, see F3 (out-of-repo)          |
| 5   | `create-blog.sh` against a real session id                                     | **PASS**, reproduces F3 as predicted                            |
| 6   | `render-post.sh` + `myst build` — does the highlighted fragment reach the page | **confirmed broken** — `louiselm-xrf`, see F4                   |
| 7   | GitLab CI pipeline                                                             | **not runnable locally** — `louiselm-8na` tracks the known risk |

## What the test suite already covers — skip these

Do not spend a round on them:

- Transcript merge/render logic against synthetic events (`tests/session/transcript_spec.lua`, 12 cases:
  chunk merging, interleaved tool calls, missing status/title fallbacks, determinism).
- Headless export against the mock agent, including timeout, agent crash during
  `session/load`, invalid config, stdout/stderr/exit-code contract
  (`tests/session/transcript_export_spec.lua`).
- `Chat:to_markdown` default path, explicit session id, disposed UI, not-attached id
  (`tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua`).
- Command registration and the `vim.ui.input` flow _with a stubbed input_
  (`tests/ui/command_spec.lua`).
- CSS namespacing against **real** `:TOhtml` output, and render-post idempotency
  (`blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh`); scaffold + mock-agent export (`test-create-blog.sh`).

## Setup

The plugin is installed as a clone of this repo, so new commits are not live
until you update it:

```vim
:lua vim.pack.update({ 'louiselm.nvim' })
```

Confirm in the buffer it opens (`:write`), restart nvim, then:

```bash
# these two must print the same commit
git -C ~/.local/share/nvim/site/pack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim log --oneline -1
git -C ~/code/louiselm log --oneline -1
node -v            # cases 5-6 need Node 20+; CI pins node:24
```

For case 6 only, matching what CI pins:

```bash
npm install -g mystmd@1.10.1   # or use npx mystmd@1.10.1 in place of `myst`
```

**Permission mode matters for case 3b.** Some sessions in this round were
deliberately launched with the underlying agent's approval gate skipped
(`--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`), by design, to see what happens under
reduced control. That's a legitimate thing to test, but it means the ACP
`session/request_permission` call never fires, so `louiselm`'s diff-review UI
never opens — not because of a remembered rule, a bug, or anything in this
repo, but because the agent process itself never asks. **Case 3b needs a
session launched *without* that flag** — confirm before running it, since
nothing in the UI signals which mode a session is in.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

Carried over from the permissions round and still true:

- **Pin the log by session id**, never `ls -t | head -1` — the newest log is the
  session you are talking to me in:
  `L=$(grep -l "<acp-session-uuid>" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*jsonrpc.log | tail -1)`.
  Get the id from the chat header or `:LouiselmSessionId`.
- **The log only holds the agent's side.** Your own prompts are not in it — which
  is exactly why `record_user` exists, and why case 1 checks the prompt text
  against what you typed, not against the log.
- **Say the tool name and give absolute paths** in prompts, or the model picks a
  different tool and the case misses.

New for this round:

- **`## ` inside agent text is indistinguishable from a section header.** The
  export writes `## User` / `## Assistant` / `## Tool:` with no escaping, and
  agents write markdown headings all the time. Any script that parses the export
  by section will over-count. Grep for `toolCallId = "..."` instead — that is the
  reliable anchor, and it is what the evidence check below uses.
- **The jsonrpc log is cumulative for the whole live conversation, not scoped to
  one turn.** Case 1's evidence check was run against the log *after* several
  more turns had already happened in the same ACP session (this QA round itself
  ran inside the session under test — the assistant answering your reports and
  the agent that produced the case-1 export are the same session). Diffing the
  export straight against the full log falsely showed 37 "missing" tool calls
  and out-of-order ids — they were all from later turns that postdated the
  export. Fix: take the log's tool-call id list, restrict it to the prefix
  ending at the last id that also appears in the export, and diff *that* prefix.
  Anything after is expected, not a bug — but say so explicitly rather than
  silently truncating.
- **Prompts as fenced code, not blockquotes.** A `> quoted` prompt often copies
  with the leading `>` attached from a rendered markdown pane, forcing an edit
  before pasting into nvim's input line. Fenced code blocks paste clean. Cases
  below now use fences for exactly this reason.
- **Flag order/state dependencies between sub-cases explicitly.** Case 2's five
  sub-points run against the same open chat/session state, back to back. If an
  earlier one leaves the UI in a bad state (stuck `decision_active`, focus in
  the wrong window, an uncaught error), a later sub-point can fail for a reason
  that has nothing to do with what it's actually testing — and that's confusing
  to debug from the outside. Case 2 below now says which sub-points are
  independent and which aren't; do the same for future multi-part cases.
- **A session's own launch flags can silently make a case untestable, with
  zero UI signal.** Ran an `Edit` during case 3b expecting the diff-review
  buffer to open; nothing opened. Spent real time checking `louiselm`'s
  remembered-permission store (exact-path match only, one unrelated rule on
  disk — not the cause) before finding it one layer out: this session's agent
  process was launched with `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions`, so the ACP
  `session/request_permission` call this whole feature depends on never fires.
  Confirmed session-specific by diffing against a sibling session from the
  same day with 17 normal permission requests. Lesson: for any case that
  depends on an approval/permission gate, state and verify the session's
  launch mode in Setup *before* running it — see the new note there.

## Cases

### 1. Live export of a real claude turn

Exercises `4e4a58b`: `Transcript:record` against payloads the real
`claude-agent-acp` sends, plus `record_user` for the prompt.

Fresh `:LouiselmChat` (claude). Note the session id (`:LouiselmSessionId`).
One prompt, chosen because it produces every block kind in one turn:

```
Do these three things in order, in this one turn. (1) Run the Bash tool on the absolute path: `wc -l /home/lotso/code/louiselm/lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua`. (2) Use the Task tool to launch one general-purpose subagent whose prompt is exactly: "List the top-level directories of /home/lotso/code/louiselm as one comma-separated line." (3) Write me a two-sentence summary of what you found.
```

When the turn ends: `:LouiselmToMarkdown`, leave the path blank, press Enter.

Expect: `louiselm: exported transcript to /home/lotso/code/louiselm/louiselm-<id>-<ts>.md`,
and in that file — a `## User` block holding **your prompt exactly as typed**, a
`## Tool:` block per tool call in the order they ran, each with the full
`rawInput`/`content`/`rawOutput` dump, and `## Assistant` blocks for the text.

Failure signature: a tool call missing entirely, tool blocks out of order,
the `## User` block absent or holding injected context markers rather than your
text, or a `## Tool:` block whose `content` is empty while the chat showed
output.

Prediction, already **checked offline and refuted** — do not spend attention on
it: I expected `merge_tool_call`'s per-field later-wins to silently drop earlier
`content` payloads. Across 7687 real multi-payload tool calls in your ACP logs,
and after replaying two real logs through the actual renderer, every earlier
payload turned out to be a placeholder, a streaming refinement, or a duplicate of
`rawInput` (e.g. a Task call's dropped `content` prompt is verbatim in
`rawInput.prompt`; a dropped diff hunk is verbatim in `rawInput.old_string`). No
unique information was lost. The live run just needs to confirm the shape, not
hunt for that.

**Result: PASS.** Evidence check (below) against the turn-1 prefix of the
jsonrpc log: 3/3 tool calls present, correct order, none missing, exactly one
`## User` block holding the prompt verbatim. Manually confirmed the `## Tool:`
blocks are in order (`wc -l` first, `Task` second with a nested `Bash` tool
call inside it via `parentToolUseId`) and the `## Assistant` block matches what
was actually said.

### 2. `:LouiselmToMarkdown` input paths

Exercises `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:266` — the real `vim.ui.input`, which
every test replaces with a stub.

With the case 1 session still open, run each and report what you see. **2.1
through 2.4 share the same open chat/session state** — if one leaves the UI odd
(stray notification, focus in the wrong place, anything that looks like the
crash below), say so before moving to the next one; don't assume a later
sub-point's result is clean.

1. `:LouiselmToMarkdown` then **Esc** at the prompt → expect nothing written and
   **no error notification** (cancel returns silently). Confirm no stray file:
   `ls -t ~/code/louiselm/louiselm-*.md | head -3`.
   **Result: PASS**, as reported.
2. `:LouiselmToMarkdown`, type `~/tmp/qa-export.md` → prediction: this **fails**
   with `could not write markdown file: ~/tmp/qa-export.md`, because
   `vim.fn.writefile` does not expand `~`. Confirm or refute; if it fails, note
   whether the message makes the cause obvious.
   **Result: prediction refuted, real bug found.** `vim.fn.writefile` doesn't
   return a failure code for a missing parent directory — it *throws* `E482`,
   which was never caught, so a raw Lua stack trace hit `:messages` instead of
   the clean notification. Filed and fixed as `louiselm-dim`
   (commit `6167df0`) — `writefile` is now wrapped in `pcall`.
   **Retest: PASS.** Clean `could not write markdown file: ...` notification,
   no stack trace.
3. `:LouiselmToMarkdown`, type `/tmp/nope/qa-export.md` (missing directory) →
   expect the same `could not write markdown file:` error, no crash, chat intact.
   **Result: same bug as 2.2**, same fix. **Retest: PASS**, same clean error.
4. `:LouiselmToMarkdown not-a-session-id` → expect `louiselm: session is not attached`.
   **Result: partially refuted, real (minor) bug found.** The error text was
   right, but it only appeared *after* being prompted for a path first — the
   not-attached check happens inside `to_markdown`, which the command only
   calls once the path prompt resolves. Filed as `louiselm-euj`, **not fixed
   this round** (small enough to batch with other UI-polish work later; not
   worth reloading the plugin twice in one round for).
   **Reconfirmed** while checking 2.5: still prompts for a path first, then
   shows `session is not attached`. Unchanged, as expected — nothing this
   round touched `louiselm-euj`.
5. After any of the above, where is the cursor? Expect focus back in the chat
   buffer, in the same mode you started in.
   **Result: PASS.** Checked by redoing 2.4 (the not-a-session-id case) and
   watching the cursor: it never moved, and mode was normal both before and
   after — same spot throughout. Focus was never stranded, even by the
   crash that used to happen here pre-`louiselm-dim`.

Failure signature: a silent no-op with no notification on a real error, a Lua
stack trace in `:messages`, or focus stranded in another window.

### 3. Export mid-stream, and during a permission decision

`Chat:to_markdown` is the **only** chat entry point that does not check
`self.decision_active` (compare `init.lua:1471`, `1648`, `1779`, `1800`, `1867`,
`1914` — all guarded — against `to_markdown` at `1543`, which checks only
`disposed`). That may be deliberate (writing a file harms nothing) or an
oversight; this case decides it.

**3a, mid-stream.** Start a long turn:

> Read /home/lotso/code/louiselm/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua and summarise each section in one line.

Export to **two distinct paths**, not the same one twice — `/tmp/qa-midstream-1.md`
while it is still streaming, `/tmp/qa-midstream-2.md` after the turn ends. (Originally
this case reused one path for both exports; that was a mistake — it makes the
superset comparison below impossible to check after the fact, since the second
write silently overwrites the first.)

Expect a normal success notification each time, a partial but well-formed first
file, the turn continuing undisturbed, and the second file a strict superset of
the first: every line the first file has, the second has too, unchanged, plus
whatever streamed in after — the transcript recorder only ever appends, nothing
is deleted or reordered retroactively.

**Result: PASS, superset confirmed.** First attempt reused `/tmp/qa-midstream.md`
for all three exports run during that turn, so only the last one survived to
inspect. Evidence check on that survivor (pinned to session
`21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384`, log restricted to the prefix ending at
the last id the export also contains — see the cumulative-log ground rule):
**17/17 tool calls present, correct order, none missing**, all 4 user turns
present, file ends cleanly at the end of the assistant's response. No error
notification at any of the three exports, no crash, turn was never disrupted.
One perceptual "glitch" (buffer looked like a wall of text appearing at once),
traced to the final assistant message landing as a single large chunk (a
27-line bulleted list) — not a dropped update or corruption, nothing to file.

Rerun with two distinct paths (`/tmp/qa-midstream-1.md` mid-stream,
`/tmp/qa-midstream-2.md` after the turn ended) proved the superset relationship
directly rather than assuming it: `cmp` reports the two files byte-identical
for their entire common length (496172 bytes), with file1 cutting off
mid-word ("...pickers and" — the streaming chunk had only delivered that much
of "pickers and headers") and file2 continuing seamlessly from there through
the rest of the turn (986 → 1049 lines). Byte-for-byte prefix, not
coincidental length growth.

**3b, during a decision.** Requires a session **without**
`--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` (see the Setup note above) — otherwise
no `session/request_permission` call is ever made and there is nothing to
open.

Reset the fixture and open a review buffer:

```bash
printf 'hello\n' > ~/code/louiselm/qa-diff-test.txt
```

> Use the Edit tool, not Bash, to change `hello` to `hello world` in /home/lotso/code/louiselm/qa-diff-test.txt

With the `louiselm-diff://` buffer open, run `:LouiselmToMarkdown` →
`/tmp/qa-decision.md`.

Expect: the input prompt opens on top of the review, the file is written, and
**after** answering the input you can still answer the review with `a`/`d`/`q`
and the turn completes normally.

Failure signature: the review closing or being answered without you (the failure
mode the guards on every other command exist to prevent), `a`/`d`/`q` going to
the input instead of the review, or the chat left with `decision_active` stuck so
`:LouiselmPermissions` keeps refusing afterwards.

**Result: PASS.** Run in session `aef3e4a2-4c64-4d24-80be-83cb9a48db4b`
(normal permission mode, confirmed via ground rules above). Review buffer
opened as expected; `:LouiselmToMarkdown` → `/tmp/qa-decision.md` succeeded
while the decision was still open — evidence: the exported markdown's tool
call block shows `status = "pending"` with the full diff (`old_string: "hello"`
→ `new_string: "hello world"`), proving the capture happened mid-decision, not
after. Log trace confirms the mechanism end to end: `session/request_permission`
fired (unlike the skip-permissions session), the tool call was `pending` at
export time, and transitioned to `completed` only after the review was
answered with `a`. `qa-diff-test.txt` read back as `hello world` afterward,
confirming the edit applied and the turn completed normally — no stuck
`decision_active`, no input/review cross-talk.

### 4. Resumed-session export vs the live export

Exercises the `user_chunk` path (`lifecycle.lua:186`) against the real agent's
`session/load` replay — the whole blog pipeline depends on it, because
`create-blog.sh` can only ever export what the agent replays.

Your logs confirm claude-agent-acp does replay `user_message_chunk`,
`agent_message_chunk`, `tool_call` and `tool_call_update` on load, so a resumed
export should not be empty. What is unknown is **fidelity**.

Restart nvim, `:LouiselmResume`, pick the case 1 session, and immediately
`:LouiselmToMarkdown` → `/tmp/qa-resumed.md` **without prompting anything first**.

Expect: the same tool calls, in the same order, and your case 1 prompt back as a
`## User` block.

Failure signature: header only and no blocks; tool calls missing while assistant
text is present; your prompt missing; blocks in a different order than case 1's
export.

Evidence: diff the two exports' structure (command in **Evidence check**). They
will not be byte-identical (`usage_update`, ids, timestamps), but the tool call
id sequence should match.

**Result: fidelity gap found, filed as `louiselm-d2o` (out-of-repo, not fixed
here).** By the time this ran, session `21a0ede3-...` had accumulated the
whole round's history, so the resumed export (`/tmp/qa-resumed.md`, 573KB, 66
tool calls, 18 user turns) is the full session replay, not just case 1's
turn — compared it against the original case-1-only export
(`louiselm-session-1-20260818-150448.md`, 3 tool calls, captured right after
that turn ended) as a prefix/subset check rather than exact-match. 2 of 3
case-1 tool calls present, correct relative order, case-1 `## User` block
verbatim. The missing one: a nested Bash call made *by* the Task subagent
(`parentToolUseId` set), present in the original live export with its full
command and output, absent from the resumed export entirely — the parent
Task call's own summary replayed fine, but its child call vanished. Confirmed
via the raw jsonrpc log that the agent process itself never re-emits that
event during replay (appears once, only during the original live turn) — not
a `louiselm` rendering bug, since `Transcript` only records what it's given.
See `louiselm-d2o` for full evidence, root-cause hypothesis, and why the test
suite couldn't have caught it (no fixture combines "replay" with "nested
subagent call"). **Not what case 4 predicted** (it predicted fidelity was
merely *unknown*, not a specific gap) — worth re-checking once case 5 runs,
since `create-blog.sh` uses the same replay path headlessly.

### 5. `create-blog.sh` against a real session id

Exercises `674939b`'s headless export path with the real agent and your real
`~/.config/nvim`, which the mock-agent tests cannot.

```bash
cd ~/code/louiselm
./blog/scripts/create-blog.sh qa-round claude/<acp-session-id-from-case-1>
```

Expect: `exported claude/<id> -> conversations/claude-<id>.md`, then
`created .../blog/post-qa-round`, exit status 0, and
`blog/post-qa-round/conversations/claude-<id>.md` holding the same content case 4
produced by hand.

Failure signature, in the order I think they are likely:

- `error: exporting ... failed:` with `timed out waiting for agent 'claude' to
load session ...` — the export gives up after 60s (`transcript_export.lua:25`)
  and a big session may legitimately take longer. Time it; if it is close to 60s,
  that constant is the finding, not your session.
- The written file is header-only (three metadata lines, no blocks) — the
  replay-fidelity failure from case 4, but through the headless path.
- Anything mentioning a _stale_ louiselm — the script prepends this checkout to
  `rtp`, but your config also loads the installed clone, so both copies are on
  `rtp` at once. If the error mentions a symbol that only exists in one of them,
  say so.

**Result: PASS.** `./blog/scripts/create-blog.sh qa-round claude/21a0ede3-...`
succeeded cleanly: `exported claude/21a0ede3-... -> conversations/claude-21a0ede3-....md`,
`created .../blog/post-qa-round`, no timeout, no stale-louiselm symbol errors.
`blog.md` scaffold matches the expected `{literalinclude} ... :lines: 1`
shape. As predicted when F3 was filed: the headless export reproduces the
same nested-tool-call gap (`louiselm-d2o`) — checked precisely for a genuine
`## Tool: ls -d ...` header (not a plain string match, since the transcript
by now also contains this bug's own filing text, which quotes the missing
toolCallId verbatim and would false-positive a naive grep); none found.
Confirms the gap lives in the shared `session/load` replay path itself, not
something specific to the interactive `:LouiselmResume` UI. Logged as a
comment on `louiselm-d2o` rather than a new finding — same bug, second
confirmation.

### 6. Does the highlighted fragment actually reach the published page

The end of the pipeline, and the part I most expect to be incomplete.

```bash
cd ~/code/louiselm/blog/post-qa-round
wc -l conversations/*.md          # pick a real range inside the file
$EDITOR blog.md                   # change `:lines: 1` to e.g. `:lines: 10-40`
cd ~/code/louiselm && ./blog/scripts/render-post.sh blog/post-qa-round
ls blog/post-qa-round             # expect *.nvim-transcript.html + nvim-transcript.css
cd blog && myst build --html --strict && cd ..
```

Then open `blog/_build/html/index.html` (or `myst start`) and **look at the
post**.

Prediction to confirm or refute: the highlighted fragment never reaches the page.
`render-post.sh` writes `<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` and `nvim-transcript.css`,
but nothing references either — `blog.md` still holds the plain
`{literalinclude}`, and `myst.yml` loads only `./blog.css` via
`site.options.style`. So I expect the page to show the excerpt as plain,
unhighlighted text, with no `<div class="nvim-transcript">` in the served HTML
and `nvim-transcript.css` absent from `_build`. If that is what you see, the
missing piece is the assembly step (swap the literalinclude for an include of the
fragment, and wire the generated CSS into the site) — that is a feature gap to
file, not a broken script.

Failure signature beyond that: `myst build --strict` failing (report the exact
warning it promoted), or `render-post.sh` erroring on the transcript's own
` ``` ` fences.

Also worth one glance: the exported transcript contains fenced code blocks and
`## ` headings of its own. Note whether an excerpt boundary lands mid-fence and
what that does to the rendered page.

**Result: prediction confirmed, filed as `louiselm-xrf`.** Used
`blog/post-qa-round` (scaffolded in case 5), `:lines: 10-40` (3033-line
source file). `render-post.sh` ran cleanly, `myst build --html --strict`
built all 3 pages with no errors. Evidence: `nvim-transcript.css` has zero
matches anywhere under `_build`; no `<link>` to it in the served page's
`<head>`; the only "nvim-transcript" string in the built output is the inert
`:class:` attribute on the plain literalinclude block, not the actual
generated `.nvim-transcript.html` fragment, which nothing ever reads —
`blog.md` still points at the raw conversation file. The rendered block does
show *some* syntax coloring (MyST's own generic `hljs`), which is why it
doesn't look broken to the eye — but it's not the nvim-generated
highlighting, and none of `nvim-transcript.css`'s rules apply to it. Priority
1: this isn't an edge case, the assembly step doesn't exist for any post.
Not fixed — real feature work, out of scope for a QA round. The
mid-fence-boundary question from the "also worth one glance" note wasn't
exercised: `:lines: 10-40` happened to land cleanly between a heading and
the next fence; noted as unverified in the bead.

### 7. GitLab CI — not runnable here

`.gitlab-ci.yml` only fires on the default branch when `blog/**` changes, and
`louiselm-8na` already records the ECONNREFUSED-under-bridge-networking risk with
repro steps. Nothing to run manually; whoever watches the first real pipeline run
closes that bead.

## Evidence check

Pin the log to the session under test first:

```bash
S=<acp-session-id>
L=$(grep -l "$S" ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/*claude-agent-acp*jsonrpc.log | tail -1)
```

```bash
python3 - "$L" <path-to-export.md> "$S" <<'EOF'
import json, re, sys
log_path, md_path, sid = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
ids = []
for line in open(log_path, errors='ignore'):
    try: d = json.loads(line)
    except Exception: continue
    if d.get('method') != 'session/update': continue
    p = d['params']
    if p.get('sessionId') != sid: continue
    u = p['update']
    if u.get('sessionUpdate') in ('tool_call', 'tool_call_update'):
        if u['toolCallId'] not in ids: ids.append(u['toolCallId'])
md = open(md_path).read()
md_ids, seen = [], set()
for t in re.findall(r'toolCallId = "([^"]+)"', md):
    if t not in seen: seen.add(t); md_ids.append(t)
print('log: %d tool calls' % len(ids))
print('export: %d tool calls' % len(md_ids))
print('in log but NOT exported:', [t for t in ids if t not in seen] or 'none')
print('order matches log:', [t for t in md_ids if t in ids] == ids)
print('user blocks:', len(re.findall(r'^## User$', md, re.M)))
EOF
```

Pass condition: `in log but NOT exported: none`, `order matches log: True`, and
at least one user block.

Validated against a known-good run before writing it here: I replayed
`20260610-132413-claude-agent-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log` through the real
`louiselm.session.transcript` renderer offline and this check reported 18/18 tool
calls with matching order.

What it cannot prove: that the _text_ of each block is complete, that your prompt
was captured verbatim (the log has no copy of it — you have to read the `## User`
block yourself), or anything about cases 2, 3 and 6, which are entirely
observational.

For case 4, compare the two exports:

```bash
diff <(grep -o 'toolCallId = "[^"]*"' ~/code/louiselm/louiselm-*.md | sed 's/.*= //') \
     <(grep -o 'toolCallId = "[^"]*"' /tmp/qa-resumed.md | sed 's/.*= //')
```

Empty diff = the resumed export saw the same tool calls in the same order.

For case 6:

```bash
grep -rl 'nvim-transcript' ~/code/louiselm/blog/_build/html/ | head
```

No hits = the fragment and its CSS never reached the built site, which is the
prediction.

## Cleanup when the round closes

```bash
rm -f ~/code/louiselm/louiselm-*.md ~/code/louiselm/qa-diff-test.txt
rm -f /tmp/qa-midstream.md /tmp/qa-midstream-1.md /tmp/qa-midstream-2.md /tmp/qa-decision.md /tmp/qa-resumed.md
rm -rf ~/code/louiselm/blog/post-qa-round ~/code/louiselm/blog/_build
```

Already in the tree before this round and unrelated to it:
`71c82ed5-9db8-44a3-9e64-e610a51b6cea.md` (a raw chat-buffer dump from the
permissions round — the lossy format this feature replaces) and
`qa-diff-test.txt`.

## Reporting back

Send me the session id, which case, what you saw, and anything surprising. I pull
the evidence myself. If something is wrong I will fix it, and you will need to
redo Setup before retesting.

## Findings this round

**F1 — `louiselm-dim`, fixed.** `Chat:to_markdown` (`init.lua:1561`) checked
`writefile(...) ~= 0` to detect a write failure, but Neovim's `writefile`
throws `E482` instead of returning nonzero when the destination's parent
directory doesn't exist — the check was dead code for that failure mode and a
raw Lua stack trace hit `:messages` instead of the intended
`could not write markdown file: ...` notification. Found in case 2.2/2.3.
Fixed by wrapping the call in `pcall` (commit `6167df0`), with a new
regression test in `tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua`. Full suite (235/235)
and `stylua --check` pass on the changed files. **Missed by the test suite
because** `tests/ui/chat_to_markdown_spec.lua` covered the success path and
the "not attached"/"disposed" errors, but no case ever pointed `writefile` at
an actually-unwritable path.

**F2 — `louiselm-euj`, filed, not fixed this round.** `LouiselmToMarkdown
<bad-id>` (`command.lua:266`) always opens the path prompt before validating
the session id, so a bad id wastes a full path entry before the correct
`session is not attached` error shows. Found in case 2.4. Deliberately
deferred — small UX-ordering issue, not a crash, and batching it into this
round's fix would have meant reloading the plugin twice. Fix direction is in
the bead: a small `Chat:is_attached(session_id)` predicate so the command can
check before prompting. **Reconfirmed in retest** (case 2.4/2.5): still
reproduces exactly as described, unchanged.

**F3 — `louiselm-d2o`, filed, out-of-repo, not fixed.** `:LouiselmResume`'s
ACP `session/load` replay silently drops nested/child tool calls (ones with
`parentToolUseId` set — e.g. a tool call made by a Task subagent) while still
replaying the parent call's own summary text. Found in case 4, comparing the
original live case-1 export against a resumed export of the same session:
the nested `ls -d ... | paste -sd, -` call (made by the "List top-level
directories" Task subagent) is present in the live export, absent entirely
from the resumed one. Root cause is outside this repo — confirmed the
missing `tool_call` event never arrives from the agent process on replay
(raw jsonrpc log), so `louiselm`'s own `Transcript` code, which only records
events it receives, isn't at fault. **Missed by the test suite because**
no fixture combines a resumed-session replay with a nested/subagent tool
call — both paths are tested separately, never together. Practical impact:
`create-blog.sh` (case 5) uses this same replay path headlessly, so blog
posts built from resumed sessions may silently omit subagent-internal detail.

**F4 — `louiselm-xrf`, filed, not fixed.** The blog publishing pipeline's
highlighted-transcript feature is fully disconnected end to end:
`render-post.sh` correctly generates `<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` and
`nvim-transcript.css`, but `blog.md`'s `{literalinclude}` was never changed
to consume the generated fragment, and `myst.yml:11`'s
`site.options.style` was never made to include the generated CSS. Found in
case 6, confirmed by inspecting the actual built `_build/html` output rather
than trusting appearances — the page does show *some* highlighting (MyST's
own generic `hljs`), which would have looked plausible enough to wave
through without pulling the evidence. Priority 1: not an edge case, doesn't
work for any post. **Missed by the test suite because**
`test-render-post.sh` only tests `render-post.sh`'s own output in isolation
— no test in the suite runs a real `myst build` and inspects the served
HTML, which is exactly the gap this manual case exists to cover.

**Refuted before the round started:** the `merge_tool_call` later-wins
truncation I predicted from reading `transcript.lua:108`. Checked against 7687
real multi-payload tool calls and two full log replays through the real renderer;
every dropped payload was recoverable from `rawInput`. Recorded here so nobody
re-derives it.

title: Inject-mode adapter titles hide the user subject
description:
DeepSeek/GLM sessions using LouiseLM's inject-mode skill context appear in the resume picker without a useful subject. The adapter persists only the beginning of the injected catalog as the session title, so the user's task is absent and cannot be recovered by LouiseLM's picker normalization.

## Observed

Screenshot: `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_1012_1920x1200_1787559124.png`, session `deepseek/session-7042e674-d0c9-4f03-81ef-5c46171d50b7`, observed 2026-08-24.

Captured ACP session/list payloads:
- `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/connections/8552aa82-b66b-482e-bd9d-4c5a27953096.jsonl`
- `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/connections/ec2827e1-c090-4643-9548-4671e86848c7.jsonl`

The exact title is 81 characters:
`<skills_instructions> Skills are sets of instructions stored in SKILL.md files. …`
It contains neither `</available_skills>` nor the user's prompt.

## Symptoms

- Resume row shows identity, timestamp, and cwd but no useful subject.
- The same adapter-backed session listing shows the same failure for DeepSeek/GLM inject-mode sessions.
- Complete Codex titles can be normalized because their injected catalog and user text are present; this truncated adapter title cannot.

## Root cause

`/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/src/session.rs:553-578` derives the title from the first user message and truncates it to `MAX_TITLE_LEN = 80`, appending `…`.

LouiseLM `/home/lotso/code/louiselm/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` builds injected prompt content with the skill catalog before AGENTS context and final user text. Therefore the adapter's first-user-message title is consumed entirely by the catalog. LouiseLM's current normalization intentionally omits an injected title when the closing catalog marker is absent, because the subject is unrecoverable.

## Why it was not caught

The closed `louiselm-vns4` work added coverage for complete injected titles and truncated/unrecoverable titles, but did not cover the adapter's 80-character first-message title policy at the adapter boundary.

## Fix direction

The narrowest durable fix is at the adapter/title boundary: derive the session title from the actual user request rather than the injected skill catalog, or provide a title/subject field independent of the prompt content. Reordering LouiseLM's injected content is a possible workaround but changes prompt ordering and should not be selected without testing model behavior. Picker parsing alone cannot reconstruct a subject that is absent from the ACP payload.

## Acceptance

- A regression test proves that a first turn containing injected skill context and a user request produces a title containing useful user-request text in `session/list`.
- The LouiseLM resume row for `session-7042e674-d0c9-4f03-81ef-5c46171d50b7` (or an equivalent fixture) displays a useful subject after cwd.

## Not covered

This diagnostic did not modify the adapter or LouiseLM code and did not run the adapter test suite. The adapter fix may belong in `/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter`.
close_reason: Implemented capability-gated embedded skill catalog resources and verified the adapter returns the final authored Text block as the session title.

title: Codex resume rows lose useful subject in inject mode
description:
## Observed

Screenshot captured 2026-08-24 at 09:55 local time: /home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_0955_1920x1200_1787558153.png. In the `:LouiselmResume` picker, the first three Codex rows end immediately after `cwd=/home/lotso/code/louiselm`, while Claude rows show useful subjects such as `Overview of available agent skills`, `Test prompt injection handling`, and `Review available agent skills`.

The current user configuration at `/home/lotso/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua:23-30` sets Codex `skills.policy = "inject"`; Claude has no agent override and therefore inherits the global native policy at lines 96-100.

## Regression / evidence

Before commit `1d4c235`, Codex rows displayed the injected title prefix, for example the prior screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260824_0937_1920x1200_1787557068.png` showed `<skills_instructions> Skills are sets of instructions stored in SKILL.md files...`, which was distracting but contained the prompt subject later in the same provider title. Commit `1d4c235` changed `discovered_session_summary()` at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:385-392` to omit any ACP title containing `<skills_instructions>` or `<available_skills>`. The result removes the entire title, including any useful user-task text after the injected catalog.

## Symptoms

- Inject-mode Codex sessions are indistinguishable by subject in the resume picker.
- Native-mode Claude sessions retain concise provider-generated subjects.
- Recency and cwd remain visible, but the row loses the most useful human-readable context.

## Root cause

Confirmed at the LouiseLM boundary: `Registry:discover_sessions()` calls ACP `session/list`; `Validation.discovery_page()` copies the optional provider `title` into `DiscoveredSession.title` at `lua/louiselm/session/validation.lua:182-215`; `discovered_session_summary()` then either renders or discards that one string. Inject mode makes the provider title include LouiseLM skill-instruction context. The current marker filter treats the whole title as unusable, and no separate subject field is retained. It is not yet confirmed whether Codex itself can provide a clean title or whether LouiseLM must derive one from persisted session content.

## Why it was not caught

The previous regression test asserted that a skill-marked title disappears entirely. It did not include useful user text after the injected catalog or assert that the subject survives. Existing ordinary-title coverage only exercises provider titles without the injected prefix.

## Fix direction

Preserve a concise subject for inject-mode sessions while hiding the injected catalog. Prefer a provider-native clean title if Codex can expose one; otherwise derive a bounded single-line subject from the user-authored portion of the persisted session data at the narrowest available boundary. Keep the full transcript and injected context intact. Compare Codex, Claude, and adapter-backed agents before choosing the fallback.

## Acceptance

- A Codex inject-mode fixture containing an injected skill catalog plus a user task displays the useful task subject after `updated=` and before `cwd=`.
- Claude native-mode rows retain their current useful subjects.
- Skill instructions and raw catalog markup are not displayed.
- DeepSeek/GLM/other adapter-backed sessions are characterized, with missing metadata handled without blank or noisy rows.
- Resume selection behavior is unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed the shared resume-picker formatter: strips complete injected skill catalogs and leading LouiseLM resource wrappers, retains recoverable user/provider subjects, orders rows as identity/updated/cwd/subject, and omits titles truncated inside hidden context. Regression failed before the fix and covers Codex, Claude, Copilot, and DeepSeek/GLM-style payloads. Focused chat suite 106/106; full MiniTest 470/470; stylua, lua-language-server, git diff check, and dependency-cycle check pass. Existing test-harness warnings remain non-failing and unrelated.

comments.text: Real ACP payload captured from `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/connections/c414dd81-1faa-485a-97f2-4b19612eef22.jsonl` confirms Codex `session/list` returns one `title` containing the complete `<skills_instructions>` + `<available_skills>` catalog, then `[@AGENTS.md](file:///...)`, then the user task. Claude native returns concise synthesized titles. Copilot prefixes the user task with `[Resource link: ...]`. The adapter-backed DeepSeek/GLM list payloads include both clean titles and titles truncated inside injected context, so no user subject is recoverable from those truncated entries. User clarified desired row order on 2026-08-24: identity, updated, cwd, then useful subject. Fix should normalize known leading LouiseLM context wrappers, preserve clean provider titles, and omit unrecoverable truncated context rather than inventing a subject.

title: Handoff provenance records a local session id, not the durable ACP identity
description:
A Handoff prompt is now recorded in the target Session transcript, but its provenance line names a
local, per-editor-instance identifier (`session-1`) instead of the durable `<agent>/<acp-session-id>`
identity. Exported transcripts therefore still cannot prove which source Session initiated a Handoff
once the editor restarts, which is the symptom louiselm-ac6z was filed to remove.

## Observed

Manual QA round 2026-08-25, build acb65c7, case 5.

Target Session claude/c91d8058-49da-44bc-8d03-568fe8213dbb.
Source Session codex/01a037a9-23d0-7fe2-9cb6-5fd1be5b84d2.
Log: /tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/c91d8058-49da-44bc-8d03-568fe8213dbb/log.jsonl

The Handoff reached the wire correctly. `session/prompt` at 06:47:20.904Z carried one 339-character
text block holding the reviewed source transcript, including the tester's manual edit:

    # louiselm session transcript

    - session: session-1
    - agent: codex
    - acp session: 01a037a9-23d0-7fe2-9cb6-5fd1be5b84d2

    ## User

    turn 1
    ...
    ## Assistant

    What should I tackle next?

    EDITED BY ME

So retention and edit fidelity both work. The defect is in the recorded provenance, not the payload.

## Symptoms

- The target transcript's Handoff entry renders `Handoff from Session: `session-1``.
- `session-1` is allocated per editor instance. After a restart it names a different Session, so an
  exported or archived transcript cannot resolve the source.
- The same rendered transcript header shows both forms side by side — `- session: session-1` and
  `- acp session: 01a037a9-...` — so the durable identity was available at the moment of recording.

## Root cause

lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2616 reads `local source_state = source_view.session:inspect()` and
line 2636 stores `source_session_id = source_state.id`. `state.id` is the registry's local counter,
assigned as `"session-" .. self.next_id` at lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:206.

The durable identity is `report_id(state.agent, state.acp_session_id)`, which is exactly what
`Chat:session_id` returns at lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2873-2885 and what `:LouiselmSessionId`
copies. The Handoff path does not use it.

Note that `Chat:open_handoff` already accepts a `source_session_id` parameter, but it is used only to
locate the source view; the recorded value is recomputed from `source_state.id`. The sole caller at
line 1985 passes `view.session:inspect().id`, so both are local ids and switching to the parameter
alone would not fix this.

`Transcript:record_handoff` and `render_entry` (lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua:158-172 and
221-232) print whatever string they are given verbatim, so they need no change.

## Why it was not caught

The regression coverage for louiselm-ac6z asserts that a Handoff entry exists and carries *a* source
id. It does not assert the id's *form*, and the test constructs Sessions whose local id is the only
id available, so a local id satisfies the assertion. The bead's own Observed section used
`<agent>/<acp-session-id>` throughout, which is the shape a reader would expect.

## Fix direction

Record `report_id(state.agent, state.acp_session_id)` for the source Session, matching
`Chat:session_id`. Handle the case where `acp_session_id` is nil — a source Session that never
reached ready has no durable identity, and recording nothing is better than recording a local
counter that will be silently wrong later.

Rejected: keeping the local id and resolving it at export time. The mapping does not survive the
editor instance, which is the whole problem.

## Acceptance

- A regression test that fails while the local id is recorded and passes once the agent-scoped id is.
- A Handoff from a live Session renders `Handoff from Session: `<agent>/<acp-session-id>`` in both
  the target chat buffer and `:LouiselmToMarkdown` output.
- The rendered value matches what `:LouiselmSessionId` copies for the source Session.

## Not covered

- The exact rendered line was derived from the code path rather than read off the tester's screen;
  the wire payload above is direct evidence only for retention and edit fidelity. If the rendered
  line turns out to carry the agent-scoped form, close this as not reproducible.
- Handoff from a Session that has not yet reached ready was not exercised.
close_reason: Completed: Handoff provenance records agent-scoped ACP identity; 500 mini.test cases, StyLua, and lua-language-server pass.

comments.author: claude/edc00380-9cc9-438e-ad38-3bb929cdc43c
comments.text:
Reproduction confirmed from the exported markdown, not derived. The "Not covered" caveat in the
description is now closed: the rendered line does carry the local id.

Export: /home/lotso/code/louiselm/louiselm-session-2-20260825-084751.md, line 9.

    # louiselm session transcript

    - session: session-2
    - agent: claude
    - acp session: c91d8058-49da-44bc-8d03-568fe8213dbb

    ## User

    <sub>Handoff from Session: `session-1`</sub>

The file makes the defect self-evident: three lines above the provenance line, the same export
prints the durable identity of its own Session (`- acp session: c91d8058-...`). Both forms are
produced by the same render, and the Handoff entry picked the one that does not survive the editor
instance.

Adjacent observation, deliberately not filed separately because it shares this root cause: the
export filename is also built from the local id (`louiselm-session-2-...`). Two exports taken from
different editor instances can therefore carry the same name while describing different Sessions.
Worth folding into the same fix if the export path is touched; not worth a bead on its own.

Incidental and not a contract: in this instance the source ACP id is still recoverable, because a
Handoff embeds the source transcript's full header (`- acp session: 01a037a9-...`) inside the prompt
body. That is a property of Handoff payloads, not of the provenance field, and it would not hold for
any other consumer of `handoff_source_session_id`.

title: blog/myst.yml + blog/blog.css: multi-post MyST site scaffold
description:
## Goal
A working MyST project under blog/, structured to hold multiple posts from the start, with a minimal starter stylesheet.

## Scope
- In scope: blog/myst.yml (MyST project/site config, article-theme base, discovers posts under blog/post-*/blog.md), a minimal blog/blog.css starter (just enough to prove the theme-attachment mechanism works — the real visual design is a separate, author-only task).
- Out of scope: the actual visual theme/branding (tracked in louiselm-0ee), any nvim-transcript-specific CSS (that ships alongside render-post.sh's output, not this scaffold).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `myst build --html` (or `myst start`) succeeds against the scaffold with zero or one placeholder post.
2. The project config is structured so adding a second blog/post-<name>/blog.md requires no myst.yml changes — multi-post support is real, not aspirational.
3. blog.css is attached and demonstrably affects the rendered page (not just present but unused).

## Testing
- Build smoke test: `myst build --html` exits 0 and produces output in the expected build directory — this is also what GitLab CI will run, so this test doubles as a CI dry-run.

## Notes
- This is the dependency root for the GitLab CI/Pages task — CI needs a buildable project to build.
- No dependency on the other tasks in this decomposition.
- Parent feature: louiselm-r1k.
close_reason: MyST scaffold implemented and verified: blog/myst.yml (pattern: 'post-*/blog.md' discovers posts with no per-post config change), blog/blog.css (wired via site.options.style, visibly non-default marker styling). Manually re-ran 'myst build --html' against the scaffold: exits 0, produces _build/html output. All 3 acceptance criteria met.

title: Rebind <leader>ll to <leader>le, add <leader>lT, propose full keymap coverage
description:
Two concrete rebinds plus a keymap-coverage proposal for `lua/louiselm/ui/keymaps.lua`.

## Concrete asks
- Rebind inline edit from `<leader>ll` to `<leader>le` (both `n` and `x` modes), freeing `l`.
- Add a new default `<leader>lT` -> `LouiselmInspectTool`.

## History check
Only one commit ever touched keymaps.lua (3860f29, "feat(ui): add default keymaps") -- it introduced the full DEFAULTS table in one shot, nothing has been renamed/removed since. The only mapping outside that table is a buffer-local `<leader>lB` for `LouiselmInspectBead`, installed ad hoc in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua` on the `louiselm-session` filetype autocmd (not registered/reset via `keymaps.lua`'s configure()/clear_installed(), so it's invisible to `:LouiselmDiagnostics`-style introspection of installed keymaps).

## Current DEFAULTS (unchanged letters)
lc Chat, ln NewSession, lr Resume, lR Resume!, ls SwitchSession(n)/SendSelection(x),
lN RenameSession, li SessionId, lI Inbox, lm ToMarkdown, lx CloseSession, lC Cancel,
lo SessionOptions, lp Permissions, lk PickSkill, lf PickFile, lb MentionBuffer.

## Proposed additions (no conflicts with the above or each other)
| Keys | Command | Mnemonic |
|---|---|---|
| `<leader>le` | LouiselmInline (moved from `ll`) | Edit |
| `<leader>lT` | LouiselmInspectTool | Tool |
| `<leader>lP` | LouiselmInspectProvenance | Provenance (`p` taken by Permissions) |
| `<leader>lB` | LouiselmInspectBead | Bead -- promote the existing ad-hoc buffer-local map into DEFAULTS so it's covered by configure()/clear_installed() like everything else |
| `<leader>lH` | LouiselmHandOff | Hand-off |
| `<leader>lF` | LouiselmForensics | Forensics (`f` taken by PickFile) |
| `<leader>lV` | LouiselmForensicsView | View |
| `<leader>lL` | LouiselmLimits | Limits |
| `<leader>ld` | LouiselmDiagnostics | Diagnostics |
| `<leader>lz` | LouiselmResumePark | cold-parked run ("zzz") -- weakest mnemonic of the set, open to a better letter |

## Deliberately left without a default keymap
The six capture/pairing commands (LouiselmCapture, LouiselmCaptureSetup, LouiselmCaptureStatus,
LouiselmCapturePair, LouiselmCaptureRevoke, LouiselmCaptureRetry) are admin/setup actions for the
mobile-pairing subsystem, not everyday chat actions. Forcing six more top-level `<leader>l*` binds
for rarely-used commands seems like the wrong default; leave them command-only unless usage data
says otherwise. Flagging so it's a conscious decision, not an oversight.

## Scope
Pure keymaps.lua table edit (plus promoting the InspectBead buffer-local map) -- no new commands,
no behavior changes to what each command does. Should be a genuine one-shot, no design doc needed.
Update tests/ui/keymaps_spec.lua and doc/louiselm.txt where they assert on `<leader>ll`.
close_reason: Rebound <leader>ll -> <leader>le, added <leader>lT and 7 more default keymaps (lP, lB, lH, lF, lV, lL, ld, lz) covering every previously-unbound louiselm command except the low-traffic capture/pairing admin group, which was deliberately left command-only. Promoted the ad-hoc buffer-local <leader>lB map into the DEFAULTS table. Updated tests/ui/keymaps_spec.lua and removed the now-obsolete tests/ui/beads_spec.lua case. Full mini.test suite green.

title: Monitor-watched CI pipeline never reports back: loop greps wrong status string, silently never exits
description:
Agent starts a Monitor background task to watch a GitLab CI pipeline, tells the user "I'll report back once it finishes," then goes silent. No automatic report ever arrives — the user has to interrupt and ask why. The agent then has to fall back to manual polling (TaskOutput / a fresh `glab ci list`) to discover the pipeline had actually already finished a minute earlier.

## Observed

Session claude/3869f178-9bdd-4a0f-981c-2b01567e1e60, workstream watching GitLab pipeline #38205 on oss-public/louiselm after pushing commit 60f1e0f. JSONL transcript: /home/lotso/.claude/projects/-home-lotso-code-louiselm/3869f178-9bdd-4a0f-981c-2b01567e1e60.jsonl, lines 217-250.

- line 225: first `Monitor` call fails: `InputValidationError: The required parameter 'description' is missing` — tool schema wasn't loaded yet (deferred-tool gotcha).
- line 231: second `Monitor` call succeeds:
  `command: "until glab ci list 2>&1 | grep -m1 \"38205\" | grep -qE \"passed|failed\"; do sleep 5; done\nglab ci list 2>&1 | head -4\necho DONE"`
  Task id `bfpnoyv8m` started. Tool result explicitly states: "You will be notified on each event. Keep working — do not poll or sleep."
- line 234: agent tells user: "Watching pipeline #38205 — I'll report back once it finishes."
- line 237: user, unprompted by any agent report: "it is ok, why didnt you report ? do you have a timer on this im interested"
- line 240-241: agent calls `TaskOutput` with `block: true, timeout: 30000`; gets `<retrieval_status>timeout</retrieval_status>`, task still `running`, 0KB output.
- line 244: agent's own diagnosis: "my loop only prints after it finishes, so it produces zero output while waiting... no notification fires until completion — bad design on my part."
- line 246: a fresh, unrelated `glab ci list` shows `(success) • #38205 ... about 1 minute ago` — i.e. the pipeline had already finished before the user even asked, but the Monitor task never fired, and per line 241 the task itself was still reported as `running`.

## Symptoms

- User sees the agent promise a follow-up report that never comes.
- Agent has no idea anything went wrong until directly challenged.
- `TaskOutput` on the still-"running" task shows zero bytes of output even though the real-world event it was waiting for had already occurred.

## Root cause

Two compounding issues, both in the ad-hoc shell command the agent wrote for the Monitor call (line 231), not in Monitor/TaskOutput themselves:

1. Vocabulary mismatch: the loop's exit condition greps for `passed|failed`, but `glab ci list`'s actual status tokens are `success`/`failed`/`running` (see line 222: "(running) • #38205"; line 246: "(success) • #38205"). "passed" never appears in glab's output, so `grep -qE "passed|failed"` never matches a successful run, and the `until` loop never exits.
2. Silent polling: because the loop body is just `sleep 5` with no `echo` per iteration, no stdout is produced while waiting. Monitor's notification model is stdout-line-driven ("each stdout line is a notification" per tool docs), so a loop that only prints after exiting produces zero notification events the entire time it runs — and since (1) means it may never exit at all, the agent can be left permanently un-notified for a background task the user is actively waiting on.

This is a structural risk, not a one-off typo: any Monitor loop that (a) greps a CLI's human-readable status words to decide when to stop, and (b) has no heartbeat output on each poll, is exposed to the same failure — wrong string guess -> infinite silent loop -> the "I'll report back" promise silently breaks with no error surfaced to agent or user.

## Why it was not caught

No fixture or convention exists for validating a Monitor loop's exit condition against a real sample of the target command's output before starting the loop. Nothing in the harness heartbeats a "still waiting, N minutes elapsed, last status: <X>" line if a Monitor task runs past some expected duration — the only way anyone finds out is if the user gets impatient and interrupts, as happened here.

## Fix direction

This is filed to track workflow/agent-behavior guidance rather than a single code fix, since Monitor/TaskOutput are harness tools, not code in this repo. Candidate mitigations, not yet chosen:
- Before starting a Monitor loop that greps a CLI's status output, run the command once first and eyeball/parse the actual token vocabulary rather than guessing (e.g. "passed" vs "success").
- Always emit a heartbeat line inside the loop body on every poll (e.g. `echo "poll: $(date +%s) status=..."`), regardless of match, so Monitor's stdout-driven notifications fire periodically even before the exit condition is met.
- Prefer a machine-readable/exit-code check (`glab ci status --live` exit code, or `--json` output field) over grepping human-facing status words, where the CLI supports it.
- Treat "I'll report back once it finishes" as a promise that needs a periodic self-check-in (e.g. re-poll via TaskOutput after N minutes) rather than pure trust in the notification firing.

## Acceptance

- Documented guidance (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md or session memory) on writing Monitor loops: verify the exit-condition string against real output first, and always heartbeat inside the loop.
- No fix in this repo's code is required; this bead's acceptance is the guidance existing and being followed in the next Monitor-based CI watch.

## Not covered

- The first-call InputValidationError (missing `description`, deferred-tool schema not loaded) is noted as compounding friction but is a separate, likely harness-level quirk, not part of this bug's root cause.
- Whether Monitor/TaskOutput's underlying notification plumbing has its own bugs is unverified — the evidence here is fully explained by the agent's own loop bug, so no harness defect is claimed.
close_reason: Documentation-only fix per bead's own acceptance criteria: guidance added to AGENTS.md.

title: Grok ACP requires approval for every trusted tool call
description:
The LouiseLM Grok Agent configuration does not enable Grok's documented always-approve/yolo permission mode, so multi-tool work requires approving each read, search, fetch, and command individually. This makes Grok's ACP integration impractical for trusted local automation and directly blocked the x_search workflow.

## Observed

- Grok documentation: /home/lotso/.grok/docs/user-guide/15-agent-mode.md
  - Agent mode documents: grok agent --always-approve stdio.
  - The option table says --always-approve is an alias for --yolo.
  - ACP session metadata documents _meta: { yoloMode: true } on session/new.
- Grok permissions documentation: /home/lotso/.grok/docs/user-guide/22-permissions-and-safety.md
  - Always-approve is the documented automation mode.
  - It remains subject to deny rules and hooks.
- LouiseLM dotfiles configuration: /home/lotso/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua:121-128
  - Current command is acp-proxy -- grok agent stdio.
  - No --always-approve or --yolo argument is present.
- Live ACP connection for Session grok/01a05666-bf8c-7c02-b6f5-e14e3f6c8726:
  - Connection log: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/connections/b43ab2ab-28f9-4557-b31b-330af82b7708.jsonl
  - line 4 session/new params contain only _meta.claudeCode.options.thinking; no _meta.yoloMode.
  - The Session emitted permission requests for web_fetch, run_terminal_command, and other tool calls at session log lines 392, 402, 533, 578, and 588.
  - Session log: /home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a05666-bf8c-7c02-b6f5-e14e3f6c8726/log.jsonl.
- The same x_search attempt required repeated manual interaction and ultimately exhausted quota; see related louiselm-bvo5.

## Symptoms

- Trusted Grok ACP sessions pause for explicit approval on every external fetch, shell command, or other non-read-only tool.
- The user must repeatedly select allow-once/allow-always while using a session.
- Tool-heavy workflows can stall, invite accidental inconsistent approvals, or consume model quota while waiting.
- The configured Grok Agent does not match Grok's documented automation setup.

## Root cause

Confirmed configuration omission: the dotfiles Grok command does not pass --always-approve/--yolo, and LouiseLM's Agent definition provides no Grok-specific options._meta.yoloMode for session/new. The ACP client already threads Agent options._meta through session creation; the missing value is in the Grok Agent configuration, not the generic permission request transport.

## Why it was not caught

The adapter matrix tested prompt rendering and normal completion, not a multi-tool Grok run. Those cases did not exercise repeated permission requests. No configuration regression asserts Grok's argv or session/new metadata against the documented always-approve contract.

## Fix direction

Use one documented mechanism at the configured Grok boundary: add --always-approve to the Grok agent command, or set Grok's session/new metadata to _meta.yoloMode=true. Prefer the mechanism that keeps the setting explicit in the LouiseLM Agent definition and preserve Grok deny rules/hooks as the hard safety boundary. Do not weaken generic ACP permission handling or silently auto-approve other Agents.

## Acceptance

- A Grok Session started from the configured LouiseLM Agent runs trusted tool calls without repeated permission prompts.
- A regression asserts the selected always-approve mechanism is present in the launched command or session/new params.
- Deny rules and hooks remain effective.
- Codex, Claude, and OpenCode permission behavior is unchanged.
- Manual Grok verification completes a bounded multi-tool x_search probe without per-call approval prompts.

## Not covered

- No change is made to the dotfiles configuration in this filing.
- The correct policy choice between command-line --always-approve and ACP yoloMode is not yet selected.
- This does not claim that all Grok automation should bypass permissions; the setting is intended for this explicitly trusted local Agent configuration.
- louiselm-bvo5 tracks the separate rate-limit/runaway-search failure.

title: Run-budget parent and leaf mutually disappear from ready without a reported cycle
description:
## Problem

After maintainer-authorized release of stale Session claims, aggregate `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6` and leaf `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5` mutually block each other even though `br dep cycles` reports no cycle. The leaf therefore remains absent from `br ready`, and the aggregate can only be returned to `in_progress` with `--force`.

## Evidence

Observed on 2026-08-30 in Session `codex/01a0517b-2081-7ff1-b37d-9d03860da2aa` after clearing both stale assignees:

- `br blocked --json` reports `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5` blocked by parent `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6`.
- The same output reports parent `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6` blocked by leaf `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5`.
- `br dep cycles --json` reports zero cycles.
- `br ready --json` contains neither issue.
- `br update louiselm-qbr.3.2.6 --status in_progress --assignee "" ...` is rejected as blocked; adding `--force` succeeds but does not make the leaf ready.

The graph has a parent-child relationship between the two issues plus an explicit dependency requiring the leaf before the aggregate. The likely cause is that readiness treats the hierarchy edge as blocking in the opposite direction from the explicit dependency, while cycle analysis does not report that mixed-edge cycle. This is a hypothesis, not yet verified against `br` internals.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an aggregate parent and a child leaf.
2. Add an explicit dependency making completion of the leaf necessary for the parent.
3. Leave both issues unassigned and make the leaf otherwise ready.
4. Run `br blocked --json`, `br ready --json`, and `br dep cycles --json`.
5. Observe that parent and leaf block one another, neither is ready, and no cycle is reported.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The aggregate/leaf relationship has one coherent scheduling direction: a runnable leaf is not blocked merely because its aggregate parent remains open or in progress.
- `br ready` exposes `louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5` once its real prerequisite work is complete.
- If a mixed hierarchy/dependency configuration can deadlock scheduling, `br dep cycles` or another validation command reports it explicitly.
- Normal status transitions do not require `--force` solely because of this mixed-edge deadlock.
- Regression coverage exercises the hierarchy-plus-explicit-dependency case.

## Not Covered

- Changing the implementation scope of either existing issue.
- Closing either issue.
- Revisiting the already completed stale-claim reconciliation.
close_reason: Removed the reciprocal parent-child edge while retaining the aggregate-to-leaf blocker. Verified leaf is ready, aggregate is blocked only by leaf, dependency cycles are empty, and the prevention rule is recorded in AGENTS.md.

comments.author: codex/01a0517b-2081-7ff1-b37d-9d03860da2aa
comments.text: Root cause confirmed in project graph: louiselm-qbr.3.2.6.5 had a parent-child dependency on louiselm-qbr.3.2.6 while the aggregate had an explicit blocks dependency on the leaf. br readiness follows both directions, but cycle detection does not report the mixed-edge loop. Fix direction: remove the redundant parent-child edge and retain the explicit aggregate-to-leaf blocker, preserving completion ordering while making the leaf runnable. No br source change is in this repository.

The durable lesson is routed to AGENTS.md under Work Tracking: aggregate completion must use one dependency direction. title: acp-proxy never logs session/new, so construction-time params cannot be verified
description:
## Observed

Found on 2026-08-30 while trying to give `louiselm-5tuq` its Live acceptance (AGENTS.md section 5).

`acp-proxy` never records `session/new` in its per-session logs. Grepping every log under `~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/` for `"method":"session/new"` returns nothing, across all sessions and all agents. `session/load` *is* recorded, because its request already carries a `sessionId` the proxy can file the entry under; a `session/new` request has no session id until the response, so it appears to be dropped rather than filed retroactively.

## Why it matters

Everything LouiseLM configures at session construction time travels in `session/new` params — `cwd`, `mcpServers`, and `_meta`. None of it can be verified after the fact.

This directly obstructed `louiselm-5tuq`. That bug was a fix that passed every automated gate while sending nothing on the wire, and the only way to distinguish "the metadata was sent and the model declined to use it" from "the metadata was never sent" is to read the request. For a new Session that read is impossible, so verification had to fall back on reading the installed plugin's source and reasoning about the code path.

A near-miss worth recording: grepping the logs for the bare string `summarized` produced apparent hits that were actually ordinary prose in session content, which reads as success. Structural greps (`"thinking":{...}`) are the only trustworthy form, and they cannot see `session/new` at all.

## Fix direction

Record `session/new` requests, buffering until the response supplies the session id if that is what filing them requires. A separate pre-session log keyed on the JSON-RPC request id would also work.

`acp-proxy` is not this repository, so this may be an upstream report rather than a change here. Filed regardless because the gap is in LouiseLM's ability to perform Live acceptance on anything configured at session construction, which section 5 of AGENTS.md requires for user-visible defects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A newly created Session's `session/new` request, including its full `_meta`, is readable from the proxy log afterwards.
- Existing `session/load` and `session/update` logging is unchanged.

## Not covered

Redaction policy, and any change to what LouiseLM itself sends.
close_reason:
Invalid as filed; no code change made. acp-proxy does log session/new — the premise was wrong because the search only covered ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/. Construction-time frames are written to proxy/connections/<connection-id>.jsonl, which src/logsink.rs:224-229 documents as 'the connection-scoped file used before a session id is known'. That is deliberate and correct: a session/new request carries no sessionId in its params, so the frame cannot be filed under a session that does not exist yet. src/proxy.rs:398-441 then correlates the pending request id with the response's sessionId and calls bind_session, after which traffic moves to the session file.

The linkage is discoverable in both directions. bind_session (logsink.rs:709) writes a session_bound record carrying the session id into the connection log, so 'grep -l <session-id> proxy/connections/*.jsonl' resolves a session back to the connection that created it. Verified: session 9f4fae89-a38b-4d73-be74-33cb34c9a4fc resolves to connection 4c4aacc0-f68c-4103-a50c-89ab7e86c4ba.

The residual is a papercut, not a defect: a session log carries no connection id of its own, so session-to-connection costs one grep across the connections directory rather than a direct lookup. Not worth a change against a repository whose contract forbids speculative work, and not filed as a follow-up.

Correction recorded on louiselm-5tuq, which this issue claimed was unverifiable: the connection log gives direct wire proof that the fix works.

title: Historical Provenance commit inspection rejects valid git output
description:
Selecting a historical Provenance commit from a Decision view fails with `louiselm: git returned malformed commit data`, even though the referenced commit is valid. This blocks the commit-detail drill-down that Case 1 uses to verify historical evidence.

## Observed

Manual QA Case 1 on 2026-08-30 in Neovim, repository `/home/lotso/code/louiselm`, screenshot `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260830_0551_1920x1200_1788061871.png`. The Decision view showed:

`Historical backlog:`
`- ref: 097bcd6d2f5c6cb021a0ff31f78280d9c02a3d5e`
`- 178 issues at decision time`
`- anchor state: closed`
`- since then: 248 added, 0 removed, 19 changed`

Moving to that SHA and invoking `<leader>lP` produced:

`louiselm: git returned malformed commit data`

The SHA is valid: `git show -s --format=fuller 097bcd6d2f5c6cb021a0ff31f78280d9c02a3d5e` succeeds. The exact source command exits successfully, but its output ends with `0x1e 0x0a` (record separator followed by a newline).

## Symptoms

- Historical backlog and drift render successfully.
- Commit inspection fails instead of opening the commit Provenance view.
- The user sees the generic malformed-data error for valid Git output.

## Root cause

The parser at `lua/louiselm/provenance/sources.lua:60-90` loops while `cursor <= #output` and requires every remaining byte sequence to end in `RECORD_SEPARATOR`. `git_log()` at `lua/louiselm/provenance/sources.lua:371-402` invokes Git with `--format=%H%x00%B%x00%x1e`; Git appends a newline after the final record separator. The parser consumes the separator, then sees the trailing newline as a new incomplete record and returns `invalid_git_log`. The UI converts that parse error to the generic message at `lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:358-360`.

## Why it was not caught

The parser tests use synthetic output ending exactly at the record separator. They do not include Git's actual trailing newline, and the historical Decision UI test constructs source data without exercising the cursor-to-commit `git log` round trip.

## Fix direction

Make the parser accept Git's valid trailing whitespace after the final record separator, while continuing to reject genuinely incomplete records and malformed fields. Keep the fix at the shared parser boundary; do not special-case the SHA or suppress the UI error.

## Acceptance

- A regression fixture containing the observed record separator plus trailing newline parses as one commit.
- From the Decision view, placing the cursor on `097bcd6d2f5c6cb021a0ff31f78280d9c02a3d5e` and invoking `<leader>lP` opens the commit Provenance view.
- Existing malformed/incomplete-record tests continue to fail closed.

## Not covered

This report does not yet establish whether the same parser failure affects every multi-commit Decision index lookup; the index itself rendered in this run. No fix was attempted in this QA round.
close_reason: Fixed at d95c5df; live acceptance confirmed by maintainer 2026-08-30

comments.author: claude/d4b23fbe-32a3-4c77-8802-687f31119e64
comments.text:
Fix applied at lua/louiselm/provenance/sources.lua:60-96 (M.parse_git_log): after consuming a record's RECORD_SEPARATOR, skip one immediately-following newline if present, since git always appends its own trailing "\n" after every --format record (confirmed via `git log -n 3 --format='%H%x00%B%x00%x1e' | od -c` in this repo), not only the final one.

Broader finding beyond the reported single-commit case ("Not covered" section): the pre-fix parser was also silently corrupting every commit after the first in a multi-commit git_log() call (e.g. the --all call at lua/louiselm/ui/provenance.lua:702) by prepending git's inter-record newline onto the next record's id field. The same fix resolves both, at the shared parser boundary, without special-casing the SHA.

Regression coverage added in tests/provenance/sources_spec.lua ("git log" group): single-commit and multi-commit fixtures with git's real trailing newline after every record separator, both now parsed correctly; existing malformed/incomplete-record paths untouched and still fail closed. Full mini.test suite (734 cases), stylua --check, and lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning all pass.

Per AGENTS.md Live Acceptance: this was reproduced live (screenshot cited in the issue), so automated gates alone do not close it. Leaving in_progress pending the maintainer confirming, from the Decision view, that placing the cursor on 097bcd6d2f5c6cb021a0ff31f78280d9c02a3d5e and invoking <leader>lP now opens the commit Provenance view instead of "git returned malformed commit data".
