title: QA round: Beads inspector, diagnostics context, reasoning fold, usage spacing, Forensics, winbar clicks
description:
# Manual QA review — since acb65c7 (last recorded round, louiselm-7rup)

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done.

**Build under test:** `acb65c7..HEAD` (25 commits, HEAD=`c56805f`). **Re-run
Setup after any fix.**

Origin: no manual round has covered anything since `acb65c7`. Six behaviors
landed since then with no prior manual pass: the Beads issue inspector
(`e58bf0d`), queued buffer diagnostics (`4b84ac4`/`52768af`), the reasoning
fold (`c56805f`), the usage-line spacing fix (`f75e2a6`), private Session
Forensics collection (`b9dfcc1`), and a Winbar click-routing fix (`437fbf0`).

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Beads issue inspector: cursor on/off an id, bad id, close keys | **passed** — claude/6f651593-5a66-4076-a6a2-b94d9ac51fcd, all 4 sub-cases confirmed |
| 2 | Queue buffer diagnostics for next prompt | **passed** — claude/827084e2-cc79-4a54-a8f4-3229ce4bcbc5, transcript shows label, header, untrusted-data framing, both entries correctly formatted |
| 3 | Reasoning fold closes and exports (`## Reasoning`) | **passed** — deepseek/session-25703dab-5664-4d3a-9b50-7baeec7710c0, 17 live-streamed chunks all folded closed, export has 4 `## Reasoning` sections with full text |
| 4 | Usage line has blank line before/after it (live + resume) | **failed** — live path OK, resume path accumulates blank lines across turns; filed `louiselm-1yei` (pre-existing, not this round's regression) |
| 5 | Session Forensics: collect, view, resource-link queued | **passed** — deepseek/session-f7dbeaea-b8d8-469a-8332-0bedf50ea18d; found+fixed `louiselm-t6j2` (Beads inspector, unrelated) and `louiselm-ysh3` (garbled filenames) along the way |
| 6 | Winbar click in a non-focused split routes to that split | **passed** — deepseek/session-652fd89d-ed42-4da6-a1d3-b789c40b08bd, claude/91086355-53e2-4be1-91ca-1c5d02b5602e (retest after `louiselm-7ios` fix) |

## Setup

Launch the dev Neovim with real agents configured (this is the project's
existing manual-test harness, unchanged by this round):

```
nvim -u manual_init.lua
```

`claude` and `deepseek` agents are pre-configured there; `deepseek` is the one
that actually streams `agent_thought_chunk` during a live prompt (needed for
case 3's live-streaming half — export `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` first, or that half
is blocked and only the mock-replay half of case 3 is testable).

For cases that don't need a live model (1, 2, 4 partly, 5, 6), you can instead
run against the mock ACP agent:

```
LOUISELM_MOCK=1 nvim -u manual_init.lua
```

(check `AGENTS.md` / `lua/louiselm/dev/mock_agent.lua` if the mock launch env
var differs — state what you actually used in your report.)

Confirm the running copy matches source before testing:

```
git -C /home/lotso/code/louiselm rev-parse HEAD   # expect c56805f...
```

Fixtures:
- Case 1 needs a chat buffer with a Beads issue id visible in the transcript
  (e.g. paste `louiselm-zmab` into a message, or reference a real one from
  `br list`), and a case with the cursor on plain text with no id nearby.
- Case 2 does **not** need a real LSP attached — `diagnostics.lua` just reads
  `vim.diagnostic.get()`, so inject fixtures directly instead of depending on
  `lua_ls` being configured/attached in the test buffer. **Order matters**:
  `Chat:mention_diagnostics()` reads `view.source_buffer`, which is fixed to
  whatever buffer was current *when the chat was attached*
  (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2630`) — not whatever has focus later. So:
  1. `:e /tmp/qa_source.lua` — a **named** file. An unnamed/scratch buffer
     here means the chat attaches to `[No Name]` and the fixture script (see
     below, which targets buffer `0`) ends up setting diagnostics on
     whatever *actually* has focus at that moment instead — a mismatch that
     silently produces "No error or warning diagnostics." with no error, as
     happened on the first attempt.
  2. `:LouiselmChat` (or `:LouiselmNewSession`) from that buffer, so it
     becomes `source_buffer`.
  3. Switch focus back to the `/tmp/qa_source.lua` window (opening chat
     steals focus into a split) before running the fixture script.
  4. *Then*, in that source-buffer window, run:
  A single-line `:lua` command still hit a separate "namespace: expected
  number, got nil" error earlier — that means the terminal was splitting the
  pasted line into separate Enter presses (no bracketed paste), so even a
  one-liner isn't safe to paste into the command line. Use a real file
  instead, which Neovim always reads as one chunk regardless of terminal
  paste behavior:
  ```
  :luafile /tmp/qa_diag.lua
  ```
  (script already written; it prints `qa_diag: 2 diagnostics set` on
  success — if you don't see that line in `:messages`, the diagnostics were
  never set and the case hasn't reached the code yet). Clear fixtures when
  done with:
  ```
  :luafile /tmp/qa_diag_reset.lua
  ```
- Case 5 needs `stdpath("state") .. "/louiselm/forensics"` to be readable
  before/after for a permissions check (`ls -la` on the written file).
- Case 6 needs two chat session windows open side by side (`:LouiselmNewSession`
  then split), each with a Winbar showing session tabs.

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Case 2 does not need a real LSP attached. The original setup assumed
  `lua_ls` would produce diagnostics; this environment has no LSP configured,
  so the case never reached the code. Inject diagnostics directly with
  `vim.diagnostic.set()` instead (see Setup) — `diagnostics.lua` only reads
  the diagnostic cache, it doesn't care where entries came from.
- Case 2, second miss (mine): I described a "queued-context fold" as visible
  before the prompt is even sent. There is no such thing — before submit,
  a context item is just an inline `[context: label]` chip on the prompt
  line (`render_chip`, `init.lua:933`); folding only happens on submit
  (`replace_submitted_prompt`, `init.lua:1213-1242`), applied per-window.
  "No fold on the brackets" pre-submit is expected, not a bug.
- Case 3: the `acp-llm-adapter` deepseek session logs
  (`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/sessions/session-<id>/log.jsonl`) also
  redact `agent_thought_chunk` content to `"[REDACTED]"`, same dead end as
  the claude proxy in case 2 — useful only to confirm *that* chunks streamed
  and *how many*, not their text. Fold-closing correctness has to be read
  visually or from an export.
- Case 2, third miss: `mention_diagnostics` reads `view.source_buffer`,
  frozen at chat-attach time, not whatever buffer/window has focus when the
  fixture script runs. Attaching chat from an unnamed buffer and then running
  `:luafile` from the chat's own split set diagnostics on the wrong buffer —
  no error anywhere, just a silent "No error or warning diagnostics." Always
  open a **named** file first, attach chat from it, then switch focus back to
  that file's window before setting fixture diagnostics.
- Don't paste multi-statement Lua onto the `:` command line in this terminal
  — even a single logical line got split into separate Enter presses
  (`namespace: expected number, got nil`, i.e. `local ns = ...` and the next
  statement ran as two separate `:lua` invocations, losing the local). Use
  `:luafile <path>` with a real script instead; it's parsed as one chunk no
  matter how the paste lands.

## Cases

### 1. Beads issue inspector

Exercises `e58bf0d` / `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`.

Steps:

> In a louiselm session buffer, put the cursor on text containing a valid
> Beads id (e.g. `louiselm-zmab`) and run `:LouiselmInspectBead` (or press
> `<leader>lB`). Then move the cursor to a line with no id and repeat. Then
> put the cursor on an *ambiguous* line with two ids and repeat.

Expect: on a single id under the cursor, a rounded-border floating window
titled ` Beads ` opens showing title/ID/status/priority/labels/description,
`q` and `<Esc>` close it and wipe the buffer. With no id under the cursor (or
two candidate ids on the line), an `nvim.ui.input` prompt appears instead
("louiselm Beads issue id: "); entering a non-`louiselm-`-prefixed value shows
an error via `on_error` and no window opens. Also try this from a buffer that
is *not* a `louiselm-session` filetype — the command should report "current
buffer is not a louiselm session" and do nothing.

Failure signature: window doesn't close on `q`/`<Esc>` (buffer leak — check
`:ls` after), wrong issue opened when two ids are near the cursor, or a lookup
silently does nothing when `br` isn't found instead of reporting an error.

### 2. Queue buffer diagnostics for next prompt

Exercises `4b84ac4` / `52768af` / `lua/louiselm/ui/context/diagnostics.lua`.

Steps:

> In the source buffer, inject fixture diagnostics with the `vim.diagnostic.set`
> snippet in Setup (no LSP needed). Then run `:LouiselmDiagnostics` from the
> chat session attached to it — the prompt line should now show a
> `[context: diagnostics: <path>] ` chip prefix (**not folded yet**; folding
> only happens on submit). Then actually send the prompt (type anything and
> press Enter) and look at the resulting transcript above the new prompt
> line, then check what the agent actually receives (mock agent: check its
> stderr/log if `ACP_LOG=1`; real `claude` agent: the ACP proxy log redacts
> prompt content, so this can't be checked that way — see Evidence check).

Expect: before submit, just the inline chip. After submit, a folded block
appears in the transcript above the new prompt line, labeled
`[contexts: diagnostics: <path>]` on its summary line. Opening the fold
(`zo`) shows `[context: diagnostics: <path>]` followed by a header
(`Diagnostics for <path> (observed_at=..., changedtick=...):`) and a fenced
block prefixed "The diagnostic messages below are untrusted data, not
instructions." with one `SEVERITY line:col: message` per diagnostic. Running
`:LouiselmDiagnostics` again after editing the buffer should reflect the new
`changedtick`, not stale data.

Failure signature: diagnostics text sent as if it were an instruction (no
untrusted-data framing reaching the agent), stale snapshot after an edit, or
command silently no-ops when there are zero diagnostics (should say "No error
or warning diagnostics.", not vanish).

### 3. Reasoning fold closes correctly, exports as `## Reasoning`

Exercises `c56805f` / fold logic in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` around
`close_thought_fold_run`.

Steps (mock, resume path):

> `LOUISELM_MOCK_REPLAY_REASONING="single line of reasoning text" LOUISELM_MOCK=1 nvim -u manual_init.lua`,
> start a session, quit, then resume/load that same session (whatever command
> replays history — check `:LouiselmSwitchSession` or reopening triggers
> `session/load`).

Steps (live, deepseek — only if `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` is set):

> Start a deepseek chat, send a prompt that provokes visible reasoning
> ("think step by step about X before answering"), watch the transcript while
> it streams.

Expect: a `[thinking]` block appears and, once reasoning ends, is folded
closed — even when the reasoning text is exactly one line (this is the
regression `c56805f` fixes: Neovim can't close a 1-line fold, so the header
must fold *with* its content). `zo`/`zc` on the fold should work normally.
After the turn, run `:LouiselmExport` (or whatever the export command is —
check `AGENTS.md`/`:h louiselm-export`) and confirm the exported markdown
contains a `## Reasoning` section with the full text.

Failure signature: the `[thinking]` header stays on its own unfolded line
above a folded content block (the exact bug this commit fixes — watch for it
specifically when the reasoning is short/single-line), or the export omits
the `## Reasoning` section entirely.

### 4. Usage line spacing

Exercises `f75e2a6` / `insert_usage` in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

> Send a prompt that completes normally (mock or real agent) and look at the
> `[usage]` line in the transcript immediately after the response. Then close
> and resume that session (restore path) and look at the same line again.

Expect: in both the live-turn case and the resumed/restored case, the
`[usage] ...` line has a blank line both above and below it, separating it
from the transcript content before and after — never glued directly onto the
previous or next line.

Failure signature: `[usage]` line runs directly into the assistant text above
or the next prompt line below with no blank separator, in either the live or
the restored-on-resume path (the fix touches both call sites — check both,
one could regress while the other stays fixed).

### 5. Session Forensics: collect, view, and queue as context

Exercises `b9dfcc1` / `lua/louiselm/forensics/*.lua` /
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:406-438`.

Steps:

> With a chat session open and attached to a real or mock agent, run
> `:LouiselmForensics`. Note the path it reports/queues. Then run
> `:LouiselmForensicsView <path>` with that path. Then send a prompt and
> check whether a `forensics: <path>` context item was queued for it.

Expect: `:LouiselmForensics` writes a JSON file under
`stdpath("state")/louiselm/forensics/`, named `<unix-time>-<record-id>.json`,
readable only by the owner (`ls -la` shows `-rw-------`, i.e. mode 384/0600 —
check the write path in `store.lua:79`, `fs_chmod(path, 384)`). Content is
bounded/sanitized (agent name, ACP session id, cwd, model, capabilities,
dirty file list — capped at 100 entries / 256 chars each per `record.lua`),
no secrets or full env dumps. `:LouiselmForensicsView` opens a scratch buffer
showing the file's raw content. The collected record is queued as a resource
link (`forensics: <path>`, `file://<path>` uri) for the *next* prompt, visible
as a queued-context fold like case 2.

Failure signature: file permissions wider than `0600`, the temp-file-then-rename
write leaves a stray `.tmp-XXXXXX` file behind on success (check the
directory after a normal run), `:LouiselmForensicsView` with no/garbage path
crashes instead of reporting "Forensics record path is required" /
"could not read Forensics record", or unsanitized data (full paths beyond the
256-char bound, more than 100 dirty files) makes it into the written record.

### 6. Winbar click in a non-focused split routes correctly

Exercises `437fbf0` / `Chat:winbar_click` in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

> Open two chat session windows side by side (`:LouiselmNewSession`, then
> `:vsplit` or open a second session in a split so both Winbars are visible
> with session tabs). Keep focus in the *left* window. Click a session tab
> in the *right* window's Winbar (mouse click, not keyboard) that is not the
> currently-open session there.

Expect: focus moves to the right window and it switches to the clicked
session — the click acts on the window it was physically clicked in, not on
whatever window had focus before the click.

Failure signature: the click is misrouted — either nothing happens, an error
about an unavailable window-bar target, or (the pre-fix bug) the *left*
window's session changes instead of the right window's.

## Evidence check

- Case 1: `:ls` after closing the floating window — no leaked scratch buffer.
- Case 2 / 5: originally proposed grepping the ACP proxy log
  (`~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/<id>/log.jsonl`) for what
  reached `session/prompt` params — dead end against the real `claude` agent,
  the proxy redacts `params.prompt` to `"[REDACTED]"` unconditionally. Use
  `:LouiselmToMarkdown` instead and grep the exported file for the queued
  text (mock agent + `ACP_LOG=1` may still work since it doesn't redact, but
  hasn't been confirmed — don't assume it does without checking).
- Case 4: `:%s/\[usage\]//gn` won't tell you about spacing — just read the
  buffer lines directly around the usage line, or `:lua print(vim.inspect(vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0, <n>-2, <n>+2, false)))`.
- Case 5: `ls -la $(nvim --headless -u manual_init.lua -c 'lua print(vim.fn.stdpath("state"))' -c 'q' 2>&1)/louiselm/forensics/` for permissions; `ls` the same dir right after a write to check for orphaned `.tmp-*` files.
- Case 6: purely visual/interactive — no artifact beyond what you see; state clearly that this rests on observation only.

## Cleanup when the round closes

- Delete any Session Forensics files written under
  `stdpath("state")/louiselm/forensics/` during testing (they may contain
  real cwd/git state from this machine).
- Close extra chat session windows/splits opened for case 6.

## Reporting back

Send me the run id, which case, what you saw, and anything surprising. I pull
the evidence myself. If something is wrong I will fix it, and you will need to
redo Setup before retesting.

## Findings this round

**Enhancement — Beads inspector should accept a bare issue id** (`louiselm-y8y1`, not fixed
— filed as a task, not a bug: current `louiselm-` prefix requirement is by
design, just less convenient than it could be).
Surfaced during case 1: all four sub-cases passed as specified, but the
manual-entry `nvim.ui.input` prompt rejects a bare suffix (`zmab`) and
requires the full `louiselm-zmab`. `valid_issue_id()` in
`lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua` could prepend `louiselm-` before validating when
the input lacks it.

**F1 — Usage-line spacing accumulates blank lines during resumed multi-turn
replay** (`louiselm-1yei`, not fixed — two attempted fixes each caused a
different regression elsewhere; filed with full root-cause trace and a
recommended direction for whoever picks it up).
Surfaced in case 4: live single-turn spacing is correct (1 blank), but each
additional replayed turn on resume leaves an orphaned blank line nothing
consumes, so N-turn resumes show N accumulated blanks before the live prompt.
Root cause: `chunk` event handling writes a prose response's trailing blank
directly into the buffer without including it in `transcript_tail`
bookkeeping — a deliberate-looking mechanism that lets tool/reasoning blocks
reuse it as their own leading separator. See the bead for the full trace.

**F2 — Beads inspector rejects any issue with no labels** (`louiselm-t6j2`,
fixed in `8aa5afd`).
Reported live while inspecting `louiselm-1yei` right after filing it (no
labels): `:LouiselmInspectBead` failed with "br returned malformed issue
data". `br show --json` omits the `labels` key entirely rather than emitting
`[]` when an issue has none; `decode_issue()` in `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua`
required it as a table unconditionally. Fixed with a failing-test-first case
in `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua`; full suite green.

**F3 — Forensics record ids render in scientific notation, garbling
filenames** (`louiselm-ysh3`, fixed in `849f5dc`).
Surfaced in case 5: `:LouiselmForensics` wrote files like
`1787715628-1787715628-2.0264597271177e+14.json`. `nvim.uv.hrtime()`'s
nanosecond value overflowed Lua's default `tostring()` into scientific
notation; `lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua` now formats it with `%d`. Fixed
with a failing-test-first case in `tests/session/api_spec.lua`; full suite
green.

**F4 — No winbar click has ever worked via a real mouse click**
(`louiselm-7ios`, fixed in `f81019a`, confirmed live).
Surfaced in case 6: not just the cross-window routing the case set out to
test — clicking *any* winbar tab did nothing, silently, no error. Isolated
with two throwaway winbar click regions independent of louiselm code: a
plain `v:lua.FuncName` click target worked, but the exact pattern this
codebase used, `v:lua.require('mod').method`, did nothing. Vim's
`%{N}@{Function}@` click syntax needs a plain dotted name it can resolve at
click-dispatch time, not a call expression — this has been broken since the
winbar-click feature was introduced (`7b31438`), invisible because unit
tests only ever called `M.winbar_click(...)` directly, bypassing real click
dispatch entirely. Fixed by registering a stable global forwarder function;
confirmed working live after the fix (sessions
deepseek/session-652fd89d-ed42-4da6-a1d3-b789c40b08bd and
claude/91086355-53e2-4be1-91ca-1c5d02b5602e).
close_reason: all descendants closed; QA round complete

title: Refuse louiselm command pickers while a permission decision is open
description:
After 0ed18d0 (louiselm-brx) the chat presents one permission decision at a time, but that queue only covers agent-initiated permission requests. The pickers louiselm opens for its own commands - file, skill, session resume, session switch, agent choice, remembered-permission management, session options - are still unqueued. Opening one while a permission picker is up makes an async provider such as the Snacks picker tear the permission picker down, its on_close fires with no item, and the request is answered cancelled without the user deciding.

Severity after 0ed18d0 is a lost prompt and a spuriously denied tool call, not a hang: the cancelled response releases the decision slot and the queue advances. That is why this is a task rather than a P0/P1 bug.

## Decision: refuse these pickers, do not queue them

Queuing every Picker.select behind the decision slot was considered and rejected:

1. Chained pickers would deadlock. Several flows open a picker from inside another picker callback: manage_permissions (rules -> revoke confirm), open_session_options (option -> value), and critically lua/louiselm/ui/diff/init.lua:114, where a review with several allow lifetimes opens a second picker WHILE holding the decision slot. That slot is only released when the second picker answers, so queuing it makes each wait on the other - the exact failure class louiselm-4wx and louiselm-brx removed.
2. Delayed popups steal input. A queued user-initiated picker opens at an arbitrary later moment, likely after the user moved on and started typing in the chat prompt, and the provider grabs input on open.
3. A leaked slot would freeze the whole UI instead of permissions only. Today a stuck decision still leaves the session picker and close_session reachable; behind one shared slot the escape hatches would be blocked too.
4. open_session_options auto-opens on state_changed -> ready and on attach (lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1070 and :1370), so with two sessions a config picker would surface long after the state change that caused it.

Refusing has none of those properties, is smaller, and cannot deadlock.

## Scope

- While a permission decision is presented (chat decision_active), user-initiated picker commands return false plus an actionable message, e.g. "answer the open louiselm permission request first".
- The auto-opened session options picker is skipped rather than reported.
- Exceptions that stay allowed on purpose: close_session, because it is the escape hatch when a decision is stuck and cancelling that permission is the right outcome when the session is being closed anyway; and cancel, which is not a picker.
- The diff review lifetime picker is untouched: it belongs to the open decision rather than competing with it.

## Acceptance

- Each guarded command returns its refusal without opening a picker while a decision is open, and works normally once the decision is answered.
- close_session still opens its confirmation while a decision is open.
- A diff review with several allow lifetimes still opens its lifetime picker.
close_reason: Implemented in b76a95d as specified: refuse, not queue. DECISION_OPEN_ERROR guards Chat:manage_permissions, switch_session, session_options, pick_file, pick_skill, resume_session, and the agent-choice path of new_session; open_session_options also returns early so the automatic picker is skipped rather than reported. close_session and cancel stay unguarded on purpose, and the diff review lifetime picker is untouched. Test: tests/ui/chat_spec.lua 'refuses command pickers while a permission decision is open' covers every guarded command, proves no extra picker opens, proves close_session still opens its confirmation, and proves the commands work again once the decision is answered. Full suite 197 cases, stylua --check, lua-language-server all clean. README documents the refusal and why it is not a queue.

title: Accept ACP nulls in session discovery
description:
## Problem

`:LouiselmResume` rejects valid ACP `session/list` responses when nullable fields are encoded as JSON `null`. Neovim decodes JSON `null` as `vim.NIL`, while discovery validation currently accepts only Lua `nil` or strings. A Codex response with `nextCursor: null` therefore reports `ACP session/list returned malformed data: nextCursor must be a string` and discards Codex sessions. The same mismatch affects nullable `SessionInfo.title` and `updatedAt`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `nextCursor: null` is treated as end-of-pagination.
2. `title: null` and `updatedAt: null` are accepted and exposed as absent optional values.
3. Non-null, non-string values for all three fields remain rejected.
4. A regression test exercises the JSON-null representation through session discovery.
5. Focused tests, full mini.test, StyLua, and lua-language-server checks pass.
close_reason: Accepted ACP JSON null for session/list nextCursor, title, and updatedAt by normalizing Neovim vim.NIL at discovery validation. Added regression coverage through the public discovery API. Focused session tests pass; full 126-case mini.test suite passes with writable XDG_STATE_HOME; stylua --check and lua-language-server checks pass.

title: Design: notify Android app from a session when an agent needs input
description:
Human-attended sessions (grill-me, qa-review) are fundamentally interactive; most other louiselm sessions are agent-driven (e.g. implementing beads work) and don't need a human at the keyboard in neovim.

Open question: how could a session push a notification to the Android app when an agent hits a point where it needs human input (a decision, a blocker, an approval) while implementing a bead — so the human (not at a desk, e.g. gardening) gets pinged instead of the agent stalling silently?

Design questions to resolve:
- What's the trigger condition for "agent needs something" vs normal progress noise?
- Transport: does this reuse existing agent-mail/push-notification plumbing, or need a new channel to the Android app?
- Should this be opt-in per session type, or inferred from session type (grill-me/qa-review = human-mode, everything else = agent-mode with notify-on-block)?
- What's the minimal actionable payload on the phone (just "come back", or enough context to answer inline)?

title: Assessment
description: A model's advisory opinion on a whole workflow document, prose included, about whether its effects are unbounded. Assessment has no authority: it never gates execution, runs in an isolated Session with an empty capability envelope, and is delivered to an operator at envelope-approval time. Verdicts are stored, keyed on hash(document) + model id + prompt version.
design: Established by the louiselm-qbr.8 grill-me session on 2026-08-26, with explicit maintainer confirmation of the final summary. Proposed by the maintainer as a second checker over prose after rejecting frontmatter-only inspection as too narrow. Named Assessment rather than Scrutiny by maintainer preference. Kept advisory because a gate reading semi-trusted document text can be told to report no hazards, while an advisory opinion read by a human has bounded blast radius.
notes: Use Assessment for the model-read opinion; use Validation for the structural check. Avoid 'review' (taken by qa-review) and 'audit' (taken by br audit). Assessment is stored rather than recomputed so its verdicts can be calibrated against what Runs actually did; staleness is expressed as absence -- 'no current Assessment' -- never as a stale verdict shown as fresh.

title: Explain the LouiseLM vision and recursive identity
description:
## Problem Statement

The README documents development and implemented APIs but does not explain why LouiseLM exists, what the name means, or how its current ACP-backed Neovim foundation relates to the larger idea-to-software vision. Readers cannot yet understand the project before reaching the technical reference.

## Solution

Add a clear product narrative and an original hero banner at the start of the README. Present LouiseLM as alpha software whose north star is turning ideas into software, explain the attention-preserving workflow and its safety boundaries, and show the current manual workflow as one replaceable configuration. Preserve the existing technical reference beneath a concise bridge describing what works today.

## User Stories

1. As a new reader, I want to understand LouiseLM and its recursive name immediately, so that I can decide whether the project matters to me.
2. As a potential user, I want the vision separated clearly from current alpha capabilities, so that I am inspired without being misled.
3. As a creative developer, I want to see a strong default workflow presented as configurable, so that I can imagine building a different workflow with the same substrate.
4. As an operator, I want the vision to preserve my attention, ownership, and approval authority, so that automation remains empowering and legible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The README uses LouiseLM as the project name and includes the exact recursive acronym: LouiseLM Organizes Unruled Intelligent Systems into Emancipated Language Meshes.
2. The opening states that LouiseLM turns ideas into software and clearly labels the project as alpha software.
3. The motivation explains that ideas arrive faster than sustained attention and uses the gardening example without clinical or medical positioning.
4. The vision covers interruption-free capture, later enrichment and explainable triage, focused deliberation, planning, dependency-shaped execution, agent implementation and review, human approval, and an observable operator control plane.
5. Neovim is presented as the deliberate home and cockpit, with headless automation and optional future capture surfaces rather than a promised editor-independent runtime.
6. Local-first ownership, configurable workflow boundaries, strong defaults, replaceable parts, and policy-controlled automation are explicit principles.
7. The current grill-me to plan to beads to coding-agent flow appears as one possible configuration; grill-me, beads, bv, bvr, particular models, and CodeCompanion are not presented as LouiseLM requirements. CodeCompanion is not mentioned.
8. Current ACP chat and session capabilities are distinguished from unimplemented idea capture, ranking, orchestration, and dashboard work.
9. An original banner depicts Louise Michel within a decentralized mesh of people, agents, models, skills, tools, voice capture, ideas, and code. It uses a red, black, and white Commune-era printmaking aesthetic fused with a modern systems diagram, informed by Metelkova street-art energy, with no labels or explanatory text.
10. Existing technical instructions remain accurate and mostly intact beneath the new narrative.

## Implementation Notes

- Expand the top of the existing README rather than replacing the technical reference.
- Add one project-local raster hero asset and reference it with a repository-relative path.
- Use project voice: one brief empowering manifesto-like passage followed by concrete language.
- The visual carries the Louise Michel reference; do not explain that reference in prose.
- Emancipation concerns ideas, workflows, and user choice, never unbounded agent authority.

## Testing Notes

- Documentation and image generation do not require an artificial red test.
- Inspect the final Markdown structure and rendered image reference.
- Run formatting, static-analysis, test, and diff checks required by the repository contract; report any unavailable gate.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing idea storage, capture devices, voice transcription, scheduling, triage, orchestration, dashboards, or agent review.
- Designing a formal plugin API, workflow event schema, storage architecture, mobile application, external daemon, graph UI, or swarm scheduler.
- Changing existing public Lua APIs or technical behavior.
close_reason: Expanded README with the agreed LouiseLM vision, recursive acronym, alpha/current-state boundary, configurable workflow example, attention and safety principles, and corrected single-file test command. Added and inspected an original 1774x887 red-black-white mesh hero as a 640 KB WebP. Verification: stylua --check passed; lua-language-server reported no problems; all 66 MiniTest cases passed after rerunning outside the read-only temp-file sandbox; git diff --check passed; external essay link returned HTTP 200.

title: Blog publishing pipeline never wires the highlighted transcript fragment into the built page
description:
`render-post.sh` generates a highlighted HTML fragment and a matching CSS
file for a transcript excerpt, but nothing in the publishing pipeline ever
references either — the built, served blog page shows the excerpt as plain
text (MyST's own generic `hljs` highlighting, not the nvim-generated one),
with no styling and no visual distinction from any other code block. This is
the last step of the blog publishing pipeline feature (`674939b`, tracked
under the now-closed `blog-publishing-pipeline` feature bead) and it does
not work at all — 0 of N published posts using this mechanism would ever
show the intended highlighted transcript.

## Observed

QA round for the transcript-export/blog-publishing features, case 6 ("does
the highlighted fragment actually reach the published page"),
2026-08-18, working from `blog/post-qa-round` (scaffolded by
`create-blog.sh` in case 5, session `21a0ede3-b65e-4f1c-935d-754f22126384`).

Steps run:
```
cd ~/code/louiselm/blog/post-qa-round
wc -l conversations/*.md   # 3033 lines
# edited blog.md: :lines: 1 -> :lines: 10-40
cd ~/code/louiselm && ./blog/scripts/render-post.sh blog/post-qa-round
# -> "render-post: wrote 1 fragment(s) and nvim-transcript.css to .../blog/post-qa-round"
ls blog/post-qa-round
# -> blog.md, conversations/, conversations-claude-21a0ede3-....L10-40.nvim-transcript.html, nvim-transcript.css
cd blog && myst build --html --strict   # built cleanly, 3 pages, no strict-mode errors
```

Evidence pulled directly from the built site:

- `find /home/lotso/code/louiselm/blog/_build -iname '*nvim-transcript*'` —
  **zero results**. The generated `nvim-transcript.css` never leaves
  `blog/post-qa-round/`; the myst build never copies or references it.
- `grep -o '<link[^>]*>' blog/_build/html/post-qa-round/blog/index.html | grep -i transcript` —
  **zero results**. No stylesheet link to it exists in the served page's
  `<head>` at all.
- The only occurrence of the string "nvim-transcript" anywhere in the built
  output is the inert JSON attribute `"class":"nvim-transcript"` on the
  plain `{literalinclude}` block — that's the `:class: nvim-transcript`
  directive on the literalinclude in `blog.md` being passed through as a CSS
  class with no matching stylesheet to give it any effect. The actual
  generated fragment file
  (`conversations-claude-21a0ede3-....L10-40.nvim-transcript.html`, produced
  by `render-post.sh`) is never included, referenced, or read by anything —
  `blog.md` still holds the plain `{literalinclude}` directive pointing at
  the raw conversation `.md` file, not the generated fragment.
- The code block that does render carries
  `class="block overflow-auto p-3 myst-code-body hljs"` — MyST's own
  generic highlight.js-based styling for an untagged code fence, applied
  because the literalinclude has no language hint. This is visually
  *something*, which is why the page doesn't look broken at a glance — but
  it is not the nvim-specific highlighting the feature is meant to produce,
  and none of `nvim-transcript.css`'s rules apply to it.
- `myst.yml` (`blog/myst.yml:11`) loads exactly one stylesheet:
  `site.options.style: ./blog.css`. No mechanism anywhere adds
  `nvim-transcript.css` to that list, conditionally or otherwise.

## Symptoms

- User sees: a published post's transcript excerpt rendered as a plain,
  unstyled code block — visually indistinguishable from any other fenced
  code block on the site, no indication a special highlighting feature was
  supposed to apply.
- System reports: nothing. `render-post.sh` reports success (and is telling
  the truth — it did produce a correct fragment and CSS file); `myst build
  --strict` succeeds with no warnings; there is no error anywhere in the
  pipeline. The gap is a missing wiring step, not a failure any current
  command surfaces.

## Root cause

`blog/scripts/render-post.sh` (writes `<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` +
`nvim-transcript.css` into the post directory) and `blog.md` / `myst.yml`
(control what MyST actually builds and styles) were built as two
disconnected halves. `blog.md`'s `{literalinclude}` directive was never
changed to consume the generated fragment instead of the raw conversation
file, and `myst.yml`'s `site.options.style` was never made to include
`nvim-transcript.css` (statically, or per-post if that file only exists for
posts using this feature). Exact files: `blog/scripts/render-post.sh`
(generation, confirmed working), `blog/post-qa-round/blog.md` (consumption,
missing), `blog/myst.yml:11` (styling, missing).

## Why it was not caught

`blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh` (referenced in QA_REVIEW.md as covered by
the existing suite) tests `render-post.sh`'s own output — CSS namespacing,
idempotency — in isolation. No test in the suite runs the full pipeline
through an actual `myst build` and inspects the served HTML, because that
requires the mystmd toolchain and a real build, which is exactly what this
manual QA case was written to cover that the suite structurally cannot
reach.

## Fix direction

Two independent pieces, both needed:
1. Have `render-post.sh` (or a follow-up step) rewrite `blog.md`'s
   `{literalinclude}` to point at the generated `.nvim-transcript.html`
   fragment instead of the raw conversation file — or have the fragment
   generation happen as part of a MyST-aware include mechanism rather than a
   side-channel file.
2. Wire `nvim-transcript.css` into the built site's stylesheet — either by
   adding it to `myst.yml`'s `site.options.style` (if it's safe to load
   globally) or by a per-post mechanism, since `style` currently only
   accepts `./blog.css` statically.

Options rejected: none evaluated yet — this bead is filed at the "confirmed
broken, here's exactly where" stage, not the "here's the patch" stage.

## Acceptance

- A post built with a `:lines:` range through the pipeline, when served,
  has a `<link>` (or equivalent) to `nvim-transcript.css` in its page head,
  and the excerpt's rendered HTML matches the generated
  `.nvim-transcript.html` fragment's content (real nvim `:TOhtml`-style
  highlighting), not the raw literalinclude passed through MyST's generic
  `hljs`.
- Regression test: build `blog/post-qa-round` (or an equivalent fixture)
  through `myst build --html --strict` and assert
  `_build/html/**/nvim-transcript.css` exists and is linked from the page
  that embeds the excerpt.

## Not covered

- Whether an excerpt range landing mid-fence (the transcript's own ` ``` `
  fences or `## ` headings) causes a *separate* rendering problem — the
  `:lines: 10-40` range used here happened to land cleanly between a
  heading and the next fence, so that specific risk wasn't exercised. Worth
  a follow-up case with a deliberately fence-straddling range.
- Whether the fix belongs in `render-post.sh`, a new orchestration script,
  or the `create-blog.sh` scaffold step — not decided here.
acceptance_criteria:
- A post built with a `% nvim-transcript: <source> :lines: N-M` marker comment, when run through `myst build --html`, has an `<iframe>` whose `src` is the absolute site-root path of the generated `<post-name>--<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` fragment, and that fragment file exists in the deployed `_build/html/` output, copied there via `project.static_files` in myst.yml (auto-maintained by render-post.mjs, not hand-edited).
- The deployed fragment's content is byte-identical to the one render-post.sh generated locally (proves the static_files copy step actually ran, not just that a stale/partial file exists).
- render-post.sh remains re-runnable: editing a `:lines:` range and re-running regenerates the fragment, blog.md's iframe block, and the myst.yml static_files entry idempotently, without destroying the marker comment that is the author's editable input.
- Regression test (blog/scripts/test-render-post.sh, part 3): a real `myst build --html --strict` against a fixture project asserts the fragment is copied into `_build/html` and that the deployed page's iframe references it at the correct absolute path -- this is the exact gap the bug's "Why it was not caught" section identified as structurally unreachable by the rest of the suite; it is now closed.

Superseded from the original criteria: no shared `nvim-transcript.css` file or `<link>` in the page head exists anymore. Investigation (see closing comment) found MyST's HTML build target does not pass raw HTML through from markdown at all (a literal `<style>`/`<pre>` in blog.md and the `{raw}` directive were both tried and confirmed broken), so delivery goes through an `<iframe>` loading a standalone per-excerpt HTML document instead -- which also makes CSS-selector namespacing and a shared stylesheet unnecessary, since the iframe already isolates each fragment's styling.
close_reason: Fixed: transcript fragments now wired into the deployed page via {iframe} + myst.yml static_files, verified by a real myst build --html --strict regression test (see comment for full design writeup).

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Fixed. Root cause confirmed and two more layers found beyond the original diagnosis:

1. Confirmed MyST's HTML build target has no raw-HTML passthrough at all: a
   literal <style>/<pre> in blog.md gets re-parsed and mangled (TOhtml's
   <span> markup silently stripped), and the {raw} directive only emits
   content for tex/typst export targets -- for html it prints the content as
   escaped literal text. Both empirically verified against myst v1.10.1.
2. `site.options.style` (myst.yml) only accepts a single string, not an
   array -- confirmed by a failed build ("style must be string").
3. The `{iframe}` directive, pointed at an absolute site-root path and paired
   with `project.static_files` in myst.yml, does deliver a fragment's exact
   bytes into the built page -- but `static_files` only accepts literal
   paths (no globs) and copyStaticFiles() flattens every declared file to
   one shared directory by basename, so two posts' same-named fragments
   would silently clobber each other without per-post-prefixed filenames.
4. `{iframe}` has no height option (only width/align/title/placeholder);
   the theme sizes the box via a fixed width-relative aspect ratio it does
   not expose. Fragment documents scroll instead of relying on a height we
   can't set.

Design landed on: standalone per-excerpt HTML documents (inline <style>,
no shared stylesheet, no CSS-selector namespacing -- the iframe's own
isolation makes both unnecessary), embedded via {iframe} at an absolute
`/<post-name>--<slug>.nvim-transcript.html` path, kept in sync with
myst.yml's static_files list by render-post.mjs on every run. blog.md's
authoring format moved from a `{literalinclude}...:class: nvim-transcript`
block to a `% nvim-transcript: <source> :lines: N-M` MyST comment (never
rendered), which render-post.mjs rewrites the following {iframe} block
against on every run without ever touching the comment itself -- this is
what keeps the pipeline re-runnable (create-blog.sh updated to match; both
its own and render-post's test suites updated, 38/38 passing, including a
new real `myst build --html --strict` end-to-end regression test that
verifies the exact wiring gap this bug reported).

Files: blog/scripts/render-post.mjs (rewritten), render-post.sh (header
doc), create-blog.sh (stub format), test-render-post.sh and
test-create-blog.sh (updated + new end-to-end case).

title: Beads inspector: bare-suffix cursor matching (local workspace only)
description:
## Goal

`<leader>lB` opens the local issue directly when the cursor sits on a bare
suffix (e.g. `04cy`, no `louiselm-` prefix), instead of falling through to
the manual `Beads issue id:` prompt.

## Scope

- In scope: `lua/louiselm/ui/beads.lua` cursor-matching path only. When the
  existing prefixed-ID scan (`issue_id_at_cursor`/`current_issue_id`, exact
  function names may have shifted -- re-read the file first) finds no match
  under the cursor, take the raw token under the cursor and try
  `br show <local-prefix>-<token>` against the local workspace (the same
  `br where`-derived prefix the louiselm-04cy fix already wires up).
- Mirror the bare-id handling louiselm-y8y1 already added to the
  manual-entry prompt path in this same file (prepend the local prefix
  before validating/looking up) -- read that code for the exact pattern
  before writing new logic.
- Out of scope: cross-workspace/sibling lookups (that is a separate task,
  louiselm-r98e's other slice). Do not add any `beads.sibling_roots` config
  or sibling-sweep code here.
- Out of scope: changing the existing prefixed-ID match (case 1, already
  shipped in 729c3f2) -- it must keep taking priority and its behavior must
  not change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Given the cursor is on a bare token (e.g. `04cy`) and `<local-prefix>-04cy`
   exists, when `<leader>lB` is pressed, then that issue opens directly, no
   prompt.
2. Given the cursor is on a bare token that does not resolve to any local
   issue, when `<leader>lB` is pressed, then the existing manual
   `Beads issue id:` prompt appears (unchanged fallback).
3. Given the cursor is on an already-fully-prefixed ID (e.g. `louiselm-04cy`),
   when `<leader>lB` is pressed, then behavior is unchanged from before this
   task (bare-suffix logic must not interfere with the existing exact-prefix
   path).

## Testing

- Add cases to `tests/ui/beads_spec.lua` following its existing fake-`br`
  pattern (no real subprocesses, per AGENTS.md determinism rules): bare-token
  hit, bare-token miss falling through to the prompt, and a regression
  confirming the existing prefixed-ID case is untouched.

## Notes

- Full design context and rejected alternatives live in the parent feature
  `louiselm-r98e` and the closed grill question `louiselm-qmmk` -- read those
  before starting if anything here is ambiguous, do not re-derive the design
  from scratch.
- Independently shippable: no dependency on the sibling-sweep task.
close_reason: done

title: Rewrite AGENTS.md for strict idiomatic Neovim Lua
description:
## Goal
Replace the inherited Rust policy with a compact, strict, idiomatic Neovim Lua engineering contract focused on correctness, clarity, simplicity, and fast delivery.

## Scope
- In scope: rewrite the existing AGENTS.md in place for louiselm.nvim; target Neovim embedded LuaJIT/Lua 5.1; define StyLua, lua-language-server, and mini.test gates; lightweight red-green-refactor; LuaCATS/public API rules; module/state/table ownership; structured errors and UI boundaries; strict config validation; safe async vim.system usage; zero runtime dependencies; Neovim API preferences; dangerous Lua escape hatches; concise editing and completion discipline.
- Out of scope: adding formatter, language-server, test harness, Makefile, or CI files; implementing plugin code; including Beads/bv workflow documentation; generic standalone Lua 5.2-5.4 compatibility.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. AGENTS.md contains no Rust/Cargo/Clippy/unsafe-specific policy and no Beads workflow section.
2. The policy is concise and project-specific, with current-stable Neovim and embedded LuaJIT/Lua 5.1 as its runtime contract.
3. The document captures every agreed quality, architecture, error-handling, validation, async/process, dependency, testing, typing, and editing rule without speculative frameworks or compatibility shims.
4. TDD is mandatory for meaningful behavior changes but explicitly lightweight and delivery-oriented.
5. Formatting/static/test completion gates are explicit, and unavailable gates must be reported rather than claimed passing.

## Testing
- Review the rendered Markdown structure and run a text search proving Rust and Beads-specific instructions are gone.
- Check the diff for whitespace errors.
- No Lua project gates are runnable yet because this task intentionally adds no Lua/tooling files.

## Notes
- Rewrite the existing file only; do not proliferate files.
- Prefer enforceable rules over explanatory handbook material.

title: Operator cold-Park discovery and resume
description:
## Goal

Let an operator discover a durable cold-Parked Run after Neovim restarts and resume its recorded ACP Session through the existing asynchronous resume path.

## Scope

- In scope: a read-only capture-service Run listing/show command, an asynchronous Lua client for it, and operator-triggered selection that calls the existing Session API load path with the recorded Agent, ACP Session id, and cwd.
- Out of scope: Android attention delivery, budget changes, Agent-triggered resume, warm-Park behavior, and Provenance actor parsing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A cold-Parked Run can be listed without exposing claim-journal internals or sensitive payloads.
2. Listing and loading are asynchronous; no Neovim main-loop wait or polling is introduced.
3. The operator can select a durable Park and resume it through ACP session/load using the persisted metadata.
4. Resume reports recoverable/lossy status and does not claim the cold Session was restored exactly.
5. Expired/disposed Runs are not offered as resumable Parks.
6. Malformed or unavailable service records produce an actionable error and do not create a replacement Session.

## Testing

- Rust CLI/store coverage for deterministic Run listing and filtering of disposed records.
- Lua service and Chat headless coverage for async discovery, selection, load_session arguments, disposal races, and failure reporting.
- Full project quality gates.

## Notes

The parent qbr.3.3 remains the durable Run/reaper umbrella. This child exists because the parent combines independent service, admission, and operator-resume slices that should be separately testable and reviewable.

title: Parse and validate Agent Skills metadata with lyaml
description:
## Goal

Replace LouiseLM's limited handwritten frontmatter parser with standards-compliant YAML parsing and a thin Agent Skills semantic validator.

## Scope

- In scope: load `lyaml` lazily whenever LouiseLM-managed local skill discovery is required; report a structured missing-dependency error and never install dependencies automatically.
- In scope: parse SKILL.md YAML frontmatter, validate required Agent Skills fields and known standard field types, and preserve the complete original SKILL.md for activation.
- In scope: recognize `disable-model-invocation` and `agents/openai.yaml policy.allow_implicit_invocation`; explicit-only wins on conflict and emits a warning.
- In scope: when optional invocation metadata is malformed or unreadable, retain a core-valid skill as picker-visible, mark it explicit-only, and warn.
- In scope: validate `allowed-tools` as metadata without granting or bypassing ACP permissions; warn when a SKILL.md exceeds 500 lines.
- In scope: ignore unknown extension fields without rejecting or warning, and remove the handwritten YAML subset parser.
- Out of scope: root precedence, symlink traversal, policy selection, catalog transport, and automatic dependency installation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. YAML features supported by LibYAML parse without adding LouiseLM-specific syntax.
2. Invalid YAML or invalid required Agent Skills metadata omits only that skill and yields an actionable diagnostic.
3. Core-valid skills survive broken optional invocation metadata as explicit-only picker entries.
4. Both known invocation controls are honored, conflicts warn, and explicit-only wins.
5. Missing `lyaml` is distinguishable from malformed skill metadata.
6. `allowed-tools` cannot change LouiseLM permission decisions.
7. MiniTest covers valid metadata, YAML syntax errors, semantic errors, extension metadata, conflicts, unknown fields, allowed-tools, and the line-count warning.

## Testing

Use fixture SKILL.md files and assert the public parser/validator result plus diagnostics. Do not test the handwritten parser after removal.

## Notes

`lyaml` is an intentional LibYAML dependency because LouiseLM should not own a partial YAML parser.
close_reason: Replaced handwritten frontmatter parsing with lazy lyaml loading and Agent Skills semantic validation; added explicit-only metadata diagnostics, dependency failure handling, documentation, and passing focused/full gates

comments.text:
# Manual QA review — Parked-Run mutation safety and expired-Park reaping (louiselm-y8vj)

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; tell me to commit or delete it when we are done
(it never gets committed — becomes the y8vj close comment / round bead).

**Build under test:** `HEAD` (`27458e3`), including `wi0y`/`psz9`/`oaib.1`/`oaib.2`/`pck2`
from this session. **Re-run Setup after any fix, and restart Neovim if a Lua fix lands.**

Origin: `louiselm-t6mx`'s Cases 3 and 4 were never run — Case 2 was blocked on the
missing operator Park path (now shipped as `:LouiselmPark`/`:LouiselmResumePark`,
`louiselm-aaw0`). `louiselm-y8vj` reopened those two cases. This round additionally
found and fixed `louiselm-pck2`: the `louiselm-capture` systemd service was
crash-looping since 2026-08-26 (`RestrictAddressFamilies` blocked the new Run
socket), which meant the reaper thread has **never run** in production. Case 4 is
the first opportunity to observe it working at all.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 3a | A cold-Parked Run refuses ordinary generation | **passed** — `louiselm-capture: invalid run: generated work requires an active attached Run`, no issue created |
| 3b | Generated-work ceiling only changes via explicit operator action | **blocked** — not exposed by any UI/command surface, see below |
| 3c | A disposed/reaped Run does not revive or accept late results | **passed** — same rejection against disposed Run `121046b7`, no issue created, not resurrected in `run list` |
| 4 | An expired Park is reaped: excluded from `run list`, retained on disk, claim released | **passed** (after fixing F2, `louiselm-hvot`) — 5 stuck Runs disposed, `louiselm-rcuv`/`louiselm-8tzl` claims released, forensics retained on disk |

## Setup

Confirm the binary the shell and `serve` use are the current release build, and that the
daemon is actually up (it was crash-looping until `louiselm-pck2` just now):

```sh
cd /home/lotso/code/louiselm
cargo build --release --manifest-path capture-service/Cargo.toml
export PATH="$PWD/capture-service/target/release:$PATH"
sha256sum "$(command -v louiselm-capture)" ~/.local/bin/louiselm-capture
systemctl --user status louiselm-capture --no-pager   # must be "active (running)", stable PID
git rev-parse --short HEAD
```

`~/.local/bin/louiselm-capture` is what `serve` and Neovim actually run (per the systemd
unit's `ExecStart`). If you rebuilt and want `serve` to pick it up, `cp` the release
binary over it and `systemctl --user restart louiselm-capture`, then re-check `status`.

Beads workspace: `~/.config/louiselm/capture.env` already sets
`LOUISELM_BEADS_WORKSPACE=/home/lotso/code/louiselm`, so the reaper (a background thread
inside `serve`, polling every 10s) will call `br` against this repo's real Beads DB when it
runs. Use a disposable test issue for Case 4's claim — never a real one.

Runs are stored durably at `~/.local/state/louiselm/workflow/runs/*.json` — that is the
forensics evidence path for "retained after reaping."

## Ground rules learned the hard way (carried over from t6mx, still true)

- **R2 (id format):** `--id` must be a real UUID (`cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid`), not a
  readable string like `qa-park-123` — the store rejects it.
- **R3 (`run list` scope):** `run list` only ever shows resumable `cold_parked` Runs. An
  `active` Run (just admitted+attached) correctly shows as `[]`. Use each mutation command's
  own success JSON as evidence of admission/attachment, not `run list`.
- **R5 (PATH inside Neovim):** if you drive a case through real Neovim, confirm
  `:lua print(vim.fn.exepath("louiselm-capture"))` resolves to the same binary as the shell,
  or you'll be testing two different builds without knowing it.
- **R6 (TTL vs. your own working speed):** don't set a TTL so short that admit→attach→park
  itself outlives it. A few minutes is enough for Case 4; you don't need t6mx's 1000ms.
- **New — tokens are not retrievable after the fact.** `run admit`'s JSON response is the
  *only* place the Run's token appears; `run list` never exposes it (that's what makes the
  `generation_actor`/`reserve_generated_work` token check meaningful as a boundary). This
  means the several `cold_parked` Runs already sitting in `run list` from this session's
  earlier `psz9`/`oaib` testing **cannot** be reused for Case 3a/3c — you don't have their
  tokens. Case 3 needs its own fresh `admit` so you have the token in hand.

## Cases

### 3a. A cold-Parked Run refuses ordinary generation

Exercises `capture-service/src/runs.rs:372-406` (`reserve_generated_work`'s state gate) and
`capture-service/src/generation.rs:94-118` (`BeadsGenerator::generate_with`), reached via the
`run generate` CLI added across `5e195a7`/`5ff2366`/`93db877`/`c01f9a8`.

Steps:

```sh
RUN_ID="$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid)"
louiselm-capture run admit --id "$RUN_ID" --generated-work-max 2 --park-ttl-ms 300000
# copy the "token" field from the JSON above
RUN_TOKEN="<paste the token>"
louiselm-capture run attach --id "$RUN_ID" --session-id "codex/qa-y8vj" --agent codex \
  --acp-session-id qa-y8vj --cwd /home/lotso/code/louiselm --load-session true
louiselm-capture run park --id "$RUN_ID" --session-id "codex/qa-y8vj" --agent codex \
  --acp-session-id qa-y8vj --cwd /home/lotso/code/louiselm --load-session true --claims ""

export LOUISELM_RUN_ID="$RUN_ID"
export LOUISELM_RUN_TOKEN="$RUN_TOKEN"
export LOUISELM_REAL_BR="$(command -v br)"
export BEADS_DB="/home/lotso/code/louiselm/.beads/beads.db"
louiselm-capture run generate --command create -- --title "qa-y8vj probe (should be rejected)"
```

Expect: the `generate` command fails before ever invoking `br` (no issue is created — confirm
with `br list --title-contains "qa-y8vj probe"` returning nothing).

Failure signature: an issue titled "qa-y8vj probe..." actually gets created — that would mean
a cold-Parked Run accepted a generation mutation.

Evidence: exact stderr line from `run generate`, plus the `br list` check showing no issue was
created. Expected text is `louiselm-capture: generated work requires an active attached Run`
(the durable state is `cold_parked`, not the executor's own softer `parked` state, so this is
the branch that fires — not the "budget is exhausted" message).

### 3b. Ceiling raise is an explicit operator action

**Not run — not exposed.** `RunClient:raise`/`resume`/`finalize_resume`
(`lua/louiselm/workflow/run_client.lua:42-44`) talk to the Unix Run socket
(`capture-service/src/run_socket.rs`), but nothing in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua` or
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua` constructs a `RunClient` or registers any command that reaches
it. There is currently no keystroke or `:Louiselm*` command that raises a ceiling. Coverage is
automated-only (`tests/workflow/run_client_spec.lua`, `tests/workflow/resume_controller_spec.lua`).
This matches t6mx's own hedge ("if exposed by the current workflow surface") — it isn't, so
there is nothing for a human to press. Not a defect in itself; flagging in case you want a
`needs-design` question about wiring an operator raise command, separate from this QA round.

### 3c. A disposed/reaped Run does not revive or accept late results

Depends on Case 4's fixture existing first (a `disposed` Run is what the reaper produces —
there is no direct "cancel now" CLI/store action; `disposed` is only reached via expiry, per
`capture-service/src/runs.rs:881`).

Steps: after Case 4 confirms `$EXPIRY_ID` is `disposed`, reuse its id/token (from the admit you
ran for Case 4) exactly like 3a:

```sh
export LOUISELM_RUN_ID="$EXPIRY_ID"
export LOUISELM_RUN_TOKEN="$EXPIRY_TOKEN"
louiselm-capture run generate --command create -- --title "qa-y8vj late-generate probe (should be rejected)"
louiselm-capture run list   # confirm $EXPIRY_ID is still absent, not resurrected
```

Expect: identical rejection to 3a (`generated work requires an active attached Run`) — the
state gate treats `disposed` the same as `cold_parked`, any non-`active` state — and the Run
does not reappear in `run list`.

Failure signature: the generate call succeeds, or the disposed Run reappears as resumable.

Evidence: stderr line, `br list` shows no new issue, `run list` output.

### 4. An expired Park is reaped: excluded from `run list`, retained on disk, claim released

Exercises `39f64f2`, `9460ece`, `731b381`, `capture-service/src/runs.rs:830-888`
(`reap_expired`), only reachable through the `serve` daemon's background thread
(`cli.rs:437-448`, polls every 10s) — this has never actually run in production before
`louiselm-pck2`'s fix.

Create a disposable Beads issue to use as the claim (never a real one):

```sh
TEST_ISSUE="$(br create 'qa-y8vj disposable claim fixture' -t task -p 4 --actor "<your session id>" | grep -oE 'louiselm-[a-z0-9]+')"
echo "$TEST_ISSUE"
```

Then:

```sh
EXPIRY_ID="$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid)"
ADMIT_JSON="$(louiselm-capture run admit --id "$EXPIRY_ID" --generated-work-max 1 --park-ttl-ms 15000)"
echo "$ADMIT_JSON"   # save the "token" as $EXPIRY_TOKEN for case 3c
louiselm-capture run attach --id "$EXPIRY_ID" --session-id "codex/qa-y8vj-expiry" --agent codex \
  --acp-session-id qa-y8vj-expiry --cwd /home/lotso/code/louiselm --load-session true
louiselm-capture run park --id "$EXPIRY_ID" --session-id "codex/qa-y8vj-expiry" --agent codex \
  --acp-session-id qa-y8vj-expiry --cwd /home/lotso/code/louiselm --load-session true \
  --claims "$TEST_ISSUE"
br show "$TEST_ISSUE"   # confirm assignee is set to codex/qa-y8vj-expiry (or however Park recorded it)
date +%s%3N            # note the time
```

Wait at least 30s past `park_expires_at_ms` (15s TTL + one or two 10s reaper polls):

```sh
sleep 35
louiselm-capture run list | grep "$EXPIRY_ID"   # expect: no output
cat ~/.local/state/louiselm/workflow/runs/"$EXPIRY_ID".json   # expect: file exists, "state":"disposed"
br show "$TEST_ISSUE"   # expect: assignee cleared/released
```

Expect: `$EXPIRY_ID` is gone from `run list`, its `.json` record on disk still exists with
`"state":"disposed"` (retained for forensics, not deleted), and `$TEST_ISSUE`'s assignee is
released.

Failure signature: `$EXPIRY_ID` still lists as resumable past expiry; the `.json` file is
missing entirely (over-aggressive cleanup, loses forensics); or `$TEST_ISSUE`'s assignee is
still set (claim never released) or some *other* issue's assignee changed (reaper touched the
wrong claim).

Evidence: `run list` before/after, the on-disk JSON's `state` field, and `br show`'s assignee
field before/after. This proves durable state; it does not prove the reaper's own log output
(not currently surfaced anywhere you can read without journald — `journalctl --user -u
louiselm-capture -n 20` will show only the `serve` process's stdout/stderr, no per-reap log
line exists in the source, so absence of a log line is not evidence of anything either way).

## Cleanup when the round closes

- Close/delete `$TEST_ISSUE` (`br update <id> --status closed` or `br delete`, your call).
- The `qa-y8vj*` and `qa-y8vj-expiry` Run records are harmless to leave — they're disposed or
  will expire/get reaped on their own 15s-5min TTLs; no live Session or real claim is attached
  to them.
- Leftover pre-existing `cold_parked` Runs from this session's earlier `psz9`/`oaib` testing
  (`303778ee…`, `3efbf80d…`, `54f4bf0b…`, `fe6413b9…`, `555af6cc…` from `t6mx`, `63a87d73…`
  from `psz9`) are not part of this round's fixtures — leave them, they'll expire on their own
  24h TTL.

## Reporting back

Send the case number, the exact Run id(s), the command output, and the failure signature if
any. I'll pull `run list` / the on-disk JSON / `br show` myself before classifying it.

## Findings this round

**F1 — `louiselm-capture` systemd unit crash-looping since 2026-08-26** (`louiselm-pck2`,
fixed, `27458e3`). `RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6` predated the Run socket feature
and blocked its `UnixListener::bind`, so `serve` exited before starting the TLS receiver too —
found while scoping this round's Setup, not from running a case. Added `AF_UNIX`, reloaded,
restarted; confirmed stable.

**F2 — the reaper had never actually disposed a Run** (`louiselm-hvot`, fixed). Found running
Case 4: fixture `121046b7-dd43-4026-8922-b1978dbad0d8` sat `cold_parked` 35+s past a 15s TTL
instead of turning `disposed`. `run list` correctly omitted it — that's a read-time expiry
filter, not evidence of reaping. Root cause: `BeadsCleanup::release` (`runs.rs:238`) called bare
`Command::new("br")`, unresolvable under the `serve` systemd unit's minimal PATH (confirmed:
`env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin br --version` → ENOENT). Worse,
`reap_expired`'s `?` on the first failing release aborted the *entire* reap pass, and
`cli.rs:444` discarded the error with `let _ =`, so this had been silently and totally broken
since inception — proved by three independent stuck Runs up to 48h past expiry, one
(`a998611f`, claim `louiselm-8tzl`) leaving a stale assignee on an already-closed issue.

Fixed: `BeadsCleanup` now takes an explicit `br` executable path (`LOUISELM_REAL_BR`, required
by `serve` whenever `LOUISELM_BEADS_WORKSPACE` is set, mirroring the pattern `BeadsGenerator`
already used); `reap_expired` now returns a `ReapSummary` and no longer lets one failing release
block reaping of unrelated Runs; `serve` logs each non-trivial reap pass instead of discarding
the result. Two new regression tests. Deployed: added `LOUISELM_REAL_BR` to
`~/.config/louiselm/capture.env`, rebuilt, redeployed `~/.local/bin/louiselm-capture`, restarted.

Live confirmation, first poll after redeploy: `louiselm-capture: reap pass disposed 5 Run(s), 0
release(s) still failing: []`. All 5 stuck Runs (the 3 above plus this round's own fixture and
one more from 2026-08-30 04:xx) are now `disposed` on disk, cleanup `completed:true`,
`louiselm-rcuv`/`louiselm-8tzl` both confirmed claim-free via `br show`.

**F3 — Case 3a and 3c retested and passed** after F2's fix. Fresh cold-Parked Run and the
disposed `121046b7` both correctly reject `run generate` with `louiselm-capture: invalid run:
generated work requires an active attached Run`; no issue created either time; the disposed Run
did not resurrect in `run list`.

title: Beads inspector: accept bare issue id (no louiselm- prefix) in manual-entry prompt
description:
