title: QA round: hidden prompt context and native folds
description:
# Manual QA review — hidden prompt context and native folds

Working file for the current round. You run the steps, I edit this file as we
learn. Untracked on purpose; when the round closes its final content becomes the
QA round bead and this file is deleted.

**Build under test:** `f2b97471b36d949387580f4219f2f1804fb2fc84`.
**Re-run Setup after any fix.**

Origin: commit `f2b9747` implements beads `louiselm-c8v` and `louiselm-3rn`:
bounded hidden Agent Skills catalogs, exact one-shot selected skill bodies, and
closed native folds containing every context accepted with a prompt.

## Status

| # | Case | State |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | Real-agent hidden catalog and slash deferral | passed — `qa_inject/01a01f16-84a9-78c2-a852-eef2c2be00c8` |
| 2 | Multiple exact contexts, native folding, and no resend | passed — `qa_inject/01a01f1a-f56b-71e2-a2cd-a21580de1825` |
| 3 | Selection-time skill read failure and retry | passed — `qa_inject/01a01f2d-ca56-7320-bb6d-d9b26900984f` |

## Setup

From the repository root, prove the checkout and create isolated fixtures:

```sh
git rev-parse --short HEAD
qa_root=/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747
mkdir -p "$qa_root/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel"
printf '%s\n' \
  '---' \
  'name: qa-catalog-sentinel' \
  'description: Identifies the violet QA sentinel' \
  '---' \
  '' \
  'When explicitly selected, reply with VIOLET-F2B9747-ORIGINAL.' \
  > "$qa_root/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md"
printf '%s\n' 'FILE-F2B9747-FIRST' 'second exact line' > "$qa_root/context.txt"
nvim -u ./manual_init.lua
```

The first command must print `f2b9747`. This recipe uses the installed and
authenticated `codex-acp`, but gives it a unique LouiseLM agent name and forces
the injection policy. In Neovim, configure this checkout before opening the
chat:

```vim
:lua assert(require("louiselm").setup({ agents = { qa_inject = { command = "codex-acp", args = {}, skills = { policy = "inject" } } }, skills = { paths = { "/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/skills" }, policy = "inject" } }))
:checkhealth louiselm
```

Health must report the agent and skill root usable. If `lyaml` is missing,
install the documented Lua 5.1 binding before continuing. Use a fresh
`:LouiselmNewSession` for each case; catalog delivery is intentionally
session-once. This setup is in-memory: after every Neovim restart, run the
setup command above again before starting a case. `manual_init.lua` deliberately
does not persist configuration; without setup it falls back to the default
DeepSeek adapter with no chat skills.

Reset the fixtures before each case:

```sh
qa_root=/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747
mv "$qa_root/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md.off" "$qa_root/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md" 2>/dev/null || true
printf '%s\n' \
  '---' \
  'name: qa-catalog-sentinel' \
  'description: Identifies the violet QA sentinel' \
  '---' \
  '' \
  'When explicitly selected, reply with VIOLET-F2B9747-ORIGINAL.' \
  > "$qa_root/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md"
```

## Ground rules learned the hard way

- Cases do not share a session. A consumed catalog or a failed selection in one
  session must not influence the next case.
- Before sending anything in every new case, the session header must end in
  `skills=inject`. If it says `skills=native` or includes the normal-config
  `AGENTS.md` context, stop: the QA setup is not active and the case is invalid.
- Copy prompts from fenced blocks exactly. A leading `/` deliberately exercises
  a different submission path from natural language.
- The fold is ephemeral UI state. Transcript exports intentionally cannot prove
  its contents or open/closed state.

## Cases

### 1. Real-agent hidden catalog and slash deferral

Exercises `f2b9747` / `lua/louiselm/skills/inject.lua` and the first accepted
prompt path in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

1. Run `:LouiselmChat` and wait for `Session: status=ready`. Confirm the header
   ends in `skills=inject`; otherwise stop without submitting either prompt.
2. Before typing, inspect the prompt. It must be plain `> ` with no
   `skill-index`, `<available_skills>`, or context chip.
3. Submit this command and wait for the turn to finish:

```text
/compact
```

4. The submitted slash command must have no context fold. Submit:

```text
Which advertised skill identifies the violet QA sentinel? Reply with only its skill name. Do not invoke or read it.
```

5. Expect the reply `qa-catalog-sentinel`. Immediately before the authored
   prompt there must be one closed fold whose summary contains only
   `skill-index`. Focus must end on the new editable `> ` prompt.
6. Without moving the cursor or running another command, write objective
   buffer/fold evidence:

```vim
:lua local l=vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0,0,-1,false); local f=-1; for i,s in ipairs(l) do if s:find("> [contexts:",1,true)==1 then f=i end end; local o={string.format("fold=%d:%d method=%s cursor=%s",f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosed(f) or -1,f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosedend(f) or -1,vim.wo.foldmethod,vim.inspect(vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)))}; vim.list_extend(o,l); vim.fn.writefile(o,"/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-1.txt")
```

Expect: the real peer identifies the private fixture from the hidden catalog;
the slash turn does not consume or render that catalog; the natural-language
turn renders it once as a closed native fold; focus returns to the draft.

Failure signature: catalog XML or a `skill-index` chip is visible before send;
the slash command gains a fold; the model cannot name the sentinel; the fold is
open, has the wrong summary, or leaves the cursor inside submitted text.

7. Run `:LouiselmSessionId` and retain the copied id as the run id.

### 2. Multiple exact contexts, native folding, and no resend

Exercises `f2b9747` / accepted context rendering and picker-body capture in
`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

1. If Neovim was restarted, rerun the QA setup command first. Start a fresh
   `:LouiselmNewSession`; the only configured agent must be `qa_inject`, and its
   ready header must end in `skills=inject`. Stop if DeepSeek/default appears.
2. Run `:LouiselmPickFile /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747`, then select
   `context.txt`.
3. Run `:LouiselmPickSkill`, then select `qa-catalog-sentinel`.
4. Confirm two compact chips remain on the editable prompt; the automatic
   catalog remains invisible. Submit:

```text
Read the attached file and selected skill. Reply only with their two uppercase tokens, in attachment order.
```

5. Expect `FILE-F2B9747-FIRST VIOLET-F2B9747-ORIGINAL`. One closed fold must
   precede the visible user prompt. Its summary order must be `skill-index`,
   `file: ...context.txt`, then `skill: qa-catalog-sentinel`.
6. Put the cursor on the summary and press `zo`. Verify the file context shows
   the exact resource-link line
   `Referenced file: /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/context.txt` and the selected
   skill context shows the complete `SKILL.md` body. The user prompt must remain
   outside the fold. Press `zc` and verify it closes normally.
7. Submit `Reply only NEXT.` without selecting more context. No second context
   fold should appear and the reply should be `NEXT`.
8. Run `:LouiselmSessionId`, retain the run id, then capture evidence:

```vim
:lua local l=vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0,0,-1,false); local f=-1; for i,s in ipairs(l) do if s:find("> [contexts:",1,true)==1 then f=i end end; local o={string.format("fold=%d:%d method=%s cursor=%s",f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosed(f) or -1,f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosedend(f) or -1,vim.wo.foldmethod,vim.inspect(vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)))}; vim.list_extend(o,l); vim.fn.writefile(o,"/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-2.txt")
```

Expect: normal fold commands work; opened contents show the exact transported
resource-link fields and selected-skill text in transport order;
closing/reopening presentation does not resend any context on the next turn.

Failure signature: chip order differs from fold order; the resource-link URI or
selected skill body is summarized, truncated, or reordered; `zo`/`zc` do not
work; the prompt is swallowed by the fold; the second turn gains a context fold
or sees an old token unexpectedly.

### 3. Selection-time skill read failure and retry

Exercises `f2b9747` / the real picker callback timing and local-failure
retention path in `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`.

Steps:

1. If Neovim was restarted, rerun the QA setup command first. Start a fresh
   `:LouiselmNewSession`; the only configured agent must be `qa_inject`, and its
   ready header must end in `skills=inject`. Stop if DeepSeek/default appears.
2. Run `:LouiselmPickSkill` but leave the picker open. In another terminal run:

```sh
mv /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md.off
```

3. Back in the picker, select `qa-catalog-sentinel`. A precise read error must
   appear, while a `skill: qa-catalog-sentinel` chip remains selected.
4. Type `retry preserved` and submit. It must fail locally: no agent turn, no
   submitted fold, and both the chip and editable text remain.
5. Capture the failed state:

```vim
:lua local l=vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0,0,-1,false); vim.fn.writefile(l,"/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-3-failure.txt")
```

6. Restore the file in the other terminal:

```sh
mv /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md.off /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/skills/qa-catalog-sentinel/SKILL.md
```

7. Submit the unchanged prompt again. It should now be accepted, consume the
   selection once, create one closed context fold, and return focus to a clean
   prompt. Capture the final state:

```vim
:lua local l=vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(0,0,-1,false); local f=-1; for i,s in ipairs(l) do if s:find("> [contexts:",1,true)==1 then f=i end end; local o={string.format("fold=%d:%d method=%s cursor=%s",f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosed(f) or -1,f>0 and vim.fn.foldclosedend(f) or -1,vim.wo.foldmethod,vim.inspect(vim.api.nvim_win_get_cursor(0)))}; vim.list_extend(o,l); vim.fn.writefile(o,"/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-3-retry.txt")
```
8. Run `:LouiselmSessionId` and retain the run id.

Expect: a real filesystem race cannot lose the selection or draft, and retry
uses the restored exact body without requiring another picker activation.

Failure signature: the chip disappears on read failure; Enter sends a turn or
creates a fold while the file is absent; the draft changes; restoring the file
still cannot submit; retry attaches the skill more than once.

## Evidence check

After each case, from the repository root run:

```sh
sed -n '1,120p' /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-1.txt
sed -n '1,160p' /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-2.txt
sed -n '1,120p' /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-3-failure.txt
sed -n '1,160p' /tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747/case-3-retry.txt
```

The first evidence line must report `method=manual`; accepted-context snapshots
must report a positive closed range, while the case 3 failure snapshot must
contain the chip and draft but no `[contexts:` summary. The remainder proves
exact visible buffer contents and prompt separation. It cannot alone prove what
the remote model received; the sentinel response and run id settle that part.

This check uses the same `foldclosed()`, buffer-line, and cursor APIs validated
against known-good headless runs in `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` (309-case full
suite passed on the build under test).

## Cleanup when the round closes

Close all QA chat sessions and remove `/tmp/louiselm-qa-f2b9747`. No permission
rules or repository files should remain. The final QA record becomes one
`qa-round` bead; then delete this working file without committing it.

## Reporting back

Send me the run id, case number, what you saw, and anything surprising. I will
pull the evidence files myself. If something is wrong I will file it before
fixing it, update this file, and tell you which cases need a fresh Setup rerun.

## Findings this round

No product findings yet.

## Results this round

- Case 1 passed on `qa_inject/01a01f16-84a9-78c2-a852-eef2c2be00c8`.
  Buffer evidence reports `skills=inject`, one closed manual fold at lines 9–20
  with summary `skill-index`, and the cursor on the final editable prompt. The
  pinned Codex rollout contains exactly one sentinel catalog block, paired with
  the natural-language prompt, followed by the exact `qa-catalog-sentinel`
  response. The preceding `/compact` transcript entry has no context fold.
- Case 2 passed on `qa_inject/01a01f1a-f56b-71e2-a2cd-a21580de1825`.
  Buffer evidence reports one closed manual fold at lines 6–27, exact summary
  order `skill-index`, file, skill, the transported resource-link URI, and the
  complete selected `SKILL.md` body. The authored prompt and later `NEXT` turn
  remain outside it, with the cursor on the final editable prompt. The rollout
  returns `FILE-F2B9747-FIRST VIOLET-F2B9747-ORIGINAL`, then shows the second
  turn contains only `Reply only NEXT.` and returns `NEXT`.
- Case 3 passed on
  `qa_inject/01a01f2d-ca56-7320-bb6d-d9b26900984f`. The failure snapshot keeps
  the `skill: qa-catalog-sentinel` chip and `retry preserved` draft with no
  submitted context fold. The pinned rollout contains exactly one retry prompt
  and one selected-skill body, followed by `VIOLET-F2B9747-ORIGINAL`, proving
  the failed local attempt did not reach the agent. The retry snapshot reports
  one closed manual fold at lines 6–25, exact `skill-index` then selected-skill
  order and body, the authored prompt outside it, and the cursor on the final
  editable prompt. A later typed `L` was present when the evidence command was
  finally captured, so initial draft cleanliness rests on the tester's manual
  observation rather than that delayed snapshot.

## Round conclusion

All three cases passed on build `f2b9747`; no product findings were discovered.
The round confirmed behavior the automated suite cannot settle alone: the real
Codex ACP payload shape, native Neovim fold interaction and focus, and a real
filesystem race between picker display and skill selection. The automated

boundaries, which is why this round found recipe problems rather than product

title: Ordinary :q exits with two live chat sessions
description:
Two live LouiseLM chat sessions are visible in :LouiselmSwitchSession, but ordinary :q still exits Neovim from the only chat window instead of warning and refusing the quit.

## Observed

Manual QA round for commit 41fec85 on 2026-08-22. The tester confirmed setup was valid: the session picker displayed two sessions. They then ran :q; Neovim closed.

Verbatim report: "setup is ok i can see 2 sessions in picker, but :q still closes neovim"

## Symptoms

- User sees two attached sessions in the picker.
- :q closes Neovim.
- Expected warning about multiple open sessions is not observed, and the process exits.

## Root cause

Unknown. The intended callback is at lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:255-270 and calls Chat:should_block_quit() before raising at line 267. The predicate is at lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1892-1908. Hypotheses include QuitPre error handling not cancelling :q as assumed, the callback not being active in the manual startup path, or the predicate seeing a different window/current-buffer/session state. Discriminate by inspecting the live QuitPre autocmd and directly evaluating the predicate in the failing setup.

## Why it was not caught

The automated test only calls Chat:should_block_quit() with fake sessions and does not execute a real Neovim :q through the registered QuitPre callback.

## Fix direction

Reproduce through the real registered autocmd and use a Neovim-supported quit cancellation mechanism at the narrowest boundary. Add a regression test that executes the production QuitPre path and proves ordinary :q remains in Neovim with two live sessions.

## Acceptance

- A regression test fails before the fix and passes after.
- With exactly one window showing a chat buffer and two live attached sessions, :q leaves Neovim open and shows an actionable warning.
- With one live session, an ordinary buffer, or another window present, :q behaves normally.

## Not covered

This round has not yet tested Cases 2-4. No fix has been attempted.
close_reason: Fixed in 5146007. QuitPre now opens a temporary duplicate chat window so the pending :q closes only that window; added production autocmd regression coverage in tests/ui/command_spec.lua. Gates: focused command suite 24/24, full MiniTest suite 330/330, stylua --check ., lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning.

title: Forensics record id renders in scientific notation, producing garbled filenames
description:
## Symptom

`:LouiselmForensics` writes files like
`1787715628-1787715628-2.0264597271177e+14.json` instead of a clean,
consistently-formatted name. Reported live during manual QA case 5.

## Evidence

```
$ ls -la ~/.local/state/nvim/louiselm/forensics/
1787677276-1787677276-1.8361102155298e+14.json
1787677426-1787677426-1.8376120166499e+14.json
1787715628-1787715628-2.0264597271177e+14.json
```

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/session/registry.lua:254` (as of this QA round):

```lua
id = string.format("%d-%s", os.time(), tostring(nvim.uv.hrtime())),
```

`nvim.uv.hrtime()` returns a nanosecond-precision value large enough that
Lua's default `tostring()` on the resulting double renders in scientific
notation once past a few significant digits, rather than a plain integer
string. `store.lua`'s `record_name()` then prepends another `os.time()`
prefix on top, producing the double-timestamp-plus-scientific-notation
filename shown above.

## Fix

Use `%d` formatting instead of `tostring()` for the hrtime component:

```lua
id = string.format("%d-%d", os.time(), nvim.uv.hrtime()),
```

Filed and fixed during manual QA round (case 5, session
deepseek/session-f7dbeaea-b8d8-469a-8332-0bedf50ea18d).

title: Health check reports 'no output' for subcommand-based agent CLIs
description:
`:checkhealth louiselm` reported "version command returned no output" for
any agent whose launch `args` represent a subcommand invocation rather than
a bare binary name (e.g. `acp-llm-adapter serve --backend deepseek`, wrapped
by a debug script) — the installed-version check silently produced no
usable version, unlike sibling agents launched with a single-token args
array (`codex-acp`, `claude-agent-acp`), which worked correctly.

## Observed

Live user report, session `claude/e1118174-fdbe-4320-9086-4d4da9517f3c`,
after running `:checkhealth louiselm`:

```
louiselm health: /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh — @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.1.14 (latest 1.6.0 available)
louiselm health: /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh — 0.66.0 (latest 0.70.0 available)
louiselm health: /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh: version command returned no output
louiselm health: /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh: version command returned no output
louiselm: codex is outdated (@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.1.14 installed, 1.6.0 upstream)
louiselm: claude is outdated (0.66.0 installed, 0.70.0 upstream)
```

The two silent failures corresponded to the `deepseek` and `glm` agent
entries in `~/dotfiles/nvim/.config/nvim/lua/config/plugins/louiselm.lua`,
both configured as:

```lua
deepseek = {
  command = "/home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh",
  args = { "acp-llm-adapter", "serve", "--backend", "deepseek" },
  ...
}
```

Reproduced directly on the command line:

```
$ /home/lotso/code/acp-llm-adapter/acp-debug.sh acp-llm-adapter serve --backend deepseek --version
(no output, exit 0)
$ acp-llm-adapter --version
acp-llm-adapter 0.7.2
$ acp-llm-adapter serve --help
Usage: acp-llm-adapter serve [OPTIONS] --backend <BACKEND>
Options: --backend <BACKEND>, --max-turn-requests <N>, -h/--help
(no --version flag on the `serve` subcommand)
```

## Symptoms

- `:checkhealth louiselm` shows "version command returned no output" for
  any agent whose `args` is a multi-token subcommand invocation.
- No outdated-version warning is possible for such agents even when one is
  warranted, since the installed version never resolves.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua` `M.check` (before the fix) unconditionally
built the version-query command as `{definition.command, ...definition.args,
"--version"}`. That assumes `--version` is a valid trailing flag for
whatever `args` represents. For a subcommand-based CLI, `--version` must
appear *before* the subcommand (`acp-llm-adapter --version`, not
`acp-llm-adapter serve --backend deepseek --version`); the `serve`
subcommand's own flag parser has no `--version` flag, so clap accepts the
process launch, `serve` starts (a real ACP server reading stdio), and it
exits 0 with no stdout once its unfed stdin hits EOF under `vim.system`,
which the code correctly reports as "no output" rather than crashing — the
inputs to that classification were simply wrong for this shape of `args`.
This is a config-construction gap, not a logic bug in the no-output
classification itself.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/agent/health_spec.lua`'s "includes wrapper args before --version"
test (from the immediately preceding commit `6b2a69f`) only exercises a
wrapper forwarding a single-token binary name (`{"codex-acp"}`), which is
flag-compatible with a trailing `--version`. No test exercised a multi-token
subcommand `args` array, which is exactly the shape that breaks.

## Fix direction

Mirror the existing `latest` field's design (`command`/`args`/`env`,
verbatim, nothing auto-appended) with a new optional per-agent `version`
override, used in place of the `command args... --version` heuristic when
present. Same shape, same validation path (`agent/config.lua`), same
top-level `Louiselm.setup()` schema (`config.lua`). Deliberately not:
sniffing the CLI's argv structure, hardcoding `acp-llm-adapter` as a special
case, or dropping `args` from the default heuristic entirely (codex/claude
still need their single-token `args` forwarded to the wrapper script for
`--version` to resolve the right binary).

## Acceptance

- `tests/agent/config_spec.lua`: 6 new cases mirroring `latest`'s coverage
  for the new `version` field (accept, default args, leave nil, reject
  malformed, reject non-table).
- `tests/agent/health_spec.lua`: "installed-version override" group — uses
  the override verbatim instead of appending `--version` to the launch args;
  uses the override's own `env` instead of the agent's launch `env`; reports
  a missing override executable gracefully without spawning.
- `tests/schema/setup_spec.lua`: accepts/rejects the per-agent `version`
  override through `Louiselm.setup()`'s closed schema.
- Verified against the real binary: `acp-debug.sh acp-llm-adapter --version`
  → `acp-llm-adapter 0.7.2`, and `Health.check` with the override configured
  → `{ok = true, version = "acp-llm-adapter 0.7.2"}`.
- Full suite green: 277/277. `stylua --check` and
  `lua-language-server --checklevel=Warning` clean on all touched files.

## Not covered

The `deepseek`/`glm` "skill discovery found 31 issue(s)" notification in the
same `:checkhealth` output is unrelated (skill metadata parsing, not agent
version checking) — not investigated as part of this bug, left for separate
filing if it's still present after this fix.
close_reason: Fixed: added optional per-agent 'version' override (lua/louiselm/agent/config.lua, lua/louiselm/agent/health.lua, lua/louiselm/config.lua), mirroring the existing 'latest' field's design — verbatim command/args/env, nothing auto-appended. Applied to the user's real dotfiles config (deepseek/glm now specify version={command=acp-debug.sh, args={acp-llm-adapter, --version}}). Verified against the real acp-llm-adapter binary through the real acp-debug.sh wrapper: Health.check now returns {ok=true, version='acp-llm-adapter 0.7.2'} instead of 'version command returned no output'. Tests: tests/agent/config_spec.lua (6 new cases), tests/agent/health_spec.lua ('installed-version override' group, 3 cases), tests/schema/setup_spec.lua (2 new cases). Full suite 277/277, stylua/lua-language-server clean.

title: Grok ACP options are unavailable in LouiseLM
description:
LouiseLM reports that a Grok ACP Session has no supported options even though Grok advertises model and reasoning-effort options. The defect blocks the operator from opening the options picker and gives no indication that the Agent exposed non-standard metadata. The maintainer reported the upstream defect through Grok's /feedback command; that channel provides no issue id or status, so upstream consideration cannot currently be verified except by a later response or observed release behavior.

## Observed

Session grok/01a0567b-0749-7552-bfe4-b98131b0b6e2, 2026-08-31, Grok Build 1.0.13 via `acp-proxy -- grok agent --always-approve stdio`.

Captured ACP evidence:
- `/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/01a0567b-0749-7552-bfe4-b98131b0b6e2/log.jsonl:5` contains the `session/new` response.
- The response advertises `grok-4.6`, `xhigh`, `high`, `medium`, and `low` under `_meta.x.ai/sessionConfig.options`.
- The connection initialize frame advertises no standard config options, and no `session/set_config_option` request was emitted because LouiseLM rejected the empty internal list first.
- The operator-visible error was `louiselm: session has no supported options`.

## Symptoms

- Grok options are visible in the ACP payload but unavailable from LouiseLM.
- `:LouiselmSessionOptions`/the options action exits before sending a request.
- Other ACP Agents using standard `result.configOptions` are unaffected.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:628-644` only normalizes `session_result.configOptions`; it ignores vendor metadata. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:3781-3782` then reports the empty normalized list as `session has no supported options`.

## Why it was not caught

Existing tests cover standard ACP `configOptions` responses and do not include a captured Grok response containing `_meta.x.ai/sessionConfig.options`.

## Fix direction

Keep the core ACP option model standard and improve the LouiseLM diagnostic when an Agent returns no standard `configOptions`. Do not silently add a Grok-specific compatibility mapping until xAI confirms whether its vendor metadata is an intentional ACP extension. Preserve standard behavior for all other Agents.

## Acceptance

- A regression test captures the Grok response shape and proves the user-facing diagnostic is specific about unsupported/non-standard option advertisement.
- Standard ACP option discovery and changing continue to pass unchanged.
- Record remains open for upstream confirmation; a future Grok release or direct response can show whether the reported upstream defect was addressed.
close_reason: Fixed in 31bd9d7; UI now identifies missing standard ACP options. Maintainer confirmed live Grok retest in grok/01a0568f-0b1b-72b1-a84e-64a3abdfc5ff; standard ACP behavior and full 801-case suite passed. Upstream /feedback remains untracked; compatibility follow-up is louiselm-305s.

title: Handle command and unknown permission requests in chat UI
description: Confirmed dogfood gap. The real claude-agent-acp file-edit probe emitted an ACP permission request and could be cancelled by a session event consumer. ui/chat/init.lua handles permission_requested only when operation.kind is file_edit; command and unknown requests are ignored, leaving the agent request unresolved in the interactive chat. Add a user-facing response path for every askable permission kind and cover a real fast-event-to-scheduled UI flow without auto-approving unscoped operations.

title: Grill-me needed: should LouiselmPickSkill preview SKILL.md content, and who owns that responsibility
description:
Do not resolve this question in passing.

Question: should the skill picker (:LouiselmPickSkill) show a preview of the
selected SKILL.md's content, and if so, where does that responsibility live —
in louiselm, or is it purely a matter of the user's vim.ui.select provider
config (e.g. Snacks)?

Context/evidence:
- lua/louiselm/ui/context/skill-picker.lua calls Picker.select (a thin wrapper
  over vim.ui.select) with items = full skill tables and
  format_item = "name — description". No content/preview field is passed.
- lua/louiselm/ui/picker.lua is a one-line passthrough to vim.ui.select,
  by design.
- README.md already documents an explicit boundary: "LouiseLM sends picker
  choices through vim.ui.select, so the active UI provider owns their layout
  ... LouiseLM intentionally does not detect or reconfigure a vim.ui.select
  provider." (README.md around line 290-307, re: Snacks wrap workaround)
- vim.ui.select's contract (items, {prompt, format_item}, callback) has no
  preview concept at all. Even a Snacks-based vim.ui.select shim only ever
  receives a formatted string per item, not a file path or body text, so no
  picker backend can preview skill content today no matter how the user
  configures it.
- AGENTS.md restricts extension points to four established boundaries
  (headless session API, typed events, permission policies, agent
  configuration) and instructs against building extension points for
  hypothetical consumers.

Threads worth pulling:
- Is "preview of SKILL.md body" valuable enough DX to justify enriching what
  louiselm passes into vim.ui.select (e.g. attaching skill.content in a field
  some providers know how to render), even though most providers will ignore
  it?
- Would that count as reconfiguring/detecting a provider (violates the
  documented boundary), or is it just "pass richer data, providers opt in"
  (does not)?
- Alternative: a dedicated `:LouiselmPickSkill` preview split built and owned
  entirely by louiselm (bypassing vim.ui.select for this one command), trading
  the "one generic picker" simplicity for a skill-specific UX.
- Is this worth doing at all given louiselm has "no external users" yet
  (AGENTS.md ยง1), or should it wait for a concrete user complaint?
close_reason: Resolved: implemented option B (kind + file metadata)

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Resolved: option B. Neovim's vim.ui.select has a stable, core kind hint field (used by e.g. the LSP code-action picker) that plugins reimplementing vim.ui.select may key off. Snacks' vim.ui.select shim already supports per-kind picker config via picker.sources.select.kinds[<kind>].

Implemented in lua/louiselm/ui/context/skill-picker.lua: M.pick now tags the vim.ui.select call with opts.kind = "louiselm_skill" and adds a file field (skill.path) to each item. This doesn't detect or reconfigure any provider — it exposes metadata a provider may opt into, same as the existing path field already carried on louiselm.skills.Skill. Content is deliberately not read at pick time (see Chat:pick_skill), so file (not content) is the only viable preview source anyway.

Verified against installed snacks.nvim source: select.lua merges picker_opts.kinds[opts.kind] into the resolved picker config, and the "file" previewer (Snacks.picker.preview.file) reads item.file. The select layout preset hides the preview pane by default (hidden = {preview}), so the README example switches to layout.preset = "default" for that kind.

Tests: extended tests/ui/context_spec.lua to assert opts.kind and item.file; TDD red confirmed before the fix. Full mini.test suite, stylua, and lua-language-server all green. README.md documents the opt-in Snacks config.

title: GitLab CI: build and deploy blog/ to blog.bartab.fr via Pages
description:
## Goal
A GitLab CI pipeline in this repo that builds blog/ with MyST and deploys it to blog.bartab.fr via GitLab Pages, with zero Neovim dependency in the CI image.

## Scope
- In scope: .gitlab-ci.yml job(s) running `myst build --html` against blog/ and publishing the result as a GitLab Pages artifact; a note on the one-time manual DNS/CNAME step needed to point blog.bartab.fr at GitLab Pages (DNS itself is outside this repo's automation).
- Out of scope: rendering nvim-transcript excerpts in CI (explicitly not done — that only ever happens locally, output is committed); anything at the bartab.fr root domain.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Pushing to the relevant branch triggers a pipeline that runs `myst build --html` against blog/ and succeeds without installing or invoking Neovim.
2. The build output is published via GitLab Pages and reachable at blog.bartab.fr (once DNS is pointed, noted as a manual prerequisite).
3. The CI job fails loudly (not silently) if blog/ fails to build — e.g. a broken literalinclude reference.

## Testing
- Pipeline run validation: a green pipeline with a published Pages artifact is the acceptance test here, not a unit test.

## Notes
- Depends on the MyST scaffold task (needs a buildable blog/ project to point CI at).
- Benefits from render-post.sh existing for a realistic end-to-end validation (a post with real rendered excerpts) but does not strictly require it — CI can be stood up and proven against the bare scaffold first.
- Parent feature: louiselm-r1k.

title: Session load hides an active-writer conflict as Internal error
description:
When Codex rejects `session/load` because another client still owns the thread, louiselm reports only `ACP session/load failed: Internal error`. The actionable server detail is discarded, so users cannot tell that they must close the original writer before retrying.

## Observed

Seen 2026-08-21 while loading Codex session `01a01fd3-bcf8-74d2-bf0c-edc7b9329101` from a second Neovim process.

`/home/lotso/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/20260821-040016-1245805-codex-acp-stdout-jsonrpc.log:2` contains: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"Internal error","data":{"details":"thread 01a01fd3-bcf8-74d2-bf0c-edc7b9329101 already has an active writer"}}}`.

The original chain was still alive: outer Neovim PID 1020909, embedded Neovim PID 1020915, codex-acp PID 1021253, and Codex app-server PID 1021279. The UI displayed only `louiselm: ACP session/load failed: Internal error`.

## Symptoms

- Session discovery succeeds and shows the expected session.
- Selecting it fails with a generic internal error.
- The user is not told to close the original session owner and retry.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:90` reduces every structured JSON-RPC error to `error_value.message`. The ACP response carries the discriminating cause in `error.data.details`, so `handle_initialized` at `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:454` loses it before emitting the session error. The adapter also arguably should promote this known conflict into its public message, but louiselm currently has the structured context and discards it unconditionally.

## Why it was not caught

Session load tests cover a plain message such as `unknown session`; they do not use an ACP error containing a generic message plus safe structured details, nor a concurrent-writer rejection from Codex.

## Fix direction

Preserve structured error context internally and produce a sanitized actionable message. Do not blindly display arbitrary `data`, which could contain sensitive adapter payloads. Either recognize a bounded safe `data.details` string under an explicit policy or have codex-acp map the active-writer conflict to its public error message and make louiselm identify the adapter/debug log for generic internal errors.

## Acceptance

- A regression test captures the exact active-writer JSON-RPC shape.
- The user-visible failure says that the thread is already open elsewhere and tells the user to close the original writer before retrying.
- Arbitrary or sensitive JSON-RPC `data` is not exposed by default.
- Other initialize, load, new, prompt, and config-option errors retain their existing context.

## Not covered

This does not fix the original chat Enter failure in `louiselm-fp3r` and does not add multi-writer support. Codex ownership is behaving as designed; this issue concerns actionable error reporting.
close_reason: Fixed in working tree. Recognizes the exact Codex active-writer detail and returns a sanitized actionable message without exposing the thread id or arbitrary ACP data. Tests: tests/session/api_spec.lua 29/29; full mini.test 315/315. Formatting: changed files pass. Project-wide StyLua/LuaLS remain blocked only by pre-existing blog/scripts/tohtml-driver.lua issues.

title: Two ui/command_spec tests depend on the developer's environment: system clipboard provider and real ACP discovery
description:
After louiselm-zpsj's lyaml provisioning took CI from 36 failures to 2, the remaining two failures in tests/ui/command_spec.lua are environment coupling of a different kind. Both reproduce identically on two Neovim versions, so neither is a flake or a version regression.

## Observed

GitHub Actions run 32735415097, commit ce0764c, 2026-08-24, repo euri10/louiselm.

- job 97456920283, Neovim v0.12.5 (stable): `Fails (2)`
- job 97456920034, Neovim v0.13.0-dev-1403 (nightly): `Fails (2)`
- Same two test names in both. stylua and lua-language-server passed on the same run.

### Failure 1 -- system clipboard

`tests/ui/command_spec.lua:201`, test "copies and reports the current ACP session id".

```
Cause: different string length
Left:  ""
Right: "codex/prior-acp"
```

The runner log contains `clipboard: No provider. Try ":checkhealth" or ":h clipboard".` twice.

The test asserts on `nvim.fn.getreg("+")` -- the real system clipboard register. A headless CI runner has no clipboard provider (no xclip/wl-copy/X display), so the write to `+` is a silent no-op and the read returns empty. The assertion is therefore testing whether the machine running the suite has a clipboard tool installed, not whether louiselm copied the right value.

### Failure 2 -- real ACP discovery within 3s

`tests/ui/command_spec.lua:708`, test "schedules real ACP discovery before notifying the UI".

```
Left:  false
Right: true
```

The `false` is `completed` from `nvim.wait(3000, function() return notification ~= nil end, 10)` -- no notification arrived inside 3 seconds. The test expects the empty-case message "louiselm: no recoverable sessions found".

Root cause is not established. The empty case should if anything resolve faster on a clean runner than on the maintainer's machine, which has real ACP session state under ~/.local/state/acp-llm-adapter/. Candidates, none confirmed:
- discovery shells out to configured agent binaries that do not exist on the runner and waits on process spawn/timeout rather than failing fast;
- the 3000ms budget is simply too tight on a shared runner;
- discovery depends on a directory or env var that exists only on a developer machine and takes a slow path when absent.

## Symptoms

- The suite cannot go green on any machine without a clipboard provider, which includes every headless CI runner and any contributor on a bare server or container.
- Failure 1 presents as a value mismatch rather than "no clipboard provider", so the environmental cause is only visible by noticing an unrelated-looking line elsewhere in the log.

## Why it was not caught

Until 8dbff06 the plugin had no CI at all, so the suite had only ever run on machines with a desktop session and a populated ACP state directory. louiselm-zpsj records the same structural gap for lyaml; these two are the residue after that one was cleared.

## Fix direction

Not chosen.

Failure 1 -- the assertion's intent is "louiselm wrote the session id to the clipboard", which does not require a real provider. Setting a scriptable `vim.g.clipboard` in tests/minimal_init.lua (or per-test) would make the register writable in-process and test the actual behaviour. Installing xclip plus a virtual display in CI is the alternative and is strictly worse: it keeps the coupling and only hides it from this one environment.

Failure 2 -- needs diagnosis before a fix. Raising the timeout without knowing why it exceeded 3s would convert a real signal into a slow test.

## Acceptance

- Both tests pass on a headless machine with no clipboard provider and no pre-existing ACP session state.
- Whatever failure 2 turns out to be is understood before the fix, not papered over with a longer wait.

## Not covered

- Whether other specs read the `+` register was not audited; only the two failing tests were examined.
- No change to CI was made for these two; they remain red deliberately so the finding stays visible.
close_reason: Both failures were one cause: no clipboard provider. Fixed with an in-process vim.g.clipboard in tests/minimal_init.lua; the ACP discovery failure was a cascade from the first test's skipped cleanup and needed no timeout change.

comments.author: lotso
comments.text:
Root cause found and fixed in tests/minimal_init.lua: the two failures were ONE cause, not two.

Bisected locally by varying one env var at a time -- both failures reproduce with DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY unset and a real HOME, and neither reproduces with a clean HOME and DISPLAY present. So clean-checkout state was irrelevant; the absent clipboard provider caused both.

The cascade: 'copies and reports the current ACP session id' restores vim.system, vim.notify and Command.configure INLINE after its assertions (command_spec.lua:206-210). MiniTest.expect.equality throws on failure, so when the clipboard assertion at :201 fails those restores never run. The spec's post_case hook only calls delete_chat_buffers() and says so in a comment ('A failing expectation skips a test's own cleanup'), so vim.system stays replaced by fake_process's stub. The next test does real ACP discovery through that dead stub, never gets a notification, and its nvim.wait(3000) returns false. Fixing the first failure removed the second with no change to the timeout -- which is why the bead said not to raise it blind.

Fix: an in-process vim.g.clipboard provider in tests/minimal_init.lua, so the + register is readable/writable with no external tool. Chosen over installing xclip+Xvfb in CI, which would have kept the coupling and merely hidden it from one environment. Side benefit: the suite no longer clobbers the developer's real system clipboard, which is why the test had to save and restore it.

Verified: tests/ui/command_spec.lua Fails (0) under the sanitized env that previously reproduced both; full suite Fails (0) and exit 0 both sanitized and in a normal desktop session; stylua and lua-language-server both exit 0.

title: Inspect referenced Beads issues from chat
description:
## Goal

From a LouiseLM chat buffer, let the user inspect a referenced Beads issue without leaving Neovim.

## Scope

- In scope: a buffer-local normal-mode `<leader>lB` mapping in chat buffers and a corresponding public command/API as appropriate.
- In scope: extract one valid Beads issue ID (for example `louiselm-kpod`) from the cursor position; when none or more than one is available, prompt for the ID rather than guessing.
- In scope: validate the chosen ID, run `br show <id> --json` asynchronously with an argument array and the workspace cwd, decode JSON with Neovim's built-in JSON decoder, and show title, status, priority, labels, and description in a closable read-only floating buffer.
- In scope: actionable error feedback for unavailable `br`, an invalid/missing issue, command failure, or malformed output.
- Out of scope: modifying Beads state; launching a shell; inferring a Beads issue from `:LouiselmSessionId`; browsing/searching issues; configuration for the mapping; a tracker abstraction.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With the cursor on exactly one valid `louiselm-…` issue ID in a chat transcript, `<leader>lB` opens a floating read-only issue-detail view for that ID.
2. With no unambiguous issue ID under the cursor, the action prompts for an explicit ID and validates it before invoking `br`.
3. The implementation never passes the ACP Session identity returned by `:LouiselmSessionId` to `br show`; Session and Beads issue identities remain distinct.
4. `br show` uses `--json` and an argument array; command output is decoded with `vim.json.decode`, not parsed from human-readable CLI text.
5. The popup has a normal-mode close mapping and does not mutate the chat buffer or tracker state.
6. Expected process/JSON/not-found failures are reported cleanly without uncaught errors.

## Testing

- Headless UI/process tests cover cursor extraction, prompt fallback, valid JSON rendering, invalid IDs, command errors, and malformed JSON.
- Run focused tests plus the full MiniTest suite, StyLua, and lua-language-server.

## Notes

This is intentionally a narrow human UX surface. A Beads issue ID is a tracker identifier such as `louiselm-kpod`; it is not a Session identity such as `codex/<ACP-session-id>`.
close_reason: Completed: inspector, keymap, tests, help, and all gates passed

title: Undo during streaming triggers repeated extmark errors
description:
Editing or undoing in the chat buffer while an Agent is still streaming can leave cached rendering boundaries beyond the shortened buffer. Each later Session event then raises a scheduled-callback error instead of rendering normally, repeatedly interrupting the operator with a Press ENTER prompt.

## Observed

Reported from Session `codex/01a04bbb-8048-70d3-bd93-420ecc9750a6` on 2026-08-29 in Neovim after the operator used `<leader>lB`, typed text, and believes they undid an edit while the Model was responding.

Screenshot: `/home/lotso/Pictures/scrot/20260829_0620_1920x1200_1787977253.png`.


Verbatim visible error, repeated at least four times:

```text
vim.schedule callback: ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1345: Invalid 'line': out of range
stack traceback:
        [C]: in function 'nvim_buf_set_extmark'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1345: in function 'mark_prompt'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1728: in function 'insert_transcript'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2390: in function 'handle_event'
        ...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2806: in function <...ack/core/opt/louiselm.nvim/lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2805>
```

## Symptoms

- The operator sees the same red callback traceback and `Press ENTER or type command to continue` prompt for successive streaming events.
- The chat remains visually stuck around line 1372 while the winbar says `Model responding`.
- UI event rendering fails at prompt-extmark placement.

## Root cause

Unknown; the leading hypothesis is stale cached line state after undo shortens the chat buffer.

`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1725-1728` inserts at cached `view.transcript_tail`, updates that cache, then calls `mark_prompt(view, view.prompt_line + #replacement)`. `mark_prompt` passes that cached-derived line directly to `nvim_buf_set_extmark` at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:1343-1348`. The chat buffer attachment at `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2790-2795` observes changes only to clear a queued prompt; it does not reconcile `prompt_line`, `transcript_tail`, response runs, or tool-line caches after undo or arbitrary buffer edits.

This would explain the artifact: `nvim_buf_set_lines(..., strict_indexing=false)` may clamp a stale insertion index, while the following extmark call rejects a stale line beyond the new buffer length. A regression reproduction must confirm this sequence before treating it as established cause.

## Why it was not caught

`tests/ui/chat_spec.lua:809-839` covers undoing streamed transcript content and then submitting the visible prompt. It does not emit another asynchronous Session event after the undo, so it never exercises `insert_transcript` or prompt-extmark placement against the shortened buffer. No test combines in-flight streaming, operator buffer undo/edit, and the production scheduled callback boundary.

## Fix direction

At the narrowest shared rendering boundary, derive insertion and prompt positions from live extmarks/buffer state and reconcile or reject stale transcript caches before applying each Session event. Preserve normal prompt editing and queued-prompt behavior; do not merely clamp `mark_prompt`, because other cached line-indexed state may remain inconsistent.

## Acceptance

- A headless UI regression reproduces the observed order: an Agent emits transcript content, the operator undoes or otherwise shortens the chat buffer while the turn remains active, and a later event arrives through the scheduled production callback.
- No scheduled-callback error or command-line `Press ENTER` interruption occurs.
- Later chunks/tools render in order, the editable prompt remains at the true transcript boundary, and submitting it sends exactly the visible draft.
- Ordinary undo/edit behavior and session switching remain covered.

## Not covered

- Whether `<leader>lB` itself contributes to the corruption; it maps to `LouiselmInspectBead`, but the precise keystroke and window/buffer sequence was not captured.
- Repairing the already-corrupted live buffer or changing whether transcript regions are user-editable.
close_reason: Fixed in 414a858: undo restored the prompt extmark but left cached Lua line indexes beyond the shortened buffer; scheduled event handling now reconciles the boundary and resets active presentation indexes. Regression covers undo followed by a tool event, later prose, and clean prompt submission. Live acceptance passed in codex/01a04bd4-9fa2-70a3-9e3f-603a7f214238: marker submitted as a standalone prompt and :messages had no extmark/scheduled-callback traceback. Gates: focused chat 140/140, full MiniTest 732/732, StyLua, LuaLS, API appendix check, diff check. QA round: louiselm-n8w8.

comments.author: codex/01a04bbb-8048-70d3-bd93-420ecc9750a6
comments.text:
Root cause confirmed with a scheduled headless regression. After a streamed multiline chunk, undo shortened the buffer from beneath cached `view.prompt_line`/`transcript_tail`/active-block indexes. The prompt extmark correctly restored to the real boundary, but the Lua indexes remained beyond the buffer; the next tool event reproduced the screenshot traceback at `mark_prompt`, and the tool row then polluted the submitted draft.

Fix: before every scheduled Session event, if the cached prompt line is outside the current buffer, recover the boundary from the existing prompt extmark and reset only the active presentation block indexes. Ordinary in-range streaming stays untouched; an initially broader reconciliation on every one-line extmark difference regressed tool ordering/folds and was rejected. The regression now proves a tool event and later prose chunk render after undo and that submission sends only the visible recovered draft.

Evidence: red test reproduced `Invalid line: out of range` through `mark_prompt -> insert_transcript -> handle_event`; focused `tests/ui/chat_spec.lua` 140/140; full MiniTest 732/732; `stylua --check .`; `lua-language-server --check . --checklevel=Warning`; `./scripts/generate-api-appendix --check`; `git diff --check` all pass.

Lessons destination: this issue comment; no standing AGENTS.md rule or design question is warranted. Live acceptance remains required by AGENTS.md: restart Neovim to load the change, repeat the undo-during-response sequence, and confirm later events render without repeated callback warnings and the visible draft remains clean.

title: Handoff context as typed resource block when target supports embeddedContext
description:
## Goal

The `## Context` section of a Handoff travels as a typed ACP resource block — `[resource] <louiselm://handoff/<source-id>>` after adapter rendering — when the target Agent supports it, and as today's flattened text otherwise.

## Scope

- In scope (`lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua`, `submit_handoff`):
  - split the reviewed buffer into its `## Handoff` and `## Context` sections;
  - when the target Session advertises `promptCapabilities.embeddedContext` (read from the Session state populated at `lua/louiselm/session/lifecycle.lua:469`), send prompt content as two blocks in order: a text block with the `## Handoff` section, then a resource block with `uri = "louiselm://handoff/<source-id>"`, `mimeType = "text/markdown"`, text = `## Context` section;
  - otherwise send the whole brief as one flattened text prompt (the behavior of the previous slice, preserved as the fallback);
  - `## Source` travels with the Context text; the target view's transcript recording (`record_handoff`) stays on the reviewed brief text regardless of transport.
- Out of scope: backend-side message-role separation in ACP adapters (the deepseek adapter concatenates blocks into one backend prompt today; the typed framing label is the accepted contract); compaction rules; buffer structure; the no-progress loop guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A target whose Session state has `embedded_context == true` receives a prompt whose content is `{ text_block, resource_block }` in that order, with the resource carrying `louiselm://handoff/<source-id>` and the full `## Context` text.
2. A target with `embedded_context == false` (or absent) receives the same brief as a single text block — byte-equivalent to the previous slice's payload for the same buffer.
3. The `## Handoff` instruction is never inside the resource block.
4. The transcript records the reviewed brief (not the block table) on the target view.
5. stylua, lua-language-server, and full mini.test gates pass.

## Testing

- Fake-session UI tests covering both capability states, asserting the exact content-block shapes through the `session:prompt` boundary.
- A regression case for the fallback path keeps the flattened-text contract pinned.

## Notes

- Design record: louiselm-93wl (closed). Depends on louiselm-mtte (review buffer) — the split reads the same buffer this slice composes.
- Do not use the Forensics `capabilities` record for this check: it misreads `embeddedContext` (louiselm-7nod). Read the Session state field set by `lifecycle.lua`, which is correct.
close_reason: Implemented in 4d74859: submit_handoff splits the reviewed brief at ## Context when the target state carries embedded_context (lifecycle.lua:469 read, not the broken Forensics field): text block carries the ## Handoff instruction, resource block (louiselm://handoff/<source>, text/markdown) carries ## Context through ## Source. Non-embedded targets and briefs whose ## Context header was edited out keep the flattened text prompt. Target transcript still records the reviewed brief text. Gates: chat spec green incl. new embedded-transport, fallback, and edited-header cases; full mini.test suite green; stylua, lua-language-server, generate-api-appendix clean.

title: Documented test setup omits lyaml, so a clean environment fails 36 tests that pass on the author's machine
description:
`scripts/install-test-deps` installs only mini.nvim. The skills feature additionally requires `lyaml`, which is present on the maintainer's machine via LuaRocks but is installed by nothing in this repository. The suite therefore passes locally and fails on any clean checkout, including CI and any new contributor's first run.

## Observed

First GitHub Actions run after wiring the plugin gates: run 32735068144, job 97455811853 (mini.test, nvim stable), repo euri10/louiselm, 2026-08-24. Identical failure on the nightly matrix leg.

- `Fails (36) and Notes (0)`, against `Fails (0)` for the same commit (8dbff06) run locally.
- 45 occurrences of `lyaml` in the failure log.
- Failures by spec: skills_spec.lua 24, ui/chat_spec.lua 8, ui/command_spec.lua 3, health_spec.lua 1.
- Representative cause, verbatim from the runner:
  `Neovim cannot find lyaml in package.path or package.cpath; install it with `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 install lyaml``
- CI Neovim was v0.12.5, i.e. NEWER than the maintainer's v0.12.2, so this is not a version regression. `stylua` and `lua-language-server` both passed on the same run, isolating the cause to the test environment rather than the source.
- Local provenance of the dependency that masks this: `luarocks --lua-version 5.1 list lyaml` reports 6.2.9-2 installed in two trees under $HOME (`~/.luarocks` and `~/.asdf/installs/lua/5.1.5/...`). Nothing in the repository puts it there.

## Symptoms

- A clean clone following AGENTS.md section 4's documented manual workflow (`./scripts/install-test-deps` then the headless MiniTest command) fails 36 cases.
- The failure presents as 36 unrelated-looking assertion mismatches across four spec files rather than one dependency error, because each test compares against expected skill data and receives the graceful-degradation warning instead.

## Root cause

`lua/louiselm/skills/discovery.lua:79` does `pcall(require, "lyaml")` and degrades gracefully to a structured `missing_dependency` diagnostic when absent. That degradation is correct product behaviour, and health_spec/skills_spec have a test for exactly that path (skills_spec.lua:667). But the remaining tests assert on real parsed skill metadata, which is unreachable without lyaml, so they receive the warning payload instead of parsed data.

The gap is in provisioning, not in the source: `scripts/install-test-deps` pins and verifies mini.nvim only, and AGENTS.md section 4 presents that script as the complete setup step.

## Why it was not caught

There was no CI for the plugin at all until 8dbff06 -- `.gitlab-ci.yml` builds only `blog/` and says so explicitly. Every prior run of the suite happened on a machine that already had lyaml, so the coupling was invisible. This is the first execution of the suite in a clean environment.

## Fix direction

Not chosen; two candidates with different contract implications.

1. Install lyaml in CI only. Unblocks the pipeline, leaves the clean-clone gap for humans.
2. Teach `scripts/install-test-deps` to provision lyaml, so the documented path is complete for CI and contributors alike. Correct, but it makes a LuaRocks/native-library toolchain a prerequisite of running the tests.

Option 2 interacts with AGENTS.md section 3, which states "Lua runtime dependencies are forbidden; use LuaJIT and stable Neovim APIs" and "mini.test is the sole test dependency". lyaml is a Lua runtime dependency with a C/LibYAML component, so either the contract wording or the skills implementation is already out of step with the other; that tension predates this bug and should be resolved deliberately rather than settled by whichever fix lands here.

## Acceptance

- The suite passes from a clean checkout using only what the repository provides and documents.
- Whichever option is chosen, AGENTS.md section 3/section 4 and `scripts/install-test-deps` agree with each other and with what the skills code actually requires.

## Not covered

- Whether lyaml should remain a dependency at all (a hand-rolled frontmatter parser was not evaluated).
- The pre-existing AGENTS.md section 3 contradiction is noted here as context; if it needs a decision it deserves its own needs-design question.
close_reason: Maintainer chose option 1: lyaml installed in CI only (ce0764c, green on run 32735415097), clean-clone gap accepted and now documented in AGENTS.md section 4 so it is a known limitation rather than a trap. The AGENTS.md section 3 contract contradiction is split to louiselm-4gif rather than settled here.

title: Copilot completion result is hidden behind an unlabeled tool row
description:
Copilot can end a completed Session with its human-facing conclusion only in a completed ACP `tool_call` named `task_complete`. LouiseLM then renders only `[tool] <id>: task_complete (completed)`, leaving the Session ready with no readable answer. The full payload is retained and contains the conclusion, but the UI gives no result-inspection cue except for image outputs.

## Observed

Live Neovim Session `copilot/7d80a2e8-1599-4805-9d4f-9969a0af14aa` on 2026-08-25, Agent configuration: Autopilot, GPT-5.6 Terra, reasoning effort medium, Allow All on.

The first limits-design turn ended with `task_complete`; its raw ACP tool payload has `status="completed"`, `title="task_complete"`, and a textual `rawOutput.content`/`content` block containing the full conclusion. A follow-up prompt, `so what is your conclusion ?`, ended with another completed `task_complete` whose retained textual result begins `Conclusion: keep the Codex extension...`. In both cases the Session reached `status=ready`, but the chat buffer showed only the completed tool row and no assistant message chunk after it.

## Symptoms

- A user sees Copilot stop apparently mid-task, even though the Agent reported completion.
- The conclusion is not visible in the transcript timeline.
- `:LouiselmInspectTool` can reveal the retained raw payload only if the user already knows that command and puts the cursor on the tool row; the ordinary completed row supplies no cue.

## Root cause

Two boundaries combine:

1. Copilot ACP emits its conclusion through a `tool_call` with `title="task_complete"`, rather than an ACP `agent_message_chunk`.
2. `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2070-2129` renders a tool update only as its id, title, and status. It adds the `:LouiselmInspectTool` hint solely for image-bearing payloads at lines 2102-2104. The full data is correctly retained by `lua/louiselm/session/transcript.lua:93-139` and is inspectable through `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2623-2627` / `lua/louiselm/ui/chat/command.lua:404-411`, but its textual result is not surfaced or signposted.

It remains unverified whether Copilot ACP should instead translate `task_complete` into a normal assistant message; the live wire behavior is valid enough for LouiseLM to retain it.

## Why it was not caught

The chat suite covers chronology and the image-only inspector hint, but not a completed non-image tool call carrying the only user-facing text result, nor a final result emitted as a tool call without a later assistant chunk.

## Fix direction

At the LouiseLM presentation boundary, make a completed tool call with retained textual output visibly inspectable, at minimum with an actionable `:LouiselmInspectTool` cue analogous to image results. Decide separately whether a known final-result tool such as `task_complete` should render its textual summary inline; do not broadly dump arbitrary tool input/output into chat because those payloads may be sensitive. Consider an upstream Copilot ACP translation only after capturing the raw framed transcript through `acp-proxy` and checking the adapter contract.

## Acceptance

- A regression fixture with a completed `task_complete`-style ACP tool payload containing text fails before the change.
- The timeline makes the payload discoverable from the completed row, and `:LouiselmInspectTool` opened on that row shows the retained result.
- The result is not lost when no later assistant message arrives.
- Ordinary tool chronology and image-result behavior remain unchanged.

## Not covered

Changing Copilot model completion behavior, exposing raw results automatically, or treating all tool payloads as safe transcript text.

comments.author: claude/edc00380-9cc9-438e-ad38-3bb929cdc43c
comments.text:
Live acceptance FAILED for the current implementation. Manual QA round 2026-08-25, build acb65c7.

Session copilot/a6c39112-8bad-4c24-9c37-bad32cf4f1df, Mode=Autopilot, Model=GPT-5.6 Terra, Reasoning Effort=medium, Allow All=On.
Log: /tmp/louiselm-qa-2026-08-25/state/acp-llm-adapter/proxy/sessions/a6c39112-8bad-4c24-9c37-bad32cf4f1df/log.jsonl

## Observed

The chat buffer rendered, in order:

    Section 11 forbids trusting external input before validation; ... (assistant prose)
    [usage] total_tokens=101883 ...
    [tool] call_S3CN4eYABhCc6QNdBcCgurLj: task_complete (completed) - text result - use :LouiselmInspectTool

The retained rawOutput.content conclusion (256 chars, begins "**Conclusion:** Section 11 forbids
unvalidated external input, ...") was NOT rendered inline. Only the status row appeared.

## Root cause: the terminal completion arrives after turn_done

The pending-terminal-completion design assumes the completed task_complete tool update is processed
before turn_done. Copilot in Autopilot emits it afterwards. Wire timestamps:

    06:28:34.245Z  agent_to_client  session/prompt RESULT  {"stopReason":"end_turn", "usage":{...}}
    06:28:36.375Z  agent_to_client  tool_call         task_complete  pending
    06:28:36.386Z  agent_to_client  tool_call_update  task_complete  completed

The task_complete frames land 2.1 seconds AFTER end_turn. At turn_done
(lua/louiselm/ui/chat/init.lua:2223-2236) view.pending_terminal_completion is still nil, so nothing
is flushed; the [usage] line is emitted; only then does the tool row render. The flush point is
never reached again for that turn.

This is the same ordering the [usage] line makes visible in the buffer: [usage] precedes the
task_complete row, which is exactly the turn_done-before-tool-update sequence.

## Why the regression test did not catch it

The added coverage drives the completed task_complete update and then turn_done. The real Agent
reverses that order. The fixture encodes the assumed sequence rather than the observed one.

## Secondary observation, not a failure

The text-result cue from the earlier narrow fix works: every completed tool update carrying textual
output rendered "- text result - use :LouiselmInspectTool", including the task_complete row itself,
and the one failed tool row correctly carried no cue. The conclusion IS reachable through
:LouiselmInspectTool, so this is a presentation failure rather than data loss.

## Note on the duplicate-suppression rule

In this Session the assistant ALSO streamed an equivalent conclusion before task_complete, so the
maintainer was not left blank. Under the current clear-on-any-later-chunk rule, if the ordering had
been the assumed one the user would have seen the conclusion twice in different wording, because the
rule asks "was the most recent event a chunk" rather than "did this turn produce prose at all"
(view.response_started already tracks the latter and is not consulted at the flush). Whichever
ordering fix is chosen, the duplicate rule needs deciding for the case where the Agent streams a
real answer AND emits task_complete in one turn.

Filed from manual QA; not fixed here because this issue is live-claimed by
codex/01a03745-630b-7282-aa02-8ceef6cf0405 (age 88m, classification fresh).

title: Evaluate md-render.nvim for LouiseLM Markdown UX
description:
Investigate whether https://github.com/delphinus/md-render.nvim could improve LouiseLM's Markdown presentation, while preserving the project's preference for a native Neovim experience and a small dependency surface.

Context:
- LouiseLM currently uses Neovim Treesitter Markdown highlighting; that appears acceptable for ordinary transcript content.
- The suspected pain point is very long pasted shell commands in human inputs, where the current chat/transcript rendering may become unwieldy or expensive.
- md-render.nvim is a separate terminal-side renderer with floating/tab/split/pager modes, rich inline formatting, tables, callouts/folds, clickable links, images/video/Mermaid, CommonMark wrapping, and Treesitter-highlighted code blocks.
- Its README states Neovim >= 0.12 and optional curl, ffmpeg/ImageMagick, Mermaid CLI, budoux.lua, icon plugins, and Treesitter parsers; assess which are actually relevant rather than treating all optional features as required.

Investigation:
1. Read the plugin source/docs enough to understand rendering architecture, lifecycle, update behavior, performance characteristics, and integration/library APIs.
2. Compare it with LouiseLM's existing chat buffer/session rendering and native Neovim facilities.
3. Reproduce or characterize representative long pasted shell commands and streamed transcript content; determine whether the problem is Markdown parsing/highlighting, line wrapping/layout, buffer growth, or something else.
4. Evaluate integration options: adopt the plugin, use a narrow piece/library API, improve LouiseLM locally, or defer. Consider Neovim version compatibility, terminal assumptions (including Kitty graphics), external executables, startup/runtime cost, ownership/lifecycle, async safety, and user-config impact.

Acceptance criteria:
- Record an evidence-backed recommendation with explicit dependency and UX trade-offs.
- Include the smallest useful test/reproduction for long pasted shell commands and any measured or observed limits.
- Identify concrete features worth borrowing or integrating, if any, without committing to a dependency before the comparison.
- If no adoption is justified, state the focused native LouiseLM improvement (or why no change is needed).
- File any separate implementation bug/design question discovered during the investigation before closing this task.

title: QA round: physical Android gardening capture
description:
# QA review: physical Android gardening capture

## Scope

- Work item: `louiselm-qbr.1.9`
- Build under test: Android fix `43aaa9b`, capture fixes `456031b`, `13dfe23`, and `f7d85fc`, Android `0.1.0` (`versionCode=1`)
- Device: Xiaomi 21081111RG, Android device serial ending in `u4ai`
- Session mode: Codex ACP full permissions/full access enabled
- Privacy: do not paste pairing QR contents, device credentials, API keys, or audio content into this review

Full permissions applies to this Codex session only. It does not bypass the
Android app's certificate pin, pairing credential, server authorization, or
device revocation.

## Preflight evidence

- [x] Debug APK exists at `android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`.
- [x] Physical device is connected and authorized through ADB.
- [x] `dev.louiselm.capture` version `0.1.0` is installed.
- [x] App-private storage is readable with `run-as` for objective UUID/status evidence.
- [x] Four older captures exist on both phone and receiver and are marked uploaded locally.
- [x] Three older captures remain queued locally; they are not the test fixture for this round.
- [x] Receiver is listening on the current LAN interface at `192.168.10.121:7391`.
- [x] Transcription is privately configured and funded; the key value was never printed or recorded here.

## Status

| Case | Behavior | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Offline recording survives app restart | Passed | UUID `cd129a0d-1ab7-4b2f-b9f8-4c77172866c0`; complete local audio/manifest, no `uploaded` marker |
| 2 | Backgrounding finalizes an active recording | Passed | UUID `506515c0-8582-4190-94b8-298a8ef95ea8`; complete local audio/manifest, no partial artifact |
| 3 | Pair and upload the same immutable UUID | Passed after F1 fix | 10 receiver captures; all 6 queued UUIDs uploaded; Case 1 UUID appears once with matching digest |
| 4 | Interrupted upload retries without duplication | Passed | UUID `4d681e60-2007-4b10-8c85-b351793e7b6c` exists once on receiver after failed attempt/retry |
| 5 | Phone reboot preserves queued work | Passed | UUID `bdf2b46b-689d-4b23-befd-60888a55f047` uploaded automatically once after reboot |
| 6 | Transcript appears in Neovim inbox | Passed | Case 1 is `completed`; tester sees its UUID and transcript text in `louiselm://capture-inbox` |
| 7 | Revocation rejects later upload and preserves audio | Passed | UUID `7c7353dc-1c2c-474a-a4c8-a39d102f82e8` remains local with `operator_action` after receiver rejection |
| 8 | Certificate replacement is rejected | Passed | UUID `fe4a8cf8-b082-4eac-9899-c19c57330d0c` rejected the replacement pin, then uploaded once after restoration |

## Case 1 — offline record and restart

Goal: prove the real microphone/storage lifecycle remains useful with no
network and after process death.

Exercises: `MainActivity.stopRecording`, `CaptureStore.complete`, and
`CaptureStore.recover`.

Steps for the human tester:

1. On the phone, disable Wi-Fi and mobile data (airplane mode is fine).
2. Open **LouiseLM Capture** and note the displayed waiting count. It should
   currently be 3.
3. Tap **Start capture**, speak a unique phrase for at least five seconds, then
   tap **Stop and save**.
4. Wait for `Capture <UUID> is durable and queued.` Record only the UUID here;
   do not transcribe the spoken phrase.
5. Force-stop the app from Android app info, reopen it while still offline, and
   report the waiting count and status text.

Expected:

- Waiting count rises from 3 to 4.
- Reopening shows the capture still waiting locally with no attention error.
- The capture has `audio.m4a` and `capture.json`, and no `uploaded` marker.

Failure signature:

- Count returns to 3, the new UUID disappears, an error is displayed, or an
  `uploaded` marker appears despite the phone being offline.

Evidence command (run by Codex after the tester reports completion):

```sh
/home/lotso/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb shell run-as dev.louiselm.capture \
  find files/captures -maxdepth 2 -type f
```

The file listing proves durable local artifacts and upload state. The tester's
observation proves the visible count/status and successful real recording.

Result (2026-08-21): **passed**.

- Tester observed the waiting count rise from 3 to 4 after force-stop/reopen.
- Full UUID: `cd129a0d-1ab7-4b2f-b9f8-4c77172866c0`.
- Manifest: Android source, 9,127 ms, 146,298 bytes, `audio/mp4`.
- The audio SHA-256 matched the manifest.
- `audio.m4a` and `capture.json` are present.
- No `uploaded` marker or partial `.recording-*`/`.incoming-*` artifact exists.

## Case 2 — background finalizes recording

Goal: prove leaving the app while recording saves rather than loses the audio.

Steps:

1. Remain offline and open the app.
2. Start a new capture and speak for at least five seconds.
3. Press Home without tapping stop.
4. Reopen the app and report its waiting count/status.

Expected: `onStop` finalizes one new immutable UUID and the waiting count rises
by one. Failure signature: no new UUID, a partial `.recording-*` file remains,
or the UI reports a storage failure.

Evidence: the same ADB file listing, pinned to the new UUID.

Result (2026-08-21): **passed**.

- The first attempt did not use Home and saved normally as
  `31d5b0a8-006e-4ab1-a063-d3fac08d227e` (6,945 ms, 111,397 bytes).
- The corrected Home-button attempt saved as
  `506515c0-8582-4190-94b8-298a8ef95ea8` (4,883 ms, 78,300 bytes).
- Tester observed 6 waiting captures, matching the two new local records.
- Both audio digests match their manifests; neither has an `uploaded` marker.
- No abandoned `.recording-*` or `.incoming-*` artifact exists.

## Case 3 — pair and publish the same UUID

Prerequisites:

- Bind the TLS receiver to `192.168.10.121:7391` and restart its user service.
- Put phone and workstation on the same trusted LAN.
- Generate a fresh one-time QR with `:LouiselmCapturePair`. Scan it directly;
  never save or paste its contents.

Steps:

1. Re-enable Wi-Fi.
2. If the app is not paired to the current certificate, tap **Pair receiver
   QR** and photograph the fresh QR shown in Neovim.
3. Tap **Sync now**.
4. Open `:LouiselmInbox` in Neovim and select the Case 1 UUID.

Expected: the exact Case 1 UUID exists once on the receiver, local storage gains
an `uploaded` marker, and Neovim opens that same capture. Failure signature:
pairing fails, upload enters attention state, the UUID changes, the receiver has
duplicates, or the inbox cannot open it.

Evidence:

```sh
louiselm-capture show <CASE-1-UUID>
/home/lotso/Android/Sdk/platform-tools/adb shell run-as dev.louiselm.capture \
  find files/captures/<CASE-1-UUID> -maxdepth 1 -type f
```

Result (2026-08-21): **passed after F1 fix**.

- Before the fix, the user saw 6 waiting after **Sync now** and WorkManager
  retained a 3h10m timing delay despite validated Wi-Fi.
- After reinstalling the fixed APK with app data preserved, the user confirmed
  pairing, tapped **Sync now**, and observed zero attention on reopen.
- Receiver count rose from 4 to 10; all six queued UUIDs gained local
  `uploaded` markers.
- Case 1 UUID `cd129a0d-1ab7-4b2f-b9f8-4c77172866c0` exists exactly once on
  the receiver with the same 146,298-byte size and SHA-256 digest.

## Case 4 — interrupted upload is idempotent

Goal: prove retry uses one UUID instead of publishing duplicates.

Steps:

1. Record a new capture on Wi-Fi and note its UUID.
2. Stop the receiver service, tap **Sync now**, wait for queued retry, then
   restart the receiver service and tap **Sync now** once.
